english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Mfitiaseɛ no Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Na asase da hɔ hunu a ɛnni bɔbea biara, na esum wɔ ebunu ani. Na Nyankopɔn honhom butu nsuo no ani.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ hann! Na ɛyɛɛ hann.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu hann no sɛ ɛyɛ. Na Onyankopɔn paee hann ne esum no mu.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ hann no sɛ adekyee, ne esum no adesae. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛdi kan ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ewiem mmra, na ɛmmɛpae nsuo no mu.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ ewiem no ɔsoro. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so mmienu ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nsuo a ɛwɔ ɔsoro aseɛ no mmoaboa ano wɔ faako, na wɔnhunu asase pɛsɛɛ. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ pɛsɛɛ no asase, na nsuo mmoano no, ɔfrɛɛ no ɛpo. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Asase mfifiri nwira, mfudeɛ, nnuaba sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na asase fifirii nwira ne nnuaba sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nkanea mmra ewiem, na ɛmmɛpae awia ne anadwo mu, na ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ mma ɛberɛ, nna ne mfeɛ nkyekyɛmu.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Bio, na ɛnyɛ nkanea wɔ ewiem, na ɛnhyerɛn wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ nkanea akɛseɛ mmienu no, sɛ kɛseɛ no nni adekyeeɛ so, na ketewa no, sɛ ɛnni anadwo so. Ɔyɛɛ nsoromma nso.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn de sisii ewiem sɛ ɛnhyerɛn wɔ asase so,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: na ɛnni adekyeeɛ ne adesaeɛ so, na ɛmpae hann ne esum no mu. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nnan ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nsuo no nnɔre abɔdeɛ a ɛte aseɛ pii, na ntakraboa ntu mfa asase so wɔ ewiem.

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ nsuboa akɛseɛ ne nketewa ahodoɔ sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ; ne ntakraboa nyinaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔ, na monyɛ ɛpo mu ma, na ntakraboa nnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nnum ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Abɔdeɛ a ɛtete aseɛ mfiri asase mu mmra, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ: Ntɔteboa a ɛwɔ fie ne wiram ne mmoa a wɔwea ne asase so mmoadoma, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ asase so mmoadoma, ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea fam nyinaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Momma yɛnyɛ onipa wɔ yɛn suban so sɛ yɛn nsɛsoɔ, na wɔnni ɛpo mu mpataa, ewiem nnomaa, ntɔteboa, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa wɔ ne suban so. Aane, Nyankopɔn suban so na ɔbɔɔ no, ɔbarima ne ɔbaa na ɔbɔɔ wɔn.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔre, na monyɛ asase so ma, na monya so tumi; na monni ɛpo mu mpataa ne ewiem nnomaa ne mmoa a wɔwɔ asase soɔ nyinaa so.

english_verse: I have provided all kinds of fruit and grain for you to eat.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, mede mfudeɛ a ɛwɔ asase ani nyinaa ne nnuaba nyinaa mama mo sɛ ɛnyɛ mo aduane.

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne ewiem nnomaa nyinaa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ nyinaa, mede nhahan mono mama wɔn sɛ wɔnni. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu deɛ ɔyɛeɛ nyinaa, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ pa ara. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nsia ne no.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Na wɔwiee ɔsoro ne asase ne deɛ ɛwɔ mu nyinaa bɔ.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa da a ɛtɔ so nson no so, na ɔtee ho, ɛfiri sɛ ɛno mu na ɔhome firii n’adwuma a ɔyɛeɛ wɔ adebɔ mu no nyinaa ho. Eden turo no

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: Na afuo mu nnua nyinaa nnya mmaa asase so, na afuo mu nhahan nyinaa nnya mfifirii, ɛfiri sɛ na AWURADE Nyankopɔn nnya ntɔɔ nsuo nguu asase no so, na na onipa a ɔbɛdɔ asase nni hɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Na nsuo firi asase so foroe, na ɛfɔɔ asase ani nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de fam dɔteɛ nwonoo onipa, na ɔhuu nkwa home guu ne hwene mu, na onipa yɛɛ ɔkra teasefoɔ.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ turo bi wɔ Eden a ɛwɔ apueeɛ fam, na ɔde onipa a ɔnwonoo no no tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnua ahodoɔ nyinaa a wɔhwɛ a, ɛyɛ fɛ, na ɛyɛ sɛ wɔdie asase no so, ne nkwa dua a ɛsi turo no mfimfini, ne papa ne bɔne ho nimdeɛ dua fifirii asase no so.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Na asuo bi tene firi Eden bɛfɔ turo no, na ɛfiri hɔ ara na emu paapae yɛɛ nsutire nnan.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Deɛ ɛdi kan no din de Pison, ɛno na ɛkonton twa Hawila asase a sika wɔ soɔ no nyinaa ho hyiae.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Na asase no so sika yɛ papa. Ɛhɔ na bedola aduhwam ne apopobibireboɔ wɔ.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na asuo a ɛtɔ so mmienu no din de Gihon. Ɛno na ɛkonton twa Kus asase nyinaa ho hyia.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na asuo a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no ne Tigri, ɛno na ɛsene wɔ Asiria apueeɛ. Na asuo a ɛtɔ so nnan ne Eufrate.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de onipa no kɔtenaa Eden turom sɛ ɔnnɔ na ɔnwɛn hɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ onipa no sɛ: Turom ha nnua nyinaa, di bi.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Na mmom papa ne bɔne ho nimdeɛ dua no deɛ, nni; ɛfiri sɛ da a wobɛdi bie no, wuo na wobɛwuo.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ sɛ onipa nko tena; mɛyɛ ne nsɛsoɔ boafoɔ mama no.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnahɔɔ tɔɔ onipa no so, na ɔdae. Na ɔyii ne mfe mpadeɛ mu baako, na ɔde nam tuaa ananmu.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de mpadeɛ a ɔyi firii onipa no mu no yɛɛ ɔbaa, na ɔde no brɛɛ onipa no.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na onipa no kaa sɛ: Ampa ara, me nnompe mu dompe, ne me honam mu nam ankasa nie. Oyi na wɔbɛfrɛ no Ɔbaa, ɛfiri sɛ Ɔbarima mu na wɔyii no firiiɛ.

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Saa nti na ɔbarima bɛgya ne na ne n’agya hɔ, na ɔde ne ho akɔbata ne yere ho, na wɔayɛ honam korɔ.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu no deda adagya, ɔbarima no ne ne yere, nanso wɔn ani anwu.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ yɛ aniteɛ kyɛne wiram mmoadoma a AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ wɔn nyinaa. Na ɔbisaa ɔbaa no sɛ: Ampa ara sɛ Onyankopɔn aka akyerɛ mo sɛ: Monnni turom ha nnua nyinaa bi?

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa no buaa ɔwɔ no sɛ: Turom ha nnua aba no, yɛdi bi;

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: nanso dua a ɛsi turo no mfimfini no aba deɛ, Onyankopɔn aka sɛ: Monnni bi, nso mommfa mo nsa nnka, na moanwu.

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbaa no sɛ: Ɛnyɛ wuo na mobɛwuo;

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: na Onyankopɔn nim sɛ da a mobɛdi bie no, mo ani bɛbue, na moayɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn ahunu papa ne bɔne.

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa no hunuu sɛ dua no yɛ sɛ wɔdie, na ɛyɛ aniwa fɛ, ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ, na ɛbɛte ani, enti ɔtee n’aba bi, na ɔdii, na ɔde bi maa ne kunu a ɔka ne ho no nso, na ɔdii.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu ani buebuee, na wɔhunuu sɛ wɔdeda adagya, enti wɔpempam borɔdɔma ahahan yɛɛ nkatanim fae.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Na wɔtee AWURADE Nyankopɔn nka sɛ ɔnam turom hɔ wɔ anwummerɛ mferɛ mu. Na Adam ne ne yere kɔhunta firii AWURADE Nyankopɔn anim wɔ turom hɔ nnua mu.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn frɛɛ Adam, na ɔbisaa no sɛ: Wowɔ he?

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Metee wo nka wɔ turom hɔ no, mesuroe, ɛfiri sɛ meda adagya, na mehuntae.

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa no sɛ: Hwan na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo sɛ woda adagya? Dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni bie no na woadie yi?

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Na Adam kaa sɛ: Ɔbaa no a wode no bɛkaa me ho no, ɔno na ɔmaa me dua no aba no bie, na mediiɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔbaa no sɛ: Adɛn na woyɛɛ saa? Na ɔbaa no se: Ɔwɔ no na ɔdaadaa me, maa mediiɛ. Onipa bu atɛn

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Ɛnam sɛ woayɛ yei nti, wɔadome wo ntɔteboa ne wiram mmoadoma nyinaa mu. Wo yafunu so na wobɛnanteɛ, na woadi dɔteɛ wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Na mede ɔtan bɛto wo ne ɔbaa no ntam, ɛne w’asefoɔ ne n’asefoɔ ntam; ɔno na ɔbɛbɔ wo tire, na wo nso woaka ne nantin.

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ɔbaa no deɛ, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dɔ na mɛma wo yea ne wo nyinsɛn mu brɛ adɔɔso. Yea mu na wobɛwo mma, na w’ani bɛgyina wo kunu, na ɔno na ɔbɛdi wo soɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na Adam deɛ, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ woatie wo yere nne, na woadi dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nnie no bie nti, wo nti wɔadome asase. Yea mu na wobɛdidi soɔ wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Na nkasɛɛ ne nnɛnkyɛnse na ɛbɛfifiri ama woɔ, na woadi afuo mu ahahan.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: W’anim fifire mu na wobɛdidie de akɔsi sɛ wobɛsane akɔ dɔteɛ mu, ɛfiri sɛ emu na wɔyii wo firiiɛ; na woyɛ dɔteɛ, na dɔteɛ mu na wobɛsane akorɔ.

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Na Adam no too ne yere din Hawa, ɛfiri sɛ ɔno na ɔyɛ ateasefoɔ nyinaa na.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ nwoma ntadeɛ maa Adam ne ne yere de hyɛɛ wɔn. Wɔpamo Adam ne Hawa firi turo no mu

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, onipa no ayɛ sɛ yɛn mu baako, hunu papa ne bɔne. Na afei, deɛ ɛbɛyɛ na wantene ne nsa ante nkwa dua no nso bi anni antena ase daa nti,

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: AWURADE Nyankopɔn tuu no firii Eden turom hɔ sɛ ɔnkɔdɔ asase a wɔfaa no firii mu no.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Na ɔpamm onipa no, na ɔde Kerubim ne ogyaframa afena a ɛdi ahim bɛsii Eden turo no anim apueeɛ fam sɛ wɔnwɛn ɔkwan a ɛde kɔ nkwa dua no ho no.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere Hawa daeɛ, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Kain. Na ɔkaa sɛ: AWURADE adaworoma manya ɔbarima.

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo ne nua Habel kaa ne ho. Na Habel yɛ odwanhwɛfoɔ, ɛna Kain nso yɛ okuafoɔ.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ nna bi akyiri no, Kain de afuom nnoɔma bɛyɛɛ AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Na Habel nso de ne nnwan mu mmakan ne wɔn a wɔadɔre no bi bɛmae. Na AWURADE ani sɔɔ Habel ne n’ayɛyɛdeɛ no,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: nanso Kain ne n’ayɛyɛdeɛ no deɛ, n’ani ansɔ. Kain bo fuu pii, na ɔmunae.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Adɛn nti na wo bo afuo na woamuna yi?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Sɛ woyɛɛ no yie a, anka w’anim rente anaa? Na sɛ woanyɛ no yie enti, bɔne butu ɛpono ano, na w’akyiri kwan na ɛhwehwɛ, nanso di ne so.

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Na Kain ka kyerɛɛ ne nua sɛ, ma yɛn nkɔ afuom. Na ɛbaa sɛ wɔwɔ afuom no, Kain sɔre tiaa ne nua Habel, na ɔkumm no.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Ɛhe na wo nua Habel wɔ? Na ɔse: Mennim, me nua so hwɛfoɔ ne me anaa?

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ yi? Wo nua mogya nne reteam frɛ me firi asase so.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Na afei wɔadome wo afiri asase a abue n’ano agye wo nua mogya afiri wo nsam no so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Sɛ wodɔ asase a, ɛrenkɔ so mma wo ne nnɔbaeɛ bio na wobɛyɛ ɔkobɔni ne asesabɔni wɔ asase so.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, woapamo me nnɛ afiri asase yi so, na mɛhunta mafiri w’anim, na mayɛ ɔkobɔni ne asesabɔni wɔ asase so, na obiara a ɔbɛhu me no, ɔbɛku me.

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛno nti obiara a ɔbɛkum Kain no, wɔbɛtɔ ne so werɛ ahodoɔ nson. Na AWURADE yɛɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ bi maa Kain, na obiara a ɔbɛhu no no anku no.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Na Kain firii AWURADE anim kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Nod asase so wɔ Eden apueeɛ. Kain asefoɔ

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Na Kain ne ne yere dae, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Henok. Na ɔkyekyeree kuro bi, na ɔde ne ba Henok din too kuro no.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Na Henok woo Irad, na Irad woo Mehuyael. Na Mehuyael woo Metusael, na Metusael woo Lamek.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Na Sila nso woo Tubalkain a ɔyɛ kɔbere mfrafraeɛ ne dadeɛ adeɛ nyinaa atomfoɔ agya. Na Tubalkain nuabaa ne Naama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Na Lamek ka kyerɛɛ ne yerenom sɛ: Ada ne Sila, montie me nne; Lamek yerenom, monyɛ aso mma m’asɛm: Mekumm ɔbarima sɛ ɔpiraa me, mekumm aberanteɛ sɛ ɔboroo me.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔtɔɔ Kain so werɛ mprɛnson a, Lamek deɛ bɛyɛ aduɔson nson. Set ne Enos awoɔ

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere daeɛ bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo ne din Set sɛ: Onyankopɔn de ɔba foforɔ asi me Habel a Kain kumm no no ananmu.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Set nso, wɔwoo ɔba maa no, na ɔtoo ne din Enos. Ɛberɛ no mu na wɔfirii aseɛ bɔɔ AWURADE din sɔree no.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Na Henok ne Onyankopɔn nantee, na wɔanhunu no bio, ɛfiri sɛ Onyankopɔn faa no kɔe.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo ne din Noa, na ɔkaa sɛ: Oyi na ɔbɛkyekyere yɛn werɛ wɔ yɛn nnwuma ne yɛn nsa ano brɛ mu wɔ asase a AWURADE adome no soɔ.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Nyankopɔn mma hunuu nnipa mmammaa sɛ wɔn ho yɛ fɛ, na wɔwarewaree wɔn mu biara a wɔpɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Me honhom rentena onipa mu nkɔsi daa, ɛfiri sɛ wɔyɛ honam, enti ne nna bɛyɛ mfeɛ ɔha aduonu.

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Nna no mu ne akyire no, na abrane akɛseɛ wɔ asase so. Na Nyankopɔn mma kɔɔ nnipa mmammaa ho na wɔwoo mma maa wɔn no, yeinom ne aberempɔn a wɔwɔ din firi tete.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hunuu sɛ nnipa bɔne dɔɔso pii wɔ asase so, na wɔn akoma mu nsusuiɛ nyinaa yɛ bɔne nko daa nyinaa.

english_verse: He was sorry that he had made them,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nuu ne ho sɛ ɔyɛɛ onipa wɔ asase soɔ, na ɛyɛɛ no ya n’akomam.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Mɛpepa nnipa a mabɔ wɔn no afiri asase ani, ampa ara, ɛfiri onipa so kɔsi ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne ewiem nnomaa so, ɛfiri sɛ manu me ho sɛ meyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Na Noa deɛ, ɔnyaa adom AWURADE anim. Noa adaka no

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Yei ne Noa ho asɛm: Na Noa yɛ onipa tenenee a ɔyɛ pɛ wɔ ne berɛ so nnipa mu. Noa ne Onyankopɔn nanteeɛ.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Na Noa woo mmammarima baasa, Sem, Ham, ne Yafet.

english_verse: God knew that everyone was terribly cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu asase, na hwɛ, asɛe, ɛfiri sɛ na nnipa nyinaa asɛe wɔn akwan wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Fa ɔwawa yɛ adaka, na yɛ mpia wɔ adaka no mu, na fa ama ka emu ne ɛho.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Noa yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no nyinaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, me, mede nsuyire bɛba asase so mabɛsɛe abɔdeɛ a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa ɔsoro ase; asase so adeɛ nyinaa rebɛwuwu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Na me ne wo bɛyɛ apam ato hɔ, na woakɔ adaka no mu, wo ne wo mma, ne wo yere, ne wo mma yerenom.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nnomaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, ne ntɔteboa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ nyinaa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, wɔn nyinaa mu mmienu mmienu mmra wo nkyɛn, na wɔanya nkwa.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Na wo deɛ, boaboa aduane nyinaa bi ano kɔ mu, na ayɛ wo ne wɔn aduane.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ: Wo ne wo fiefoɔ nyinaa, monkɔ adaka no mu, ɛfiri sɛ wo na mahu wo sɛ ɔteneneeni m’anim, ɛberɛ yi mu.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Mmoa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu, fa nson nson, anini ne abedeɛ. Na mmoa a wɔn ho nteɛ mu, fa mmienu mmienu, onini ne ɔbedeɛ;

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: ewiem nnomaa mu nso fa nson nson, anini ne abedeɛ, na wɔn ase nnya nkwa asase nyinaa ani.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: mmienu mmienu baa Noa nkyɛn adaka no mu, onini ne ɔbedeɛ, sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ Noa no.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Na nnanson akyiri no, nsuyire baa asase so.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Na osuo tɔɔ asase so pii adaduanan, awia ne anadwo.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Saa da yi ara mu na Noa ne ne yere, ne ne mma, Sem, Ham ne Yafet, ne ne mma yerenom baasa akɔhyɛ adaka no mu.

english_verse: They took along every kind of animal, tame and wild, including the birds.
translation_verse: Na mmoadoma nyinaa, ntɔteboa, mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ, ntuboa nyinaa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ,

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: ne wɔn na ɛkɔɔ mu. Honam a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa mu mmienu mmienu na wɔbaa Noa nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Wɔn a ɛbaeɛ no, na wɔyɛ honam nyinaa mu anini ne abedeɛ, sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no; na AWURADE too no mu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nsuo no boroo so kɔɔ soro basafa nson ne fa kataa mmepɔ so.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na abɔdeɛ a ɛte aseɛ nyinaa, nnomaa, ntɔteboa, wiram mmoa, mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ, ne nnipa nyinaa;

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na nsuo no yirii wɔ asase so nna ɔha aduonum.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaee Noa ne mmoadoma nyinaa ne ntɔteboa nyinaa a wɔne no wɔ adaka no mu nyinaa. Na Onyankopɔn maa mframa bɔ faa asase so, na nsuo no ano brɛɛ ase.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na ebunu no nsuo aniwa sisii, na ɔsoro mpomma mu totoe, maa osuo a ɛfiri soro no gyaee tɔ;

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na ɛda a ɛtɔ so dunson wɔ bosome nson no mu na adaka no kɔsii Ararat mmepɔ soɔ.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Na nsuo no kɔɔ so twee ara kɔsii bosome a ɛtɔ so du no so; na saa bosome yi ara na da a ɛdi kan no na mmepɔ atifi dedaa adie.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔsomaa anene. Na ɔfirii adi, na ɔdii akɔneaba de kɔsii sɛ nsuo no wee asase soɔ.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa aburuburo sɛ ɔnkɔhwɛ sɛ nsuo no awe wɔ asase ani anaa.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Nanso aburuburo no annya ne nan sibea, na ɔsane baa ne nkyɛn adaka no mu, ɛfiri sɛ na nsuo no da so wɔ asase nyinaa ani. Na ɔtenee ne nsa faa no baa ne nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnanson bio, na ɔsomaa aburuburo firii adaka no mu bio.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Na aburuburo no baa ne nkyɛn anwummerɛ, na hwɛ, ngo dua ahahan frɔmfrɔm tua n’ano. Noa hunuu sɛ nsuo no awe asase so.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnanson bio no, ɔsomaa aburuburo no; na wansane amma ne nkyɛn bio.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Bosome a ɛtɔ so mmienu no da a ɛtɔ so aduonu nson no na na asase so awo koraa.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ:

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: Firi adaka no mu, wo ne wo yere, wo mma ne wɔn yerenom a wɔka wo ho;

english_verse: Let out the birds, animals, and reptiles, so they can mate and live all over the earth.”
translation_verse: mmoadoma a wɔka wo ho nyinaa a ɛfiri honam nyinaa mu, nnomaa ne ntɔteboa ne deɛ ɛwea asase soɔ nyinaa ne wo mfiri adi, na wɔnwo, na wɔnnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: After Noah and his family had left the boat,
translation_verse: Na Noa ne ne yere, ne ne mma ne wɔn yerenom firii adi;

english_verse: the living creatures left in groups of their own kind. The Lord's Promise for the Earth
translation_verse: mmoadoma nyinaa, wɔn a wɔwea nyinaa ne nnomaa nyinaa, ne deɛ nkwa wɔ mu biara, sɛdeɛ wɔn mmoaban teɛ, firi adaka no mu firii adi. Noa afɔrebɔ

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na Noa sii afɔrebukyia maa AWURADE, na ɔfaa ntɔteboa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu bi ne nnomaa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu bi de wɔn bobɔɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ wɔ bukyia no so.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE tee afɔdeɛ no hwam no, ɔkaa no n’akoma mu sɛ: Onipa nti merennome asase bio, ɛfiri sɛ onipa akoma mu adwene yɛ bɔne firi ne mmɔfraase, na merensɛe deɛ ɛte aseɛ nyinaa bio, sɛdeɛ mayɛ yi.

english_verse: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat; winter and summer, day and night.
translation_verse: Nna a asase wɔ hɔ yi nyinaa, oguo ne otwa, awɔ ne ahuhuro, asuso ne ɔpɛ, awia ne anadwo rennyae da.

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa Noa ne ne mma, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo na monnɔɔso, na monhyɛ asase so ma.

english_verse: All animals, birds, reptiles, and fish will be afraid of you. I have placed them under your control,
translation_verse: Na mo ho hu ne mo ho suro mmra asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne ewiem nnomaa nyinaa, deɛ ɛwea fam nyinaa ne ɛpo mu mpataa nyinaa so; mo nsa na wɔde wɔn ahyɛ.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Deɛ ɛkeka ne ho a ɛwɔ nkwa nyinaa, ɛnyɛ mo aduane; mede ne nyinaa mama mo, sɛdeɛ mede nhahan mono memaa mo no.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Nam a ne mogya da so wɔ ne mu nko na monnnie.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na mo deɛ, monwo na monnɔ, na monnɔɔso wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa ne ne mma a wɔka ne ho no sɛ:

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, afei merema m’apam atim hɔ ama mo ne mo asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi mo akyi,

english_verse: This includes the birds and the animals that came out of the boat.
translation_verse: ɛne akra a ɛtete aseɛ a ɛka mo ho nyinaa, nnomaa, ntɔteboa ne asase so mmoadoma a wɔne mo wɔ hɔ firi adaka no mu nyinaa.

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: Na mama me ne mo apam yi agyina hɔ, sɛ meremfa nsuyire mensɛe abɔdeɛ nyinaa bio, na nsuyire remma mmɛsɛe asase bio.

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Me nyankontɔn na mede masi mununkum mu, na ayɛ me ne asase ntam apam no ho nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Na sɛ mede mununkum meba asase so a, wɔbɛhunu nyankontɔn no wɔ mununkum no mu;

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: na makae m’apam a ɛwɔ me ne mo, ne abɔdeɛ nyinaa mu ateasefoɔ ntam no, na nsuo annane nsuyire ansɛe abɔdeɛ nyinaa bio.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Na nyankontɔn no bɛba mununkum mu, na mahwɛ, na mede makae daa apam a ɛwɔ Onyankopɔn ne nnipa ne abɔdeɛ mu ateasefoɔ a ɛwɔ asase soɔ nyinaa no ntam.

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Noa mma a wɔfirii adaka no mu firii adie ne Sem, Ham ne Yafet; na Ham ne Kanaan n’agya.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Noa mma baasa no. Wɔn mu na nnipa firi petee asase nyinaa soɔ.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Na Noa firii aseɛ yɛɛ kua, na ɔyɛɛ bobeturo.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔnom nsa no bi, na ɔboroe, na ɔda ne ntomadan mu a ne ho da hɔ.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Na Kanaan agya Ham kɔhunuu n’agya adagya mu, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom baanu no wɔ adihɔ.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
translation_verse: Na Sem ne Yafet faa ntoma de guu wɔn mmatiri so nam nkyirinkyire de kɔkataa wɔn agya adagya so, na wɔdanee wɔn ani kyerɛɛ akyire, na wɔanhunu wɔn agya adagya mu.

english_verse: When Noah sobered up and learned what his youngest son had done,
translation_verse: Na Noa ani so tete firii ne nsaborɔ mu na ɔtee deɛ ne ba kumaa no ayɛ no no,

english_verse: he said, “I now put a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest slave of his brothers.
translation_verse: ɔkaa sɛ: Wɔadome Kanaan, ɔbɛyɛ nkoa mu akoa ama ne nuanom.

english_verse: I ask the Lord my God to bless Shem and make Canaan his slave.
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa nso sɛ: Nhyira ne Sem Nyankopɔn, AWURADE, na Kanaan nyɛ wɔn akoa.

english_verse: I pray God will give Japheth more and more land and let him take over the territory of Shem. May Canaan be his slave.”
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn mma Yafet ase ntrɛ, na ɔntena Sem ntomadan mu, na Kanaan nyɛ wɔn akoa.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Noa nna a ɔdiiɛ nyinaa yɛ mfeɛ ahankron aduonum, na ɔwui.

english_verse: After the flood Shem, Ham, and Japheth had many descendants. The Descendants of Japheth
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Noa mma Sem, Ham ne Yafet awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ. Na nsuyire no akyi, wɔwoo mma.

english_verse: This completes the list of Noah's descendants. After the flood their descendants became nations and spread all over the world.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Noa mma mmusua, sɛdeɛ wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ teɛ wɔ wɔn amanaman mu. Na ɛfiri yeinom mu na nsuyire no akyi amanaman petee asase soɔ.

english_verse: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
translation_verse: Na wɔtuu kwan faa apueeɛ no, wɔhunuu asasetam bi wɔ Sinear asase so, na wɔtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔkaa sɛ: Wiɛ, momma yɛnkyekyere kuro, na yɛnto abantenten a n’atifi bɛduru soro, na yɛmfa nnye din, na yɛanhwete asase nyinaa ani.

english_verse: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE siane bɛhwɛɛ kuro ne abantenten a nnipa mma retoɔ no.

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, wɔyɛ ɔman baako, na wɔn nyinaa ka kasa korɔ; na deɛ wɔafiri aseɛ reyɛ nie; na afei, biribiara rentumi nsi wɔn deɛ wɔsusu sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no biara ho kwan.

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Wiɛ, momma yɛnsiane nkɔ hɔ na yɛnkɔyɛ wɔn kasa basabasa, na wɔn mu biara ante ne yɔnko kasa bio.

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Enti na wɔfrɛ hɔ Babel, ɛfiri sɛ ɛhɔ na AWURADE yɛɛ asase nyinaa kasa basabasa. Ɛfiri hɔ na AWURADE bɔɔ wɔn hwetee asase nyinaa ani. Sem awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ (

english_verse: Two years after the flood, when Shem was
translation_verse: Na Sem woo Arfaksad no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanum na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Arpachshad had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo Sela no akyi no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanan ne mmiɛnsa, na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Shelah had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Sela woo Eber no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanan ne mmiɛnsa na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Eber had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo Peleg no akyi no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanan aduasa na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Peleg had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Peleg woo Reu no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanu ne nkron na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Reu had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Reu woo Serug no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanu ne nson, na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Serug had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Serug woo Nahor no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ahanu na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Nahor had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Nahor woo Tera no akyiri no, ɔdii mfeɛ ɔha ne dunkron na ɔwoo mmammarima ne mmammaa.

english_verse: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
translation_verse: Na Tera faa ne ba Abram ne ne nana Lot, a ɔyɛ Haran ba, ne n’ase Sarai, ne ba Abram yere, na ɔne wɔn firii Ur a ɛwɔ Kaldea sɛ wɔrekɔ Kanaan asase so. Na wɔduruu Haran no, wɔtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Abram sɛ: Wo deɛ, firi w’asase so ne w’abusua mu ne w’agya fie kɔ asase a mɛkyerɛ woɔ no so.

english_verse: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
translation_verse: Na mɛyɛ wo ɔman kɛseɛ, na mahyira wo, na mama wo din ayɛ kɛseɛ, na woayɛ nhyira.

english_verse: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
translation_verse: Na mɛhyira wɔn a wɔhyira woɔ, na wɔn a wɔdome woɔ no, mɛdome wɔn; na wo mu na wɔbɛhyira asase so mmusua nyinaa.

english_verse: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
translation_verse: Na Abram twaa mu asase no so kɔduruu baabi a wɔfrɛ hɔ Sekem wɔ More pɔ no ho. Nso berɛ no mu na Kanaanfoɔ wɔ asase no so.

english_verse: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yii ne ho kyerɛɛ Abram kaa sɛ: W’asefoɔ na mede asase yi bɛma wɔn. Na ɔsii afɔrebukyia wɔ hɔ maa AWURADE a ɔyii ne ho kyerɛɛ no no.

english_verse: Abram traveled to the hill country east of Bethel and camped between Bethel and Ai, where he built another altar and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔtu firii hɔ kɔɔ Betel apueeɛ bepɔ bi so. Na ɔsii ne ntomadan a Betel da n’atɔeɛ, na Ai da apueeɛ; na ɔsii afɔrebukyia maa AWURADE wɔ hɔ, na ɔsɔree AWURADE.

english_verse: Later, Abram started out toward the Southern Desert. Abram in Egypt
translation_verse: Na Abram dii atutena ara kɔɔ Negeb. Abram kɔ Misraim

english_verse: The crops failed, and there was no food anywhere in Canaan. So Abram and his wife Sarai went to live in Egypt for a while. But just before they got there, Abram said, “Sarai, you are really beautiful!
translation_verse: Na ɔreyɛ aduru Misraim asase soɔ no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne yere Sarai sɛ: Hwɛ, menim sɛ woyɛ ɔbaa a wo ho yɛ fɛ,

english_verse: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
translation_verse: na sɛ Misraimfoɔ hu wo a, wɔbɛka sɛ: Ne yere nie, na wɔaku me, na wɔama woatena ase.

english_verse: Please save my life by saying you are my sister.”
translation_verse: Enti ka sɛ, me nua ne wo, na wo nti wɔayɛ me yie, na matena ase.

english_verse: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Na Abram duruu Misraim no, Misraimfoɔ hunuu ne yere no sɛ ne ho yɛ fɛ sɛ.

english_verse: The king's officials told him about her, and she was taken to his house.
translation_verse: Na Farao atitire hunuu no, na wɔkɔkamfoo no kyerɛɛ Farao, na wɔbɛfaa ɔbaa no kɔɔ Farao fie.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Na ne nti ɔyɛɛ Abram yie; na ɔnyaa nnwan, anantwie, mfunumu, nkoa, mfenaa, mfunumubereɛ ne yoma.

english_verse: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
translation_verse: Na Abram yere Sarai ho asɛm no nti AWURADE de ɔhaw akɛseɛ haa Farao ne ne fie.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Abram kaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ me yi? Adɛn nti na woanka ankyerɛ me sɛ ɔyɛ wo yerɛ?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na wose: Ɔyɛ me nua? Anka meremfa no nware no; na afei, hwɛ wo yere nie, fa no na kɔ wo kwan.

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Na Farao tuu nnipa maa no sɛ wɔnkɔgya no ne ne yere ne deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa kwan.

english_verse: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
translation_verse: Na Abram ne ne yere ne deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa, ne Lot nso, firii Misraim baa Negeb.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Na Abram anya ne ho sɛ, mmoa, dwetɛ ne sika mu.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: Na ɔdii atutena firi Negeb kɔduruu Betel, deɛ akane na ne ntomadan sie no, wɔ Betel ne Ai ntam,

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: deɛ afɔrebukyia a ɔsii kane no wɔ. Na Abram sɔree AWURADE wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Na Lot nso a ɔne Abram nam no wɔ nnwan ne anantwie ne ntomadan.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Na Abram ka kyerɛɛ Lot sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, mma akasakasa mmma me ne wo ntam, ne me mmoahwɛfoɔ ne wo mmoahwɛfoɔ ntam, na yɛyɛ anuanom.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Ɛnyɛ asase no nyinaa na ɛda w’anim yi? Mesrɛ wo, twe wo ho firi me ho, sɛ wofa benkum a, mɛfa nifa, na sɛ wofa nifa a, mɛfa benkum.

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Lot maa n’ani so hwɛɛ Yordan kanko nyinaa de kɔsi Soar hunuu sɛ ne nyinaa so wɔ nsuo te sɛ AWURADE turo no, te sɛ Misraim, ansa na AWURADE resɛe Sodom ne Gomora no.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Na Lot yii Yordan kanko no nyinaa, na ɔtu faa apueeɛ fam; na anuanom no dii mpaapaemu.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Abram tenaa Kanaan asase so, na Lot deɛ, ɔtenaa Yordan kanko no nkuro mu, na ɔtutuu ne ntomadan ara de kɔduruu Sodom.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Nso na Sodomfoɔ yɛ atirimuɔdenfoɔ ne nnebɔneyɛfoɔ kɛse, AWURADE anim. Abram kɔtena Hebron

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Na Lot tee ne ho firii Abram ho no, AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Abram sɛ: Ma w’ani so, na firi deɛ wowɔ hɔ hwɛ atifi fam ne anafoɔ fam, apueeɛ ne atɔeɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: Na asase a wohunu yi nyinaa, wo ne w’asefoɔ na mede bɛma mo daa.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Na mɛma w’asefoɔ adɔɔso sɛ asase so mfuturo. Na sɛ obi tumi kan asase so mfuturo a, ɛnneɛ na ɔbɛtumi akan w’asefoɔ nso.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Sɔre, fa asase no tentene ne ne tɛtrɛtɛ mu, na wo na mede bɛma woɔ.

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Abram tutuu ne ntomadan, na ɔbɛtenaa Mamre pɔ a ɛwɔ Hebron no ho, na ɔsii afɔrebukyia maa AWURADE wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Na Sinear hene Amrafel, Elasar hene Ariok, Elam hene Kedorlaomer ne Goiim hene Tideal berɛ so no,

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: wɔne Sodom hene Bera ne Gomora hene Birsa, Adma hene Sinab ne Seboim hene Semeber ne Bela hene dii ako.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Na afe a ɛtɔ so dunan mu no, Kedorlaomer ne ahemfo a wɔkeka ne ho no bɛkum Refaim wɔ Asterot-karnaim, ne Susifoɔ wɔ Ham, ne Emifoɔ Kiriataim mpaperɛ so,

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: ne Horifoɔ wɔ wɔn bepɔ Seir so de kɔsii El-paran a ɛwɔ ɛserɛ soɔ no.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Na wɔsane baa Enmispat, , na wɔkaa Amalekfoɔ asase nyinaa ne Amorifoɔ nso a wɔte Haseson-tamar no gui.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: Na wɔne Elam hene Kedorlaomer, Goiim hene Tideal, Sinear hene Amrafel ne Elasar hene Ariok de bɛbɔɔ ani wɔ Sidim bonhwa mu, ahemfo baanan a wɔreko atia baanum.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Na Sidim bonhwa mu yɛ ama amena ara nko. Na Sodom ne Gomora ahemfo dwanee. Na ebinom totɔɔ amena no mu, na wɔn a aka no dwane kɔɔ bepɔ so.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa Sodom ne Gomora nnoɔma ne wɔn nnuane nyinaa de sii mu kɔe.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa Abram nua ba Lot a ɔte Sodom ne n’ahodeɛ kɔe.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Na odwanefoɔ bi bɛka kyerɛɛ Hebrini Abram a ɔte Amorini Mamre, Eskol ne Aner nua no pɔ mu; na wɔne Abram wɔ apam. Abram gye Lot

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Na Abram tee sɛ wɔafa ne nua ba dommum no, ɔde ne mmarima a wɔawo wɔn wɔ ne fie ahasa ne dunwɔtwe tuu ɔsa tii wɔn kɔduruu Dan.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Na ɔne ne nkoa kyɛɛ wɔn ho mu baa wɔn so anadwo, na wɔbobɔɔ wɔn, na wɔtaa wɔn kɔduruu Hoba a ɛda Damasko benkum no.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Na ɔde nnoɔma no nyinaa ne ne nua ba Lot ne ne nnoɔma ne mmaa no nso ne nkurɔfoɔ no sane bae. Melkisedek hyira Abram

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔsane firii Kedorlaomer ne ahemfo a ɛkeka ne ho so nkonimdie reba no, Sodom hene firi kɔhyiaa no wɔ Sawe bonhwa mu.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Na Salem hene Melkisedek de paanoo ne bobesa brɛɛ no; na ɔyɛ ɔsorosoro Nyankopɔn sɔfoɔ.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyiraa no sɛ: Ɔsorosoro Nyankopɔn a ɔyɛ ɔsoro ne asase wura no nhyira nka Abram.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Na nhyira ne ɔsorosoro Nyankopɔn a ɔde w’atamfo ahyɛ wo nsa. Na Abram maa no nnoɔma no nyinaa mu ntotosoɔ du du.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Na Sodom hene ka kyerɛɛ Abram sɛ: Fa nnipa no ma me, na fa ahodeɛ no.

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Na Abram ka kyerɛɛ Sodom hene no sɛ: Mema me nsa so mekyerɛ AWURADE, ɔsorosoro Nyankopɔn a ɔyɛ ɔsoro ne asase wura no,

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: sɛ ɛfiri asaawa so de kɔsi mpaboa homa soɔ, meremfa biribiara a ɛyɛ wo deɛ, na woanka sɛ: Me na mama Abram anya ne ho;

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: gye deɛ mmeranteɛ no adie no nko, ne mmarima a wɔne me kɔeɛ no, Aner, Eskol ne Mamre nya wɔn kyɛfa.

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Nsɛm yi akyiri no, AWURADE asɛm baa Abram nkyɛn anisoadehunu mu sɛ: Nsuro, Abram, mene wo kyɛm, na w’akatua bɛdɔɔso pii.

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Na Abram bisaa sɛ: AWURADE Nyankopɔn, ɛdeɛn na wode bɛma me? Menni ba na menam, na deɛ ɔbɛdi m’adeɛ ne Damaskoni Eliesa anaa?

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Na Abram kaa sɛ: Ao, me deɛ, woamma me asefoɔ, na hwɛ, me fienipa na ɔbɛdi m’adeɛ.

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE asɛm baa ne nkyɛn sɛ: Ɛnyɛ oyi na ɔbɛdi w’adeɛ, na deɛ ɔbɛfiri wo ara w’asene mu na ɔbɛdi w’adeɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Na ɔde no firii adi kaa sɛ: Hwɛ ɔsoro ɛ, na kan nsoromma sɛ wobɛtumi akan anaa? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ w’asefoɔ bɛyɛ ne no.

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Na Abram gyee AWURADE diiɛ, na ɔbuu yei sɛ tenenee maa no.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mene AWURADE a ɔde wo firii Ur a ɛwɔ Kaldea no, sɛ mede asase yi bɛma wo sɛ agyapadeɛ.

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa sɛ: AWURADE Nyankopɔn, ɛdeɛn na mede bɛhunu sɛ mɛnya?

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa nantwie ba a wadi mfeɛ mmiɛnsa, abirekyie a wadi mfeɛ mmiɛnsa, odwennini a wadi mfeɛ mmiɛnsa, anyankuku ne aborɔnoma ba brɛ me.

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Na ɔde yei nyinaa brɛɛ no, na ɔpaepaee wɔn mu mmienu mmienu, na ɔde afaafa no kyerɛkyerɛɛ anim totoo hɔ; na nnomaa no deɛ, wampaapae wɔn mu.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Na nnomaa a wɔdi nam bɛsisii mmoa afunu no so, na Abram pamm wɔn.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Na owia reyɛ akɔtɔ no, Abram daa nnahɔɔ, na hwɛ, ehu sum kabii duruu no.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Na awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ nnan mu na wɔbɛsane aba ha, ɛfiri sɛ Amorifoɔ amumuyɛ nnya nnurui.

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Na owia tɔeɛ na esum kusuu duruiɛ no, hwɛ, biribi a ɛte sɛ gyaframa a ɛrefiri wisie ne tɛnee a ɛredɛre bɛfaa afaafa no ntam.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Da no ara na AWURADE ne Abram yɛɛ apam sɛ: W’asefoɔ na mede asase yi mama wɔn ɛfiri Misraim asubɔnten ho de kɔsi asubɔnten kɛseɛ, Eufrate asubɔnten ho:

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: Hetifoɔ, Perisifoɔ, Refaimfoɔ,

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: Amorifoɔ, Kanaanfoɔ, Girgasifoɔ ne Yebusifoɔ.

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Na Abram yere Sarai nwo mma no. Na ɔwɔ afenaa bi a ɔyɛ Misraimni a ne din de Hagar.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: Na Sarai ka kyerɛɛ Abram sɛ: Hwɛ, AWURADE asi m’awoɔ ho kwan, enti kɔ m’afenaa nkyɛn, ebia mɛnya ne ho mma. Na Abram tiee Sarai.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Na Abram tenaa Kanaan asase so mfirinhyia du no, ne yere Sarai faa n’afenaa Hagar a ɔyɛ Misraimni no de no maa ne kunu awareɛ.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔɔ Hagar ho, na ɔnyinsɛnee. Na ɔhunuu sɛ wanyinsɛn no, ɔbuu n’awuraa animtia.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Na Sarai ka kyerɛɛ Abram sɛ: Asɛmmɔne a wadi me da wo so. Me na mede m’afenaa mato wo kokom, na ɔhunuu sɛ wanyinsɛn nti, ɔbu me animtia. AWURADE mmu me ne wo ntam atɛn.

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Abram ka kyerɛɛ Sarai sɛ: Hwɛ, w’afenaa wɔ wo nsam, yɛ no sɛdeɛ ɛyɛ w’ani soɔ. Na Sarai tanee n’ani maa no dwane firii ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ hunuu no nsuo aniwa bi ho wɔ ɛserɛ so wɔ Sur kwan so nsuo aniwa no ho.

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa sɛ: Hagar, Sarai afenaa, wofiri he na woreba, na worekɔ he ni? Na ɔse: Mefiri m’awuraa Sarai anim na meredwane.

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sane kɔ w’awuraa nkyɛn, na kɔbrɛ wo ho ase ma no.

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, woanyinsɛn, na wobɛwo ɔba, na wobɛto ne din Ismael, sɛ AWURADE ate w’amanehunu.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛyɛ onipa a ɔte sɛ ɛserɛ so afunumu. Ne nsa bɛtia nnipa nyinaa, na nnipa nyinaa nsa atia no, na ɔbɛsɔre atia ne nuanom nyinaa.

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ AWURADE a ɔne no kasaeɛ no din sɛ: Wone El-roi, na ɔse: Mahunu deɛ ɔhu me no ampa anaa?

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Enti wɔfrɛ asubura no sɛ: Beer-lahai-roi, na hwɛ, ɛwɔ Kades ne Bared ntam.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Na mɛma m’apam ada me ne wo ntam, na mama woadɔ kɛse no ara.

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Na Abram daa hɔ de n’anim butuu fam; na Onyankopɔn ne no kasaa sɛ:

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Na wɔremfrɛ wo din Abram bio, na mmom wɔbɛfrɛ wo Abraham, ɛfiri sɛ mayɛ wo aman pii agya.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Na mɛma woadɔ pii pa ara, na mɛyɛ wo aman, na ahemfo afiri wo mu.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Na mɛma me ne wo ne w’asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi w’akyire no apam agyina wɔ wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ mu, na ayɛ daa apam, na mayɛ wo ne w’asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi w’akyire no Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Na mede asase a woyɛ so hɔhoɔ yi, Kanaan asase nyinaa, bɛma wo ne w’asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi w’akyire, sɛ daa agyapadeɛ, na mayɛ wɔn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: Abraham, you and all future members of your family must promise to obey me.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Abraham sɛ: Wo deɛ, di m’apam so, wo ne w’asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi w’akyi wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ mu.

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Na montwitwa mo ho twetia, na ayɛ me ne mo ntam apam no ho nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima momonoto biara a wɔntwaa no twetia no, saa onipa no wɔbɛtwa no afiri ne man mu, ɛfiri sɛ wato m’apam.

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Abraham sɛ: Wo yere Sarai deɛ, mfrɛ no Sarai bio, na mmom Sara.

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Na mɛhyira no, na mama wo ne mu ɔba nso, ampa ara, mɛhyira no. Ɔbɛyɛ aman, na aman ahemfo bɛfiri ne mu.

english_verse: Then he asked God, “Why not let Ishmael inherit what you have promised me?”
translation_verse: Na Abraham ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ: O, ɛnneɛ anka ma Ismael nya w’anim adom ɛ!

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ampaneampa, wo yere Sara bɛwo ɔba ama wo, na woato ne din Isak. Na mɛma me ne no apam no agyina ayɛ daa apam ama n’asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi n’akyire no.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: Na Ismael ho deɛ, matie wo. Hwɛ, mɛhyira no, na mama no awo, na wadɔɔso pii pa ara. Atitire dummienu na ɔbɛwoɔ, na mayɛ no ɔman kɛseɛ.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Na m’apam deɛ, me ne Isak a Sara bɛwo no ama wo afeda sɛsɛɛ no na ɛbɛpam ama no agyina.

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Na ɔne no wiee kasa no, Onyankopɔn firii Abraham nkyɛn kɔɔ ɔsoro.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: Na ne fie mmarima nyinaa, wɔn a wɔwoo wɔn ne fie ne wɔn a wɔde sika totɔɔ wɔn wɔ ahɔhoɔ nkyɛn, wɔtwitwaa wɔn twetia kaa ne ho.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yii ne ho kyerɛɛ Abraham wɔ Mamre pɔ mu, na ɔte ne ntomadan pono ano awia ketee.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n’ani so hwɛe, na hwɛ, mmarima baasa abɛgyina ne ntentensoɔ. Na ɔhunuu wɔn no, ɔfirii ne ntomadan pono ano tuu mmirika kɔhyiaa wɔn, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: kaa sɛ: Me wura, sɛ manya w’anim adom a, mesrɛ wo, nsiane w’akoa ho nkɔ.

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Ma wɔnkɔsa nsuo kakraa bi mmra, na monhohoro mo nan ase, na monhome dua yi ase.

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: Moanya abɛfa mo akoa nkyɛn yi, merekɔ makɔfa paanoo kakra maba, na mode adwodwo mo akoma, na ɛno akyiri no moakɔ. Na wɔse: Yɛ sɛdeɛ woaka yi.

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Na Abraham yɛɛ ntɛm kɔɔ Sara nkyɛn ntomadan mu kaa sɛ: Yɛ ntɛm, fa esiam pa susukoraa mmiɛnsa, fete to taterɛ.

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: Na Abraham tuu mmirika kɔɔ anantwie mu kɔkyeree nantwie ba a ɔyɛ na ɔde maa ɔsomfoɔ bi, na ɔyɛɛ ntɛm siesiee no.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: Na Abraham faa nufosuo ani sradeɛ ne nufosuo ne nantwie ba nam a ɔsiesiee no no, na ɔde bɛsii wɔn anim; na ɔno deɛ, ɔgyinaa wɔn nkyɛn dua no ase, maa wɔdidii.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: Na wɔbisaa Abraham sɛ: Wo yere Sara wɔ he? Na ɔse: Hwɛ, ɔwɔ ntomadan mu.

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Na Abraham ne Sara nyinaa anyininyini a wɔadi mfirinhyia pii, na deɛ ɛyɛ mmaa no to atwa wɔ Sara ho.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Enti Sara seree ne mu kaa sɛ: Sɛ manya awie aberewa bɔ na me wura nso abɔ akɔkoraa yi, na mɛnya anigyeɛ?

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Abraham sɛ: Adɛn nti na Sara seree sɛ: Ampaneampa ara manyini yi mɛwo ɔba?

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Biribi yɛ AWURADE yɛna anaa? Berɛ a mahyɛ no, mɛsane aba wo nkyɛn afeda sɛsɛɛ no na Sara anya ɔba.

english_verse: Sarah was so frightened that she lied and said, “I didn't laugh.” “Yes, you did!” he answered. Abraham Prays for Sodom
translation_verse: Na Sara sanee sɛ: Menseree, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔsuro. Na ɔse: Dabi, woasere. Abraham di ma Sodomfoɔ

english_verse: When the three men got ready to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked part of the way with them.
translation_verse: Na mmarima no sɔre firii hɔ danee wɔn ani kyerɛɛ Sodom, na Abraham kɔgyaa wɔn kwan.

english_verse: The Lord said to himself, “I should tell Abraham what I am going to do,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Memfa deɛ merebɛyɛ yi mensie Abraham anaa?

english_verse: since his family will become a great and powerful nation that will be a blessing to all the other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Ɛfiri sɛ ampa ara Abraham bɛyɛ ɔman a ɛso na wɔwɔ tumi, na ne mu na wɔbɛhyira wiase aman nyinaa.

english_verse: I have chosen him to teach his family to obey me forever and to do what is right and fair. If they do, I will give Abraham many descendants, just as I promised.”
translation_verse: Na mahu no mayi no sɛ ɔnhyɛ ne mma ne ne fiefoɔ a ɛbɛdi n’akyire sɛ wɔnni AWURADE kwan so nyɛ tenenee ne atɛntenenee adeɛ, na AWURADE ama deɛ waka no Abraham ho no aba ne so.

english_verse: ?” “Because of them, I won't destroy the city,” was the Lord's answer.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Sodom ne Gomora so nteamu so, na wɔn nnebɔne yɛ duru dodo nti,

english_verse: Now I am going down to see for myself if those people really are that bad. If they aren't, I would like to know.”
translation_verse: meresiane makɔhwɛ sɛ wɔayɛ sɛdeɛ nteamu a ɛduru me nkyɛn no teɛ no a; na sɛ ɛnte saa, mahunu.

english_verse: The men turned and started toward Sodom. But the Lord stayed with Abraham.
translation_verse: Na mmarima no danee wɔn ani firii hɔ kɔɔ Sodom; na Abraham deɛ, na ɔda so gyina AWURADE anim ara.

english_verse: And Abraham asked him, “Lord, when you destroy the evil people, are you also going to destroy those who are good?
translation_verse: Na Abraham twe bɛn bisaa sɛ: Wobɛpra ɔteneneeni ne ɔbɔnefoɔ abom agu anaa?

english_verse: You surely wouldn't let them be killed when you destroy the evil ones. You are the judge of all the earth, and you do what is right.”
translation_verse: Yei mpare wo sɛ wobɛdi saa asɛm yi sɛ wobɛkum ɔteneneeni ne ɔdebɔneyɛni afra, na ɔteneneeni ayɛ sɛ ɔdebɔneyɛni; yei mpare wo. Deɛ ɔbu asase nyinaa atɛn no remmu atɛntenenee anaa?

english_verse: Abraham answered, “I am nothing more than the dust of the earth. Please forgive me, Lord, for daring to speak to you like this.
translation_verse: Na Abraham buaa sɛ: Hwɛ, meyɛ mfuturo ne nso deɛ, nanso masi me bo sɛ me ne AWURADE bɛkasa:

english_verse: Then Abraham said, “I don't have any right to ask you, Lord, but what would you do if you find only
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Hwɛ, masi me bo sɛ me ne AWURADE bɛkasa. Ebia wɔbɛhunu aduonu wɔ hɔ. Na ɔse: Aduonu no nti merensɛe hɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Abraham said, “Please don't get angry, Lord, if I speak just once more. Suppose you find only
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Mma AWURADE bo mmfu, na menkasa baako pɛ yi: Ebia wɔbɛhunu edu wɔ hɔ. Na ɔse: Edu no nti merensɛe hɔ.

english_verse: After speaking with Abraham, the Lord left, and Abraham went back home.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ne Abraham kasa wieeɛ no, ɔkɔe, na Abraham sane baa ne fie.

english_verse: That evening, while Lot was sitting near the city gate, the two angels arrived in Sodom. When Lot saw them, he got up, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Na abɔfoɔ baanu no duruu Sodom anwummerɛ; na Lot te Sodom kuro pono ano. Na Lot hunuu wɔn no, ɔsɔre kɔhyiaa wɔn, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase kaa sɛ:

english_verse: and said, “Gentlemen, I am your servant. Please come to my home. You can wash your feet, spend the night, and be on your way in the morning.” They told him, “No, we'll spend the night in the city square.”
translation_verse: Me wuranom, mesrɛ mo, mommane mmra mo akoa fie mmɛsoɛ anadwo yi, na monhohoro mo nan ase, na anɔpatutu moasɔre akɔ mo kwan. Na wɔse: Dabi, yɛbɛda abɔntene so.

english_verse: But Lot kept insisting, until they finally agreed and went home with him. He quickly baked some bread, cooked a meal, and they ate.
translation_verse: Na ɔsrɛɛ wɔn dendeenden. Na wɔmanee ne nkyɛn baa ne fie, na ɔtoo wɔn pono, na ɔtoo apiti maa wɔdii.

english_verse: Before Lot and his guests could go to bed, every man in Sodom, young and old, came and stood outside his house
translation_verse: Na wɔnnya nkɔdaeɛ no, Sodom kurom hɔfoɔ bɛtwaa ɛdan no ho hyiae, ɛfiri mmɔfra so kɔsi mpanimfoɔ so, ɔman mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: and started shouting, “Where are your visitors? Send them out, so we can have sex with them!”
translation_verse: Na wɔfrɛɛ Lot ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mmarima a wɔbaa wo nkyɛn anadwo yi no wɔ he? Yi wɔn brɛ yɛn, na yɛne wɔn nna.
