translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Afei ansa na me kunu de ne ho bɛfam me ho, ɛfiri sɛ me ne no awo mmammarima baasa. Enti ɔtoo no din Lewi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Yei deɛ mɛyi AWURADE ayɛ. Enti ɔtoo no din Yuda. Na n’awoɔ mu twee.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Na Rahel hunuu sɛ ɔnwo mma Yakob no, ɔtwee ne nuabaa no ho kora, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Ma me mma, na anyɛ saa a, mɛwu.

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob bo fuu Rahel kaa sɛ: Mesi Nyankopɔn a ɔkame wo wo yam mma no ananmu anaa?

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, m’afenaa Bilha nie, wo ne no nna, na ɔnwo ngu me srɛ so, na me nso mennya ne ho mma.

english_verse: Then Rachel let Jacob marry Bilhah,
translation_verse: Na ɔde n’abaawa Bilha maa no awareɛ, na Yakob ne no dae.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Na Bilha nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima maa Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn adi m’asɛm, na watie me nne nso ama me ɔba. Enti ɔtoo no din Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Na Rahel abaawa Bilha nyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima a ɔtɔ so mmienu maa Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Ako akɛseɛ na me ne me nuabaa adie, nso matumi no. Na ɔtoo no din Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Na Lea hunuu sɛ n’awoɔ mu atwe no, ɔde n’abaawa Silpa maa Yakob awareɛ.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Na Lea abaawa Silpa woo ɔbabarima maa Yakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Aba yie. Na ɔtoo no din Gad.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: M’ahotɔ nie! Na mmaa bɛfrɛ me deɛ wɔahyira no. Na ɔtoo no din Aser.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Na ayuo twaberɛ mu no, Ruben firii adi kɔhunuu dudaim wɔ wiram, na ɔde brɛɛ ne na Lea. Na Rahel ka kyerɛɛ Lea sɛ: Ma me wo ba dudaim yi bi ɛ!

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛnnɔɔso sɛ woafa me kunu? Na worebɛgye me ba dudaim nso anaa? Na Rahel se: Wo ba dudaim no nti ma ɔne wo nkɔda anadwo yi.

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Na anwummerɛ a Yakob firi wiram reba no, Lea firii adi kɔhyiaa no kaa sɛ: Bra me nkyɛn, ɛfiri sɛ ampa ara mede me ba dudaim matɔ wo. Na ɔne no daa anadwo no.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tiee Lea, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima a ɔtɔ so nnum maa Yakob.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn atua me ka, sɛ mede m’abaawa mama me kunu awareɛ. Na ɔtoo no din Isakar.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn akyɛ me akyɛdeɛ pa, afei deɛ, me kunu ne me bɛtena yie, ɛfiri sɛ mawo mmammarima baasia mama no. Na ɔtoo no din Sebulon.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyiri no, ɔwoo ɔbabaa, na ɔtoo no din Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Onyankopɔn ayi m’ahohora.

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo no din Yosef sɛ: AWURADE mma me ɔba foforɔ nka ne ho. Laban ne Yakob nnaadaa

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Na Rahel woo Yosef no, Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ: Gya me kwan na menkɔ me kurom ne m’asase so.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Fa me yerenom ne me mma a wɔn nti mesomm woɔ no ma me. Wo ara wonim me som a masom woɔ.

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Na Yakob see no sɛ: Wo ara wonim sɛdeɛ masom wo afa ne sɛdeɛ wo mmoakuo ayɛ wɔ m’aseɛ.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Mebaa wo nkyɛn no, na deɛ wowɔ no sua, na afei aseɛ atrɛ ayɛ pii, na AWURADE ahyira wo baabiara a mefa. Na afei da bɛn na menhwɛ me fie nso?

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na memma woɔ? Na Yakob se: Mma me biribiara; sɛ wobɛyɛ saa adeɛ yi ama me deɛ a, mɛsane mabɛyɛne wo nnwan na mahwɛ wɔn.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Ɛnnɛ mɛkɔ makɔfa wo nnwan nyinaa mu, na mayiyi emu nnwan a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan nyinaa ne nnwammire nyinaa wɔ nnwanten no mu ne mmirekyie no mu nworonnworan ne ntokontrama. Wɔn a wɔtete sɛɛ na ɛnyɛ m’akatua.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Na daakye bi a wobɛka m’akatua ho asɛm no, me tenenee abua ama me wɔ w’anim. Mmirekyie no mu biara a ne ho nyɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan, ne nnwanten no mu deɛ ɔnyɛ odwammire no, ma wɔmmu no awifodeɛ wɔ me nsam.

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Na Laban se: Hwɛ, ma no nyɛ sɛdeɛ woaka yi ɛ!

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Na da no ara ɔyiyii mpapo a wɔn ho yɛ nsensannsensan ne nworonnworan, ne mmirekyibereɛ a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan nyinaa, obiara a fufuo wɔ ne ho, ne nnwanten no mu nnwammire nyinaa. Na ɔde wɔn hyɛɛ ne mmammarima nsa.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Na ɔde nnansa kwan too ɔne Yakob ntam, na Yakob yɛnee Laban nnwan a ɛkaeɛ no.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Na Yakob faa sɛsɛ dua, ɛdwono dua ne kyɛnkyɛn dua mman mono, na ɔyiyii ho nsema fitafitaa maa mmaa no ho fitaa no fifirii adi.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Na ɔde mmaa a ɔyiyii ho no guu anomeeɛ adaaseɛ a nnwan no rebɛnom mu nsuo no mu wɔ nnwan no anim, na wɔba nsunom a, wɔanyenyem so.

english_verse: in front of the branches, and their young were spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Na nnwan no nyenyem mmaa no so, na wɔwowoo nsensannsensan, ntokontrama ne nworonnworan.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Na Yakob yiyii nnwammaa no, na ɔde nnwan no ani kyerɛɛ Laban nnwan no mu nsensannsensan ne nnwammire nyinaa. Na ɔyɛɛ ɔno ara nnwankuo nko wɔ fa baabi, na wamfa wɔn amfra Laban nnwan no mu.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Na sɛ daa nnwan a wɔn ho yɛ den no nyenyem a, na Yakob de mmaa no akɔgu adaaseɛ no mu wɔ nnwan no anim, na wɔanyenyem mmaa no so.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Na nnwan no yɛ nofonofo deɛ a, ɔmfa ngu mu. Na wɔn a wɔyɛ mmerɛ no yɛɛ Laban dea, na wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ den no yɛɛ Yakob dea.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no yɛɛ kɛseɛ pa ara, na ɔnyaa nnwan pii ne mfenaa ne nkoa ne yoma ne mfunumu.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtee Laban mmammarima nsɛm a wɔkaeɛ no sɛ: Yakob afa deɛ ɛyɛ yɛn agya deɛ nyinaa; na ɛno na ɔde anya saa agyapadeɛ yi nyinaa.

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu Laban anim, na hwɛ, ɛnte no sɛdeɛ na ɛteɛ kane no.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Sane kɔ wo nananom asase so ne w’abusua mu, na mɛdi w’akyi.

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Na Yakob soma maa wɔkɔfrɛɛ Rahel ne Lea baa wiram wɔ ne nnwan no nkyɛn,

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mehunu mo agya anim sɛ ɛnte me sɛdeɛ na ɛteɛ kane no; nanso m’agya Nyankopɔn adi m’akyi.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Na mo ara monim sɛ m’ahoɔden nyinaa na mede masom mo agya,

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: na mo agya asisi me, adane m’akatua ani mprɛdu; nanso Onyankopɔn amma no kwan amma no anyɛ me bɔne biara.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔka sɛ: Wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama no nyɛ w’akatua a, na nnwan no nyinaa awowo ntokontrama. Na sɛ ɔka sɛ: Wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ nsensannsensan no nyɛ w’akatua a, na nnwan no nyinaa awowo nsensannsensan.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn agye mo agya mmoakuo ama me.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Na Nyankopɔn bɔfoɔ ka kyerɛɛ me daeɛ mu sɛ: Yakob! Na mese: Menie.

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ma w’ani so hwɛ, adwennini no a wɔreforo nnwan no nyinaa yɛ nsensannsensan ne ntokontrama ne nworonnworan: Ɛfiri sɛ mahunu deɛ Laban ayɛ woɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Mene Nyankopɔn a wohyiaa no Betel faako a wosraa ɛhɔ dum na wohyɛɛ bɔ maa me no; afei sɔre firi asase yi so, na sane kɔ w’abusua asase so.

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ɔmmu yɛn ahɔhoɔ anaa? Ɛsiane sɛ watɔn yɛn, na wadi yɛn tiri sika awie,

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: na ahonyadeɛ a Onyankopɔn gyee yɛn agya nsam no yɛ yɛn ne yɛn mma dea. Enti afei yɛ deɛ Onyankopɔn aka akyerɛ woɔ nyinaa. Yakob dwane firi Laban anim

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Na Yakob sɔre faa ne mma ne ne yerenom tenatenaa yoma so,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: na ɔfaa ne mmoakuo nyinaa ne n’ahodeɛ a ɔnyaeɛ nyinaa ne mmoakuo a ɔnyaeɛ wɔ Mesopotamia no nyinaa sii mu sɛ ɔrekɔ n’agya Isak nkyɛn wɔ Kanaan asase so.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔ rekɔtwitwa ne nnwan ho nwi. Na Rahel wiaa n’agya abusua honi.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Na Yakob wiaa ne ho dwanee, ɛfiri sɛ wankra Aramni Laban.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Na ɔne deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa dwanee, na ɔsɔre twaa asubɔnten no, na ɔde n’ani kyerɛɛ Gilead bepɔ. Laban ti Yakob

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no, wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ Yakob adwane.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Na Laban faa ne nkurɔfoɔ kaa ne ho tii no nnanson kwan, na ɔbɛtoo no Gilead bepɔ so.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Aramni Laban nkyɛn anadwo daeɛ mu sɛ: Hwɛ yie, na woankasa papa anaa bɔne so ankyerɛ Yakob.

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔtoo Yakob. Na Yakob asi ne ntomadan wɔ bepɔ no so, na Laban ne ne nkurɔfoɔ nso sii wɔn deɛ Gilead bepɔ so.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Na Laban bisaa Yakob sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ yi, sɛ woawia wo ho adwane me, na woasoa me mmammaa kɔ sɛ wɔn a wɔde nkrantɛ afa wɔn nnommum yi?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na woahunta adwane, na woawia wo ho afiri me nkyɛn? Adɛn na woanka ankyerɛ me, na mamfa anigyeɛ ne nnwom, mpintin ne nsankuo mannya wo kwan?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na woamma mamfe me mmammarima ne me mmammaa ano anya wɔn kwan? Yei deɛ, woadi no nkwasea so.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Mewɔ tumi sɛ anka me ne mo di no bɔne; nanso nnora anadwo no, mo agya ne Nyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ yie, na woankasa papa anaa bɔne so ankyerɛ Yakob.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Na afei deɛ korɔ ara na wopɛ sɛ wokorɔ, ɛfiri sɛ gyina na w’ani agyina w’agya fie; na adɛn nti na woawia m’anyame?

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bua see Laban sɛ: Na mesuro, ɛfiri sɛ mesusuu sɛ wobɛgye wo mmammaa afiri me nsam.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Na deɛ wobɛhunu w’anyame wɔ ne nsa mu no rentena ase. Yɛn nkurɔfoɔ yi anim na hwehwɛ deɛ ɛyɛ wo dea wɔ me nkyɛn, na fa kɔ. Na Yakob nnim sɛ Rahel na ɔwiaeɛ.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔɔ Yakob ntomadan mu ne Lea ntomadan ne mfenaa baanu no ntomadan mu, nanso wanhunu. Na ɔfiri Lea ntomadan mu kɔɔ Rahel ntomadan mu.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Na Rahel afa abusua honi no de ahyehyɛ yoma so adwa mu atena so. Na Laban de ne nsa kekaa ntomadan mu hɔ nyinaa, nanso wanhunu.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Mma no nnyɛ me wura abufuo sɛ mentumi mensɔre wɔ w’anim, ɛfiri sɛ mabu me nsa. Na ɔpɛe pɛe pɛe, nanso wanhunu ahoni no.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Na Yakob bo fui, na ɔne Laban hamee, na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ: Me mfomsoɔ ne sɛn, na me bɔne ne sɛn na wosa me yerɛdɛdɛdɛdɛ yi?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Na wobɛhwehwɛɛ me nnoɔma mu nyinaa yi, wo fie mu adeɛ bɛn na woahunu wɔ mu? Saa! Fa bɛto me nkurɔfoɔ ne wo nkurɔfoɔ anim wɔ ha, na wɔmmu yɛn baanu ntam atɛn.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Wɔn a mmoa kumm wɔn no mamfa mammrɛ wo, me na metuaa so ka. Deɛ wɔwiaa no awia ne deɛ wɔwiaa no anadwo, me nsa mu na wobisaeɛ.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛyɛɛ me nie: Ahuhuro dee me awia, na awɔ dee me anadwo, na m’ani soroe.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Sɛ m’agya Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, ne Isak suro annyina m’akyiri a, anka afei wogyaa me kwan nsapan. Me brɛ ne me nsa ano adwumayɛ na Onyankopɔn hunuiɛ, na ɔkaa w’anim nnora anadwo.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Na Laban bua see Yakob sɛ: Mma mmaa yi, me mma a, na mmammarima yi, me mma a, na nnwan yi, me nnwan a, na deɛ wohunu yi nyinaa, me dea. Na me mmammaa yi, anaasɛ wɔn mma a wɔawo wɔn yi, ɛdeɛn na mɛtumi de ayɛ wɔn nnɛ?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Afei bra ma yɛmpam, me ne wo, na ɛnyɛ me ne wo ntam adanseɛ.

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Na Yakob faa ɔboɔ de yɛɛ odum sii hɔ.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ ne nkurɔfoɔ sɛ: Mommoaboa aboɔ ano! Na wɔtasee aboɔ yɛɛ no kuo; na wɔdidii wɔ ekuo no so hɔ.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Na Laban frɛɛ hɔ Yegarsahaduta, na Yakob deɛ, ɔfrɛɛ hɔ Galeed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Na Laban kaa sɛ: Ekuo yi ne me ne wo ntam adanseɛ nnɛ. Enti wɔfrɛ hɔ Galeed,

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: ne Mispa, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Sɛ yɛtete mu a, AWURADE nhwɛ me ne wo ntam.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Sɛ woteetee me mmammaa, na woware yerenom ka me mma ho a, obi nka yɛn ho deɛ, nanso Onyankopɔn ne me ne wo ntam danseni.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Aboɔkuo yi ne adanseɛ, na odum yi nso yɛ adanseɛ, sɛ me deɛ, merensiane ekuo yi ho memma wo nkyɛn, na wo nso, worensiane ekuo yi ne odum yi ho mma me nkyɛn mmɛyɛ bɔne.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bɔɔ afɔdeɛ wɔ bepɔ no so, na ɔfrɛɛ ne nkurɔfoɔ sɛ wɔmmɛdidi; na wɔdidii na wɔtenaa bepɔ no so anadwo no.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Na Laban sɔree anɔpatutu, na ɔfee ne nananom ne ne mmammaa no ano hyiraa wɔn, na ɔsii mu sane kɔɔ ne kurom.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii ne kwan so sɛ ɔrekɔ; na Nyankopɔn abɔfoɔ bɛhyiaa no.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu wɔn no, ɔkaa sɛ: Nyankopɔn asafo nie. Na ɔtoo hɔ din: Maha-naim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Na Yakob tuu abɔfoɔ dii n’anim kɔɔ ne nua Esau nkyɛn Seir asase so wɔ Edom wiram.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛdeɛ monka nkyerɛ me wura Esau ne sɛ: W’akoa Yakob se: Mekɔtenaa Laban nkyɛn na ɛhɔ na mewɔ de abɛduru sɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Manya anantwie, mfunumu, nnwan, mmirekyie ne nkoa ne mfenaa; na masoma sɛ wɔmmɛka nkyerɛ me wura, sɛdeɛ mɛnya w’anim adom.

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Na abɔfoɔ no sane baa Yakob nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Yɛakɔ wo nua Esau nkyɛn, na ɔno nso ne mmarima ahanan reba abɛhyia wo.

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob suroo sɛ, na ne ho yeraa no. Na ɔkyɛɛ nkurɔfoɔ a wɔwɔ ne nkyɛn ne nnwan, mmirekyie, anantwie ne yoma no mu akuo mmienu

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: kaa sɛ: Sɛ Esau ba kuo baako so bɛku wɔn a, ekuo a ɛbɛka no bɛnya kwan adwane.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: M’agya Abraham Nyankopɔn ne m’agya Isak Nyankopɔn, AWURADE a wosee me sɛ: Sane kɔ w’asase so ne w’abusua mu, na mɛyɛ wo yie no,

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, yi me firi me nua Esau nsam, ɛfiri sɛ mesuro no sɛ ɔbɛba abɛku me, ne ɛnanom ne wɔn mma nyinaa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Wo na wokaa sɛ: Yie na mɛyɛ woɔ, na mɛma w’asefoɔ ayɛ sɛ mpoano anwea a dodoɔ nti wɔntumi nkan.

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:

translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Na ɛdɔm a mehyiaa wɔn yi ase ne sɛn? Na ɔse: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na mɛnya me wura anim adom.

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Deɛ mewɔ dɔɔso, me nua, ma w’adeɛ ntena hɔ mma wo.

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: Dabi da, mesrɛ wo, sɛ manya w’anim adom a, gye m’ayɛyɛdeɛ a ɛwɔ me nsam yi, na w’anim a mahunu yi te sɛdeɛ obi hunu Nyankopɔn anim, ɛfiri sɛ w’ani asɔ me.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, gye nhyira a wɔde abrɛ woɔ yi, ɛfiri sɛ Onyankopɔn adom me, na mewɔ ade nyinaa. Na ɔhyɛɛ no, na ɔgyee.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Ma yɛnsim nkɔ, na menni w’anim.

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me wura nim sɛ mma a wɔyɛ mmerɛ ne nnwan ne anantwie a wɔma nufoɔ ka me ho, na sɛ wɔpia wɔn dodo da koro a, nnwankuo no nyinaa bɛwuwu.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Enti ma me wura nsene nni n’akoa anim, na me deɛ, mɛnante brɛoo, sɛdeɛ mmoa a wɔdi m’anim ne mma no bɛtumi de akɔsi sɛ mɛduru me wura nkyɛn wɔ Seir.

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Ma mennya wo nnipa a wɔka me ho yi bi. Na ɔse: Na wɔnyɛ dɛn? Ma mennya me wura anim adom.

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii mu kɔɔ Sukot, na ɔsii dan maa ne ho, na ɔbobɔɔ asese maa ne mmoa. Yei nti na wɔfrɛ hɔ Sukot.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Na Yakob firii Mesopotamia no, ɔnam bɛduruu Sekem kuro a ɛwɔ Kanaan asase soɔ no mu dwoodwoo, na ɔsisii ne ntomadan wɔ kuro no anim.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔɔ asase a ɔsii ne ntomadan wɔ soɔ no wɔ Sekem agya Hamor mma nkyɛn nnwetɛbena ɔha.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔsii afɔrebukyia wɔ hɔ, na ɔtoo no: El-elohe-Israel.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Na Lea ne Yakob babaa Dina firii adi sɛ ɔrekɔhwɛ asase no so mmaa.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Na asase no so otitire Hewini Hamor ba Sekem hunuu no, na ɔkyeree no too no mmɔnaa guu ne ho fi.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ba Dina sɔɔ Sekem ani, na ɔdɔɔ ababaa no, na ɔkorɔkorɔɔ no.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Na Sekem ka kyerɛɛ n’agya Hamor sɛ: Kɔgye ababaa yi awareɛ ma me.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Na Yakob tee sɛ wagu ne babaa Dina ho fi. Nanso ɛnam sɛ na ne mmammarima no wɔ ne mmoa nkyɛn wɔ wiram no, enti ɔyɛɛ komm de kɔsii sɛ wɔbaa fie.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Na Yakob mmammarima teeɛ no, wɔfirii wiram bae. Na ɛyɛɛ mmarima no ya, na wɔn bo fuu pa ara, sɛ Sekem adi Israel ho nkwaseasɛm sɛ ɔne Yakob babaa akɔda; adeɛ a ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Na Hamor ne wɔn kasaa sɛ: Me ba Sekem akoma fam mo babaa no ho; mesrɛ mo, momfa no mma no aware.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Na mo ne yɛn nni ayewareɛ, na momfa mo mmammaa mma yɛn, na mo nso monware yɛn mmammaa.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Na mo ne yɛn ntena, na asase na ɛda mo anim yi, montena so nyɛ so adwuma nnya so adeɛ.

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Na Sekem ka kyerɛɛ Dina n’agya ne ne nuanom sɛ: Momma mennya mo anim adom, na biribiara a mobɛse me no, mɛma.

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Monnye me etire adeɛ dodoɔ ne akyɛdeɛ biara, na biribiara a mobɛse me no, mɛma; na momfa ababaa no mma me awareɛ.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Na Yakob mmammarima no kasa de nnaadaa buaa Sekem n’agya Hamor ɛfiri sɛ wagu wɔn nuabaa Dina ho fi.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Yɛntumi saa adeɛ yi yɛ, sɛ yɛde yɛn nua bɛma ɔbarima a ɔyɛ momonoto, ɛfiri sɛ ɛno yɛ ahohora ma yɛn.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Na yei mu nko na yɛbɛpene mo sɛ mobɛdane ayɛ sɛ yɛn, na wɔatwitwa mo mu mmarima nyinaa twetia.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Ɛno na yɛde yɛn mmammaa bɛma mo, na yɛabɛfa mo mmammaa nso aware, na yɛne mo atena, na yɛayɛ ɔman korɔ.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Na sɛ moantie yɛn, na moantwitwa twetia a, ɛnneɛ yɛbɛfa yɛn babaa akɔ.

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nsɛm no sɔɔ Hamor ne ne ba Sekem ani.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Enti Sekem antwetwe ne ho sɛ ɔbɛyɛ saa adeɛ no, ɛfiri sɛ na Yakob babaa no sɔ n’ani, na aberanteɛ no animuonyam sene n’agya fiefoɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Na Hamor ne ne ba Sekem kɔɔ wɔn kuro aboboano, na wɔne wɔn kurom mmarima kɔkasaa sɛ:

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: Nnipa yi, wɔne yɛn te asomdwoeɛ mu, enti momma wɔntena asase yi so, na wɔnyɛ so adwuma. Na asase yi, hwɛ, ɛda wɔn anim kakraa. Momma yɛmfa wɔn mmammaa nware, na yɛmfa yɛn mmammaa nso mma wɔn.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Na yei nko mu na nnipa no bɛpene sɛ wɔne yɛn bɛtena, na yɛayɛ ɔman korɔ; sɛ yɛn mu mmarima nyinaa bɛtwitwa twetia, sɛdeɛ wɔatwitwa no.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Wɔn mmoa ne wɔn ahonyadeɛ ne wɔn afieboa nyinaa renyɛ yɛn dea anaa? Momma yɛmpene so ma wɔn, na wɔne yɛn ntena.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa a ne yea kaa wɔn no, Yakob mmammarima baanu, Simeon ne Lewi a wɔyɛ Dina nuanom, fefaa wɔn nkrantɛ kɔɔ kuro no so mpofirim kɔkunkumm mmarima nyinaa.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Na wɔde nkrantɛ kumm Hamor ne ne ba Sekem; na wɔde Dina firii Sekem fie hɔ bae.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob mmammarima no baa atɔfoɔ no so bɛfom kuro no mu nnoɔma fae, ɛfiri sɛ wɔagu wɔn nua no ho fi.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Wɔn nnwan, wɔn anantwie, wɔn mfunumu ne deɛ ɛwɔ kuro no mu ne deɛ ɛwɔ mfuo mu no, wɔfae.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Na wɔn ade nyinaa ne wɔn mma nyinaa ne wɔn yerenom, wɔfaa wɔn nnommum fom deɛ ɛwɔ fie nyinaa.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Simeon ne Lewi sɛ: Moaha me ama me ho abɔn wɔn a wɔte asase yi soɔ, Kanaanfoɔ ne Perisifoɔ. Na me deɛ, meyɛ asafo a mesua yi, wɔbɛboaboa wɔn ano aba me so abɛku me, na wɔasɛe me ne me fie.

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Ɔnyɛ yɛn nuabaa sɛ odwamamfoɔ anaa?

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Na momma yɛnsɔre nkɔ Betel, na menkɔsi afɔrebukyia wɔ hɔ memma Onyankopɔn a m’ahohiahia da ɔtiee me na ɔdii m’akyire wɔ kwan a mekɔeɛ no mu no.

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔde wɔn anyame ananafoɔ a ɛwɔ wɔn nsam nyinaa ne wɔn aso mu nkaa maa Yakob, na ɔde siee dupɔn bi a ɛwɔ Sekem ho no ase.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Na wɔsii mu sɛ wɔrekorɔ no, Nyankopɔn ho hu baa nkuro a atwa wɔn ho ahyia no so, na wɔanti Yakob mma no.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Na ɔsii hɔ afɔrebukyia, na ɔfrɛɛ hɔ: El-betel, ɛfiri sɛ da a ɔredwane afiri ne nua anim no, ɛhɔ na Onyankopɔn yii ne ho kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Na Rebeka abaawa panin Debora wui, na wɔsiee no Betel aseɛ fam wɔ odum bi ase, na ɔtoo dua no din Alon-bakut.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Na asase a mede mama Abraham ne Isak no, wo na mede bɛma woɔ; na w’asefoɔ a wɔbɛdi w’akyire no na mede asase no bɛma wɔn.

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Na Yakob de odum sii deɛ ɔne no kasaeɛ hɔ, ɔboɔ dum, na ɔhwiee ɔnom afɔdeɛ guu so, na ɔde ngo guu so.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Na Yakob frɛɛ deɛ ɔne Onyankopɔn kasaeɛ hɔ Betel. Rahel wuo

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Na wɔtutu firi Betel kɔe. Na aka kwan tiaa bi na wɔaduru Efrat no, awoɔ kaa Rahel, na awoɔ no denee no.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Na n’awoɔ mu yɛɛ den no, awogyefoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro, na yei nso wobɛwo ɔbabarima.

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na ne kra refiri ne mu na ɔreyɛ awuo no, ɔtoo no din Ben-oni, na n’agya deɛ, ɔfrɛɛ no Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na Rahel wui, na wɔsiee no ɛkwan a ɛde Efrat no nkyɛn.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii ne da so dum, ɛne Rahel da so dum de bɛsi nnɛ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Na Israel tutu kɔsii ne ntomadan wɔ Eder abantenten akyiri nohoa.

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ Israel te asase no soɔ no, Ruben ne n’agya abaawayerɛ Bilha kɔdae, na Israel tee. Yakob mmammarima (

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Na Yakob baa n’agya Isak nkyɛn wɔ Mamre, wɔ Kiriat-arba , deɛ Abraham ne Isak tenaeɛ sɛ ahɔhoɔ no.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esau waree Kanaanfoɔ mmaa: Hetini Elon babaa Ada, ne Hewini Sibeon ba Ana babaa Oholibama,

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: ne Ismael babaa Basmat, Nebaiot nuabaa.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Na Oholibama woo Yeus ne Yalam ne Kora. Yeinom ne Esau mma a wɔwoo wɔn wɔ Kanaan asase soɔ.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Esau faa ne yerenom ne ne mmammarima ne ne mmammaa ne ne fiefoɔ nyinaa ne ne mmoa ne n’anantwie nyinaa ne n’ahonyadeɛ a ɔnyaeɛ wɔ Kanaan asase soɔ nyinaa, na ɔfirii ne nua Yakob ho kɔɔ asase bi so,

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ wɔn ahonyadeɛ dɔɔso sene deɛ wɔde tena faako, na asase a wɔyɛ so ahɔhoɔ no, wɔn mmoa dodoɔ nti na wɔnsene so.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Esau, a ɔno ara ne Edom no kɔtenaa Seir bepɔ so.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Esau mma mu atitire: Esau abakan Elifas mma: Otitire Teman, otitire Omar, otitire Sefo, otitire Kenas,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: otitire Kora, otitire Gatam, ne otitire Amalek. Yeinom ne Elifas atitire wɔ Edom asase so; yeinom ne Ada mma.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Esau ba Reuel mma: Otitire Nahat, otitire Sera, otitire Sama, ne otitire Misa. Yeinom ne Reuel atitire wɔ Edom asase so; yeinom ne Esau yere Basmat mma.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Esau yere Oholibama mma: Otitire Yeus, otitire Yalam, otitire Kora. Yeinom ne Esau yere Oholibama, Ana ba, atitire no.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Esau mma, na yeinom ne wɔn atitire no; Seir Asefoɔ (

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Na Lotan mma ne Hori ne Hemam, na Lotan nuabaa ne Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Sobal mma: Alwan, Manahat, Ebal, Sefo ne Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Sibeon mma: Aya ne Ana. Oyi ne Ana a na ɔhwɛ n’agya Sibeon mfunumu no, a ɔhunuu nsuohyeɛ aniwa wɔ ɛserɛ soɔ no.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Ana mma: Dison ne Oholibama, a ɔyɛ Ana babaa.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Dison mma: Hemdan, Esban, Itran ne Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Eser mma: Bilhan, Saawan ne Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Disan mma: Us ne Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Horifoɔ atitire: Otitire Lotan, otitire Sobal, otitire Sibeon, otitire Ana,

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: otitire Dison, otitire Eser, otitire Disan. Yeinom ne Horifoɔ atitire sɛdeɛ wɔn mmusua teɛ wɔ Seir asase soɔ. Edom Ahemfo (

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Esau atitire no din, sɛdeɛ wɔn mmusuakuo, wɔn tenabea ne wɔn din teɛ: Otitire Timna, otitire Alwa, otitire Yetet,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: otitire Oholibama, otitire Ela, otitire Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: otitire Kenas, otitire Teman, otitire Mibsar,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: otitire Magdiel, otitire Iram. Yeinom ne Edom no atitire, sɛdeɛ wɔn tenabea teɛ wɔ asase a wɔnyaeɛ no soɔ.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Na Yakob tenaa asase a n’agya yɛɛ so hɔhoɔ a ɛne Kanaan asase no so.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no se: Wɔatu ha; na metee sɛ wɔreka sɛ: Momma yɛnkɔ Dotan. Na Yosef tii ne nuanom, na ɔkɔhunuu wɔn wɔ Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Na ɛsiane sɛ Yosef yɛ ne nkɔkoraaberɛ mu ba nti, na Israel dɔ no sene ne mma nyinaa; enti ɔpam batakari fɛfɛ bi maa no.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom hunuu sɛ wɔn agya dɔ no sene wɔn nyinaa no, wɔtanee no, na wɔmfa abodwoɔ ne no nkasa.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Na Yosef soo daeɛ, na berɛ a ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom no, wɔtanee no senee akane no.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Montie daeɛ a maso yi:

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, na yɛrekyekyere ayuo afiafi wɔ afuom. Na m’afi no sɔre gyinaa kyirebenn, na hwɛ, mo afiafi no twaa m’afi ho hyiae, na ɛrekoto m’afi no.

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kyerɛ sɛ worebɛdi yɛn so hene anaasɛ worebɛdi yɛn so tumi? Na ne daeɛ ne ne nsɛm no nti wɔkɔɔ so tanee no bebree.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsoo daeɛ foforɔ bio, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Hwɛ, maso daeɛ bio, na hwɛ, owia ne ɔsrane ne nsoromma dubaako akoto me.

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya ne ne nuanom no, n’agya kaa n’anim sɛ: Daeɛ bɛn na woaso yi? Kyerɛ sɛ, me ne wo na ne wo nuanom bɛba abɛkoto fam wɔ w’anim?

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom ani beree no; na n’agya deɛ, ɔde nsɛm no siee. Wɔtɔn Yosef ma wɔde no kɔ Misraim

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom de wɔn agya nnwan kɔɔ adidie wɔ Sekem.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Sɛ wonim sɛ wo nuanom rewɛn mmoa wɔ Sekem. Bra na mensoma wo wɔn nkyɛn. Na ɔse: Menie.

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ na kɔhwɛ sɛ wo nuanom ne nnwan no ho yɛ anaa; na sane bɛka kyerɛ me. Na ɔsomaa no firii Hebron bonhwa mu, na ɔkɔduruu Sekem.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi hunuu no, na hwɛ, na ɔrewɔ wira no mu ntwɛtwɛdɛ. Na ɔbarima no bisaa no sɛ: Worehwehwɛ deɛn?

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me nuanom na merehwehwɛ wɔn; mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me faako a wɔrehwɛ wɔn mmoa no.

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom hunuu no akyirikyiri na ɔnnya nnuruu wɔn nkyɛn no, wɔpamm ne tiri so sɛ wɔbɛku no.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Na wɔsesee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔdaeɛsofoɔ no na ɔreba no.

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Afei mommra mma yɛnku no mfa no nto mmura yi bi mu, na yɛnka sɛ: Aboa bɔne bi na awe no, na yɛahwɛ deɛ ne daeɛ no bɛyɛ.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Na Ruben teeɛ no, ɔgyee no firii wɔn nsam kaa sɛ: Mommma yɛnnku no.

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Monnhwie mogya nngu, na momfa no nto ɛserɛ so ha abura yi mu; na mommfa mo nsa nnka no. Ɔreyɛ na anka wayi no afiri wɔn nsam de no asane akɔma n’agya.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Na Yosef duruu ne nuanom nkyɛn no, wɔworɔɔ n’atadeɛ ne batakari fɛfɛ a ɔhyɛ no,

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Na wɔtenaa ase didii. Na wɔmaa wɔn ani so hwɛe, wɔhunuu Ismaelfoɔ akwantufoɔkuo bi a wɔfiri Gilead rekɔ Misraim ne wɔn yoma a wɔsoso hyehwam ne akyenkyennuro ne kurobo sɛ wɔreba.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Sɛ yɛkum yɛn nua na yɛsi ne mogya so a, mfasoɔ bɛn na ɛwɔ mu?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Mommra mma yɛntɔn no mma Ismaelfoɔ. Mommma yɛmmfa yɛn nsa nnka no, ɛfiri sɛ ɔyɛ yɛn nua ne yɛn mogya. Na ne nuanom no tiee no.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Na Midianfoɔ adwadifoɔ bi rebɛsene. Na wɔtwetwee Yosef yii no firii abura no mu, na wɔtɔn no maa Ismaelfoɔ no gyee nnwetɛbena aduonu. Na wɔde Yosef kɔɔ Misraim.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Na Ruben sane baa abura no so, na hwɛ, na Yosef nni abura no mu. Na ɔsunsuanee ne ntadeɛ mu,

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: na ɔsane baa ne nuanom nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Abɔfra no nni hɔ, na afei ɛdeɛn na menyɛ?

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa Yosef atadeɛ no, na wɔkumm ɔpapo bi, na wɔde atadeɛ no bɔɔ mogya no mu.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Na wɔsoma maa wɔde batakari fɛfɛ no brɛɛ wɔn agya bɛkaa sɛ: Yei na yɛahunu, hwɛ sɛ wo ba no atadeɛ ni anaa?

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛeɛ no, ɔkaa sɛ: Ɛyɛ me ba no atadeɛ a! Aboa bɔne bi na awe no, ampa ara wɔatete Yosef mu.

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob sunsuanee ne ntadeɛ mu, na ɔde ayitoma bɔɔ n’asene, na ɔsuu ne ba no kyɛree.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Na ne mmammarima nyinaa ne ne mmammaa nyinaa bae sɛ wɔbɛkyekyere ne werɛ, nanso wamma wɔankyekyere ne werɛ. Na ɔkaa sɛ: Mede awerɛhoɔ yi ara bɛkɔ me ba nkyɛn wɔ Asamando. Na n’agya suu no.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Na Midianfoɔ no kɔtɔnee no wɔ Misraim maa Potifar a ɔyɛ Farao piani ne n’ankɔbeafoɔ so panin no.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ berɛ no ara mu Yuda firii ne nuanom nkyɛn kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Adulamni bi a wɔfrɛ no Hira nkyɛn.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Na Yuda hunuu Kanaanni bi a wɔfrɛ no Sua babaa bi wɔ hɔ, ɔwaree no na ɔne no dae.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo no din Er.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio woo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo no din Onan.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio woo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo no din Sela. Na ɔwoo no no, na ɔwɔ Kesib.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Na Yuda waree yerɛ bi a wɔfrɛ no Tamar maa n’abakan Er.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na Yuda abakan Er dii amumuyɛsɛm AWURADE anim, na AWURADE kumm no.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ Onan sɛ: Kɔ wo nua yere no ho, na fa ne kunafoɔ, na wo mma ma wo nua no.

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Na Onan nim sɛ mma no renyɛ ne dea, na ɛbaa sɛ, sɛ ɔkɔ ne nua yere no ho a, ɔma ne ho gu fam sɛe, na wanwo mma amma ne nua.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Na deɛ ɔyɛeɛ no yɛɛ bɔne wɔ AWURADE anim, enti ɔkumm ɔno nso.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Na afei Yuda ka kyerɛɛ n’ase Tamar sɛ: Kɔtena kuna mu wɔ w’agya fie kɔsi sɛ me ba Sela bɛnyini. Ɛfiri sɛ ɔse, anyɛ saa a, ɔno nso bɛwu sɛ ne nuanom. Na Tamar kɔ kɔtenaa n’agya fie.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Na ɛkyɛree kyɛreeɛ no, Sua babaa, Yuda yere no, wui. Na Yuda werɛ kyekyereeɛ no, ɔne n’adamfo Hira Adulamni no kɔɔ ne nnwan ho twitwafoɔ nkyɛn wɔ Timnat.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Tamar sɛ: Hwɛ, w’ase rekɔ Timnat akɔtwitwa ne nnwan ho.

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Na ɔyii ne kuna ntadeɛ firii ne ho, na ɔde nkatanimu kataa n’anim, na ɔsakyeraa ne ho kɔtenaa Enaim kurotia wɔ Timnat kwan ho, ɛfiri sɛ wahunu sɛ Sela anyini, na wɔamfa no amma no awareɛ.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Na Yuda hunuu no no, ɛsiane sɛ wakata n’anim nti, ɔbuu no sɛ odwamamfoɔ.

english_verse: and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
translation_verse: Na ɔmane kɔɔ ne nkyɛn ɔkwan no ho kaa sɛ: Ma mene wo nkɔda ɛ, nso na ɔnnim sɛ n’ase a. Na ɔse: Ɛdeɛn na wobɛma me na wone me ada?

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Mɛma wɔde abirekyie ba afiri mmoa mu abrɛ wo. Na ɔse: Ɛnneɛ ma me awowadeɛ kɔsi sɛ wode bɛba.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na memfa mensi wo awowa? Na ɔse: Wo nsɔanokaa ne wo homa ne wo nsam poma. Na ɔde maa no, na ɔkɔɔ ne ho, na ɔne no nyinsɛnee.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔree, na ɔkɔe, na ɔyii ne nkatanimu firii ne ho, na ɔhyɛɛ ne kuna ntadeɛ no.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Na Yuda de abirekyie ba no maa n’adamfo Adulamni no sɛ ɔmfa nkɔgye n’awowadeɛ no wɔ ɔbaa no nsam mmrɛ no, nanso wanhu no.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa kurom hɔfoɔ sɛ: Odwamamfoɔ a ɔte Enaim kwan ho no wɔ he? Na wɔse: Odwamamfoɔ biara nni ha.

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsane baa Yuda nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Manhu no, nanso kurom hɔfoɔ se: Odwamamfoɔ biara nni hɔ.

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda se: Ma no mfa, na yɛn ani anwu. Hwɛ, mama wode abirekyie ba yi akɔma no, na woanhu no.

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Na ɛbɛyɛ abosome mmiɛnsa akyiri no, wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Yuda sɛ: W’ase Tamar abɔ adwaman ama no anyinsɛn. Na Yuda kaa sɛ: Monkɔfa no mmra na wɔnhye no.

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔfaa Tamar baeɛ no, ɔsoma maa wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ n’ase no sɛ: Ɔbarima a ne nnoɔma nie no, ne me na anyinsɛn. Na ɔse: Hwehwɛ mu na hwɛ, deɛ nsɔanokaa, homa ne poma yi yɛ ne dea?

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Na Yuda ani hunuiɛ no, ɔkaa sɛ: Ɔtene sene me, ɛfiri sɛ mamfa no mamma me ba Sela. Nanso ɔne no anna bio.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Na ɔrewoɔ no, ɔbaako yii ne nsa, na awogyefoɔ no sɔɔ mu de asaawa kɔkɔɔ kyekyeree ne nsa no kaa sɛ: Oyi na ɔfirii adi kane.

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwee ne nsa kɔɔ mu no, hwɛ, ne nua no firii adi, na ɔkaa sɛ: Hwɛ sɛdeɛ woatete mu? Wo so na ntemu no wɔ. Enti wɔtoo no din Peres.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Na akyire yi no, ne nua a asaawa kɔkɔɔ bɔ ne nsa soɔ no bae, na ɔtoo no din Sera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Na wɔde Yosef kɔɔ Misraim. Na Farao piani Potifar a ɔyɛ ankɔbeafoɔ so panin na ɔyɛ Misraimni no tɔɔ no Ismaelfoɔ a wɔde no kɔɔ hɔ no nsam.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Na ne wura hunuu sɛ AWURADE di n’akyi na AWURADE ma deɛ ɔyɛ nyinaa yɛ yie n’abasa soɔ no,

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Yosef nyaa n’anim adom, na ɔsom no; na ɔde no sii ne fie so, na ɔde deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ ne nsa.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Na ɔde deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na ɔwɔ hɔ nti, ɔnhwɛ biribiara gye aduane a ɔno ara die. Nso na Yosef ho ne n’anim yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ akyire yi no, Yosef wura yere tuu n’ani sii ne so, na ɔkaa sɛ: Wo ne me mmɛda.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Nanso wampene, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne wura yere no sɛ: Hwɛ, sɛ me wura anya me nti ɔnhwɛ deɛ ɛwɔ ne fie, na ɔde deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa ahyɛ me nsa.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Obiara nyɛ kɛseɛ nsene me efie ha, na ɔnkame me biribiara gye wo, ɛnam sɛ ne yere ne woɔ ntira. Na adɛn na menyɛ amumuyɛ kɛseɛ yi, na menyɛ bɔne mentia Onyankopɔn?

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛ Yosef saa daa daa, nanso Yosef antie sɛ ɔne no bɛda na ama ne nsa aka no.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Na da koro bi a ɔkɔɔ ɛdan no mu sɛ ɔrekɔyɛ n’adwuma, na efie hɔfoɔ no mu biara nni hɔ no,

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: ne wura yere no sɔɔ n’atadeɛ mu kaa sɛ: Wo ne me mmɛda! Na Yosef gyaa n’atadeɛ no wɔ ne nsam dwane firii adi.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ɔfrɛfrɛɛ ne fiefoɔ ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monhwɛ, wakɔfa Hebrini yi aba rebɛdi yɛn ho fɛw; waba me nkyɛn sɛ ɔne me rebɛda, na mede nne kɛseɛ meteaa mu;

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: na ɔtee sɛ memaa me nne soɔ meteaa mu no, ɔgyaa n’atadeɛ wɔ me nsam, na ɔdwane firii adi.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Na ɔde n’atadeɛ no guu ne nkyɛn kɔsii sɛ ne wura baa fie.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: na memaa me nne so meteaa mu no, ɔgyaa n’atadeɛ wɔ me nsam, na ɔdwane firii adie.

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Na Yosef wura no faa no de no kɔtoo afiase, deɛ ɔhene nneduafoɔ guo, na ɔdaa afiase hɔ. Onyankopɔn di Yosef akyi

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dii Yosef akyi, na ɔdom no, na ɔmaa n’anim baa nyam wɔ afiasehwɛni no anim.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Na afiasehwɛni no de nneduafoɔ a wɔwɔ afiase hɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na biribiara a na wɔyɛ no wɔ hɔ no, ɔno na na ɔhwɛ soɔ.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Afiasehwɛni no anha ne ho anhwɛ biribiara a ɛwɔ Yosef nsam, ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE dii n’akyi, na deɛ ɔyɛeɛ nyinaa, AWURADE maa no yɛɛ yie.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔde wɔn kɔguu afiase wɔ ankɔbeafoɔ panin no fie, faako a Yosef da hɔ.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Na ankɔbeafoɔ panin no maa Yosef hwɛɛ wɔn so som wɔn; na wɔkyɛree afiase hɔ kakra.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Na Misraimhene nsahyɛni ne ne paanootoni a na wɔgu afiase hɔ no baanu nyinaa sosoo daeɛ anadwo korɔ, ɛsono oyi daeɛ ne n’asekyerɛ, na ɛsono oyi nso daeɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Na Yosef kɔɔ wɔn nkyɛn anɔpa kɔhwɛɛ wɔn, na hwɛ, na wɔayeyɛ mosomosoo.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛasoso daeɛ, nso obiara nni hɔ a ɔbɛkyerɛ aseɛ. Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Nkyerɛaseɛ mfiri Onyankopɔn hɔ anaa? Monka nkyerɛ me ɛ!

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Ɛnna nsahyɛfoɔ panin no kaa ne daeɛ no kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me daeɛ mu no, na hwɛ, bobe bi si m’anim,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: na bobe no apae nkorabata mmiɛnsa, na ayɛ sɛdeɛ ɛrefefɛ, na anyini agu nhyerɛne, na abɔ esia ayɛ aba a abereɛ.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kuruwa kura me, na metetee bobe aba no mekyi guu Farao kuruwa no mu, na mede kuruwa no hyɛɛ Farao nsa.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ne nkyerɛaseɛ nie: Nkorabata mmiɛnsa no yɛ nnansa.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Na aka nnansa na Farao ayi wo afiri ha de wo asane akɔdi wo dibea bio, na wode Farao kuruwa ahyɛ ne nsa sɛ kane a na woyɛ ne nsahyɛni no.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ ɛyɛ a, kae me, na sɛ ɛsi wo yie a, yɛ me adɔeɛ, na bɔ me din kyerɛ Farao, na bɛyi me ɛdan yi mu,

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ wia na wɔwiaa me Hebrifoɔ asase soɔ, na ɛha nso menyɛɛ hwee a anka ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde me bɛto amena yi mu.

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Na paanootofoɔ panin no hunuu sɛ nkyerɛaseɛ no yɛ no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me nso, me daeɛ mu no, na hwɛ, paanoo nkɛntɛn mmiɛnsa a ɛsisi soɔ wɔ m’atifi.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Na kɛntɛn a ɛdi soro no mu na Farao anomu atɔduane nyinaa bi wɔ; na nnomaa redidi wɔ kɛntɛn no mu wɔ m’atifi.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef buaa sɛ: Ne nkyerɛaseɛ nie: Nkyerɛnkyɛ mmiɛnsa no yɛ nnansa;

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: na aka nnansa na Farao ayi wo afiri ha, na wakɔsɛne wo dua so ma nnomaa adi wo nam afiri wo ho.

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa a ɛyɛ Farao awoda no, ɔtoo ne nkoa nyinaa pono, na ɔyii nsahyɛfoɔ panin ne paanootofoɔ mu panin no de wɔn baa ne nkoa anim;

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: na ɔsane de nsahyɛfoɔ mu panin no sii ne nsahyɛ so bio a ɔde kuruwa hyɛ Farao nsa.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Na paanootofoɔ panin no deɛ, ɔsɛnee no, sɛdeɛ Yosef kyerɛɛ wɔn aseɛ no.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Nanso nsahyɛfoɔ panin no ankae Yosef, na ne werɛ firii no.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na mfeɛ mmienu akyiri no, Farao soo daeɛ, na hwɛ, ɔgyina Nil asubɔnten no ho.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwibereɛ nson a wɔn ho yɛ fɛ na wɔn ho tua wɔn ho firi asubɔnten no mu ba bɛdidii ɛserɛ no mu.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Na ɔsane soo daeɛ bio, na hwɛ, ayuo mmɛtem nson a ɛtoatoa soɔ na abɔ ma refifiri wɔ nan korɔ so.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mmɛtem nson nkorowankorowa a apueeɛ mframa akusa no fifiri dii akyire bae.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Na mmɛtem nkorowankorowa no memenee mmɛtem nson a ɛtoatoa soɔ na ayuo wɔ mu no. Na Farao nyanee, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ daeɛ.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa no ne ho dwanee no, na ɔsoma maa wɔkɔfrɛfrɛɛ Misraim atwerɛfoɔ nyinaa ne ɛhɔ anyansafoɔ nyinaa, na Farao kaa ne daeɛ no kyerɛɛ wɔn, nanso obiara antumi ankyerɛ no aseɛ.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Ɛnna nsahyɛfoɔ mu panin no ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Makae me mfomsoɔ nnɛ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Berɛ a Farao bo fuu ne nkoa na ɔde me ne paanootofoɔ panin no kɔtoo afiase wɔ ankɔbeafoɔ panin fie no,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: yɛsosoo daeɛ anadwo korɔ no ara, me ne no na ɛsonsono yɛn daeɛ a yɛsosoeɛ ne ebiara nkyerɛaseɛ.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Na Hebrini aberanteɛ bi a ɔyɛ ankɔbeafoɔ panin no akoa ne yɛn na ɛwɔ hɔ, na yɛkekaa yɛn daeɛ kyerɛɛ no no, ɔkyerɛɛ yɛn yɛn daeɛ no ase, sɛdeɛ ebiara teɛ.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Na sɛdeɛ ɔkyerɛɛ yɛn aseɛ no, saa ara na ɛbaeɛ. Wɔde me sane kɔdii me dibea, na ɔno deɛ, wɔsɛnee no.

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Na Farao soma maa wɔkɔfrɛɛ Yosef, na wɔyɛɛ ntɛm yii no firii afiase hɔ; na ɔyii ne tirinwi, na ɔsakyeraa ne ntadeɛ, na ɔbaa Farao anim.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Maso daeɛ, nso obiara nni hɔ a ɔtumi kyerɛ aseɛ; na wo na mate wo nka sɛ, wote daeɛ a, wotumi kyerɛ aseɛ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef buaa Farao sɛ: Ɛnni me fam, na mmom Onyankopɔn na ɔmfa mmuaeɛ pa mma Farao.

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me daeɛ mu no, hwɛ, na megyina Asubɔntene Nil nsunoa.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwie nson a wɔn ho tua wɔn ho na wɔn ho yɛ fɛ firi nsuo no mu ba bɛdidii wɔ wiram hɔ.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwie nson foforɔ nso a wɔyɛ kanyaa na wɔn ho yɛ tane yie, na wɔafomfɔn a menhunuu wɔn ho tane no so bi wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so da dii wɔn akyiri bae.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Na wɔduruu wɔn yafunu mu no, obi anhunu sɛ wɔaduru wɔn yafunu mu, na wɔn ho da so yɛ tane sɛ kane no ara. Ɛnna menyaneeɛ.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Na mehunuu wɔ me daeɛ mu sɛ ayuo mmɛtem nson a ɛtoatoa soɔ na abɔ ma refifiri nan korɔ so.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mmɛtem nson a ahoa na ɛyɛ ntraantraa na apueeɛ mframa ama no akusa dii akyire fifirii.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Na mmɛtem ntraantraa no memenee mmɛtem nson a ɛyɛ no. Na maka makyerɛ atwerɛfoɔ no, nso obiara antumi ankyerɛ me aseɛ.

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Farao daeɛ no yɛ bafua; Onyankopɔn rekyerɛ Farao deɛ ɔrebɛyɛ.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Anantwie pa nson no yɛ mfeɛ nson, na mmɛtem nson pa no nso yɛ mfeɛ nson; ɛyɛ daeɛ korɔ.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Na anantwie nson a wɔafomfɔn a wɔn ho yɛ tane a wɔdii wɔn akyiri baeɛ no ne mmɛtem nson nkorowankorowa a apueeɛ mframa akusa no bɛyɛ mfirinhyia nson kɔm.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Asɛm no te sɛ deɛ maka makyerɛ Farao no ara. Deɛ Onyankopɔn rebɛyɛ no na ɔde akyerɛ Farao yi:

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mfirinhyia nson reba a aduane bebree bɛba Misraim asase nyinaa soɔ.

english_verse: when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyiri no, ɛkɔm bɛba mfirinhyia nson ama nnipa werɛ afiri aduane bebrebe no nyinaa wɔ Misraim asase so, na ɛkɔm no bɛhye asase no.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɔm a ɛbɛdi akyire no nti wɔrenhunu asase no so aduane bebrebe no bio, ɛfiri sɛ ɛkɔm no mu bɛyɛ dendeenden.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Na daeɛ no a ɛyɛɛ mmɔho mmienu maa Farao no ase ne sɛ, Onyankopɔn ahyɛ saa adeɛ no ampa, na Onyankopɔn rebɛyɛ no ntɛmntɛm.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Na afei ma Farao nhwehwɛ onipa a ɔyɛ ɔbadwemma ne onyansafoɔ mfa no nsi Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Na Farao nyɛ yei, na ɔnsisi asase no so ahwɛfoɔ, na wɔnnyegye Misraim asase so aduane so ntotosoɔ nnum nnum mfeɛ nson a aduane bebree wɔ mu no mu.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Na ma wɔmmoaboa mfirinhyia pa a ɛrebɛba yi mu aduane nyinaa ano, na wɔmfa ayuo ngugu asan so sɛdeɛ Farao bɛhyɛ, na ɛnyɛ nkuro mu aduane, na wɔmfa nsie.
