english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Na ayɛ aduane a wɔakora ama asase no de asie mfirinhyia nson kɔm a ɛbɛba Misraim asase soɔ no, na asase no ansɛe wɔ ɛkɔm no mu. Yosef animuonyamhyɛ

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Na asɛm no sɔɔ Farao ne ne nkoa nyinaa ani.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Yɛbɛtumi anya onipa bi a ɔte sɛ oyi a Nyankopɔn honhom wɔ ne mu yi anaa?

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Ɛnam sɛ Onyankopɔn de yei nyinaa akyerɛ woɔ yi, obiara nni hɔ a ɔyɛ ɔbadwemma ne onyansafoɔ sɛ woɔ.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Wobɛdi me fie so, na w’anomu asɛm so na me man nyinaa bɛdie, gye ahennwa nko so na mɛsene woɔ.

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, mede wo masi Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Na Farao yii nsɔanokaa firii ne nsa de hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na ɔhyɛɛ no nwera pa atadeɛ, na ɔde sika atweaban too ne kɔn mu.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa no tenaa ne teaseɛnam a ɛtɔ so mmienu mu, na wɔteaa mu dii n’anim sɛ: Monkoto! Na ɔde no sii Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Mene Farao, na obiara renkwati wo nyɛ biribiara wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Yosef Safnat-panea. Na ɔde On sɔfoɔ Potifera babaa Asnat maa no awareɛ.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Na ahotɔ mfeɛ nson no mu no, aduane pii baa asase no so maa no buu so.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Na ɔboaboaa mfeɛ nson a ɛbaa Misraim asase soɔ no mu aduane nyinaa ano, na ɔde aduane no siee nkuro no mu; nkuraa a atwa ahyia no mu aduane na ɔde siee nkuro no mu.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Na Yosef boaboaa ayuo ano pii pa ara sɛ mpoano anwea de kɔsii sɛ wɔgyaee kan, ɛfiri sɛ na ɛnni ano.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Na wɔwoo mma baanu maa Yosef ansa na ɛkɔm mfirinhyia no reduro; wɔn na On sɔfoɔ Potifera ba Asnat wo maa no.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef too abakan no din Manase, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Onyankopɔn ama me werɛ afiri m’amaneɛ ne m’agya fie nyinaa.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo deɛ ɔtɔ so mmienu no din Efraim, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Onyankopɔn ama madɔ wɔ m’amanehunu asase yi so.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Na ahotɔ a ɛbaa Misraim asase so mfeɛ nson no to twae.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɔm mfeɛ nson no firii aseɛ bae, sɛdeɛ Yosef kaeɛ no, na ɛkɔm baa nsase nyinaa so na Misraim asase nyinaa so deɛ, na aduane wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Na ɛberɛ a ɛkɔm kaa Misraim asase nyinaa no, na ɔman no kɔsu kɔm kyerɛ Farao. Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Misraim nyinaa sɛ: Monkɔ Yosef nkyɛn, deɛ ɔbɛka akyerɛ mo no, monyɛ.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɔm no baa asase no so nyinaa. Na Yosef buebuee aduanekora adan no nyinaa, na ɔtɔnee aburoo maa Misraimfoɔ no, na ɛkɔm no mu yɛɛ den Misraim asase so.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Na aman nyinaa baa Misraim bɛtɔɔ aduane wɔ Yosef nkyɛn, ɛfiri sɛ ɛkɔm no mu yɛɛ den wɔ asase no nyinaa so.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu sɛ aduane wɔ Misraim no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne mmammarima no sɛ: Adɛn na mohwehwɛ mo ho anim yi?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Monhwɛ, mate sɛ aduane wɔ Misraim. Monsiane nkɔ hɔ nkɔtɔ bi wɔ hɔ mmrɛ yɛn, na yɛntena ase, na yɛanwu.

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosef nuanom mu du siane kɔɔ Misraim aduanetɔ.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Na Yosef nua Benyamin deɛ, Yakob ansoma no anka ne nuanom no ho ankɔ, na ɔse: Ebia na mmusuo bi ato no.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no de wɔn ho fraa wɔn a wɔbaa aduanetɔ no mu, ɛfiri sɛ na ɛkɔm no aba Kanaan asase so bi.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne asase no so tumfoɔ, ɔne deɛ ɔtɔn aduane ma asase no sofoɔ nyinaa. Na Yosef nuanom ba bɛkotoo no de wɔn anim butubutuu fam.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef kaee daeɛ a ɔsosoo no wɔn ho no; na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moyɛ akwansrafoɔ, asase yi adagya na morebɛhwehwɛ.

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dabi, me wura, na aduanetɔ na wo nkoa baeɛ.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Yɛn nyinaa yɛ ɔbarima baako mma, yɛyɛ anokwafoɔ, wo nkoa nyɛ akwansrafoɔ.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Dabi, na asase yi adagya na moreba abɛhwehwɛ.

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔse: Wo nkoa yɛ anuanom dummienu. Yɛyɛ ɔbarima baako mma wɔ Kanaan asase so, na hwɛ, ɔkaakyire no wɔ yɛn agya nkyɛn nnɛ, na ɔbaako deɛ ɔnni hɔ.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Yei ho na mɛsɔ mo ahwɛ: Sɛ Farao te aseɛ yi, moremfiri ha nkɔ gye sɛ mo nua kumaa no ba ha ansa.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Monsoma mo mu baako, na ɔnkɔfa mo nua no mmra, na mo deɛ, mongu afiase na wɔnhwehwɛ mo nsɛm mu, sɛ nokorɛ wɔ mu a; anyɛ saa deɛ a, sɛ Farao te aseɛ yi, moyɛ akwansrafoɔ.

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Na ɔde wɔn kɔguu afiase mu nnansa.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monyɛ yei, na montena ase, na me deɛ, mesuro Onyankopɔn.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Sɛ moyɛ anokwafoɔ a, momma wɔnkyere mo nuanom yi mu baako ntena mo nnedua fie ha, na mo deɛ, ɛkɔm a ɛwɔ mo afie mu nti, monsoa aduane nkɔ.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Na momfa mo nua kumaa no mmrɛ me, na mo nsɛm ayɛ nokorɛ, na moanwu. Na wɔyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Na wɔsesee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ampa ara, yɛdi yɛn nua no ho fɔ, sɛ yɛhunuu n’ahohiahia, na ɔsrɛɛ yɛn mmɔborɔhunu, na yɛantie; enti na saa ɔhaw yi aba yɛn soɔ.

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Na Ruben buaa wɔn sɛ: Manka ankyerɛ mo sɛ: Monnyɛ abɔfra no bɔne biara, na moantie? Na hwɛ, ne mogya na wɔrehwehwɛ yi.

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Na wɔnnim sɛ Yosef te, ɛfiri sɛ ɔkyeame na ɔdi wɔn ntam yi wɔn ano.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Na ɔdanee ne ho firii wɔn nkyɛn kɔsui. Na ɔsane baa wɔn nkyɛn bio ne wɔn bɛkasae, na ɔyii Simeon wɔ wɔn mu, na ɔkyekyeree no wɔn anim hɔ ara. Yosef nuanom sane kɔ Kanaan

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosef hyɛɛ sɛ wɔmfa aburoo nhyehyɛ wɔn nkotokuo mama, na wɔnnane wɔn mu biara dwetɛ nhyɛ ne kotokuo mu, na wɔmma wɔn akwan so aduane. Na wɔyɛɛ wɔn saa.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Na wɔde wɔn aburoo no soasoaa wɔn mfunumu, na wɔfirii hɔ kɔe.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Na wɔn mu baako buee ne kotokuo ano sɛ ɔrema n’afunumu aduane wɔ asoɛeɛ no, ɔhunui, na hwɛ, na ne dwetɛ no hyɛ ne kotokuo ano.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Wɔadane me dwetɛ no ama me, na hwɛ, ɛhyɛ me kotokuo mu. Na wɔn akoma tutui, na wɔde ahopopoɔ sesee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na Onyankopɔn ayɛ yɛn yi?

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa wɔn agya Yakob nkyɛn Kanaan asase so, na wɔkaa deɛ ɛyɛɛ wɔn nyinaa kyerɛɛ no sɛ:

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: Ɔbarima a ɔyɛ asase no wura no poopoo n’ani kasa kyerɛɛ yɛn, na ɔbuu yɛn asase no so akwansrafoɔ.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Na yɛsee no sɛ: Yɛyɛ anokwafoɔ, yɛnyɛ akwansrafoɔ.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Yɛyɛ yɛn agya mma anuanom dummienu, ɔbaako na ɔnni hɔ, na akumaa no wɔ yɛn agya nkyɛn wɔ Kanaan asase so seesei.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima a ɔyɛ asase no wura no ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Yei na mede bɛhunu sɛ moyɛ anokwafoɔ: Monnya mo nua baako wɔ me nkyɛn, na momfa aduane nkɔ nkɔhwɛ mo afiafi,

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: na momfa mo nua kumaa no mmrɛ me, na mahunu sɛ monyɛ akwansrafoɔ, na moyɛ anokwafoɔ, na mayi mo nua no ama mo, na moadi asase yi so dwa.

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ wɔreyiyi wɔn nkotokuo mu adeɛ no, na hwɛ, wɔn mu biara dwetɛ boaa hyɛ ne kotokuo mu. Na wɔne wɔn agya hunuu wɔn dwetɛ mmoaa no, wɔsuroe.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Na wɔn agya Yakob ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moagye me nsam mma: Yosef nni hɔ, Simeon nni hɔ, na morebɛfa Benyamin nso akɔ. Me so na yei nyinaa ba!

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Na Ruben ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Sɛ mamfa no mansane mammrɛ wo a, kum me mmammarima baanu. Fa no hyɛ me nsa, na mede no bɛsane abrɛ wo.

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Me ba ne mo renkɔ, ɛfiri sɛ ne nua awu, na aka ɔno nko, na sɛ mmusuo bi kɔto no wɔ kwan a morekorɔ no mu a, ɛnneɛ mode me dwono bɛkɔ Asamando awerɛhoɔ mu.

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Na ɛkɔm no mu yɛɛ den wɔ asase no so.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Na wɔwiee aduane a wɔde firi Misraim baeɛ no die no, wɔn agya ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monsane nkɔtɔ aduane kakra mmrɛ yɛn.

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Na sɛ woremma no nkɔ a, ɛnneɛ yɛrensiane nkɔ hɔ, ɛfiri sɛ ɔbarima no ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Sɛ mo nua no nka mo ho a, monsi m’anim.

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Na Israel kaa sɛ: Adɛn nti na moyɛ me bɔne seyie, sɛ moka kyerɛɛ ɔbarima no sɛ mowɔ nua bie?

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Bisa na ɔbarima no bisaa yɛn, yɛn ne yɛn abusua ho asɛm sɛ: Mo agya da so te ase anaa? Mowɔ nua bi anaa? Deɛ ɔbisabisaeɛ yi ara na yɛbuaeɛ. Yɛbɛyɛ dɛn ahunu sɛ ɔbɛbisa yɛn sɛ: Momfa mo nua mmra?

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ n’agya Israel sɛ: Ma abɔfra no ne me nkɔ, na yɛnsim nkɔ, na yɛne wo ne yɛn mma atena ase, na yɛanwu.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Medi ne ho agyinamu; me nsam na hwehwɛ no. Sɛ mamfa no mammrɛ wo ammɛgyina w’anim a, ɛnneɛ mayɛ wo bɔne daa nyinaa.

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Na wɔn agya Israel ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ ɛte saa a, ɛnneɛ monyɛ yei: Momfa asase yi so nnepa ngu mo adeɛ mu, na momfa ayɛyɛdeɛ nkɔma ɔbarima no, akyenkyennuro kakra, ɛwoɔ kakra, ohwam, kurobo, nkateɛ ne sorɔno aba nkɔma ɔbarima no.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Na momfa dwetɛ foforɔ nkura, ne dwetɛ a wɔdane maa mo wɔ mo nkotokuo ano no, monkura nsane nkɔ; ebia ɛyɛ anifasoɔ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Na momfa mo nua no, na monsim nsane nkɔ ɔbarima no nkyɛn.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn mma ɔbarima no nhu mo mmɔbɔ, na ɔnnyaa mo nua no ne Benyamin mma mo. Na me deɛ, me mma firi me nsa a, na wɔafiri me nsa!

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Na mmarima no faa ayɛyɛdeɛ no, na wɔfaa dwetɛ mmɔho kurae ne Benyamin, na wɔsɔre siane kɔɔ Misraim kɔgyinaa Yosef anim.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef hunuu Benyamin sɛ ɔka wɔn ho no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne fie panin sɛ: Fa nnipa yi kɔ fie, na kum mmoa siesie yɛ aduane, na nnipa yi ne me rebɛdidi awia yi.

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Yosef kaeɛ no, na ɔde nnipa no kɔɔ Yosef fie.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na nnipa no suroo sɛ wɔde wɔn akɔ Yosef fie, na wɔkaa sɛ: Dwetɛ a ɛsane kekaa yɛn nkotokuo mu kane no nti na wɔde yɛn aba ha yi, na wabɛtoa yɛn ato ahyɛ yɛn so afa yɛn ne yɛn mfunumu ayɛ nkoa.

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Na wɔtwe pinii Yosef fie panin no ne no kasae wɔ efie no pono ano

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: sɛ: Owura, yɛpa wo kyɛw, yɛsiane baa ha kane bɛtɔɔ aduane.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Na yɛkɔduruu asoɛeɛ na yɛsanesanee yɛn nkotokuo ano no, na hwɛ, yɛn nyinaa dwetɛ hyehyɛ yɛn nkotokuo ano, yɛn dwetɛ sɛdeɛ wɔkariiɛ no pɛ, na yɛkura de asane aba.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Nso yɛkura dwetɛ foforɔ aba de rebɛtɔ aduane. Yɛnnim onii ko a ɔde yɛn dwetɛ no hyehyɛɛ yɛn nkotokuo no mu.

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Asomdwoeɛ nka mo, monnsuro. Mo Nyankopɔn ne mo agya Nyankopɔn ama mo mo nkotokuo mu ademudeɛ, mo dwetɛ no kaa me nsa. Na ɔyii Simeon brɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no de nnipa no hyɛnee Yosef fie, na ɔmaa wɔn nsuo hohoroo wɔn nan ho, na ɔmaa wɔn mfunumu aduane.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Na wɔsiesiee ayɛyɛdeɛ no twɛn ba a Yosef bɛba awigyina no, ɛfiri sɛ na wɔate sɛ wɔrebɛdidi hɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Na Yosef baa fie no, wɔde ayɛyɛdeɛ a wɔkura no kɔɔ ɛdan mu kɔmaa no, na wɔkotoo fam wɔ n’anim.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef bisaa wɔn sɛ wɔn ho yɛ anaa; na ɔse: Mo agya akɔkoraa a mokaa ne ho asɛm no ho yɛ anaa? Ɔda so te ase anaa?

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Na wɔse: W’akoa, yɛn agya no ho yɛ, ɔda so te ase. Na wɔbobɔɔ wɔn mu ase kotoo no.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n’ani so hunuu ne nua Benyamin, ne na ba no, ɔbisaa sɛ: Mo nua kumaa a mokaa me ne ho asɛm no ni anaa? Na ɔse: Onyankopɔn nnom wo, me ba.

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Na Yosef yɛɛ no ntɛm, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔnhunu deɛ ɔnyɛ wɔ ne nua no ho, na na ɔrehwehwɛ baabi akɔsu, na ɔhyɛnee ne pia mu kɔsuu wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhohoroo n’anim, na ɔfirii adi, na ɔhyɛɛ ne ho so kaa sɛ: Momfa aduane mmɛsisi hɔ.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Na wɔde ne deɛ sii fa, na wɔde wɔn deɛ sisii fa, na wɔde Misraimfoɔ a wɔne no redidie no deɛ sisii fa, ɛfiri sɛ Misraimfoɔ ne Hebrifoɔ ntumi nnidi, na Misraimfoɔ kyi.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛtenatenaa n’anim, ɔpanin sɛdeɛ ne panin teɛ, ne akumaa sɛdeɛ n’akumaa teɛ, na ɛyɛɛ nnipa no nyinaa nwanwa.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Na wɔgyegyee aduane no firii n’anim brɛɛ wɔn, na Benyamin deɛ boroo wɔn nyinaa deɛ so mprenum. Na wɔnonnomee, na wɔne no ani gyee.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: na fa me kuruwa, mekyerɛ dwetɛ kuruwa no, hyɛ akumaa no kotokuo ano ka n’aburoo dwetɛ no ho. Na ɔyɛɛ sɛdeɛ Yosef kaeɛ no.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Adeɛ kyeeɛ ara pɛ, na wɔgyaa mmarima no ne wɔn mfunumu kwan.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Wɔfirii kuro no mu kɔeɛ na wɔnnya nnuruu akyirikyiri no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne fie panin no sɛ: Sɔre, ti mmarima no, na sɛ woto wɔn a, ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Adɛn nti na mode bɔne tua papa ka?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɛnyɛ yei na me wura nom mu na ɔde yɛ ne nyankomadeɛ anaa? Deɛ moayɛ yi, moayɛ bɔne.

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔtoo wɔn no, ɔkaa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Adɛn nti na me wura ka saa nsɛm yi? Ɛmpare wo nkoa sɛ wɔbɛyɛ saa adeɛ yi.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Hwɛ, dwetɛ a yɛhunuu no yɛn nkotokuo ano no, yɛde asane afiri Kanaan asase so abrɛ wo; na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na yɛbɛwia wo wura fie dwetɛ anaa sika?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Wo nkoa yi mu deɛ wobɛhunu no ne nkyɛn no, ma no nwu, na yɛn nso yɛbɛyɛ me wura nkoa.

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ɛnyɛ sɛdeɛ moseɛ no. Na deɛ wɔbɛhunu no ne nkyɛn no nyɛ m’akoa, na mo deɛ, mobɛdi bem.

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔn nyinaa yɛɛ ntɛm soɛsoɛɛ wɔn nkotokuo totoo fam, na wɔsanesanee wɔn nkotokuo ano.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Na ɔhwehwɛe, ɔfirii aseɛ firi ɔpanin no deɛ so de kɔsii akumaa no deɛ so. Na wɔhunuu kuruwa no wɔ Benyamin kotokuo mu.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔsunsuanee wɔn ntadeɛ mu, na wɔde wɔn nnesoa soasoaa wɔn mfunumu sane kɔɔ kuro no mu.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Na Yuda ne ne nuanom baa Yosef fie, na ɔda so wɔ hɔ, na wɔhwehwee n’anim ase.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdeɛn adeɛ na moayɛ yi? Monnim sɛ onipa a ɔte sɛ me nim nkɔmhyɛ anaa?

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda kaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na yɛnse me wura? Na ɛdeɛn na yɛnka? Na yɛnyi yɛn ano sɛn? Onyankopɔn ahunu wo nkoa amumuyɛ. Hwɛ, yɛyɛ me wura nkoa, yɛne deɛ wɔhunuu ne nsam kuruwa no.

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ɛmpare me sɛ meyɛ saa. Na deɛ wɔhunuu kuruwa no wɔ ne nsa mu no, ɔno ara na ɔbɛyɛ m’akoa, na mo deɛ, monsim mfa asomdwoeɛ nkɔ mo agya nkyɛn. Yuda srɛ ma Benyamin

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yuda twe pinii no kaa sɛ: Me wura, mesrɛ wo, ma w’akoa nkasa me wura aso mu, na mma wo bo mmfu w’akoa, na wote sɛ Farao ara.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Me wura bisaa ne nkoa sɛ: Mowɔ agya anaa nua bi?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Na yɛka kyerɛɛ me wura sɛ: Yɛwɔ agya akɔkoraa ne ne nkɔkoraa ba kumaa bi. Ne nua awu, na ne na ba a aka ara ne no, na n’agya dɔ no.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Na woka kyerɛɛ wo nkoa sɛ: Momfa no mmrɛ me, na memfa m’ani menhwɛ no.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Na yɛsee me wura sɛ: Abɔfra no ntumi nnya n’agya hɔ, na sɛ ɔgya n’agya hɔ a, n’agya bɛwu.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Na wosee wo nkoa sɛ: Sɛ mo nua kumaa no anka mo ho amma a, monnsi m’anim bio.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Na yɛkɔɔ w’akoa, m’agya, nkyɛn no, yɛkaa me wura nsɛm no kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Na yɛn agya ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Monsane nkɔtɔ aduane kakra mmrɛ yɛn.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Na yɛse: Yɛrentumi nsiane nkɔ. Sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho a, yɛbɛsiane akɔ. Yɛrentumi nkɔ ɔbarima no anim, gye sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ɛnna w’akoa, yɛn agya, ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Mo ara monim sɛ mma baanu na me yere wo maa me.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Na ɔbaako firii me nkyɛn kɔe, na mese: Ampa ara teteɛ na wɔatete no mu, na ɛfiri hɔ no, menhunuu no.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mofa oyi nso firi me nkyɛn na mmusuo bi kɔto no a, mode me tiri dwono nam awerɛhoɔ mu na ɛbɛkɔ Asamando.

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Na afei sɛ mekɔ w’akoa, m’agya, nkyɛn na abɔfra yi nka yɛn ho a, — nso n’akoma da abɔfra yi ho, —

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Na w’akoa dii abɔfra yi ho agyinamu wɔ m’agya anim sɛ: Sɛ mamfa no mammrɛ wo a, ɛnneɛ na mayɛ m’agya bɔne daa nyinaa.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Na afei mesrɛ wo, ma w’akoa ntena ha nsi abɔfra no ananmu nyɛ me wura akoa, na ma abɔfra no ne ne nuanom nkɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Na sɛ abɔfra no nka me ho a, mɛkɔ m’agya anim sɛn? Ɛnneɛ na merekɔhunu bɔne a ɛbɛto m’agya no.

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Na afei na Yosef ntumi nhyɛ ne ho so wɔ wɔn a wɔgyinagyina ne ho no nyinaa anim, na ɔteaa mu sɛ: Momma nnipa nyinaa mfiri me ho mfiri adi. Na Yosef reyi ne ho adie akyerɛ ne nuanom no, na onipa biara nnyina ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa ne nne so sui, na Misraimfoɔ no ne Farao fiefoɔ tee.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Mene Yosef, m’agya da so te ase anaa? Na ne nuanom antumi ammua no, na mmom wɔn ho dwirii wɔn wɔ n’anim.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Montwe mpini me. Na wɔtwe pinii no. Na ɔse: Mene mo nua Yosef a motɔn no baa Misraim no.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Na afei mommma no nnyɛ mo ya, nso mo bo mmfu mo ho mo ho sɛ motɔn me baa ha, ɛfiri sɛ nkwagyeɛ nti na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Na mfeɛ mmienu ni a ɛkɔm aba asase yi soɔ, na aka mfeɛ nnum bio a funtum ne otwa nni mu.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim sɛ memma monnya nkaeɛ wɔ asase so, na mennye mo nkwa a ɛbɛma dodoɔ no ara afiri mu afire.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Na afei ɛnyɛ mo na mosomaa me baa ha, na mmom Onyankopɔn na ɔde me abɛyɛ sɛ Farao n’agya ne ne fie nyinaa wura ne Misraim asase nyinaa sodifoɔ.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Monyɛ ntɛm nkɔ m’agya nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wo ba Yosef seɛ nie: Onyankopɔn de me ayɛ Misraim nyinaa so wura. Siane bra me nkyɛn. Nkyɛ!

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na bɛtena Gosen asase so, na woabɛn me, wo ne wo mma ne wo nananom ne wo nnwan ne w’anantwie ne deɛ wowɔ nyinaa,

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: na mɛhwɛ wo wɔ hɔ, ɛfiri sɛ mfeɛ nnum kɔm da so reba, na ohia anhia wo ne wo fiefoɔ ne deɛ wowɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mo ani ahunu, na me nua Benyamin nso ani ahunu sɛ m’ano na mede mekasa mekyerɛ mo yi.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Na monka m’animuonyam a mewɔ wɔ Misraim nyinaa nkyerɛ m’agya ne deɛ moahunu nyinaa, na monyɛ ntɛm mfa m’agya nsiane mmra ha.

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsɔɔ ne nua Benyamin kɔn mu na ɔsuiɛ; na Benyamin nso sui wɔ ne kɔn ho.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔfefee ne nuanom nyinaa ano, na ɔsuu wɔ wɔn so, na ɛno akyiri no ne nuanom no ne no kasae.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Na wɔtee nka wɔ Farao fie sɛ: Yosef nuanom aba. Na ɛsɔɔ Farao ne ne nkoa ani.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Ka kyerɛ wo nuanom sɛ: Yei na monyɛ: Momfa nnoɔma nsoasoa mo mmoa no, na monkɔ Kanaan asase so

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: nkɔfa mo agya ne mo fiefoɔ mmra me nkyɛn, na mɛma mo Misraim asase so deɛ ɛyɛ, na moadi asase no sradeɛ.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Yei na monyɛ. Momfa nteaseɛnam mfiri Misraim asase so nkɔma mo mma ne mo yerenom, na monkɔfa mo agya mmra.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mo nso monnwennwene mo nnoɔma ho, na Misraim asase nyinaa so deɛ ɛyɛ yɛ mo dea.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no yɛɛ saa. Na Yosef maa wɔn nteaseɛnam sɛdeɛ Farao anomu asɛm seɛ, na ɔmaa wɔn akwansoduane.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ɔmaa wɔn nyinaa ntadeɛ nsakyeraho mmaako mmaako, na Benyamin deɛ, ɔmaa no nnwetɛbena ahasa ne ntadeɛ nsakyeraho nnum.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Na deɛ ɔde kɔmaa n’agya nso nie: Mfunumu du a wɔsoso Misraim nnepa no bie ne mfunumubereɛ du a wɔsoso aburoo ne paanoo ne akwansoduane a ɛbɛyɛ n’agya dea.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Na ɔgyaa ne nuanom kwan maa wɔkɔe. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo bo nnkɔfu mo ho mo ho wɔ ɔkwan so oo! Yakob ho sane no

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔfirii Misraim foro kɔɔ Kanaan asase so wɔn agya Yakob nkyɛn,

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yosef da so te ase, na ɔdi Misraim asase nyinaa so. Na ne tirim yɛɛ no naa, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔnnye wɔn nni.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Na wɔkaa nsɛm a Yosef aka akyerɛ wɔn no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no, na ɔhunuu nteaseɛnam a Yosef asoma de rebɛfa no no, wɔn agya Yakob ho sanee no.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Na Israel kaa sɛ: Ɛdɔɔso, me ba Yosef da so te ase. Mɛkɔ makɔhu no ansa na mawu.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Mfiase no Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Na asase da hɔ hunu a enni bɔbea biara na Onyankopɔn honhom butuw nsu no ani.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Ɛnyɛ hann! Na ɛyɛɛ hann.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu hann no sɛ eye. Na Onyankopɔn paee hann ne sum no mu.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ hann no sɛ: Adekyee, na esum no de, ɔfrɛɛ no adesae. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a edi kan nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Ntrɛwmu mmra nsu no ntam, na ɛmmɛpae nsu no mu.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ ntrɛw mu no ɔsoro. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so abien nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Nsu a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase no mmoaboa ano wɔ faako, na wonhu asase kesee. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ kesee no asase, na nsu mmoaano no, ɔfrɛɛ no ɛpo. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ asase mfifi nwura frɔmfrɔm, nhaban a ɛsow aba, nnua a ɛsow nnuaba sɛnea ne su te a n'aba wɔ mu, wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na asase fifii wura, nhaban a ɛsow aba sɛnea ne su te, ne nnua a ɛsow nnuaba a n'aba wɔ mu sɛnea ne su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so abiɛsa nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Akanea mmra ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu, na ɛmmɛpae awia ne anadwo mu, na ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne ne bere nkyekyem ne nna ne mfe;

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: na ɛnyɛ akanea wɔ ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu, na ɛnharan asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ akanea akɛse abien no, ɔkanea kɛse no, sɛ enni awia so, ne ɔkanea ketewa no, sɛ enni anadwo so, ne nsoromma nso.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn de sisii ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu sɛ ɛnharan asase so,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: na enni awia ne anadwo so, na ɛmpae hann ne esum no mu. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so anan nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Nsu no nnɔ abɔde a ɛte ase manyamanya, na ntakraboa ntu mfa asase so ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no ani.

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ nsuboa akɛse ne abɔde a ɛte ase a ɛkeka ne ho a ɛyɛ nsu mu manyamanya nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ɛne nnomaa a wɔwɔ ntaban nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔ, na monyɛ ɛpo mu nsu mu ma, na ntakraboa nnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so anum nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Asase mma abɔde a ɛtete ase mfi mmra, sɛnea wɔn su te; ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne asase so mmoadoma, sɛnea wɔn su te. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ asase so mmoadoma sɛnea wɔn su te, ne ntɔteboa sɛnea wɔn su te, ne mmoa a wɔwea fam nyinaa sɛnea wɔn su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Momma yɛnyɛ onipa wɔ yɛn suban so sɛ yɛn sɛso, na wonni ɛpo mu mpataa ne wim nnomaa ne ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa wɔ ne suban so, Yiw Onyankopɔn suban so na ɔbɔɔ no, ɔbarima ne ɔbea na ɔbɔɔ wɔn.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn, na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔre, na monyɛ asase so ma, na monni so tumi, na munni ɛpo mu mpataa ne wim nnomaa ne mmoa a wɔkeka wɔn ho wɔ asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne wim nnomaa nyinaa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa a ɔkra a ɛte ase wɔ wɔn mu no, mede nhaban momono mama wɔn sɛ wonni. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu nea ɔyɛe nyinaa, na hwɛ, eye papa. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so asia nen.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Na wowiee ɔsoro ne asase ne nea ɛwɔ mu nyinaa.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa da a ɛto so ason no, na ɔtew ho, efisɛ ɛno mu na Onyankopɔn home fii n'adwuma a ɔbɔe na ɔyɛe nyinaa ho. Adebɔ su: Eden turo

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: Na afuw mu nnua nyinaa nnya mmaa asase so, na afuw mu nhaban nyinaa nnya mfifii, efisɛ AWURADE Nyankopɔn nnya ntɔɔ osu nguu asase so ɛ, na onipa a ɔbɛdɔw asase nni hɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Na nsu fi asase so foroe, na ɛfɔw asase ani nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de fam dɔte nwenee onipa, na ohuw nkwa home guu ne hwene mu, na onipa yɛɛ ɔkra teasefo.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ turo bi wɔ Eden a ɛwɔ apuei fam, na ɔde onipa a ɔnwenee no, tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnua ahorow nyinaa a wɔhwɛ a, ɛyɛ fɛ, na eye sɛ wodi asase no so, ne nkwa dua a esi turo no mfinimfini, ne papa ne bɔne hu dua fifii asase so.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Na asu bi fi Eden bɛfɔw turo no, na efi hɔ ara na emu paepae yɛɛ nsuti anan.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Nea edi kan no din de Pison, ɛno na ɛkɔntɔn twa Hawila asase a sika wɔ so no nyinaa ho hyia;

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: na asase no so sika ye; ɛhɔ na bedola ne apopobibiribo wɔ.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na asu a ɛto so abien no din de Gihon, ɛno na ɛkɔntɔn twa Kus asase nyinaa ho hyia.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na asu a ɛto so abiɛsa ne Tigri, ɛno na ɛsen wɔ Asaria apuei. Na asu a ɛto so anan ne Eufrate.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de onipa no kɔtenaa Eden turom sɛ ɔnnɔw na ɔnwɛn hɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ onipa no sɛ: Turom ha nnua nyinaa, di bi.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Na papa ne bɔne hu dua no de, nni, efisɛ da a wubedi bi no, owu na wubewu.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kae sɛ: Enye sɛ onipa nko tena, mɛyɛ ne sɛso boafo mama no.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnahɔɔ tɔɔ onipa no so, na ɔdae, na oyii ne mfe pare mu biako, na ɔde nam tuaa anan mu.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de mfe pare a oyi fii onipa no mu no yɛɛ ɔbea, na ɔde no brɛɛ onipa no.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na onipa no kae sɛ: Ampa ara me nnompe mu dompe ne me honam mu nam ankasa ni. Oyi na wɔbɛfrɛ no ɔbea, efisɛ ɔbarima mu na woyii no fii.

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Ne saa nti na ɔbarima begyaw ne na ne n'agya, na ɔde ne ho akɔbata ne yere ho, na wɔayɛ ɔhonam koro.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu no deda adagyaw, ɔbarima no ne ne yere, na wɔn ani nwu.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ yɛ anifere kyɛn wuram mmoadoma a AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ wɔn nyinaa. Na obisaa ɔbea no sɛ: Ampa sɛ Nyankopɔn aka sɛ Munnni turom ha nnua nyinaa bi?

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Turom ha nnua aba no, yedi bi,

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: nanso dua a esi turo no mfinimfini no aba de, Onyankopɔn aka sɛ: Munnni bi, nso mommfa mo nsa nnka, na moanwu.

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no sɛ: Ɛnyɛ owu na mubewu:

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: na Onyankopɔn nim sɛ da a mubedi bi no, mo ani bebue, na moayɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn, ahu papa ne bɔne.

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no hui sɛ dua no ye sɛ wodi, na ɛyɛ aniwa fɛ, na dua no dɔ kɔn na ɛbɛtew ani no, ɔtew n'aba no bi, na odii, na ɔde bi maa ne kunu a ɔka ne ho no nso, na odii.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu ani buebuei, na wohui sɛ wɔdeda adagyaw, na wɔpompam borɔdɔma ahaban yɛɛ nkataanim fae.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Na wɔtee AWURADE Nyankopɔn nka sɛ ɔnam turom hɔ wɔ anwummere mfare mu. Na Adam no ne ne yere kohintaw fii AWURADE Nyankopɔn anim wɔ turom hɔ nnua mu.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn frɛɛ Adam, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wowɔ he?

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Na ose: Metee wo nka wɔ turom hɔ no, misuroe, efisɛ meda adagyaw, na mihintawee.

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Hena na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo sɛ woda adagyaw? Dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni bi no na woadi yi?

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Na Adam se: Ɔbea no a wode no bɛkaa me ho no, ɔno na ɔmaa me dua no aba bi na midii.

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woyɛɛ saa? Na ɔbea no se: Ɔwɔ no na ɔdaadaa me na midii.

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Sɛ woayɛ eyi nti, wɔadome wo ntɔteboa ne wuram mmoadoma nyinaa mu. Wo yafunu so na wobɛnantew, na woadi dɔte wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Na mede ɔtan mɛto wo ne ɔbea no ntam, ɛne w'asefo ne n'asefo ntam; ɔno na ɔbɛbɔ wo ti, na wo nso woaka ne nantin.

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ɔbea no de, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔdɔ na mɛma wo yaw ne wo nyinsɛn mu brɛ adɔɔso. Ɛyaw mu na wobɛwo mma, na w'ani begyina wo kunu, na ɔno na obedi wo so.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na Adam de, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ woatie wo yere nne, na woadi dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni no bi nti, wo nti wɔadome asase. Ɛyaw mu na wubedidi so, wo nkwa nna nyinaa,

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: na nsɔe ne nnɛnkyɛnse na ebefifi ama wo, na woadi afuw so ahaban.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: W'anim fifiri mu na wubedidi de akosi sɛ wobɛsan akɔ dɔte mu, efisɛ emu na woyii wo fii, na woyɛ dɔte, na dɔte mu na wobɛsan akɔ.

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Na Adam too ne yere din Hawa, efisɛ ɔno na wayɛ ateasefo nyinaa na.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ nhoma ntade maa Adam ne ne yere de hyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kae sɛ: Hwɛ, onipa no ayɛ sɛ yɛn mu biako ahu papa ne bɔne. Na afei, nea ɛbɛyɛ na wanteɛ ne nsa antew nkwa dua no nso bi anni antena ase daa nti,

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: AWURADE Nyankopɔn tuu no fii Eden turom hɔ sɛ ɔnkɔdɔw asase a wɔfaa no fii mu no.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Na ɔpam onipa no, na ɔde Kerubim ne gyaframa afoa a edi ahim besii Eden turo no anim apuei fam sɛ wɔnwɛn ɔkwan a ɛkɔ nkwa dua no ho no.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere Hawa hyiae, na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Kain, na ɔkae se: AWURADE adaworoma, manya ɔbarima.

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo ne nua Habel kaa ne ho. Na Habel yɛɛ oguanhwɛfo, na Kain de, ɔyɛɛ okuafo.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ɛbae sɛ nna bi akyi no, Kain de afum nneɛma bɛyɛɛ AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Na Habel nso de ne nguan mu mmakan ne wɔn a wɔadɔ no bi bɛmae. Na AWURADE ani sɔɔ Habel ne n'ayɛyɛde no,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: nanso Kain ne n'ayɛyɛde de, n'ani ansɔ. Na Kain bo fuwii pii, na omunae.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ ɛdɛn nti na wo bo afuw, na ɛdɛn nti na woamuna yi?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Sɛ woyɛ papa a, anka w'anim rentew anaa? Na sɛ woanyɛ papa nti, bɔne butuw ɔpon ano, na w'akyi kwan na ɛrehwehwɛ, nanso di no so.

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Na Kain ka kyerɛɛ ne nua Habel sɛ ɔmma wɔnkɔ afum, na ɛbae sɛ wɔwɔ afum no, Kain sɔre hyɛɛ ne nua Habel, na okum no.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Ɛhe na wo nua Habel wɔ? Na Kain buae sɛ: Minnim, me nua so hwɛfo ne me anaa?

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Ɛdɛn na woayɛ yi? Wo nua mogya nne teɛm frɛ me fi asase so.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Na afei wɔadome wo afi asase a abue n'ano agye wo nua mogya afi wo nsam no so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Sɛ wodɔw asase a, ɛrenkɔ so mma wo ne nnɔbae bio, wobɛbɔ asesa na waye ɔkobɔfo wɔ asase so.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, woapam me nnɛ afi asase so, na mehintaw mafi w'anim, na mayɛ ɔsesafo ne ɔkobɔfo wɔ asase so, na obiara a obehu me no, obekum me.

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛno nti obiara a obekum Kain no, wobedi ne were ahorow asɔn. Na AWURADE yɛɛ sɛnkyerɛnne bi maa Kain, na obiara a obehu no no ankum no.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Na Kain fii AWURADE anim kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Nod asase so wɔ Eden apuei. Kain Asefo

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Na Kain ne ne yere Hawa dae, na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Enok. Na ɔkyekyeree kurow bi, na ɔde ne ba Enok din too kurow no.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Na wɔwoo Irad maa Enok, na Irad woo Mehuyael, na Mehuyael woo Metusael, na Metusael woo Lamek. Lamek ne ne yerenom

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Na Sila nso woo Tubal-kain a ɔyɛ kɔbere mfrafrae ne dade ade nyinaa atomfo agya. Na Tubal-kain ne nuabea ne Naama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Na Lamek ka kyerɛɛ ne yerenom sɛ: Ada ne Sila, muntie me nne; Lamek yerenom, monyɛ aso mma m'asɛm: Mikum aberante bi sɛ opiraa me, na mikum aberante sɛ ɔboroo me.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wodi Kain so were mpɛn ason a, Lamek de bɛyɛ aduɔsɔn asɔn. Set ne Enos awo

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere dae bio, na ɔwoo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Set a ase ne: Nsiananmu, sɛ Onyankopɔn de ɔba foforo asi me Habel a Kain kum no no anan mu.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Set nso, wɔwoo ba maa no, na ɔtoo no din Enos. Ɛbere no mu na wofii ase bɔɔ AWURADE din sɔree no.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Adam nna a odii nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduasa, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Set nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne dumien, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Enos nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne anum, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Kenan nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne du, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Mahalaleel nna nyinaa si mfe ahanwɔtwe aduakron anum, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Yared nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduosia abien, na owui.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Na Enok ne Nyankopɔn nantewee; na wanhu no efisɛ Onyankopɔn faa no kɔe.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Metusela nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduosia akron, na owui.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: na ɔtoo no din Noa, na ɔkae sɛ: Oyi na ɔbɛkyekye yɛn werɛ wɔ yɛn nnwuma ne yɛn nsa ano brɛ mu wɔ asase a AWURADE adome no so.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Lamek nna nyinaa si mfirihyia ahansɔn aduɔsɔn asɔn, na owui.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn mma huu nnipa mmabea sɛ wɔn ho yɛ fɛ, na wɔwarewaree wɔn mu biara a wɔpɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Me honhom rentena onipa mu nkosi daa, efisɛ wɔyɛ ɔhonam, enti wɔn nna nyɛ mfe ɔha aduonu.

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Nna no mu na abran akɛse wɔ asase so, na akyiri yi nso a Onyankopɔn mma kɔɔ nnipa mmabea ho na wɔwoo mma maa wɔn no, eyinom ne abirempɔn a wɔwɔ din fi tete.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hui sɛ nnipa bɔne dɔɔso pii wɔ asase so, na wɔn komam adwene nyinaa yɛ bɔne nko daa nyinaa.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Mɛpopa nnipa a mabɔ wɔn no mafi asase ani, efi onipa so kosi ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne wim nnomaa so, efisɛ manu me ho sɛ meyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Na Noa de, onyaa ɔdom wɔ AWURADE anim. Noa adaka no

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Eyi ne Noa ho asɛm: Noa yɛ onipa trenee a ɔyɛ pɛ, wɔ ne bere so nnipa mu. Noa ne Onyankopɔn na ɛnantewee.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Na Noa woo mmabanin baasa, Sem, Ham ne Yafet.

english_verse: God knew that everyone was terribly cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu asase, na hwɛ, asɛe, efisɛ nnipa nyinaa asɛe wɔn akwan wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Fa ɔwawa yɛ adaka, na yɛ mpia wɔ adaka no mu, na fa ama tare emu ne ɛho.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Noa yɛɛ sa; sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no nyinaa pɛpɛɛpɛ, saa ara na ɔyɛe.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mede nsuyiri mɛba asase so mabɛsɛe abɔde a nkwa home wɔ mu nyinaa ɔsoro ase; asase so ade nyinaa rebewuwu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Na me ne wo bɛpam ato hɔ, na woakɔ adaka no mu, wo, ne wo mma, ne wo yere, ne wo mma yerenom.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nnomaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ne ntɔteboa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, wɔn nyinaa mu abien abien mmra wo nkyɛn, na wɔanya nkwa.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Na wo de, boaboa aduan a wodi nyinaa bi ano kɔ mu, na ayɛ wo ne wɔn aduan.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ: Wo ne wo fi nyinaa, monkɔ adaka no mu, efisɛ wo na mahu wo ɔtreneeni m'anim bere yi mu.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Mmoa a wɔn ho tew nyinaa mu, fa ason asɔn, anini ne abere. Na mmoa a wɔn ho ntew mu, fa abien abien, onini ne ɔbere;

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: wim nnomaa mu nso, ason asɔn, anini ne abere, na wɔn ase nnya nkwa asase nyinaa ani.

english_verse: Seven days from now I will send rain that will last for
translation_verse: Efisɛ aka ɛha nnansɔn na matɔ osu magu asase so adaduanan awia ne anadwo, na mapopa ade a nkwa wom nyinaa afi asase ani.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: abien abien ne Noa kɔɔ adaka no mu, onini ne ɔbere, sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ Noa no.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Na nnansɔn akyi no, nsuyiri baa asase so.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Na osu tɔɔ asase so pii adaduanan awia ne anadwo.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Saa da yi ara mu na Noa ne ne mma, Sem, Ham ne Yafet, ne Noa yere ne ne mma yerenom baasa kɔɔ adaka no mu,

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: wɔne Noa kɔɔ adaka no mu, ɔhonam a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa mu abien abien.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Na wɔn a ɛbae no, ɔhonam nyinaa mu anini ne abere na ɛbae, sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no, na AWURADE too no mu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nsu no boroo so kɔɔ soro basafa ason ne fa kataa mmepɔw so.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na abɔde a ɛkeka ne ho asase so nyinaa wuwui, nnomaa, ntɔteboa, wuram mmoa, mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa, ne nnipa nyinaa,

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na nsu no boroo so wɔ asase so nna ɔha aduonum.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaee Noa ne mmoadoma nyinaa ne ntɔteboa a wɔne no wɔ adaka no mu no nyinaa, na Onyankopɔn maa mframa bɔ faa asase so, na nsu no ano brɛɛ ase.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na ebun no nsu aniwa sisiwii, na ɔsoro mfɛnsere mu totoe, na osu a efi soro no gyaee tɔ.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na ɔsram a ɛto so asɔn, ɔsram no da a ɛto so dunsɔn na adaka no kɔtaa Ararat mmepɔw so.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Na nsu no kɔɔ so twee ara kosii ɔsram a ɛto so du no so. Na ɔsram a ɛto so du no da a edi kan no na mmepɔw atifi dedaa adi.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔsomaa kwaakwaadabi; na ofii adi, na odii akɔneaba de kosii sɛ nsu no yowee asase so.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa aborɔnoma fii ne nkyɛn sɛ ɔnkɔhwɛ sɛ nsu no ayow wɔ asase ani anaa.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Nanso aborɔnoma no annya ne nan sibea, na ɔsan baa ne nkyɛn adaka no mu, efisɛ nsu no da so wɔ asase nyinaa ani ara. Na ɔteɛɛ ne nsa faa no baa ne nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnansɔn bio, na ɔsomaa aborɔnoma fii adaka no mu bio.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Na aborɔnoma no baa ne nkyɛn anwummere, na hwɛ, ngodua ahaban frɔmfrɔm tua n'ano; na Noa hui sɛ nsu no ayow asase so.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnansɔn bio, na ɔsomaa aborɔnoma no; na wansan amma ne nkyɛn bio.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so aduonu ason no na asase so awo koraa.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ:

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: Fi adaka no mu, wo ne wo yere ne wo mma ne wo mma yerenom a wɔka wo ho;

english_verse: After Noah and his family had left the boat,
translation_verse: Na Noa ne ne mma ne ne yere ne ne mma yerenom fii adi;

english_verse: the living creatures left in groups of their own kind. The Lord's Promise for the Earth
translation_verse: mmoadoma nyinaa, wɔn a wɔwea nyinaa ne nnomaa nyinaa, nea ɛkeka ne ho asase so nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn mmoaban te, fi adaka no mu fii adi.

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na Noa sii afɔremuka maa AWURADE, na ɔfaa ntɔteboa a wɔn ho tew nyinaa mu bi ne nnomaa a wɔn ho tew nyinaa mu bi de wɔn bobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ muka no so. Onyankopɔn bɔhyɛ

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE tee afɔre no huam, na ɔkae ne komam sɛ: Onipa nti meremmɔ asase dua bio, efisɛ onipa komam adwene yɛ bɔne fi ne mmofraase, na merensɛe nea ɛte ase nyinaa bio, sɛnea mayɛ yi.

english_verse: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat; winter and summer, day and night.
translation_verse: Nna nyinaa a asase wɔ hɔ yi, ogu ne otwa, awɔw ne ahohuru, asusow ne ɔpɛ, awia ne anadwo rennyae da.

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa Noa ne ne mma, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ Monwo na monnɔɔso, na monhyɛ asase so ma.

english_verse: All animals, birds, reptiles, and fish will be afraid of you. I have placed them under your control,
translation_verse: Na mo ho hu ne mo ho suro mmra asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne wim nnomaa nyinaa, nea ɛwea fam nyinaa ne ɛpo mu mpataa nyinaa so; mo nsa na wɔde wɔn ahyɛ.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Nea ɛkeka ne ho a ɛwɔ nkwa nyinaa, ɛnyɛ mo aduan; mede ne nyinaa mama mo, sɛnea mede nhabanmono memaa mo no.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Nam a ne mogya wɔ ne mu nko na munnni.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na mo de, monwo na monnɔ, na monyɛ asase so manyamanya, na monnɔɔso wɔ so.

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa ne ne mma a wɔka ne ho no sɛ:

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: Na me nso, hwɛ, merema m'apam atim hɔ ama mo ne mo asefo a ebedi mo akyi,

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: Na mama me ne mo apam yi agyina hɔ, sɛ meremfa nsuyiri mensɛe abɔde nyinaa bio, na nsuyiri remma mmɛsɛe asase bio.

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Me nyankontɔn na mede masi omununkum mu, na ayɛ me ne asase ntam apam no ho sɛnkyerɛnne.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Na sɛ mede omununkum meba asase so a, wobehu nyankontɔn no wɔ omununkum no mu,

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: na makae m'apam a ɛwɔ me ne mo ne abɔde nyinaa mu ateasefo ntam no, na nsu annan nsuyiri ansɛe ɔhonam nyinaa bio.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Na nyankontɔn no bɛba omununkum mu, na mahwɛ, na mede makae daa apam a ɛwɔ Onyankopɔn ne abɔde a ɛwɔ asase so nyinaa ntam no.

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Noa mma a wofii adaka no mu fii adi no ne Sem ne Ham ne Yafet; na Ham ne Kanaan n'agya.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Noa mma baasa no. Wɔn mu na nnipa fi petee asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Na Noa fii ase yɛɛ kua, na ɔyɛɛ bobeturo.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔnom nsa no bi, na ɔbowee, na ɔda ne ntamadan mu a ne ho da hɔ.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Na Kanaan n'agya Ham kohuu n'agya adagyaw mu, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom baanu no wɔ adiwo.
