english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n'ani so huu ne nua Benyamin, ne na ba no, ɔkae sɛ: Mo nua kumaa a mokaa me ne ho asɛm no ni anaa? Na ose: Onyankopɔn nnom wo, me ba.

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Na Yosef yɛɛ no hare so, efisɛ ne yam hyehye no ma ne nua no, na ɔhwehwɛ baabi akosu, na ɔhyɛn ne pia mu kosui wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhohoroo n'anim, na ofii adi, na ɔhyɛɛ ne ho so kae sɛ: Momfa aduan mmesisi hɔ.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Na wɔde ne de sii fa, na wɔde wɔn de sisii fa, na wɔde Misraimfo a wɔne wɔn didi no de sisii fa, efisɛ Misraimfo ne Hebrifo ntumi nnidi, na Misraimfo kyi.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛtenatenaa n'anim, ɔpanyin sɛnea ne panyin te, ne akumaa sɛnea n'akumaa te, na ɛyɛɛ nnipa no nyinaa nwonwa.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Na wogyigyee aduan no fii n'anim brɛɛ wɔn, na Benyamin de boroo wɔn nyinaa de so mpɛn anum. Na wɔnonnomee, na wɔne no ani gyei.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ade kyee ara pɛ, na wogyaa mmarima no ne wɔn mfurum kwan.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Wofii kurow no mu kɔe na wonnya nnuu akyirikyiri no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne fie panyin no sɛ: Sɔre, tiw mmarima no, na sɛ woto wɔn a, ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ, ɛdɛn nti na mode bɔne tua papa ka?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɛnyɛ nea me wura nom mu, na ɔde yɛ n'anyankomade anaa? Nea moayɛ yi, moayɛ bɔne.

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔtoo wɔn no, ɔkaa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ ɛdɛn nti na me wura ka saa nsɛm yi? Ɛmpare wo nkoa sɛ wɔbɛyɛ saa ade yi.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Hwɛ, dwetɛ a yehui wɔ yɛn nkotoku mu no, yɛde asan afi Kanaan asase so abrɛ wo; na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na yebewia wo wura fi dwetɛ anaa sika?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Wo nkoa yi mu nea wubehu wɔ ne nkyɛn no, ma onwu, na yɛn nso yɛbɛyɛ me wura nkoa.

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Ɛnyɛ sɛnea muse no: nea wobehu wɔ ne nkyɛn no nyɛ m'akoa, na mo de, mubedi bem.

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔn nyinaa yɛɛ ntɛm soɛsoɛɛ wɔn nkotoku no totoo fam, na wɔsansan ano.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Na ɔhwehwɛɛ mu, ofii ase fi ɔpanyin de so de kosii akumaa de so; na wohuu kuruwa no wɔ Benyamin kotoku mu.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wosunsuanee wɔn ntade mu, na wɔde wɔn nnosoa soasoaa wɔn mfurum san kɔɔ kurow no mu.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Na Yuda ne ne nuanom baa Yosef fi, na ɔda so wɔ hɔ, na wɔkotowkotow n'anim.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Dɛn ade na moayɛ yi? Munnim sɛ onipa a ɔte sɛ me nim nkɔmhyɛ anaa?

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda se: Dɛn na yense me wura? Na dɛn na yɛnka? Na yenyi yɛn ano dɛn? Onyankopɔn ahu wo nkoa amumɔyɛ. Hwɛ, yɛyɛ me wura nkoa, yɛne nea wohuu kuruwa no wɔ ne nsam no.

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Na ose: Ɛmpare me sɛ mɛyɛ saa. Na nea wohuu kuruwa no wɔ ne nsam no, ɔno ara na ɔbɛyɛ m'akoa, na mo de, munsim mfa asomdwoe nkɔ mo agya nkyɛn. Yuda srɛ ma Benyamin

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yuda twiw bɛn no kae sɛ: Me wura, mesrɛ wo, ma w'akoa nkasa me wura asom, na mma wo bo mmfuw w'akoa, na wote sɛ, Farao ara.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Me wura bisaa ne nkoa sɛ: Mowɔ agya anaa onua bi?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Na yɛka kyerɛɛ me wura sɛ: Yɛwɔ agya akwakoraa ne ne nkwakoraa ba kumaa bi. Ne nua awu, na ne na ba a aka ara ne no, na n'agya dɔ no.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Na woka kyerɛɛ wo nkoa sɛ: Momfa no mmrɛ me, na memfa m'ani menhwɛ no.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Na yesee me wura sɛ: Abofra no ntumi nnyaw n'agya, na sɛ ogyaw n'agya a, n'agya bewu.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Na wusee wo nkoa sɛ: Sɛ mo nua kumaa no anka mo ho amma a, morenhu m'anim bio.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Na yɛkɔɔ w'akoa, m'agya nkyɛn no, yɛkaa me wura nsɛm no kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Na yɛn agya ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Monsan nkɔtɔ aduan kakra mmrɛ yɛn.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Na yese: Yɛrentumi nsian nkɔ. Sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho a, yebesian akɔ. Yɛrentumi nkohu ɔbarima no anim, gye sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ɛnna w'akoa, yɛn agya, ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Mo ara munim sɛ mma baanu na me yere wo maa me.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Na obiako fii me nkyɛn kɔe, na mise: Ampa ara ɔtetew na wɔatetew no mu, na efi hɔ no, minhuu no ɛ.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mofa oyi nso fi me nkyɛn na abew bi kɔbew no a, mode me ti dwen nam awerɛhow mu na ɛbɛkɔ asaman.

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Na afei sɛ mekɔ w'akoa, m'agya, nkyɛn na abofra yi nka yɛn ho a, esiane sɛ ne koma da abofra so nti,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Na w'akoa dii abofra yi ho agyinam wɔ m'agya anim sɛ: Sɛ mamfa no mammrɛ wo a, ɛnne na mayɛ m'agya bɔne daa nyinaa.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Na afei mesrɛ wo, ma w'akoa ntena ha nsi abofra no ananmu nyɛ me wura akoa, na ma abofra no ne ne nuanom nkɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Na sɛ abofra no nka me ho a, mɛkɔ m'agya anim dɛn? Ɛnne na merekohu bɔne a ɛbɛto m'agya no.

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Na afei Yosef ntumi nhyɛ ne ho so wɔ wɔn a wogyinagyina ne ho no nyinaa anim, na ɔteɛɛm sɛ: Momma nnipa nyinaa mfi me ho mfi adi. Na Yosef reyi ne ho adi akyerɛ ne nuanom no, na onipa biara nnyina ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa ne nne so sui, na Misraimfo no ne Farao fifo tee.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Mene Yosef, m'agya da so te ase anaa? Na ne nuanom no antumi ammua no, na mmom wɔn ho dwiriw wɔn wɔ n'anim.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Muntwiw mmɛn me. Na wotwiw bɛn no. Na ose: Mene mo nua Yosef a motɔn no baa Misraim no.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Na afei mommma ɛnnyɛ mo yaw, nso mo bo mmfuw mo ho mo ho sɛ motɔn me baa ha, efisɛ nkwagye nti na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Na mfe abien ni a ɔkɔm baa asase yi so, na aka mfe anum bio a ɔfɛtɛw ne otwa nni mu.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim sɛ memma munnya nkae wɔ asase so, na minnye mo nkwa a ɛbɛma dodow no ara afi mu afi.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Na afei ɛnyɛ mo na mosomaa me baa ha, na mmom Onyankopɔn na ɔde me abɛyɛ sɛ Farao n'agya ne ne fi nyinaa wura ne Misraim asase nyinaa sodifo.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Monyɛ ntɛm nkɔ m'agya nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wo ba Yosef se ni: Onyankopɔn de me ayɛ Misraim nyinaa so wura. Sian bra me nkyɛn. Nkyɛ!

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na bɛtena Gosen asase so, na woabɛn me, wo ne wo mma ne wo nenanom ne wo nguan ne w'anantwi ne nea wowɔ nyinaa,

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: na mɛhwɛ wo wɔ hɔ, efisɛ mfe anum kɔm da so reba, na ohia anhia wo ne wo fifo ne nea wowɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mo ani ahu na me nua Benyamin nso ani ahu, sɛ m'ano na mede mekasa mekyerɛ mo yi.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Na monka m'anuonyam a mewɔ wɔ Misraim nyinaa nkyerɛ m'agya ne nea moahu nyinaa, na monyɛ ntɛm mfa m'agya nsian mmra ha.

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Ɛnna osoo ne nua Benyamin kɔn mu na osui; na Benyamin nso sui wɔ ne kɔn ho.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ofifew ne nuanom nyinaa ano, na osui wɔ wɔn so, na ɛno akyi no ne nuanom no ne no kasae.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Na wɔtee nka wɔ Farao fi sɛ Yosef ne nuanom aba. Na ɛsɔɔ Farao ne ne nkoa ani.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Ka kyerɛ wo nuanom sɛ: Eyi na monyɛ: Momfa nneɛma nsoasoa mo mmoa no, na monkɔ Kanaan asase so

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: nkɔfa mo agya ne mo fifo mmra me nkyɛn, na mɛma mo Misraim asase so nea eye, na moadi asase no srade.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Eyi na monyɛ: Momfa nteaseɛnam mfi Misraim asase so nkɔma mo mma ne mo yerenom, na monkɔfa mo agya mmra.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mo nso munnnwinnwen mo nneɛma ho, na Misraim asase nyinaa so nea eye yɛ mo dea.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma yɛɛ sa. Na Yosef maa wɔn nteaseɛnam sɛnea Farao anom asɛm se, na ɔmaa wɔn akwansoduan.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ɔmaa wɔn nyinaa ntade nsakraho mmiako mmiako, na Benyamin de, ɔmaa no nnwetɛbona ahasa ne ntade nsakraho anum.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Na nea ɔde kɔmaa n'agya nso ni: Mfurum du a wɔsoso Misraim nnepa no bi ne mfurummere du a wɔsoso aburow ne abodoo ne aduan a ɛbɛyɛ n'agya akwansoduan.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Na ogyaa ne nuanom kwan ma wɔkɔe. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo bo nnkofuw mo ho mo ho wɔ ɔkwan so oo! Yakob ho san no

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ɛnna wofii Misraim foro kɔɔ Kanaan asase so wɔn agya Yakob nkyɛn,

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yosef da so te ase, na odi Misraim asase nyinaa so. Na ne komam yɛɛ no naa, efisɛ onnye wɔn nni.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Na wɔkaa nsɛm a Yosef aka akyerɛ wɔn no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no, na ohuu nteaseɛnam a Yosef asoma de rebɛfa no no, wɔn agya Yakob honhom ho san no.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Na Israel kae sɛ: Ɛdɔɔso, me ba Yosef da so te ase. Mɛkɔ makohu no ansa na mawu.

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Na Israel ne nea ɔwɔ nyinaa siim, na oduu Beer-seba, na ɔbɔɔ afɔre maa n'agya Isak Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nam anadwo anisoadehu mu ka kyerɛɛ Israel sɛ: Yakob, Yakob! Na ose: Mini.

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Na ose: Mene Onyankopɔn, w'agya Nyankopɔn no. Nsuro sɛ wubesian akɔ Misraim, na mɛyɛ wo ɔman kɛse wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Me ne wo besian akɔ Misraim, na mede wo masan maba nso, na Yosef abasa so na wobewu.

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Lea mmammarima a ɔwo maa Yakob wɔ Mesopotamia, ne ne babea Dina, ne mmammarima ne ne mmabea nyinaa si akra aduasa abiɛsa.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Farao bɛfrɛ mo, na obisa mo sɛ: Mo adwuma ne dɛn a,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Silpa a Laban de no maa ne babea Lea no mma a ɔwo maa Yakob, wosi akra dunsia.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Bilha a Laban de no maa ne ba Rahel no mma a ɔwo maa Yakob, akra no nyinaa si baasɔn.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Akra a wɔne Yakob kɔɔ Misraim a wofi n'asen mu, Yakob mma yerenom nka ho a, akra no nyinaa si aduosia asia.

english_verse: Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of
translation_verse: Na Yosef mma a wɔwoo wɔn Misraim no yɛ akra baanu. Yakob fi akra a wɔbaa Misraim no nyinaa si aduɔsɔn.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa Yuda dii n'anim kɔɔ Yosef nkyɛn sɛ ommedi n'anim nkyerɛ no Gosen kwan. Na woduu Gosen asase so.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Na Yosef siesiee ne nteaseɛnam kohyiaa n'agya Israel wɔ Gosen. Na ɔde ne ho kɔkyerɛɛ no no, osoo ne kɔn mu, na osui ara kyeree mu wɔ ne kɔn ho.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Afei a manya mahu w'anim sɛ woda so te ase yi, wɔmma mintiw me nenanom wɔ asamando.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom ne n'agya fifo sɛ: Merekɔ makɔka makyerɛ Farao sɛ: Me nuanom ne m'agya fifo a wɔwɔ Kanaan asase so no aba me nkyɛn.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na nnipa no yɛ nguanhwɛfo, na mmoa na wɔyɛn, na wɔde wɔn nguan ne wɔn anantwi ne nea wɔwɔ nyinaa aba.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: munse no sɛ: Wo nkoa yɛ mmoahwɛfo fi yɛn mmofraase de besi nnɛ, yɛn ne yɛn agyanom, na moatena Gosen asase so, efisɛ Misraimfo kyi mmoahwɛfo nyinaa.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Na Farao bisaa ne nuanom no sɛ: Mo adwuma ne dɛn? Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Wo nkoa yɛ mmoahwɛfo, yɛn ne yɛn agyanom nso.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Farao bio sɛ: Yɛaba sɛ yɛrebɛtena asase yi so, efisɛ wo nkoa nnya adidibea mma wɔn nguan, efisɛ ɔkɔm no mu yɛ den wɔ Kanaan asase so. Enti afei yɛsrɛ wo, ma wo nkoa ntena Gosen asase so.

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: W'agya ne wo nuanom aba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Misraim asase na ɛda w'anim yi, asase no mu nea eye no, ma w'agya ne wo nuanom ntena hɔ. Ma wɔntena Gosen asase so, na sɛ wunim sɛ wɔn mu bi yɛ nsiyɛfo a, fa wɔn si me mmoa a mewɔ so.

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Na Yosef de n'agya Yakob kogyinaa Farao anim. Na Yakob hyiraa Farao.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Na Farao bisaa Yakob sɛ: Wo nkwa mu mfirihyia si ahe?

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hyiraa Farao, na ofii Farao anim kɔe.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Na Yosef maa n'agya ne ne nuanom tenabea, na ɔmaa wɔn asase wɔ Misraim wɔ nea asase no ye, wɔ Rameses asase so, sɛnea Farao hyɛe no.

english_verse: Joseph also provided food for their families. A Famine in Egypt
translation_verse: Na Yosef bɔɔ n'agya ne ne nuanom ne n'agya fifo nyinaa akɔnhama sɛnea abusua biara dodow te.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Na aduan nni asase biara so, na ɔkɔm no mu yɛɛ den yiye maa Misraim asase ne Kanaan asase tɔɔ ɔkɔm no anim piti.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Na Yosef boaboaa sika a ɛwɔ Misraim asase ne Kanaan asase so nyinaa wɔ aburow a wɔbɛtɔe no mu, na Yosef de sika no kɔɔ Farao fi.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Na sika sae Misraimfo ne Kanaanfo ho asase so no, Misraimfo nyinaa baa Yosef nkyɛn sɛ: Ma yɛn aduan ɛ! Adɛn nti, na sɛ sika asa nti yenwuwu w'anim?

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef se: Momfa mo mmoa mmra na sɛ mo sika asa a, mɛma mo bi magye mo mmoa.

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Na afe no twaam no, afe a edi so no, wɔbaa ne nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛremfa nhintaw me wura sɛ yɛn sika asa, na mmoa akuwakuw no yɛ me wura dea, na biribiara nkae wɔ me wura anim sɛ yɛn honam ne yɛn asase nko.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛn nti na yɛn ne yɛn asase nwu w'anim? Tɔ yɛn ne yɛn asase, na ma yɛn aduan, na yɛde yɛn ho ne yɛn asase bɛsom Farao, na ma yɛn aduaba, na yɛntena ase, na yɛanwu amma asase yi anna mpan.

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Na Yosef tɔɔ Misraim asase nyinaa maa Farao, na Misraimfo nyinaa tontɔn wɔn mfuw, efisɛ ɔkɔm no den wɔn, na asase no dan Farao dea.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Gyee asɔfo asase nko na wantɔ, efisɛ Farao ahyɛ kyɛfa bi ama asɔfo no, na wodi wɔn kyɛfa a Farao de ma wɔn no nti, wɔantɔn wɔn asase.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ nkurɔfo no sɛ: Monhwɛ, nnɛ matɔ mo ne mo nsaase mama Farao, na hwɛ, mo aduaba a momfa nkodua asase no so ni.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Na nea ɛbɛsow no, momfa nkyɛm anum mu biako mma Farao, na emu abupɛn anan no nyɛ mo dea, na mode bi adua mo mfuw mu, na mode bi ayɛ mo ne mo fifo ne mo mma aduan.

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Na wose: Woagye yɛn nkwa; ma yennya me wura anim dom ara, na yɛbɛyɛ Farao nkoa.

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Na Yosef hyɛɛ eyi ho mmara wɔ Misraim a ɛwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ, sɛ wɔmfa Misraim asase so ade biara nkyɛm anum mu biako mma Farao, gye asɔfo asase nko na anyɛ Farao dea.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Na Israel tenaa Misraim asase a ɛwɔ Gosen no so, na wonyaa mu ade, wɔdɔe, na wɔn ase fɛee sɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Israel nna dui sɛ ɔbɛkɔ ne nsamankyi, na ɔfrɛɛ ne ba Yosef ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ manya w'anim dom a, fa wo nsa ka m'asen mu, na yɛ me adɔe di me nokware, na nsie me Misraim!

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Na mɛda m'agyanom nkyɛn, na soa me fi Misraim kosie me wɔ wɔn asiebea. Na Yosef kae se: Mɛyɛ sɛnea woaka yi.

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kae se: Ka me ntam. Na ɔkaa no ntam. Na Israel bɔɔ ne mu ase kyerɛɛ mpa no atifi.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na nsɛm yi akyi no, wɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, w'agya yare. Na ɔfaa ne mmammarima baanu, Manase ne Efraim, kaa ne ho.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Hwɛ, wo ba Yosef reba wo nkyɛn. Na Israel miaa n'ani tenaa ne mpa so.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn yii ne ho kyerɛɛ me wɔ Lus a ɛwɔ Kanaan asase so, na ohyiraa me,

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: na ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ, mɛma woadɔ, na mama woadɔɔso, mɛyɛ wo aman asafo, na mede asase yi mɛma w'asefo a wobedi w'akyi no sɛ daa agyapade.

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Na afei wo mma baanu a wɔwoo maa wo wɔ Misraim asase so ansa na mereba wo nkyɛn Misraim no, wɔnyɛ me dea. Efraim ne Manase nyɛ me dea sɛ: Ruben ne Simeon.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na wo mma a wubenya wɔn wɔ wɔn akyi no, na ɛnyɛ wo dea, na wɔde wɔn nuanom din bɛfrɛ wɔn wɔ wɔn agyapade mu.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Na me de, mifi Padan mebae no, Rahel wui m'anim wɔ Kanaan asase so wɔ ɔkwan mu, na aka ɔkwantiaa bi na wadu Efrat, na misiee no hɔ wɔ Efrat a ɛne Betlehem no kwan nkyɛn.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Mansusuw sɛ mehu w'anim, na hwɛ, Onyankopɔn ama mahu wo mma nso.

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Na Yosef yii wɔn fii ne nantam, na ɔponoo ne mu de n'anim butuw fam.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Na Yosef faa wɔn baanu nyinaa de ne nifa soo Efraim mu de no kyerɛɛ Israel benkum, de ne benkum soo Manase mu de no kyerɛɛ Israel nifa, na ɔde wɔn bɛn no.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Israel teɛɛ ne nifa too Efraim a ɔyɛ akumaa no atifi, ne ne benkum too Manase atifi, na ɔboapa na ɔyɛɛ ne nsa saa, efisɛ Manase ne abakan.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Na ohyiraa Yosef sɛ: Onyankopɔn a m'agyanom Abraham ne Isak nantew n'anim no, Onyankopɔn a wayɛn me me nkwa nna nyinaa de abesi nnɛ,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: abɔfo a woyii me bɔne nyinaa mu no nhyira mmofra yi, na wɔmfa me din ne m'agyanom Abraham ne Isak din mfrɛ wɔn, na wɔnnɔɔso nyɛ pii wɔ asase mfinimfini.

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Yosef hui sɛ n'agya de ne nsa nifa ato Efraim atifi no, anyɛ no dɛ, na osoo n'agya nsa sɛ onyi mfi Efraim atifi nkɔto Manase atifi.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ n'agya sɛ: M'agya, ɛnyɛ sɛ ɛte ne no, na oyi ne abakan, fa wo nifa to n'atifi.

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Na n'agya ampene na ose: Minim, me ba, minim; ɔno nso bɛyɛ ɔman, na ɔno nso adɔ, nanso ɛnyɛ dɛn ara a, ne nua kumaa no bɛso asen no, na n'asefo bɛyɛ aman pii.

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na ɛda no ohyiraa wɔn sɛ: Wo na Israel de wo behyira sɛ: Onyankopɔn nyɛ wo sɛ Efraim ne Manase. Na ɔde Efraim dii Manase kan.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, merewu, na Onyankopɔn bedi mo akyi, na ɔde mo asan akɔ mo agyanom asase so.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yakob frɛɛ ne mma se: Mommoaboa mo ho ano, na menka mo nea ɛbɛyɛ mo, nna a edi akyiri no mu.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: Yakob mma, munhyia, na muntie; muntie mo agya Israel!

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Ruben, m'abakan ne wo, m'ahoɔden ne me mmaninyɛ asefi. Wowɔ nidi a ɛkyɛn so, ne tumi a ɛkyɛn so.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Wuhinhim sɛ nsu, enti wo kanni befi wo nsa, efisɛ woforoo w'agya nnae. Ɛno mu na wuguu wo ho fi, me mpa na ɔforoe!

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon ne Lewi yɛ anuanom. Wɔn nkrante yɛ anuɔden akode.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Me kra, nnkɔ wɔn agyina mu, na m'anuonyam, nkɔfra wɔn asafo mu. Efisɛ wɔn abufuw mu na wokum nnipa, na wɔn ahupoo mu na wɔsɛee anantwi.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɔadome wɔn abufuw, sɛ ɛso dodo, ne wɔn anibere, sɛ emu yɛ den. Mɛkyekyɛ wɔn mu wɔ Yakob mu, na mabɔ wɔn mapete Israel mu.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Yuda, wo na wo nuanom beyi wo ayɛ; wo nsa bɛhyɛ w'atamfo kɔn so; w'agya mma bɛkotow w'anim.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Ogyata ba ne Yuda; hanam so na wode anyin, me ba. Ɔkotow, obutuw sɛ gyata ne gyatabere; hena na ɔbɛhwanyan no?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Ahempoma remfi Yuda nsa, na mmarahyɛ poma remfi n'anan ntam, kosi sɛ ɛsodifo a aman bɛyɛ osetie ama no no bɛba.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ɔsa n'afurum ba wɔ bobe mu, ne n'afurummere ba wɔ bobe pa mu. Ɔhoro n'atade wɔ nsa mu, ne ne ntama wɔ bobe aba mogya mu.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Bobesa bɛma n'ani ayɛ kɔɔ, na nufusu ama ne se ayɛ fitaa.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Sebulon tenabea bɛkyerɛ mpoano, na wahwɛ nea ahyɛn gyinagyina, na ɔne Sidon abɔ ɔhye.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isakar yɛ afurum hoɔdenfo, obutuw mmoaban ntam;

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: na ohu sɛ ɔhomebea no ye, na asase no yɛ fɛ, na ɔbrɛ ne mmati ase de gye adesoa, na ɔde ɔsom adwuma ayi tow.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan bebu ne nkurɔfo atɛn sɛ Israel mmusuakuw mu biara.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan bɛyɛ ɔkwan so wɔ, ɔtempɔn so ahurutoa. Ɔka ɔpɔnkɔ nantin, na ne so tenafo ahwe n'akyi.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: AWURADE, wo nkwagye na mehwɛ no kwan.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: Gad, asafo bi retoa no, na ɔno nso atoa wɔn aka wɔn nantin.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Aser aduan bɛyɛ sradeduan, na ɔbɛma ahennuan a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftali yɛ ɔforote a wɔato no sraha; ɔka adɛdɛsɛm.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Yosef yɛ dua a ɛsow aba baa, dua a ɛsow aba wɔ nsu aniwa so baa; n'abaa tratra ɔfasu.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Mmɛmmatofo hyɛɛ no yaw, wɔtotow no, na wɔtaa no.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Nanso na ne tadua kura no pintinn, na ne basa mu yɛɛ den. Efi Yakob tumfo no nsam, efi ɔhwɛfo a ɔyɛ Israel botan no mu.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Efi w'agya Nyankopɔn, ɔmmoa wo, na efi Tweaduampɔn hɔ, onhyira wo, ɔmfa ɔsorosoro nhyira, ne ebun a ɛtrɛtrɛw ase mu nhyira, ne nufu ne yafunu mu nhyira, nhyira wo.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: W'agya nhyira aboro m'agyanom nhyira so akodu tete nteredee nkoko no ahye so noho; ɛmmra Yosef atifi, nea woyii no fii ne nuanom mu no mpampam.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benyamin yɛ pataku a ɔtetew mmoa mu; odi hanam anɔpa, na anwummere nso ɔkyɛ asade mu.

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Eyinom nyinaa ne Israel mmusuakuw dumien no, na eyi ne nea wɔn agya ka kyerɛɛ wɔn de hyiraa wɔn. Sɛnea wɔn nhyira te mmiako mmiako na ohyiraa wɔn. Yakob wu ne ne sie

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Afuw no ne ɔbodan a ɛwɔ mu no, wɔtɔe wɔ Het mma nkyɛn.

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hyɛɛ ne mma samansew wiei no, ɔboaa ne nan ano guu mpa no so, na oguu ahome a edi akyiri, na otiw ne nananom wɔ asamando.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Na Yosef de n'anim kobutuw n'agya anim, na osu guu no so, na ofew n'ano.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Na nna a wɔde suu no no twaam no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ Farao fifo sɛ: Sɛ manya ɔdom wɔ mo anim a, munkoyi Farao asitiw sɛ:

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: M'agya ma mekaa no ntam sɛ: Hwɛ, merewu, na ɔda a mabɔ wɔ Kanaan asase so mafa no mu, ɛhɔ na kosie me. Enti ma menkɔ minkosie m'agya, na mensan memmra.

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kae se: Kɔ na kosie w'agya, sɛnea ɔma wokaa ntam no.

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Na woduu Atad awiporowbea a ɛwɔ Yordan agya no hɔ no, wotwaa kwadwom kɛse a emu yɛ den wɔ hɔ, na ogyam n'agya nnansɔn.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɛhɔfo, Kanaanfo no, huu osu a wosuu no Atad awiporowbea hɔ no, wɔkae sɛ: Eyi de, Misraimfo ayi a emu yɛ den ni. Enti wɔfrɛɛ hɔ sɛ: Abelmisraim ase ne: Misraimfo ayiyɛ, ɛwɔ Yordan agya noho.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Na ne mma yɛɛ no sɛnea ɔhyɛɛ wɔn no.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Na ne mma soaa no kɔɔ Kanaan asase so kosiee no wɔ: Makpela afuw so ɔbodan a ɛwɔ Mamre ntentenso a Abraham tɔɔ no wɔ Hetini Efron nkyɛn de yɛɛ asiei no mu.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Yosef siee n'agya wiei no, ɔne ne nuanom ne wɔn a wɔne no kɔe kosiee n'agya no nyinaa san baa Misraim. Yosef de ne nuanom mfomso kyɛ

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne nuanom hui sɛ wɔn agya awu no, wɔkae sɛ: Ebia Yosef bɛtan yɛn, na watua yɛn bɔne a yɛyɛɛ no nyinaa so ka.

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Na wɔma wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: W'agya hyɛe ansa na ɔrewu sɛ:

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: Monka nkyerɛ Yosef sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, fa wo nuanom amumɔyɛ ne wɔn bɔne kyɛ wɔn, efisɛ wɔayɛ wo bɔne. Na afei yɛsrɛ wo, fa w'agya Nyankopɔn nkoa amumɔyɛ no kyɛ wɔn. Na wɔkaa saa kyerɛɛ no no, Yosef sui.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom nso bae betwa hwee n'anim kae sɛ: Hwɛ, yɛyɛ wo nkoa.

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munnsuro, na migyina Onyankopɔn ananmu anaa?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Na mo de, mudwen me ho bɔne, nanso Onyankopɔn de, na ɔde rebɛyɛ papa, sɛ ɔbɛyɛ nea ada adi nnɛ yi, sɛ obegye nnipa pii nkwa.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Na afei munnsuro. Na mɛhwɛ mo ne mo mma. Na ɔkyekyee wɔn werɛ twaa wɔn bo tɔɔ wɔn yam.

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne n'agya fifo tenaa Misraim, na Yosef dii mfirihyia ɔha ne du.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Na Yosef huu Efraim mmanana. Manase ba Makir mma nso, wɔwoo wɔn guu Yosef srɛ so. Yosef wu

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Merebetiw nananom wɔ asamando, na Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo ampa, na wabeyi mo afi asase yi so akɔ asase a ɔkaa ho ntam kyerɛɛ Abraham ne Isak ne Yakob no so.

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef maa Israel mma kaa ntam, na ɔkae sɛ: Ampa ara Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo, na monsoa me nnompe mfi ha nkɔ.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne ne nuanom nyinaa ne wɔn bere sofo no nyinaa wuwui.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no wowoe, na wɔdɔe pii pa ara, na wɔn ase fɛee, na wɔn ho yɛɛ den papaapa; na wɔyɛɛ asase no so ma.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Na ɔhene foforo bi a onnim Yosef bedii Misraim so.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne man sɛ: Hwɛ, Israelfo no dɔɔso, na wɔn ho yɛ den sen yɛn.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Momma yɛmpɛ nyansa kwan bi mfa wɔn mfa so, na wɔannɔɔso, na sɛ ɔsa bi ba a, wɔankɔdɔm yɛn atamfo ne yɛn ammɛko, na wɔansɔre asase yi so ankɔ.

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Na wosisii wɔn so adwumayɛfo so mpanyimfo sɛ wɔmfa nnwuma a ɛyɛ den nhyɛ wɔn so. Na wɔkyekyeree adekora nkurow Pitom ne Rameses maa Farao.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Nanso dodow a wɔhyɛɛ wɔn so no, dodow ara na wɔdɔe, na wɔtrɛwee. Na Misraimfo suroo Israelfo no.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Na wɔde anyadi yawyaw dii Israelfo,

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: na wɔmaa wɔn asetena fonoo wɔn wɔ dɔte ne ntayaa ho adwuma den ne afum adwumayɛ ahorow nyinaa, ne nnwuma horow nyinaa mu nyadi yawyaw a wɔde dii wɔn mu.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Na Misraim hene ka kyerɛɛ Hebrifo awogyefo a wɔn mu biako din de Sifra, na obiako din de Pua no sɛ:

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: Sɛ mokogye Hebrifo mmea awo, na muhu agua no so sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbarima a, munkum no; na sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbea de a, momma ɔntena ase.

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Na awogyefo no suro Onyankopɔn, enti wɔanyɛ sɛnea Misraim hene ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na mmom wogyee mmammarima no nkwa.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Na Misraim hene frɛɛ awogyefo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na moyɛ saa, na moma mmarima no tena ase?

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Na awogyefo no ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Hebrifo mmea nte sɛ Misraimfo mmea, na wɔn de, wɔyɛ pirimpirim; awogyefo no nnya nnuu wɔn nkyɛn no, na wɔawo dedaw.

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Na esiane sɛ awogyefo no suro Onyankopɔn nti, ɔmaa wɔn afi mu yɛɛ yiye.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao hyɛɛ ne man nyinaa sɛ: Ɔbabanin biara a wɔbɛwo no no, monkɔtow no nkyene asubɔnten Nil mu, na mmabea nyinaa de, momma wɔntena hɔ.

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi a ofi Lewi fi kɔwaree Lewi babea bi.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo babarima; na ohui sɛ ne ho yɛ fɛ no, ɔde no siei asram abiɛsa.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na ontumi nkora no so bio no, ɔfaa mmɛw adaka bi de ama ne mannɔ sraa ho, na ɔde abofra no too mu, na ɔde kɔtoo wura mu wɔ asubɔnten no ano.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Na ne nuabea kogyinaa akyirikyiri sɛ ɔrehwɛ nea ɛbɛyɛ no.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Na Farao babea sian baa asu no ano aguare, na ne mmaawa repase asu no kɔn so; na ohuu adaka no wɔ wura no mu no, ɔsomaa n'abaawa sɛ ɔnkɔfa mmra.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Na obuee so no, ohuu akokoaa no, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ abarimaa a ɔresu. Na ɔyɛɛ no mmɔbɔ, na ose: Hebrifo mma no bi ni.

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ne nuabea no ka kyerɛɛ Farao babea no sɛ: So menkɔ menkɔfrɛ Hebrifo mmea no mu nufumafo bi memmrɛ wo, na ɔmmɛma akokoaa no nufu mma wo anaa?

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Na Farao babea no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ ɛ! Na ababaa no kɔe kɔfrɛɛ abofra no na ankasa bae.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Na Farao babea no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa abofra yi kɔ kɔma no nufu ma me, na metua wo ka. Na ɔbea no faa abofra no kɔmaa no nufu.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Na abofra no nyinii, na ɔde no kɔmaa Farao babea no, na ɔdan ne ba. Na ɔtoo no din Mose, efisɛ ose: Nsu mu na miyii no fii. Mose guan kɔ Midian

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Na Mose nyinii no, da bi ofii adi kɔɔ ne nuanom nkyɛn sɛ ɔrekɔhwɛ wɔn adwumayɛ no; na ohui sɛ Misraimni bi reboro ne nuanom mu bi a ɔyɛ Hebrini.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛɛ ha ne ha, na ohui sɛ obi nni hɔ no, ɔbɔɔ Misraimni no ade kum no, na ɔde no siee nwea mu.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, ofii adi, na hwɛ, Hebrifo baanu reko. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ nea odi fɔ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woboro wo yɔnko?

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Na ose: Hena na ɔde wo sii yɛn so otitiriw ne sennifo? Wopɛ sɛ wukum me sɛnea wukum Misraimni no anaa? Na Mose suroe, na ose: Asɛm no anya afi!

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Na Farao tee asɛm yi no, anka ɔhwehwɛ Mose akum no, nanso Mose guan fii Farao anim kɔtenaa Midian asase so. Na ɔkɔtenaa asubura bi so.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Nso Midian sɔfo wɔ mmabea baasɔn; na wɔbae bɛtow nsu de hyehyɛɛ adaase no amaama sɛ wɔrema wɔn agya nguan anom.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Na nguanhwɛfo bi bae bɛpam wɔn; na Mose sɔre boaa wɔn, na ɔmaa wɔn nguan no nomee.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa wɔn agya Reuel nkyɛn no, ɔkae sɛ: Ɛyɛɛ dɛn na nnɛ de, moaba ntɛm sɛɛ?

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Na wose: Misraimni bi na oyii yɛn fii nguanhwɛfo no nsam, na ɔtow nsu po maa yɛn, na ɔmaa nguan no nomee.

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne mmabea no sɛ: Na ɔwɔ he? Ɛdɛn nti na mugyaw ɔbarima no? Monkɔfrɛ no na ommedidi.

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Na Mose penee sɛ ɔne ɔbarima no bɛtena. Na ɔde ne babea Sipora maa Mose aware.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo babanin, na Mose too no din Gersom, ase ne: Baabi hɔho, efisɛ ose: Mayɛ ɔhɔho wɔ ananafo asase so.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Na nna dodow yi mu no ɛbae sɛ Misraim hene wui. Na ɔsom no nti Israelfo no sii apini, na wosu frɛe, na wɔn som no mu sufrɛ no koduu Onyankopɔn anim.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tee wɔn apinisi no, na Onyankopɔn kaee n'apam a ɔne Abraham ne Isak ne Yakob pamee no.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hwɛɛ Israelfo no, na Onyankopɔn huu wɔn tebea a wɔwɔ mu no.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Bere bi a Mose rehwɛ n'ase Yetro, Midian sɔfo no, nguan, na ɔkaa wɔn de wɔn kɔɔ sare no akyi noho, na oduu Onyankopɔn bepɔw Horeb ho.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo beyii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ no wɔ nkyɛkyerɛ bi mfinimfini gyaframa mu, na ɔhwɛe, na hwɛ, nkyɛkyerɛ no redɛw, nanso nkyɛkyerɛ no nhyew.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Na Mose se: Eyi de, mɛman makɔhwɛ ahwɛde kɛse yi, dekode a enti nkyɛkyerɛ no nhyew.

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hui sɛ waman rehwɛ no, Onyankopɔn fi nkyɛkyerɛ no mu frɛe sɛ: Mose, Mose! Na ose: Mini!

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE kae sɛ: Ntwiw mmɛn ha! Yi wo nan ase mpaboa, na nea wugyinae hɔ yɛ asase kronkron.

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae bio sɛ: Mene w'agya Nyankopɔn no, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no. Ɛnna Mose kataa n'ani, efisɛ osuro sɛ ɔbɛhwɛ Onyankopɔn.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Ohu na mahu me man a ɛwɔ Misraim no amanehunu, na wɔn su a wɔn so ahwɛfo nti wosu frɛ no mate.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na masian sɛ merebeyi wɔn Misraimfo nsam, na matutu wɔn afi asase no so akɔ asase pa a ɛtrɛw so, asase a nufusu ne wo sen wɔ so: Kanaanfo, Hetifo, Amorifo, Perisifo, Hewifo, Yebusifo tenabea hɔ.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, Israelfo no sufrɛ adu m'anim, na mahu ɔhaw a Misraimfo de haw wɔn no.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Na afei bra na mensoma wo Farao nkyɛn, na koyi me man Israelfo no fi Misraim.

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ: Hena ne me a merekɔ Farao nkyɛn makoyi Israelfo afi Misraim?

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Medi w'akyi; na eyi bɛyɛ wo sɛnkyerɛnne sɛ me na mesomaa wo: wunya yi ɔman no fi Misraim ba a, mobɛsom Nyankopɔn wɔ bepɔw yi so.

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ: Na sɛ midu Israelfo nkyɛn, na meka mekyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo agyanom Nyankopɔn na asoma me mo nkyɛn, na wɔka kyerɛ me sɛ: Ne din de dɛn a, dɛn na minse wɔn?

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Mose bio sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Israel mma sɛ: AWURADE, mo agyanom Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn na wasoma me mo nkyɛn yi, eyi ne me din de kosi daa, na eyi na wɔmfa nkae me awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɔ na kɔboa Israel mpanyimfo ano, na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE, mo nananom Nyankopɔn, Abraham, Isak ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no ayi ne ho akyerɛ me sɛ: Ɔhwɛ na mabɛhwɛ mo ne nea wɔreyɛ mo wɔ Misraim no.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na mise: Meyi mo afi Misraim amanehunu no mu akɔ Kanaanfo, Hetifo, Amorifo, Perisifo, Hewifo ne Yebusifo asase so, asase a nufusu ne wo sen wɔ so no.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Na wobetie wo nne, na wo ne Israel mpanyimfo nkɔ Misraim hene nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: AWURADE, Hebrifo Nyankopɔn, abehyia yɛn, enti yɛsrɛ wo, ma yɛnkɔ sare so nnansa kwan nkɔbɔ AWURADE, yɛn Nyankopɔn, afɔre.

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Na me de, minim sɛ wɔde nsa a ɛyɛ den hyɛ Misraim hene mpo a, ɔremma mo kwan nkɔ.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Enti mɛteɛ me nsa de m'anwonwade a mɛyɛ wɔ hɔ no nyinaa mabobɔ Misraim, na ɛno akyi na ɔbɛma moakɔ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mmea mmisabisa wɔn afipamfo ne wɔn afitenafo nkyɛn dwetɛ nnwinne ne sika nnwinne ne ntama, na momfa nhyehyɛ mo mmammarima ne mo mmabea, na Misraimfo nneɛma no nyɛ mo asade.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Na Mose buaa AWURADE sɛ: Na sɛ wɔannye me anni, na wɔantie me nne, na wɔka sɛ: AWURADE nyii ne ho adi nkyerɛɛ wo ɛ!

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dɛn na ekura wo nsam yi?

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Na ose: Poma. Na ose: Tow kyene fam! Na ɔtow kyenee fam, na ɛdan ɔwɔ. Na Mose guan fii ho.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Teɛ wo nsa na so ne dua mu. Na ɔteɛɛ ne nsa kyeree no, na ɛdan poma wɔ ne nsam.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Nea ɛbɛyɛ na wɔagye adi sɛ Awurade, wɔn agyanom Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no, ayi ne ho akyerɛ wo nen.

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no bio sɛ: Fa wo nsa hyɛ wo kokom! Na ɔde ne nsa hyɛɛ ne kokom, na oyii, na hwɛ, ɛho agu kwata fitaa sɛ sukyerɛma.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Na ose: Fa wo nsa san hyɛ wo kokom! Na ɔsan de ne nsa hyɛɛ ne kokom, na oyi fii ne kokom, na hwɛ, adan sɛ ne honam ara.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔannye nsɛnkyerɛnne abien yi nso anni na wɔantie wo nne a, ɛnne kɔsaw asubɔnten no mu nsu kohwie gu asase kesee so, na nsu a wosawee, asu no mu no bɛdan mogya wɔ asase kesee no so.

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, AWURADE! Me de, ɛde besi nnɛ anaa efi bere a wo ne w'akoa kasae yi, m'ano ntew; me kasa yɛ nyaa na me tɛkrɛma nso yɛ duru.

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hena na ɔyɛɛ onipa ano? Anaasɛ hena na ɔyɛ mum anaa ɔsotifo, anaa ɔdehufo anaa onifuraefo? Ɛnyɛ me AWURADE ara?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Na afei kɔ, na me ara medi w'ano akyi na makyerɛ wo nea ka.

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, AWURADE! Soma onipa foforo biara a wopɛ.

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE bo fuw Mose, na ose: So minnim sɛ wo nua Aaron, Lewini no, nim kasa? Na hwɛ, wafi adi rebehyia wo, na sɛ ohu wo a, ne koma bɛtɔ ne yam.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Na poma yi a wode bɛyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne no, fa kura wo nsam. Mose san kɔ Misraim

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kɔe, na ɔsan kɔɔ n'ase Yetro nkyɛn, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma mensan menkɔ me nuanom a wɔwɔ Misraim no nkyɛn menkɔhwɛ sɛ wɔda so tete ase anaa. Na Yetro ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa asomdwoe kɔ.

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose wɔ Midian sɛ: San kɔ Misraim, efisɛ nnipa a wɔhwehwɛ wo akum wo no nyinaa awuwu.

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Na Mose faa ne yere ne ne mma de wɔn tenatenaa mfurum so, na ɔsan baa Misraim asase so. Na Mose faa Onyankopɔn poma no kurae.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sɛ wosan kɔ Misraim a, hwɛ na yɛ anwonwade a mede mahyɛ wo nsa no nyinaa Farao anim; na me de, mepirim ne koma, na ɔremma ɔman no nkɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Na ka kyerɛ Farao sɛ: Sɛnea AWURADE se ni: M'abakan ne Israel.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Na mise wo sɛ: Ma me ba nkɔ nkɔsom me. Na sɛ woampene amma wankɔ a, hwɛ, me de, mekum w'abakan.

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɛtoaa no ɔkwan so, asoɛe a wɔdaa hɔ no, pɛe sɛ okum no.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sipora faa twɛrebo de twaa ne ba no twetia, na ɔtow kyenee ne nan ase kae sɛ: Woyɛ mogya ayeforokunu ma me!

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ɛnna ogyaa no. Ɛnna twetiatwa no nti ɔkae sɛ: Mogya ayeforokunu ne wo.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Kɔ sare so kohyia Mose. Na ɔkɔe kɔtoo no wɔ Onyankopɔn bepɔw no ho, na ofew n'ano.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa AWURADE nsɛm a ɔde asoma no no nyinaa ne nsɛnkyerɛnne a ɔde ahyɛ ne nsa no nyinaa kyerɛɛ Aaron.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔ kɔboaboaa Israelfo mpanyimfo nyinaa ano.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Na Aaron kaa nsɛm a AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose no nyinaa kyerɛɛ wɔn, na ɔyɛɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne no wɔ ɔman no anim.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no gye dii. Na wɔtee sɛ AWURADE abɛhwɛ Israelfo na wahu wɔn amanehunu no, wɔbobɔɔ wɔn mu ase sɔree.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Na ɛyɛe no, Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, se ni: Ma me man nkɔ na wɔnkɔhyɛ fa mma me wɔ sare so.

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Na Farao se: Hena ne AWURADE a metie ne nne na mama Israel akɔ? Minnim AWURADE no, na Israel nso, meremma wɔnkɔ.

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Na wose: Hebrifo Nyankopɔn abehyia yɛn; enti ma yɛnkɔ sare so nnansa kwan, na yɛnkɔbɔ Awurade, yɛn Nyankopɔn, afɔre, na wamfa owuyare anaa nkrante ammetoa yɛn.

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Na Farao se: Monhwɛ, afei nnipa no adɔɔso wɔ asase no so, na morepɔn wɔn afi wɔn adwumayɛ mu yi!

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Na da no ara Farao hyɛɛ ɔman no adwumayɛ so ahwɛfo ne wɔn aboafo sɛ:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: Mommma ɔman no sare a wɔde yɛ ntayaa no bio sɛ kan no; wɔn ankasa nkɔpɛ sare no.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Na ntayaa dodow a wɔyɛ daa no, munnye wɔn, munnyi so bi, efisɛ wɔyɛ anihawfo, enti na wosu sɛ: Ma yɛnkɔ nkɔbɔ yɛn Nyankopɔn afɔre no.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Momma wɔn adwuma a emu yɛ duru, na wɔnyɛ, na wɔantie nsɛnhunu.

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no adwumayɛ so ahwɛfo ne wɔn aboafo no bae bɛka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Sɛ Farao se ni: Meremma mo sare bio.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Mo ara monkɔ nkɔpɛ sare wɔ nea mubenya; na mo adwuma no nso, wɔrentew so hwee.

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no bɔ petee Misraim asase nyinaa so kɔboaboaa awi ntwakae ano de yɛɛ sare mesemese no.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Na adwumayɛ so ahwɛfo no piapiaa wɔn kae sɛ: Munwie mo da koro adwuma wɔ ne bere mu, sɛ bere a sare wɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Na wɔhwee Israelfo ahwɛfo a Farao adwumayɛ so ahwɛfo no de asisi wɔn so no kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na moanwie ntayaa a wɔahyɛ mo no nnɛ ne nnɛra nyinaa, sɛ kan no?

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israelfo ahwɛfo no bae besu kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo ne wo nkoa di no saa?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Wɔmmaa wo nkoa sare bi ɛ, nso wose yɛnyɛ ntayaa; na hwɛ, wɔhwe wo nkoa, nso ɛyɛ wo ara wo nkurɔfo no mfomso.

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Na ose: Anihawfo, anihawfo na moyɛ. Enti na moka sɛ: Ma yɛnkɔ nkɔbɔ AWURADE afɔre.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Enti monkɔ nkɔyɛ adwuma, na sare de, wɔremma mo, nso ntayaa no dodow de, mobɛma ara.

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Munnyi mo da koro adwuma mu ntayaa no so ara da, no, Israelfo adwumayɛ so ahwɛfo no hui sɛ amane na ato wɔn.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Na wofi Farao nkyɛn reba no, wɔbɛtoo Mose ne Aaron a wogyina hɔ rebehyia wɔn,

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE nhwɛ mo mmu atɛn sɛ moama yɛn ho abɔn wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim, na mode nkrante ahyɛ wɔn nsa sɛ wɔmfa nkum yɛn. Mose kasa kyerɛ AWURADE

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Na Mose san baa AWURADE nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: AWURADE, adɛn na woayɛ ɔman yi bɔne sɛɛ? Adɛn na wosomaa me yi?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Na efi bere a mebaa Farao nkyɛn na mede wo din me ne no kasae no, wayɛ ɔman yi bɔne, na wo nso wunnyee wo man ɛ!

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Afei ansa na worebehu nea mɛyɛ Farao, efisɛ wɔde nsa a ɛyɛ den bɛma wama wɔakɔ, na wɔde nsa a ɛyɛ den bɛma wapam wɔn afi n'asase so mpo.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: na miyii me ho mekyerɛɛ Abraham, Isak ne Yakob sɛ Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn, na me din YHWH no de, mamma wɔamfa anhu me.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Nanso mama m'apam a me ne wɔn pamee no agyina, sɛ mede Kanaan asase a ɛyɛ wɔn ahɔhobea asase a wɔyɛɛ so ahɔho no mɛma wɔn.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Nanso mate Israelfo a Misraimfo di wɔn nya no apinisi, na makae m'apam no.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Ɛno nti ka kyerɛ Israelfo sɛ: Mene AWURADE, na megye mo afi Misraim nkoasom no ase, na mayi mo mafi wɔn anyadi no mu, na mede basa a ateɛ ne atemmu akɛse magye mo.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na mɛfa mo mayɛ me man, na mayɛ mo Onyankopɔn, na moahu sɛ mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn a ogyee mo fii Misraim nkoasom ase no.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na mede mo mɛkɔ asase a mekaa ntam sɛ mede mɛma Abraham, Isak ne Yakob no so, na mede mɛma mo sɛ agyapade. Mene Awurade.

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa saa kyerɛɛ Israelfo no; nanso ahometew ne nkoasom dennen no nti wɔantie Mose.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: Kɔ na kɔka kyerɛ Misraim hene Farao sɛ ɔmma Israelfo mfi n'asase so nkɔ.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Awurade sɛ: Hwɛ, Israelfo no ntie me, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na Farao betie me a meyɛ ano mu momonoto yi.

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
