translation_verse: Na AWURADE ne Mose ne Aaron kasae, na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnkɔ Israelfo ne Misraim hene Farao nkyɛn nkoyi Israelfo no mfi Misraim asase so.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne wɔn agyanom afi mu atitiriw: Israel abakan Ruben mma ne: Hanok ne Palu, Hesron ne Karmi; eyinom ne Ruben mmusua.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Na Simeon mma ne: Yemuel ne Yamin ne Ohad ne Yakin ne Sohar ne Saul a ɔyɛ Kanaanni bea bi ba; eyinom ne Simeon mmusua.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gerson mma ne: Libni ne Simei wɔ wɔn mmusua horow mu:

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Merari mma ne Mahli ne Musi. Eyinom ne Lewi mmusua, sɛnea wɔn awo ntoatoaso te.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Na Ishar mma ne: Kora ne Nefeg ne Sikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Na Usiel mma ne: Misael ne Elsafan ne Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Na Aaron faa Aminadab babea Eliseba a ɔyɛ Nahson ne nua waree, na ɔwoo Nadab, Abihu, Eleasar ne Itamar maa no.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Na Kora mma ne: Asir, Elkana ne Abiasaf; eyinom ne Kora mma mmusua.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Aaron ba Eleasar faa Putiel mma mu bi waree, na ɔwoo Pinehas maa no. Eyinom ne Lewifo agyanom atitiriw sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Aaron ne Mose a Awurade ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munyi Israelfo mfi Misraim asase so sɛ wɔn dɔm te no.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Wɔne wɔn a wɔne Misraim hene Farao kasae sɛ wobeyi Israelfo afi Misraim akɔ no, Mose ne Aaron no ni.

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na da a AWURADE ne Mose kasae Misraim asase so no,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mene Awurade, ka nea mɛka makyerɛ wo nyinaa kyerɛ Misraim hene Farao.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Hwɛ, ano mu momonoto ne me, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na Farao betie me?

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, madan wo Onyankopɔn mama Farao, na wo nua Aaron bɛyɛ wo diyifo.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Wo de, wobɛka nea mɛhyɛ wo nyinaa, na wo nua Aaron bɛka akyerɛ Farao sɛ ɔmma Israelfo mfi n'asase so nkɔ.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Nanso Farao rentie mo; na mede me nsa mɛto Misraim so, na mayi m'asafo, me man Israelfo no, mafi Misraim asase so wɔ atemmu akɛse mu.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ meteɛ me nsa wɔ Misraim so na miyi Israelfo mifi wɔn mu a, na Misraimfo behu sɛ mene AWURADE.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ wɔn no ara.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: Sɛ Farao ka kyerɛ mo sɛ monyɛ anwonwade bi a, ɛno de ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma to fam wɔ Farao anim, na ɛbɛdan ɔtweaseɛ.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔyɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ wɔn no; na Aaron de ne poma no too fam wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim, na ɛdan ɔtweaseɛ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Na Farao nso frɛfrɛɛ anyansafo ne ntafowayifo bae. Na wɔn Misraim akɔmfo no nso de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nyinaa de wɔn mpoma totoo fam, na ɛdannan atweaseɛ, nanso Aaron poma no memmenee wɔn mpoma no.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Na Farao koma pirimii ara, na wantie wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE kae no. Ɔhaw ahorow ba Misraim

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Farao koma yɛ den, ɔmpene sɛ ɔman no bɛkɔ.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn anɔpa; hwɛ, ɔrefi adi akɔ asu no ano; na kogyina asu no ano hyia no, na fa wo poma a ɛdan ɔwɔ no kura.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: AWURADE, Hebrifo Nyankopɔn na wasoma me wo nkyɛn sɛ: Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me sare so, na hwɛ, wuntiei de abedu sesɛɛ.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Eyi na wode behu sɛ mene AWURADE: Hwɛ, mede poma a mikurae yi merebɔ asu yi mu nsu mu, na ɛbɛdan mogya.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Na mpataa a ɛwɔ asu no mu bewuwu, na nsu no bɛbɔn na Misraimfo bekyi sɛ wɔbɛnom asu no mu nsu.

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma, na teɛ wo nsa wɔ Misraim nsu so, wɔn nsubɔnten so, wɔn asuasu so ne wɔn atare so ne wɔn nsu a ɛtaataa hɔ nyinaa so, na ɛnnan mogya; na mogya aba Misraim asase nyinaa so, nnua ade ne abo ade mu.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ wɔn no; na ɔmaa poma no so, na ɔde bɔɔ nsu a ɛwɔ asu no mu no mu wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim; na nsu a ɛwɔ asu no mu nyinaa dan mogya.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mpataa a ɛwɔ asu no mu wuwui, na asu no bɔnee, na Misraimfo antumi annom asu no mu nsu, na mogya kataa Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Na Misraim akɔmfo de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara. Na Farao koma pirimii ara, na wantie wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE kae no.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Na Farao dan ne ho kɔɔ ne fi, na eyi nso wannwen ho.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Na Misraimfo nyinaa tutuu asu no ho mmura sɛ wɔrepɛ nsu anom, efisɛ wontumi nnom asu no mu nsu.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Na nnansɔn a AWURADE dan nsu no betwaa mu.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Ma me man no nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Na sɛ woampene amma wɔankɔ a, hwɛ, mede mpɔtorɔ mɛhaw w'asase nyinaa.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Na asu no bɛdɔ mpɔtorɔ manyamanya, na wɔafoforo aba wo fi ne wo dabekyiri ne wo mpa so ne wo nkoa afi ne wo nkurɔfo mu ne w'afononoo mu ne wo mmɔre akorow mu.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na wo ne wo manfo ne wo nkoa nyinaa so na mpɔtorɔ no bɛforo aba. Mpɔtorɔ no

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma, na teɛ wo nsa nsubɔnten ne asuasu ne atare so, na ma mpɔtorɔ mmra Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Aaron teɛɛ ne nsa wɔ Misraim nsu so, na mpɔtorɔ bae bɛkataa Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Na akɔmfo no de wɔn asumansɛm no yɛɛ saa ara maa mpɔtorɔ foro baa Misraim asase so.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao frɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kae sɛ: Mompa AWURADE kyɛw na onyi mpɔtorɔ no mfi me ne me man so, na mɛma ɔman no akɔ akɔbɔ afɔre ama AWURADE.

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Wo ara kyerɛ me da ko a enkosi na mempa kyɛw memma wo ne wo nkoa ne wo man, na wonyi mpɔtorɔ no mfi wo ne wo fi so, na wɔnka asu no nko mu.

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ose: Ɔkyena. Na ose: Ɛnyɛ sɛ wokae no, na woahu sɛ obi bi nni hɔ a ɔte sɛ AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Na mpɔtorɔ no befi wo ne wo fi ne wo nkoa ne wo man so; asu no mu nko na wɔbɛka.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron fii Farao anim kɔe. Na Mose teɛɛm frɛɛ AWURADE wɔ mpɔtorɔ a ɔde aba Farao so no ho.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛe sɛ Mose kae no, na mpɔtorɔ no wuwui afi mu ne adiwo ne wuram.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Na wɔboaboaa wɔn ano akuwakuw, na asase no so bɔnee.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Na Farao hui sɛ wanya ahotɔ no, ɔhyɛɛ ne koma den, na wantie wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE kae no. Mfutuma dan dwiw

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Teɛ wo poma no bɔ asase so mfutuma na ɛnnan dwiw wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Na wɔyɛɛ saa, na Aaron teɛɛ ne nsa de poma no bɔɔ asase so mfutuma, na ɛdan dwiwwɔ nnipa ne mmoa so. Na asase so mfutuma nyinaa dan dwiw Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Na akɔmfo no de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara sɛ wɔrema dwiw aba, nanso wɔantumi. Na dwiw no baa nnipa ne mmoa so.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ɛnna akɔmfo no ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Onyankopɔn nsatea ni. Na Farao koma pirimii ara na wantie wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE kae no. Nwansena pii ba

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tua ahema kogyina Farao anim; hwɛ, ɔrefi adi aba nsu no ano; na ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Ma me man no nkɔ na wɔnkɔsom me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ woremma me man no nkɔ a, hwɛ, mɛma nwansena ahorow aba wo ne wo nkoa ne wo man ne w'afi so, na nwansena no bɛyɛ Misraimfo afi mu ne asase a wɔte so no so amaama.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛɛ saa. Na nwansena a wɔdɔɔso pii baa Farao fi ne ne nkoa afi ne Misraim asase nyinaa so. Na nwansena no nti asase no so sɛee.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kae sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔbɔ afɔre mma mo Nyankopɔn wɔ asase yi so.

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Na Mose se: Ɛmfata sɛ wɔyɛ no saa, efisɛ Misraim akyide na yɛde bɛbɔ afɔre ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn. Hwɛ, sɛ yɛde Misraim akyide bɔ afɔre wɔ wɔn anim a, so wɔrensiw yɛn abo?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Yɛbɛnantew nnansa ɔkwan akɔ sare so, na yɛakɔbɔ afɔre ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn, sɛnea waka akyerɛ yɛn no.

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kae sɛ: Me de, mɛma mo kwan na moakɔ akɔbɔ afɔre ama AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn wɔ sare so, na akyirikyiri nko na monnkɔ; mompa kyɛw mma me.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, merebefi wo nkyɛn makɔ makɔpa AWURADE kyɛw na nwansena no afi Farao ne ne nkoa ne ne man so ɔkyena; na nkontompo nko na Farao nntwa bio sɛ ɔremma ɔman no nkɔ nkɔbɔ afɔre mma AWURADE.

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose fii Farao anim kɔe kɔpaa AWURADE kyɛw.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛɛ nea Mose kae no, na oyii nwansena no fii Farao ne ne nkoa ne ne man so; anka biako po.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Na Farao pirim ne koma saa bere yi nso, na wamma ɔman no ankɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifo Nyankopɔn, se ni: Ma me man no nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: hwɛ, AWURADE nsa bɛda wo mmoa a wɔwɔ wuram so, na ɔde owu a ano yɛ den kɛse bɛba apɔnkɔ, mfurum, yoma, anantwi ne nguan so.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de nsonoe bɛto Israel mmoa ne Misraim mmoa ntam, na nea ɛyɛ Israelfo dea no mu biara renwu.

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hyɛɛ da sɛ: Ɔkyena na AWURADE bɛyɛ eyi wɔ asase so.

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, AWURADE yɛɛ saa ade no, na Misraim mmoa nyinaa wuwui, na Israelfo mmoa no mu biako po anwu.

english_verse: When the king found out, he was still too stubborn to let the people go. Sores
translation_verse: Na Farao soma kɔhwɛe, na hwɛ, Israel mmoa mu biako po nwui ɛ. Nanso Farao koma yɛɛ den ara, na wamma ɔman no ankɔ. Mpɔmpɔ yaredɔm

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: Momfa fononoo mu nso nsa ma, na Mose ntow mpete ahunum wɔ Farao anim,

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: na ɛnnan Misraim asase nyinaa so tutuw, na ɛnyɛ nnipa ne mmoa ho mpobia a ɛpaepae tutu akuru Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Na wɔsesaw fononoo mu nso, na wokogyinaa Farao anim, na Mose de petee ahunum, na ɛdan nnipa ne mmoa ho mpobia a ɛpaepae tutu akuru.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Na mpobia no nti akɔmfo no antumi annyina Mose anim, efisɛ mpobia no asisi akɔmfo no ne Misraimfo nyinaa.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao koma, na wantie wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose no. Ɔsoro abo

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tua ahema kogyina Farao anim, na ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifo Nyankopɔn no, se ni: Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Na afei de, merema me haw nyinaa aba wo koma so ne wo nkoa ne wo man mu, na woahu sɛ obiara nni hɔ a ɔte sɛ me wɔ asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Na afei sɛ mateɛ me nsa na mede owuyare mabɔ wo ne wo man a, anka wɔatwa wo afi asase so.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Nanso eyi nti na mema wugyina hɔ, sɛ meyi me tumi adi makyerɛ wo, na wɔaka me din ho asɛm asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Woda so ma wo ho so na wusiw me man kwan sɛ woremma wɔnkɔ,

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: hwɛ, ɔkyena sesɛɛ mɛma ɔsoro abo a emu yɛ duru pa a ɛso bi mmaa Misraim da fi da a wɔhyɛɛ ase de abedu nnɛ yi atɔ.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Na afei soma ma wɔnkɔfa wo mmoa ne wo biribiara a ɛwɔ wuram mmra ntɛm; onipa biara ne afieboa biara a wobehu no wuram na wɔamfa no amma ofie no, ɔsoro abo no gu wɔn so a, wobewuwu.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Farao nkoa mu nea osuro AWURADE asɛm no de ne nkoa ne ne mmoa guan baa ofie;

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: na nea wammu AWURADE asɛm no gyaw ne nkoa ne ne mmoa wɔ wuram.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Teɛ wo nsa kɔ ahunmu, na ɔsoro abo ntɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so, nnipa ne mmoa ne wuram nhaban nyinaa so wɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔsoro abo ne ogya a ɛdɛw framfram toatoam a ano yɛ den pii pa a ɛso bi mmaa Misraim asase nyinaa so da fi da a ɛyɛɛ ɔman no bae.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Gye Gosen asase a Israelfo wɔ hɔ no so nko na ɔsoro abo no bi antɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao soma bɛfrɛɛ Mose ne Aaron ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Eyi de, mayɛ bɔne, AWURADE ne ɔtreneeni, na me ne me man ne abɔnefo.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Mompa AWURADE kyɛw, na Onyankopɔn aprannaa ne ɔsoro abo no nnyae, na adɔɔso, na mɛma moakɔ na morentena ha bio.

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mifi adi mifi kurow no mu ara pɛ a, mɛtrɛw me nsam makyerɛ AWURADE, na aprannaa no to betwa, na ɔsoro abo no antɔ bio, na woahu sɛ AWURADE na asase wɔ no.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Na wo ne wo nkoa de, minim sɛ munnya nsuroo AWURADE Nyankopɔn ɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Na eguu asaawa ne atoko so, nso na atoko no ayɛ mmɛtem, na asaawa nso reyɛ agu nhwiren.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Na awi ne kɔkɔte de, angu so bi, efisɛ ɛno ka akyiri.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na Mose fii Farao nkyɛn, na ofii kurow no mu kɔtrɛw ne nsam kyerɛɛ AWURADE, na aprannaa ne abo no to twae, na osu gyaee asase no so gu.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Na Farao hui sɛ osutɔ ne amparuwbo ne aprannaa no to atwa no, ɔsan yɛɛ bɔne bio, na ɔhyɛɛ ne koma den, ɔno ne ne nkoa.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Na Farao koma pirimii ara, na wamma Israelfo no ankɔ, sɛnea AWURADE nam Mose so kae no.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn, na mahyɛ ne koma ne ne nkoa koma den, na mayi me nsɛnkyerɛnne yi adi wɔ wɔn mu,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: na woaka nea meyɛe wɔ Misraim ne me nsɛnkyerɛnne a miyii adi wɔ wɔn mu no wɔ wo ba ne wo ba ba asom, na moahu sɛ mene AWURADE.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifo Nyankopɔn no, se ni: Wobɛkame wo ho asebrɛ wɔ m'anim akosi da bɛn? Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Na sɛ woampene amma me man ankɔ a, hwɛ, ɔkyena mɛma mmoadabi aba w'asase yi so,

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: na wɔabɛkata asase ani a obi renhu asase ani, na wɔabedi nnikae a amparuwbo no gyaw ma ɛka maa mo no, na wɔabedi nnua a ɛrefefɛw ama mo wɔ mfuw mu no nyinaa,

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: na wɔabɛyeyɛ w'afi mu ne wo nkoa nyinaa afi mu ne Misraimfo nyinaa afi mu amaama sɛnea w'agyanom ne w'agyanom agyanom nhuu bi pɛn fi da a wɔbaa asase so de bedu nnɛ. Na ɔdan ne ho fii Farao anim.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao nkoa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Da bɛn ara na oyi nteetee yɛn ara nkosi? Ma nnipa no nkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE wɔn Nyankopɔn. So wunnya nhui sɛ Misraim resɛe?

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Na wɔde Mose ne Aaron san baa Farao anim bio, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn. Hefo ne wɔn a wɔbɛkɔ no?

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Yɛde yɛn mmofra ne yɛn mpanyin na ɛrekɔ; yɛde yɛn mmabanin ne yɛn mmabea, yɛn nguan ne yɛn anantwi na ɛrekɔ, efisɛ yɛwɔ fa bi hyɛ ma AWURADE.

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: A, ɛnne AWURADE nni mo akyi ɛ, sɛ merema mo ne mo mma akɔ yi. Maahu sɛ bɔne na mopɛ sɛ moyɛ yi.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Dabida! Mo mmarima na monkɔ nkɔsom Awurade, na ɛno ara na mohwehwɛ. Na wɔpam wɔn fii Farao anim.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mmoadabi no nti teɛ wo nsa wɔ Misraim asase so, na wɔmmra Misraim asase so, na wɔmmɛwe asase no so nhaban nyinaa, nea amparuwbo no gyawee no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Na Mose teɛɛ ne poma wɔ Misraim asase so, na AWURADE maa apuei mframa bɔ faa asase no so da no nyinaa ne anadwo no nyinaa. Na ade kyee na apuei mframa no de mmoadabi no aba.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Na mmoadabi no baa Misraim asase no nyinaa so, na wobeguu Misraim asase no so nyinaa, na wɔdɔɔso pii. Ebi nnii wɔn anim mmae pɛn a ɛte sɛ wɔn, na wɔn akyi nso ebi remma saa bio.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Na wɔkataa asase no nyinaa ani ma esum duruu asase no so, na wodii asase no so nhaban nyinaa ne nnua a amparuwbo no gyawee no so aba nyinaa, na biribiara anka a ɛyɛ momono wɔ nnua mu ne mfuw mu nhaban mu wɔ Misraim asase no so nyinaa.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao yɛɛ ntɛm soma kɔfrɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kae sɛ: Mayɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn ne mo bɔne.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Na afei, fa me bɔne firi me prɛko yi nko, na mompa AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn kyɛw, na onyi owu yi nko mfi me so.

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Na ofii Farao anim kɔe kɔpaa AWURADE kyɛw.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa atɔe mframa a ano yɛ den pii bae, na ɛbɛfaa mmoadabi no kɔe, na ɛde wɔn koguu mmɛw po mu; mmoadabi no biako po anka Misraim asase no so baabiara.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao koma, na wamma Israelfo no ankɔ. Esum duru

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Teɛ wo nsa kɔ ahunmu, na esum nnuru Misraim asase so, na ɛnyɛ esum a woso mu a ɛbɛyɛ yiye.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Na Mose teɛɛ ne nsa kɔɔ ahunmu, na esum kabii duruu Misraim asase no nyinaa so nnansa.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Obiara anhu ne yɔnko, na obiara ansɔre ne tenabea nnansa; na Israelfo nyinaa de, wonyaa hann wɔ nea wɔte hɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao frɛɛ Mose sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE; mo nguan ne mo anantwi nko na wɔmfa nsie ha; mo mma nso ne mo nkɔ.

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Ɛsɛ sɛ wode afɔrebɔde a wokum na wɔhyew nso hyɛ yɛn nsa, na yɛde akɔbɔ ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Na yɛn mmoa nso ne yɛn bɛkɔ, ɛrenka tɔte po; na ɛnonom bi na yɛde rekɔsom AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn. Na yɛn de, yennim nea yɛde bɛsom AWURADE gye sɛ yedu hɔ ansa.

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao koma, na wampɛ sɛ ɔma wɔkɔ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fi me so kɔ, hwɛ wo ho yiye, na nhu m'anim bio; na da a wubehu m'anim no, wubewu.

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buae sɛ: Yiw mate! Meremma w'anim bio.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mɛma ɔhaw biako aba Farao ne Misraim so bio, na ɛno akyi no, ɔbɛma moafi ha akɔ; ɔbɛma moakɔ koraa, ɔpam mpo na ɔbɛpam mo afi ha.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Afei kasa ma ɔman no nte sɛ: Mmarima ne mmea mmisabisa wɔn nnamfonom hɔ dwetɛ nnwinne ne sika nnwinne.

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa ɔman no anim yɛɛ nyam wɔ Misraimfo anim; nso ɔbarima Mose no yɛ kɛse pa wɔ Misraim asase no so wɔ Farao nkoa ne ɔman no anim.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Sɛ Awurade se ni: Anadwo dasu mu no, mefi adi mafa Misraim,

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: na Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa bewuwu, efi Farao abakan a ɔtena n'agua so, so de kosi afenaa a ɔwɔ owiyammo akyi abakan ne mmoa mmakan nyinaa so.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Na osu kɛse a ɛso bi mmae da, na ɛso bi remma bio bɛba Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma nyinaa de, ɔkraman po rentwe ne tɛkrɛma nhyɛ wɔn, efi nnipa so kosi mmoa so, na moahu sɛ AWURADE apae Misraim ne Israel ntam.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Na wo nkoa yi nyinaa besian aba me nkyɛn abɛkotow me aka sɛ: Fi adi kɔ, wo ne ɔman a edi w'akyi no nyinaa. Na ɛno akyi no mefi makɔ. Na ɔde abufuhyew fii Farao nkyɛn kɔe.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Farao rentie mo, na ama m'anwonwade adɔɔso wɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron yɛɛ anwonwade yi nyinaa wɔ Farao anim, na AWURADE pirim Farao koma, na wamma Israelfo no amfi n'asase so ankɔ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron wɔ Misraim asase so sɛ:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: Momfa ɔsram yi nyɛ asram ti, na ɛnyɛ mo afe mu ɔsram a edi kan.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Monka nkyerɛ Israel asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Ɔsram yi da a ɛto so du no, wɔmfa nguammaa mmiako mmiako, sɛnea wɔn mpanyin fi tetee; ofi biako oguammaa biako.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Na momfa no nsie nkodu ɔsram yi da a ɛto so dunan; na Israel asafo mu no nyinaa nkunkum wɔn anwummere.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Na wɔmfa mogya no bi nsra adan a wobedi wɔ mu no apongua abien ne aponguatifi no ho.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Na wonni nam no anadwo no ara; wɔmfa ogya ntoto, na wɔmfa apiti ne fan nwenenwene nni.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Munnni no amono, na mommfa nsu nnnoa, na mmom momfa ogya ntoto, ne ti ne n'asrɛ ne n'ayamde no.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Na munnnyaw bi nnsie na ade nnkye so; na sɛ ebi ka na ade kye so a, momfa ogya nhyew.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛnea munni no ni: Monkyekyere mo asen, na mo mpaboa nhyehyɛ mo anan, na mo mpoma nkurakura mo nsam, na munni no hare so. Ɛyɛ AWURADE twam.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na merebetwam Misraim asase so anadwo yi, na makum Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, efi nnipa so kosi mmoa so, na mebu Misraim anyame nyinaa atɛn, mene AWURADE.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mogya no nyɛ sɛnkyerɛnne mma mo, afi a mowowɔ mu no mu; na sɛ mihu mogya no a, matwa mo ho, na merebɔ Misraim asase a, amane bi amma mo so ammɛsɛe mo.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Na ɛda yi nyɛ mo nkae, na monhyɛ ho fa mma AWURADE, mo awo ntoatoaso mu. Monyɛ no afahyɛ, daa atɔremude.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Nnansɔn na munni apiti. Da a edi kan no ara na momma mmɔkaw to ntwa mo afi mu, efisɛ obiara a obedi mmɔkaw abodoo fi da a edi kan no de kosi da a ɛto so ason no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi Israel mu.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Na da a edi kan no munhyia nhyia kronkron, na da a ɛto so ason no nso munhyia nhyia kronkron. Wɔnnyɛ adwuma biara wɔ mu, gye nea obiara bedi nko ho adwuma na monyɛ.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Na monhyɛ apiti fa no, efisɛ saa da yi ara na miyii mo dɔm no mifii Misraim asase so. Ɛno nti munni da yi mo awo ntoatoaso mu nyɛ no daa atɔremude.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Ɔsram a edi kan no da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere no mumfi apiti di ase nkosi ɔsram no da a ɛto so aduonu biako anwummere.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Nnansɔn na mommma wonnhu mmɔkaw wɔ mo afi mu, efisɛ obiara a obedi abodoo a akaw no, ɔhɔho oo, nea wɔwoo no asase no so oo, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi Israel asafo mu.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Munnni biribiara a akaw, munni apiti wɔ mo tenabea nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose frɛɛ Israel mpanyimfo nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munyiyi nguan mfa, sɛnea mo mmusua te, na munkum twam no.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Na momfa adwerɛ kasiaw mmɔ mogya a ɛwɔ yawa mu no mu, na momfa yawa no mu mogya no bi nsra aponguatifi ne apongua abien no ho, na mo mu biara mmfi adi mmfi ne fi pon ano nkosi anɔpa.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Efisɛ AWURADE rebetwam abobɔ Misraimfo, na sɛ ohu mogya no wɔ aponguatifi ne apongua abien no ho a, AWURADE betwa ɔpon no ho, na ɔrento ɔsɛefo no kwan mma ɔmma mo afi mu mmɛbobɔ mo.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Na ɛba sɛ mudu asase a AWURADE de bɛma mo sɛnea ɔkae no so a, munni ɔsom yi so.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mo mma bisa mo sɛ: Mo som yi ase ne dɛn a?

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase sɔree. Na Israelfo no siim kɔe kɔyɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose ne Aaron no, saa ara na wɔyɛe. Wokum Misraimfo mmakan

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na anadwo dasu mu no AWURADE bobɔɔ Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, efi Farao abakan a ɔtena n'agua so so de kosi dommum a ɔwɔ deduadan mu abakan so, ne afieboa mmakan nyinaa.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao sɔree anadwo no ara, ɔne ne nkoa nyinaa ne Misraimfo nyinaa, na osu kɛse baa Misraim, efisɛ na ofi biara nni hɔ a funu nni mu.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ Mose ne Aaron anadwo no kae sɛ: Monsɔre mfi me man mu, mo ne Israelfo no, na monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE, sɛnea mokae no.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mo nguan ne mo anantwi nso, momfa wɔn, sɛnea mokae no, na monkɔ, na munhyira me nso.

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Na Misraimfo piapiaa ɔman no sɛ wɔnyɛ ntɛm mfi asase no so, efisɛ wose: Yɛn nyinaa rewuwu.

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no soasoaa wɔn mmɔre ansa na ɛrekaw kyekyeree wɔn mmɔre akorow wɔ wɔn ntama mu de sisii wɔn kɔn ho.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no yeyɛe sɛnea Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na wobisabisaa Misraimfo hɔ dwetɛ nnwinne ne sika nnwinne ne ntama.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa ɔman no anim baa nyam, Misraimfo anim, na wɔde nea wobisae maa wɔn. Na wɔfaa Misraimfo agyapade no kɔe. Israelfo fii Misraim

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no siim fii Rameses kɔɔ Sukot, wɔbɛyɛ mmarima a wɔnam fam mpem ahorow ahansia, mmofra mfra mu.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Na afrafrafo pii nso ne wɔn kɔe, ne nguan ne anantwi, mmoa pii pa.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Na wɔde mmɔre a wɔde fi Misraim bae no totoo apiti fam, na ɛnkawee ɛ, efisɛ Misraimfo no pam wɔn, na wɔantumi antwentwɛn wɔn nan ase, na wonsiesiee akwansoduan nso ɛ.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Ɛyɛ anadwo a wodi ma AWURADE a oyii wɔn fii Misraim asase so no, anadwo no ara na wodi ma AWURADE wɔ Israelfo nyinaa mu wɔn awo ntoatoaso mu.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: Eyi ne twam no ho ahyɛde: Ɔnanani biara nnni bi.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Na obiara akoa a ɔde sika atɔ no no, twa no twetia ansa na wadi bi.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Mo nkyɛn tenafo ne ɔpaani nnni bi.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Ofi biako mu na wonni, wɔmmfa nam no bi mmfi fie hɔ mmfi adi, na mummmu ne dompe bi.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel asafo nyinaa nyɛ saa.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Na sɛ obi abɛsoɛ wo nkyɛn hɔho na ɔpɛ sɛ odi twam ma AWURADE a, ma wontwa ne mmarima nyinaa twetia, na ɛno ansa na ɔmmɛn mmedi, na ɔnyɛ sɛ nea wɔwoo no asase no so; na momonoto biara de, onnni bi.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mmara koro nna hɔ mma okuroni ne ɔhɔho a ɔbɛsoɛ mo mu.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo nyinaa yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose ne Aaron no; saa ara na wɔyɛe.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na da no ara, AWURADE yii Israelfo no fii Misraim asase so, sɛnea wɔn asafo te.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: Yɛ mmakan nyinaa, Israelfo mu ade biara a ebue yafunu ano wɔ nnipa ne afieboa mu, kronkron ma me, na me dea.

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE de wo nya du Kanaanfo ne Hetifo ne Amorifo ne Hewifo ne Yebusifo asase a ɔkaa w'agyanom ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wo, asase a nufusu ne wo sen so no so a, ɛno de, fa ɔsom yi som no ɔsram yi so.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nnansɔn na di apiti, na da a ɛto so ason no, hyɛ fa ma AWURADE.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Wonni apiti nnansɔn no, na mma wonnhu wo nkyɛn mmɔkaw abodoo anaa mmɔkaw w'asase so baabiara.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na da no bɔ din kyerɛ wo ba sɛ: Nea AWURADE yɛɛ me bere a mifii Misraim no ntia.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɛnyɛ wo wo nsa so sɛnkyerɛnne ne w'aniwa ntam nkae ade, na AWURADE mmara no atena w'anom, efisɛ nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii wo fii Misraim.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Enti di atɔremude yi so wɔ ne bere mu afe daa.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE de wo du Kanaanfo asase so, sɛ ɔkaa wo ne w'agyanom ntam, na ɔde ma wo a,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: yi ade biara a ebue yafunu ano ma AWURADE, na w'afieboa a wowɔ no mma nyinaa a wobue yafunu ano a wɔyɛ anini, fa ma AWURADE.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Na mfurum mmakan nyinaa de, fa oguan sesa, na sɛ woansesa a, bu ne kɔn mu. Na nnipa mmakan a wɔwɔ wo mmammarima mu nyinaa de, sesa gye wɔn.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔkyena bi wo ba bisa wo sɛ: Eyi ase ne dɛn, a, ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii yɛn Misraim fii nkoasom mu.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Na Farao pirim ne koma na ɔmpene sɛ ɔbɛma yɛakɔ no, AWURADE kum Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, efi nnipa mmakan so kosi afieboa mmakan so. Ɛno nti na me nso mede anini a ebue yafunu ano no nyinaa mebɔ AWURADE afɔre, nanso me mma mu mmakan nyinaa de, mesesa gye wɔn.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Na ɛnyɛ wo nsa so sɛnkyerɛnne ne w'aniwa ntam nkae ntamabamma, sɛ nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii yɛn fii Misraim. Omununkum dum ne ogya dum

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Farao maa ɔman no kwan no, Onyankopɔn amfa wɔn ankɔfa Filistifo asase so kwan a ɛnware no, efisɛ Onyankopɔn se: Na ɔman no ankohyia ɔsa annu wɔn ho, na wɔansan ankɔ Misraim.

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Enti Onyankopɔn de ɔman no kɔntɔn faa sare so kwan a ɛda mmɛw po ho no so. Na Israelfo no kɔɔ amia mu fii Misraim asase so kɔe.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Na Mose faa Yosef nnompe no, efisɛ Yosef aka Israelfo ntam sɛ: Ɔhwɛ na Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo, na momfa me nnompe mfi ha nkɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Na wosiim fii Sukot kɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ Etam, wɔ sare no ano.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ Israelfo ma wɔnnan nkɔbɔ nsra wɔ Pihahirot anim wɔ Migdol ne po ntam, wɔ Baalsefon anim; ne ntentenso na monkɔbɔ nsra no wɔ po no ano.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Na Farao bɛka Israelfo ho sɛ: Wɔrewɔ asase no so ntwɛtwɛdɛ, sare aka wɔn atom.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Na mepirim Farao koma ma watiw wɔn, na mɛhyɛ m'anim nyam Farao ne ne dɔm nyinaa so, na Misraimfo ahu sɛ mene AWURADE. Na wɔyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Misraim hene sɛ ɔman no aguan kɔ. Na Farao ne ne nkoa koma sakrae wɔ ɔman no ho, na wose: Ɛdɛn na yɛayɛ yi, sɛ yɛama Israel agyae yɛn som kɔ yi?

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Na osiesiee ne teaseɛnam, na ɔfaa ne man kaa ne ho,

english_verse: He commanded his officers in charge of his
translation_verse: na ɔfaa nteaseɛnam a wɔapaw ahansia ne Misraim nteaseɛnam nyinaa ne nteaseɛnam no nyinaa so asahene.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Misraim hene Farao koma ma otiw Israelfo no, efisɛ Israelfo no nam nsa a ɛyɛ den so na efi kɔe.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Na Misraimfo tiw wɔn, Farao nteaseɛnam apɔnkɔ nyinaa ne n'apɔnkɔsotefo ne ne dɔm no, na wɔbɛtoo wɔn sɛ wɔabɔ nsra wɔ po no ano a ɛkyerɛ Pihahirot wɔ Baalsefon anim.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Na Farao bɛnee no, Israelfo no momaa wɔn ani so, na hwɛ, Misraimfo di wɔn akyi reba. Na Israelfo no suroe pii, na wosu frɛɛ AWURADE.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: So adamoa a enni Misraim nti na woafa yɛn aba ha sɛ yemmewuwu sare so yi? Ɛdɛn nti na woyɛɛ yɛn sɛɛ, sɛ wuyii yɛn fii Misraim bae yi?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ɛno ɛnyɛ asɛm a yɛkaa wo wɔ Misraim sɛ: Gyae ma yɛnsom Misraim, no ni? Efisɛ eye ma yɛn mmom sɛ anka yɛsom Misraim sen sɛ yɛrebewuwu sare so yi.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Munnsuro, munnyina pintinn, na monhwɛ AWURADE nkwagye a ɔde rebɛkyerɛ mo nnɛ, na Misraimfo a muhu wɔn nnɛ yi, morenhu wɔn da biara da bio.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: AWURADE bɛko ama mo, na mo de, monyɛ komm!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ɛdɛn na wusu frɛ me? Ka kyerɛ Israelfo ma wonsim.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Na wo de, ma wo poma no so, na teɛ wo nsa ɛpo no so, na bae mu, na Israelfo no nnantew asase kesee so mfa po no mfinimfini.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Na me de, hwɛ, mepirim Misraimfo koma, na wɔabedi wɔn akyi, na mɛhyɛ m'anim nyam wɔ Farao ne ne dɔm nyinaa, ne nteaseɛnam ne n'apɔnkɔfo no so,

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: na Misraimfo no ahu sɛ mene AWURADE sɛ mahyɛ m'anim nyam wɔ Farao ne ne nteaseɛnam ne n'apɔnkɔfo no so.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Onyankopɔn bɔfo a odi Israel dɔm anim no twee ne ho bedii wɔn akyi, na omununkum dum no fii wɔn anim begyinaa wɔn akyi,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: na ebefii Misraim dɔm ne Israel dɔm no ntam, na ɛyɛ omununkum ne sum, nanso ɛma hann anadwo, na amma eyinom antumi ammɛn eyinom anadwo no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Na Mose teɛɛ ne nsa ɛpo no so. Na AWURADE de apuei mframa dennen maa ɛpo no kɔe anadwo no nyinaa, na ɔdan po no ma ɛyɛɛ asase kesee, na nsu no mu bae.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no nam asase kesee so faa ɛpo no mfinimfini, na nsu no yɛɛ wɔn ɔfasu wɔn nifa ne wɔn benkum.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa srabere mu no, AWURADE faa ogya ne mununkum dum no mu hwɛɛ Misraim dɔm no, na ɔmaa Misraim dɔm no ho yeraw wɔn,

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: na ohunhuan wɔn nteaseɛnam anan maa ne nantew mu yɛɛ duru. Na Misraimfo no se: Momma yenguan wɔ Israel anim, efisɛ AWURADE reko tia Misraim ama wɔn.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Teɛ wo nsa ɛpo no so, na nsu no nsan mmra Misraimfo ne wɔn nteaseɛnam ne wɔn apɔnkɔfo no so.

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose teɛɛ ne nsa ɛpo no so, na ade rekye anɔpa no, ɛpo no san n'akyi bɛsenee sɛnea ɛte, na Misraimfo no guan behyiae; na AWURADE kaa wɔn guu po no mfinimfini.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Na nsu no san akyiri bɛkataa Farao dɔm nyinaa, nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔfo a wotiw wɔn baa ɛpo no mu no so; wɔn mu biako mpo anka.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no nam asase kesee so faa ɛpo no mfinimfini, na nsu no yɛɛ wɔn ɔfasu wɔn nifa ne wɔn benkum.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE gyee Israel nkwa da no fii Misraim nsam, na Israel huu Misraimfo no sɛ wɔawuwu gu po no ano.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Na Israel huu nsa kɛse a AWURADE de kyerɛɛ Misraim so no, na ɔman no suroo AWURADE, na wogyee AWURADE ne n'akoa Mose dii.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose ne Israelfo no too dwom yi maa AWURADE kae sɛ: Mɛto AWURADE dwom, na ɔma na wama ne ho so, ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefo no, watow wɔn agu po mu.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: M'ahoɔden ne me dwonto ne AWURADE, na wayɛ me nkwagye. Ɔno ne me Nyankopɔn, na mɛkamfo no. Ɔyɛ m'agya Nyankopɔn, na mɛma no so.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: AWURADE yɛ dɔmmarima, AWURADE ne ne din.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Farao nteaseɛnam ne ne dɔm no, watow wɔn agu po mu, na n'akofo a wɔapaw wɔn no, wɔamemmem mmɛw po mu.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Ebun akata wɔn so, wɔamem kɔ ase tɔnn sɛ ɔbo.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: AWURADE, wode tumi ahyɛ wo nsa nifa anuonyam, AWURADE wo nsa nifa no dwerɛw atamfo no.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Na wo tumi a ɛso no ara na wode butuw wɔn a wɔsɔre hyɛ wo no. Wosoma w'abufuhyew ba, ɛhyew wɔn sɛ sakran.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Na wo hwene mu ahome mu na nsu no ano boae; asorɔkye gyinae sɛ ekuw, abun kyekyeree ɛpo yam.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Ɔtamfo no kae sɛ: Metiw, mɛto wɔn, mɛkyɛ asade no mu, wɔbɛmee me kra. Mɛtwe me nkrante, me nsa bɛsɛe wɔn.

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Wode wo mframa huwii, ɛpo no kataa wɔn so; wɔmemee sɛ sumpii wɔ nsu kɛse no mu.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: Hena na ɔte sɛ wo, AWURADE, wɔ anyame mu? Hena na ɔte sɛ wo, kronkronyɛ mu onuonyamfo, nea ne ho yɛ hu ayeyi mu, anwonwadeyɛfo.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Wode w'adɔe gyaa ɔman a woagye wɔn yi, wode w'ahoɔden kyerɛɛ wɔn kwan kɔɔ wo kronkronyɛ tenabea.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Aman tee, na wɔn ho wosowee, ahopopo kaa wɔn a wɔte Filistia.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Ɛno na Edom asafohempanyin ho dwiriw wɔn, Moab ahoɔdenfo no, nketenkete kitaa wɔn, Kanaanfo nyinaa hodwowee.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ehu ne osuro gu wɔn so, wo basa kɛseyɛ nti wɔayeyɛ komm sɛ ɔbo, kosi sɛ wo man betwam, AWURADE, kosi sɛ ɔman a wunyaa wɔn no betwam.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Wode wɔn bɛba abɛtɛw wɔn, w'agyapade bepɔw no so, AWURADE, nea wode hɔ ayɛ wo tenabea, kronkronbea a, AWURADE, wo nsa asiesie no.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: AWURADE bedi hene de bɛkɔ akosi daa daa.

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Na Farao apɔnkɔ ne ne nteaseɛnam ne n'apɔnkɔfo baa ɛpo no mu, na AWURADE maa ɛpo no mu nsu no san bɛkataa wɔn so, na Israelfo no nam asase kesee so faa ɛpo no mfinimfini.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Na odiyifobea Miriam a ɔyɛ Aaron ne nua no faa mpintin kurae, na mmea no nyinaa de mpintin ne asaw fii dii n'akyi.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Na Miriam gyee wɔn so sɛ: Monto AWURADE dwom, na wadi nkonim anuonyam mu; ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefo no, watow wɔn agu po mu. Mara nsu a ɛyɛ nwene

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose maa Israel tu fii mmɛw po ho na wofi kɔɔ Sur sare so; na wɔnantew sare no so nnansa, na wonnya nsu.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Na woduu Mara no, na wontumi nnom Mara nsu, efisɛ ɛyɛ nwene. Enti wɔtoo hɔ din Mara

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no kasae huhuhuhu hyɛɛ Mose sɛ: Dɛn na yɛnnom?

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Na osu frɛɛ AWURADE, na AWURADE kyerɛɛ no dua bi, na ɔde too nsu no mu, na nsu no yɛɛ dɛ. Ɛhɔ na ɔhyɛɛ ahyɛde ne atemmu maa wɔn, na ɛhɔ nso na ɔsɔɔ wɔn hwɛe,

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ otie na wubetie AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nne, na woayɛ nea ɛteɛ wɔ n'anim, na woatie ne mmara nsɛm, na woadi n'ahyɛde nyinaa so a, ɛnne meremfa ɔyare a mede miguu Misraim so no biara mingu wo so: na mene AWURADE, wo yaresafo no.

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Na woduu Elim a nsubura dumien ne nkyeresia aduɔsɔn wɔ. Na wɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ nsu no ho.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Na wotu fii Elim, na Israelfo asafo no nyinaa baa Sin sare a ɛda Elim ne Sinai ntam no so. Wofii Misraim asase so no, ɔsram a ɛto so abien no da a ɛto so dadu nnanum ne no.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo mu no nyinaa nwiinwii hyɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sare so hɔ.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Anka AWURADE mma yenwuwu ne nsa ano Misraim asase a yɛtete nam nkutu ho a yedidi mee no so! Na moayi yɛn aba sare yi so sɛ mode ɔkɔm rebekunkum asafo mu yi nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, merebɛma aduan afi soro atɔ ama mo, na ɔman no mfi adi da biara nkɔtase nea ɛbɛso wɔn ano da koro, na mensɔ wɔn menhwɛ sɛ wobedi me mmara so anaasɛ wɔrenni.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so asia no, wɔresiesie nea wɔfa no a, ɛnyɛ nea wɔtase daa no mmɔho.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no nyinaa sɛ: Anwummere na mubehu sɛ Awurade na oyii mo Misraim asase so;

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: na anɔpa na mubehu Awurade anuonyam, efisɛ wate mo anwiinwii a munwiinwii hyɛ Awurade no; na yɛn de, dɛn ne yɛn na munwiinwii hyɛ yɛn?

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose se: Awurade bɛma mo nam adi anwummere, ne aduan adi amee anɔpa, efisɛ Awurade ate mo anwiinwii a munwiinwii hyɛ no no; na dɛn ne yɛn? Ɛnyɛ yɛn na munwiinwii hyɛ, na mmom Awurade.

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Israelfo asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Muntwiw mmɛn Awurade anim, efisɛ wate mo anwiinwii no.

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Na Aaron rekasa akyerɛ Israelfo asafo nyinaa no, wɔdannan wɔn ani kyerɛɛ sare so, na hwɛ, Awurade anuonyam yii adi omununkum no mu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mate Israelfo anwiinwii no.

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Anwummere mubedi nam, na anɔpa moadi aduan amee, na moahu sɛ mene Awurade mo Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Na anwummere no, mmoka maa wɔn ho so bae bɛkataa nsra no so; na anɔpa no, obosu guu nsra no ho hyiae.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Na obosu a egui no kɔɔ ɔsoro, na hwɛ, biribi nkorowankorowa nketenkete gugu sare no ani, nketenkete te sɛ fam bosu nkyenkyenee.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no hui no, wosisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ɛdɛn ni? Efisɛ wonnim dekode. Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Eyi ne aduan a Awurade de ama mo sɛ munni.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Nsɛm a Awurade ahyɛ ni: Montase bi sɛnea obiara bedi: Omer mmiako mmiako, sɛnea mo nnipa dodow si na montase. Obiara ntase mma wɔn a wɔwɔ ne ntamadan mu no.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no yɛɛ sa; na wɔtasee, ebinom de pii, ebinom de kakraa bi.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Obiara nnnyaw bi mmma ade nnkye so.

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Nanso wɔantie Mose, na ebinom gyaw bi ma ade kyee so; na ɛdɔɔ mmoawa na ɛbɔnee. Na Mose bo fuw wɔn.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Na wɔtasee anɔpa anɔpa, obiara sɛnea obedi; na owia mu yɛ den a, na anan.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so asia no, wɔtasee aduan no mmɔho, obiako de omer abien. Na asafo no mu mpanyimfo nyinaa bae bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Nea Awurade aka ni: Ɔkyena yɛ ɔhome, homeda kronkron a wodi ma Awurade, monto nea mowɔ to, na monnoa nea mowɔ noa; na nea ɛbɛka no, momfa nsie nkosi anɔpa.

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Na wɔde siei kosii anɔpa, sɛnea Mose hyɛe no; na ammɔn, nso mmoawa bi nni mu.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Munni no nnɛ, na ɛnnɛ yɛ homeda a wodi ma Awurade; ɛnnɛ morenhu bi wuram.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nnansia na montase, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no yɛ homeda, ɛda no de, ebi rentɔ.

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so ason no, nkurɔfo no mu bi fii adi sɛ wɔkɔtase, nanso wɔannya bi.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mobɛkame m'ahyɛde ne me mmara so di akosi da bɛn?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Monhwɛ, sɛ Awurade ama mo homeda nti na da a ɛto so asia no ɔma mo nnanu aduan; montenatena mo afi mu; mma obiara mmfi adi mmfi ne tenabea da a ɛto so ason no.

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no homee da a ɛto so ason no.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo frɛɛ no: Mana, nso ɛte sɛ yisa aba fitaa, na ne dɛ te sɛ tetare a ɛwo wɔ mu.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Asɛm a Awurade ahyɛ ni: Momfa ebi nhyɛ omer ma mfa nsie awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba mo akyi no, na wɔahu aduan a mede memaa mo dii wɔ sare so bere a miyii mo Misraim asase so no.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa kuruwa bi, na fa mana omer ma gu mu, fa si Awurade anim, na wɔmfa nsie mo awo ntoatoaso.

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no, Aaron de sii Adanse no anim sɛ wɔde resie.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Nso omer yɛ olonka abupɛn du mu biako.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo no nyinaa tu fii Sin sare so, wɔn atutena a wodii no AWURADE anom asɛm so no mu, na wɔbɛbɔɔ nsra wɔ Refidim; nso na nsu a ɔman no bɛnom nni hɔ
