translation_verse: Na gyigye mpata sika no Israelfo no nsam, na fa ma ahyiae ntamadan no mu som no, na ɛnyɛ Israelfo no nkae, AWURADE anim, na wɔmfa mpata mma mo kra. Asankasɔn

english_verse: If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔbɛyɛ bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno ahuam ahwɛ no, wobetwa no afi ne man mu akyene.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
translation_verse: na dwira ho ma ɛnyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron; obiara a ɔka no nyɛ kronkron.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: for dedicating the tent and chest,
translation_verse: Na fa sra ahyiae ntamadan no ne Adanse adaka no,

english_verse: the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils,
translation_verse: ne ɔpon no ne ɛho nneɛma no nyinaa ne kaneadua no ne ɛho nneɛma no ne aduhuamhyew muka no,

english_verse: When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil,
translation_verse: Na sra Aaron ne ne mma no ngo yɛ wɔn kronkron, na wonni me asɔfo.

english_verse: and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Eyi nyɛ ɔsra ngo kronkron mma me, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu,

english_verse: So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves.
translation_verse: wonnhwie nngu onipa honam so, na munnsusuw so nnyɛ bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno; ɛyɛ kronkron, ɛnyɛ kronkron mma mo.

english_verse: If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.” The Sweet-Smelling Incense
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔbɛfra bi a ɛte sɛ ɛno anaasɛ ɔde bi bɛka ɔhɔho no, wobetwa no afi ne man mu akyene.

english_verse: Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy.
translation_verse: na fa yɛ aduhuam a wɔhyew, adufrafo nyansa so adufrae a wɔaposa a ɛyɛ gyenennyenen ne kronkron.

english_verse: Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy.
translation_verse: Na siw bi fekɔfekɔ, na fa bi si Adanse no anim ahyiae ntamadan no mu, nea me ne wo behyia no: Ɛnyɛ mo akronkronne mu ade kronkron.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mabɔ Hur ba Uri ba Besalel a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu din mafrɛ no,

english_verse: I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you:
translation_verse: Na me ara, hwɛ, mafa Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu maka ne ho; na nnipa a wɔwɔ nyansa koma nyinaa, mede nyansa mahyɛ wɔn komam na wɔnyɛ nea mahyɛ wo yi nyinaa;

english_verse: Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said: The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own.
translation_verse: Na wo nso ka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Me home nna no ara na munni; na ɛyɛ me ne mo ntam sɛnkyerɛnne, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu, na moahu sɛ me AWURADE na meyɛ mo kronkron.

english_verse: Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nnansia na wɔmfa nyɛ adwuma, na da a ɛto so ason no yɛ ɔhome mu homeda a ɛyɛ kronkron ma AWURADE; obiara a ɔyɛ adwuma homeda no, okum na wobekum no.

english_verse: This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
translation_verse: Me ne Israel ntam sɛnkyerɛnne ne no de kosi daa; na nnansia na AWURADE de yɛɛ ɔsoro ne asase, na da a ɛto so ason no ɔhomee na odwudwoo ne koma.

english_verse: When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_verse: Na ɔne Mose wiee kasa Sinai bepɔw so no, ɔmaa no adanse apon abien, abopon a wɔde Nyankopɔn nsatea akyerɛw so.

english_verse: Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
translation_verse: Na wotuaa ahema bobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre; na ɔman no tenaa ase didi nomee, na wɔsɔre gorui.

english_verse: Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kae sɛ: Monyɛ mo ho kronkron mma AWURADE nnɛ, sɛ obiara bɛsɔre ahyɛ ne ba ne ne nua po, na mode nhyira aba mo so nnɛ.

english_verse: After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no hui sɛ Mose akyɛ na onsian mfi bepɔw no so mma no, ɔman no boaa wɔn ho ano baa Aaron nkyɛn besee no sɛ: Sɔre yɛ anyame ma yɛn, na wonni yɛn anim, efisɛ Mose yi, ɔbarima a okoyii yɛn fii Misraim bae no de, yennim nea ayɛ no.

english_verse: Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Aaron ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munyiyi sika nkaa a ɛwowɔ mo yerenom ne mo mmabanin ne mo mmabea asom mfa mmrɛ me.

english_verse: then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull. All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
translation_verse: Na ogyei wɔ wɔn nsam, na ɔde pɛe yeyɛe, na ɔyɛɛ no nantwi a wɔagu; na wɔkae sɛ: Israel, eyinom ne wo anyame a woyii wo fii Misraim asase so bae no.

english_verse: When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Aaron hui no, osii afɔremuka wɔ n'anim; na Aaron paee sɛ: Ɔkyena ne AWURADE afahyɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sian kɔ, na wo man a wode wɔn fi Misraim asase so bae no redi asɛmmɔne;

english_verse: They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: wɔaman afi ɔkwan a mekyerɛɛ wɔn no so ntɛm; wɔayɛ nantwi ba a wɔagu, na wɔasɔre no abɔ afɔre ama no aka sɛ: Israel, eyinom ne wo anyame a woyii wo fii Misraim asase so bae no.

english_verse: and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
translation_verse: Mahu ɔman yi, na hwɛ, wɔyɛ ɔman a wɔn kɔn asen; na afei ma me kwan na me bo nhuru nhyɛ wɔn, na memmene wɔn, na memfa wo menyɛ ɔman kɛse.

english_verse: Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind: Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them.
translation_verse: Na Mose paa AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn kyɛw sɛ: AWURADE, ɛdɛn nti na wo bo huru hyɛ ɔman a wode ahoɔden kɛse ne nsa a ɛyɛ den koyii wɔn Misraim asase so bae no?

english_verse: If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
translation_verse: Ɛdɛn nti na Misraimfo nka sɛ: Adwemmɔne bi nti na obeyii wɔn kɔe sɛ okokum wɔn mmepɔw so na wapra wɔn afi asase ani? San fi w'abufuhyew no mu, na ma bɔne a worebɛyɛ wo man no nyɛ wo yaw.

english_verse: Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
translation_verse: Kae Abraham, Isak ne Israel, wo nkoa a wokaa wɔn wo ankasa wo ntam ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mɛma w'asefo adɔɔso sɛ ɔsoro nsoromma, na asase a maka ho asɛm yi nyinaa, mede mɛma w'asefo na wɔadi so akosi daa, no.

english_verse: So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nuu ne ho wɔ bɔne a ɔkae sɛ ɔrebɛyɛ ne man no ho.

english_verse: Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
translation_verse: Na apon no yɛ Onyankopɔn adwuma, na kyerɛw no yɛ Onyankopɔn kyerɛw a wɔakurukyerɛw apon no so.

english_verse: When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua tee sɛ ɔman no rebɔ ose na wɔreyɛ gyegyeegye no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ɔko gyegyeegye wɔ nsra no mu.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
translation_verse: Na ose: Ɛnyɛ nkonimdi ho sebɔ gyegyeegye na ɛnyɛ nkogu ho nteɛm gyegyeegye, na mmom dwomsogye gyegyeegye na mete yi.

english_verse: As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Na Mose bɛn nsra no na ohuu nantwi ba ne asaw no ara pɛ, ne bo fuwii, na ɔtow apon a ɛwɔ ne nsam no gui ma ɛbobɔe bepɔw no ase.

english_verse: He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it.
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa nantwi ba a wɔyɛe no de gya hyewee, na ɔyam no muhumuhu de petee nsu ani maa Israelfo no nomee.

english_verse: Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Dɛn na ɔman yi yɛɛ wo na wode bɔne kɛse aba wɔn so yi?

english_verse: Aaron answered: Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Aaron se: Mma me wura bo mmfuw, wo ara wunim ɔman yi sɛ bɔne ara na wɔde asi wɔn anim.

english_verse: They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Yɛ anyame ma yɛn na wonni yɛn anim, efisɛ Mose yi, ɔbarima a okoyii yɛn fii Misraim asase so bae no, yennim nea ayɛ no.

english_verse: Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
translation_verse: Na misee wɔn sɛ: Wɔn a wɔwɔ sika bi no, wonyi. Na wɔde maa me, na metow guu gya mu, na nantwi ba yi fii mu bae.

english_verse: So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!” Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses,
translation_verse: ogyinaa nsraban no tia kae sɛ: Nea ɔwɔ AWURADE afa mmra me nkyɛn. Na Lewifo nyinaa boaboaa wɔn ho ano baa ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn se: Momfa mo nkrante mmobɔ mo asen, na muntwa mu nkɔ, na monsan mmra, mfi nsra no tia nkɔ tia, na munkunkum mo nuanom ne mo nnamfonom ne mo afipamfo.

english_verse: The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about
translation_verse: Na Lewifo no yɛe sɛnea Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na ɛda no ɔman no mu nnipa bɛyɛ mpensa totɔe.

english_verse: The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, Mose ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Mo de, moayɛ bɔne kɛse, na afei mɛforo makɔ AWURADE nkyɛn, ebia metumi mapata ama mo bɔne no.

english_verse: Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god.
translation_verse: Na Mose san kɔɔ AWURADE nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Ao, bɔne kɛse na ɔman yi ayɛ, na wɔayɛ sika anyame afa.

english_verse: But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
translation_verse: Na afei, sɛ wode wɔn bɔne no bekyɛ a! Na sɛ ɛnte saa a, popa me nso fi wo nhoma a woakyerɛw no mu ɛ!

english_verse: The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Nea wayɛ me bɔne no, ɔno na mɛpopa no mafi me nhoma mu.

english_verse: Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
translation_verse: Na afei kɔ, na kogya ɔman no kɔ nea maka makyerɛ wo no; hwɛ, me bɔfo bedi w'anim; nanso da a mɛba mabɛhwɛ wɔn no, metua wɔn wɔn bɔne so ka.

english_verse: So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔayɛ nantwi ba a Aaron yɛe no nti, AWURADE haw ɔman no.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sim fi ha kɔ, wo ne ɔman a wukoyii wɔn fii Misraim bae no, kɔ asase a mekaa ɛho ntam mekyerɛɛ Abraham, Isak ne Yakob sɛ: w'asefo na mede mɛma wɔn, no so.

english_verse: It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
translation_verse: kɔ asase a nufusu ne ɛwo sen so no so; na merentena wo mu ne wo nkɔ, efisɛ woyɛ ɔman a wo kɔn asen, na mammene wo ɔkwan no mu.

english_verse: Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Moyɛ ɔman a mo kɔn asen; sɛ metena mo mu kakraa bi me ne mo kɔ a, anka mɛhyew mo; na afei munyi mo ho ahokekade, na minhu nea mɛyɛ mo.

english_verse: and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry. The Lord Is with His People
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israelfo no yiyii wɔn ho ahokekade fi bepɔw Horeb ho hɔ ara.

english_verse: Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there.
translation_verse: Na Mose faa ntamadan no de kosii nsra no akyi akyirikyiri, na ɔfrɛɛ no ahyiae ntamadan. Na obiara a ɔhwehwɛ AWURADE no fi adi kɔ ahyiae ntamadan no a ɛwɔ nsra no akyi no ho.

english_verse: Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Mose fi adi kɔ ntamadan no ho a, ɔman no nyinaa sɔresɔre kogyinagyina wɔn ntamadan ano, na wɔde Mose akyi hwɛ ara kosi sɛ ɔhyɛn ntamadan no mu.

english_verse: Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent. The Lord Promises To Be with His People
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ne Mose di nhwɛanim kasa sɛ onipa ne ne yɔnko kasa. Na ɔsan ba nsra no mu a, ne somfo Nun ba Yosua a ɔyɛ abofra no de, omfi ntamadan no mu.

english_verse: Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Awurade sɛ: Hwɛ wo ara na woka kyerɛ me sɛ: Fa ɔman yi kɔ, nanso womma minhu nea wobɛsoma no na ɔne me akɔ. Nanso wo ara na woaka sɛ: Mede wo din minim wo, na woanya m'anim dom nso.

english_verse: If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
translation_verse: Enti mesrɛ wo, sɛ manya w'anim dom a, ma minhu wo kwan ɛ, na mahu wo, na manya w'anim dom; na hu sɛ nkurɔfo yi yɛ wo man a!

english_verse: The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: M'anim ne wo bɛkɔ, na mama woakɔhome.

english_verse: Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ w'anim ne yɛn renkɔ a, ɛnne mfa yɛn mfi ha nkɔ.

english_verse: But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn na wɔde behu wɔ ha sɛ me ne wo man yi anya w'anim dom, ɛnyɛ wo kɔ a wo ne yɛn bɛkɔ no? Na me ne wo man yi adɛnsow wɔ aman a wɔwɔ asase ani nyinaa mu.

english_verse: So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Asɛm a woaka yi nso, mɛyɛ, efisɛ woanya m'anim adom, na mede wo din minim wo.

english_verse: The Lord answered: All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name,
translation_verse: Na ose: Mɛma me papa nyinaa asen w'anim, na mɛpae me din YHWH wɔ w'anim; na medom nea medom no, na mihu nea mihu no mmɔbɔ no mmɔbɔ.

english_verse: but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die.
translation_verse: Na ose: Wuntumi nhu m'anim, efisɛ onipa renhu m'anim nnya nkwa.

english_verse: There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Hwɛ, ɔkwan wɔ me nkyɛn ha, na gyina ɔbotan no so;

english_verse: and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by.
translation_verse: na sɛ m'anuonyam resen a, mede wo mɛhyɛ ɔbo tokuru mu, na mede me nsa makata wo so masen ansa,

english_verse: Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_verse: na mayi me nsa, na woahu m'akyi fam; na m'anim de, worenhu.

english_verse: The Lord said: I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Hwɛ, me de, merepam apam: wo man no nyinaa anim na mɛyɛ anwonwade a wɔnyɛɛ bi da asase nyinaa so ne amanaman nyinaa mu, na ɔman a wɔwɔ wɔn mu no nyinaa ahu AWURADE nnwuma, na ade a merebɛyɛ wo no bɛyɛ hu.

english_verse: Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top.
translation_verse: Na siesie wo ho sie anɔpa, na foro bra Sinai bepɔw so anɔpa, na gyina hɔ twɛn me bepɔw no atifi.

english_verse: No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.”
translation_verse: Mma obiara nnka wo ho mmforo mmma, na mma wonnhu obiara nso bepɔw no so baabiara, na mma nguan anaa anantwi mmmedidi bepɔw no ho.

english_verse: So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Na osen abopon abien sɛ kan de no, na Mose tuaa ahema foro kɔɔ Sinai bepɔw no so, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na ɔfaa abopon abien no kuraa ne nsam.

english_verse: Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE betwaam n'anim, na ɔpaee sɛ: YHWH, YHWH , Onyankopɔn mmɔborohunufo ne ɔdomfo, nea n'abodwo kyɛ na n'adɔeyɛ ne ne nokware dɔɔso pii,

english_verse: Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Mose yɛɛ ntɛm kotow fam sɔree;

english_verse: He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.” A Promise and Its Demands (Exodus
translation_verse: na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE, sɛ manya w'anim dom a, mesrɛ wo, ma AWURADE ntena yɛn mu ne yɛn nkɔ, efisɛ wɔyɛ ɔman a wɔn kɔn asen; na fa yɛn amumɔyɛ ne yɛn bɔne firi yɛn, na fa yɛn yɛ wo de. AWURADE ne wɔn yɛ apam (Eksodɔs

english_verse: Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Afe mu mpɛn abiɛsa na wo mmarima nyinaa mmepue AWURADE Nyankopɔn, Israel Nyankopɔn, no anim.

english_verse: I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god!
translation_verse: Na nsɔre onyame foforo bi, efisɛ AWURADE a ne din ne oninkufo no yɛ Onyankopɔn ninkufo:

english_verse: The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
translation_verse: Ade biara a ebue ɔyafunu ano ne wo mmoa nyinaa mmakan a wɔyɛ anini no, nantwi oo, oguan oo, me dea.

english_verse: Don't make metal images of gods.
translation_verse: Nyɛ anyame a wɔagu mfa. Afahyɛ abiɛsa no

english_verse: I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today.
translation_verse: Di nea mehyɛ wo nnɛ yi so. Hwɛ, meretu Amorini ne Kanaanni ne Hetini ne Perisini ne Hewini ne Yebusini no afi w'anim.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap.
translation_verse: Hwɛ wo ho yiye na wo ne nea ɔte asase a worekɔ so no so no ampam, na wɔammɛdan wo mu afiri;

english_verse: Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: na mmom mummubu wɔn afɔremuka na mummuru wɔn ɔbo adum, na muntwitwa wɔn Asera nnua ngu.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals.
translation_verse: na wo ne nea ɔte asase no so ampam, na wodi wɔn anyame akyi bɔ aguaman na wɔbɔ wɔn anyame afɔre a, obi ammɛfrɛ wo na woankodi n'afɔrebɔde no bi,

english_verse: Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
translation_verse: Di apiti nnapɔnna no: nnansɔn na di apiti, sɛ mehyɛɛ wo no, ɔsram Abib mu, efisɛ ɔsram Abib mu na wufi Misraim bae.

english_verse: You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son. Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
translation_verse: Na afurum abakan de, fa oguan ba sesa no, na sɛ woansesa no a, ɛnne bu ne kɔn mu. Wo mmammarima mu mmakan nyinaa, sesa gye wɔn; na obiara mmfa ne nsapan mmmepue m'anim.

english_verse: Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting.
translation_verse: Nnansia na yɛ adwuma, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no de, home, fɛntɛm bere mu ne otwa bere mu na home.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Na hyɛ wo nnapɛn fa no, awitwa bere mu adekan de no, ɛne anoboa afahyɛ no, afedan mu.

english_verse: As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
translation_verse: Na metu amanaman no afi w'anim, na matrɛw w'ahye mu; na woreforo akopue AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim afirihyia mu mpɛn abiɛsa no a, obiara ani remmere w'asase.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
translation_verse: Mfa mmɔkaw nka w'afɔre a wobɔ no mogya ho, na mma ade nnkye twam afahyɛ afɔre no so.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
translation_verse: W'asase so adekan a ɛbɛba kan no fa bra AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn fi. Nnoa oguan ba ne na nufu mu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kyerɛw nsɛm yi fa, efisɛ nsɛm yi so na migyina me ne wo ne Israelfo no apam. Mose de abopon no ba

english_verse: Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining.
translation_verse: Na Mose fi Sinai bepɔw so resian no, na adanse apon abien no kura ne nsam; nanso na Mose onnim sɛ ɔne AWURADE kasae nti, n'anim were ahyerɛn.

english_verse: When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him.
translation_verse: Na Aaron ne Israelfo no nyinaa huu Mose no, na hwɛ, n'anim were hyerɛn; na wosuroe sɛ wɔbɛbɛn no.

english_verse: Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them.
translation_verse: Na Mose frɛɛ wɔn, na Aaron ne asafo no mu mpanyimfo no nyinaa san baa ne nkyɛn, na Mose ne wɔn kasae.

english_verse: Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, Israelfo no nyinaa twiw bae, na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn nea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no Sinai bepɔw so no nyinaa.

english_verse: The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne wɔn wiee ɔkasa no, ɔde nkataanim kataa n'anim.

english_verse: Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Mose rekɔ AWURADE anim ne no akɔkasa a, oyi nkataanim no de kosi sɛ obefi adi; na ofii adi bɛkaa nea wɔahyɛ no no kyerɛɛ Israelfo no.

english_verse: They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no huu Mose anim were no sɛ ahyerɛn; na ɔde nkataanim no san kataa n'anim kosii sɛ ɔkɔɔ mu ne no kɔkasae.

english_verse: You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nnansia na wɔmfa nyɛ adwuma, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no nyɛ mo homeda kronkron a mode home ma AWURADE; obiara a ɔbɛyɛ mu adwuma no, wobekum no.

english_verse: Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath. Offerings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Monnsɔ ogya mo tenabere nyinaa homeda. Soma afɔrebɔde (Eksodɔs

english_verse: The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made.
translation_verse: Na mmea a wɔwɔ nyansa koma nyinaa de wɔn nsa too asaawa, na wɔde nea wɔtoe no bae, bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa;

english_verse: onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
translation_verse: ne apopobibiri abo ne nsisimu abo a wɔde bɛyɛ asɔfotade ne adɛbo no.

english_verse: And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_verse: Wɔn na ɔde komam nyansa ahyɛ wɔn ma sɛ wonni adwinni horow nyinaa, sikadwumfo ne duadwumfo ne ɔnwemfo a odi bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa mu adwinni ne ntamanwemfo de: wɔn a wodi adwinni biara, ne wɔn a wɔbɔ wɔn tirim di adwinni horow.

english_verse: If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded:
translation_verse: Na mo mu koma mu anyansafo nyinaa mmra mmɛyɛ ade a AWURADE ahyɛ nyinaa,

english_verse: and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons. Gifts for the Lord
translation_verse: ɔsom ntade a wɔde som kronkronbea hɔ, ɔsɔfo Aaron ntade kronkron no ne ne mma ntade a wɔde bedi asɔfo no. Ɔman no afɔrebɔde

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ ni:

english_verse: I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze;
translation_verse: Munyi soma afɔrebɔde wɔ mo mu mmrɛ AWURADE; obiara a ne koma ka no mfa soma afɔrebɔde mmrɛ AWURADE: sika ne dwetɛ ne kɔbere,

english_verse: blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: ne bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa ne mmirekyi nwi,

english_verse: tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: ne adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ ne sukraman nhoma ne ɔkanto nnua,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or
translation_verse: ne kanea no ho ngo ne nnuhuam a wɔde bɛyɛ ɔsra ngo ne ɔhyew aduhuam,

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it;
translation_verse: adaka no ne ne mpoma, mpata agua no ne mmɔhɔɔ a etwa mu no,

english_verse: the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: ɔpon no ne ne mpoma ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa ne kyerɛ abodoo no,

english_verse: the lamp with its equipment and oil;
translation_verse: kaneadua no ne ɛho nneɛma ne n'akanea ne kanea no ho ngo,

english_verse: the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent;
translation_verse: ne aduhuamhyew muka no ne ne mpoma ne ɔsra ngo no ne ɔhyew aduhuam no ne tenabea no ano nkataano no;

english_verse: the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand;
translation_verse: ɔhyew afɔremuka no ne ne kɔbere ntontan no, ne mpoma ne ɛho nneɛma nyinaa, asankasɔn no ne ne ntaase;

english_verse: the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance;
translation_verse: adiwo no ho mmɔhɔɔ no, n'adum ne ne nnyinaso ne adiwo no abobow ano nkataano no,

english_verse: the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard;
translation_verse: tenabea no ho mmofunnua ne ɛho ntampehama;

english_verse: Moses finished speaking, and everyone left.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo no nyinaa fii Mose anim kɔe.

english_verse: Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes.
translation_verse: Na wɔbae, obiara a ne koma kanyan no, ne obiara a ne honhom kaa no, na wɔde AWURADE soma afɔrebɔde bae sɛ wɔmfa nyɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ne ɛho som nneɛma nyinaa ne ntade kronkron no.

english_verse: Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather.
translation_verse: ne obiara a ne nsam wɔ bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa ne mmirekyi nwi ne adwennini nhoma kɔkɔɔ ne sukraman nhoma no de bae;

english_verse: Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
translation_verse: obiara a okura dwetɛ ne kɔbere mfraefrae soma afɔrebɔde ma AWURADE no de bae. Na obiara a ne nsam wɔ ɔkanto nnua a wɔde bɛyɛ ɔsom nneɛma no biara no nso de bae.

english_verse: And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
translation_verse: na mmea a wɔn koma kaa wɔn nyansa mu nyinaa too mmirekyi nwi asaawa.

english_verse: The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest.
translation_verse: Na mpanyimfo no de apopobibiri abo ne nsisimu abo a wɔde bɛyɛ asɔfotade ne adɛbo no bae,

english_verse: They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests.
translation_verse: ne nnuhuam ne ngo a wɔde bɛyɛ akanea ngo ne ɔsra ngo ne ɔhyew aduhuam no.

english_verse: Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts. Bezalel and Oholiab (Exodus
translation_verse: Na Israelfo mu mmarima ne mmea nyinaa a wɔn koma kaa wɔn sɛ wɔmfa nnwuma a Awurade nam Mose so hyɛe sɛ wɔnyɛ no ho biribi mmra no de ayamye ayɛyɛde brɛɛ Awurade. Ntamadan si ho adwumayɛfo Ntomadan sie ho adwumayɛfoɔ (Eksodɔs

english_verse: Moses said to the people of Israel: The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Monhwɛ, AWURADE afrɛ Hura ba Uri ba Besalel a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu,

english_verse: The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others.
translation_verse: na ɔde ahyɛ ne komam sɛ ɔnkyerɛ ebinom nso, ɔno ne Ahisamak ba Oholiab a ofi Dan abusuakuw mu no.

english_verse: and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning,
translation_verse: Na wogyee soma afɔrebɔde a Israelfo de bae sɛ wɔmfa nyɛ kronkronbea som ho adwuma no nyinaa Mose anim sɛ wɔde bɛyɛ. Na wɔkɔɔ so ara de ayamye ayɛyɛde brɛɛ no daa anɔpa.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.”
translation_verse: bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ɔman no ama nea wɔde ba adɔɔso sen nea ɛbɛso adwuma a Awurade hyɛe sɛ wɔnyɛ no.

english_verse: So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did.
translation_verse: Na Mose hyɛ ma wɔpaee nsra no mu sɛ: Ɔbarima oo, ɔbea oo, obiara mmfa biribi mmmɛyɛ kronkronbea no ho soma afɔrebɔde bio.

english_verse: But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done. The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no de gyaee ba. Efisɛ nea wɔanya no dɔɔso ma adwuma no nyinaa sɛ wɔde bɛyɛ ama ebi aka. Ntamadan no siesie

english_verse: and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ntama no anum toatoaa so ma biako toaa biako so, na ɔde ntama no anum nso toatoaa so ma biako toaa biako so.

english_verse: These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ntama no anum toatoae yɛɛ no biako, na ɔde asia nso toatoae yɛɛ no biako.

english_verse: and the two panels were fastened at the loops with
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ kɔbere nkɔtɔkorɔ aduonum de toatoaa ntamadan no, na ayɛ biako.

english_verse: Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Na ɔde adwennini nhoma a wɔahyɛ no kɔkɔɔ yɛɛ ntamadan no nkataso, na ɔde sukraman nhoma yɛɛ ɛno so nkataso.

english_verse: Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
translation_verse: Na ntaaboo awotwe ne ne dwetɛ nnyinaso dunsia na ɛwɔ hɔ, taaboo biara ase nnyinaso abien.

english_verse: Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side
translation_verse: Na tenabea no akyi fam a ɛkyerɛ atɔe no, ɔde ntaaboo asia kosisii hɔ.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: na ɛpam ho fi fam de rekɔ, nanso ɛyɛ mu kodu ne hin so, nea kaa a edi kan no tua hɔ. Saa na ɔyɛɛ n'abien nyinaa ntwea abien no so.

english_verse: Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Na ɔde mfinimfini mmeamu no beaa ntaaboo no mfinimfini de twaa mu fi ti koduu ti.

english_verse: The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through. The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Na ɔde sika duraduraa ntaaboo no ho, na ɔde sika yɛɛ ɛho nkaa no sɛ ɛnyɛ mmeamu no hyehyɛbea, na ɔde sika duraduraa mmeamu no ho.

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Na ɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira nwenee nkyeremu de yɛɛ ntamadan no ano nkataano.

english_verse: They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: Na ɔde bibiri ne asaawa a ɛbere dum ne adidi ne asaawa fitaa a wɔafira yɛɛ mmɔhɔɔ; ɔyɛɛ no ntamanwene mu adwinni a kerubim wɔ mu.

english_verse: They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ ho ɔkanto adum anan, na ɔde sika duraduraa ho; ne nkoropɛe yɛ sika; na ɔde dwetɛ nnyinaso anan guu ase.

english_verse: They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ ɛho adum anum ne nkoropɛe, na ɔde sika duraduraa n'atifi ne ne mmeae ho, na ne nnyinaso anum yɛ kɔbere.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Mfitiaseɛ no Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Na asase da hɔ hunu a ɛnni bɔbea biara, na esum wɔ ebunu no ani. Na Onyankopɔn honhom butu nsuo no ani.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ hann! Na ɛyɛɛ hann.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu hann no sɛ ɛyɛ. Na Onyankopɔn paee hann ne esum no mu.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ hann no sɛ adekyee, ne esum no adesae. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛdi kan ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ewiem mmra, na ɛmmɛpae nsuo no mu.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ ewiem no ɔsoro. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so mmienu ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nsuo a ɛwɔ ɔsoro aseɛ no mmoaboa ano wɔ faako, na wɔnhunu asase pɛsɛɛ. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ pɛsɛɛ no asase, na nsuo mmoano no, ɔfrɛɛ no ɛpo. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Asase mfifiri nwira, mfudeɛ, nnuaba sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na asase fifirii nwira ne nnuaba sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nkanea mmra ewiem, na ɛmmɛpae awia ne anadwo mu, na ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ mma mmerɛ, nna ne mfeɛ nkyekyɛmu.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Bio, na ɛnyɛ nkanea wɔ ewiem, na ɛnhyerɛn wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ nkanea akɛseɛ mmienu no, sɛ kɛseɛ no nni adekyeeɛ so, na ketewa no, sɛ ɛnni anadwo so. Ɔyɛɛ nsoromma nso.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn de sisii ewiem sɛ ɛnhyerɛn wɔ asase so,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: na ɛnni adekyeeɛ ne adesaeɛ so, na ɛmpae hann ne esum no mu. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nnan ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Nsuo no nnɔre abɔdeɛ a ɛte aseɛ pii, na ntakraboa ntu mfa asase so wɔ ewiem.

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ nsuboa akɛseɛ ne nketewa ahodoɔ sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ; ne ntakraboa nyinaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔ, na monyɛ ɛpo mu ma, na ntakraboa nnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nnum ne no.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Abɔdeɛ a ɛtete aseɛ mfiri asase mu mmra, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ: Ntɔteboa a ɛwɔ fie ne wiram ne mmoa a wɔwea ne asase so mmoadoma, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ asase so mmoadoma, ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea fam nyinaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ. Na Onyankopɔn hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Momma yɛnyɛ onipa wɔ yɛn suban so sɛ yɛn nsɛsoɔ, na wɔnni ɛpo mu mpataa, ewiem nnomaa, ntɔteboa, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa wɔ ne suban so. Aane, Nyankopɔn suban so na ɔbɔɔ no, ɔbarima ne ɔbaa na ɔbɔɔ wɔn.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔre, na monyɛ asase so ma, na monya so tumi; na monni ɛpo mu mpataa ne ewiem nnomaa ne mmoa a wɔwɔ asase soɔ nyinaa so.

english_verse: I have provided all kinds of fruit and grain for you to eat.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, mede mfudeɛ a ɛwɔ asase ani nyinaa ne nnuaba nyinaa mama mo sɛ ɛnyɛ mo aduane.

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne ewiem nnomaa nyinaa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ nyinaa, mede nhahan mono mama wɔn sɛ wɔnni. Na ɛyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu deɛ ɔyɛeɛ nyinaa, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ pa ara. Na adeɛ sae, na adeɛ kyee, da a ɛtɔ so nsia ne no.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Na wɔwiee ɔsoro ne asase ne deɛ ɛwɔ mu nyinaa bɔ.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa da a ɛtɔ so nson no so, na ɔtee ho, ɛfiri sɛ ɛno mu na ɔhome firii n’adwuma a ɔyɛeɛ wɔ adebɔ mu no nyinaa ho. Eden turo no

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: Na afuo mu nnua nyinaa nnya mmaa asase so, na afuo mu nhahan nyinaa nnya mfifirii, ɛfiri sɛ na AWURADE Nyankopɔn nnya ntɔɔ nsuo nguu asase no so, na na onipa a ɔbɛdɔ asase nni hɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Na nsuo firi asase so foroe, na ɛfɔɔ asase ani nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de fam dɔteɛ nwonoo onipa, na ɔhuu nkwa home guu ne hwene mu, na onipa yɛɛ ɔkra teasefoɔ.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ turo bi wɔ Eden a ɛwɔ apueeɛ fam, na ɔde onipa a ɔnwonoo no no tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnua ahodoɔ nyinaa a wɔhwɛ a, ɛyɛ fɛ, na ɛyɛ sɛ wɔdie asase no so, ne nkwa dua a ɛsi turo no mfimfini, ne papa ne bɔne ho nimdeɛ dua fifirii asase no so.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Na asuo bi tene firi Eden bɛfɔ turo no, na ɛfiri hɔ ara na emu paapae yɛɛ nsutire nnan.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Deɛ ɛdi kan no din de Pison, ɛno na ɛkonton twa Hawila asase a sika wɔ soɔ no nyinaa ho hyiae.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Na asase no so sika yɛ papa. Ɛhɔ na bedola aduhwam ne apopobibireboɔ wɔ.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na asuo a ɛtɔ so mmienu no din de Gihon. Ɛno na ɛkonton twa Kus asase nyinaa ho hyia.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na asuo a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no ne Tigri, ɛno na ɛsene wɔ Asiria apueeɛ. Na asuo a ɛtɔ so nnan ne Eufrate.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de onipa no kɔtenaa Eden turom sɛ ɔnnɔ na ɔnwɛn hɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ onipa no sɛ: Turom ha nnua nyinaa, di bi.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Na mmom papa ne bɔne ho nimdeɛ dua no deɛ, nni; ɛfiri sɛ da a wobɛdi bie no, wuo na wobɛwuo.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ sɛ onipa nko tena; mɛyɛ ne nsɛsoɔ boafoɔ mama no.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnahɔɔ tɔɔ onipa no so, na ɔdae. Na ɔyii ne mfe mpadeɛ mu baako, na ɔde nam tuaa ananmu.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de mpadeɛ a ɔyi firii onipa no mu no yɛɛ ɔbaa, na ɔde no brɛɛ onipa no.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na onipa no kaa sɛ: Ampa ara, me nnompe mu dompe, ne me honam mu nam ankasa nie. Oyi na wɔbɛfrɛ no Ɔbaa, ɛfiri sɛ Ɔbarima mu na wɔyii no firiiɛ.

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Saa nti na ɔbarima bɛgya n’agya ne na hɔ, na ɔde ne ho akɔbata ne yere ho, na wɔayɛ honam korɔ.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu no deda adagya, ɔbarima no ne ne yere, nanso wɔn ani anwu.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ yɛ aniteɛ kyɛne wiram mmoadoma a AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ wɔn nyinaa. Na ɔbisaa ɔbaa no sɛ: Ampa ara sɛ Onyankopɔn aka akyerɛ mo sɛ: Monnni turom ha nnua nyinaa bi?

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa no buaa ɔwɔ no sɛ: Turom ha nnua aba no, yɛdi bi;

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: nanso dua a ɛsi turo no mfimfini no aba deɛ, Onyankopɔn aka sɛ: Monnni bi, nso mommfa mo nsa nnka, na moanwu.

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbaa no sɛ: Ɛnyɛ wuo na mobɛwuo;

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: na Onyankopɔn nim sɛ da a mobɛdi bie no, mo ani bɛbue, na moayɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn ahunu papa ne bɔne.

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa no hunuu sɛ dua no yɛ sɛ wɔdie, na ɛyɛ aniwa fɛ, ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ, na ɛbɛte ani, enti ɔtee n’aba bi, na ɔdii, na ɔde bi maa ne kunu a ɔka ne ho no nso, na ɔdii.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu ani buebuee, na wɔhunuu sɛ wɔdeda adagya, enti wɔpempam borɔdɔma ahahan yɛɛ nkatanim fae.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Na wɔtee AWURADE Nyankopɔn nka sɛ ɔnam turom hɔ wɔ anwummerɛ mferɛ mu. Na Adam ne ne yere kɔhunta firii AWURADE Nyankopɔn anim wɔ turom hɔ nnua mu.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn frɛɛ Adam, na ɔbisaa no sɛ: Wowɔ he?

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Metee wo nka wɔ turom hɔ no, mesuroe, ɛfiri sɛ meda adagya, na mehuntae.

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa no sɛ: Hwan na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo sɛ woda adagya? Dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni bie no na woadie yi?

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Na Adam kaa sɛ: Ɔbaa no a wode no bɛkaa me ho no, ɔno na ɔmaa me dua no aba no bie, na mediiɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔbaa no sɛ: Adɛn na woyɛɛ saa? Na ɔbaa no se: Ɔwɔ no na ɔdaadaa me, maa mediiɛ. Onipa bu atɛn

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Ɛnam sɛ woayɛ yei nti, wɔadome wo ntɔteboa ne wiram mmoadoma nyinaa mu. Wo yafunu so na wobɛnanteɛ, na woadi dɔteɛ wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Na mede ɔtan bɛto wo ne ɔbaa no ntam, ɛne w’asefoɔ ne n’asefoɔ ntam; ɔno na ɔbɛbɔ wo tire, na wo nso woaka ne nantin.

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ɔbaa no deɛ, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dɔ na mɛma wo yea ne wo nyinsɛn mu brɛ adɔɔso. Yea mu na wobɛwo mma, na w’ani bɛgyina wo kunu, na ɔno na ɔbɛdi wo soɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na Adam deɛ, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ woatie wo yere nne, na woadi dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nnie no bie nti, wo nti wɔadome asase. Yea mu na wobɛdidi soɔ wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Na nkasɛɛ ne nnɛnkyɛnse na ɛbɛfifiri ama woɔ, na woadi afuo mu ahahan.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: W’anim fifire mu na wobɛdidie de akɔsi sɛ wobɛsane akɔ dɔteɛ mu, ɛfiri sɛ emu na wɔyii wo firiiɛ; na woyɛ dɔteɛ, na dɔteɛ mu na wobɛsane akorɔ.

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Na Adam too ne yere din Hawa, ɛfiri sɛ ɔno na ɔyɛ ateasefoɔ nyinaa na.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ nwoma ntadeɛ maa Adam ne ne yere de hyɛɛ wɔn. Wɔpamo Adam ne Hawa firi turo no mu

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, onipa no ayɛ sɛ yɛn mu baako, ahunu papa ne bɔne. Na afei, deɛ ɛbɛyɛ na wantene ne nsa ante nkwa dua no nso bi anni antena ase daa nti,

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: AWURADE Nyankopɔn tuu no firii Eden turom hɔ sɛ ɔnkɔdɔ asase a wɔfaa no firii mu no.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Na ɔpamm onipa no, na ɔde Kerubim ne ogyaframa afena a ɛdi ahim bɛsii Eden turo no anim apueeɛ fam sɛ wɔnwɛn ɔkwan a ɛde kɔ nkwa dua no ho no.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere Hawa daeɛ, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Kain. Na ɔkaa sɛ: AWURADE adaworoma manya ɔbarima.

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo ne nua Habel kaa ne ho. Na Habel yɛ odwanhwɛfoɔ, ɛna Kain nso yɛ okuafoɔ.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa sɛ nna bi akyiri no, Kain de afuom nnoɔma bɛyɛɛ AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Na Habel nso de ne nnwan mu mmakan ne wɔn a wɔadɔre no bi bɛmae. Na AWURADE ani sɔɔ Habel ne n’afɔrebɔdeɛ no,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: nanso Kain ne n’afɔrebɔdeɛ no deɛ, n’ani ansɔ. Kain bo fuu pii, na ɔmunae.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Adɛn nti na wo bo afuo na woamuna yi?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Sɛ woyɛɛ no yie a, anka w’anim rente anaa? Na sɛ woanyɛ no yie enti, bɔne butu ɛpono ano, na w’akyiri kwan na ɛhwehwɛ, nanso di ne so.

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Na Kain ka kyerɛɛ ne nua sɛ, ma yɛn nkɔ afuom. Na ɛbaa sɛ wɔwɔ afuom no, Kain sɔre tiaa ne nua Habel, na ɔkumm no.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Ɛhe na wo nua Habel wɔ? Na ɔse: Mennim, me nua so hwɛfoɔ ne me anaa?

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ yi? Wo nua mogya nne reteam frɛ me firi asase so.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Na afei wɔadome wo afiri asase a abue n’ano agye wo nua mogya afiri wo nsam no so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Sɛ wodɔ asase a, ɛrenkɔ so mma wo ne nnɔbaeɛ bio na wobɛyɛ ɔkobɔni ne asesabɔni wɔ asase so.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, woapamo me nnɛ afiri asase yi so, na mɛhunta mafiri w’anim, na mayɛ ɔkobɔni ne asesabɔni wɔ asase so, na obiara a ɔbɛhu me no, ɔbɛku me.

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛno nti obiara a ɔbɛkum Kain no, wɔbɛtɔ ne so werɛ ahodoɔ nson. Na AWURADE yɛɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ bi maa Kain, na obiara a ɔbɛhu no no anku no.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Na Kain firii AWURADE anim kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Nod asase so wɔ Eden apueeɛ. Kain asefoɔ

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Na Kain ne ne yere dae, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Henok. Na ɔkyekyeree kuro bi, na ɔde ne ba Henok din too kuro no.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Na Henok woo Irad, na Irad woo Mehuyael. Na Mehuyael woo Metusael, na Metusael woo Lamek.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Na Sila nso woo Tubalkain a ɔyɛ kɔbere mfrafraeɛ ne dadeɛ adeɛ nyinaa atomfoɔ agya. Na Tubalkain nuabaa ne Naama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Na Lamek ka kyerɛɛ ne yerenom sɛ: Ada ne Sila, montie me nne; Lamek yerenom, monyɛ aso mma m’asɛm: Mekumm ɔbarima sɛ ɔpiraa me, mekumm aberanteɛ sɛ ɔboroo me.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔtɔɔ Kain so werɛ mprɛnson a, Lamek deɛ bɛyɛ aduɔson nson. Set ne Enos awoɔ

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere daeɛ bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo ne din Set sɛ: Onyankopɔn de ɔba foforɔ asi me Habel a Kain kumm no no ananmu.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Set nso, wɔwoo ɔba maa no, na ɔtoo ne din Enos. Ɛberɛ no mu na wɔfirii aseɛ bɔɔ AWURADE din sɔree no.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Na Henok ne Onyankopɔn nantee, na wɔanhunu no bio, ɛfiri sɛ Onyankopɔn faa no kɔe.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo ne din Noa, na ɔkaa sɛ: Oyi na ɔbɛkyekyere yɛn werɛ wɔ yɛn nnwuma ne yɛn nsa ano brɛ mu wɔ asase a AWURADE adome no soɔ.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Nyankopɔn mma hunuu nnipa mmammaa sɛ wɔn ho yɛ fɛ, na wɔwarewaree wɔn mu biara a wɔpɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Me honhom rentena onipa mu nkɔsi daa, ɛfiri sɛ wɔyɛ honam, enti ne nna bɛyɛ mfeɛ ɔha aduonu.

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Nna no mu ne akyire no, na abrane akɛseɛ wɔ asase so. Na Nyankopɔn mma kɔɔ nnipa mmammaa ho na wɔwoo mma maa wɔn no, yeinom ne aberempɔn a wɔwɔ din firi tete.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hunuu sɛ nnipa bɔne dɔɔso pii wɔ asase so, na wɔn akoma mu nsusuiɛ nyinaa yɛ bɔne nko daa nyinaa.

english_verse: He was sorry that he had made them,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nuu ne ho sɛ ɔyɛɛ onipa wɔ asase soɔ, na ɛyɛɛ no ya n’akomam.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Mɛpepa nnipa a mabɔ wɔn no afiri asase ani, ampa ara, ɛfiri onipa so kɔsi ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne ewiem nnomaa so, ɛfiri sɛ manu me ho sɛ meyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Na Noa deɛ, ɔnyaa adom AWURADE anim. Noa adaka no

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Yei ne Noa ho asɛm: Na Noa yɛ onipa tenenee a ɔyɛ pɛ wɔ ne berɛ so nnipa mu. Noa ne Onyankopɔn nanteeɛ.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Na Noa woo mmammarima baasa, Sem, Ham, ne Yafet.

english_verse: God knew that everyone was terribly cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hunuu asase, na hwɛ, asɛe, ɛfiri sɛ na nnipa nyinaa asɛe wɔn akwan wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Fa ɔwawa yɛ adaka, na yɛ mpia wɔ adaka no mu, na fa ama ka emu ne ɛho.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Noa yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no nyinaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, me, mede nsuyire bɛba asase so mabɛsɛe abɔdeɛ a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa ɔsoro ase; asase so adeɛ nyinaa rebɛwuwu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Na me ne wo bɛyɛ apam ato hɔ, na woakɔ adaka no mu, wo ne wo mma, ne wo yere, ne wo mma yerenom.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nnomaa sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, ne ntɔteboa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ nyinaa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ, wɔn nyinaa mu mmienu mmienu mmra wo nkyɛn, na wɔanya nkwa.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Na wo deɛ, boaboa aduane nyinaa bi ano kɔ mu, na ayɛ wo ne wɔn aduane.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ: Wo ne wo fiefoɔ nyinaa, monkɔ adaka no mu, ɛfiri sɛ wo na mahu wo sɛ ɔteneneeni m’anim, ɛberɛ yi mu.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Mmoa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu, fa nson nson, anini ne abedeɛ. Na mmoa a wɔn ho nteɛ mu, fa mmienu mmienu, onini ne ɔbedeɛ;

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: ewiem nnomaa mu nso fa nson nson, anini ne abedeɛ, na wɔn ase nnya nkwa asase nyinaa ani.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: mmienu mmienu baa Noa nkyɛn adaka no mu, onini ne ɔbedeɛ, sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ Noa no.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Na nnanson akyiri no, nsuyire baa asase so.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Na osuo tɔɔ asase so pii adaduanan, awia ne anadwo.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Saa da yi ara mu na Noa ne ne yere, ne ne mma, Sem, Ham ne Yafet, ne ne mma yerenom baasa akɔhyɛ adaka no mu.

english_verse: They took along every kind of animal, tame and wild, including the birds.
translation_verse: Na mmoadoma nyinaa, ntɔteboa, mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ, ntuboa nyinaa, sɛdeɛ wɔn su teɛ,

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: ne wɔn na ɛkɔɔ mu. Honam a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa mu mmienu mmienu na wɔbaa Noa nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Wɔn a ɛbaeɛ no, na wɔyɛ honam nyinaa mu anini ne abedeɛ, sɛdeɛ Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no; na AWURADE too no mu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nsuo no boroo so kɔɔ soro basafa nson ne fa na ɛkataa mmepɔ so.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na abɔdeɛ a ɛte aseɛ nyinaa, nnomaa, ntɔteboa, wiram mmoa, mmoa a wɔwea asase soɔ, ne nnipa nyinaa;

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na nsuo no yirii wɔ asase so nna ɔha aduonum.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaee Noa ne mmoadoma nyinaa ne ntɔteboa nyinaa a wɔne no wɔ adaka no mu nyinaa. Na Onyankopɔn maa mframa bɔ faa asase so, na nsuo no ano brɛɛ ase.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na ebunu no nsuo aniwa sisii, na ɔsoro mpomma mu totoe, maa osuo a ɛfiri soro no gyaee tɔ;

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na ɛda a ɛtɔ so dunson wɔ bosome nson mu no, adaka no kɔsii Ararat mmepɔ so.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Na nsuo no kɔɔ so twee ara kɔsii bosome a ɛtɔ so du no so; na saa bosome no ara, ne da a ɛdi kan no na mmepɔ atifi dedaa adie.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔsomaa anene. Na ɔfirii adi, na ɔdii akɔneaba de kɔsii sɛ nsuo no wee asase soɔ.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa aburuburo sɛ ɔnkɔhwɛ sɛ nsuo no awe wɔ asase ani anaa.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Nanso aburuburo no annya ne nan sibea, na ɔsane baa ne nkyɛn adaka no mu, ɛfiri sɛ na nsuo no da so wɔ asase nyinaa ani. Na ɔtenee ne nsa faa no baa ne nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnanson bio, na ɔsomaa aburuburo firii adaka no mu bio.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Na aburuburo no baa ne nkyɛn anwummerɛ, na hwɛ, ngo dua ahahan frɔmfrɔm tua n’ano. Noa hunuu sɛ nsuo no awe asase so.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnanson bio no, ɔsomaa aburuburo no; na wansane amma ne nkyɛn bio.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Bosome a ɛtɔ so mmienu no da a ɛtɔ so aduonu nson no na na asase so awo koraa.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ:

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: Firi adaka no mu, wo ne wo yere, wo mma ne wɔn yerenom a wɔka wo ho;

english_verse: Let out the birds, animals, and reptiles, so they can mate and live all over the earth.”
translation_verse: mmoadoma a wɔka wo ho nyinaa a ɛfiri honam nyinaa mu, nnomaa ne ntɔteboa ne deɛ ɛwea asase soɔ nyinaa ne wo mfiri adi, na wɔnwo, na wɔnnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: After Noah and his family had left the boat,
translation_verse: Na Noa ne ne yere, ne ne mma ne wɔn yerenom firii adi;

english_verse: the living creatures left in groups of their own kind. The Lord's Promise for the Earth
translation_verse: mmoadoma nyinaa, wɔn a wɔwea nyinaa ne nnomaa nyinaa, ne deɛ nkwa wɔ mu biara, sɛdeɛ wɔn mmoaban teɛ, firi adaka no mu firii adi. Noa afɔrebɔ

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na Noa sii afɔrebukyia maa AWURADE, na ɔfaa ntɔteboa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu bi ne nnomaa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa mu bi de wɔn bobɔɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ wɔ bukyia no so.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE tee afɔdeɛ no hwam no, ɔkaa no n’akoma mu sɛ: Onipa nti merennome asase bio, ɛfiri sɛ onipa akoma mu adwene yɛ bɔne firi ne mmɔfraase, na merensɛe deɛ ɛte aseɛ nyinaa bio, sɛdeɛ mayɛ yi.

english_verse: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat; winter and summer, day and night.
translation_verse: Nna a asase wɔ hɔ yi nyinaa, oguo ne otwa, awɔ ne ahuhuro, asuso ne ɔpɛ, awia ne anadwo rennyae da.

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa Noa ne ne mma, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo na monnɔɔso, na monhyɛ asase so ma.

english_verse: All animals, birds, reptiles, and fish will be afraid of you. I have placed them under your control,
translation_verse: Na mo ho hu ne mo ho suro mmra asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne ewiem nnomaa nyinaa, deɛ ɛwea fam nyinaa ne ɛpo mu mpataa nyinaa so; mo nsa na wɔde wɔn ahyɛ.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Deɛ ɛkeka ne ho a ɛwɔ nkwa nyinaa, ɛnyɛ mo aduane; mede ne nyinaa mama mo, sɛdeɛ mede nhahan mono memaa mo no.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Nam a ne mogya da so wɔ ne mu nko na monnnie.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na mo deɛ, monwo na monnɔ, na monnɔɔso wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Noa ne ne mma a wɔka ne ho no sɛ:

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, afei merema m’apam atim hɔ ama mo ne mo asefoɔ a ɛbɛdi mo akyi,

english_verse: This includes the birds and the animals that came out of the boat.
translation_verse: ɛne akra a ɛtete aseɛ a ɛka mo ho nyinaa, nnomaa, ntɔteboa ne asase so mmoadoma a wɔne mo wɔ hɔ firi adaka no mu nyinaa.

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: Na mama me ne mo apam yi agyina hɔ, sɛ meremfa nsuyire mensɛe abɔdeɛ nyinaa bio, na nsuyire remma mmɛsɛe asase bio.

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Me nyankontɔn na mede masi mununkum mu, na ayɛ me ne asase ntam apam no ho nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Na sɛ mede mununkum meba asase so a, wɔbɛhunu nyankontɔn no wɔ mununkum no mu;

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: na makae m’apam a ɛwɔ me ne mo, ne abɔdeɛ nyinaa mu ateasefoɔ ntam no, na nsuo annane nsuyire ansɛe abɔdeɛ nyinaa bio.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Na nyankontɔn no bɛba mununkum mu, na mahwɛ, na mede makae daa apam a ɛwɔ Onyankopɔn ne nnipa ne abɔdeɛ mu ateasefoɔ a ɛwɔ asase soɔ nyinaa no ntam.

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Noa mma a wɔfirii adaka no mu firii adie ne Sem, Ham ne Yafet; na Ham ne Kanaan n’agya.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Noa mma baasa no. Wɔn mu na nnipa firi petee asase nyinaa soɔ.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Na Noa firii aseɛ yɛɛ kua, na ɔyɛɛ bobeturo.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔnom nsa no bi, na ɔboroe, na ɔda ne ntomadan mu a ne ho da hɔ.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Na Kanaan agya Ham kɔhunuu n’agya adagya mu, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom baanu no wɔ adihɔ.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
