translation_verse: Na wɔfrɛɛ Rebeka ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo ne ɔbarima yi bɛkɔ anaa? Na ɔse: Mɛkɔ.

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Na wɔgyaa wɔn nua Rebeka ne n’abaawa panin ne Abraham somfoɔ no ne ne nnipa no kwan.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Na wɔhyiraa Rebeka see no sɛ: Yɛn nuabaa, dane mpem du ahodoɔ mpem mpem, na w’asefoɔ mfa wɔn atamfoɔ apono nni.

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Na Rebeka ne ne mmaawa sɔree, na wɔtenatenaa yoma so dii ɔbarima no akyi, na ɔsomfoɔ no de Rebeka sii mu kɔe.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Na Isak firi Lahai-roi abura ho bae, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔte Negeb asase no so.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔsomfoɔ no sɛ: Ɔbarima bɛn na ɔnam wira mu rebɛhyia yɛn yi? Na ɔsomfoɔ no se: Ɛyɛ me wura. Na ɔfaa ne nkatanimu de kataa n’anim.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomfoɔ no kaa deɛ ɔyɛeɛ no nyinaa kyerɛɛ Isak.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Na Isak de no kɔɔ ne na Sara ntomadan mu, na ɔwaree Rebeka, na ɔyɛɛ no ɛyerɛ, na ɔdɔ no. Na Isak werɛ kyekyeree, ne na wuo no akyi.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo Simran, Yoksan, Medan, Midian, Isbak ne Sua maa no.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Na Yoksan woo Seba ne Dedan. Na Dedan mma ne Asurfoɔ, Letusfoɔ ne Leumfoɔ.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Na Midian mma ne Hefa, Hefer, Hanok, Abida ne Eldaa. Yeinom nyinaa ne Ketura mma.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: Na mmaa nkae mma a Abraham wɔ no deɛ, berɛ a Abraham te aseɛ no, ɔkyɛɛ wɔn adeɛ, na ɔgyaa wɔn kwan firii ne ba Isak ho maa wɔkɔɔ apueeɛ asase no so. Abraham wuo ne ne sie

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Na Abraham wuo akyiri no, Onyankopɔn hyiraa ne ba Isak. Na Isak tenaa Lahai-roi abura no ho. Ismael awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ (

english_verse: Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah.
translation_verse: Na yei ne Abraham ba Ismael a Misraimni Hagar, Sara afenaa no, wo maa Abraham no awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ:

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: Misma, Duma, Masa,

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: Hadad, Tema, Yetur, Nafis ne Kedema.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Ismael mma, na yeinom ne wɔn din, sɛdeɛ wɔn nkuraa ne wɔn nsraban teɛ, atitire dummienu ne wɔn aman.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: Na wɔtena firi Hawila kɔsii Sur a ɛwɔ Misraim ntentensoɔ de rekɔ Asiria no. Na ɔne ne nuanom antena no asomdwoeɛ mu. Esau ne Yakob awoɔ

english_verse: Isaac was the son of Abraham,
translation_verse: Na yeinom ne Abraham ba Isak awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ: Abraham woo Isak.

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Na Isak srɛɛ AWURADE maa ne yere, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔyɛ obonini. Na AWURADE tiee n’adesrɛ no, na ne yere Rebeka nyinsɛnee.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Na nkɔkoaa no pempem wɔn ho wɔ ne yam. Na ɔse: Sɛ ɛte saa a, na mete ase reyɛ deɛn? Na ɔkɔbisaa AWURADE.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Aman mmienu na ɛwɔ wo yam, na nkurɔfoɔ ahodoɔ mmienu na ɛbɛtete wɔn ho mu afiri wo yafunu mu. Na ɔman no baako bɛdi baako so, na ɔpanin no bɛsom akumaa no.

english_verse: the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau.
translation_verse: Na deɛ ɔdi kan firi baeɛ no, na ne ho yɛ kɔɔ, ne ho nyinaa wɔ enwi kusuu. Enti wɔtoo no din Esau.

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Na mmɔfra no nyinii. Na Esau nim ahayɔ yie, na ɔyɛ ɔhamuni, na Yakob deɛ na ɔyɛ onipa a ɔmpɛ kasa a daa ɔte ntomadan mu.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Na Isak dɔ Esau, ɛfiri sɛ na ne hanam yɛ no dɛ; na Rebeka deɛ, ɔdɔ Yakob.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Yakob noaa aduane bi, na Esau firi wiram baeɛ no, na wabrɛ.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Na Esau ka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Ma me adeɛ kɔkɔɔ yi bi menni ɛ, na mabrɛ.

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: Tɔn wo panin ma me nnɛ.

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, wuo na merebɛwuo yi, na ɔpanin yi bɛyɛ me deɛn?

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: Ka ntam kyerɛ me nnɛ. Na ɔkaa ntam kyerɛɛ no tɔn ne panin maa Yakob.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob maa Esau paanoo ne asedua a wanoa; na ɔdii, na ɔdidi nomee, na ɔsɔre kɔe. Na sɛdeɛ Esau ammu ne panin ne no.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Na ɛkɔm baa asase no so, ɛsono ɛkɔm a ɛbaa Abraham berɛ soɔ no. Na Isak kɔɔ Filistifoɔ hene Abimelek nkyɛn wɔ Gerar.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yii ne ho kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsiane nkɔ Misraim, tena asase a mɛkyerɛ woɔ yi so.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Tena asase yi so sɛ ɔhɔhoɔ, na mɛdi w’akyi na mahyira wo, ɛfiri sɛ wo ne w’asefoɔ na mede nsase yi nyinaa bɛma mo, na mɛma ntam a mekaa w’agya Abraham no agyina.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Na mɛma w’asefoɔ adɔre sɛ ɔsoro nsoromma, na mede nsase yi nyinaa bɛma w’asefoɔ, na w’asefoɔ mu na wɔbɛhyira asase so amanaman nyinaa,

english_verse: because Abraham did everything I told him to do.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ Abraham tiee me nne, na ɔdii me nsiesieeɛ, me mmara nsɛm, m’ahyɛdeɛ ne me mmara so.

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: Na Isak tenaa Gerar.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Na ɛhɔfoɔ no bisaa no ne yere ho asɛm no, ɔkaa sɛ: Me nua ne no. Na ɔsuro sɛ ɔbɛka sɛ: Me yere ne no, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Anyɛ saa a, Rebeka nti ɛhafoɔ bɛku me; ɛfiri sɛ ne ho yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Na ɔkyɛree hɔ no, Filistifoɔ hene Abimelek hwɛɛ mpomma mu hunui, na hwɛ, Isak ne ne yere Rebeka rewewe.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek frɛɛ Isak sɛ: Hwɛ, ampa ara ɔyɛ wo yere, na ɛyɛɛ dɛn na wose: Ɔyɛ me nua yi? Na Isak ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛfiri sɛ medwenee sɛ: Anyɛ saa a, ne nti mɛwu.

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Na Abimelek kaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ yɛn yi? Ɛkaa kumaa bi na anka ɔman yi muni bi ne wo yere dae, na anka wode mmusuo aba yɛn so.

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek hyɛɛ ne nkurɔfoɔ nyinaa sɛ: Deɛ ɔbɛka ɔbarima yi anaa ne yere no, wuo na ɔbɛwuo.

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Na Isak duaa mfudeɛ wɔ asase no so, na ɔnyaa nnɔbaeɛ mmɔho ɔha; afirinhyia no ara mu ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE hyiraa no.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Na Isak nyaa ne ho, na ɔkɔɔ so ara nyaa ne ho kɔsii sɛ ɔyɛɛ kɛseɛ pa ara.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: Na ɔnyaa nnwankuo ne anantwikuo ne nkoa pii. Na Filistifoɔ no ani beree no.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ka kyerɛɛ Isak sɛ: Firi yɛn nkyɛn kɔ, na wowɔ tumi dodo sene yɛn.

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Na Isak sane tetee nsubura a n’agya Abraham berɛ so wɔtutuiɛ a Abraham wuo akyi Filistifoɔ sisii no no mu. Na ɔtotoo no din sɛdeɛ n’agya totoeɛ no ara.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Na Isak nkoa funuu bonhwa no mu, na wɔhunuu nsupa abura wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Na Gerar mmoahwɛfoɔ ne Isak mmoahwɛfoɔ dii so aperepereɛ kaa sɛ: Nsuo no yɛ yɛn dea! Enti Isak too abura no din Esek, ɛfiri sɛ wɔne no hamee.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Na wɔtuu asubura foforɔ, na ɛno ho nso wɔpereperee, enti ɔfrɛɛ no Sitna.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Na wɔfirii hɔ kɔtuu abura foforɔ, na ɛno deɛ, wɔampere, enti ɔtoo no din Rehobot, na ɔkaa sɛ: Afei deɛ AWURADE ama yɛn mu atrɛ, na yɛadɔre wɔ asase yi so.

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Na ɔfirii hɔ kɔɔ Beer-seba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yii ne ho kyerɛɛ no anadwo no ara kaa sɛ: Mene w’agya Abraham Nyankopɔn, nsuro, na medi w’akyi. Mɛhyira wo, na m’akoa Abraham nti mɛma w’asefoɔ adɔre.

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Na ɔsii afɔrebukyia wɔ hɔ, na ɔsɔree AWURADE, na ɔsii ne ntomadan wɔ hɔ. Na Isak nkoa tuu asubura wɔ hɔ. Abraham ne Abimelek yɛ apam

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ne n’adamfo Ahusat ne ne safohene Pikol firi Gerar baa ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Na Isak ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdeɛn nti na moaba me nkyɛn yi? Sɛ motane me, na moapamo me afiri mo nkyɛn.

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Yɛahunu pefee sɛ AWURADE di w’akyi. Na yɛse: Ma ntam nna yɛne wo ntam. Na ma yɛne wo mpam,

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: sɛ worenyɛ yɛn bɔne biara; sɛdeɛ yɛanka woɔ, na yɛayɛ wo papa nko ara, na yɛagya wo kwan asomdwoeɛ mu no. Afei wone deɛ AWURADE ahyira no.

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo wɔn pono, na wɔdidi nomee.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Na wɔsɔree anɔpatutu kekaa ntam kyerɛkyerɛɛ wɔn ho, na Isak gyaa wɔn kwan, na wɔde asomdwoeɛ firi ne nkyɛn kɔe.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Na da no ara Isak nkoa ba bɛkaa no abura a wɔtuiɛ no ho asɛm sɛ: Yɛato nsuo.

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ no Siba. Enti kuro no din de Beer-seba de bɛsi nnɛ yi ara. Esau ananafoɔ yerenom

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Na Isak bɔɔ akɔkoraa na n’ani so yɛɛ no kusukusu na ɔnhunu adeɛ yie no, ɔmaa wɔfrɛɛ ne ba panin Esau ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me ba! Na ɔgyee so sɛ: Agya, menie.

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Mabɔ akora, na mennim me wuda.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Afei fa w’ahayɔdeɛ, w’agyan kotokuo ne w’agyan kɔ wiram kɔpɛ hanam brɛ me,

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: na noa akɔnnɔduane sɛdeɛ mepɛ brɛ me, na menni, na me nhyira wo ansa na mawu.

english_verse: Rebekah had been listening, and as soon as Esau left to go hunting,
translation_verse: Ɛberɛ a Isak rekasa akyerɛ ne ba Esau no, Rebeka tee. Na Esau kɔɔ wiram sɛ ɔrekɔkum nam aba.

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: Na Rebeka ka kyerɛɛ ne ba Yakob sɛ: Hwɛ, metee sɛ w’agya rekasa kyerɛ wo nua Esau sɛ:

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: Kɔpɛ hanam brɛ me, na noa m’akɔnnɔduane, na menni, na menhyira wo AWURADE anim ansa na mawu.

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: Na afei, me ba, tie me nne, sɛdeɛ merehyɛ woɔ yi:

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Kɔ mmoakuo no mu kɔkyere mmirekyie mma pa mmienu brɛ me, na memfa menyɛ akɔnnɔduane memma w’agya sɛdeɛ ɔpɛ;

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: na fa kɔma w’agya, na ɔnni, na ɔnhyira wo ansa na wawu.

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ ne na Rebeka sɛ: Hwɛ, me nua Esau ho wɔ nwi, na me deɛ, me ho yɛ toromtorom.

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Ebia m’agya bɛka me ho ahwɛ, na mayɛ n’ani so sɛ ɔdaadaafoɔ, na mede nnome maba me so, na ɛnyɛ nhyira.

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ne na ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo nnome mmra me so, me ba, tie me nne ara, na kɔkyere wɔn brɛ me.

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔkyeree wɔn brɛɛ ne na, na ne na de yɛɛ akɔnnɔduane sɛdeɛ n’agya pɛ.

english_verse: Then she took Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Rebeka faa ne ba panin Esau ntadeɛ fɛfɛ a ɛwɔ ne nkyɛn wɔ ɛdan mu de hyɛɛ ne ba kumaa Yakob.

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: Na ɔde mmirekyie mma no nwoma duraduraa ne nsa ne ne kɔn a ɛho yɛ toromtorom no ho.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: Na ɔde akɔnnɔduane ne paanoo a wasiesie no hyɛɛ ne ba Yakob nsa.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Na ɔde kɔɔ n’agya nkyɛn, na ɔse: M’agya! Na ɔgyee so sɛ: Menie, ɛyɛ wo hwan a, me ba?

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Ɛyɛ me, w’abakan Esau. Mayɛ sɛdeɛ wokyerɛɛ me no. Mesrɛ wo, sɔre, tena ase, na di me hanam, na wo kra nhyira me.

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na Isak bisaa ne ba no sɛ: Ɛyɛɛ dɛn na wonyaa no ntɛm sɛɛ yi, me ba? Na ɔse: Ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn na ɔmaa me hyiaa yie.

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Na Isak ka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Twe pini me, na menka wo menhwɛ, me ba, sɛ ampa ara sɛ me ba Esau ne wo anaasɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno a.

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob twe pinii n’agya Isak, na ɔde ne nsa kaa ne ho hwɛe, na ɔkaa sɛ: Ɛnne no yɛ Yakob nne, na nsa no deɛ, ɛyɛ Esau nsa.

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa no sɛ: Ampa ara sɛ wone me ba Esau anaa? Na ɔse: Mene no.

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Fa pini me nkyɛn, na menni me ba hanam, na me kra nhyira wo. Na ɔde brɛɛ no, na ɔdii, na ɔde bobesa brɛɛ no, na ɔnomee.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: Na n’agya Isak ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Twe pini bɛfe m’ano ɛ, me ba.

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwe pinii kɔfee n’ano. Na Isak huaa n’atadeɛ mu hwa hwɛe, na ɔhyiraa no sɛ: Hwɛ, me ba ho hwa te sɛ afuo a AWURADE ahyira soɔ mu hwa.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn mma wo ɔsoro bosuo ne asase mu sradeɛ bi, ne aburoo ne nsa pii.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Aman nsom wo, na nkurɔfoɔ nkoto wo. Yɛ wo nuanom so wura, na wo na mma nkoto wo. Wɔadome wɔn a wɔdome woɔ, na wɔahyira wɔn a wɔhyira woɔ. Esau srɛ Isak hɔ nhyira

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Na Isak wiee Yakob hyira na Yakob firii n’agya nkyɛn firii adi ara pɛ na ne nua Esau firi n’ahayɔ baeɛ.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔno nso bɛnoaa akɔnnɔduane de brɛɛ n’agya ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: M’agya sɔre ɛ, na di wo ba hanam, na wo kra nhyira me!

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Na n’agya Isak see no sɛ: Ɛyɛ wo hwan a? Na ɔse: Ɛyɛ me, wo ba, w’abakan Esau.

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Na Isak de ahopopoɔ kɛseɛ pa ara kaa sɛ: Hwan mpo ne deɛ ɔkɔyɛɛ ha de brɛɛ me, na medii ne nyinaa na mehyiraa no ansa na woreba yi? Nso ɔbɛyɛ deɛ wɔahyira no.

english_verse: Esau cried out in great distress, “Father, give me a blessing too!”
translation_verse: Esau tee n’agya nsɛm no, ɔde su kɛseɛ ne awerɛhoɔ pii teaa mu denden ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: M’agya, hyira me nso bi.

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Wo nua de nnaadaa aba abɛgye wo nhyira.

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ne din nne Yakob anaa? Mprenu ni na watwintwane m’anan mu. Wafa me panin, na hwɛ, afei nso wagye me nhyira. Na ɔse: Woamfa nhyira bi ansie me?

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Na Isak bua see Esau sɛ: Hwɛ, mede no mayɛ wo so wura, na mede ne nuanom nyinaa mayɛ ne nkoa. Na mede aburoo ne nsa mawowa no. Na afei wo deɛ, ɛdeɛn na menyɛ woɔ, me ba?

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Na Esau ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: M’agya, nhyira baako pɛ na wowɔ? Hyira me nso, m’agya. Na Esau maa ne nne so sui.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Na n’agya Isak bua see no sɛ: Hwɛ, asase a sradeɛ nni mu ne deɛ ɔsoro bosuo ngu soɔ so na wobɛtena.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Wo nkrantɛ so na wonam bɛtena aseɛ, na wobɛsom wo nua. Nanso ɛbɛba sɛ wobɔ mmɔden kentene wo ho a, wobɛyi ne kɔnnua afiri wo kɔn so. Esau repɛ Yakob aku no

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Na Esau tanee Yakob wɔ nhyira a n’agya de hyiraa no no nti. Na Esau kaa no n’akoma mu sɛ: Nna a wɔde bɛsu m’agya no reyɛ abɛn, na merebɛkum me nua Yakob.

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔkaa ne ba panin Esau nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ Rebeka. Na ɔsoma maa wɔkɔfrɛɛ ne ba kumaa Yakob, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, wo nua Esau rekyekyere ne werɛ sɛ ɔrebɛku wo.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Afei, me ba, tie me nne, na sɔre dwane kɔ me nua Laban nkyɛn wɔ Haran,

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: na tena ne nkyɛn nna tiaa kɔsi sɛ wo nua anibereɛ no bɛfiri ne mu,

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: kɔsi sɛ wo nua abufuo bɛdane afiri wo soɔ, na ne werɛ afiri deɛ woyɛɛ no no, ansa na masoma ama wɔabɛfa wo wɔ hɔ aba. Na adɛn nti koraa na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwere mo baanu da koro? Isak ma Yakob kɔ Laban nkyɛn

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Na Rebeka ka kyerɛɛ Isak sɛ: Het mmammaa nti m’asetena afono me. Sɛ Yakob kɔware yerɛ Het mmammaa mu, sɛ yeinom a wɔwɔ ɛha yi a, na me mmerɛ ngui, na mete ase reyɛ deɛn bio?

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Na Isak frɛɛ Yakob, na ɔhyiraa no hyɛɛ no sɛ: Nware ɛyerɛ wɔ Kanaan mmammaa mu.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Sɔre kɔ Mesopotamia kɔ wo na n’agya Betuel fie, na kɔware wɔ wo na nua Laban mmammaa mu bi.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn nhyira wo, na ɔmma wo nnɔ, na ɔmma wo nyɛ bebree, na woayɛ aman asafo;

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: na ɔmfa Abraham nhyira nhyira wo, wo ne w’asefoɔ a wɔka wo ho, na woanya asase a woyɛ so hɔhoɔ a Onyankopɔn de ama Abraham yi.

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Na Isak gyaa Yakob kwan, na ɔkɔɔ Mesopotamia wɔ Aramni Betuel ba Laban a ɔyɛ Yakob ne Esau wɔn na Rebeka nuabarima no nkyɛn. Esau ware ɔbaa foforɔ

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Na Esau hunuu sɛ Isak ahyira Yakob, ama wagya no kwan sɛ ɔnkɔ Mesopotamia nkɔware yerɛ wɔ hɔ. Afei ɔhunuu bio sɛ ɔhyiraa no hyɛɛ no sɛ: Nware Kanaan mmammaa mu yerɛ,

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: na Yakob tiee n’agya ne ne na, na ɔkɔɔ Mesopotamia.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Na Esau hunuu sɛ Kanaan mmammaa nyɛ wɔ n’agya Isak ani soɔ no,

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: ɔsii mu kɔɔ Ismael nkyɛn kɔwaree Abraham ba Ismael babaa, Nebaiot nuabaa Mahalat kaa ne yerenom no ho. Yakob daeɛso wɔ Betel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Na Yakob firi Beer-seba sii mu kɔɔ Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Na ɔduruu baabi no ɔsoɛɛ hɔ anadwo no, ɛfiri sɛ na owia akɔtɔ. Na ɔfaa hɔ aboɔ no mu baako de yɛɛ sumiiɛ, na ɔdaa hɔ.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: Na ɔsoo daeɛ, na hwɛ, na atwedeɛ bi si fam a atifi pem soro, na hwɛ, Nyankopɔn abɔfoɔ redi so aforosiane.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, AWURADE gyina atifi, na ɔse: Mene AWURADE, w’agya Abraham Nyankopɔn ne Isak Nyankopɔn; asase a woda soɔ yi mede bɛma wo ne w’asefoɔ.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: Na w’asefoɔ bɛyɛ sɛ asase so mfuturo, na woatrɛ akɔ atɔeɛ ne apueeɛ, atifi fam ne anafoɔ fam. Na wo ne w’asefoɔ mu na wɔbɛhyira wiase mmusuakuo nyinaa.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mɛdi w’akyi, na mahwɛ wo so baabiara a wobɛkorɔ, na mama woasane aba asase yi so. Na merennya wo de bɛkɔ akɔsi sɛ mɛma deɛ maka makyerɛ woɔ yi aba mu.

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob nyane firii ne nna mu no, ɔkaa sɛ: Ampa ara, AWURADE wɔ ha yi, nanso me deɛ, manhunu.

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsuroe, na ɔse: Ɛha yi yɛ hu ampa. Ɛha nyɛ baabiara sɛ Nyankopɔn fie, na ɛha ne ɔsoro aboboano.

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Na Yakob sɔree anɔpatutu, na ɔfaa ɔboɔ a ɔde yɛɛ sumiiɛ no de yɛɛ odum sii hɔ, na ɔhwiee ngo guu so.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ hɔ: Betel, nanso akane no na kuro no din de Lus.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Na Yakob hyɛɛ bɔ kaa sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE Nyankopɔn bɛdi m’akyi ahwɛ me so ɔkwan a merebɛtuo yi mu, na wama me aduane madi ne atadeɛ mahyɛ,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: na wasane me asomdwoeɛ mu de me aba m’agya fie a, ɛnneɛ AWURADE bɛyɛ me Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔboɔ yi a mede mayɛ odum asi hɔ yi bɛyɛ Nyankopɔn fie. Na deɛ wobɛma me nyinaa, mɛma wo so ntotosoɔ du du.

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii mu kɔɔ nnipa a wɔte apueeɛ fam asase so.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Na ɔhunui asubura bi wɔ wiram, na hwɛ, nnwankuo mmiɛnsa boaboa ho wɔ hɔ, ɛfiri sɛ abura no mu nsuo na wɔsa ma nnwankuo no nom, na ɔboɔ kokuroo da abura no ano.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wɔboa nnwankuo nyinaa ano, na wɔmuni ɔboɔ no firi abura no ano, na wɔma nnwan no nom, na wɔmuni ɔboɔ no to abura no so bio wɔ ne daberɛ hɔ.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bisaa wɔn sɛ: Me nuanom, mofiri he? Na wɔse: Yɛfiri Haran.

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔsee wɔn sɛ: Monim Nahor ba Laban anaa? Na wɔse: Yɛni no.

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa wɔn sɛ: Ne ho yɛ? Na wɔbuaa sɛ: Ne ho yɛ, na hwɛ, ne babaa Rahel ne nnwan na ɛreba yi.

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Hwɛ, adeɛ nnya nsae koraa, na ɛberɛ a wɔboaboa mmoakuo ano nnya nnurui. Momma nnwan no nsuo nnom, na monkɔ mma wɔnkɔdidi.

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Yɛntumi, gye sɛ wɔaboaboa nnwankuo no nyinaa ano, na wɔamuni ɔboɔ no afiri abura no ano, ansa na yɛama nnwan no anom.

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ne wɔn da so rekasa no, Rahel ne n’agya nnwan no bae, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔyɛ odwanhwɛfoɔ.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Na Yakob fee Rahel ano, na ɔmaa ne nne so sui.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Rahel sɛ ɔyɛ n’agya busuani, na ɔyɛ Rebeka ba. Na Rahel tutuu mmirika kɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Na Laban tee ne nua ba Yakob nka no, ɔtuu mmirika kɔhyiaa no, na ɔyɛɛ no atuu fee n’ano, na ɔde no baa ne fie. Na ɔbɔɔ n’amanneɛ kyerɛɛ Laban.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Na Laban ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ampa, woyɛ me dompe ne me honam. Na ɔtenaa ne nkyɛn bɛyɛ bosome. Yakob som Laban de ware Lea ne Rahel

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Na Laban bisaa Yakob sɛ: Ɛnam sɛ woyɛ me busuani nti, wobɛsom me kwa anaa? Kyerɛ me deɛ ɛnyɛ w’akatua.

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Na Lea animma yɛ nketewa, na Rahel ho yɛ fɛ, na n’anim yɛ nyam.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob dɔ Rahel, na ɔkaa sɛ: Wo ba kumaa Rahel nti mɛsom wo mfeɛ nson.

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Na Laban se: Ɛyɛ sɛ mede no mema woɔ sene sɛ mede no bɛma onipa foforɔ bie; tena me nkyɛn.

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Na Rahel nti Yakob som mfeɛ nson, na dɔ a ɔdɔ no nti ɛyɛɛ n’ani so sɛ nna mfuamfua bi.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ: Fa me yere ma me, na me nna no adu, na mene no nna.

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Na Laban boaboaa kurom hɔfoɔ nyinaa ano, na ɔtoo pono.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Na anadwofa no ɔde ne ba Lea brɛɛ no, na ɔne no dae.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Na adeɛ kyeeɛ no, Yakob hunuu sɛ ɛyɛ Lea mmom. Na ɔbisaa Laban sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ me yi? Ɛnyɛ Rahel nti na mesom woɔ? Na adɛn nti na woadaadaa me yi?

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Laban se: Yɛn ha deɛ, wɔnyɛ no saa, wɔmma akumaa nware ansa na wɔde abakan ama.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Di ne nkyɛn nnawɔtwe yi, na yɛde oyi nso bɛma wo, som a wobɛsom me mfeɛ nson bio ho.

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hunuu sɛ wɔtane Lea no, ɔbuee ne yafunu mu, na Rahel deɛ, ɔyɛɛ obonini.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Na Lea nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔtoo no din Ruben, na ɔse: AWURADE ahwɛ m’amaneɛ, na afei deɛ, me kunu bɛdɔ me.

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔkaa sɛ: AWURADE ate sɛ wɔtane me nti na ɔde oyi nso ama me. Na ɔtoo no din Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Afei ansa na me kunu de ne ho bɛfam me ho, ɛfiri sɛ me ne no awo mmammarima baasa. Enti ɔtoo no din Lewi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Yei deɛ mɛyi AWURADE ayɛ. Enti ɔtoo no din Yuda. Na n’awoɔ mu twee.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Na Rahel hunuu sɛ ɔnwo mma Yakob no, ɔtwee ne nuabaa no ho kora, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Ma me mma, na anyɛ saa a, mɛwu.

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob bo fuu Rahel kaa sɛ: Mesi Nyankopɔn a ɔkame wo wo yam mma no ananmu anaa?

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, m’afenaa Bilha nie, wo ne no nna, na ɔnwo ngu me srɛ so, na me nso mennya ne ho mma.

english_verse: Then Rachel let Jacob marry Bilhah,
translation_verse: Na ɔde n’abaawa Bilha maa no awareɛ, na Yakob ne no dae.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Na Bilha nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima maa Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn adi m’asɛm, na watie me nne nso ama me ɔba. Enti ɔtoo no din Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Na Rahel abaawa Bilha nyinsɛnee bio, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima a ɔtɔ so mmienu maa Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Na Rahel kaa sɛ: Ako akɛseɛ na me ne me nuabaa adie, nso matumi no. Na ɔtoo no din Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Na Lea hunuu sɛ n’awoɔ mu atwe no, ɔde n’abaawa Silpa maa Yakob awareɛ.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Na Lea abaawa Silpa woo ɔbabarima maa Yakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Aba yie. Na ɔtoo no din Gad.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: M’ahotɔ nie! Na mmaa bɛfrɛ me deɛ wɔahyira no. Na ɔtoo no din Aser.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Na ayuo twaberɛ mu no, Ruben firii adi kɔhunuu dudaim wɔ wiram, na ɔde brɛɛ ne na Lea. Na Rahel ka kyerɛɛ Lea sɛ: Ma me wo ba dudaim yi bi ɛ!

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛnnɔɔso sɛ woafa me kunu? Na worebɛgye me ba dudaim nso anaa? Na Rahel se: Wo ba dudaim no nti ma ɔne wo nkɔda anadwo yi.

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Na anwummerɛ a Yakob firi wiram reba no, Lea firii adi kɔhyiaa no kaa sɛ: Bra me nkyɛn, ɛfiri sɛ ampa ara mede me ba dudaim matɔ wo. Na ɔne no daa anadwo no.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tiee Lea, na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima a ɔtɔ so nnum maa Yakob.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn atua me ka, sɛ mede m’abaawa mama me kunu awareɛ. Na ɔtoo no din Isakar.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Na Lea kaa sɛ: Onyankopɔn akyɛ me akyɛdeɛ pa, afei deɛ, me kunu ne me bɛtena yie, ɛfiri sɛ mawo mmammarima baasia mama no. Na ɔtoo no din Sebulon.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyiri no, ɔwoo ɔbabaa, na ɔtoo no din Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima, na ɔse: Onyankopɔn ayi m’ahohora.

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo no din Yosef sɛ: AWURADE mma me ɔba foforɔ nka ne ho. Laban ne Yakob nnaadaa

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Na Rahel woo Yosef no, Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ: Gya me kwan na menkɔ me kurom ne m’asase so.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Fa me yerenom ne me mma a wɔn nti mesomm woɔ no ma me. Wo ara wonim me som a masom woɔ.

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Na Yakob see no sɛ: Wo ara wonim sɛdeɛ masom wo afa ne sɛdeɛ wo mmoakuo ayɛ wɔ m’aseɛ.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Mebaa wo nkyɛn no, na deɛ wowɔ no sua, na afei aseɛ atrɛ ayɛ pii, na AWURADE ahyira wo baabiara a mefa. Na afei da bɛn na menhwɛ me fie nso?

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na memma woɔ? Na Yakob se: Mma me biribiara; sɛ wobɛyɛ saa adeɛ yi ama me deɛ a, mɛsane mabɛyɛne wo nnwan na mahwɛ wɔn.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Ɛnnɛ mɛkɔ makɔfa wo nnwan nyinaa mu, na mayiyi emu nnwan a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan nyinaa ne nnwammire nyinaa wɔ nnwanten no mu ne mmirekyie no mu nworonnworan ne ntokontrama. Wɔn a wɔtete sɛɛ na ɛnyɛ m’akatua.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Na daakye bi a wobɛka m’akatua ho asɛm no, me tenenee abua ama me wɔ w’anim. Mmirekyie no mu biara a ne ho nyɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan, ne nnwanten no mu deɛ ɔnyɛ odwammire no, ma wɔmmu no awifodeɛ wɔ me nsam.

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Na Laban se: Hwɛ, ma no nyɛ sɛdeɛ woaka yi ɛ!

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Na da no ara ɔyiyii mpapo a wɔn ho yɛ nsensannsensan ne nworonnworan, ne mmirekyibereɛ a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama ne nworonnworan nyinaa, obiara a fufuo wɔ ne ho, ne nnwanten no mu nnwammire nyinaa. Na ɔde wɔn hyɛɛ ne mmammarima nsa.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Na ɔde nnansa kwan too ɔne Yakob ntam, na Yakob yɛnee Laban nnwan a ɛkaeɛ no.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Na Yakob faa sɛsɛ dua, ɛdwono dua ne kyɛnkyɛn dua mman mono, na ɔyiyii ho nsema fitafitaa maa mmaa no ho fitaa no fifirii adi.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Na ɔde mmaa a ɔyiyii ho no guu anomeeɛ adaaseɛ a nnwan no rebɛnom mu nsuo no mu wɔ nnwan no anim, na wɔba nsunom a, wɔanyenyem so.

english_verse: in front of the branches, and their young were spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Na nnwan no nyenyem mmaa no so, na wɔwowoo nsensannsensan, ntokontrama ne nworonnworan.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Na Yakob yiyii nnwammaa no, na ɔde nnwan no ani kyerɛɛ Laban nnwan no mu nsensannsensan ne nnwammire nyinaa. Na ɔyɛɛ ɔno ara nnwankuo nko wɔ fa baabi, na wamfa wɔn amfra Laban nnwan no mu.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Na sɛ daa nnwan a wɔn ho yɛ den no nyenyem a, na Yakob de mmaa no akɔgu adaaseɛ no mu wɔ nnwan no anim, na wɔanyenyem mmaa no so.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Na nnwan no yɛ nofonofo deɛ a, ɔmfa ngu mu. Na wɔn a wɔyɛ mmerɛ no yɛɛ Laban dea, na wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ den no yɛɛ Yakob dea.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no yɛɛ kɛseɛ pa ara, na ɔnyaa nnwan pii ne mfenaa ne nkoa ne yoma ne mfunumu.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtee Laban mmammarima nsɛm a wɔkaeɛ no sɛ: Yakob afa deɛ ɛyɛ yɛn agya deɛ nyinaa; na ɛno na ɔde anya saa agyapadeɛ yi nyinaa.

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu Laban anim, na hwɛ, ɛnte no sɛdeɛ na ɛteɛ kane no.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Sane kɔ wo nananom asase so ne w’abusua mu, na mɛdi w’akyi.

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Na Yakob soma maa wɔkɔfrɛɛ Rahel ne Lea baa wiram wɔ ne nnwan no nkyɛn,

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mehunu mo agya anim sɛ ɛnte me sɛdeɛ na ɛteɛ kane no; nanso m’agya Nyankopɔn adi m’akyi.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Na mo ara monim sɛ m’ahoɔden nyinaa na mede masom mo agya,

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: na mo agya asisi me, adane m’akatua ani mprɛdu; nanso Onyankopɔn amma no kwan amma no anyɛ me bɔne biara.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔka sɛ: Wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ ntokontrama no nyɛ w’akatua a, na nnwan no nyinaa awowo ntokontrama. Na sɛ ɔka sɛ: Wɔn a wɔn ho yɛ nsensannsensan no nyɛ w’akatua a, na nnwan no nyinaa awowo nsensannsensan.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn agye mo agya mmoakuo ama me.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Na Nyankopɔn bɔfoɔ ka kyerɛɛ me daeɛ mu sɛ: Yakob! Na mese: Menie.

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ma w’ani so hwɛ, adwennini no a wɔreforo nnwan no nyinaa yɛ nsensannsensan ne ntokontrama ne nworonnworan: Ɛfiri sɛ mahunu deɛ Laban ayɛ woɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Mene Nyankopɔn a wohyiaa no Betel faako a wosraa ɛhɔ dum na wohyɛɛ bɔ maa me no; afei sɔre firi asase yi so, na sane kɔ w’abusua asase so.

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ɔmmu yɛn ahɔhoɔ anaa? Ɛsiane sɛ watɔn yɛn, na wadi yɛn tiri sika awie,

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: na ahonyadeɛ a Onyankopɔn gyee yɛn agya nsam no yɛ yɛn ne yɛn mma dea. Enti afei yɛ deɛ Onyankopɔn aka akyerɛ woɔ nyinaa. Yakob dwane firi Laban anim

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Na Yakob sɔre faa ne mma ne ne yerenom tenatenaa yoma so,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: na ɔfaa ne mmoakuo nyinaa ne n’ahodeɛ a ɔnyaeɛ nyinaa ne mmoakuo a ɔnyaeɛ wɔ Mesopotamia no nyinaa sii mu sɛ ɔrekɔ n’agya Isak nkyɛn wɔ Kanaan asase so.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔ rekɔtwitwa ne nnwan ho nwi. Na Rahel wiaa n’agya abusua honi.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Na Yakob wiaa ne ho dwanee, ɛfiri sɛ wankra Aramni Laban.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Na ɔne deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa dwanee, na ɔsɔre twaa asubɔnten no, na ɔde n’ani kyerɛɛ Gilead bepɔ. Laban ti Yakob

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa no, wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ Yakob adwane.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Na Laban faa ne nkurɔfoɔ kaa ne ho tii no nnanson kwan, na ɔbɛtoo no Gilead bepɔ so.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Aramni Laban nkyɛn anadwo daeɛ mu sɛ: Hwɛ yie, na woankasa papa anaa bɔne so ankyerɛ Yakob.

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔtoo Yakob. Na Yakob asi ne ntomadan wɔ bepɔ no so, na Laban ne ne nkurɔfoɔ nso sii wɔn deɛ Gilead bepɔ so.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Na Laban bisaa Yakob sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na woayɛ yi, sɛ woawia wo ho adwane me, na woasoa me mmammaa kɔ sɛ wɔn a wɔde nkrantɛ afa wɔn nnommum yi?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na woahunta adwane, na woawia wo ho afiri me nkyɛn? Adɛn na woanka ankyerɛ me, na mamfa anigyeɛ ne nnwom, mpintin ne nsankuo mannya wo kwan?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na woamma mamfe me mmammarima ne me mmammaa ano anya wɔn kwan? Yei deɛ, woadi no nkwasea so.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Mewɔ tumi sɛ anka me ne mo di no bɔne; nanso nnora anadwo no, mo agya ne Nyankopɔn kasa kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ yie, na woankasa papa anaa bɔne so ankyerɛ Yakob.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Na afei deɛ korɔ ara na wopɛ sɛ wokorɔ, ɛfiri sɛ gyina na w’ani agyina w’agya fie; na adɛn nti na woawia m’anyame?

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bua see Laban sɛ: Na mesuro, ɛfiri sɛ mesusuu sɛ wobɛgye wo mmammaa afiri me nsam.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Na deɛ wobɛhunu w’anyame wɔ ne nsa mu no rentena ase. Yɛn nkurɔfoɔ yi anim na hwehwɛ deɛ ɛyɛ wo dea wɔ me nkyɛn, na fa kɔ. Na Yakob nnim sɛ Rahel na ɔwiaeɛ.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Na Laban kɔɔ Yakob ntomadan mu ne Lea ntomadan ne mfenaa baanu no ntomadan mu, nanso wanhunu. Na ɔfiri Lea ntomadan mu kɔɔ Rahel ntomadan mu.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Na Rahel afa abusua honi no de ahyehyɛ yoma so adwa mu atena so. Na Laban de ne nsa kekaa ntomadan mu hɔ nyinaa, nanso wanhunu.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Mma no nnyɛ me wura abufuo sɛ mentumi mensɔre wɔ w’anim, ɛfiri sɛ mabu me nsa. Na ɔpɛe pɛe pɛe, nanso wanhunu ahoni no.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Na Yakob bo fui, na ɔne Laban hamee, na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Laban sɛ: Me mfomsoɔ ne sɛn, na me bɔne ne sɛn na wosa me yerɛdɛdɛdɛdɛ yi?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Na wobɛhwehwɛɛ me nnoɔma mu nyinaa yi, wo fie mu adeɛ bɛn na woahunu wɔ mu? Saa! Fa bɛto me nkurɔfoɔ ne wo nkurɔfoɔ anim wɔ ha, na wɔmmu yɛn baanu ntam atɛn.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Wɔn a mmoa kumm wɔn no mamfa mammrɛ wo, me na metuaa so ka. Deɛ wɔwiaa no awia ne deɛ wɔwiaa no anadwo, me nsa mu na wobisaeɛ.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛyɛɛ me nie: Ahuhuro dee me awia, na awɔ dee me anadwo, na m’ani soroe.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Sɛ m’agya Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, ne Isak suro annyina m’akyiri a, anka afei wogyaa me kwan nsapan. Me brɛ ne me nsa ano adwumayɛ na Onyankopɔn hunuiɛ, na ɔkaa w’anim nnora anadwo.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Na Laban bua see Yakob sɛ: Mma mmaa yi, me mma a, na mmammarima yi, me mma a, na nnwan yi, me nnwan a, na deɛ wohunu yi nyinaa, me dea. Na me mmammaa yi, anaasɛ wɔn mma a wɔawo wɔn yi, ɛdeɛn na mɛtumi de ayɛ wɔn nnɛ?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Afei bra ma yɛmpam, me ne wo, na ɛnyɛ me ne wo ntam adanseɛ.

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Na Yakob faa ɔboɔ de yɛɛ odum sii hɔ.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ ne nkurɔfoɔ sɛ: Mommoaboa aboɔ ano! Na wɔtasee aboɔ yɛɛ no kuo; na wɔdidii wɔ ekuo no so hɔ.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Na Laban frɛɛ hɔ Yegarsahaduta, na Yakob deɛ, ɔfrɛɛ hɔ Galeed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Na Laban kaa sɛ: Ekuo yi ne me ne wo ntam adanseɛ nnɛ. Enti wɔfrɛ hɔ Galeed,

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: ne Mispa, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Sɛ yɛtete mu a, AWURADE nhwɛ me ne wo ntam.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Sɛ woteetee me mmammaa, na woware yerenom ka me mma ho a, obi nka yɛn ho deɛ, nanso Onyankopɔn ne me ne wo ntam danseni.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Aboɔkuo yi ne adanseɛ, na odum yi nso yɛ adanseɛ, sɛ me deɛ, merensiane ekuo yi ho memma wo nkyɛn, na wo nso, worensiane ekuo yi ne odum yi ho mma me nkyɛn mmɛyɛ bɔne.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bɔɔ afɔdeɛ wɔ bepɔ no so, na ɔfrɛɛ ne nkurɔfoɔ sɛ wɔmmɛdidi; na wɔdidii na wɔtenaa bepɔ no so anadwo no.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Na Laban sɔree anɔpatutu, na ɔfee ne nananom ne ne mmammaa no ano hyiraa wɔn, na ɔsii mu sane kɔɔ ne kurom.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii ne kwan so sɛ ɔrekɔ; na Nyankopɔn abɔfoɔ bɛhyiaa no.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu wɔn no, ɔkaa sɛ: Nyankopɔn asafo nie. Na ɔtoo hɔ din: Maha-naim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Na Yakob tuu abɔfoɔ dii n’anim kɔɔ ne nua Esau nkyɛn Seir asase so wɔ Edom wiram.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛdeɛ monka nkyerɛ me wura Esau ne sɛ: W’akoa Yakob se: Mekɔtenaa Laban nkyɛn na ɛhɔ na mewɔ de abɛduru sɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Manya anantwie, mfunumu, nnwan, mmirekyie ne nkoa ne mfenaa; na masoma sɛ wɔmmɛka nkyerɛ me wura, sɛdeɛ mɛnya w’anim adom.

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Na abɔfoɔ no sane baa Yakob nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Yɛakɔ wo nua Esau nkyɛn, na ɔno nso ne mmarima ahanan reba abɛhyia wo.

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob suroo sɛ, na ne ho yeraa no. Na ɔkyɛɛ nkurɔfoɔ a wɔwɔ ne nkyɛn ne nnwan, mmirekyie, anantwie ne yoma no mu akuo mmienu

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: kaa sɛ: Sɛ Esau ba kuo baako so bɛku wɔn a, ekuo a ɛbɛka no bɛnya kwan adwane.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: M’agya Abraham Nyankopɔn ne m’agya Isak Nyankopɔn, AWURADE a wosee me sɛ: Sane kɔ w’asase so ne w’abusua mu, na mɛyɛ wo yie no,

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, yi me firi me nua Esau nsam, ɛfiri sɛ mesuro no sɛ ɔbɛba abɛku me, ne ɛnanom ne wɔn mma nyinaa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Wo na wokaa sɛ: Yie na mɛyɛ woɔ, na mɛma w’asefoɔ ayɛ sɛ mpoano anwea a ne dodoɔ nti wɔntumi nkan.

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Na ɔtenaa hɔ anadwo no; na ɔyii deɛ ɛwɔ ne nsa mu bi sɛ ɔde rekɔkyɛ ne nua Esau,

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Na monka nsi so sɛ: Hwɛ, w’akoa Yakob wɔ yɛn akyi. Afei ɔkaa sɛ: Mede ayɛyɛdeɛ a ɛdi m’anim yi merekɔpata no, ansa na mahunu n’anim; ebia ɔbɛhwɛ m’anim.

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Na Yakob too ɛhɔ din Peni-el, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Me ne Onyankopɔn adi nhunuanimu, nso me kra anya nkwa.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Na ɔde hyɛɛ ne nkoa nsa akuakuo, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa no sɛ: Monsene nni m’anim, na momma kuo ne kuo ntam ntwe.

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ deɛ ɔdi kan no sɛ: Sɛ me nua Esau bɛhyia wo, na ɔbisa wo sɛ: Hwan nipa ne wo, na ɛhe na worekorɔ, na yeinom a ɛdi w’anim yi yɛ hwan dea?

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: W’akoa Yakob dea; ɛyɛ ayɛyɛdeɛ a wasoma de rebrɛ me wura Esau; na hwɛ, ɔno nso wɔ yɛn akyi.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ deɛ ɔtɔ so mmienu ne deɛ ɔtɔ so mmiɛnsa ne wɔn a wɔdi mmoakuo no akyire nyinaa nso sɛ: Sɛ mokɔhunu Esau a, monka asɛm korɔ yi ara nkyerɛ no.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Na ayɛyɛdeɛ no sene dii n’anim; na ɔno deɛ, ɔtenaa nsraban no mu anadwo no. Yakob ne ɔbɔfoɔ bi tentam

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Na ɛkaa Yakob nko ara. Na ɔbarima bi ne no bɛtentamee kɔduruu adekyeeɛ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no hunuu sɛ ɔntumi no no, ɔkaa n’asene tokuro mu, na Yakob dwonku hwanee tentam a ɔne no tentameeɛ no mu.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no kaa sɛ: Ma menkɔ, na adeɛ rekye. Na Yakob buaa sɛ: Meremma wonkɔ gye sɛ wohyira me.

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no bisaa no sɛ: Wo din de sɛn? Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Yakob.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Wɔremfrɛ wo din Yakob bio, na wɔbɛfrɛ no Israel, ɛfiri sɛ wo ne Onyankopɔn ne nnipa ako, na woatumi.

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bisaa no sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me wo din. Na ɔse: Adɛn nti na worebisa me din? Na ɔbarima no hyiraa no wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Na ɔtwaa mu wɔ Peniel berɛ a na owia apue no, na ɔtɔ gu so ne dwonku a ahwan no nti.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Enti Israelfoɔ nni ntini a ɛwɔ asene mu akwaa tokuro mu no de bɛduru nnɛ, ɛfiri sɛ ɔkaa Yakob dwonkuo tokuro mu, n’asene mu ntini no so.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii ne kwan so sɛ ɔrekɔ; na Nyankopɔn abɔfoɔ bɛhyiaa no.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hunuu wɔn no, ɔkaa sɛ: Nyankopɔn asafo nie. Na ɔtoo hɔ din: Maha-naim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Na Yakob tuu abɔfoɔ dii n’anim kɔɔ ne nua Esau nkyɛn Seir asase so wɔ Edom wiram.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛdeɛ monka nkyerɛ me wura Esau ne sɛ: W’akoa Yakob se: Mekɔtenaa Laban nkyɛn na ɛhɔ na mewɔ de abɛduru sɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Manya anantwie, mfunumu, nnwan, mmirekyie ne nkoa ne mfenaa; na masoma sɛ wɔmmɛka nkyerɛ me wura, sɛdeɛ mɛnya w’anim adom.

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Na abɔfoɔ no sane baa Yakob nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Yɛakɔ wo nua Esau nkyɛn, na ɔno nso ne mmarima ahanan reba abɛhyia wo.

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob suroo sɛ, na ne ho yeraa no. Na ɔkyɛɛ nkurɔfoɔ a wɔwɔ ne nkyɛn ne nnwan, mmirekyie, anantwie ne yoma no mu akuo mmienu

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: kaa sɛ: Sɛ Esau ba kuo baako so bɛku wɔn a, ekuo a ɛbɛka no bɛnya kwan adwane.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: M’agya Abraham Nyankopɔn ne m’agya Isak Nyankopɔn, AWURADE a wosee me sɛ: Sane kɔ w’asase so ne w’abusua mu, na mɛyɛ wo yie no,

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, yi me firi me nua Esau nsam, ɛfiri sɛ mesuro no sɛ ɔbɛba abɛku me, ne ɛnanom ne wɔn mma nyinaa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Wo na wokaa sɛ: Yie na mɛyɛ woɔ, na mɛma w’asefoɔ ayɛ sɛ mpoano anwea a ne dodoɔ nti wɔntumi nkan.

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Na ɔtenaa hɔ anadwo no; na ɔyii deɛ ɛwɔ ne nsa mu bi sɛ ɔde rekɔkyɛ ne nua Esau,

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Na monka nsi so sɛ: Hwɛ, w’akoa Yakob wɔ yɛn akyi. Afei ɔkaa sɛ: Mede ayɛyɛdeɛ a ɛdi m’anim yi merekɔpata no, ansa na mahunu n’anim; ebia ɔbɛhwɛ m’anim.

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Na Yakob too ɛhɔ din Peni-el, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Me ne Onyankopɔn adi nhunuanimu, nso me kra anya nkwa.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Na ɔde hyɛɛ ne nkoa nsa akuakuo, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa no sɛ: Monsene nni m’anim, na momma kuo ne kuo ntam ntwe.

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ deɛ ɔdi kan no sɛ: Sɛ me nua Esau bɛhyia wo, na ɔbisa wo sɛ: Hwan nipa ne wo, na ɛhe na worekorɔ, na yeinom a ɛdi w’anim yi yɛ hwan dea?

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: W’akoa Yakob dea; ɛyɛ ayɛyɛdeɛ a wasoma de rebrɛ me wura Esau; na hwɛ, ɔno nso wɔ yɛn akyi.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ deɛ ɔtɔ so mmienu ne deɛ ɔtɔ so mmiɛnsa ne wɔn a wɔdi mmoakuo no akyire nyinaa nso sɛ: Sɛ mokɔhunu Esau a, monka asɛm korɔ yi ara nkyerɛ no.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Na ayɛyɛdeɛ no sene dii n’anim; na ɔno deɛ, ɔtenaa nsraban no mu anadwo no. Yakob ne ɔbɔfoɔ bi tentam

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Na ɛkaa Yakob nko ara. Na ɔbarima bi ne no bɛtentamee kɔduruu adekyeeɛ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no hunuu sɛ ɔntumi no no, ɔkaa n’asene tokuro mu, na Yakob dwonku hwanee tentam a ɔne no tentameeɛ no mu.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no kaa sɛ: Ma menkɔ, na adeɛ rekye. Na Yakob buaa sɛ: Meremma wonkɔ gye sɛ wohyira me.

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no bisaa no sɛ: Wo din de sɛn? Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Yakob.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Wɔremfrɛ wo din Yakob bio, na wɔbɛfrɛ no Israel, ɛfiri sɛ wo ne Onyankopɔn ne nnipa ako, na woatumi.

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bisaa no sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me wo din. Na ɔse: Adɛn nti na worebisa me din? Na ɔbarima no hyiraa no wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Na ɔtwaa mu wɔ Peniel berɛ a na owia apue no, na ɔtɔ gu so ne dwonku a ahwan no nti.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔde mmaawa no ne wɔn mma dii anim, na Lea ne ne mma dii hɔ, na Rahel ne Yosef dii akyire.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Na ɔno ara deɛ ɔsene dii wɔn anim, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase kɔɔ fam mprɛnson de kɔsii sɛ ɔduruu ne nua nkyɛn.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Na Esau tuu mmirika bɛhyiaa no yɛɛ no atuu, na ɔde ne tiri too ne kɔn ho, na ɔfee n’ano, na wɔsui.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Na Esau maa n’ani so hunuu mmaa no ne wɔn mma no, ɔkaa sɛ: Hwannom ne yeinom a wɔka wo ho yi? Na Yakob buaa sɛ: Ɛyɛ mma a Onyankopɔn de adom w’akoa.

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Na mmaawa no twe pinii, wɔn ne wɔn mma, na wɔbobɔɔ wɔn mu ase.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Na Lea nso ne ne mma twe pinii bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase, na akyire yi no Yosef ne Rahel twe pinii bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Na ɛdɔm a mehyiaa wɔn yi ase ne sɛn? Na ɔse: Sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ na mɛnya me wura anim adom.

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Deɛ mewɔ dɔɔso, me nua, ma w’adeɛ ntena hɔ mma wo.

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa sɛ: Dabi da, mesrɛ wo, sɛ manya w’anim adom a, gye m’ayɛyɛdeɛ a ɛwɔ me nsam yi, na w’anim a mahunu yi te sɛdeɛ obi hunu Nyankopɔn anim, ɛfiri sɛ w’ani asɔ me.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, gye nhyira a wɔde abrɛ woɔ yi, ɛfiri sɛ Onyankopɔn adom me, na mewɔ ade nyinaa. Na ɔhyɛɛ no, na ɔgyee.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kaa sɛ: Ma yɛnsim nkɔ, na menni w’anim.

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me wura nim sɛ mma a wɔyɛ mmerɛ ne nnwan ne anantwie a wɔma nufoɔ ka me ho, na sɛ wɔpia wɔn dodo da koro a, nnwankuo no nyinaa bɛwuwu.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
