english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ɛmpare me sɛ meyɛ saa. Na deɛ wɔhunuu kuruwa no wɔ ne nsa mu no, ɔno ara na ɔbɛyɛ m’akoa, na mo deɛ, monsim mfa asomdwoeɛ nkɔ mo agya nkyɛn. Yuda srɛ ma Benyamin

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yuda twe pinii no kaa sɛ: Me wura, mesrɛ wo, ma w’akoa nkasa me wura aso mu, na mma wo bo mmfu w’akoa, na wote sɛ Farao ara.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Me wura bisaa ne nkoa sɛ: Mowɔ agya anaa nua bi?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Na yɛka kyerɛɛ me wura sɛ: Yɛwɔ agya akɔkoraa ne ne nkɔkoraa ba kumaa bi. Ne nua awu, na ne na ba a aka ara ne no, na n’agya dɔ no.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Na woka kyerɛɛ wo nkoa sɛ: Momfa no mmrɛ me, na memfa m’ani menhwɛ no.

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Na yɛsee me wura sɛ: Abɔfra no ntumi nnya n’agya hɔ, na sɛ ɔgya n’agya hɔ a, n’agya bɛwu.

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Na wosee wo nkoa sɛ: Sɛ mo nua kumaa no anka mo ho amma a, monnsi m’anim bio.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Na yɛkɔɔ w’akoa, m’agya, nkyɛn no, yɛkaa me wura nsɛm no kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Na yɛn agya ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Monsane nkɔtɔ aduane kakra mmrɛ yɛn.

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Na yɛse: Yɛrentumi nsiane nkɔ. Sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho a, yɛbɛsiane akɔ. Yɛrentumi nkɔ ɔbarima no anim, gye sɛ yɛn nua kumaa no ka yɛn ho.

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ɛnna w’akoa, yɛn agya, ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Mo ara monim sɛ mma baanu na me yere wo maa me.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Na ɔbaako firii me nkyɛn kɔe, na mese: Ampa ara teteɛ na wɔatete no mu, na ɛfiri hɔ no, menhunuu no.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mofa oyi nso firi me nkyɛn na mmusuo bi kɔto no a, mode me tiri dwono nam awerɛhoɔ mu na ɛbɛkɔ Asamando.

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Na afei sɛ mekɔ w’akoa, m’agya, nkyɛn na abɔfra yi nka yɛn ho a, — nso n’akoma da abɔfra yi ho, —

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Na w’akoa dii abɔfra yi ho agyinamu wɔ m’agya anim sɛ: Sɛ mamfa no mammrɛ wo a, ɛnneɛ na mayɛ m’agya bɔne daa nyinaa.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Na afei mesrɛ wo, ma w’akoa ntena ha nsi abɔfra no ananmu nyɛ me wura akoa, na ma abɔfra no ne ne nuanom nkɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Na sɛ abɔfra no nka me ho a, mɛkɔ m’agya anim sɛn? Ɛnneɛ na merekɔhunu bɔne a ɛbɛto m’agya no.

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Afei na Yosef ntumi nhyɛ ne ho so wɔ wɔn a wɔgyinagyina ne ho no nyinaa anim, na ɔteaa mu sɛ: Momma nnipa nyinaa mfiri me ho mfiri adi. Na Yosef reyi ne ho adie akyerɛ ne nuanom no, na onipa biara nnyina ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa ne nne so sui, na Misraimfoɔ no ne Farao fiefoɔ tee.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Mene Yosef, m’agya da so te ase anaa? Na ne nuanom antumi ammua no, na mmom wɔn ho dwirii wɔn wɔ n’anim.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Montwe mpini me. Na wɔtwe pinii no. Na ɔse: Mene mo nua Yosef a motɔn no baa Misraim no.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Na afei mommma no nnyɛ mo ya, nso mo bo mmfu mo ho mo ho sɛ motɔn me baa ha, ɛfiri sɛ nkwagyeɛ nti na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Na mfeɛ mmienu ni a ɛkɔm aba asase yi soɔ, na aka mfeɛ nnum bio a funtum ne otwa nni mu.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn somaa me dii mo anim sɛ memma monnya nkaeɛ wɔ asase so, na mennye mo nkwa a ɛbɛma dodoɔ no ara afiri mu afire.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Na afei ɛnyɛ mo na mosomaa me baa ha, na mmom Onyankopɔn na ɔde me abɛyɛ sɛ Farao n’agya ne ne fie nyinaa wura ne Misraim asase nyinaa sodifoɔ.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Monyɛ ntɛm nkɔ m’agya nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wo ba Yosef seɛ nie: Onyankopɔn de me ayɛ Misraim nyinaa so wura. Siane bra me nkyɛn. Nkyɛ!

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na bɛtena Gosen asase so, na woabɛn me, wo ne wo mma ne wo nananom ne wo nnwan ne w’anantwie ne deɛ wowɔ nyinaa,

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: na mɛhwɛ wo wɔ hɔ, ɛfiri sɛ mfeɛ nnum kɔm da so reba, na ohia anhia wo ne wo fiefoɔ ne deɛ wowɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mo ani ahunu, na me nua Benyamin nso ani ahunu sɛ m’ano na mede mekasa mekyerɛ mo yi.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Na monka m’animuonyam a mewɔ wɔ Misraim nyinaa nkyerɛ m’agya ne deɛ moahunu nyinaa, na monyɛ ntɛm mfa m’agya nsiane mmra ha.

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsɔɔ ne nua Benyamin kɔn mu na ɔsuiɛ; na Benyamin nso sui wɔ ne kɔn ho.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔfefee ne nuanom nyinaa ano, na ɔsuu wɔ wɔn so, na ɛno akyiri no ne nuanom no ne no kasae.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Na wɔtee nka wɔ Farao fie sɛ: Yosef nuanom aba. Na ɛsɔɔ Farao ne ne nkoa ani.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Ka kyerɛ wo nuanom sɛ: Yei na monyɛ: Momfa nnoɔma nsoasoa mo mmoa no, na monkɔ Kanaan asase so

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: nkɔfa mo agya ne mo fiefoɔ mmra me nkyɛn, na mɛma mo Misraim asase so deɛ ɛyɛ, na moadi asase no sradeɛ.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Yei na monyɛ. Momfa nteaseɛnam mfiri Misraim asase so nkɔma mo mma ne mo yerenom, na monkɔfa mo agya mmra.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mo nso monnwennwene mo nnoɔma ho, na Misraim asase nyinaa so deɛ ɛyɛ yɛ mo dea.

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no yɛɛ saa. Na Yosef maa wɔn nteaseɛnam sɛdeɛ Farao anomu asɛm seɛ, na ɔmaa wɔn akwansoduane.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ɔmaa wɔn nyinaa ntadeɛ nsakyeraho mmaako mmaako, na Benyamin deɛ, ɔmaa no nnwetɛbena ahasa ne ntadeɛ nsakyeraho nnum.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Na deɛ ɔde kɔmaa n’agya nso nie: Mfunumu du a wɔsoso Misraim nnepa no bie ne mfunumubereɛ du a wɔsoso aburoo ne paanoo ne akwansoduane a ɛbɛyɛ n’agya dea.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Na ɔgyaa ne nuanom kwan maa wɔkɔe. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo bo nnkɔfu mo ho mo ho wɔ ɔkwan so oo! Yakob ho sane no

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔfirii Misraim foro kɔɔ Kanaan asase so wɔn agya Yakob nkyɛn,

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yosef da so te ase, na ɔdi Misraim asase nyinaa so. Na ne tirim yɛɛ no naa, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔnnye wɔn nni.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Na wɔkaa nsɛm a Yosef aka akyerɛ wɔn no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no, na ɔhunuu nteaseɛnam a Yosef asoma de rebɛfa no no, wɔn agya Yakob ho sanee no.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Na Israel kaa sɛ: Ɛdɔɔso, me ba Yosef da so te ase. Mɛkɔ makɔhu no ansa na mawu.

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Na Israel ne deɛ ɔwɔ nyinaa sii mu, na ɔduruu Beer-seba, na ɔbɔɔ afɔdeɛ maa n’agya Isak Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nam anadwo anisoadehunu mu ka kyerɛɛ Israel sɛ: Yakob, Yakob! Na ɔse: Menie.

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Mene Onyankopɔn, w’agya Nyankopɔn no. Nsuro sɛ wobɛsiane akɔ Misraim, na mɛyɛ wo ɔman kɛseɛ wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Me ne wo bɛsiane akɔ Misraim, na mede wo asane aba nso, na Yosef deɛ, ne nsa so na wo bɛwuo.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Farao bɛfrɛ mo, na ɔbisa mo sɛ: Mo adwuma ne sɛn a?

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Akra a wɔne Yakob kɔɔ Misraim a wɔfiri n’asene mu, Yakob mma yerenom mfram, akra no nyinaa yɛ aduosia nsia.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa Yuda dii n’anim kɔɔ Yosef nkyɛn sɛ ɔmmɛdi n’anim nkyerɛ no Gosen kwan. Na wɔduruu Gosen asase so.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Na Yosef siesiee ne nteaseɛnam kɔhyiaa n’agya Israel wɔ Gosen. Na ɔde ne ho kɔkyerɛɛ no no, ɔsɔɔ ne kɔn mu, na ɔsui ara kyɛree wɔ ne kɔn ho.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Afei a manya mahunu w’anim sɛ woda so te aseɛ yi, wɔmma menti nananom wɔ asamando.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom ne n’agya fiefoɔ sɛ: Merekɔ makɔka akyerɛ Farao sɛ: Me nuanom ne m’agya fiefoɔ a wɔwɔ Kanaan asase soɔ no aba me nkyɛn.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Na nnipa no yɛ nnwanhwɛfoɔ, na mmoa na wɔyɛne, na wɔde wɔn nnwan ne wɔn anantwie ne deɛ wɔwɔ nyinaa aba.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: Monse no sɛ: Wo nkoa yɛ mmoahwɛfoɔ firi yɛn mmɔfraase de bɛsi nnɛ, yɛn ne yɛn nananom, na moatena Gosen asase so, ɛfiri sɛ Misraimfoɔ kyiri mmoahwɛfoɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Na Farao bisaa ne nuanom no sɛ: Mo adwuma ne sɛn? Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo nkoa yɛ mmoahwɛfoɔ, yɛn ne yɛn nananom nso.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Farao bio sɛ: Yɛaba sɛ yɛrebɛtena asase yi so, ɛfiri sɛ wo nkoa nnya adidibea mma wɔn nnwan, ɛfiri sɛ ɛkɔm no mu yɛ den wɔ Kanaan asase so. Enti afei yɛsrɛ wo, ma wo nkoa ntena Gosen asase so.

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: W’agya ne wo nuanom aba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Misraim asase na ɛda w’anim yi, asase no mu deɛ ɛyɛ no, ma w’agya ne wo nuanom ntena hɔ. Ma wɔntena Gosen asase so. Na sɛ wonim sɛ wɔn mu bi yɛ nsiyɛfoɔ a, fa wɔn si me mmoa a mewɔ so.

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Na Yosef de n’agya Yakob kɔgyinaa Farao anim. Na Yakob hyiraa Farao.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Na Farao bisaa Yakob sɛ: Wo nkwa mu mfirinhyia yɛ ahe?

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hyiraa Farao, na ɔfirii Farao anim kɔe.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Na Yosef maa n’agya ne ne nuanom tenaberɛ, na ɔmaa wɔn asase wɔ Misraim wɔ deɛ asase no yɛ, wɔ Rameses asase so, sɛdeɛ Farao hyɛeɛ no.

english_verse: Joseph also provided food for their families. A Famine in Egypt
translation_verse: Na Yosef bɔɔ n’agya ne ne nuanom ne n’agya fiefoɔ nyinaa akɔnhoma, sɛdeɛ abusua biara dodoɔ teɛ. Ɛkɔm no

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Na aduane nni asase biara so, na ɛkɔm no mu yɛɛ den yie maa Misraim asase ne Kanaan asase tɔɔ ɛkɔm no anim piti.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Na Yosef prapraa sika a ɛwɔ Misraim asase ne Kanaan asase soɔ nyinaa wɔ aburoo a wɔbɛtɔeɛ no mu, na Yosef de sika no kɔɔ Farao fie.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Na sika saa Misraimfoɔ ne Kanaanfoɔ ho no, Misraimfoɔ nyinaa baa Yosef nkyɛn sɛ: Ma yɛn aduane ɛ! Adɛn na sɛ sika asa nti, yɛnwuwu w’anim?

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef se: Momfa mo mmoa mmra, na sɛ mo sika asa a, mɛma mo bi magye mo mmoa.

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Na afe no twaa mu no, afe a ɛdi soɔ no, wɔbaa ne nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛremfa nhunta me wura sɛ yɛn sika asa na mmoa akuakuo no yɛ me wura dea, na biribiara nkae wɔ me wura anim sɛ yɛn honam ne yɛn asase nko.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na yɛn ne yɛn asase nwu w’anim? Tɔ yɛn ne yɛn asase, na ma yɛn aduane, na yɛde yɛn ho ne yɛn asase bɛsom Farao. Ma yɛn aduaba, na yɛntena ase, na yɛanwu amma asase yi anna mpan.

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Na Yosef tɔɔ Misraim asase nyinaa maa Farao. Na Misraimfoɔ nyinaa tontɔnee wɔn mfuo, ɛfiri sɛ ɛkɔm no denee wɔn, na asase no danee Farao dea.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Gye asɔfoɔ nsase nko na wantɔ, ɛfiri sɛ na Farao ahyɛ kyɛfa bi ama asɔfoɔ no, na wɔdi wɔn kyɛfa a Farao de ma wɔn no nti, wɔantɔn wɔn asase.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ nkurɔfoɔ no sɛ: Monhwɛ, ɛnnɛ matɔ mo ne mo asase mama Farao, na hwɛ, mo aduaba a momfa nkɔdua asase no soɔ nie.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Na deɛ ɛbɛsoɔ no, momfa nkyekyɛmu nnum mu baako mma Farao, na emu abupɛn nnan no nyɛ mo dea, na mode bi adua mfuo mu, na mode bi ayɛ mo ne mo fiefoɔ ne mo mma aduane.

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Woagye yɛn nkwa; ma yɛnnya me wura anim adom ara, na yɛbɛyɛ Farao nkoa.

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Na Yosef hyɛɛ yei ho mmara wɔ Misraim a ɛwɔ hɔ de bɛsi nnɛ, sɛ wɔmfa Misraim asase so adeɛ biara nkyekyɛmu nnum mu baako mma Farao, gye asɔfoɔ asase nko na anyɛ Farao dea. Yakob adesrɛ a ɛtwa toɔ

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Na Israel tenaa Misraim asase so wɔ Gosen, na wɔnyaa mu adeɛ, na wɔdɔree, na wɔn ase trɛɛ pa ara.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Israel nna duruu sɛ ɔbɛwuo no, ɔfrɛɛ ne ba Yosef ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ manya w’anim adom a, fa wo nsa ka m’asene mu, na yɛ me adɔeɛ di me nokorɛ, na nsie me Misraim!

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Ɛda a mɛtoa nananom no, soa me firi Misraim kɔsie me wɔ me nananom amusieeɛ. Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Mɛyɛ sɛdeɛ woaka yi.

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Ka me ntam. Na ɔkaa no ntam. Na Israel bɔɔ ne mu ase kyerɛɛ mpa no atifi.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na nsɛm yi akyiri no, wɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, w’agya yare. Na ɔfaa ne mmabarima baanu, Manase ne Efraim kaa ne ho.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Yakob sɛ: Hwɛ, wo ba Yosef reba wo nkyɛn. Na Israel miaa n’ani tenaa ne mpa so.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn yii ne ho kyerɛɛ me wɔ Lus a ɛwɔ Kanaan asase soɔ, na ɔhyiraa me

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: ka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ, mɛma woadɔ, na mama woadɔɔso, mɛyɛ wo aman asafo, na mede asase yi bɛma w’asefoɔ a wɔbɛdi w’akyire no sɛ daa agyapadeɛ.

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Na afei wo mma baanu a wowoo wɔn wɔ Misraim asase soɔ ansa na mereba wo nkyɛn wɔ Misraim no, wɔnyɛ me dea. Efraim ne Manase nyɛ me dea te sɛ Ruben ne Simeon.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na wo mma a wobɛnya wɔn wɔ wɔn akyiri no na ɛnyɛ wo dea, na wɔde wɔn nuanom din bɛfrɛ wɔn wɔ wɔn agyapadeɛ mu.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Na me deɛ, mefiri Padan baeɛ no, Rahel wui m’anim wɔ Kanaan asase so wɔ kwan mu, na aka kwantiaa bi na wɔaduru Efrat, na mesiee no hɔ wɔ Efrat no kwan nkyɛn.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Mansusu sɛ mɛhunu w’anim, na hwɛ, Onyankopɔn ama mahunu wo mma nso.

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Na Yosef yii wɔn firii Yakob nantam, na ɔponoo ne mu de n’anim butuu fam.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Na Yosef faa wɔn baanu nyinaa de ne nifa sɔɔ Efraim mu de no kyerɛɛ Israel benkum, de ne benkum sɔɔ Manase mu de no kyerɛɛ Israel nifa, na ɔde wɔn pinii ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Israel tenee ne nifa too Efraim a ɔyɛ akumaa no atifi, ne ne benkum too Manase atifi, ɔboapa na ɔyɛɛ ne nsa saa, ɛfiri sɛ Manase ne abakan.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyiraa Yosef sɛ: Onyankopɔn a me nananom Abraham ne Isak nantee n’anim no, Onyankopɔn a wayɛne me me nkwa nna nyinaa de abɛsi nnɛ.

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔfoɔ a ɔyii me bɔne nyinaa mu no, nhyira mmɔfra yi, na wɔmfa me din ne me nananom Abraham ne Isak din mfrɛ wɔn, na wɔnnɔɔso nyɛ pii wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Yosef hunuu sɛ n’agya de ne nsa nifa ato Efraim atifi no, anyɛ no dɛ, na ɔsɔɔ n’agya nsa sɛ ɔnyi mfiri Efraim atifi nkɔto Manase atifi.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: M’agya, ɛnyɛ sɛ ɛteɛ ne no, na oyi ne abakan, fa wo nifa to n’atifi.

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Na n’agya ampene, na ɔse: Menim, me ba, menim; ɔno nso bɛyɛ ɔman, na ɔno nso ayɛ kɛse, nanso ne nua kumaa no bɛso asene no, na n’asefoɔ bɛyɛ aman pii.

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na ɛda no ɔhyiraa wɔn sɛ: Wo na Israel de wo bɛhyira sɛ: Onyankopɔn nyɛ wo sɛ Efraim ne Manase. Na ɔde Efraim dii Manase kan.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, merewu, na Onyankopɔn bɛdi mo akyi, na ɔde mo asane akɔ mo nananom asase so.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yakob frɛɛ ne mma sɛ: Mommoaboa mo ano, na menka mo deɛ ɛbɛyɛ mo, nna a ɛdi akyire no mu.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: Yakob mma, monhyia na montie, montie mo agya Israel!

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Ruben, m’abakan ne wo; m’ahoɔden ne me mmaninyɛ asefire. Woboro so anidie mu, woboro so tumi mu.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Wohinhim sɛ nsuo, enti wo kandie bɛfiri wo nsa, ɛfiri sɛ woforoo w’agya nnaeɛ. Ɛno mu na woguu ɛho fi, — me mpa na woforoeɛ!

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon ne Lewi yɛ anuanom. Wɔn nkrantɛ yɛ aniɛden akodeɛ.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Me kra, nnkɔ wɔn agyina mu, na m’animuonyam nkɔfra wɔn asafo mu. Ɛfiri sɛ wɔn abufuo mu na wɔkum nnipa, na wɔn ahokyerɛ mu na wɔsɛee anantwie.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɔadome wɔn abufuo, sɛ ɛso, ne wɔn anibereɛ, sɛ emu yɛ den. Mɛkyekyɛ wɔn mu wɔ Yakob mu, na mabɔ wɔn ahwete Israel mu.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Yuda, wo na wo nuanom bɛyi wo ayɛ; wo nsa bɛtia w’atamfo kɔn so; w’agya mma bɛkoto w’anim.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Gyata ba ne Yuda; hanam so na wode anyini, me ba. Ɔkotoe, ɔbutuu sɛ gyata ne gyatabereɛ; hwan na ɔbɛhwanyan no?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Ahempoma remfiri Yuda nsa, na mmarahyɛ poma remfiri ne nan ntam de kɔsi sɛ ɛsodifoɔ a aman bɛyɛ setie ama no no bɛba.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ɔsa n’afunumu ba wɔ bobe mu, ne n’afunumu bereɛ ba wɔ bobe pa mu. Ɔsi n’atadeɛ wɔ nsa mu, ne ne ntoma wɔ bobe aba mogya mu.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Bobesa bɛma n’ani ayɛ kɔɔ, na nufosuo ama ne se ayɛ fitaa.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Sebulon tenabea bɛkyerɛ mpoano, na wahwɛ deɛ ahyɛn gyinagyina, na ɔne Sidon abɔ hyeɛ.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isakar yɛ afunumu hoɔdenfoɔ, ɔbutu mmoaban ntam;

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: na ɔhunu sɛ homebea no yɛ ne asase no sɛ ɛyɛ fɛ, na ɔbrɛ ne mmatiri ase de gye adesoa, na ɔde ɛsom adwuma ayi toɔ.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan bɛbu ne nkurɔfoɔ atɛn sɛ Israel mmusuakuo mu biara.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan bɛyɛ ɔkwan so ɔwɔ, tempɔn so ahuritia. Ɔka ɔpɔnkɔ nantin, na ne so tenafoɔ ahwe n’akyi.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: AWURADE, wo nkwagyeɛ na mehwɛ no kwan.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: Gad, asafo bi retoa no, na ɔno nso atoa wɔn aka wɔn nantin.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Aser aduane bɛyɛ sradeduane, na ɔbɛma ahennuane a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftali yɛ ɔforoteɛ a wɔato no sraha; ɔka nsɛm dɛdɛ.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Yosef yɛ dua a ɛso aba mman, dua a ɛso aba wɔ nsuo aniwa soɔ mman; ne mman tratra ɔfasuo.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Mmɛmmatofoɔ hyɛɛ no yea, wɔtotoo no, na wɔtaa no.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Nanso na ne tadua kura no pintinn, na ne basa mu yɛɛ den. Ɛfiri Yakob Tumfoɔ no nsam, ɛfiri ɔhwɛfoɔ a ɔyɛ Israel botan no mu.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Ɛfiri w’agya Nyankopɔn, ɔmmoa wo, na ɛfiri Tweaduampɔn hɔ, ɔnhyira wo. Ɔmfa ɔsorosoro nhyira, ne ebunu a ɛtrɛtrɛ aseɛ mu nhyira, ne nufoɔ ne yafunu mu nhyira nhyira wo.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: W’agya nhyira a ɛyɛ kɛseɛ boro daa daa mmepɔ no nhyira a ɛkɔduru tete nteredee nkokoɔ no ahyeɛso nohoa; ɛmmra Yosef atifi, deɛ wɔyii no firii ne nuanom mu no mpampam.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benyamin yɛ pataku a ɔtete mmoa mu; ɔdi hanam anɔpa, na anwummerɛ nso ɔkyɛ asadeɛ mu.

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Yeinom nyinaa ne Israel mmusuakuo dummienu no, na yei ne deɛ wɔn agya ka kyerɛɛ wɔn de hyiraa wɔn. Sɛdeɛ wɔn nhyira teɛ mmaako mmaako na ɔhyiraa wɔn. Yakob wuo ne ne sie

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Afuo no ne ɔbodan a ɛwɔ mu no, wɔtɔɔ no Het mma nsam.

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hyɛɛ ne mma nsamanseɛ wieeɛ no, ɔboaa ne nan ano guu mpa no so, na ɔguu n’ahome a ɛdi akyire, na ɔtii ne nananom wɔ asamando.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Na Yosef de n’anim kɔbutuu n’agya anim, na ɔsu guu ne so, na ɔfee n’ano.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Na nna a wɔde suu no no twaa mu no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ Farao fiefoɔ sɛ: Sɛ manya adom wɔ mo anim a, monkɔyi Farao asotire sɛ:

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: M’agya maa mekaa no ntam sɛ: Hwɛ, merewu, na ɛda a mabɔ no Kanaan asase so mafa no mu, ɛhɔ na kɔsie me. Enti afei ma menkɔ menkɔsie m’agya, na mensane memmra.

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kaa sɛ: Kɔ, na kɔsie w’agya, sɛdeɛ ɔmaa wokaa ntam no.

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Na wɔduruu Atad ayuporebea a ɛwɔ Yordan agya nohoa no, wɔtwaa kwadwom kɛseɛ a emu yɛ den wɔ hɔ, na ɔgyam n’agya nnanson.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɛhɔfoɔ, Kanaanfoɔ no, hunuu esu a wɔsuu no Atad ayuporebea hɔ no, wɔkaa sɛ: Yei deɛ, Misraimfoɔ ayie a emu yɛ den nie. Enti wɔfrɛ hɔ sɛ Abel-misraim ɛwɔ Yordan agya nohoa.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Na ne mma yɛɛ no sɛdeɛ ɔhyɛɛ wɔn no.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Na ne mma soaa no kɔɔ Kanaan asase so kɔsiee no wɔ Makpela afuo so ɔbodan a ɛwɔ Mamre ntentensoɔ a Abraham tɔɔ ɛne afuo no wɔ Hetini Efron nkyɛn de yɛɛ asieeɛ no mu.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Na Yosef siee n’agya wieeɛ no, ɔne ne nuanom ne wɔn a wɔne no kɔsiee n’agya no nyinaa sane baa Misraim. Yosef ma ne nuanom awerɛhyɛmu

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef nuanom hunuu sɛ wɔn agya awuo no, wɔkaa sɛ: Ebia Yosef bɛtane yɛn, na watua yɛn bɔne a yɛyɛɛ no nyinaa so ka.

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Na wɔmaa wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: W’agya hyɛe ansa na ɔrewuo sɛ:

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: Monka nkyerɛ Yosef sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, fa wo nuanom amumuyɛ ne wɔn bɔne kyɛ wɔn, ɛfiri sɛ wɔayɛ wo bɔne. Na afei yɛsrɛ wo, fa w’agya Nyankopɔn nkoa amumuyɛ no kyɛ wɔn. Na wɔkaa saa kyerɛɛ Yosef no, ɔsui.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom nso ba bɛtwa hwee n’anim kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, yɛyɛ wo nkoa.

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monnsuro, na megyina Nyankopɔn ananmu anaa?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Na mo deɛ modwenee me ho bɔne nanso Onyankopɔn deɛ, na ɔde rebɛyɛ papa. Sɛ ɔbɛyɛ deɛ ada adi nnɛ yi, na ɔbɛgye nnipa pii nkwa.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Na afei monnsuro; na mɛhwɛ mo ne mo mma. Na ɔkyekyeree wɔn werɛ kaa wɔn akoma too wɔn yam. Yosef wuo

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne n’agya fiefoɔ tenaa Misraim, na Yosef dii mfirinhyia ɔha ne du.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Na Yosef hunuu Efraim mmanana. Manase ba Makir mma nso, wɔwoo wɔn guu Yosef srɛ so.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Merebɛti nananom wɔ asamando, na Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo ampa, na wabɛyi mo afiri asase yi so akɔ asase a ɔkaa ho ntam kyerɛɛ Abraham ne Isak ne Yakob no so.

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef maa Israel mma kaa ntam na ɔkaa sɛ: Ampa ara, Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo, na monsoa me nnompe mfiri ha nkɔ.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne ne nuanom nyinaa ne wɔn berɛ sofoɔ no nyinaa wuwui.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no wowoe, na wɔdɔree bebree, na wɔn ase kyenee, na wɔn ho yɛɛ den papaapa; na wɔyɛɛ asase no so ma.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Na ɔhene foforɔ bi sɔree Misraim a na ɔnnim Yosef.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne man sɛ: Hwɛ, Israelfoɔ no dɔɔso, na wɔn ho yɛ den sene yɛn.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Momma yɛmfa nyansa kwan bi so ne wɔn nni, na wɔannɔɔso, na sɛ ɛsa bi ba a, wɔankɔka yɛn atamfoɔ ho ne yɛn ammɛko, na wɔansɔre asase yi so ankɔ.

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Na wɔsisii wɔn so adwumayɛfoɔ so mpanimfoɔ sɛ wɔmfa nnesoadeɛ a emu yɛ duro nhyɛ wɔn so. Na wɔkyekyeree adekora nkuro Pitom ne Raamses maa Farao.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Nanso dodoɔ a wɔhyɛɛ wɔn soɔ no, dodoɔ no ara na wɔdɔreeɛ, na wɔtrɛe. Na Misraimfoɔ suroo Israelfoɔ no.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Na wɔde nyadie yaya dii Israelfoɔ.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Wɔmaa wɔn asetena fonoo wɔn wɔ dɔteɛ ne ntaayaa ho adwuma a ɛyɛ den ne afuom adwumayɛ ahodoɔ ne nnwuma ahodoɔ nyinaa mu nyadie yaya a wɔde dii wɔn mu.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Na Misraimhene ka kyerɛɛ Hebrifoɔ awogyefoɔ a wɔn mu baako din de Sifra, na ɔbaako din de Pua no sɛ:

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: Sɛ mokɔgye Hebrifoɔ mmaa awoɔ, na awoeɛ hɔ mohunu sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbarima a, monku no; na sɛ ɔyɛ ɔbaa deɛ a, momma no ntena ase.

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Na awogyefoɔ no suro Onyankopɔn, enti wɔanyɛ sɛdeɛ Misraimhene ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na mmom wɔgyee mmabanin no nkwa.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Na Misraimhene frɛɛ awogyefoɔ no bisaa wɔn sɛ: Adɛn nti na moyɛ saa, na momma mmarima no tena aseɛ?

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Na awogyefoɔ no buaa Farao sɛ: Hebrifoɔ mmaa nte sɛ Misraimfoɔ mmaa, ɛfiri sɛ wɔn deɛ, wɔyɛ pirimpirim; awogyefoɔ no nnya nnuruu wɔn nkyɛn no, na wɔawo dada.

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Na ɛsiane sɛ awogyefoɔ no suro Onyankopɔn nti, ɔmaa wɔn afie mu yɛɛ yie.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao hyɛɛ ne man nyinaa sɛ: Ɔbabanin biara a wɔbɛwo no no, monkɔto no ntwene asubɔnten no mu, na mmammaa nyinaa deɛ, momma wɔntena ase.

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi a ɔfiri Lewi fie kɔwaree Lewi babaa bi.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa no nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabanin; na ɔhunuu sɛ ne ho yɛ fɛ no, ɔde no siee abosome mmiɛnsa.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na ɔntumi nkora no bio no, ɔfaa mmɛwa adaka bi de ama ne ɛhyɛ sraa ho, na ɔde abɔfra no too mu, na ɔde kɔsii wira mu wɔ asuo no ano.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Na ne nuabaa kɔgyinaa akyirikyiri sɛ ɔrehwɛ deɛ ɛbɛyɛ no.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Na Farao babaa siane baa asuo no ano adwareɛ, na ne mmaawa repasa asuo no nsunoa. Berɛ a Farao babaa hunuu adaka no wɔ wira no mu no, ɔsomaa n’abaawa sɛ ɔnkɔfa mmra.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbuee soɔ no, ɔhunuu akɔkoaa no, na hwɛ, na ɔyɛ abarimaa a ɔresu. Na ɔyɛɛ no mmɔbɔ, na ɔse: Hebrifoɔ mma no bi nie.

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ne nuabaa no ka kyerɛɛ Farao babaa no sɛ: Menkɔ menkɔfrɛ Hebrifoɔ mmaa no mu nufomafoɔ bi memmrɛ wo, na ɔmmɛma akɔkoaa no nufoɔ mma wo anaa?

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Na Farao babaa no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ! Na ababaa no kɔ kɔfrɛɛ abɔfra no na bae.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Na Farao babaa no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa abɔfra yi kɔ kɔma no nufoɔ ma me, na mɛtua wo ka. Na ɔbaa no faa abɔfra no kɔmaa no nufoɔ.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Na abɔfra no nyinii, na ɔde no kɔmaa Farao babaa no, na ɔdanee ne ba. Na ɔtoo no din Mose, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Nsuo mu na meyii no firiiɛ. Mose dwane kɔ Midian

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Na Mose nyiniiɛ no, da bi ɔfirii adi kɔɔ ne nuanom nkyɛn sɛ ɔrekɔhwɛ wɔn adwumayɛ no; na ɔhunuu sɛ Misraimni bi reboro ne nuanom mu bi a ɔyɛ Hebrini.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛɛ ha ne ha, na ɔhunuu sɛ obiara nni hɔ no, ɔbɔɔ Misraimni no kumm no, na ɔde no siee anwea mu.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Na adeɛ kyeeɛ no, ɔfirii adi, na hwɛ, na Hebrifoɔ baanu reko. Na ɔbisaa deɛ ɔdi fɔ no sɛ: Adɛn nti na woboro wo yɔnko?

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Hwan na ɔde wo sii yɛn so otitire ne osennifoɔ? Wopɛ sɛ woku me sɛdeɛ wokum Misraimni no anaa? Na Mose suroe, na ɔse: Ampa ara, asɛm no apue!

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Na Farao tee asɛm yi no, anka ɔrehwehwɛ Mose aku no, nanso Mose dwane firii n’anim kɔtenaa Midian asase so wɔ subura bi ho.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Nso na Midian sɔfoɔ wɔ mmammaa baason; na wɔba bɛtoo nsuo de hyehyɛɛ adaaseɛ no amaama sɛ wɔrema wɔn agya nnwan anom.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Na nnwanhwɛfoɔ bi ba bɛpamm wɔn; na Mose sɔre boaa wɔn, na ɔmaa wɔn nnwan no nomee.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa wɔn agya Reuel nkyɛn no, ɔbisaa wɔn sɛ: Ɛyɛɛ dɛn na ɛnnɛ deɛ, moaba ntɛm seyie?

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Na wɔbuaa sɛ: Misraimni bi na ɔgyee yɛn firii nnwanhwɛfoɔ no nsam, na ɔtoo nsuo mpo maa yɛn, na ɔmaa nnwan no nomee.

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbisaa ne mmammaa no sɛ: Na ɔwɔ he? Adɛn nti na mogyaa ɔbarima no hɔ? Monkɔfrɛ no na ɔmmɛdidi.

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Na Mose penee sɛ ɔne Midian sɔfoɔ no bɛtena. Na ɔde ne babaa Sipora maa Mose awareɛ.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo ɔbabanin, na Mose too no din Gersom, ɛfiri sɛ ɔse: Mayɛ hɔhoɔ wɔ ananafoɔ asase so.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Na nna dodoɔ yi akyiri no, ɛbaa sɛ Misraimhene wui. Na nkoasom no nti Israelfoɔ no sii apini, na wɔsu frɛe, na wɔn sufrɛ no kɔduruu Nyankopɔn anim.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tee wɔn apinisie no, ɔkaee n’apam a ɔne Abraham ne Isak ne Yakob pameeɛ no.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hwɛɛ Israelfoɔ no, ɔhunuu wɔn tebea a wɔwɔ mu no.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Berɛ bi a Mose rehwɛ n’ase Yetro, Midian sɔfoɔ nnwan no, ɔkaa wɔn de wɔn kɔɔ ɛserɛ no akyiri nohoa, kɔduruu Nyankopɔn bepɔ Horeb ho.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ bɛyii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ no wɔ nkyɛkyerɛ bi mfimfini gyaframa mu, na Mose hwɛe, na hwɛ, na nkyɛkyerɛ no redɛre, nanso na nhye.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Yei deɛ, mɛmane makɔhwɛ ahwɛdeɛ kɛseɛ yi, adekodeɛ a enti nkyɛkyerɛ no nhyeɛ.

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hunuu sɛ wamane rehwɛ no, ɔfiri nkyɛkyerɛ no mu frɛɛ sɛ: Mose, Mose! Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Menie!

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE kaa sɛ: Ntwe mpini ha! Yi wo nan ase mpaboa, na faako a wogyina hɔ yɛ asase kronkron.

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa sɛ: Mene w’agya Nyankopɔn no, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no. Ɛnna Mose kataa n’anim, ɛfiri sɛ na ɔsuro sɛ ɔbɛhwɛ Onyankopɔn.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa sɛ: Ampa ara, mahunu me man a ɛwɔ Misraim no amanehunu, na wɔn su a wɔn so ahwɛfoɔ nti wɔsu frɛ no, mate.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na masiane sɛ merebɛyi wɔn Misraimfoɔ nsam, na matu wɔn afiri asase no so akɔ asase pa a ɛtrɛ so, asase a nufosuo ne ɛwoɔ sene wɔ soɔ: Kanaanfoɔ, Hetifoɔ, Amorifoɔ, Perisifoɔ, Hewifoɔ ne Yebusifoɔ tenabea hɔ.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, Israelfoɔ no sufrɛ no aduru m’anim, na mahunu ɔhaw a Misraimfoɔ de ha wɔn no nso.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Na afei bra, na mensoma wo Farao nkyɛn, na kɔyi me man Israelfoɔ no firi Misraim.

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mose bisaa Onyankopɔn sɛ: Hwan ne me a merekɔ Farao nkyɛn makɔyi Israelfoɔ afiri Misraim?

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mɛdi w’akyi; na yei bɛyɛ wo nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ sɛ me na mesomaa woɔ. Wonya yi ɔman no firi Misraim ba a, mobɛsom Onyankopɔn wɔ bepɔ yi so.

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Na Mose bisaa Onyankopɔn sɛ: Na sɛ meduru Israelfoɔ nkyɛn, na meka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo nananom Nyankopɔn asoma me mo nkyɛn, na wɔbisa me sɛ: Ne din de sɛn a, sɛn na mense wɔn?

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Mose bio sɛ: Sɛdeɛ ka kyerɛ Israelfoɔ no nie: AWURADE, mo nananom Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn na wasoma me mo nkyɛn. Na yei ne me din de kɔsi daa, na yei na wɔmfa nkae me, awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɔ, na kɔboaboa Israel mpanimfoɔ ano, na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE, mo nananom Nyankopɔn, Abraham, Isak ne Yakob Nyankopɔn no ayi ne ho akyerɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ na mabɛhwɛ mo ne deɛ wɔreyɛ mo wɔ Misraim no.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na mese: Mɛyi mo afiri Misraim amanehunu no mu akɔ Kanaanfoɔ, Hetifoɔ, Amorifoɔ, Perisifoɔ, Hewifoɔ ne Yebusifoɔ asase so, asase a nufosuo ne ɛwoɔ sene wɔ soɔ no.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛtie wo nne, na wo ne Israel mpanimfoɔ nkɔ Misraimhene nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: AWURADE, Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn, abɛhyia yɛn, enti yɛsrɛ wo, ma yɛnkɔ ɛserɛ so nnansa kwan nkɔbɔ AWURADE, yɛn Nyankopɔn, afɔdeɛ.

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Na me deɛ, menim sɛ wɔde nsa a ɛyɛ den hyɛ Misraimhene mpo a, ɔremma mo kwan mma mo nkɔ;

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: enti mɛtene me nsa de m’anwanwadeɛ a mɛyɛ wɔ hɔ no nyinaa mabɔ Misraim, na ɛno akyiri na ɔbɛma moakɔ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mmaa mmisabisa wɔn afipamfoɔ ne wɔn afitenafoɔ nkyɛn dwetɛ nnwinneɛ ne sika nnwinneɛ ne ntoma, na momfa nhyehyɛ mo mmammarima ne mo mmammaa, na Misraimfoɔ nnoɔma no nyɛ mo asadeɛ.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Na Mose buaa AWURADE sɛ: Na sɛ wɔannye me anni, na wɔantie me nne, na wɔka sɛ: AWURADE nyii ne ho adi nkyerɛɛ wo ɛ!

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na ɛwɔ wo nsam yi?

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Poma. Na ɔse: To twene fam! Na ɔto twenee fam, na ɛdanee ɔwɔ. Na Mose dwane firii ho.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tene wo nsa sɔ ne dua mu. Na ɔtenee ne nsa kyeree no, na ɛdanee poma wɔ ne nsam.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Deɛ ɛbɛyɛ na wɔagye adi sɛ AWURADE, wɔn nananom Nyankopɔn, Abraham Nyankopɔn, Isak Nyankopɔn ne Yakob Nyankopɔn na ayi ne ho akyerɛ wo ne no.

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no bio sɛ: Fa wo nsa hyɛ wo kokom! Na ɔde ne nsa hyɛɛ ne kokom, na ɔyii, na hwɛ, na ɛho agu kwata fitaa sɛ sukyerɛmma.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Na ɔse: Fa wo nsa sane hyɛ wo kokom! Na ɔsane de ne nsa hyɛɛ ne kokom, na ɔyi firii ne kokom no, na adane sɛ ne honam ara.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔannye nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ mmienu yi anni na wɔantie wo nne a, ɛnneɛ kɔsa Asubɔntene Nil mu nsuo kɔhwie gu asase pɛsɛɛ so. Na nsuo a wosaa no asuo no mu no bɛdane mogya wɔ asase pɛsɛɛ no so.

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, AWURADE! Me deɛ, ɛde bɛsi nnɛ anaa ɛfiri berɛ a wo ne w’akoa kasaeɛ yi, m’ano nte; me kasa yɛ nyaa, na me tɛkyerɛma yɛ duru.

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwan na ɔyɛɛ onipa ano? Anaasɛ hwan na ɔyɛ emum anaa ɔsotifoɔ, ɔdehunufoɔ anaa onifirani? Ɛnyɛ me AWURADE ara?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Na afei kɔ, na me ara mɛdi w’ano akyi na makyerɛ wo deɛ ka.

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, AWURADE! Soma obi foforɔ biara a wopɛ.

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE bo fuu Mose, na ɔse: Adɛn mennim sɛ Aaron wo nua Lewini no, nim kasa? Na hwɛ, wafiri adi rebɛhyia wo, na sɛ ɔhu wo a, n’akoma bɛtɔ ne yam.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Na poma yi a wode bɛyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ no, fa kura. Mose sane kɔ Misraim

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sane kɔɔ n’ase Yetro nkyɛn, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma mensane menkɔ me nuanom a wɔwɔ Misraim no nkyɛn menkɔhwɛ sɛ wɔda so tete ase anaa. Na Yetro ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa asomdwoeɛ kɔ.

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose wɔ Midian sɛ: Sane kɔ Misraim, ɛfiri sɛ nnipa a na wɔrehwehwɛ wo aku woɔ no nyinaa awuwu.

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Na Mose faa ne yere ne ne mma de wɔn tenatenaa mfunumu so, na ɔsane baa Misraim asase so. Na Mose faa Nyankopɔn poma no kurae.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sɛ wosane kɔ Misraim a, hwɛ na yɛ anwanwadeɛ a mede mahyɛ wo nsa no nyinaa Farao anim; na me deɛ, mɛpirim n’akoma, na ɔremma ɔman no nkɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Na ka kyerɛ Farao sɛ: Sɛdeɛ AWURADE seɛ nie: M’abakan ne Israel.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Na mese wo sɛ: Ma me ba nkɔ nkɔsom me. Na sɛ woampene amma no ankɔ a, hwɛ, me deɛ, mɛkum w’abakan.

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɛtoaa no ɔkwan so asoɛeɛ bi pɛɛ sɛ ɔku no.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sipora faa twerɛboɔ de twaa ne ba no twetia, na ɔto twenee ne nan ase kaa sɛ: Woyɛ mogya ayeforɔkunu ma me!

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔgyaa no. Ɛno na twetiatwa no nti Sipora kaa sɛ: Mogya ayeforɔkunu ne wo.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Kɔ ɛserɛ so kɔhyia Mose. Na ɔkɔ kɔtoo no wɔ Nyankopɔn bepɔ no ho, na ɔfee n’ano.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa AWURADE nsɛm a ɔde asoma no no nyinaa ne nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ a ɔde ahyɛ ne nsa no nyinaa kyerɛɛ Aaron.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔ kɔboaboaa Israelfoɔ mpanimfoɔ no nyinaa ano.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Na Aaron kaa nsɛm a AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose no nyinaa kyerɛɛ wɔn, na ɔyɛɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ no wɔ ɔman no anim.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no gye dii. Na wɔtee sɛ AWURADE abɛhwɛ Israelfoɔ na wahunu wɔn amanehunu no, wɔbɔɔ wɔn mu ase sɔree.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Na yei akyi no, Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, seɛ nie: Ma me man nkɔ na wɔnkɔhyɛ fa mma me wɔ ɛserɛ so.

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Na Farao se: Hwan ne AWURADE a mɛtie ne nne na mama Israel akorɔ? Mennim AWURADE no, na Israel nso, meremma wɔnkɔ.

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Na wɔse: Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn abɛhyia yɛn; enti ma yɛnkɔ ɛserɛ so nnansa kwan, na yɛnkɔbɔ AWURADE, yɛn Nyankopɔn afɔdeɛ, na wamfa owuyadeɛ anaa nkrantɛ ammɛtua yɛn.

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Na Farao kaa sɛ: Monhwɛ, afei a nnipa no adɔɔso wɔ asase no so, na morepɔn wɔn afiri wɔn adwumayɛ mu yi!

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Na da no ara Farao hyɛɛ ɔman no adwumayɛ so ahwɛfoɔ ne wɔn aboafoɔ no sɛ:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: Mommma ɔman no ɛserɛ a wɔde bɛyɛ ntaayaa no bio sɛ akane no; wɔn ara wɔnkɔboaboa ɛserɛ ano mfa.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Na ntaayaa dodoɔ a na wɔyɛ daa no, monnye wɔn, monnyi so bi, ɛfiri sɛ wɔyɛ anihafoɔ, enti na wɔsu sɛ: Ma yɛnkɔ nkɔbɔ yɛn Nyankopɔn afɔdeɛ no.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Momma wɔn adwuma a emu yɛ den na wɔnyɛ, na wɔantie nsenhunu.

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no adwumayɛ so ahwɛfoɔ ne wɔn aboafoɔ no firii adi bɛka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Sɛ Farao seɛ nie: Meremma mo ɛserɛ bio.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Mo ara monkɔ nkɔpɛ ɛserɛ wɔ deɛ mobɛnya bie; na mo adwuma no nso wɔrente so hwee.

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no bɔ petee Misraim asase nyinaa so kɔboaboaa ayuo ntwakaeɛ ano de yɛɛ ɛserɛ mehemehe no.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Na akafoɔ no piapiaa wɔn kaa sɛ: Monwie mo da koro adwuma wɔ ne berɛ mu, sɛ berɛ a na ɛserɛ wɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Na wɔhwee Israelfoɔ ahwɛfoɔ a Farao adwumayɛ so ahwɛfoɔ de asisi wɔn soɔ no kaa sɛ: Ɛdeɛn nti na moanwie ntaayaa a wɔahyɛ mo nnɛ ne nnora no nyinaa sɛ akane no?

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israelfoɔ ahwɛfoɔ no ba bɛsu kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Ɛdeɛn nti na wo ne wo nkoa redi no saa?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Wɔmmaa wo nkoa ɛserɛ biara, nso wɔse yɛnyɛ ntaayaa; na hwɛ, wɔahwe wo nkoa, nso ɛyɛ wo ara wo nkurɔfoɔ no mfomsoɔ.

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Na Farao buaa sɛ: Anihafoɔ, anihafoɔ na moyɛ. Enti na mose: Ma yɛnkɔ nkɔbɔ AWURADE afɔdeɛ.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Enti monkɔ nkɔyɛ adwuma, na ɛserɛ deɛ, wɔremma mo, nso ntaayaa no dodoɔ deɛ, mobɛma ara.

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Na wɔkaa sɛ: Monnyi mo da koro adwuma mu ntaayaa no so ara da, na Israelfoɔ adwumayɛ so ahwɛfoɔ no hunuu sɛ amaneɛ na ato wɔn.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Na wɔfiri Farao nkyɛn reba no, wɔbɛtoo Mose ne Aaron a wɔgyina hɔ rebɛhyia wɔn,

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE nhwɛ mo mmu atɛn, sɛ moama yɛn ho abɔn wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim, na mode nkrantɛ ahyɛ wɔn nsa sɛ wɔmfa nku yɛn. Mose kasa kyerɛ AWURADE

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Na Mose sane baa AWURADE nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: AWURADE, adɛn na woayɛ ɔman yi bɔne sei? Adɛn na wosomaa me yi?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Na ɛfiri berɛ a mebaa Farao nkyɛn na mede wo din ne no kasaeɛ no, Farao ayɛ ɔman yi bɔne, na wo nso wonnyee wo man!

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Afei ansa na worebɛhunu deɛ mɛyɛ Farao, ɛfiri sɛ mede nsa a ɛyɛ den bɛma wama wɔakɔ, na mede nsa a ɛyɛ den bɛma wapamo wɔn afiri n’asase so mpo. Onyankopɔn frɛ Mose

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: a meyii me ho mekyerɛɛ Abraham ne Isak ne Yakob sɛ Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn, na me din YHWH no deɛ, mamma wɔamfa anhu me.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Nanso mama m’apam a me ne wɔn pameeɛ no agyina, sɛ mede Kanaan asase a ɛyɛ wɔn ahɔhobea asase a wɔyɛɛ so ahɔhoɔ no bɛma wɔn.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Nanso mate Israelfoɔ a Misraimfoɔ di wɔn nya no apinisie, na makae m’apam no.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Ɛno nti ka kyerɛ Israelfoɔ sɛ: Mene AWURADE, na mɛgye mo afiri Misraim nkoasom mu, na mayi mo afiri wɔn nyadie no mu, na mede basa a atene ne atemmuo akɛseɛ magye mo.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na mɛfa mo mayɛ me man, na mayɛ Onyankopɔn ama mo, na moahunu sɛ mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn a ɔgyee mo firii Misraim nkoasom mu.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na mede mo bɛkɔ asase a mekaa ntam sɛ mede bɛma Abraham, Isak, Yakob no so, na mede bɛma mo sɛ agyapadeɛ. Mene AWURADE.

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa saa kyerɛɛ Israelfoɔ no; nanso ahometeɛ ne nkoasom denden no nti wɔantie no.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: Kɔ, kɔka kyerɛ Misraimhene Farao sɛ ɔmma Israelfoɔ mfiri n’asase so nkɔ.

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mose kasae wɔ AWURADE anim sɛ: Hwɛ, Israelfoɔ ntie me, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na Farao bɛtie me a meyɛ ano mu momonoto yi.

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ne Mose ne Aaron kasae, na ɔhyɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnkɔ Israelfoɔ ne Misraimhene Farao nkyɛn nkɔyi Israelfoɔ no mfiri Misraim asase so. Mose ne Aaron mmusua

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne wɔn nananom afie mu atitire: Israel abakan Ruben mma ne: Hanok, Palu, Hesron ne Karmi; yeinom ne Ruben mmusua.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Na Simeon mma ne: Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yakin, Sohar ne Saulo a ɔyɛ Kanaanni baa bi ba; yeinom ne Simeon mmusua.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Na Gerson mma ne: Libni ne Simei wɔ wɔn mmusua ahodoɔ mu.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Merari mma ne: Mahli ne Musi. Yeinom ne Lewi mmusua, sɛdeɛ wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ teɛ.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Na Ishar mma ne: Kora, Nefeg ne Sikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Na Usiel mma ne: Misael, Elsafan ne Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Na Aaron faa Aminadab babaa Elisaba a ɔyɛ Nahson nua waree, na ɔwoo Nadab, Abihu, Eleasa ne Itamar maa no.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Na Kora mma ne: Asir, Elkana ne Abiasaf; yeinom ne Kora mma mmusua.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Na Aaron ba Eleasa faa Putiel mma mu bi waree, na ɔwoo Pinehas maa no. Yeinom ne Lewifoɔ nananom atitire sɛdeɛ wɔn mmusua teɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Aaron ne Mose a AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monyi Israelfoɔ mfiri Misraim asase so sɛdeɛ wɔn dɔm teɛ no.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Wɔne wɔn a wɔne Misraimhene Farao kasaa sɛ wɔbɛyi Israelfoɔ afiri Misraim akorɔ no, Mose ne Aaron korɔ no ara nie. AWURADE DE N’ASƐM MA MOSE

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na da a AWURADE ne Mose kasaa Misraim asase soɔ no,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mene AWURADE, ka deɛ mɛka makyerɛ woɔ nyinaa kyerɛ Misraimhene Farao.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa no AWURADE anim sɛ: Hwɛ, ano mu momonoto ne me, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na Farao bɛtie me?

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, madane wo Onyankopɔn ama Farao, na wo nua Aaron bɛyɛ wo diyifoɔ.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Wo deɛ, wobɛka deɛ mehyɛ woɔ nyinaa, na wo nua Aaron bɛka akyerɛ Farao sɛ ɔmma Israelfoɔ mfiri n’asase so nkɔ.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Nanso Farao rentie mo; na mede me nsa bɛto Misraim so, na mayi m’asafo, me man Israelfoɔ no, afiri Misraim asase so wɔ atemmuo akɛseɛ mu.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ metene me nsa wɔ Misraim so na meyi Israelfoɔ firi wɔn mu a, na Misraimfoɔ bɛhunu sɛ mene AWURADE.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: Sɛ Farao ka kyerɛ mo sɛ monyɛ anwanwadeɛ bi a, ɛnneɛ ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma no to fam wɔ Farao anim, na ɛbɛdane ɔwɔ.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔyɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ wɔn no; na Aaron de ne poma no too fam wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim, na ɛdanee ɔwɔ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Na Farao nso frɛfrɛɛ anyansafoɔ ne ntafowayifoɔ bae. Na Misraim akɔmfoɔ no nso de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nyinaa de wɔn mpoma totoo fam, na ɛdanedanee awɔ, nanso Aaron poma no memenee wɔn mpoma no.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Na Farao akoma pirimii ara, na wantie wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE kaeɛ no. Ɔhaw ahodoɔ ba Misraim

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Farao akoma yɛ den, ɔmpene sɛ ɔman no bɛkorɔ.
