english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn anɔpa; berɛ a ɔrefiri adi akɔ Asuo Nil ano; na kɔgyina asubɔnten no ano hyia no, na fa wo poma a ɛdanee ɔwɔ no kura.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: AWURADE, Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn, na wasoma me wo nkyɛn sɛ: Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me ɛserɛ so, na hwɛ, wontiee de abɛduru sɛsɛɛ.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE seɛ nie: Yei na wode bɛhunu sɛ mene AWURADE: Hwɛ, mede poma a mekura yi merebɔ nsuo a ɛwɔ Nil mu, na ɛbɛdane mogya.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Na mpataa a ɛwɔ asuo no mu bɛwuwu, na nsuo no bɛbɔn na Misraimfoɔ bɛkyiri sɛ wɔbɛnom asuo no mu nsuo.

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma, na tene wo nsa wɔ Misraim nsuo so, wɔn nsubɔntene, wɔn asuasu ne wɔn ntareɛ ne wɔn nsuo a ɛtaataa hɔ nyinaa so, na ɛnnanedane mogya; na mogya bɛba Misraim asase nyinaa so, nnua ne aboɔ nsuhina mu.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ wɔn no; na Aaron maa poma no so, na ɔde bɔɔ nsuo a ɛwɔ asubɔntene no mu wɔ Farao ne ne nkoa anim; na nsuo a ɛwɔ asuo no mu nyinaa danee mogya.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mpataa a ɛwɔ asuo no mu wuwui, na asuo no bɔnee, na Misraimfoɔ antumi annom asuo no mu nsuo, na mogya kataa Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Na Misraim akɔmfoɔ de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara. Na Farao akoma pirimii ara, na wantie wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE kaeɛ no.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Na Farao danee ne ho kɔɔ ne fie, na wamfa yei nso anto n’akomam.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Na Misraimfoɔ nyinaa tutuu asuo no ho mmura sɛ wɔrepɛ nsuo anom, ɛfiri sɛ na wɔntumi nnom asubɔntene no mu nsuo.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Na nnanson a AWURADE danee asuo no bɛtwaa mu.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE seɛ nie: Ma me man no nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Na sɛ woampene amma wɔankɔ a, hwɛ, mede mponkyerɛne bɛha w’asase nyinaa.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Na asuo no bɛdɔre mponkyerɛne pii, na wɔafoforo aba wo fie ne wo dabekyire, wo mpa so, wo nkoa afie, wo nkurɔfoɔ mu, w’afononoo mu ne wo mmɔre nkodoɔ mu.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na wo ne wo manfoɔ ne wo nkoa nyinaa so na mponkyerɛne no bɛforo aba. Mponkyerɛne no

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa wo poma no, na tene wo nsa wɔ nsubɔntene, asuasu, ne ntareɛ so, na ma mponkyerɛne mmra Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Aaron tenee ne nsa wɔ Misraim nsuo so, na mponkyerɛne ba bɛkataa Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Na akɔmfoɔ no de wɔn asumansɛm no yɛɛ saa ara maa mponkyerɛne foro baa Misraim asase so.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao frɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kaa sɛ: Mompa AWURADE kyɛw na ɔnyi mponkyerɛne no mfiri me ne me man so, na mɛma ɔman no akɔ akɔbɔ afɔdeɛ ama AWURADE.

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Wo ara kyerɛ me da ko a ɛnkɔsie na mempa kyɛw memma wo ne wo nkoa ne wo man, na wɔnyi mponkyerɛne no mfiri wo ne wo fie so, na wɔnka asuo no nko ara mu.

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Ɔkyena. Na Mose kaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ sɛ deɛ woaka no, na woahunu sɛ obiara biara nni hɔ a ɔte sɛ AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Na mponkyerɛne no bɛfiri wo ne wo fie ne wo nkoa ne wo man so; asuo no mu nko ara na wɔbɛka.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron firii Farao anim kɔe. Na Mose teaa mu frɛɛ AWURADE wɔ mponkyerɛne a ɔde aba Farao soɔ no ho.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Mose kaeɛ no, na mponkyerɛne no wuwui, afie mu ne adihɔ ne wiram.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Na wɔboaboaa wɔn ano akuakuo, na asase no so bɔnee.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Na Farao hunuu sɛ wanya ahotɔ no, ɔpirim n’akoma, na wantie wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE kaeɛ no. Mfuturo danee edwie

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Aaron sɛ: Tene wo poma no bɔ asase so mfuturo na ɛnnane edwie wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Na wɔyɛɛ saa, na Aaron tenee ne nsa de poma no bɔɔ asase so mfuturo, na ɛdanee edwie wɔ nnipa ne mmoa so. Na asase so mfuturo nyinaa danee edwie Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Na akɔmfoɔ no de wɔn asumansɛm yɛɛ saa ara sɛ wɔrema edwie aba, nanso wɔantumi. Na edwie no baa nnipa ne mmoa so.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ɛnna akɔmfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Nyankopɔn nsateaa nie. Na Farao akoma pirimii ara na wantie wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE kaeɛ no. Nwansena pii ba

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tua anɔpahema kɔgyina Farao anim; berɛ a ɔrefiri adi aba nsuo no ano; na ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE seɛ nie: Ma me man no nkɔ na wɔnkɔsom me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ woremma me man no nkɔ a, hwɛ, mɛma nwansena ahodoɔ aba wo ne wo nkoa ne wo man ne w’afie so, na nwansena no bɛyɛ Misraimfoɔ afie mu ne asase a wɔte soɔ no so amaama.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛɛ saa. Na nwansena a wɔdɔɔso pii baa Farao fie ne ne nkoa afie ne Misraim asase nyinaa so. Na nwansena no nti asase no so sɛee.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kaa sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔbɔ afɔdeɛ mma mo Nyankopɔn wɔ asase yi so.

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Ɛmfata sɛ wɔyɛ no saa, ɛfiri sɛ Misraim akyiwadeɛ na yɛde bɛbɔ afɔdeɛ ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn. Hwɛ, sɛ yɛde Misraim akyiwadeɛ bɔ afɔdeɛ wɔ wɔn anim a, wɔrensi yɛn aboɔ anaa?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Yɛbɛnante nnansa kwan akɔ ɛserɛ so, na yɛakɔbɔ afɔdeɛ ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn, sɛdeɛ waka akyerɛ yɛn no.

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kaa sɛ: Me deɛ, mɛma mo kwan na moakɔbɔ afɔdeɛ ama AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn wɔ ɛserɛ so, na akyirikyiri nko na monnkorɔ; mompa kyɛw mma me.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Hwɛ, merebɛfiri wo nkyɛn makɔ makɔpa AWURADE kyɛw na nwansena no afiri Farao ne ne nkoa ne ne man so ɔkyena; na nkontompo nko ara na Farao nntwa bio sɛ ɔremma ɔman no nkɔ nkɔbɔ afɔdeɛ mma AWURADE.

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose firii Farao anim kɔ kɔpaa AWURADE kyɛw.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yɛɛ deɛ Mose kaeɛ no, na ɔyii nwansena no firii Farao ne ne nkoa ne ne man so; anka baako mpo.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Na Farao pirim n’akoma saa berɛ yi nso, na wamma ɔman no ankɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn no seɛ nie: Ma me man no nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: hwɛ, AWURADE nsa bɛda wo mmoa a wɔwɔ wiram so, na ɔde owuo a ano yɛ den kɛse bɛba apɔnkɔ, mfunumu, yoma, anantwie ne nnwan so.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de nsonsonoeɛ bɛto Israel mmoa ne Misraim mmoa ntam, na deɛ ɛyɛ Israelfoɔ dea no mu biara renwu.

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hyɛɛ da sɛ: Ɔkyena na AWURADE bɛyɛ yei wɔ asase soɔ.

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Na adeɛ kyeeɛ no, AWURADE yɛɛ saa adeɛ no, na Misraim mmoa nyinaa wuwui, na Israel mmoa no mu baako mpo anwu.

english_verse: When the king found out, he was still too stubborn to let the people go. Sores
translation_verse: Na Farao soma maa wɔkɔhwɛe, na hwɛ, na Israelfoɔ mmoa no mu baako mpo nwui. Nanso Farao akoma yɛɛ den ara, na wamma ɔman no ankɔ. Mpɔmpɔ yaredɔm

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: Momfa fononoo mu nso nsa ma, na Mose nto mpete ahunum wɔ Farao anim,

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: na ɛnnane Misraim asase nyinaa so tutuo, na ɛnyɛ nnipa ne mmoa ho mpɔmpɔ a ɛpaepae tutu akuro Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Na wɔsesaa fononoo mu nso, na wɔkɔgyinaa Farao anim, na Mose de petee ahunum, na ɛdanee nnipa ne mmoa ho mpɔmpɔ a ɛpaepae tutu akuro.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Na mpɔmpɔ no nti akɔmfoɔ no antumi annyina Mose anim, ɛfiri sɛ na mpɔmpɔ no asisi akɔmfoɔ ne Misraimfoɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao akoma, na wantie wɔn, sɛdeɛ AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose no. Ɔsoro aboɔ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tua anɔpahema kɔgyina Farao anim, na ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn no seɛ nie: Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Na afei deɛ, merema me haw nyinaa aba w’akoma so ne wo nkoa ne wo man mu, na woahunu sɛ obiara nni hɔ a ɔte sɛ me wɔ asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Na afei sɛ matene me nsa na mede owuyadeɛ mabɔ wo ne wo man a, anka wɔatwa wo afiri asase so.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Nanso yei nti na mema wogyina hɔ, sɛ mɛyi me tumi adi makyerɛ wo, na wɔaka me din ho asɛm asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Woda so ma wo ho so na wosi me man kwan sɛ woremma wɔnkɔ.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɔkyena sɛsɛɛ mɛma ɔsoro aboɔ a emu yɛ duro pa a ɛso bi mmaa Misraim da firi da a wɔhyɛɛ aseɛ de abɛduru nnɛ yi atɔ.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Na afei soma ma wɔnkɔfa wo mmoa ne wo biribiara a ɛwɔ wiram mmra ntɛm; onipa biara afieboa biara a wɔbɛhu no wiram na wɔamfa no amma fie no, sɛ ɔsoro aboɔ no gu wɔn so a, wɔbɛwuwu.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Farao nkoa mu, deɛ ɔsuro AWURADE asɛm no de ne nkoa ne ne mmoa dwane baa fie;

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: na deɛ wammu AWURADE asɛm no deɛ, ɔgyaa ne nkoa ne ne mmoa wɔ wiram.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tene wo nsa kɔ ahunum, na ɔsoro aboɔ ntɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so, nnipa ne mmoa ne wiram nhahan nyinaa so wɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔsoro aboɔ ne ogya a ɛdɛre framfram toatoam a ɛfra ɔsoro aboɔ no mu a ano yɛ den pii pa a ɛso bi mmaa Misraim asase nyinaa so da firi da a ɛyɛɛ ɔman no bae.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Gye Gosen asase a Israelfoɔ wɔ soɔ no so nko na ɔsoro aboɔ no bi antɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao soma maa wɔbɛfrɛɛ Mose ne Aaron ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Yei deɛ, mayɛ bɔne, AWURADE ne ɔteneneeni, na me ne me man ne abɔnefoɔ.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Mompa AWURADE kyɛw, na Nyankopɔn aprannaa ne ɔsoro aboɔ no nnyae, na adɔɔso, na mɛma moakɔ na morentena ha bio.

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mefiri adi mefiri kuro no mu ara pɛ a, mɛtrɛ me nsam makyerɛ AWURADE, na aprannaa no to bɛtwa, na ɔsoro aboɔ no antɔ bio, na woahunu sɛ AWURADE na asase wɔ no.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Na wo ne wo nkoa deɛ, menim sɛ monnya nsuroo AWURADE Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Na ɛguu asaawa ne atokoɔ so, nso na atokoɔ no ayɛ mmɛtem, na asaawa no nso reyɛ agu nhyerɛne.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Na ayuo ne kɔkɔte deɛ, angu so bi, ɛfiri sɛ ɛno ka akyi.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na Mose firii Farao nkyɛn, na ɔfirii kuro no mu kɔtrɛɛ ne nsam kyerɛɛ AWURADE, na aprannaa ne ɔsoro aboɔ no to twae, na osuo no gyaee asase no so guo.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Na Farao hunuu sɛ osutɔ ne ɔsoro aboɔ ne aprannaa no to atwa no, ɔsane yɛɛ bɔne bio, na ɔpirimm n’akoma, ɔno ne ne nkoa.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Na Farao akoma pirimii ara, na wamma Israelfoɔ no ankɔ, sɛdeɛ AWURADE nam Mose so kaeɛ no.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Kɔ Farao nkyɛn, na mapirim ɔne ne nkoa akoma, na mayi me nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ yi adi wɔ wɔn mu,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: na woaka deɛ meyɛeɛ wɔ Misraim ne me nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ a meyii no adie wɔ wɔn mu no wɔ wo ba ne wo ba ba aso mu, na moahunu sɛ mene AWURADE.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron kɔɔ Farao nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE, Hebrifoɔ Nyankopɔn no seɛ nie: Wobɛma wo ho so wɔ m’anim akɔsi da bɛn? Ma me man nkɔ nkɔsom me.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Na sɛ woampene amma me man ankɔ a, hwɛ, ɔkyena mɛma ntutummɛ aba w’asase so,

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: na wɔabɛkata ani a obi renhunu asase ani, na wɔabɛdi nnikaeɛ a ɔsoro aboɔ no gya maa no ka maa mo no, na wɔabɛdi nnua a ɛrefefɛ ama mo wɔ mfuo mu no nyinaa,

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: na wɔabɛyeyɛ w’afie mu ne wo nkoa nyinaa afie mu ne Misraimfoɔ nyinaa afie mu amaama, sɛdeɛ wo nananom ne wɔn nananom nhunuu bi pɛn firi da a wɔbaa asase soɔ bɛduru nnɛ. Na ɔdanee ne ho firii Farao nkyɛn.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao nkoa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Da bɛn ara na oyi nteetee yɛn ara nkɔsie? Ma nnipa no nkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE wɔn Nyankopɔn. Wonnya nhunuu sɛ Misraim resɛe anaa?

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Na wɔde Mose ne Aaron sane baa Farao anim bio, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn. Ɛhefoɔ ne wɔn a wɔbɛkɔ no?

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose se: Yɛde yɛn mmɔfra ne yɛn mpanin na ɛrekorɔ; yɛde yɛn mmabanin ne yɛn mmammaa, yɛn nnwan ne yɛn anantwie na ɛrekorɔ, ɛfiri sɛ yɛwɔ fa bi hyɛ ma AWURADE.

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: A, ɛnneɛ AWURADE nni mo akyi ɛ, sɛ merema mo ne mo mma akorɔ yi! Mahunu sɛ bɔne na mopɛ sɛ moyɛ yi.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Dabi da! Mo mmarima na monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE, na ɛno ara na mohwehwɛ. Na wɔpamm wɔn firii Farao anim. Ntutummɛ no

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Ntutummɛ no nti tene wo nsa wɔ Misraim asase so, na wɔmmra Misraim asase so, na wɔmmɛwe asase no so nhahan nyinaa, deɛ ɔsoro aboɔ no gyaeɛ no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Na Mose tenee ne poma no wɔ Misraim asase so, na AWURADE maa apueeɛ mframa bɔ faa asase no so da no nyinaa ne anadwo no nyinaa. Na adeɛ kyeeɛ no, apueeɛ mframa no de ntutummɛ no bae.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Na ntutummɛ no baa Misraim asase no so nyinaa, na wɔbɛguu Misraim nyinaa, na wɔdɔɔso pii. Ebi nnii wɔn anim mmaa pɛn a ɛte sɛ wɔn, na wɔn akyiri nso ebi remma saa bio.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Na wɔkataa asase no nyinaa ani maa esum duruu asase no so, na wɔdii asase no so nhahan nyinaa ne nnua a ɔsoro aboɔ no gyaeɛ no so aba nyinaa, na biribiara anka a ɛyɛ mono wɔ nnua mu ne mfuo mu nhahan mu wɔ Misraim asase no so nyinaa.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao yɛɛ ntɛm soma maa wɔkɔfrɛɛ Mose ne Aaron kaa sɛ: Mayɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn ne mo bɔne.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Na afei, fa me bɔne kyɛ me prɛko yi nko ara, na mompa AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn kyɛw, na ɔnyi owuo yi nko mfiri me so.

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Na ɔfirii Farao nkyɛn kɔ kɔpaa AWURADE kyɛw.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa atɔeɛ mframa a ano yɛ den pii bae, na ɛbɛfaa ntutummɛ no kɔe, na ɛde wɔn kɔguu Mmɛwa Po mu; ntutummɛ no baako mpo anka Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao akoma, na wamma Israelfoɔ no ankɔ. Esum duru

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tene wo nsa kɔ ahunum, na esum nnuru Misraim asase so, na ɛnyɛ esum a wosɔ mu a ɛbɛyɛ yie.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Na Mose tenee ne nsa kɔɔ ahunum, na esum kabii duruu Misraim asase no nyinaa so nnansa.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Obiara anhunu ne yɔnko, na obiara ansɔre ne tenabea nnansa; na Israelfoɔ nyinaa deɛ, wɔnyaa hann wɔ deɛ na wɔteɛ hɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao frɛɛ Mose sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE; mo nnwan ne mo anantwie nko ara na wɔmfa nsie ha; mo mma nso ne mo nkɔ.

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Ɛsɛ sɛ wode afɔrebɔdeɛ a wɔkum na wɔhyeɛ nso hyɛ yɛn nsa, na yɛde akɔbɔ ama AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Na yɛn mmoa nso ne yɛn bɛkɔ, ɛrenka tɔte mpo; na ɛnonom bi na yɛde rekɔsom AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn. Na yɛn deɛ, yɛnnim deɛ yɛde bɛsom AWURADE gye sɛ yɛaduru ansa.

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Farao akoma, na wampɛ sɛ ɔma wɔkɔ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Firi me so kɔ, hwɛ wo ho yie, na mma m’anim bio; na da a wobɛba m’anim no, wobɛwu.

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buaa sɛ: Aane mate! Meremma w’anim bio.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mɛma ɔhaw baako aba Farao ne Misraim so bio, na ɛno akyiri no, ɔbɛma moafiri ha akɔ koraa; pamo mpo na ɔbɛpamo mo afiri ha.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Afei kasa ma ɔman no nte sɛ: Mmarima ne mmaa mmisabisa wɔn nnamfonom hɔ dwetɛ nnwinneɛ ne sika nnwinneɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa ɔman no anim baa nyam wɔ Misraimfoɔ anim; nso ɔbarima Mose no yɛ kɛseɛ pa wɔ Misraim asase no so wɔ Farao nkoa ne ɔman no anim.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE seɛ nie: Anadwo dasuo mu no, mɛfiri adi mafa Misraim,

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: na Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa bɛwuwu, ɛfiri Farao abakan a ɔtena n’adwa soɔ so de kɔsi afenaa a ɔwɔ oyuyammoɔ akyire abakan ne mmoa mmakan nyinaa so.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Na osu kɛseɛ a ɛso bi mmaa da, na ɛso bi nso remma bio bɛba Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma nyinaa deɛ, ɔkraman mpo rentwe ne tɛkyerɛma ntia wɔn, ɛfiri nnipa so kɔsi mmoa so, na moahunu sɛ AWURADE apae Misraim ne Israel ntam.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Na wo nkoa yi nyinaa bɛsiane aba me nkyɛn abɛkoto me aka sɛ: Firi adi kɔ, wo ne ɔman a ɛdi w’akyire no nyinaa. Na ɛno akyiri no mɛfiri makɔ. Na ɔde abufuhyeɛ firii Farao nkyɛn kɔe.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Farao rentie mo, na ama m’anwanwadeɛ adɔɔso wɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron yɛɛ anwanwadeɛ yi nyinaa wɔ Farao anim, na AWURADE pirim Farao akoma, na wamma Israelfoɔ no amfiri n’asase so ankɔ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron wɔ Misraim asase so sɛ:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: Momfa bosome yi nyɛ abosome ti, na ɛnyɛ mo afe mu bosome a ɛdi kan.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Monka nkyerɛ Israel asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Bosome yi da a ɛtɔ so du no, wɔmfa nnwammaa mmaako mmaako, sɛdeɛ wɔn mpanimfie teteɛ; efie baako adwammaa baako.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Na momfa no nsie nkɔduru bosome yi da a ɛtɔ so dunan; na Israel asafo mu no nyinaa nkɔku wɔn anwummerɛ.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Na wɔmfa mogya no bi nsra adan a wɔbɛdi wɔ mu no aponnwa mmienu ne aponnwatifi no ho.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Na wɔnni nam no anadwo no ara; wɔmfa ogya ntoto, na wɔmfa apiti ne fan nwononwono nni.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Monnni no amono, na mommfa nsuo nnnoa, na mmom momfa ogya ntoto no mua a, ne ti ne n’asrɛ ne n’ayamdeɛ nyinaa ka ho.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Na monnnya bi nnsie na adeɛ nnkye so. Na sɛ ebi ka na adeɛ kye so a, momfa ogya nhye.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛdeɛ monni no nie: Monkyekyere mo asene, na mo mpaboa nhyehyɛ mo nan, na mo mpoma nkurakura mo nsam, na monni no herɛ so: Ɛyɛ AWURADE twam.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na merebɛtwam Misraim asase so anadwo yi, na makum Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, ɛfiri nnipa so kɔsi mmoa so, na mɛbu Misraim anyame nyinaa atɛn, mene AWURADE.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mogya no nyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ mma mo, afie a mowowɔ mu no mu, na sɛ mehunu mogya no a, masiane mo ho, na merebɔ Misraim asase a, ɔyaredɔm biara amma mo so ammɛsɛe mo.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Na ɛda yi nyɛ mo nkaeɛ, na monhyɛ ho fa mma AWURADE, mo awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ mu; monyɛ no afahyɛ, daa atorɔmudeɛ. Apiti afahyɛ no

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Nnanson na monni apiti. Da a ɛdi kan no ara na monyi mmɔreka nyinaa mfiri mo afie mu, ɛfiri sɛ obiara a ɔbɛdi mmɔreka paanoo firi da a ɛdi kan no de akɔsi da a ɛtɔ so nson no, wɔbɛtwa saa ɔkra no afiri Israel mu.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛdi kan no monhyia nhyia kronkron, na da a ɛtɔ so nson no nso monhyia nhyia kronkron. Wɔnnyɛ adwuma biara wɔ mu, gye deɛ obiara bɛdie nko ho adwuma na monyɛ.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Na monhyɛ apiti fa no, ɛfiri sɛ saa da yi ara na meyii mo dɔm no firii Misraim asase soɔ. Ɛno nti monni da yi mo awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ mu nyɛ no daa atorɔmudeɛ.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Bosome a ɛdi kan no da a ɛtɔ so dunan no anwummerɛ no momfiri apiti die ase nkɔsi bosome no da a ɛtɔ so aduonu baako anwummerɛ.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Nnanson na mommma wɔnnhunu mmɔreka wɔ mo afie mu, ɛfiri sɛ obiara a ɔbɛdi paanoo a emu aka no, ɔhɔhoɔ oo, deɛ wɔwoo no asase no soɔ oo, wɔbɛtwa saa ɔkra no afiri Israel asafo mu.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Monnni biribiara a emu aka. Monni apiti mo tenabea nyinaa. Twam afahyɛ mfitiaseɛ

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose frɛɛ Israel mpanimfoɔ nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monyiyi nnwan mfa, sɛdeɛ mo mmusua teɛ, na monkum twam aboa no.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Na momfa adwera esia mmɔ mogya a ɛwɔ yaawa mu no mu, na momfa yaawa no mu mogya no bi nsra aponnwatifi ne aponnwa mmienu no ho, na mo mu biara mmfiri adi mmfiri ne fie pono ano kɔsi anɔpa.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE bɛtwam abobɔ Misraimfoɔ, na sɛ ɔhunu mogya no wɔ aponnwatifi ne aponnwa mmienu no ho a, AWURADE bɛsiane pono no ho, na ɔremma ɔsɛefoɔ no kwan mma ɔmma mo afie mmɛbobɔ mo.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Na sɛ moduru asase a AWURADE de bɛma mo sɛdeɛ ɔkaeɛ no so a, monni ɛsom yi so.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mo mma bisa mo sɛ: Mo som yi aseɛ ne sɛn a,

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase sɔree. Na Israelfoɔ sii mu kɔ kɔyɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose ne Aaron no. Wɔkum Misraimfoɔ mmakan

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na anadwo dasuo mu no, AWURADE bobɔɔ Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, ɛfiri Farao abakan a ɔtena n’adwa soɔ so de kɔsi dommum a ɔwɔ deduadan mu abakan so ne afieboa mmakan nyinaa.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao sɔree anadwo no ara, ɔne ne nkoa nyinaa ne Misraimfoɔ nyinaa, na esu kɛseɛ baa Misraim, ɛfiri sɛ na efie biara nni hɔ a efunu nni mu.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Mose ne Aaron anadwo no kaa sɛ: Monsɔre mfiri me man mu, mo ne Israelfoɔ no, na monkɔ nkɔsom AWURADE, sɛdeɛ mokaeɛ no.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mo nnwan ne mo anantwie nso, momfa wɔn, sɛdeɛ mokaeɛ no, na monkɔ, na monhyira me nso.

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Na Misraimfoɔ piapiaa ɔman no sɛ wɔnyɛ ntɛm mfiri asase no so, ɛfiri sɛ wɔse: Yɛn nyinaa rewuwu.

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no soasoaa wɔn mmɔre ansa na ɛreka, kyekyeree wɔn mmɔre nkodoɔ wɔ wɔn ntoma mu de sisii wɔn kɔn ho.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no yeyɛɛ sɛdeɛ Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn no, na wɔbisabisaa Misraimfoɔ hɔ dwetɛ nnwinneɛ, sika nnwinneɛ ne ntoma.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa ɔman no anim baa nyam, Misraimfoɔ anim, na wɔde deɛ wɔbisaeɛ maa wɔn. Na wɔfaa Misraimfoɔ agyapadeɛ no kɔe. Israelfoɔ firi Misraim

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no sii mu firii Rameses kɔɔ Sukot, wɔbɛyɛ mmarima a wɔnam fam, mpem ahansia, wɔankan mmaa ne mmɔfra anka ho.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Na afrafrafoɔ pii nso ne wɔn kɔe, ne nnwan ne anantwie, mmoa pii pa ara.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Na wɔde mmɔre a wɔde firi Misraim baeɛ no totoo apiti ɔfam, na na ɛnkae, ɛfiri sɛ Misraimfoɔ no pamm wɔn, a wɔantwentwɛn wɔn nan ase, na wɔannya kwan nso ansiesie akwansoduane.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Ɛyɛ anadwo a AWURADE ankasa dii Israelfoɔ no afoofi na ɔyii wɔn firii Misraim asase so. Wɔhyɛ ho fa de ma AWURADE wɔ Israelfoɔ nyinaa mu wɔn awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ mu. Twam no ho nhyehyɛɛ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: Yei ne twam no ho ahyɛdeɛ: Ɔnanani biara nnni bi.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Na obiara akoa a ɔde sika atɔ no no, twa no twetia ansa na wadi bi.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Mo nkyɛn tenafoɔ ne ɔpaani nnni bi.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Efie baako mu na wɔnnie, wɔmmfa nam no bi mmfiri fie hɔ mmfiri adi, na mommmu ne dompe bi.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israel asafo nyinaa nyɛ saa.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Na sɛ obi abɛyɛ wo nkyɛn hɔhoɔ na ɔpɛ sɛ ɔdi twam ma AWURADE a, ma wɔntwa ne mmarima nyinaa twetia, na ɛno ansa na ɔmpinkyɛ mmɛdie, na ɔnyɛ sɛ deɛ wɔwoo no asase no soɔ; na momonoto biara deɛ, ɔnnni bi.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mmara koro nna hɔ mma okuromani ne ɔhɔhoɔ a ɔbɛsoɛ mo mu.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ nyinaa yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose ne Aaron no; saa ara na wɔyɛeɛ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na da no ara AWURADE yii Israelfoɔ no firii Misraim asase so, sɛdeɛ wɔn asafo teɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: Yɛ mmakan nyinaa, Israelfoɔ mu adeɛ biara a ɛbue yafunu ano wɔ nnipa ne afieboa mu, kronkron ma me, na me dea. Apiti afahyɛ no

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE nya de wo duru Kanaanfoɔ, Hetifoɔ, Amorifoɔ, Hewifoɔ ne Yebusifoɔ asase a ɔkaa wo nananom ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma woɔ, asase a nufosuo ne ɛwoɔ sene soɔ no so a, ɛno deɛ, fa ɛsom yi som no bosome yi mu.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nnanson na di apiti, na da a ɛtɔ so nson no, hyɛ fa ma AWURADE.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Wɔnni apiti nnanson no, na mma wɔnnhunu wo nkyɛn mmɔreka paanoo anaa mmɔreka w’asase baabiara.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɛda no, bɔ din kyerɛ wo ba sɛ: Deɛ AWURADE yɛɛ me berɛ a mefirii Misraim no ntira.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɛnyɛ wo nsa so nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ ne w’aniwa ntam nkaeɛ adeɛ, na AWURADE mmara no atena w’anomu, ɛfiri sɛ nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii wo firii Misraim.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Enti di atorɔmudeɛ yi so wɔ ne berɛ mu afe daa. Mmakan no

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE de wo duru Kanaanfoɔ asase so, sɛ deɛ ɔkaa wo ne wo nananom ntam, na ɔde ma wo a,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: yi adeɛ biara a ɛbue yafunu ano ma AWURADE, na w’afieboa a wowɔ no mma nyinaa a wɔbue yafunu ano a wɔyɛ anini, fa ma AWURADE.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Na mfunumu mmakan nyinaa deɛ, fa odwan sesa, na sɛ woansesa a, bu ne kɔn mu. Na nnipa mmakan a wɔwɔ wo mmammarima mu nyinaa deɛ, sesa gye wɔn.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔkyena bi wo ba bisa wo sɛ: Yei aseɛ ne sɛn a, ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii yɛn firii Misraim nkoasom mu.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Na Farao pirim n’akoma na ɔmpene sɛ ɔbɛma yɛakorɔ no, AWURADE kumm Misraim asase so mmakan nyinaa, ɛfiri nnipa mmakan so kɔsi afieboa mmakan so. Ɛno nti na me nso mede anini a ɛbue yafunu ano no nyinaa mebɔ AWURADE afɔdeɛ, nanso me mma mu mmakan nyinaa deɛ, mesesa agye wɔn.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Na ɛnyɛ wo nsa so nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ ne w’aniwa ntam nkaeɛ adeɛ, sɛ nsa a ɛyɛ den na AWURADE de yii yɛn firii Misraim. Mununkum dum ne ogya dum

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Farao maa ɔman no kwan no, Onyankopɔn amfa wɔn ankɔfa Filistifoɔ asase so kwan a ɛnwareɛ no, ɛfiri sɛ Onyankopɔn se: Na ɔman no ankɔhyia ɔsa annu wɔn ho, na wɔansane ankɔ Misraim.

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Enti Onyankopɔn de ɔman no konton faa ɛserɛ so kwan a ɛda Mmɛwa Po ho no so. Na Israelfoɔ no kaa ntoa firii Misraim asase so kɔe.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Na Mose faa Yosef nnompe no, ɛfiri sɛ Yosef aka Israelfoɔ ntam sɛ: Hwɛ na Onyankopɔn bɛba abɛhwɛ mo, na momfa me nnompe mfiri ha nkɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔsii mu firii Sukot kɔkyeree nsraban wɔ Etam, wɔ ɛserɛ no ano.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ Israelfoɔ no ma wɔnnane nkɔkyere nsraban wɔ Pihahirot anim wɔ Migdol ne po ntam, wɔ Baalsefon anim; ne ntentensoɔ na monkyere nsraban no wɔ po no ano.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Na Farao bɛka no Israelfoɔ ho sɛ: Wɔrewɔ asase no so ntwɛtwɛdɛ, ɛserɛ aka wɔn atom.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Na mɛpirim Farao akoma ama no ati wɔn, na mɛhyɛ m’anim nyam Farao ne ne dɔm nyinaa so, na Misraimfoɔ ahunu sɛ mene AWURADE. Na Israelfoɔ yɛɛ saa.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Misraimhene sɛ ɔman no adwane kɔ. Na Farao ne ne nkoa akoma sakyerae wɔ ɔman no ho, na wɔse: Ɛdeɛn na yɛayɛ yi, sɛ yɛama Israel agyae yɛn som korɔ yi?

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Na ɔsiesiee ne teaseɛnam, na ɔfaa ne man kaa ne ho,

english_verse: He commanded his officers in charge of his
translation_verse: na ɔfaa nteaseɛnam a wɔayie ahansia ne Misraim nteaseɛnam nyinaa ne nteaseɛnam no nyinaa so asahene.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pirim Misraimhene Farao akoma maa no tii Israelfoɔ no, ɛfiri sɛ Israelfoɔ no de ahosɛpɛ kɛseɛ na ɛfiri kɔeɛ.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Na Misraimfoɔ tii wɔn, Farao nteaseɛnam apɔnkɔ nyinaa ne n’apɔnkɔfoɔ ne ne dɔm no, na wɔbɛtoo wɔn sɛ wɔakyere nsraban wɔ po no ano a ɛkyerɛ Pihahirot wɔ Baalsefon anim.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Na Farao bɛneeɛ no, Israelfoɔ no memaa wɔn ani so, na hwɛ, na Misraimfoɔ di wɔn akyiri reba. Na Israelfoɔ no suroo pii, na wɔsu frɛɛ AWURADE.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Adamena a ɛnni Misraim nti na woafa yɛn aba ha sɛ yɛmmɛwuwu ɛserɛ soɔ yi? Ɛdeɛn nti na woayɛ yɛn sɛɛ yi, sɛ woyii yɛn firii Misraim baeɛ yi?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ɛnyɛ asɛm a yɛkaa wo wɔ Misraim sɛ: Gyae ma yɛnsom Misraim, no nie? Ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ ma yɛn mmom sɛ anka yɛsom Misraim sene sɛ yɛbɛwuwu ɛserɛ so.

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Monnsuro, monnyina pintinn, na monhwɛ AWURADE nkwagyeɛ a ɔde rebɛkyerɛ mo nnɛ, na Misraimfoɔ a mohu wɔn nnɛ yi, morenhu wɔn da biara da bio.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: AWURADE bɛko ama mo, na mo deɛ, monyɛ komm!

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Adɛn na wosu frɛ me? Ka kyerɛ Israelfoɔ ma wɔnkɔ wɔn anim.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Na wo deɛ, ma wo poma no so, na tene wo nsa ɛpo no so, na bae mu, na Israelfoɔ no nnante asase pɛsɛɛ so mfa po no mfimfini.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Na me deɛ, hwɛ, mɛpirim Misraimfoɔ akoma, na wɔabɛdi wɔn akyi, na mɛhyɛ m’anim nyam wɔ Farao ne ne dɔm nyinaa, ne nteaseɛnam ne n’apɔnkɔfoɔ no so,

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: na Misraimfoɔ no ahunu sɛ mene AWURADE, sɛ mahyɛ m’anim nyam wɔ Farao ne ne nteaseɛnam ne n’apɔnkɔfoɔ no so.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Nyankopɔn bɔfoɔ a ɔdi Israel dɔm anim no twee ne ho bɛdii wɔn akyire, na mununkum dum no firii wɔn anim bɛgyinaa wɔn akyi,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: na ɛbɛfirii Misraim dɔm ne Israel dɔm ntam, na ɛyɛ mununkum ne esum, nanso ɛma hann anadwo, na amma yeinom antumi ammɛn yeinom anadwo no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Na Mose tenee ne nsa ɛpo no so. Na AWURADE de apueeɛ mframa denden maa ɛpo no kɔe anadwo no nyinaa, na ɔdanee po no maa no yɛɛ asase pɛsɛɛ, na nsuo no mu baee.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no nam asase pɛsɛɛ so faa ɛpo no mfimfini, na nsuo no yɛɛ wɔn ɔfasuo wɔn nifa ne wɔn benkum.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa nsraberɛ mu no AWURADE faa ogya ne mununkum dum no hwɛɛ Misraim dɔm no, na ɔmaa Misraim dɔm no ho yeraa wɔn,

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: na ɔhwinhwan wɔn nteaseɛnam nan maa ne nanteɛ mu yɛɛ du. Na Misraimfoɔ no se: Momma yɛnnwane wɔ Israel anim, ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE reko tia Misraim ama wɔn.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Tene wo nsa ɛpo no so, na nsuo no nsane mmra Misraimfoɔ ne wɔn nteaseɛnam ne wɔn apɔnkɔfoɔ no so.

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose tenee ne nsa ɛpo no soɔ, na adeɛ rekye anɔpa no, ɛpo no sanee n’akyi bɛsenee sɛdeɛ na ɛteɛ, na Misraimfoɔ no dwane bɛhyiae. Na AWURADE kaa wɔn guu po no mfimfini.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Na nsuo no sanee akyire bɛkataa Farao dɔm, nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔfoɔ a wɔtii wɔn baa ɛpo no mu no nyinaa so, wɔn mu baako mpo anka.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no nam asase pɛsɛɛ so faa ɛpo no mfimfini, na nsuo no yɛɛ wɔn ɔfasuo wɔn nifa ne wɔn benkum.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE gyee Israel nkwa da no firii Misraim nsam, na Israel hunuu Misraimfoɔ no sɛ wɔawuwu gu ɛpo no ano.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Na Israel hunuu nsa kɛseɛ a AWURADE de kyerɛɛ Misraim soɔ no, na ɔman no suroo AWURADE, na wɔgyee AWURADE ne n’akoa Mose diiɛ.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose ne Israelfoɔ too dwom yi maa AWURADE kaa sɛ: Mɛto AWURADE dwom, na ma na wama ne ho soɔ, ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefoɔ no, wato wɔn agu ɛpo mu.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: M’ahoɔden ne me dwontoɔ ne AWURADE, na wayɛ me nkwagyeɛ. Ɔno ne me Nyankopɔn, na mɛkamfo no. Ɔyɛ m’agya Nyankopɔn, na mɛma no so.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: AWURADE yɛ dɔmmarima, AWURADE ne ne din.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Farao nteaseɛnam ne ne dɔm no, wato wɔn agu ɛpo mu, na n’akofoɔ a wɔayi wɔn no, wɔamemmem Mmɛwa Po mu.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Ebunu akata wɔn so, wɔamem kɔ aseɛ tɔnn sɛ ɔboɔ.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: AWURADE, wode tumi ahyɛ wo nsa nifa animuonyam, AWURADE, wo nsa nifa no dwɛre atamfoɔ no.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Na wo tumi a ɛso no ara na wode butu wɔn a wɔsɔre tia woɔ no. Wosoma w’abufuhyeɛ ba, ɛhye wɔn sɛ nkyɛnkyɛmma.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Na wo hwene mu ahome mu na nsuo no ano boaeɛ; asorɔkyeɛ gyinaa sɛ ekuo; abunu kyekyeree ɛpo yam.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Ɔtamfoɔ no kaa sɛ: Mɛti wɔn, mɛto wɔn, mɛkyɛ asase no mu, wɔbɛmee me kra. Mɛtwe me nkrantɛ, me nsa bɛsɛe wɔn.

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Wode wo mframa hui, ɛpo no kataa wɔn so; wɔmemee sɛ sumpii wɔ nsu kɛseɛ no mu.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: Hwan na ɔte sɛ woɔ, AWURADE, wɔ anyame mu? Hwan na ɔte sɛ woɔ, kronkronyɛ mu onimuonyamfoɔ, deɛ ne ho yɛ hu ayeyie mu, anwanwadeɛyɛfoɔ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Wode w’adɔeɛ gyaa ɔman a woagye wɔn yi, wode w’ahoɔden kyerɛɛ wɔn kwan kɔɔ wo kronkronyɛ tenabea.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Aman tee, na wɔn ho wosoe, ahopopoɔ kaa wɔn a wɔte Filistia.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Ɛno na Edom asafohempanin ho dwirii wɔn, Moab ahoɔdenfoɔ no, nketenkete kutaa wɔn, Kanaanfoɔ nyinaa hodwoe.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ehu ne suro gu wɔn so, wo basa kɛseyɛ nti wɔayeyɛ komm sɛ ɔboɔ, kɔsi sɛ wo man bɛtwam, O AWURADE, kɔsi sɛ ɔman a wogyee wɔn no bɛtwam.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Wode wɔn bɛba, na woabɛtɛ wɔn w’agyapadeɛ bepɔ no so, AWURADE, faako a wode hɔ ayɛ wo tenabea, kronkronbea a, AWURADE, wo nsa asiesie no.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: AWURADE bɛdi hene de bɛkɔ akɔsi daa daa. Miriam dwom

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Na Farao apɔnkɔ ne ne nteaseɛnam ne n’apɔnkɔfoɔ baa ɛpo no mu, na AWURADE maa ɛpo no sane bɛkataa wɔn so, na Israelfoɔ no nam asase pɛsɛɛ so faa ɛpo no mfimfini.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Na odiyifoɔ baa Miriam a ɔyɛ Aaron nua no faa akasae kurae, na mmaa no nyinaa de akasae ne asa firi dii n’akyi.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Na Miriam gyee wɔn so sɛ: Monto AWURADE dwom, na wadi nkonim animuonyam mu; ɔpɔnkɔ ne ne sotefoɔ no, wato wɔn agu ɛpo mu. Mara nsuo a ɛyɛ nwono

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose maa Israel tu firii Mmɛwa Po ho, na wɔfiri hɔ kɔɔ Sur serɛ so; na wɔnantee ɛserɛ no so nnansa, na wɔnnya nsuo.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Na wɔduruu Mara no, na wɔntumi nnom Mara nsuo, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ nwono. Enti wɔtoo hɔ din Mara.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no kasaa huhuhuhu tiaa Mose sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na yɛnnom?

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Na ɔsu frɛɛ AWURADE, na AWURADE kyerɛɛ no dua bi, na ɔde too nsuo no mu, na nsuo no yɛɛ dɛ. Ɛhɔ na ɔhyɛɛ ahyɛdeɛ ne atemmuo maa wɔn, na ɛhɔ nso na ɔsɔɔ wɔn hwɛeɛ,

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: na Mose kaa sɛ: Sɛ wobɛtie AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nne, na woayɛ deɛ ɛtene wɔ n’anim, na woatie ne mmara nsɛm, na woadi n’ahyɛdeɛ nyinaa so a, ɛnneɛ meremfa yadeɛ a mede meguu Misraim soɔ no biara mengu wo so; na mene AWURADE, wo yaresafoɔ no.

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Na wɔduruu Elim a nsubura dummienu ne akyiresua aduɔson wɔ no. Na wɔkyeree nsraban wɔ nsuo no ho hɔ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Elim, na Israelfoɔ asafo no nyinaa baa Sin serɛ a ɛda Elim ne Sinai ntam no so. Wɔfirii Misraim asase soɔ no, bosome a ɛtɔ so mmienu no da a ɛtɔ so dadu nnanum ne no.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ asafo mu no nyinaa nwiinwii tiaa Mose ne Aaron ɛserɛ so hɔ.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Anka AWURADE mma yɛnwuwu ne nsa ano, Misraim asase a na yɛtete nam nkukuo ho na yɛdidi meeɛ no so! Na moayi yɛn aba ɛserɛ yi so sɛ mode ɛkɔm rebɛkunkum asafo mu yi nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, merebɛma aduane afiri soro atɔ ama mo, na ɔman no mfiri adi da biara nkɔtase deɛ ɛbɛso wɔn ano da koro, na mensɔ wɔn menhwɛ sɛ wɔbɛdi me mmara so anaasɛ wɔrenni so.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so nsia no, wɔresiesie deɛ wɔfa no a, nyɛ deɛ wɔtase daa no mmɔho.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron ka kyerɛɛ Israelfoɔ no nyinaa sɛ: Anwummerɛ na mobɛhunu sɛ AWURADE na ɔyii mo Misraim asase soɔ;

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: na anɔpa na mobɛhunu AWURADE animuonyam, ɛfiri sɛ wate mo anwiinwii a monwiinwii tia AWURADE no; na yɛn deɛ, yɛne hwannom a monwiinwii tia yɛn?

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose se: AWURADE bɛma mo nam adi anwummerɛ, ne aduane adi amee anɔpa, ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE ate mo anwiinwii a monwiinwii tia no no; na yɛn ne hwannom koraa? Ɛnyɛ yɛn na monwiinwii tia, na mmom AWURADE.

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Ka kyerɛ Israelfoɔ asafo no nyinaa sɛ: Montwe mpini AWURADE anim, ɛfiri sɛ wate mo anwiinwii no.

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Na Aaron rekasa akyerɛ Israelfoɔ asafo nyinaa no, wɔdanedanee wɔn ani kyerɛɛ ɛserɛ so, na hwɛ, AWURADE animuonyam yii adi mununkum no mu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mate Israelfoɔ anwiinwii no.

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Anwummerɛ mobɛdi nam, na anɔpa moadi aduane amee, na moahunu sɛ mene AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Na anwummerɛ no, mmoko maa wɔn ho so ba bɛkataa nsraban no so; na anɔpa no, obosuo guu nsraban no ho hyiae.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Na obosuo a ɛguiɛ no gyaeɛ no, na hwɛ, na biribi nkorowankorowa nketenkete gugu ɛserɛ no ani, nketenkete te sɛ fam bosuo nkyenkyeneeɛ.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no hunuiɛ no, wɔsesee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ɛdeɛn nie? Ɛfiri sɛ na wɔnnim adekodeɛ. Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Yei ne aduane a AWURADE de ama mo sɛ monnie no.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ nie: Montase bi sɛdeɛ obiara bɛdie, bɛyɛ olonka mmaako mmaako; sɛdeɛ mo nnipa dodoɔ teɛ na montase. Obiara ntase mma wɔn a wɔwɔ ne ntomadan mu no.

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no yɛɛ saa; na wɔtasee, ebinom deɛ pii, ebinom deɛ kakraa bi.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Obiara nnnya bi mmma adeɛ nnkye so.

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Nanso wɔantie Mose, na ebinom gyaa bi ma adeɛ kyee so; na ɛdɔree mmoaa na ɛbɔnee. Na Mose bo fuu wɔn.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Na wɔtasee anɔpa anɔpa, obiara sɛdeɛ ɔbɛdie; na owia mu yɛ den a, na anane.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so nsia no, wɔtasee aduane no mmɔho, ɔbaako deɛ olonka dummienu. Na asafo no mu mpanimfoɔ nyinaa ba bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Deɛ AWURADE aka nie: Ɔkyena yɛ ɔhome, homeda kronkron a wɔdi ma AWURADE, monto deɛ mowɔ to, na monnoa deɛ mowɔ noa; na deɛ ɛbɛka no, momfa nsie nkɔsi anɔpa.

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Na wɔde sie kɔsii anɔpa, sɛdeɛ Mose hyɛeɛ no; na ammɔn, nso na mmoaa biara nni mu.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Monni no nnɛ, na ɛnnɛ yɛ homeda a wɔdi ma AWURADE; ɛnnɛ morenhunu bi wiram.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nnansia na montase, na ɛda a ɛtɔ so nson no yɛ homeda, ɛda no deɛ, ebi rentɔ.

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛtɔ so nson no, nkurɔfoɔ no mu bi firii adi sɛ wɔrekɔtase, nanso wɔannya bi.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Mobɛpo m’ahyɛdeɛ ne me mmara so die akɔsi da bɛn?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Monhwɛ, sɛ AWURADE ama mo homeda nti na da a ɛtɔ so nsia no ɔma mo nnanu aduane; montenatena mo afie mu; mma obiara mmfiri adi mmfiri ne tenabea da a ɛtɔ so nson no.

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no homee da a ɛtɔ so nson no.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ frɛɛ aduane no “mana”; nso ɛte sɛ wisa aba fitaa, na ne dɛ te sɛ taterɛ a ɛwoɔ wɔ mu.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa sɛ: Asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ nie: Momfa ebi nhyɛ olonka ma mfa nsie awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ a ɛbɛba mo akyire no, na wɔahunu aduane a mede memaa mo diiɛ wɔ ɛserɛ soɔ berɛ a meyii mo Misraim asase soɔ no.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Fa kuruwa bi, na fa mana olonka ma gu mu, fa si AWURADE anim, na wɔmfa nsie mo awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no, Aaron de sii Adanseɛ no anim sɛ wɔde resie.

english_verse: The Israelites ate manna for
translation_verse: Nso olonka yɛ efa du mu baako.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ asafo no nyinaa tu firii Sin serɛ no so, wɔn atutena a wɔdii no AWURADE anomu asɛm soɔ no mu, na wɔbɛkyeree nsraban wɔ Refidim, nso na nsuo a ɔman no bɛnom nni hɔ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Enti ɔman no ne Mose hamee, na wɔse: Ma yɛn nsuo nnom. Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Adɛn nti na mo ne me ham? Adɛn nti na mosɔ AWURADE hwɛ?

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nanso sukɔm dee ɔman no wɔ hɔ; na ɔman no nwiinwii tiaa Mose kaa sɛ: Adɛn nti na woyii yɛn firii Misraim sɛ wode sukɔm rebɛkum yɛn, yɛn mma ne yɛn mmoa yi?

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Na Mose su frɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na mennyɛ memma ɔman yi? Aka kumaa na wɔasi me aboɔ.

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Sene di ɔman no anim, na fa Israel mpanin mu bi ka wo ho, na fa wo poma a wode bɔɔ Asuo Nil mu no kura wo nsam kɔ.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mɛgyina w’anim wɔ Horeb botan no so hɔ, na bɔ ɔbotan no, na nsuo bɛfiri mu aba, na ɔman no anom. Na Mose yɛɛ saa wɔ Israel mpanin no anim.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no ham ne sɔ a wɔsɔɔ AWURADE hwɛɛ sɛ “AWURADE wɔ yɛn mu anaasɛ ɔnni yɛn mu” no nti, ɔfrɛɛ hɔ Masa ne Meriba. Wɔdi Amalek so nkonim

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Na Amalek bae ne Israel bɛkoe wɔ Refidim.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Yi mmarima ma yɛn, na firi adi kɔ, na wo ne Amalek nkɔko. Ɔkyena me deɛ, mɛgyina kokoɔ no atifi, na makura Nyankopɔn poma no wɔ me nsam.

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Na Yosua yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Mose ka kyerɛɛ no no, ne Amalek kɔkoe, na Mose, Aaron ne Hur foroo kokoɔ no kɔɔ atifi.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Mose ma ne nsa so a, Israel di nim, na sɛ ɔgyaa ne nsam a, Amalek di nim.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Na Mose nsa yɛɛ duru, enti wɔfaa ɔboɔ de too n’ase, na ɔtenaa so, na Aaron ne Hur sosɔɔ ne nsa no mu, ɔbaako wɔ ha, na ɔbaako nso wɔ ha, na ne nsa no yɛɛ pintinn kɔsii sɛ owia tɔeɛ.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Na Yosua dwɛree Amalek ne ne man nkrantɛ ano.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Twerɛ yei hyɛ nwoma bi mu fa yɛ nkaeɛ, na ka hyɛ Yosua aso mu sɛ pepa na mɛpepa Amalek nkaeɛ afiri asase so.

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sii afɔrebukyia, na ɔtoo din Yahwe-nissi ,

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: na ɔkaa sɛ: AWURADE aka ntam, AWURADE ne Amalek bɛdi ako firi awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ so de akɔsi awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ so.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Na obi ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Hwɛ, w’ase Yetro, ne wo yere ne ne mma baanu reba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
