translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no tu kɔkyeree nsraban wɔ Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wɔfiri tu kɔkyeree nsraban wɔ Sared subonhwa mu.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wɔfiri tu kɔkyeree nsraban wɔ Asubɔnten Arnon a ɛsene serɛ soɔ a ɛfiri Amori hyeɛ soɔ no agya, ɛfiri sɛ Arnon ne ɛhyeɛ a ɛda Moab ne Amori ntam.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Enti wɔka no AWURADE akodie nwoma no mu sɛ: Wɔnam ahumtuo so ko faa Waheb ne Arnon nsubɔnhwa no,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ne deɛ nsubɔnhwa no sene a ɛdane kɔ Ar tenabea na ɛtwere Moab hyeɛ ho no.

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wɔfiri kɔɔ Beer, asubura a AWURADE kaa ho asɛm kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Boa ɔman no ano na mɛma wɔn nsuo anom, no.

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ɛberɛ no mu na Israel too dwom yi sɛ: Asubura, tue! Monnye no so!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Asubura a atitire tuiɛ na ɔman mu mmapɔmma funufunuiɛ, wɔde ahempoma ne wɔn mpoma. Na wɔfiri serɛ so kɔɔ Matana;

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: na wɔfiri Matana kɔɔ Nahaliel; na wɔfiri Nahaliel kɔɔ Bamot;

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: na wɔfiri Bamot kɔɔ bonhwa a ɛwɔ Moab petee mu, Pisga atifi a ɛkyerɛ anwea pradada soɔ no mu. Wɔdi Sihon ne Og so nkonim

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: na Hesbon ne Amorifoɔ hene Sihon kuro, ɔno na ɔne kane Moabhene koeɛ, na ɔgyee ne nsam n’asase nyinaa kɔsii Arnon ano.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Na Israel somaa abɔfoɔ kɔɔ Amorifoɔ hene Sihon nkyɛn kɔkaa sɛ:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: Ma memfa w’asase so; yɛremmane mfuo mu ne nturo mu, yɛrennom abura mu nsuo bi; ɔhene tempɔn so na yɛbɛnanteɛ akɔsi sɛ yɛbɛtwam w’asase soɔ.

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Na Sihon amma Israel antwam n’asase so; na ɔboaa ne man nyinaa ano firi bɛhyiaa Israel, ɛserɛ so, na ɔbaa Yahas ne Israel bɛkoe.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Na Israel kumm no nkrantɛ ano faa n’asase firi Arnon kɔɔ Yabok so kɔduruu Amonfoɔ ho, ɛfiri sɛ na Amonfoɔ no hyeɛ so hɔ yɛ den.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Na Israel faa nkuro yi nyinaa, na Israel tenaa Amorifoɔ nkuro no nyinaa mu, Hesbon ne ɛho nkuro nyinaa mu;

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ɛno nti na mmebufoɔ no ka sɛ: Mommra Hesbon! Momma wɔnkyekye na wɔnsiesie Sihon kuro no.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Na ogya bi firii Hesbon, ogyaframa firii Sihon kuro kɛseɛ mu; ɛhyee Moab kuro Ar, Arnon sorɔnsorɔmmea so awuranom.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Wo Moab, due! Kemos man, moayera! Wama ne mmammarima adwanedwane, na ne mmammaa adane Amorifoɔ hene Sihon nnommum.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Na yɛabɔ wɔn agu, Hesbon ayera akɔduru Dibon; yɛasɛe wɔn akɔfa Nofa de akɔduru Medeba.

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no tenaa Amorifoɔ asase so.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na Mose somaa maa wɔkɔsraa Yaser, na wɔfaa ne nkuraa, na ɔtuu Amorifoɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Na wɔdanee wɔn ho foro kɔɔ Basan kwan so. Na Basan hene Og firii adi bɛhyiaa wɔn, ɔno ne ne man nyinaa, sɛ wɔrebɛko wɔ Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Nsuro no, na mede no ne ne man nyinaa ne n’asase mahyɛ wo nsa, na woayɛ no sɛdeɛ woyɛɛ Amorifoɔ hene Sihon a ɔtenaa Hesbon no.

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Na wɔkunkum no ne ne mma ne ne man nyinaa a obiara antumi anya kwan anwanne, na wɔfaa asase no dii so.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no tu kɔkyeree nsraban wɔ Moab mpaperɛ so Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko agya.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: Na Moab suroo ɔman no pii, ɛfiri sɛ na wɔdɔɔso, na ehu kaa Moab, Israelfoɔ no nti.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Na Moab ka kyerɛɛ Midian mpanimfoɔ sɛ: Afei ɛdɔm yi bɛdi yɛn ho adeɛ nyinaa, sɛdeɛ nantwie di asase so wira no. Saa berɛ no mu no Sipor ba Balak na na ɔyɛ Moab hene.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa abɔfoɔ kɔɔ Beor ba Bileam nkyɛn wɔ Petor a ɛda asubɔnten no ano, ne manfoɔ asase so, sɛ wɔnkɔhyia no sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔman bi firi Misraim aba, na hwɛ, wɔabɛkata asase ani, na wɔn ara na wɔgu m’anim yi.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Na afei bra bɛdome ɔman no ma me, ɛfiri sɛ wɔyɛ den sene me, sɛ ebia mɛtumi maku wɔn, na mapamo wɔn afiri asase yi so anaa; na menim sɛ deɛ wohyira no no, wɔahyira no, na deɛ wodome no no, wɔadome no.

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Na Moab mpanin ne Midian mpanin no sii mu kɔe, na adebisa akatua no kura wɔn nsam; na wɔkɔɔ Bileam nkyɛn de Balak asɛm no kɔtoo n’anim.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Montena ha anadwo yi, na mede mmuaeɛ bɛbrɛ mo, sɛdeɛ AWURADE bɛkasa akyerɛ me no. Na Moab asafohene no ne Bileam tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Bileam nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Mmarima bɛn na wɔne wo wɔ hɔ yi?

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ: Moabhene Sipor ba Balak na ɔsoma maa wɔbaa me nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɔman a wɔfiri Misraim baeɛ no abɛkata asase ani. Afei bra bɛdome wɔn ma me, sɛ ebia mɛtumi ne wɔn ako na mapam wɔn anaa.

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛne wɔn nnkɔ; nkɔdome ɔman no, na wɔahyira wɔn.

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam sɔree anɔpa, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Balak asafohene no sɛ: Monkɔ mo asase so, na AWURADE ampene amma me kwan sɛ me ne mo nkɔ.

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Na Moab asafohene no sɔre baa Balak nkyɛn bɛkaa sɛ: Bileam ampene sɛ ɔne yɛn bɛba.

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Na Balak sane somaa atitire a wɔdɔɔso na wɔn anim yɛ nyam sene wɔn.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔɔ Bileam nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ Sipor ba Balak seɛ nie: Afei deɛ, mma biribi nnsi wo me nkyɛn ba kwan,

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: na mɛhyɛ wo animuonyam pii, na biribiara a wobɛka akyerɛ me no, mɛyɛ: Enti bra ara na bɛdome ɔman yi ma me.

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Na Bileam buaa see Balak nkoa no sɛ: Sɛ Balak de ne fie a dwetɛ ne sika ahyɛ mu ma, ma me mpo a, merentumi memmu AWURADE me Nyankopɔn asɛm so menkɔyɛ biribi ketewa anaa kɛseɛ.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Na afei mo nso montena ha anadwo yi, na menhunu deɛ AWURADE bɛsane aka akyerɛ me.

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Bileam nkyɛn anadwo bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ hyia na mmarima yi bɛhyiaa woɔ a, sɔre na ɛne wɔn nkɔ; nanso asɛm a mɛka makyerɛ woɔ no nko na di soɔ. N’afunumu gye no nkwa

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Ɛnna Bileam sɔree anɔpa hyehyɛɛ n’afunumu na ɔne Moab atitire no sii mu kɔe.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Na ɔrekorɔ no, Onyankopɔn bo fui, na AWURADE bɔfoɔ bɛgyinaa ɔkwan no so sɛ ɔbɛsi no kwan; nso na ɔte n’afunumu so, na ne nkoa baanu ne no na ɛnam.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Na afunumu no hunuu AWURADE bɔfoɔ no sɛ ɔgyina ɔkwan mu kura nkrantɛ a watwe wɔ ne nsam na afunumu no mane firii kwan no so kɔfaa wiram; na Bileam hwee afunumu no sɛ ɔredane no aba ɔkwan mu.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE bɔfoɔ no kɔgyinaa bobe nturo ntam nammɔnkorɔ kwan mu a ɔfasuo wɔ ha ne ha.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Na afunumu no hunuu AWURADE bɔfoɔ no no, ɔde ne ho miaa ɔfasuo no, na ɔkaa Bileam nan miaa ɔfasuo no ho; na ɔkɔɔ so hwee no ara.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ no twe kɔɔ anim kɔgyinaa deɛ ɛhɔ yɛ hihiaa a ɔkwan nni hɔ a wɔbɛdane akɔ nifa anaa benkum.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Na afunumu no hunuu AWURADE bɔfoɔ no no, ɔbutuu fam, Bileam ase; na Bileam bo fui, na ɔde abaa bɔɔ afunumu no.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE buee afunumu no ano, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na mayɛ woɔ a woabɔ me mprɛnsa yi?

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ afunumu no sɛ: Sɛ woagoro me ho ntira. Sɛ mekura nkrantɛ a, anka sɛsɛɛ maku wo.

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Na afunumu no ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛnyɛ w’afunumu ne me a woatena me so ara de abɛsi nnɛ da yi? Mayɛ wo sei pɛn anaa? Na ɔse: Dabi.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE buee Bileam ani, na ɔhunuu AWURADE bɔfoɔ no sɛ ɔgyina ɔkwan mu kura nkrantɛ a watwe wɔ ne nsam, na ɔkoto de n’anim butuu fam tim.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Adɛn nti na wobɔɔ w’afunumu no mprɛnsa yi? Hwɛ, maba sɛ merebɛsi wo kwan, ɛfiri sɛ wo kwan no ntene wɔ m’anim;

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: na afunumu no hunuu me, na ɔmane firii m’anim mprɛnsa yi; sɛ wammane amfiri m’anim a, anka sɛsɛɛ maku wo dada, na ɔno deɛ, magye no nkwa.

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE bɔfoɔ no sɛ: Mayɛ bɔne na mennim sɛ wo na wogyina ɔkwan mu rehyia me; na afei, sɛ ɛyɛ bɔne w’ani so deɛ a, mɛsane m’akyi.

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfoɔ no ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛne mmarima no nkɔ; na asɛm a mɛka makyerɛ woɔ no nko na ka. Na Bileam ne Balak atitire no sii mu kɔe.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Na Balak tee sɛ Bileam reba no, ɔfiri kɔhyiaa no, Moab kuro a ɛda Arnon a ɛyɛ ɛhyeɛ no soɔ no mu, wɔ nhyenoa hɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛnyɛ soma na mesomaa sɛ wɔmmɛhyia wo mmra? Adɛn nti na woamma me nkyɛn? Wonnye nni sɛ mɛtumi ahyɛ wo animuonyam anaa?

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Hwɛ, afei maba wo nkyɛn. Mɛtumi maka asɛm bi anaa? Asɛm a Onyankopɔn de hyɛ m’anomu no, ɛno na mɛka.

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Na Bileam ne Balak kɔe, na wɔduruu Kiriat-husot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Na Balak de anantwie ne nnwan bɔɔ afɔdeɛ, maa wɔde kɔmaa Bileam atitire a wɔne no wɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na adeɛ kyeeɛ no, Balak faa Bileam, na ɔde no foro kɔɔ Baal sorɔnsorɔmmea so; na ɔfiri hɔ hunuu ɔman no ano.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Sisi afɔrebukyia nson ma me wɔ ha, na pɛ anantwinini nson ne adwennini nson fa brɛ me ha.

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Na Balak yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Bileam ka kyerɛɛ no no; na Balak ne Bileam de nantwinini baako ne odwennini baako bɔɔ hyeɛ afɔdeɛ, afɔrebukyia no biara so.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Kɔgyina wo hyeɛ afɔdeɛ no ho, na menkɔ. Ebia AWURADE bɛhyia me, na ade ko a ɔbɛma mahunu no, mɛka makyerɛ wo. Na ɔsii mu kɔɔ kokoɔ pataa bi so.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɛhyiaa Bileam, na Bileam kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Masisi afɔrebukyia nson, na mede nantwinini ne odwennini mabɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ w’afɔrebukyia biara so.

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de asɛm hyɛɛ Bileam anomu sɛ: Sane kɔ Balak nkyɛn, na sei na kasa.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Na ɔsane kɔɔ ne nkyɛn, na hwɛ, na ɔgyina ne hyeɛ afɔdeɛ no ho, ɔno ne Moab atitire nyinaa.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Na ɔkasaa sɛ: Aram na Balak kɔfaa me firiiɛ, Moabhene no faa me firii apueeɛ mmepɔ mu sɛ: Bra bɛdome Yakob ma me, na bɛbɔ Israel dua.

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mɛdome deɛ Onyankopɔn nnomee no no, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mɛbɔ deɛ AWURADE mmɔɔ no dua no dua?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Abotan atifi na mefiri mehu no, na nkokoɔ so na mefiri megyene no: Hwɛ, ɔman a ne nko bɛtena nie, na wɔremmu wɔn mfra wiase aman.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Hwan na ɔbɛkan Yakob mfuturo ne Israel abupɛn nnan mu baako dodoɔ? Ma menwu ateneneefoɔ wuo, na ma m’awie nyɛ sɛ wɔn deɛ.

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na wode ayɛ me yi? M’atamfoɔ nnome nti na mekɔfaa wo baeɛ, na hwɛ, nhyira na wohyira.

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Na ɔbuaa sɛ: Ɛnyɛ deɛ AWURADE de hyɛ m’anomu no na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ yie na meka? Bileam nkɔmhyɛ a ɛtɔ so mmienu

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛnneɛ bra na yɛnkɔ faako a wobɛhu wɔn; wɔn fa nko na wobɛhunu, na worenhunu wɔn nyinaa; na dome wɔn ma me wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Na ɔde no kɔɔ Sofim serɛ so Pisga bepɔ atifi, na ɔsii afɔrebukyia nson, na ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ wɔ afɔrebukyia no biara so.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Gyina w’afɔrebukyia no ho ara, na me deɛ, merekɔ makɔhwɛ.

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɛhyiaa Bileam, na ɔde asɛm hyɛɛ n’anomu sɛ: Sane kɔ Balak nkyɛn, na sei na kasa.

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa ne nkyɛn, na hwɛ, na ɔgyina ne hyeɛ afɔdeɛ no ho, na Moab atitire no ne no gyinagyina hɔ; na Balak ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na AWURADE kaeɛ?

english_verse: Balaam answered: “Pay close attention to my words—
translation_verse: Na ɔkasaa mmebuo mu sɛ: Sɔre, Balak, na tie; yɛ aso ma me, Sipor ba.

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn nyɛ onipa, na wadi atorɔ, anaa onipa ba, na wanu ne ho. Ɔno deɛ, ɔbɛka asɛm bi na ɔrenyɛ, anaasɛ ɔbɛkasa na ɔremma no ntim?

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Wanhunu amumuyɛ Yakob mu, na wanhunu ɔhaw Israel mu. AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn di n’akyi, na ɔhene ho ahurisie wɔ ne mu.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn ayi wɔn afiri Misraim, n’ahoɔden te sɛ ɛkoɔ deɛ.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Ampa ara, adebisa nni Yakob mu, na nkɔmhyɛ nni Israel mu: Afei na wɔbɛka wɔ Yakob ne Israel ho sɛ: Ɛdeɛn na Onyankopɔn ayɛ yi!

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɔman yi sɔre sɛ gyatabereɛ, na ɔma ne ho so sɛ gyata: Ɔremmutu, gye sɛ wadi bɔnam, na wanom atɔfoɔ mogya ansa.

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Nnome wɔn koraa, na nhyira nso nhyira wɔn koraa.

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Na Bileam bua ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Manka mankyerɛ wo sɛ: Biribiara a AWURADE bɛka no, ɛno na mɛyɛ anaa? Bileam nkɔmhyɛ a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Bra na memfa wo menkɔ baabi foforɔ, ebia ɛbɛsɔ Onyankopɔn ani sɛ wobɛdome wɔn ama me wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na Balak faa Bileam kɔɔ Peor atifi a ɛhwɛ anwea pradada no soɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Sisi afɔrebukyia nson ma me wɔ ha, na fa anantwinini nson ne adwennini nson brɛ me ha.

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Na Balak yɛɛ sɛdeɛ Bileam kaeɛ no, na ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ wɔ afɔrebukyia biara so.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Na Bileam hunuu sɛ asɔ AWURADE ani sɛ ɔhyira Israel no, wankɔ abisa sɛdeɛ ɔkɔɔ kane no, na mmom ɔde n’ani kyerɛɛ ɛserɛ no so.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Na Bileam maa n’ani so, na ɔhunuu Israel sɛ wɔgu hɔ mmusua mmusua; na Nyankopɔn honhom baa ne so,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: na ɔkasae sɛ: Beor ba Bileam asɛm a wanya sɛ ɔreka, ɔbarima a n’ani hunu adeɛ yie no asɛm a wanya,

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: deɛ ɔte Nyankopɔn nsɛm no na ɔreka yi, deɛ ɔhunu Tweaduampɔn anisoadeɛ, na ɔrehwe ase a, wɔte n’ani soɔ no:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Sɛdeɛ wo ntomadan si yɛ fɛ, O Yakob, wo tenabea no, O Israel!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: Ɛyere sɛ asubɔnka, sɛ asuo ho nturo, te sɛ pɛprɛ nnua a AWURADE atɛ, te sɛ nsuo ho ntweneduro.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Na ne mmokiti mu nsuo bu so, na n’asefoɔ tena nsuo pii mu. Ne hene so sene Agag, na wɔbɛma n’ahennie so.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn na ɔyii no firii Misraim, n’ahoɔden te sɛ ɛkoɔ deɛ. Ɔbɛmene amanaman a wɔyɛ n’atamfo, na wadwerɛ wɔn nnompe, na ɔde n’agyan awowɔ wɔn.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Ɔkoto, ɔbutu sɛ gyata ne gyatabereɛ, hwan na ɔbɛma no asɔreɛ? Nhyira ne wɔn a wɔhyira woɔ, na nnome ne wɔn a wɔdome woɔ. Balak gya no kwan

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak bo fuu Bileam, na ɔbɔɔ ne nsam; na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: M’atamfoɔ nnome nti na mehyiaa woɔ, na hwɛ, nhyira na woahyira wɔn mprɛnsa yi.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Na afei dwane kɔ deɛ wofire! Mekaa sɛ anka mɛhyɛ wo animuonyam, na hwɛ, AWURADE asi w’animuonyam ho kwan.

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: Sɛ Balak de ne fie a dwetɛ ne sika ahyɛ mu ma, ma me mpo a, merentumi mentra AWURADE asɛm memfiri m’akomam menkɔyɛ papa anaa bɔne; deɛ AWURADE bɛka no, ɛno na mɛka?

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, merekɔ me man mu: Bra na menkasa menkyerɛ wo deɛ ɔman yi bɛyɛ wo man nna a ɛdi akyire no mu.

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Na ɔkasaa sɛ: Beor ba Bileam asɛm a wanya sɛ ɔreka, ɔbarima a n’ani hunu adeɛ yie no asɛm a wanya,

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: deɛ ɔte Nyankopɔn nsɛm a ɔhunu ɔsorosoroni no ho nimdeɛ no, deɛ ɔhunu Tweaduampɔn anisoadeɛ na ɔrehwe ase a, wɔte n’ani soɔ no:

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Mehu no, nso ɛnyɛ seesei, mehwɛ no, nso ɔmmɛn: Nsoromma bɛpue Yakob mu, na ahempoma bɛfiri Israel mu asɔre, na wadwerɛ Moab afanan nyinaa na wabubu ɔko huuyɛ mma no nyinaa.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛfa Edom adi so, na wafa n’atamfo asase Seir adi so, na Israel bɛyɛ ahoɔdenneɛ ara.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Na obi a ɔfiri Yakob mu bɛdi tumi, na wasɛe wɔn a wɔaka wɔ kuro no mu no.

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Afei ɔhwɛɛ Amalek na ɔtoaa ne kasa no so sɛ: Amanaman mu dikanfo ne Amalek, nanso n’awieeɛ bɛwie no ɔsɛeɛ mu.

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛɛ Kenifoɔ toaa ne kasa no so kaa sɛ: Wo tenabea si hɔ pintinn, na wode wo pirebuo asie ɔbotan mu;

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: nanso wɔbɛsɛe Kain, de akɔsi sɛ Asur bɛfa wo nnommum.

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Na ahyɛn bɛfiri Kitim fam aba, na wɔabɛbrɛ Asur ase abrɛ Eber ase; na ɔno ara nso, awie no ɔsɛeɛ mu.

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Bileam sɔreeɛ, na ɔsii mu sane kɔɔ n’atenaeɛ; na Balak nso kɔɔ ne kwan.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Na Israel tenaa Sitim. Na ɔman no firii aseɛ ne Moab mmabaa bɔɔ adwaman;

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: na wɔhyiahyiaa ɔman no kɔɔ wɔn anyame afɔreduane ho; na ɔman no didii na wɔsɔree wɔn anyame no;

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: na Israel de ne ho bɔɔ Baal-peor ho. Na AWURADE bo fuu Israel;

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa ɔman no mu atitire no nyinaa, na sensɛne wɔn ma AWURADE, owia so, na AWURADE abufuhyeɛ no nsane mfiri Israel so.

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israel atemmufoɔ no sɛ: Monkunkum mo mmarima a wɔde wɔn ho kɔbɔɔ Baal-peor ho no.

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, ɔbarima bi firi Israelfoɔ no mu bae a ɔde Midianni baa bi baa ne nuanom nkyɛn wɔ Mose ani so ne Israelfoɔ asafo no nyinaa ani so; ɛberɛ a wɔn deɛ, na wɔresu ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Na Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron ba Eleasa ba Pinehas hunuiɛ no, ɔsɔre firii asafo no mu kɔfaa pea kurae,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: na ɔdii Israelni no akyi kɔɔ pia no mu, na ɔwowɔɔ wɔn baanu no, Israelni ne ɔbaa no nyinaa hwiree n’ayaase; na ɔhaw no to twa firii Israelfoɔ no so.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron ba Eleasa ba Pinehas asianka m’abufuo afiri Israelfoɔ so, sɛ watwe me ho ninkunu wɔ wɔn mu a enti manhye Israelfoɔ wɔ me ninkuntwe mu.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: na ayɛ ɔno ne n’asefoɔ a wɔbɛba n’akyire no daa asɔfodie apam, ɛfiri sɛ watwe ninkunu ama ne Nyankopɔn, na wapata ama Israelfoɔ.

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Na Israelni a wɔkum no ne Midianni baa no din ne Simri, Salu ba a ɔyɛ Simeonfoɔ mpanimfie mu bapɔmma.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Na Midianni baa a wɔkum no no din de Kosbi, Sur a ɔyɛ Midianfoɔ mu agya fie so panin no ba.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ, wɔn nso a wɔde wɔn aniteɛ teetee mo, na wɔde daadaa mo de kɔsom Baal-peor, ne wɔn nuabaa Kosbi, Midian safohene no babaa a wɔkum no da a Peor ho haw no baeɛ no asɛm no nti.

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Na ɔhaw no akyiri no, AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron ba Eleasa sɛ:

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: Monkan Israelfoɔ asafo no nyinaa dodoɔ mfiri deɛ wadi mfirinhyia aduonu soɔ mfa nkɔ, sɛ wɔn mpanimfie teɛ, Israel mu nnipa a wɔtumi kɔ sa nyinaa.

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yuda mma, sɛdeɛ wɔn mmusua teɛ nie: Sela deɛ, Selafoɔ abusua; Peres deɛ, Peresfoɔ abusua; Sera deɛ, Serafoɔ abusua.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn, Moab mpaperɛ so, Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko sɛ:

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Na Palu mma: Eliab.

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Eliab ba: Nemuel ne Datan ne Abiram. Yeinom ne Datan ne Abiram a wɔfrɛɛ wɔn firii asafo no mu no a wɔne Mose ne Aaron hameeɛ, Kora asafo no mu, wɔn ham a wɔne AWURADE hameeɛ no mu;

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: na asase buee n’anomu menee wɔn ne Kora, na asafo no wuwuiɛ, na ogya hyee mmarima ahanu aduonum no, na wɔbɛyɛɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ no.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Nanso Kora mma deɛ, wɔanwuwu.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Nso na ɔbarima biara mfra yeinom mu a ɔfiri nnipa a Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron kan wɔn berɛ a wɔkan Israelfoɔ wɔ Sinai serɛ soɔ no,

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Na Aaron nso, wɔwoo Nadab ne Abihu, Eleasa ne Itamar maa no;

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: Yeinom na wɔnkyɛ asase no mma wɔn na wɔnni soɔ, sɛdeɛ wɔn din dodoɔ teɛ.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Tonto so na wɔmfa nkyɛ agyapadeɛ mma wɔn a wɔdɔɔso ne wɔn a wɔsua. Lewifoɔ mmusua

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,
translation_verse: Na Lewifoɔ a wɔkan wɔn sɛdeɛ wɔn mmusua teɛ nie: Gerson deɛ, Gersonfoɔ abusua; Kohat deɛ, Kohatfoɔ abusua; Merari deɛ, Merarifoɔ abusua.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Yeinom ne Lewifoɔ mmusua: Libnifoɔ abusua, Hebronfoɔ abusua, Mahlifoɔ abusua, Musifoɔ abusua, Korafoɔ abusua. Na Kohat woo Amram.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Na Amram yere din ne Yokebed, Lewi ba a wɔwoo no Misraim no; na ɔwoo Aaron ne Mose ne wɔn nuabaa Miriam maa Amram.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: nanso Nadab ne Abihu de anana gya bi baa AWURADE anim no, wɔwuwui.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne wɔn a Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa kan wɔn, kan a wɔkan Israelfoɔ Moab mpaperɛ soɔ Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko no mu no.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE aka akyerɛ wɔn sɛ wuo na wɔbɛwuwu serɛ soɔ, na wɔn mu biara anka, gye Yefune ba Kaleb ne Nun ba Yosua nko.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛgyinaa Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ne mmapɔmma no ne asafo mu no nyinaa anim, ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no ano kaa sɛ:

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: Yɛn agya wuu ɛserɛ so, nso ɔno deɛ, na ɔmfra asafo a wɔhyia tiaa AWURADE, Kora asafo no mu, na ɔno ara ne bɔne nti na ɔwuiɛ; nso na ɔnni mmammarima.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na yɛn agya din mpepa mfiri n’abusua mu ɛnam sɛ ɔnni babarima nti? Ma yɛn agyapadeɛ yɛn agya ne nuanom mu.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Na Mose de wɔn asɛm no baa AWURADE anim.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: Selofehad mmammaa asɛm no tene, na ma wɔn agyapadeɛ na wɔnni so wɔn agya nuanom mu, na ma wɔn agya agyapadeɛ no nyɛ wɔn dea.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔnni babaa nso a, ɛnneɛ momfa n’agyapadeɛ mma ne nuammarimanom;

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: na sɛ ɔnni nuabarima nso a, momfa n’agyapadeɛ mma n’agya nuanom.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na sɛ n’agya nni nuanom nso a, momfa n’agyapadeɛ mma ne bogya a ɔbɛn no n’abusua mu na ɔnni so. Na yei nyɛ ahyɛdeɛ ne mmara mma Israelfoɔ, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. Wɔyi Yosua sɛ Israel kannifoɔ (Deuteronomium

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Foro Abarim bepɔ yi na kɔhwɛ asase a mede merema Israelfoɔ no;

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: na sɛ wonya hunu a, wo nso woati wo nananom, sɛdeɛ Aaron tii n’agyanom no,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ moyɛɛ m’asɛm ho asoɔden Sin serɛ so, asafo no ham mu a anka ɛsɛ sɛ moyɛ me kronkron, nsuo no ho wɔ wɔn ani soɔ no.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: Ma AWURADE, honam nyinaa ahonhom Nyankopɔn, mpɛ ɔbarima bi nsi asafo no so

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: a ɔbɛdi wɔn anim afiri adie na ɔbɛdi wɔn anim aba mu, deɛ ɔde wɔn bɛfiri adie na ɔde wɔn aba mu, na AWURADE asafo no anyɛ sɛ nnwan a wɔnni hwɛfoɔ.

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa Nun ba Yosua, ɔbarima a honhom wɔ ne mu no, na fa wo nsa gu ne so.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Na fa no gyina Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ne asafo mu no nyinaa anim, na hyɛ no mmara wɔn anim;

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: na fa w’animuonyam no bi hyɛ no, na Israelfoɔ asafo mu no nyinaa ntie no.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Na ɔnkɔgyina Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa anim, na ɔmmisa urim atemmuo mma no, AWURADE anim; wɔmfa n’asɛm so mfiri adi, na wɔmfa n’asɛm so mmra mu, ɔno ne Israelfoɔ a wɔka ne ho nyinaa, ne asafo mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Na Mose yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na ɔfaa Yosua de no kɔgyinaa Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ne asafo mu no nyinaa anim,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: na ɔde ne nsa guu ne so na ɔhyɛɛ no mmara, sɛdeɛ AWURADE nam Mose so kaeɛ no.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: abupɛn du mu baako nka nnwammaa nson no mu koro biara ho;

english_verse: This sacrifice to please me was first offered at Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Ɛnyɛ daa hyeɛ afɔdeɛ a wɔhyehyɛeɛ wɔ Sinai bepɔ soɔ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam a ɛyɛ AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: na aduane afɔdeɛ esiam abupɛn du mu baako a wɔde ngo afɔre nka odwennini baako ho, ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam a wɔhye ma AWURADE ne no.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: Hyɛ Israelfoɔ no na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: M’ayɛyɛdeɛ, m’aduane a wɔde bɔ ogya afɔdeɛ ma no yi ehwa hwanhwam ma me no, monhwɛ na momfa mmrɛ me ne berɛ a ɛsɛ mu.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Ogya afɔdeɛ a momfa mmrɛ AWURADE nie: Nnwanten mma mmienu a wɔadi afe afe a wɔdi mu na wɔmfa mmɔ da koro hyeɛ afɔdeɛ daa.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Na fa esiam olonka abupɛn du mu baako yɛ aduane afɔdeɛ a wɔde ngodua aba a wɔasie ngo susutoa abupɛn nnan mu baako afɔre.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Na n’ahwiesa susutoa abupɛn nnan mu baako nka adwammaa baako ho. Kronkronbea hɔ na hwie nsa a wɔhwie no ma AWURADE.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Na mo abosome foforɔ mfitiaseɛ nso, momfa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ mmrɛ AWURADE: Anantwinini mmienu ne odwennini baako, nnwanten mma nson a wɔadi afe afe a wɔdi mu;

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: na aduane afɔdeɛ esiam abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa a wɔde ngo afɔre nka nantwinini baako ho, na aduane afɔdeɛ esiam abupɛn du mu mmienu a wɔde ngo afɔre nka odwennini baako ho,

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: Na bosome a ɛdi kan da a ɛtɔ so dunan no yɛ AWURADE Twam.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Na bosome no ara da a ɛtɔ so dunum no yɛ dapɔnna, nnanson na wɔnni apiti paanoo.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Da a ɛdi kan no monhyia nhyia kronkron; monnyɛ adwumaden biara;

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na momfa ogya afɔdeɛ a ɛyɛ ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ mmrɛ AWURADE, anantwinini mmienu ne odwennini baako ne nnwanten mma nson a wɔadi afe afe; monhwɛ sɛ wɔdi mu;

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ, esiam a wɔde ngo afɔre abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa nka nantwinini baako ho, na abupɛn du mu mmienu nka odwennini no ho,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: na abupɛn du mu baako nka nnwammaa nson no mu biara ho;

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Saa ara na nnanson no mu da biara momfa aduane mmɛbɔ ogya afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam ma AWURADE; wɔnyɛ yei mpae daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɛho ahwiesa no so.

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: Na sɛ mo adapɛn afahyɛ duru a, aduanekan da a mode mo aduane foforɔ afɔdeɛ rebrɛ AWURADE no, monhyia nhyia kronkron; monnyɛ adwumaden biara;

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na momfa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ mmra na ɛnyi hwa hwanhwam mma AWURADE: Anantwinini mmienu ne odwennini baako ne nnwanten mma nson a wɔadi afe afe;

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ, esiam a wɔde ngo afɔre abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa nka nantwinini baako biara ho, abupɛn du mu mmienu nka odwennini no ho,

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: ne ɔpapo baako a wɔde bɛpata ama mo;

english_verse: The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: monyɛ yei ne ɛho ahwiesa no nka daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ no ho; monhwɛ sɛ wɔdi mu.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: Na bosome a ɛtɔ so nson no da a ɛdi kan no, monhyia nhyia kronkron; monnyɛ adwumaden biara; ɛnyɛ mo totorobɛntohyɛn da.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ: Esiam a wɔde ngo afɔre abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa nka nantwinini no ho, abupɛn du mu mmienu nka odwennini no ho,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: na abupɛn du mu baako nka nnwammaa nson no mu koro biara ho;

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: ne ɔpapo baako a wɔde bɛbɔ bɔne ho afɔdeɛ de apata ama mo;

english_verse: These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me. The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness (Leviticus
translation_verse: ɛsono bosome foforɔ so hyeɛ afɔdeɛ, ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ, ne daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ, ne ɛho ahwiesa sɛdeɛ ɛteteɛ; na ɛnyɛ AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam. Nnipa asebrɛ da afɔdeɛ

english_verse: The tenth day of the seventh month is the Great Day of Forgiveness. On that day you must rest from all work and come together for worship. Show sorrow for your sins by going without food,
translation_verse: Na bosome a ɛtɔ so nson no ara da a ɛtɔ so du no, monhyia nhyia kronkron, na monni mmuada; monnyɛ adwuma biara;

english_verse: and bring to the altar one young bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na momfa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam mmrɛ AWURADE: Nantwinini baako, odwennini baako, nnwanten mma a wɔadi afe afe nson a wɔdi mu;

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ esiam a wɔde ngo afɔre abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa nka nantwinini no ho, abupɛn du mu mmienu nka odwennini no ho,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: abupɛn du mu baako nka nnwammaa nson no mu koro biara ho;

english_verse: A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices. The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo baako, ɛsono bɔne ho afɔdeɛ ne daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ ne ɛho ahwiesa. Asese afahyɛ afɔdeɛ

english_verse: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
translation_verse: Na bosome a ɛtɔ so nson no da a ɛtɔ so dunum no, monhyia nhyia kronkron; monnyɛ adwumaden biara na monhyɛ fa nnanson mma AWURADE.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ; esiam abupɛn du mu mmiɛnsa a wɔde ngo afɔre nka anantwinini dummiɛnsa no mu koro biara ho, abupɛn du mu mmienu nka adwennini mmienu no ho,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: na abupɛn du mu baako nka nnwammaa dunan no mu koro biara ho;

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo baako; ɛsono daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ, ɛho aduane ne ɛho ahwiesa.

english_verse: On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Ɛda a ɛtɔ so nwɔtwe no, monhyia afahyɛ nhyiamu; monnyɛ adwumaden biara;

english_verse: Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na momfa hyeɛ afɔdeɛ a ɛne ogya afɔdeɛ a ɛyi hwa hwanhwam mmrɛ AWURADE: Nantwinini baako, odwennini baako, nnwanten mma a wɔadi afe afe nson a wɔdi mu;

english_verse: You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal.
translation_verse: nantwinini ne odwennini ne nnwammaa no ho aduane afɔdeɛ ne ahwiesa, wɔn dodoɔ sɛdeɛ ɛteɛ wɔ mmara no mu;

english_verse: And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔdeɛ papo baako; ɛsono daa ɔhyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne ɛho aduane afɔdeɛ ne ɛho ahwiesa.

english_verse: You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
translation_verse: Yeinom na monyɛ mma AWURADE, mo afa a mohyɛ no mu; ɛsono mo bɔhyɛ adeɛ ne mo ayamyi afɔdeɛ, mo hyeɛ afɔdeɛ ne mo aduane afɔdeɛ ne mo ahwiesa ne mo asomdwoeɛ afɔdeɛ.

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord had told him about the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfoɔ no sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
translation_verse: Na Mose kasa kyerɛɛ Israelfoɔ mmusuakuo no so atitire sɛ: Yei ne asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ:

english_verse: When one of you men makes a promise to the Lord, you must keep your word.
translation_verse: Sɛ obi hyɛ AWURADE bɔ anaasɛ ɔka ntam tua ne kra adeɛ bi a, ɔmmmu n’asɛm so; deɛ ɛfiri n’anomu nyinaa, ɔnyɛ.

english_verse: Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔbaa bi hyɛ AWURADE bɔ de tua ne ho biribi berɛ a ɔda so wɔ n’agya fie, ne mmabaaberɛ mu,

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: Na sɛ da a n’agya teɛ no wampene a, ɛnneɛ ne bɔhyɛ nyinaa ne n’ahotua a ɔde tuaa ne kra biribie no rennyina hɔ. Na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no, ɛfiri sɛ n’agya ampene.

english_verse: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
translation_verse: na ne kunu te, na da a ɔteɛ no ɔyɛ komm a, ɛnneɛ ne bɔhyɛ no gyina hɔ, na tua a ɔde atua ne kra biribie no gyina hɔ.

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: Na sɛ da a ne kunu teɛ no, wampene a, na wasane ne bɔhyɛ a ɛda ne soɔ ne deɛ ɛfirii n’anomu a ɔde tuaa ne kra biribie no, na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no.

english_verse: Widows and divorced women must keep every promise they make to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa kunafoɔ anaa deɛ wɔako no bɔhyɛ deɛ, adeɛ biara a ɔtua ne kra no da ne so.

english_verse: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ne kunu fie na ɔhyɛ bɔ anaasɛ ɔde ntam tua ne kra biribi,

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
translation_verse: na ne kunu te, na ɔyɛ komm, na wammara no a, ne bɔhyɛ no nyinaa gyina hɔ, na adeɛ biara a watua ne kra no gyina hɔ.

english_verse: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ ne kunu sane no da a ɔteeɛ no a, ɛnneɛ adeɛ biara a afiri n’anomu a ɔde hyɛɛ bɔ anaasɛ ɔde tuaa ne kra biribie no rennyina hɔ; ne kunu asane, na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no.

english_verse: Her husband has the final say about any promises she makes to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɔhyɛ nyinaa ne ahotua ntam a wɔde brɛ ɔkra ase nyinaa, ne kunu na ɔmma no nnyina hɔ na ne kunu na ɔnsane;

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
translation_verse: na sɛ daa ne kunu no nnka ho hwee a, ɛnneɛ ɔhyɛ ne bɔhyɛ no nyinaa anaa n’ahotua no nyinaa mu den, ɛfiri sɛ da a ɔteeɛ no, wanka ho hwee;

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
translation_verse: na sɛ ɔteeɛ no akyi ansa na ɔresane a, ɛnneɛ ɔsoa ne yere amumuyɛ.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne ahyɛdeɛ a AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɛnna ɔbarima ne ne yere ntam, ɛne agya ne ne babaa a ɔwɔ ne mmabaaberɛ mu, n’agya fie, ntam.

english_verse: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
translation_verse: Tɔ Midianfoɔ so were ma Israelfoɔ, na ɛno akyiri no woati wo mpanimfoɔ wɔ asamando.

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
translation_verse: Na Mose kasa kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Momma mo mu mmarima mmia ntu Midian so sa, na wɔmfa AWURADE aweretɔ mmra Midianfoɔ so.

english_verse: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
translation_verse: Na wɔyiyii Israel mpempem ahodoɔ mu nnipa mpem dummienu a wɔamia rekɔ ɔsa, abusuakuo biara mu apem;

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: na Mose somaa wɔn maa wɔkɔɔ ɔsa no, abusuakuo biara mu apem, wɔne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ba Pinehas a na kronkronbea hɔ nnoɔma no ne osebɔ ntotorobɛnto no wɔ ne nsam no.

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Na wɔne Midian kɔkoe, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no, na wɔkunkum mmarima nyinaa;

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no faa Midian mmaa ne mmɔfra nnommum, na wɔfom wɔn anantwie ne wɔn nnwan ne wɔn ahodeɛ nyinaa;

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: na wɔtotoo wɔn tenabea nkuro ne wɔn nsraban nyinaa mu gya.

english_verse: Israel's soldiers gathered together everything they had taken from the Midianites, including the captives and the animals.
translation_verse: Na wɔde asadeɛ no nyinaa ne nnipa ne mmoa a wɔfaeɛ no nyinaa

english_verse: Then they returned to their own camp in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, where Moses, Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders met the troops outside camp.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ne asafo no mmapɔmma nyinaa firi nsraban no mu firii adi kɔhyiaa wɔn.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moagye mmaa no nyinaa nkwa anaa?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Enti monkunkum mmɔfra no mu mmarima nyinaa, na mmaa no mu biara a ɔnim ɔbarima na ɔne ɔbarima ada no nso, monku no;

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: na mmɔfra no mu mmaa a wɔnhunuu mmarima nna no deɛ monnye wɔn nkwa na momfa wɔn.

english_verse: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
translation_verse: Na mo ara nso, mommɔ nsraban ntena mu nsraban no akyi nnanson; mo mu biara a wakum obie ne obiara a waka ɔtɔfoɔ no, monnwira mo ho da a ɛtɔ so mmiɛnsa ne da a ɛtɔ so nson no, mo ne mo nnommum no.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Na atadeɛ biara ne nwoma adeɛ biara ne adeɛ a wɔde abirekyie nwi ayɛ nyinaa ne dua adeɛ biara, monnwira ho.

english_verse: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire. After you take it out, sprinkle it with the water that purifies. Everything else should only be sprinkled with the water. Do all of this, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
translation_verse: adeɛ biara a ɛkɔ ogya mu no, momma no mfa ogya mu na ɛho nte, nanso momfa ahodwira nsuo nnwira ho. Na adeɛ biara a ɛnkɔ ogya mu no, momma no mfa nsuo mu.

english_verse: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and after that, you will be clean and may return to the camp.” Everything Taken from the Midianites Is Divided
translation_verse: Na monsi mo ntadeɛ da a ɛtɔ so nson no, na mo ho nte, na ɛno akyi ansa na mommra nsraban no mu. Asadeɛ mu kyekyɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
translation_verse: firi wɔn fa a wɔnyaeɛ no mu, na fa ma Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa sɛ AWURADE mmasoɔ adeɛ.

english_verse: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
translation_verse: enti na yɛde AWURADE ayɛyɛdeɛ reba yi, obiara a ɔnyaa sika nnwinneɛ, basa so nkapo, bakɔn so nkapo, nsɔanonkaa, nsomuadeɛ ne kɔmuadeɛ, sɛ wɔmfa mpata mma yɛn kra, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa yɛɛ sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.

english_verse: women and gave them to Eleazar to be dedicated to the Lord. Then from the half that belonged to the people, Moses set aside one out of every
translation_verse: Nso asadeɛ a ɛyɛ asadeɛ a ɛdɔm no faeɛ no nkaeɛ yɛ nnwan apem ahansia ne mpem aduɔson nnum.

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: ne akra mmabunu a wɔyɛ mpem aduasa mmienu a wɔnhunuu mmarima da.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo nkoa abu akofoɔ a wɔwɔ yɛn nsam no ano, na wɔn mu biara anyera;

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa gyee wɔn hɔ sika no, nnwinneɛ no nyinaa;

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Deɛ akofoɔ no fom kaa ho no, wɔn ara fae.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa gyee sika no, apem apem ne ɔha ɔha so asafohene no nsam, na wɔde baa ahyiaeɛ ntomadan no mu sɛ ɛnyɛ Israelfoɔ no nkaeɛ adeɛ, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: except Caleb and Joshua. They remained faithful to the Lord,
translation_verse: Gye Kenisini Yefune ba Kaleb ne Nun ba Yosua, ɛfiri sɛ wɔn na wɔadi AWURADE akyiri nokorɛ mu.

english_verse: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
translation_verse: na wɔabrɛ asase no ase AWURADE anim ansa na moasane a, ɛnneɛ na moayɛ mo asɛdeɛ AWURADE ne Israel ho, na asase yi nyɛ mo agyapadeɛ, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
translation_verse: Na Ruben mma ne Gad mma no wɔ mmoa pii a wɔdɔɔso pa ara, na wɔhunuu Yaser ne Gilead asase, na hwɛ, na ɛhɔ yɛ baabi a ɛyɛ ma mmoa.

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: Na Gad mma ne Ruben mma no ba bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Ɔsɔfoɔ Eleasa ne asafo no mu mmapɔmma no sɛ:

english_verse: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
translation_verse: asase a AWURADE abrɛ no aseɛ Israel asafo anim no, yɛ asase a ɛyɛ ma mmoa; na yɛn wo nkoa wɔ mmoa.

english_verse: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
translation_verse: Na wɔkaa sɛ: Sɛ yɛn anim aba nyam wɔ w’anim a, ma wɔmfa asase yi mma wo nkoa na yɛnni so, na mfa yɛn ntwa Yordan.

english_verse: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Gad mma ne Ruben mma no sɛ: Mo nuanom nkɔko, na mo deɛ, montena ha?

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Na adɛn na motu Israelfoɔ akoma sɛdeɛ wɔrentwa nkɔ asase a AWURADE de ama wɔn no soɔ?

english_verse: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
translation_verse: Saa na mo nananom yɛeɛ berɛ a mesomaa wɔn firi Kades-barnea sɛ wɔnkɔhwɛ asase no,

english_verse: They went as far as Eshcol Valley, then returned and told the people that we should not enter it.
translation_verse: na wɔforo kɔduruu Eskol subonhwa no mu, na wɔhunuu asase no, wɔbɛtuu Israelfoɔ no akoma, na wɔankɔ asase a AWURADE de ama wɔn no so;

english_verse: The Lord became very angry.
translation_verse: na AWURADE bo fui da no, na ɔkaa ntam sɛ:

english_verse: Moses said: You promised that you would be ready to fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ mobɛyɛ yei na moamia wɔ AWURADE anim akɔko,

english_verse: but he was so angry with the others that he forced them to wander around in the desert for
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bo fuu Israel, na ɔmaa wɔkyinkyinii ɛserɛ so mfirinhyia aduanan kɔsii sɛ awoɔ ntoatoasoɔ a wɔyɛɛ AWURADE anim bɔne no nyinaa wiee sa.

english_verse: So Moses gave the Machirites the region of Gilead, and they settled there.
translation_verse: Na Mose de Gilead maa Manase ba Makir, na ɔtenaa mu.

english_verse: Now you people of Reuben and Gad are doing the same thing and making the Lord even angrier.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, moasɔre asi mo nananom ananmu, mmarima nnebɔneyɛfoɔ asefoɔ, sɛ mode AWURADE abufuhyeɛ no bi reka ho de aba Israel so ara.

english_verse: If you reject the Lord, he will once again abandon his people and leave them here in the desert. And you will be to blame!
translation_verse: Sɛ mosane firi AWURADE akyi a, ɔbɛgya wɔn hɔ bio, ɛserɛ so, na moasɛe ɔman mu yi nyinaa.

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad replied: Let us build places to keep our sheep and goats, and towns for our wives and children,
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔtwe pinii no kaa sɛ: Yɛbɛgyegye nnwammuo wɔ ha ama yɛn mmoa, na yɛakyekyere nkuro nso ama yɛn mma;

english_verse: where they can stay and be safe. Then we'll prepare to fight and lead the other tribes into battle.
translation_verse: na yɛn deɛ, yɛamia asɔ akodeɛ mu adi Israelfoɔ anim akɔsi sɛ yɛde wɔn bɛduru wɔn tenabea ansa; na yɛn mma ntenatena nkuro a ɛyɛ den no mu, asase no sotefoɔ no nti.

english_verse: We will stay with them until they have settled in their own tribal lands.
translation_verse: Yɛrensane mma yɛn afie de bɛkɔ akɔsi sɛ Israelfoɔ no nyinaa bɛnya wɔn agyapadeɛ mmaako mmaako adi soɔ.

english_verse: The land on this side of the Jordan River will be ours, so we won't expect to receive any on the other side.
translation_verse: Na yɛne wɔn remfa agyapadeɛ wɔ Yordan agya ne akyire, ɛfiri sɛ yɛn agyapadeɛ abɛfiri Yordan agya ha wɔ apueeɛ fam ama yɛn.

english_verse: You also agreed to cross the Jordan and stay with the rest of the Israelites, until the Lord forces our enemies out of the land. If you do these things,
translation_verse: na mo mu wɔn a wɔamia nyinaa bɛtwa Yordan adi AWURADE anim akɔsi sɛ ɔbɛpamo n’atamfo afiri n’anim,

english_verse: But if you don't keep your promise, you will sin against the Lord and be punished.
translation_verse: Na sɛ moanyɛ saa a, hwɛ, na moayɛ AWURADE bɔne, na monhunu yie sɛ, mo bɔne bɛyi mo ama.

english_verse: Go ahead and build towns for your wives and children, and places for your sheep and goats. Just be sure to do what you have promised.
translation_verse: Monkyekyere nkuro mma mo mma na monnyegye ban mma mo nnwan, na deɛ afiri mo anomu no, monyɛ.

english_verse: The men from Reuben and Gad answered: Sir, we will do just what you have said.
translation_verse: Na Gad mma ne Ruben mma no ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Wo nkoa bɛyɛ sɛdeɛ me wura ahyɛ no.

english_verse: Our wives and children and sheep and cattle will stay here in the towns in Gilead.
translation_verse: Yɛn mma ne yɛn yerenom ne yɛn nnwan ne yɛn anantwie nyinaa ntena Gilead nkuro mu hɔ;

english_verse: But those of us who are prepared for battle will cross the Jordan and fight for the Lord.
translation_verse: na wo nkoa mu wɔn a wɔamia rekɔ ɔsa nyinaa bɛtwam adi AWURADE anim akɔko, sɛdeɛ me wura kaeɛ no.

english_verse: “Make sure that the tribes of Gad and Reuben prepare for battle and cross the Jordan River with you. If they do, then after the land is in your control, give them the region of Gilead as their tribal land.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ Gad mma ne Ruben mma ne mo twa Yordan, wɔn a wɔamia di AWURADE anim rekɔ ɔsa nyinaa, na wɔnya brɛ asase no ase mo anim a, ɛnneɛ momfa Gilead asase mma wɔn na wɔnni so;

english_verse: But if they break their promise, they will receive land on the other side of the Jordan, like the rest of the tribes.”
translation_verse: na sɛ wɔammia ne mo antwa a, ɛnneɛ Kanaan asase so na wɔmma wɔnnya tenabea wɔ mo mu.

english_verse: The tribes of Gad and Reuben replied, “We are your servants and will do whatever the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Na Gad mma ne Ruben mma buaa sɛ: Deɛ AWURADE aka akyerɛ wo nkoa no, saa ara na yɛbɛyɛ:

english_verse: We will cross the Jordan River, ready to fight for the Lord in Canaan. But the land we will inherit as our own will be on this side of the river.”
translation_verse: Yɛn deɛ, yɛbɛmia adi AWURADE anim atwam akɔ Kanaan asase so, na yɛn agyapadeɛ a yɛanya Yordan agya ha no atena yɛn hɔ.

english_verse: So Moses gave the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh the territory and towns that King Sihon the Amorite had ruled, as well as the territory and towns that King Og of Bashan had ruled.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Mose de Amorifoɔ hene Sihon ahennie ne Basan hene Og ahennie, asase no ne n’ahyeɛ mu nkuro, asase no so nkuro a atwa ahyia nyinaa maa Gad mma ne Ruben mma ne Yosef ba Manase abusuakuo fa.

english_verse: The tribe of Gad rebuilt the towns of Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
translation_verse: Na Gad mma no kyekyeree Dibon ne Atarot ne Aroer,

english_verse: Atroth-Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
translation_verse: ne Atrot-sofan ne Yaser ne Yogbeha,

english_verse: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran. They built walls around them and also built places to keep their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ne Bet-nimra ne Bet-haran, nkuro a wɔatoto ho afasuo ne nnwammuo.

english_verse: The tribe of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
translation_verse: Na Ruben mma no kyekyeree Hesbon, Eleale, Kiriataim,

english_verse: Sibmah, as well as the towns that used to be known as Nebo and Baal-Meon. They renamed all those places.
translation_verse: Nebo ne Baal-meon ne Sibma, na wɔtotoo nkuro a wɔkyekyereeɛ no din.

english_verse: The clan of Machir from the tribe of East Manasseh went to the region of Gilead, captured its towns, and forced out the Amorites.
translation_verse: Na Manase ba Makir mma sii mu kɔɔ Gilead kɔfae, na wɔpamm Amorifoɔ a wɔwɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: Jair from the Manasseh tribe captured villages and renamed them “Villages of Jair.”
translation_verse: Na Manase ba Yair sii mu kɔfaa wɔn atenaeɛ no, na ɔfrɛɛ no Yair atenaeɛ.

english_verse: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
translation_verse: Na Noba sii mu kɔfaa Kenat ne ɛho nkurowa, na ɔde ne din Noba toe.

english_verse: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
translation_verse: Mose twerɛɛ faako a wɔtu firiiɛ ne akwan a wɔtwaeɛ, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na yeinom ne wɔn akwantuo mu asoɛeɛ firi faako a wɔtutu firiiɛ no:

english_verse: After the Israelites left Rameses, they camped at Succoth,
translation_verse: Na Israelfoɔ no tu firii Rameses kɔkyeree nsraban Sukot.

english_verse: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Sukot kɔkyeree nsraban Etam a ɛwɔ nsɛnoa.

english_verse: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Etam dane baa Pi-hahirot a ɛwɔ Baal-sefon anim, na wɔkyeree nsraban Migdol anim.

english_verse: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Hahirot anim kɔtwaa ɛpo no kɔɔ ɛserɛ so, na wɔnantee Etam serɛ so nnansa kwan kɔkyeree nsraban Mara.

english_verse: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Elim kɔkyeree nsraban Mmɛwa Po ano.

english_verse: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Mmɛwa Po ano kɔkyeree nsraban Sin serɛ so.

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Alus kɔkyeree nsraban Refidim; na ɛhɔ na ɔman no annya nsuo annom.

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Refidim kɔkyeree nsraban Sinai serɛ so.

english_verse: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Kades kɔkyeree nsraban Hor bepɔ ho, Edom asase ano.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Na Ɔsɔfoɔ Aaron foro kɔɔ Hor bepɔ so, sɛdeɛ AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, kɔwuu wɔ hɔ, Israelfoɔ Misraim asase so fire afe a ɛtɔ so aduanan soɔ, bosome a ɛtɔ so nnum no da a ɛdi kan.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Na Kanaanni, Arad hene a ɔte Negeb no tee sɛ Israelfoɔ no reba.

english_verse: and finally in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Na wɔtu firii Abarim mmepɔ so kɔkyeree nsraban Moab mpaperɛ so, Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko no.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Na wɔkyeree Yordan ho nsraban firi Bet-yesimot kɔsii Abel-sitim, Moab mpaperɛ so. Wɔnsɛe Kanaanfoɔ

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose Moab mpaperɛ so, Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko no sɛ:

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: Kasa kyerɛ Israelfoɔ no sɛ: Sɛ motwa Yordan kɔ Kanaan asase so a,

english_verse: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ mompamo asase no sotefoɔ nyinaa mfiri mo anim, na monsɛe wɔn aboɔ ahoni nyinaa, na wɔn ahoni a wɔaguo no, monsɛe ne nyinaa, na monsɛe wɔn nsorɔnsorɔmmea nyinaa.

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Na momfa asase no ntena so, na mo na mede asase no mama mo sɛ monni soɔ.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Na momfa tontobɔ so nkyɛ asase no mu mma mo mmusuakuo no: Abusuakuo a ɛso no, momma ne kyɛfa nso, na deɛ ɛsua no, momma ne kyɛfa nsua; deɛ obiara tonto bɛbɔ no, ɛhɔ na ɛnyɛ ne deɛ; monnyegye mo kyɛfa sɛdeɛ mo nananom mmusuakuo teɛ.

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Na sɛ moampamo asase no sotefoɔ amfiri mo anim a, ɛnneɛ wɔn mu wɔn a mobɛgya wɔn no bɛdane mo aniwa mu nkasɛɛ ne mo mfe mu nnunsini, na wɔateetee mo, asase a mote soɔ no so.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Na sɛdeɛ mesusuu sɛ mɛyɛ wɔn no, saa ara na mɛyɛ mo.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
translation_verse: Hyɛ Israelfoɔ no mmara na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ moduru Kanaan asase no so a, .
