translation_verse: Enti montwitwa mo akoma twetia, na monnsene mo kɔn bio.

english_verse: The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn yɛ anyame mu Nyankopɔn, ne Awurade mu Awurade, Onyankopɔn kɛseɛ no, Otumfoɔ a ne ho yɛ hu a ɔnhwɛ nnipa anim na ɔnnye adanmudeɛ;

english_verse: The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing.
translation_verse: ɔbu atɛn ma awisiaa ne okunafoɔ, na ɔdɔ ɔhɔhoɔ ma no aduane ne nkataho.

english_verse: And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: Enti monnɔ ahɔhoɔ, ɛfiri sɛ moyɛɛ ahɔhoɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
translation_verse: Ɔno ne w’ayeyie, na ɔne wo Nyankopɔn a wayɛ nnoɔma akɛseɛ a ɛyɛ hu a w’ani ahunu yi ama woɔ.

english_verse: The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Enti dɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, na hwɛ n’ahwɛdeɛ, n’ahyɛdeɛ ne n’atemmudeɛ ne ne mmara nsɛm nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power
translation_verse: Na monhunu nnɛ, monhunu AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn ntea, ne kɛseyɛ, ne nsa a ɛyɛ den ne ne basa a watene mu

english_verse: when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people.
translation_verse: ne ne nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ ne ne nneyɛɛ a ɔyɛɛ no Misraim a ɔde yɛɛ Misraimhene Farao ne n’asase nyinaa,

english_verse: And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
translation_verse: ne deɛ ɔyɛɛ Misraim dɔm ne n’apɔnkɔ ne ne nteaseɛnam a wɔde reti mo a ɔmaa Mmɛwa Po mu nsuo bu faa wɔn soɔ, na AWURADE sɛee wɔn, de abɛduru nnɛ da yi,

english_verse: You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here.
translation_verse: ne deɛ ɔyɛɛ mo ɛserɛ so bɛsii sɛ moduruu ha yi,

english_verse: And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
translation_verse: ne deɛ ɔyɛɛ Ruben ba Eliab mma Datan ne Abiram a asase buee n’anomu menee wɔn ne wɔn afie ne wɔn ntomadan ne wɔn a wɔdii wɔn akyire nyinaa firii Israel nyinaa mfimfini no;

english_verse: With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
translation_verse: na mo ani ahunu AWURADE nneyɛɛ akɛseɛ a ɔyɛeɛ no nyinaa.

english_verse: Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land
translation_verse: Enti monni mmara nsɛm a merehyɛ mo nnɛ yi nyinaa so, na mo ho ayɛ den, na moakɔ akɔfa asase a moretwam akɔ so akɔfa no,

english_verse: that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time.
translation_verse: na mo nna aware asase a AWURADE kaa mo nananom ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wɔn ne wɔn asefoɔ no so, asase a nufosuo ne ɛwoɔ sene wɔ soɔ.

english_verse: It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops.
translation_verse: Na asase a worekɔ akɔfa no nte sɛ Misraim asase a mofiri so baeɛ a woguu w’aba na wode wo nan guguu so nsuo sɛ ɛfan turo mu no;

english_verse: But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven,
translation_verse: na asase a moretwam akɔ so akɔfa no yɛ mmepɔ ne mmonhwa asase a ɛnom ɔsoro nsuo,

english_verse: because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
translation_verse: asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn hwɛ so daa, a n’ani wɔ so firi afe mfitiaseɛ kɔsi afe awieeɛ.

english_verse: The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him,
translation_verse: Na sɛ motie me mmara nsɛm a mede merema mo nnɛ yi, sɛ mode mo akoma nyinaa bɛdɔ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn na moasom no a,

english_verse: But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods,
translation_verse: Monhwɛ mo ho yie na wɔannaadaa mo akoma, na moammane ankɔsom anyame foforɔ ansɔre wɔn,

english_verse: the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
translation_verse: na AWURADE abufuo annɛre antia mo, na wanto ɔsoro mu sɛ osuo nntɔ na asase mmma ne nnɔbaeɛ, na moansɛe ntɛm so amfiri asase pa a AWURADE de rema mo no so.

english_verse: Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them.
translation_verse: Enti momfa me nsɛm yi nsie mo akoma ne mo kra mu, na fa yɛ nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ kyekyere wo nsa, na ɛnyɛ w’aniwa ntam nkaeɛ abotire;

english_verse: Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
translation_verse: na momfa nkyerɛkyerɛ mo mma, na kasa ho w’afitena mu ne wo kwan so nanteɛ mu ne wo nna mu ne wo sɔreɛ mu;

english_verse: Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
translation_verse: na twerɛ gu wo fie aponnwa ho ne w’aponkɛseɛ so;

english_verse: Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
translation_verse: na wo nna ne wo mma nna adɔɔso asase a AWURADE kaa wo nananom ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wɔn no so, sɛdeɛ ɔsoro a ɛkata asase soɔ yi nna teɛ.

english_verse: Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants,
translation_verse: Na sɛ mobɛdi mmara nsɛm a merehyɛ mo yi so ayɛ, na moadɔ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn anante n’akwan nyinaa so na moabata ne ho a,

english_verse: he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ AWURADE bɛtutu amanaman yi nyinaa afiri mo anim, na moafa amanaman akɛseɛ a wɔyɛ den sene mo.

english_verse: You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Baabiara a mo nan bɛtia no bɛyɛ mo deɛ, ɛfiri ɛserɛ so ne Lebanon, ɛfiri Asubɔntene Eufrate ho, kɔsi akyiri po no ano bɛyɛ mo asase.

english_verse: No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Obiara rentumi nnyina mo anim; AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn de mo ho hu ne mo ho suro bɛgu asase a mobɛfa soɔ nyinaa so, sɛdeɛ ɔka kyerɛɛ mo no. Nhyira ne nnome

english_verse: Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you.
translation_verse: Sɛ motie AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn mmara nsɛm a merehyɛ mo nnɛ yi a, mobɛnya nhyira,

english_verse: But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
translation_verse: na sɛ moantie AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn mmara nsɛm na momane firi ɔkwan a merehyɛ mo nnɛ yi so kɔdi anyame foforɔ a monni wɔn akyiri a, mobɛnya nnome.

english_verse: After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de wo duru asase a worekɔ akɔfa no so a, ka nhyira no Gerisim bepɔ so ne nnome no nso Ebal bepɔ so.

english_verse: Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there,
translation_verse: Na morebɛtwa Yordan akɔ akɔfa asase a AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn de rema mo no, na mobɛfa atena so.

english_verse: be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_verse: Enti monhwɛ yie na monyɛ ahyɛdeɛ ne atemmudeɛ a mede meresi mo anim nnɛ yi nyinaa.

english_verse: Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land.
translation_verse: Yeinom ne ahyɛdeɛ ne atemmudeɛ a monhwɛ nyɛ no asase a AWURADE wo nananom Nyankopɔn de rema wo sɛ fa no soɔ, nna a mode te asase soɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Sɛeɛ na monsɛe ɔsombea a amanaman a morekɔtu wɔn no som wɔn anyame, mmepɔ atentene so ne nkokoɔ so ne dua mono biara ase no nyinaa;

english_verse: Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there.
translation_verse: na monnwiri wɔn afɔrebukyia, na mommubu wɔn aboɔ adum, na momfa ogya nhye wɔn abosompɔ, na mommobɔ wɔn anyame ahoni, na monsɛe wɔn din mfiri hɔ. Faako a wɔnsom Onyankopɔn

english_verse: The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat. But the Lord will give you cattle, sheep, and goats, and you can butcher any of those animals at home and eat as much as you want.
translation_verse: Sɛ faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛyi de ne din ato hɔ no ne wo ntam ware a, ɛnneɛ kum w’anantwie ne wo nnwan a AWURADE de ama woɔ no bi, sɛdeɛ mehyɛɛ woɔ no, na di no wo kuro mu, sɛdeɛ wo kra kɔn dɔ;

english_verse: It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
translation_verse: sɛdeɛ wɔdi ɔwansane ne ɔforoteɛ no, saa ara nso na die; obi a ne ho nteɛ ne deɛ ne ho teɛ nyinaa nni.

english_verse: Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
translation_verse: nni, na ɛnsi wo ne wo mma a wɔdi w’akyire yie, sɛ woreyɛ deɛ ɛtene AWURADE ani soɔ.

english_verse: If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful. Worship the Lord in the Right Way Moses said:
translation_verse: Hwɛ na tie nsɛm a merehyɛ woɔ nyinaa na ɛnsi wo ne wo mma a wɔdi w’akyire yie daa, sɛ woreyɛ deɛ ɛyɛ na ɛtene AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ani so. Wɔnnni ahoni akyi

english_verse: Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn twitwa amanaman a worekɔ hɔ akɔtu wɔn no firi w’anim, na wotu wɔn tena wɔn asase so a,

english_verse: But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?”
translation_verse: hwɛ wo ho yie na sɛeɛ a wɔasɛe wɔn afiri w’anim no akyiri no wɔn akyiridie anyɛ wo fidie, na woammisa wɔn anyame akyiri kwan sɛ: Amanaman yi som wɔn anyame sɛn? Na me nso menyɛ saa.

english_verse: No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nyɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn saa, na n’akyiwadeɛ a ɔtane nyinaa na wɔayɛ ama wɔn anyame, na wɔn mmammarima ne wɔn mmammaa mpo, wɔde ogya hye wɔn ma wɔn anyame.

english_verse: Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
translation_verse: Asɛm a merehyɛ mo nyinaa, monhwɛ nni so; mfa bi nka ho na nyi bi nso mfiri mu.

english_verse: Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.”
translation_verse: na nsɛnkyerɛnneɛ anaa anwanwadeɛ a ɔka kyerɛɛ woɔ no ba mu na ɔka sɛ: Ma yɛnkɔ nkɔdi anyame foforɔ a wonni wɔn akyi nkɔsom wɔn a,

english_verse: If the prophet says this, don't listen! The Lord your God will be watching to find out whether or not you love him with all your heart and soul.
translation_verse: ntie odiyifoɔ anaa ɔdaeɛsofoɔ no nsɛm no. Ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn resɔ mo ahwɛ na wahunu sɛ mode mo akoma nyinaa ne mo kra nyinaa bɛdɔ no anaa.

english_verse: You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling,
translation_verse: AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn akyi na monnie, na ɔno na monsuro no, na ne mmara nsɛm so na monnie, na ne nne na montie, na monsom no, na mommata ne ho.

english_verse: because he rescued you from slavery in Egypt. If a prophet tells you to disobey the Lord your God and to stop worshiping him, then that prophet is evil and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Na odiyifoɔ anaa ɔdaeɛsofoɔ no, monku no, ɛfiri sɛ wakasa sɛ mommane mfiri AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn a ɔyii mo firii Misraim asase soɔ na ɔgyee mo firii nkoafie no ho de retwetwe wo afiri ɔkwan a wahyɛ wo sɛ nante mu no so; na tu bɔne no firi wo mu.

english_verse: And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
translation_verse: na Israel nyinaa ntie na wɔnsuro, na wɔankɔ so anni wo mu asɛmmɔne a ɛte seyie.

english_verse: After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns.
translation_verse: Sɛ wote wo nkuro a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woatena mu no bi nka sɛ:

english_verse: You may hear that some worthless people have talked everyone there into worshiping other gods, even though these gods had never done anything for them.
translation_verse: Mmarima mmabusufoɔ bi asɔre wo mu adaadaa wɔn nkurɔfoɔ sɛ: Momma yɛnkɔ nkɔsom anyame foforɔ a monnim wɔn a,

english_verse: You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country,
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ hwehwɛ mu na bisabisa mu yie; na hwɛ sɛ asɛm no wom ampa sɛ wɔayɛ saa akyiwadeɛ yi wɔ wo mu a,

english_verse: you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too.
translation_verse: kum na fa nkrantɛ kum kuro no mufoɔ. Fa nkrantɛ sɛe ɛno ne deɛ ɛwom nyinaa ne emu afieboa pasapasa;

english_verse: That's why you must do what the Lord your God says is right. I am giving you his laws and teachings today, and you must obey them.
translation_verse: Sɛ wobɛtie AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nne adi ne mmara nsɛm a merehyɛ wo nnɛ yi nyinaa so ayɛ deɛ ɛtene AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ani so a.

english_verse: Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods. Animals That Can Be Eaten (Leviticus
translation_verse: na ɔman kronkron ne wo ma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, na wo na AWURADE ayi wo sɛ yɛ no ahodeɛ man, asase so aman nyinaa mu.

english_verse: You can eat any clean bird.
translation_verse: Anomaa biara a ne ho teɛ no, monni.

english_verse: Don't eat any disgusting animals.
translation_verse: Nni akyiwadeɛ biara.

english_verse: It is all right to eat meat from any animals that have divided hoofs and also chew the cud.
translation_verse: Na atɔteboa biara a ɔwɔ tɔte a emu apaeɛ, na ne tɔte mu apae nta mmienu, na ɔpu wesa, mmoa mu no, ɔno na monnie.

english_verse: But don't eat camels, rabbits, and rock badgers. These animals chew the cud but do not have divided hoofs. You must treat them as unclean.
translation_verse: Nanso yeinom deɛ, monnni, wɔn a wɔpu wesa ne wɔn a wɔn tɔte mu apae koraa no mu: Yoma, adanko ne atwaboa, ɛfiri sɛ wɔpu wesa deɛ, nanso wɔn tɔte mu mpae, wɔn ho nte mma mo;

english_verse: And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!
translation_verse: ne prako nso, ɛfiri sɛ ne tɔte mu apae deɛ, nanso ɔmpu nwesa, ne ho nte mma mo. Monnni wɔn nam, na monnka wɔn afunu.

english_verse: You can eat any fish that has fins and scales. But there are other creatures that live in the water,
translation_verse: Yei ne deɛ monnie, deɛ ɛwɔ nsuom nyinaa mu, deɛ ɛwɔ tɛtɛ ne abon nyinaa, monni.

english_verse: and if they do not have fins and scales, you must not eat them. Treat them as unclean.
translation_verse: Na biribiara a ɛnni tɛtɛ ne abon no, monnni: Ɛho nte mma mo.

english_verse: Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them.
translation_verse: Na ntuboa a wɔwea nyinaa ho nte mma mo; monnni.

english_verse: However, you are allowed to eat certain kinds of winged insects.
translation_verse: Ntuboa a wɔn ho teɛ nyinaa, monni.

english_verse: You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. You may give it to foreigners who live in your town or sell it to foreigners who are visiting your town. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. Give the Lord Ten Percent of Your Harvest Moses said:
translation_verse: Monnni aboa funu; fa ma ɔhɔhoɔ a ɔwɔ wo kuro apono mu ma no nni anaasɛ tɔn ma ɔnanani, ɛfiri sɛ woyɛ ɔman kronkron ma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn. Nnoa odwan ba wɔ ne na nufosuo mu. Ntotosoɔ du du ho mmara

english_verse: People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: W’adeɛ a woduaeɛ nnɔbaeɛ a w’afuo ma daa afirinhyia no, yi so ntotosoɔ du du.

english_verse: Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Na di no wɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim wɔ faako a ɔbɛyi sɛ ne din ntena no, w’aburoo, wo nsa ne wo ngo so ntotosoɔ du du, w’anantwie ne wo nnwan mmakan, na woasua AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn suro nna nyinaa.

english_verse: But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest,
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn hyira wo na sɛ ɔkwan no ware a wontumi nsoa, ɛfiri sɛ faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ayi sɛ ɔde ne din bɛto hɔ no ne wo ntam ware a,

english_verse: then sell this part and take the money there instead.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ dane no sika, na kyekyere sika no kura, na sim kɔ faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ayie no.

english_verse: When you and your family arrive, spend the money on food for a big celebration. Buy cattle, sheep, goats, wine, beer, and if there are any other kinds of food that you want, buy those too.
translation_verse: Na fa sika no tɔ adeɛ biara a wo kra kɔn dɔ, nantwie ne odwan ne bobesa ne nsa biara a ɛyɛ den ne adeɛ biara a wo kra pɛ, na di no hɔ, AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim, na ma wo ne wo fie ani nnye.

english_verse: And since people of the Levi tribe won't own any land for growing crops, remember to ask the Levites to celebrate with you.
translation_verse: Na Lewini a ɔwɔ wo kuro apono mu no, mma wo werɛ mmfiri no, ɛfiri sɛ ɔnni kyɛfa ne agyapadeɛ biara sɛdeɛ wo deɛ wowɔ.

english_verse: Every third year, instead of using the ten percent of your harvest for a big celebration, bring it into town and put it in a community storehouse.
translation_verse: Mfeɛ mmiɛnsa awieeɛ no, yi w’afe no mu nnɔbaeɛ so ntotosoɔ du du gugu wo kuro apono mu,

english_verse: The Levites have no land of their own, so you must give them food from the storehouse. You must also give food to the poor who live in your town, including orphans, widows, and foreigners. If they have enough to eat, then the Lord your God will be pleased and make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: na Lewini, ɛfiri sɛ ɔnni kyɛfa ne agyapadeɛ biara sɛdeɛ wo deɛ wowɔ no, ne ɔhɔhoɔ ne awisiaa ne okunafoɔ a wɔwɔ wo kuro apono mu mmra mmɛdi mmee, na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ahyira wo, wo nsa ano adwuma a woyɛ nyinaa mu.

english_verse: After the Lord your God gives land to each of you, there may be poor Israelites in the town where you live. If there are, then don't be mean and selfish with your money.
translation_verse: Sɛ wo nuanom mu biara dane ohiani wɔ kuro biara apono mu, w’asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woɔ no so a, mpirim w’akoma, na mmua wo nsa so ntia wo nua hiani.

english_verse: Every seven years you must announce, “The Lord says loans do not need to be paid back.” Then if you have loaned money to another Israelite, you can no longer ask for payment.
translation_verse: Na sɛdeɛ wɔnnyaa mu nkyɛ nie: Ɔdefɛmni biara a ɔde biribi afɛm ne yɔnko mfa nkyɛ no; ɔnnhyɛ ne yɔnko ne ne nua sɛ ɔntua, ɛfiri sɛ wɔapae no adekyɛ afe ama AWURADE.

english_verse: This law applies only to loans you have made to other Israelites. Foreigners will still have to pay back what you have loaned them.
translation_verse: Ɔnanani deɛ, hyɛ no ma no ntua, nanso wo biribi a ɛwɔ wo nua nkyɛn deɛ, fa kyɛ.

english_verse: No one in Israel should ever be poor. The Lord your God is giving you this land, and he has promised to make you very successful, if you obey his laws and teachings that I'm giving you today. You will lend money to many nations, but you won't have to borrow. You will rule many nations, but they won't rule you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛhyira wo sɛdeɛ ɔka kyerɛɛ woɔ no, na wode afɛm amanaman pii, na wo deɛ, worenkɔfɛm, na wobɛdi amanaman pii so, na wo deɛ, wɔrenni wo so.

english_verse: Instead, be kind and lend them what they need.
translation_verse: Na bue wo nsam ma no, na fɛm no deɛ ɛbɛso ne hia a ɛhia no no.

english_verse: Be careful! Don't say to yourself, “Soon it will be the seventh year, and then I won't be able to get my money back.” It would be horrible for you to think that way and to be so selfish that you refuse to help the poor. They are your relatives, and if you don't help them, they may ask the Lord to decide whether you have done wrong. And he will say that you are guilty.
translation_verse: Hwɛ yie na w’akomam amma ahuhusɛm bi sɛ: Afe a ɛtɔ so nson, gyae-mukyɛ afe no abɛn, na woannya wo nua hiani no ho adwemmɔne sɛ woremma no hwee, na wanteam amfrɛ AWURADE antia wo, na annane wo bɔne.

english_verse: You should be happy to give the poor what they need, because then the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: Yi wo yam ma no, na mma no nnyɛ w’akoma ahi sɛ wobɛma no; na saa adeɛ yi nti AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛhyira wo, wo nnwuma nyinaa ne deɛ wode wo nsa bɛka nyinaa mu.

english_verse: But if the animal is lame or blind or has something else wrong with it, you must not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛdɛm bi wɔ ne ho, ɔtɔ apakye anaasɛ n’ani afira, anaasɛ ɛdɛmmɔne biara wɔ ne ho a, mfa no mmɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn afɔdeɛ;

english_verse: And don't just tell them they are free to leave—
translation_verse: Na sɛ woregya no kwan ama no afa ne ho afiri wo nkyɛn akɔdi a, mma no nnkɔ nsapan:

english_verse: give them sheep and goats and a good supply of grain and wine. The more the Lord has given you, the more you should give them.
translation_verse: Fa wo nnwan ne w’ayuporebea ne wo nsakyi-amena no bi kyɛ no; adeɛ a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de ahyira woɔ no bi na fa ma no.

english_verse: But one of your slaves may say, “I love you and your family, and I would be better off staying with you, so please don't make me leave.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛba sɛ ɔka kyerɛ wo sɛ: Meremfiri wo nkyɛn, na medɔ wo ne wo fie, ɛfiri sɛ ɔdi yie wɔ wo nkyɛn a,

english_verse: Take the slave to the door of your house and push a sharp metal rod through one earlobe and into the door. Such slaves will belong to you for life, whether they are men or women.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ fa fitiiɛ fiti n’aso mu aponnwa ho na ɔnyɛ w’akoa daa; na w’afenaa nso yɛ no saa ara.

english_verse: If the first-born animal of a cow or sheep or goat is a male, it must be given to the Lord. Don't put first-born cattle to work or cut wool from first-born sheep.
translation_verse: W’anantwie ne wo nnwan mmakan anini a wɔbɛwoɔ no, yɛ wɔn kronkron ma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn. Mfa wo nantwie abakan nyɛ adwuma, na ntwitwa wo nnwan abakan ho.

english_verse: You can butcher it where you live, and eat it just like the meat of a deer or gazelle that you kill while hunting. Even those people who are unclean and unfit for worship can have some.
translation_verse: wo kuro apono mu na die, deɛ ne ho nteɛ ne deɛ ne ho teɛ nyinaa, sɛdeɛ wɔdi ɔwansane ne ɔforoteɛ no;

english_verse: But you must never eat the blood of an animal—let it drain out on the ground.
translation_verse: ne mogya nko na nnie, hwie gu fam sɛ nsuo.

english_verse: People of Israel, you must celebrate Passover in the month of Abib, because one night in that month years ago, the Lord your God rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Hwɛ bosome Abib na di Twam ma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, ɛfiri sɛ bosome Abib mu na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn yii wo firii Misraim anadwo.

english_verse: People of Israel, if you want to enjoy a long and successful life, make sure that everyone is treated with justice in the land the Lord is giving you. Don't Set Up Sacred Poles or Stones Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Asɛntenenee nko ara akyi na die, na woanya nkwa, na woakɔfa asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woɔ no.

english_verse: Eat thin bread for the next six days. Then on the seventh day, don't do any work. Instead, come together and worship the Lord. The Harvest Festival (Exodus
translation_verse: Nnansia na di apiti, na da a ɛtɔ so nson no nyɛ afahyɛ nhyiam mma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn; nyɛ adwuma biara.

english_verse: The Passover sacrifice must be a cow, a sheep, or a goat, and you must offer it at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Enti kum Twam afɔdeɛ no ma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, nnwan ne anantwie, faako a AWURADE ayi sɛ ne din ntena no.

english_verse: Don't offer the Passover sacrifice in just any town where you happen to live.
translation_verse: Nkum Twam no wɔ wo nkuro a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woɔ no biara mu,

english_verse: It must be offered at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. Kill the sacrifice at sunset, the time of day when you left Egypt.
translation_verse: gye faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛyi sɛ ne din ntena no, ɛhɔ na kum Twam no anwummerɛ a owia rekɔtɔ no, wo Misraim fire berɛ no mu;

english_verse: Then cook it and eat it there at the place of worship, returning to your tents the next morning.
translation_verse: na ma no mmen na di no faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛkyerɛ hɔ, na adeɛ kye a, woasane akɔ wo ntomadan mu.

english_verse: And don't set up a sacred stone! The Lord hates these things.
translation_verse: na mfa ɔboɔ dum nsi hɔ mfa; na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn akyiwadeɛ ne no.

english_verse: When you build the altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God, don't set up a sacred pole for the worship of the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Ntɛ nnua biara mfa nyɛ abosompɔ wɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn afɔrebukyia a worebɛsie no ho;

english_verse: go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped and celebrate the Harvest Festival in honor of the Lord your God. Bring him an offering as large as you can afford, depending on how big a harvest he has given you. Be sure to take along your sons and daughters and all your servants. Also invite the poor, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Na ma w’ani nnye AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim, wo ne wo babarima ne wo babaa ne w’akoa ne w’afenaa ne Lewini a ɔwɔ wo kuro apono mu ne ɔhɔhoɔ ne awisiaa ne okunafoɔ a wɔwɔ mo mu, faako a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛyi sɛ ne din ntena no;

english_verse: The bigger the harvest the Lord gives you, the bigger your gift should be. Treat Everyone with Justice Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Obiara mma deɛ ne nsa bɛso soɔ, sɛdeɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nhyira a ɔde ahyira woɔ no teɛ. Atemmufoɔ ne atemmuo ho asɛm

english_verse: Each year there are three festivals when all Israelite men must go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. These are the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters. And don't forget to take along a gift for the Lord.
translation_verse: Afirinhyia baako mu mprɛnsa na wo mmarima nyinaa mmɛyi wɔn ho adi AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn anim faako a ɔbɛkyerɛ hɔ. Apiti nnapɔnna, adapɛn dapɔnna ne asese nnapɔnna mu; na wɔmmfa nsapan mmmɛyi wɔn ho adi AWURADE anim.

english_verse: If an ox or a sheep has something wrong with it, don't offer it as a sacrifice to the Lord your God—he will be disgusted! Put To Death People Who Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Mfa nantwie anaa odwan a ne ho wɔ dɛm anaa adebɔne biara mmɔ afɔdeɛ mma AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, ɛfiri sɛ ɛyɛ n’akyiwadeɛ.

english_verse: So when you hear that someone in your town is committing this disgusting sin, you must carefully find out if that person really is guilty.
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛ wo na wote a, ɛnneɛ hwehwɛ mu yie; na sɛ wohunu sɛ ɛyɛ nokorɛ, na asɛm no wom sɛ wɔayɛ saa akyiwadeɛ yi wɔ Israel a,

english_verse: When other Israelites hear about it, they will be afraid and obey the decisions of the court. The King Moses said:
translation_verse: na yi bɔne no firi Israel, na ɔman no nyinaa nte na wɔnsuro, na wɔanni ahantansɛm bio. Ɔhene yie ne n’asɛdeɛ

english_verse: People of Israel, after you capture the land the Lord your God is giving you, and after you settle on it, you will say, “We want a king, just like the nations around us.”
translation_verse: Sɛ woduru asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woɔ no so na wofa tena so, na woka sɛ: Mɛsi me so hene sɛ amanaman a wɔatwa me ho ahyia no nyinaa a,

english_verse: Go ahead and appoint a king, but make sure that he is an Israelite and that he is the one the Lord has chosen.
translation_verse: fa deɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛyi no no si wo so hene; wo nuanom mu bi na fa no si wo so hene; mfa ɔnanani bi a ɔnyɛ wo nua nsi wo so hene.

english_verse: The king should not have many horses, especially those from Egypt. The Lord has said never to go back there again.
translation_verse: Nanso ɔhene no mma n’apɔnkɔ nnnɔɔso, na ɔmmma ɔman no nnsane nnkɔ Misraim nkɔpɛ apɔnkɔ dodoɔ; na AWURADE aka akyerɛ mo sɛ monnsane mmfa ɔkwan yi so bio.

english_verse: And the king must not have a lot of wives—they might tempt him to be unfaithful to the Lord. Finally, the king must not try to get huge amounts of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Nanso ɔmmma ne yerenom nnnɔɔso, na n’akoma ammane; saa ara na ɔmmma ne dwetɛ ne sika nnnɔɔso pii.

english_verse: The official copy of God's laws will be kept by the priests of the Levi tribe. So, as soon as anyone becomes king, he must go to the priests and write out a copy of these laws while they watch.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔte n’ahennie adwa so a, ɔnhwɛ mmara yi nwoma a ɛda asɔfoɔ ne Lewifoɔ anim no so ntwerɛ bi mfa;

english_verse: Each day the king must read and obey these laws, so that he will learn to worship the Lord with fear and trembling
translation_verse: na ɛntena ne nkyɛn, na ɔnkenkan mu, ne nkwa nna nyinaa, na wasua AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn suro, ne mmara yi mu nsɛm nyinaa ne ahyɛdeɛ yi so hwɛ ne ɛsodie,

english_verse: and not think that he's better than everyone else. If the king completely obeys the Lord's commands, he and his descendants will rule Israel for many years.
translation_verse: na n’akoma amma ne ho so ansene ne nuanom, na wammane amfiri mmara nsɛm no ho ankɔ nifa anaa benkum, na ama ne nna aware n’ahennie mu, ɔno ne ne mma, Israel mu.

english_verse: So when I want to speak to them, I will choose one of them to be a prophet like you. I will give my message to that prophet, who will tell the people exactly what I have said.
translation_verse: Mɛma odiyifoɔ so mama wɔn wɔn nuanom mu sɛ wo; na mede me nsɛm bɛhyɛ n’anomu, na waka deɛ mɛhyɛ no nyinaa akyerɛ wɔn.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe, including the priests, will not receive any land. Instead, they will receive part of the sacrifices that are offered to the Lord,
translation_verse: Wɔmmma Lewifoɔ asɔfoɔ, Lewi abusuakuo nyinaa nnnya kyɛfa ne agyapadeɛ biara Israel mu: AWURADE gya afɔdeɛ so adeɛ ne n’agyapadeɛ a wɔnnie;

english_verse: because he has promised to provide for them in this way.
translation_verse: na ɔrennya agyapadeɛ ne nuanom mu; AWURADE ne n’agyapadeɛ, sɛdeɛ ɔka kyerɛɛ no no.

english_verse: When you sacrifice a bull or sheep, the priests will be given the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
translation_verse: Na yei nyɛ asɔfoɔ no kyɛfa a ɛfiri ɔman no nsam mfiri wɔn a wɔbɔ afɔdeɛ no nkyɛn, nantwie oo, odwan oo: Wɔmfa basa ne abɔgyeɛ ne efuro mma ɔsɔfoɔ no;

english_verse: Give these gifts to the priests, because the Lord has chosen them and their descendants out of all the tribes of Israel to be his special servants at the place of worship.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ ɔno na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ayi no afiri wo mmusuakuo nyinaa mu, sɛ ɔnnyina nsom AWURADE din mu, ɔno ne ne mma, nna nyinaa. Lewifoɔ kyɛfa

english_verse: Any Levite can leave his hometown, and go to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped,
translation_verse: Na sɛ Lewini bi firi wo nkuro no biara mu, firi Israel mu baabiara a wakɔsoɛ, na ɔde ne pɛ nyinaa ba bɛtena faako a AWURADE bɛkyerɛ a,

english_verse: and then be a special servant of the Lord there, just like all the other Levites.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ ɔnsom AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn din mu sɛ ne nuanom Lewifoɔ a wɔgyina AWURADE anim hɔ nyinaa yɛ no.

english_verse: Soon you will go into the land that the Lord your God is giving you. The nations that live there do things that are disgusting to the Lord, and you must not follow their example.
translation_verse: Sɛ wonya duru asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema woɔ no so a, nsua amanaman no nneyɛɛ a ɛyɛ akyiwadeɛ no yɛ.

english_verse: The Lord is disgusted with anyone who does these things, and that's why he will help you destroy the nations that are in the land.
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE akyiwadeɛ ne wɔn a wɔyɛ yeinom nyinaa, na akyiwadeɛ yi nti na ɔretu wɔn afiri w’anim yi.

english_verse: Never be guilty of doing any of these disgusting things! A Prophet like Moses Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Wo ne AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ntena no amudie mu.

english_verse: You will go in and take the land from nations that practice magic and witchcraft. But the Lord your God won't allow you to do those things.
translation_verse: Na amanaman yi a worekɔtu wɔn yi tie abayifoɔ ne nkɔmhyɛfoɔ, na wo deɛ, AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn mmaa wo kwan sɛ yɛ no saa. Wɔntie Onyankopɔn diyifoɔ no

english_verse: Instead, he will choose one of your own people to be a prophet just like me, and you must do what that prophet says.
translation_verse: Odiyifoɔ a ɔfiri wo mu a ɔfiri wo nuanom mu te sɛ me na AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn bɛma no so ama woɔ, ɔno na montie no.

english_verse: You were asking for a prophet the day you were gathered at Mount Sinai and said to the Lord, “Please don't let us hear your voice or see this terrible fire again—if we do, we will die!”
translation_verse: Sɛdeɛ wobisaa AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn wɔ Horeb adwabɔ da no sɛ: Mma mennte AWURADE me Nyankopɔn nne bio, na mma mennhunu ogya kɛseɛ yi bio, na manwu!

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: Moses, they have said the right thing.
translation_verse: Ɛno na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Deɛ wɔaka no wɔaka no yie:

english_verse: Since the message comes from me, anyone who doesn't obey the message will have to answer to me.
translation_verse: Na ɛbɛba sɛ obiara a ɔrentie me nsɛm a ɔbɛka no me din mu no, me na mɛbisa no ne hɔ.

english_verse: But if I haven't spoken, and a prophet claims to have a message from me, you must kill that prophet, and you must also kill any prophet who claims to have a message from another god. Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Na odiyifoɔ a ɔbɛma ne ho so aka asɛm bi, me din mu, a menhyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnka, ne deɛ ɔbɛkasa anyame foforɔ din mu no, odiyifoɔ ko no bɛwu.

english_verse: You may be asking yourselves, “How can we tell if a prophet's message really comes from the Lord?”
translation_verse: Ebia wobɛka no w’akoma mu sɛ: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na yɛbɛhunu asɛm a AWURADE nkaeɛ no?

english_verse: You will know, because if the Lord says something will happen, it will happen. And if it doesn't, you will know that the prophet was falsely claiming to speak for the Lord. Don't be afraid of any prophet whose message doesn't come from the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɛ odiyifoɔ bi kasa wɔ AWURADE din mu, na asɛm korɔ no amma mu anaa ɛnyɛ nokorɛ a, na asɛm no mfiri AWURADE; ahantan mu na odiyifoɔ no kasaeɛ, nsuro no.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord your God has promised that if you obey his laws and teachings I'm giving you, and if you always love him, then he will give you the land he promised your ancestors. When that happens, you must name three more Safe Towns in the new territory.
translation_verse: na sɛ wodi mmara nsɛm a merehyɛ wo nnɛ yi nyinaa so yɛ, na wodɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn na wonante n’akwan so nna nyinaa a, ɛnneɛ yiyi nkuro mmiɛnsa bio ka mmiɛnsa yi ho fa,

english_verse: Soon you will go into the land and attack the nations. The Lord your God will destroy them and give you their lands, towns, and homes. Then after you are settled,
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn twitwa amanaman a ɔde wɔn asase rema woɔ no, na wotu wɔn tena wɔn nkuro ne wɔn adan mu a,

english_verse: For example, suppose you and a friend go into the forest to cut wood. You are chopping down a tree with an ax, when the ax head slips off the handle, hits your friend, and kills him. You can run to one of the Safe Towns and save your life.
translation_verse: sɛ ebia obi ne ne yɔnko kɔ kwaeɛ mu kɔto nnua, na ne nsa ma abonnua so de retwa dua, na dadeɛ no hɔn firi ne dua mu bɔ ne yɔnko ma no wu a, ɛnneɛ ɔnnwane nkɔ nkuro yi baako mu na ɔnnya nkwa;

english_verse: You don't deserve to die, since you did not mean to harm your friend. But he did get killed, and his relatives might be very angry. They might even choose one of the men from their family to track you down and kill you. If it is too far to one of the Safe Towns, the victim's relative might be able to catch you and kill you.
translation_verse: na mogya ho weretɔfoɔ amfa abufuhyeɛ anti onipakumfoɔ no na ɔkwan no wareɛ nti, wankɔto no anku no; nso na ɛnsɛ sɛ onipa kumfoɔ no wuo, ɛfiri sɛ berɛ a atwam no na ɔntane ne yɔnko no.

english_verse: That's why I said there must be three Safe Towns.
translation_verse: Enti na merehyɛ wo sɛ yiyi nkuro mmiɛnsa fa.

english_verse: But what if you really do commit murder? Suppose one of you hates a neighbor. So you wait in a deserted place, kill the neighbor, and run to a Safe Town.
translation_verse: Na sɛ obi tane ne yɔnko na ɔtɛ no sɔre to hyɛ ne so, na ɔde adeɛ bɔ no ma no wu, na ɔdwane kɔ nkuro yi baako mu a,

english_verse: If that happens, the leaders of your town must send messengers to bring you back from the Safe Town. They will hand you over to one of the victim's relatives, who will put you to death.
translation_verse: ɛnneɛ ne kurom mpanimfoɔ nsoma mma wɔnkɔfa no mfiri hɔ, na wɔmfa no nhyɛ mogya ho weretɔfoɔ no nsa, na ɔnwu.

english_verse: Israel, for the good of the whole country, you must kill anyone who murders an innocent person. Never show mercy to a murderer! Property Lines Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Mma w’ani nhu no mmɔbɔ, na yi mogya a ɛdi bem ho afobuo firi Israel, na ɛnsi wo yie.

english_verse: In the land the Lord is giving you, there are already stones set up to mark the property lines between fields. So don't move those stones. Witnesses Must Tell the Truth Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ntwe wo yɔnko hyeɛ a tetefoɔ atwa no w’agyapadeɛ a woanya mu wɔ asase a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema wo sɛ fa no so. Adansefoɔ ho asɛm

english_verse: Before you are convicted of a crime, at least two witnesses must be able to testify that you did it.
translation_verse: Ɔdanseni baako nnsɔre nntia obi, amumuyɛ biara anaa bɔne biara ho, bɔne biara a wɔyɛ mu; adansefoɔ baanu anaa baasa anomu nsɛm so na asɛm biara nnyina.

english_verse: If you accuse someone of a crime, but seem to be lying,
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔdansekurumfoɔ bi sɔre tia obi di no mfomsoɔ ho adanseɛ a,

english_verse: If you have to go to war, you may find yourselves facing an enemy army that is bigger than yours and that has horses and chariots. But don't be afraid! The Lord your God rescued you from Egypt, and he will help you fight.
translation_verse: Sɛ woretu sa ne w’atamfo akɔko na wohunu apɔnkɔ ne nteaseɛnam ne ɔman a wɔdɔɔso sene woɔ a, nsuro wɔn, ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn a ɔde wo firi Misraim asase so baeɛ no ka wo ho.

english_verse: Before you march into battle, a priest will go to the front of the army
translation_verse: Na sɛ mobɛn dɔm no a, ɔsɔfoɔ no mpinkyɛ mmɛkasa nkyerɛ ɔman no,

english_verse: and say, “Soldiers of Israel, listen to me! Today when you go into battle, don't be afraid of the enemy, and when you see them, don't panic.
translation_verse: na ɔnka nkyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Israel, tie, morebɛn dɔm nnɛ ne mo atamfoɔ akɔko, mommma mo akoma nntu, monnsuro na mo ho mmpopo, na mommma wɔn ho nnyɛ mo hu,

english_verse: The Lord your God will fight alongside you and help you win the battle.”
translation_verse: ɛfiri sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ne mo na ɛnam ne mo atamfoɔ rekɔko ama mo na wagye mo.

english_verse: Then the tribal officials will say to the troops: If any of you have built a new house, but haven't yet moved in, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to live in your new house.
translation_verse: Na ahwɛfoɔ no nkasa nkyerɛ ɔman no sɛ: Onii ko a wasi dan foforɔ na ɔmmuee ano no, ma no nsane nkɔ ne fie, na wantɔ ɔko mu na obi ankɔbue ɛdan no ano.

english_verse: If any of you have planted a vineyard but haven't had your first grape harvest, you may go home. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to enjoy your grapes.
translation_verse: Na onii ko a watɛ bobeturo na ɔnnya nyii ano no, ma no nsane nkɔ ne fie, na wantɔ ɔko mu, na obi anyi ano.

english_verse: If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
translation_verse: Na onii ko a wagye ɔbaa bi awadeɛ na ɔnnya nhyiaa no no, ma no nsane nkɔ ne fie, na wantɔ ɔko mu na obi ammfa no sɛ ɔyerɛ.

english_verse: Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
translation_verse: Na ahwɛfoɔ no nkɔ so nkasa nkyerɛ ɔman no sɛ: Onii ko a ɔsuro na n’akoma tuo no, ma no nsane nkɔ ne fie, na wamma ne nuanom akoma annane sɛ ne deɛ.

english_verse: When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ahwɛfoɔ no wie ɔman no kasakyerɛ a, wɔmfa asafohene nsisi ɔman no ti.

english_verse: Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals.
translation_verse: Na amanaman yi nkuro a AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn de rema wo sɛ di soɔ no mu deɛ, mma biribiara a ɛhome nnnya nkwa,

english_verse: He has commanded you to completely wipe out the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: na sɛe wɔn pasapasa: Hetifoɔ, Amorifoɔ, Kanaanfoɔ, Perisifoɔ, Hewifoɔ ne Yebusifoɔ, sɛdeɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn hyɛɛ woɔ no.

english_verse: If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na wɔankyerɛ mo wɔn akyiwadeɛ a wɔyɛ ma wɔn anyame no nyinaa bi yɛ, na moanyɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn bɔne.

english_verse: When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down.
translation_verse: Sɛ wotua kuro bi nna pii ne no reko afa a, mfa akuma nsɛe hɔ nnua, na ɛso aba bi na die, na mmu ngu. Afuo mu dua yɛ onipa na woasɛe no?

english_verse: You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
translation_verse: Nanso nnua a wonim sɛ ɛnyɛ nnua a wɔdie no deɛ, sɛe no na twa fa yɛ kuro a ɛne wo redi ako no ntuaban kɔsi sɛ wobɛbrɛ no aseɛ.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Mfiase no Onyankopɔn bɔɔ ɔsoro ne asase.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Na asase da hɔ hunu a enni bɔbea biara na Onyankopɔn honhom butuw nsu no ani.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Ɛnyɛ hann! Na ɛyɛɛ hann.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu hann no sɛ eye. Na Onyankopɔn paee hann ne sum no mu.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ hann no sɛ: Adekyee, na esum no de, ɔfrɛɛ no adesae. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a edi kan nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Ntrɛwmu mmra nsu no ntam, na ɛmmɛpae nsu no mu.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ ntrɛw mu no ɔsoro. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so abien nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Nsu a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase no mmoaboa ano wɔ faako, na wonhu asase kesee. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn frɛɛ kesee no asase, na nsu mmoaano no, ɔfrɛɛ no ɛpo. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ asase mfifi nwura frɔmfrɔm, nhaban a ɛsow aba, nnua a ɛsow nnuaba sɛnea ne su te a n'aba wɔ mu, wɔ asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na asase fifii wura, nhaban a ɛsow aba sɛnea ne su te, ne nnua a ɛsow nnuaba a n'aba wɔ mu sɛnea ne su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so abiɛsa nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Akanea mmra ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu, na ɛmmɛpae awia ne anadwo mu, na ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne ne bere nkyekyem ne nna ne mfe;

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: na ɛnyɛ akanea wɔ ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu, na ɛnharan asase so. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ akanea akɛse abien no, ɔkanea kɛse no, sɛ enni awia so, ne ɔkanea ketewa no, sɛ enni anadwo so, ne nsoromma nso.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn de sisii ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no mu sɛ ɛnharan asase so,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: na enni awia ne anadwo so, na ɛmpae hann ne esum no mu. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so anan nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Nsu no nnɔ abɔde a ɛte ase manyamanya, na ntakraboa ntu mfa asase so ɔsoro ntrɛwmu no ani.

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ nsuboa akɛse ne abɔde a ɛte ase a ɛkeka ne ho a ɛyɛ nsu mu manyamanya nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ɛne nnomaa a wɔwɔ ntaban nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔ, na monyɛ ɛpo mu nsu mu ma, na ntakraboa nnɔɔso asase so.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so anum nen.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Asase mma abɔde a ɛtete ase mfi mmra, sɛnea wɔn su te; ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne asase so mmoadoma, sɛnea wɔn su te. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn yɛɛ asase so mmoadoma sɛnea wɔn su te, ne ntɔteboa sɛnea wɔn su te, ne mmoa a wɔwea fam nyinaa sɛnea wɔn su te. Na Onyankopɔn hui sɛ eye.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Momma yɛnyɛ onipa wɔ yɛn suban so sɛ yɛn sɛso, na wonni ɛpo mu mpataa ne wim nnomaa ne ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn bɔɔ onipa wɔ ne suban so, Yiw Onyankopɔn suban so na ɔbɔɔ no, ɔbarima ne ɔbea na ɔbɔɔ wɔn.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa wɔn, na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monwo, na monnɔre, na monyɛ asase so ma, na monni so tumi, na munni ɛpo mu mpataa ne wim nnomaa ne mmoa a wɔkeka wɔn ho wɔ asase so nyinaa so.

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na asase so mmoadoma nyinaa ne wim nnomaa nyinaa ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa a ɔkra a ɛte ase wɔ wɔn mu no, mede nhaban momono mama wɔn sɛ wonni. Na ɛyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu nea ɔyɛe nyinaa, na hwɛ, eye papa. Na ade sae, na ade kyee, da a ɛto so asia nen.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Na wowiee ɔsoro ne asase ne nea ɛwɔ mu nyinaa.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn hyiraa da a ɛto so ason no, na ɔtew ho, efisɛ ɛno mu na Onyankopɔn home fii n'adwuma a ɔbɔe na ɔyɛe nyinaa ho. Adebɔ su: Eden turo

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: Na afuw mu nnua nyinaa nnya mmaa asase so, na afuw mu nhaban nyinaa nnya mfifii, efisɛ AWURADE Nyankopɔn nnya ntɔɔ osu nguu asase so ɛ, na onipa a ɔbɛdɔw asase nni hɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Na nsu fi asase so foroe, na ɛfɔw asase ani nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de fam dɔte nwenee onipa, na ohuw nkwa home guu ne hwene mu, na onipa yɛɛ ɔkra teasefo.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ turo bi wɔ Eden a ɛwɔ apuei fam, na ɔde onipa a ɔnwenee no, tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnua ahorow nyinaa a wɔhwɛ a, ɛyɛ fɛ, na eye sɛ wodi asase no so, ne nkwa dua a esi turo no mfinimfini, ne papa ne bɔne hu dua fifii asase so.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Na asu bi fi Eden bɛfɔw turo no, na efi hɔ ara na emu paepae yɛɛ nsuti anan.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Nea edi kan no din de Pison, ɛno na ɛkɔntɔn twa Hawila asase a sika wɔ so no nyinaa ho hyia;

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: na asase no so sika ye; ɛhɔ na bedola ne apopobibiribo wɔ.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Na asu a ɛto so abien no din de Gihon, ɛno na ɛkɔntɔn twa Kus asase nyinaa ho hyia.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na asu a ɛto so abiɛsa ne Tigri, ɛno na ɛsen wɔ Asaria apuei. Na asu a ɛto so anan ne Eufrate.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de onipa no kɔtenaa Eden turom sɛ ɔnnɔw na ɔnwɛn hɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ onipa no sɛ: Turom ha nnua nyinaa, di bi.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: Na papa ne bɔne hu dua no de, nni, efisɛ da a wubedi bi no, owu na wubewu.

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kae sɛ: Enye sɛ onipa nko tena, mɛyɛ ne sɛso boafo mama no.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn maa nnahɔɔ tɔɔ onipa no so, na ɔdae, na oyii ne mfe pare mu biako, na ɔde nam tuaa anan mu.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn de mfe pare a oyi fii onipa no mu no yɛɛ ɔbea, na ɔde no brɛɛ onipa no.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na onipa no kae sɛ: Ampa ara me nnompe mu dompe ne me honam mu nam ankasa ni. Oyi na wɔbɛfrɛ no ɔbea, efisɛ ɔbarima mu na woyii no fii.

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Ne saa nti na ɔbarima begyaw ne na ne n'agya, na ɔde ne ho akɔbata ne yere ho, na wɔayɛ ɔhonam koro.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu no deda adagyaw, ɔbarima no ne ne yere, na wɔn ani nwu.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ yɛ anifere kyɛn wuram mmoadoma a AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ wɔn nyinaa. Na obisaa ɔbea no sɛ: Ampa sɛ Nyankopɔn aka sɛ Munnni turom ha nnua nyinaa bi?

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Turom ha nnua aba no, yedi bi,

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: nanso dua a esi turo no mfinimfini no aba de, Onyankopɔn aka sɛ: Munnni bi, nso mommfa mo nsa nnka, na moanwu.

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no sɛ: Ɛnyɛ owu na mubewu:

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: na Onyankopɔn nim sɛ da a mubedi bi no, mo ani bebue, na moayɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn, ahu papa ne bɔne.

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no hui sɛ dua no ye sɛ wodi, na ɛyɛ aniwa fɛ, na dua no dɔ kɔn na ɛbɛtew ani no, ɔtew n'aba no bi, na odii, na ɔde bi maa ne kunu a ɔka ne ho no nso, na odii.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu ani buebuei, na wohui sɛ wɔdeda adagyaw, na wɔpompam borɔdɔma ahaban yɛɛ nkataanim fae.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Na wɔtee AWURADE Nyankopɔn nka sɛ ɔnam turom hɔ wɔ anwummere mfare mu. Na Adam no ne ne yere kohintaw fii AWURADE Nyankopɔn anim wɔ turom hɔ nnua mu.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn frɛɛ Adam, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wowɔ he?

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Na ose: Metee wo nka wɔ turom hɔ no, misuroe, efisɛ meda adagyaw, na mihintawee.

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Hena na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo sɛ woda adagyaw? Dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni bi no na woadi yi?

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Na Adam se: Ɔbea no a wode no bɛkaa me ho no, ɔno na ɔmaa me dua no aba bi na midii.

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woyɛɛ saa? Na ɔbea no se: Ɔwɔ no na ɔdaadaa me na midii.

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ ɔwɔ no sɛ: Sɛ woayɛ eyi nti, wɔadome wo ntɔteboa ne wuram mmoadoma nyinaa mu. Wo yafunu so na wobɛnantew, na woadi dɔte wo nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Na mede ɔtan mɛto wo ne ɔbea no ntam, ɛne w'asefo ne n'asefo ntam; ɔno na ɔbɛbɔ wo ti, na wo nso woaka ne nantin.

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ɔbea no de, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔdɔ na mɛma wo yaw ne wo nyinsɛn mu brɛ adɔɔso. Ɛyaw mu na wobɛwo mma, na w'ani begyina wo kunu, na ɔno na obedi wo so.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na Adam de, ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ woatie wo yere nne, na woadi dua a mehyɛɛ wo sɛ nni no bi nti, wo nti wɔadome asase. Ɛyaw mu na wubedidi so, wo nkwa nna nyinaa,

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: na nsɔe ne nnɛnkyɛnse na ebefifi ama wo, na woadi afuw so ahaban.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: W'anim fifiri mu na wubedidi de akosi sɛ wobɛsan akɔ dɔte mu, efisɛ emu na woyii wo fii, na woyɛ dɔte, na dɔte mu na wobɛsan akɔ.

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Na Adam too ne yere din Hawa, efisɛ ɔno na wayɛ ateasefo nyinaa na.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn yɛɛ nhoma ntade maa Adam ne ne yere de hyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyankopɔn kae sɛ: Hwɛ, onipa no ayɛ sɛ yɛn mu biako ahu papa ne bɔne. Na afei, nea ɛbɛyɛ na wanteɛ ne nsa antew nkwa dua no nso bi anni antena ase daa nti,

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: AWURADE Nyankopɔn tuu no fii Eden turom hɔ sɛ ɔnkɔdɔw asase a wɔfaa no fii mu no.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Na ɔpam onipa no, na ɔde Kerubim ne gyaframa afoa a edi ahim besii Eden turo no anim apuei fam sɛ wɔnwɛn ɔkwan a ɛkɔ nkwa dua no ho no.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere Hawa hyiae, na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Kain, na ɔkae se: AWURADE adaworoma, manya ɔbarima.

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Na ɔwoo ne nua Habel kaa ne ho. Na Habel yɛɛ oguanhwɛfo, na Kain de, ɔyɛɛ okuafo.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na ɛbae sɛ nna bi akyi no, Kain de afum nneɛma bɛyɛɛ AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Na Habel nso de ne nguan mu mmakan ne wɔn a wɔadɔ no bi bɛmae. Na AWURADE ani sɔɔ Habel ne n'ayɛyɛde no,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: nanso Kain ne n'ayɛyɛde de, n'ani ansɔ. Na Kain bo fuwii pii, na omunae.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ ɛdɛn nti na wo bo afuw, na ɛdɛn nti na woamuna yi?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Sɛ woyɛ papa a, anka w'anim rentew anaa? Na sɛ woanyɛ papa nti, bɔne butuw ɔpon ano, na w'akyi kwan na ɛrehwehwɛ, nanso di no so.

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Na Kain ka kyerɛɛ ne nua Habel sɛ ɔmma wɔnkɔ afum, na ɛbae sɛ wɔwɔ afum no, Kain sɔre hyɛɛ ne nua Habel, na okum no.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisaa Kain sɛ: Ɛhe na wo nua Habel wɔ? Na Kain buae sɛ: Minnim, me nua so hwɛfo ne me anaa?

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE se: Ɛdɛn na woayɛ yi? Wo nua mogya nne teɛm frɛ me fi asase so.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Na afei wɔadome wo afi asase a abue n'ano agye wo nua mogya afi wo nsam no so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Sɛ wodɔw asase a, ɛrenkɔ so mma wo ne nnɔbae bio, wobɛbɔ asesa na waye ɔkobɔfo wɔ asase so.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, woapam me nnɛ afi asase so, na mehintaw mafi w'anim, na mayɛ ɔsesafo ne ɔkobɔfo wɔ asase so, na obiara a obehu me no, obekum me.

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛno nti obiara a obekum Kain no, wobedi ne were ahorow asɔn. Na AWURADE yɛɛ sɛnkyerɛnne bi maa Kain, na obiara a obehu no no ankum no.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Na Kain fii AWURADE anim kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Nod asase so wɔ Eden apuei. Kain Asefo

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Na Kain ne ne yere Hawa dae, na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo Enok. Na ɔkyekyeree kurow bi, na ɔde ne ba Enok din too kurow no.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Na wɔwoo Irad maa Enok, na Irad woo Mehuyael, na Mehuyael woo Metusael, na Metusael woo Lamek. Lamek ne ne yerenom

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Na Sila nso woo Tubal-kain a ɔyɛ kɔbere mfrafrae ne dade ade nyinaa atomfo agya. Na Tubal-kain ne nuabea ne Naama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Na Lamek ka kyerɛɛ ne yerenom sɛ: Ada ne Sila, muntie me nne; Lamek yerenom, monyɛ aso mma m'asɛm: Mikum aberante bi sɛ opiraa me, na mikum aberante sɛ ɔboroo me.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wodi Kain so were mpɛn ason a, Lamek de bɛyɛ aduɔsɔn asɔn. Set ne Enos awo

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Na Adam ne ne yere dae bio, na ɔwoo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Set a ase ne: Nsiananmu, sɛ Onyankopɔn de ɔba foforo asi me Habel a Kain kum no no anan mu.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Set nso, wɔwoo ba maa no, na ɔtoo no din Enos. Ɛbere no mu na wofii ase bɔɔ AWURADE din sɔree no.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Adam nna a odii nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduasa, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Set nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne dumien, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Enos nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne anum, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Kenan nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron ne du, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Mahalaleel nna nyinaa si mfe ahanwɔtwe aduakron anum, na owui.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Yared nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduosia abien, na owui.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Na Enok ne Nyankopɔn nantewee; na wanhu no efisɛ Onyankopɔn faa no kɔe.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Metusela nna nyinaa si mfe ahankron aduosia akron, na owui.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: na ɔtoo no din Noa, na ɔkae sɛ: Oyi na ɔbɛkyekye yɛn werɛ wɔ yɛn nnwuma ne yɛn nsa ano brɛ mu wɔ asase a AWURADE adome no so.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Lamek nna nyinaa si mfirihyia ahansɔn aduɔsɔn asɔn, na owui.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn mma huu nnipa mmabea sɛ wɔn ho yɛ fɛ, na wɔwarewaree wɔn mu biara a wɔpɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Me honhom rentena onipa mu nkosi daa, efisɛ wɔyɛ ɔhonam, enti wɔn nna nyɛ mfe ɔha aduonu.

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Nna no mu na abran akɛse wɔ asase so, na akyiri yi nso a Onyankopɔn mma kɔɔ nnipa mmabea ho na wɔwoo mma maa wɔn no, eyinom ne abirempɔn a wɔwɔ din fi tete.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hui sɛ nnipa bɔne dɔɔso pii wɔ asase so, na wɔn komam adwene nyinaa yɛ bɔne nko daa nyinaa.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Mɛpopa nnipa a mabɔ wɔn no mafi asase ani, efi onipa so kosi ntɔteboa ne mmoa a wɔwea ne wim nnomaa so, efisɛ manu me ho sɛ meyɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Na Noa de, onyaa ɔdom wɔ AWURADE anim. Noa adaka no

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Eyi ne Noa ho asɛm: Noa yɛ onipa trenee a ɔyɛ pɛ, wɔ ne bere so nnipa mu. Noa ne Onyankopɔn na ɛnantewee.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Na Noa woo mmabanin baasa, Sem, Ham ne Yafet.

english_verse: God knew that everyone was terribly cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn huu asase, na hwɛ, asɛe, efisɛ nnipa nyinaa asɛe wɔn akwan wɔ asase so.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Fa ɔwawa yɛ adaka, na yɛ mpia wɔ adaka no mu, na fa ama tare emu ne ɛho.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Noa yɛɛ sa; sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no nyinaa pɛpɛɛpɛ, saa ara na ɔyɛe.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mede nsuyiri mɛba asase so mabɛsɛe abɔde a nkwa home wɔ mu nyinaa ɔsoro ase; asase so ade nyinaa rebewuwu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Na me ne wo bɛpam ato hɔ, na woakɔ adaka no mu, wo, ne wo mma, ne wo yere, ne wo mma yerenom.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nnomaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ne ntɔteboa, sɛnea wɔn su te, ne mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa, sɛnea wɔn su te, wɔn nyinaa mu abien abien mmra wo nkyɛn, na wɔanya nkwa.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Na wo de, boaboa aduan a wodi nyinaa bi ano kɔ mu, na ayɛ wo ne wɔn aduan.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Noa sɛ: Wo ne wo fi nyinaa, monkɔ adaka no mu, efisɛ wo na mahu wo ɔtreneeni m'anim bere yi mu.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Mmoa a wɔn ho tew nyinaa mu, fa ason asɔn, anini ne abere. Na mmoa a wɔn ho ntew mu, fa abien abien, onini ne ɔbere;

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: wim nnomaa mu nso, ason asɔn, anini ne abere, na wɔn ase nnya nkwa asase nyinaa ani.

english_verse: Seven days from now I will send rain that will last for
translation_verse: Efisɛ aka ɛha nnansɔn na matɔ osu magu asase so adaduanan awia ne anadwo, na mapopa ade a nkwa wom nyinaa afi asase ani.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: abien abien ne Noa kɔɔ adaka no mu, onini ne ɔbere, sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ Noa no.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Na nnansɔn akyi no, nsuyiri baa asase so.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Na osu tɔɔ asase so pii adaduanan awia ne anadwo.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Saa da yi ara mu na Noa ne ne mma, Sem, Ham ne Yafet, ne Noa yere ne ne mma yerenom baasa kɔɔ adaka no mu,

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: wɔne Noa kɔɔ adaka no mu, ɔhonam a nkwa home wɔ wɔn mu nyinaa mu abien abien.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Na wɔn a ɛbae no, ɔhonam nyinaa mu anini ne abere na ɛbae, sɛnea Onyankopɔn hyɛɛ no no, na AWURADE too no mu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nsu no boroo so kɔɔ soro basafa ason ne fa kataa mmepɔw so.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na abɔde a ɛkeka ne ho asase so nyinaa wuwui, nnomaa, ntɔteboa, wuram mmoa, mmoa a wɔwea asase so nyinaa, ne nnipa nyinaa,

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na nsu no boroo so wɔ asase so nna ɔha aduonum.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn kaee Noa ne mmoadoma nyinaa ne ntɔteboa a wɔne no wɔ adaka no mu no nyinaa, na Onyankopɔn maa mframa bɔ faa asase so, na nsu no ano brɛɛ ase.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Na ebun no nsu aniwa sisiwii, na ɔsoro mfɛnsere mu totoe, na osu a efi soro no gyaee tɔ.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na ɔsram a ɛto so asɔn, ɔsram no da a ɛto so dunsɔn na adaka no kɔtaa Ararat mmepɔw so.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Na nsu no kɔɔ so twee ara kosii ɔsram a ɛto so du no so. Na ɔsram a ɛto so du no da a edi kan no na mmepɔw atifi dedaa adi.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔsomaa kwaakwaadabi; na ofii adi, na odii akɔneaba de kosii sɛ nsu no yowee asase so.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa aborɔnoma fii ne nkyɛn sɛ ɔnkɔhwɛ sɛ nsu no ayow wɔ asase ani anaa.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Nanso aborɔnoma no annya ne nan sibea, na ɔsan baa ne nkyɛn adaka no mu, efisɛ nsu no da so wɔ asase nyinaa ani ara. Na ɔteɛɛ ne nsa faa no baa ne nkyɛn wɔ adaka no mu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛn nnansɔn bio, na ɔsomaa aborɔnoma fii adaka no mu bio.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Na aborɔnoma no baa ne nkyɛn anwummere, na hwɛ, ngodua ahaban frɔmfrɔm tua n'ano; na Noa hui sɛ nsu no ayow asase so.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
