english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Na ɔde hyɛɛ ne nkoa nsa akuwakuw, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa no sɛ: Monsen nni me kan, na momma kuw ne kuw ntam mpan.

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ nea odi kan no sɛ: Sɛ me nua Esau behyia wo, na obisa wo sɛ: Hena nipa ne wo, na ɛhe na worekɔ, na eyinom a edi w'anim yi yɛ hena dea?

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: W'akoa Yakob dea; ɛyɛ ayɛyɛde a wasoma de rebrɛ me wura Esau; na hwɛ, ɔno nso wɔ yɛn akyi.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ nea ɔto so abien ne nea ɔto so abiɛsa ne wɔn a wodi mmoakuw no akyi nyinaa nso sɛ: Sɛ mukohu Esau a, monka asɛm yi nkyerɛ no.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Na ayɛyɛde no sen dii n'anim; na ɔno de, ɔtenaa nsra no mu anadwo no.

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Na ɔde wɔn twaa asubɔnten no, na ɔmaa nea ɔwɔ nyinaa twae. Yakob ne ɔbɔfo bi tentam

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Na ɛkaa Yakob nko ara. Na ɔbarima bi ne no bɛtentamee koduu adekyee.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no hui sɛ ontumi no no, ɔkaa n'asen so tokuru mu, na Yakob dwonku huanee tentam a ɔne no tentamee no mu.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no kae sɛ: Ma menkɔ, na ade rekye. Na Yakob se: Meremma wonkɔ gye sɛ wuhyira me.

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Na obisaa no sɛ: Wo din de dɛn? Na ose: Yakob.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Wɔremfrɛ wo din Yakob bio, na wɔbɛfrɛ wo Israel, ase ne: Onyankopɔn kofoni, efisɛ wo ne Nyankopɔn ne nnipa ako, na woatumi.

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bisaa no sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me wo din. Na ose ɛdɛn nti na wubisa me din? Na ohyiraa no wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Otwaa mu wɔ Peniel, bere a na owia apue no, na ɔtɔ gu so ne dwonku a ahuan no nti.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Enti Israelfo nni ntini a ɛwɔ asen mu akwaa tokuru mu no de besi nnɛ, efisɛ ɔkaa Yakob dwonku tokuru mu, n'asen mu ntini no so.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔde mmaawa no ne wɔn mma dii anim, na Lea ne ne mma dii hɔ, na Rahel ne Yosef dii akyiri.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Na ɔno ankasa de, ɔsen dii wɔn anim, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase kɔɔ fam mpɛn ason de kosii sɛ oduu ne nua no nkyɛn.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Na Esau tuu mmirika behyiaa no yɛɛ no atuu, na ɔde ne ti too ne kɔn ho, na ofew n'ano, na wosui.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n'ani so huu mmea no ne wɔn mma no, ɔkae sɛ: Henanom ne eyinom a wɔka wo ho yi? Na ose: ɛyɛ mma a Onyankopɔn de adom w'akoa.

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Na mmaawa no twiw bɛnee, wɔn ne wɔn mma, na wɔbobɔɔ wɔn mu ase.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Na Lea nso ne ne mma twiw bɛnee bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase, na akyiri no Yosef ne Rahel twiw bɛnee bobɔɔ wɔn mu ase.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Na ɛdɔm a mihyiaa wɔn yi ase ne dɛn? Na ose: Sɛ ɛbɛyɛ na menya me wura anim dom.

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kae sɛ: Nea mewɔ dɔɔso, me nua, ma wo de ntena hɔ mma wo.

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Na Yakob kaa se: Dabida, mesrɛ wo, sɛ manya w'anim dom a, gye m'ayɛyɛde a ɛwɔ me nsam yi, na w'anim a mahu yi te sɛ obi hu Nyankopɔn anim, efisɛ w'ani asɔ me.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, gye nhyira a wɔde abrɛ wo yi, efisɛ Onyankopɔn adom me, na mewɔ ade nyinaa. Na ɔhyɛɛ no, na ogyei.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ma yensim nkɔ, na minni w'anim.

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me wura nim sɛ mma a wɔyɛ mmerɛw ne nguan ne anantwi a wɔma nufu ka me ho, na sɛ wopia wɔn dodo da koro a, nguankuw no nyinaa bewuwu.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Enti ma me wura ntwam nni n'akoa kan, na me de, mɛnantew brɛoo, sɛnea mmoa a wodi m'anim ne mma no betumi, de akosi sɛ medu me wura nkyɛn wɔ Seir.

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Na Esau kae sɛ: Ma minnyaw wo nnipa a wɔka me ho yi bi. Na ose: Na wɔnyɛ dɛn? Ma minnya me wura anim dom.

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Na Yakob siim kɔɔ Sukot, na osii dan wɔ hɔ, na ɔbobɔɔ asese maa ne mmoa; enti wɔfrɛ hɔ Sukot, ase ne: Asese.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Na Yakob fii Mesopotamia no, ɔnam beduu Sekem kurow a ɛwɔ Kanaan asase so no mu dwoodwoo, na osisii ne ntamadan wɔ kurow no anim.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔɔ asase a osii ne ntamadan wɔ so no wɔ Sekem n'agya Hamor mma nkyɛn, nnwetɛbona ɔha.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Na osii afɔremuka wɔ hɔ, na ɔtoo no: El-Elohe-Israel, ase ne: Onyankopɔn, Israel Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Na Lea babea Dina a ɔwoo no maa Yakob no fii adi sɛ ɔrekɔhwɛ asase no so mmea.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Na asase no so otitiriw Hewini Hamor ba Sekem huu no no, ɔkyeree no, too no mmonaa guu ne ho fi.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Na Sekem koma fam Yakob ba Dina ho, na ɔdɔɔ ababaa no, na otwaa ne bo too ne yam.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Na Sekem ka kyerɛɛ n'agya Hamor sɛ: Kogye ababaa yi aware ma me.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Na Yakob tee sɛ wahyɛ ne babea Dina ne no ada no; nso na ne mmammarima wɔ ne mmoa nkyɛn wɔ wuram, enti Yakob yɛɛ komm de kosii sɛ wɔbaa fie.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Na Yakob mmammarima tee no, wofii wuram bae. Na ɛyɛɛ mmarima no yaw, na wɔn bo fuwii pa ara, sɛ Sekem adi Israel ho nkwaseasɛm sɛ ɔne Yakob babea akɔda, ade a ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔyɛ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Na Hamor ne wɔn kasae sɛ: Me ba Sekem akoma fam mo babea no ho, mesrɛ mo, momfa no mma no aware.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Na mo ne yɛn nni ayeware, na momfa mo mmabea mma yɛn, na mo nso monware yɛn mmabea.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Na mo ne yɛn ntena, na asase na ɛda mo anim yi, montena so nyɛ so adwuma nnya so ade.

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Na Sekem ka kyerɛɛ, Dina n'agya ne ne nuanom sɛ: Momma minnya mo anim dom, na biribiara a mubese me no, mɛma.

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Munnye me tiade dodow ne akyɛde biara, na biribiara a mubese me no, mɛma, na momfa ababaa no mma me aware.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Na Yakob mmammarima no kasae de nnaadaa buaa Sekem ne n'agya Hamor, efisɛ wagu wɔn nuabea Dina ho fi,

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Yɛrentumi saa ade yi yɛ, sɛ yɛde yɛn nua bɛma ɔbarima a ɔyɛ momonoto, efisɛ ɛno yɛ ahohora ma yɛn.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Na eyi mu nko na yɛbɛpene mo, sɛ mobɛdan ayɛ sɛ yɛn, na wɔatwa mo mu mmarima nyinaa twetia.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Ɛno na yɛde yɛn mmabea bɛma mo, na yɛabɛfa mo mmabea nso aware, na yɛne mo atena, na yɛayɛ ɔman koro.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Na sɛ moantie yɛn, na moantwa twetia a, ɛnne yɛbɛfa yɛn babea akɔ.

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nsɛm no sɔɔ Hamor ne Hamor ba Sekem ani,

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: sɛ ɔbɛyɛ saa ade no, efisɛ Yakob babea no sɔ n'ani, na ɔwɔ anuonyam sen n'agya fifo nyinaa.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Na Hamor ne ne ba Sekem kɔɔ wɔn kurow abobow ano, na wɔne wɔn kurom mmarima kɔkasae sɛ:

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: Nnipa yi, wɔne yɛn te asomdwoe mu, enti momma wɔntena asase yi so, na wɔnyɛ so adwuma. Na asase yi, hwɛ, ɛda wɔn anim haharaa. Momma yɛmfa wɔn mmabea nware, na yɛmfa yɛn mmabea nso mma wɔn.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Na eyi nko mu na nnipa no bɛpene sɛ wɔne yɛn bɛtena, na yɛayɛ ɔman koro: sɛ yɛn mu mmarima nyinaa betwa twetia, sɛnea wɔatwa no.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: So wɔn mmoa ne wɔn ahonyade ne wɔn afieboa nyinaa renyɛ yɛn dea anaa? Momma yɛmpene wɔn ara, na wɔne yɛn ntena.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so abiɛsa a ne yaw kaa wɔn no, Yakob mmammarima baanu, Simeon ne Lewi a wɔyɛ Dina nuanom, fofaa wɔn nkrante kɔɔ kurow no so mpofirim kokum mmarima nyinaa.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Na wɔde nkrante kum Hamor ne ne ba Sekem; na wɔde Dina fii Sekem fi hɔ bae.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob mmammarima no baa atɔfo no so bɛfow kurow no mu nneɛma, efisɛ wɔagu wɔn nua ho fi.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Wɔn nguan, anantwi ne wɔn mfurum ne nea ɛwɔ kurow no mu ne nea ɛwɔ mfuw mu no, wɔfae,

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: ne wɔn ahode nyinaa, wɔn mma nyinaa ne wɔn yerenom, wɔfaa wɔn nnommum, fow nea ɛwɔ fie nyinaa.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob ka kyerɛɛ, Simeon ne Lewi sɛ: Moahaw me ama me ho abɔn wɔn a wɔte asase yi so, Kanaanfo ne Perisifo. Na me de, meyɛ asafo a misua yi, wɔbɛboaboa wɔn ho ano aba me so abekum me, na wɔasɛe me ne me fi.

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Na wose: So ɔnyɛ yɛn nuabea sɛ oguamanfo anaa?

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Na momma yɛnsɔre nkɔ Betel, na minkosi afɔremuka wɔ hɔ memma Onyankopɔn a m'ahohia da otiee me, na odii m'akyi wɔ ɔkwan a mekɔe no mu no.

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔde wɔn anyame ananafo a ɛwɔ wɔn nsam nyinaa ne wɔn aso mu nkaa maa Yakob, na Yakob de koraa dupɔn bi a ɛwɔ Sekem ho no ase.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Na wosiim sɛ wɔrekɔ no; Onyankopɔn ho hu baa nkurow a atwa wɔn ho ahyia no so, na wɔantiw Yakob mma no.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Na osii hɔ afɔremuka, na ɔfrɛɛ hɔ: El-betel, ase ne: Betel Nyankopɔn, efisɛ da a ɔreguan afi ne nua anim no, ɛhɔ na Onyankopɔn yii ne ho kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Na Rebeka gyigyefo Debora wui, na wosiee no Betel anafo fam wɔ odum bi ase, na ɔtoo no din Alonbakut.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Na asase a mede mama Abraham ne Isak no, wo na mede mɛma wo; na w'asefo a wobedi w'akyi no na mede asase no mɛma wɔn.

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Na Yakob de odum sii nea ɔne no kasae hɔ, ɔbodum, na ohwiei ɔnom afɔre guu so, na ɔde ngo guu so.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Na Yakob frɛɛ nea ɔne Nyankopɔn kasae hɔ Betel.

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Na wotutu fii Betel kɔe. Na aka ɔkwan tiaa bi na wɔadu Efrat no, awo kaa Rahel, na awo no den no.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Na n'awo no mu yɛɛ den no, awogyefo no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro, na eyi nso wobɛwo babarima.

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na ne kra refi ne mu na ɔreyɛ awu no, ɔtoo no din Benoni, ase ne: M'amanehunu ba, na n'agya de, ɔfrɛɛ no Benyamin ase ne: Ahotɔ ba.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na Rahel wui, na wosiee no Efrat a ɛne Betlehem no kwan nkyɛn

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Na Yakob sii ne da so dum, ɛne Rahel da so dum de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Na Israel tutu kosii ne ntamadan wɔ Eder abantenten akyi no ho.

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Na Israel te asase no so no, Ruben ne n'agya abaawayere Bilha kɔdae, na Israel tee. Yakob mma (

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Na Yakob baa n'agya Isak nkyɛn wɔ Mamre, wɔ Kiriat-arba a ɛne Hebron, nea Abraham ne Isak tenae sɛ ahɔho no.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esau waree Kanaanfo mmea: Hetini Elon babea Ada ne Hewini Sibeon ba Ana babea Ohlibama,

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: ne Ismael babea Basmat, Nebaiot ne nuabea.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Na Oholibama woo Yeus ne Yalam ne Kora. Eyinom ne Esau mma a wɔwoo wɔn maa no wɔ Kanaan asase so.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Esau faa ne yerenom ne ne mmammarima ne ne mmabea ne ne fifo nyinaa ne ne mmoa ne n'anantwi nyinaa ne n'ahonyade a onyae wɔ Kanaan asase so nyinaa, na ofii ne nua Yakob ho kɔɔ asase bi so.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Efisɛ wɔn ahonyade dɔɔso sen nea wɔde tena faako, na asase a wɔyɛ so ahɔho no, wɔn mmoa dodow nti na wɔnsen so.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Na Esau a ɔno ara ne Edom no kɔtenaa Seir bepɔw so.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Esau mma mu atitiriw: Esau abakan Elifas mma: Atitiriw Teman, Omar, Sefo, Kenas,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: Kora, Gatam ne Amalek. Eyinom ne Elifas atitiriw wɔ Edom asase so; eyinom ne Ada mma.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Esau ba Reuel mma: Atitiriw Nahat, Sera, Sama, ne Misa. Eyinom ne Reuel atitiriw wɔ Edom asase so; eyinom ne Esau yere Basmat mma.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Esau yere Oholibama mma: Atitiriw Yeus, Yalam ne Kora. Eyinom ne Esau yere Oholibama, Ana ba, atitiriw no.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Esau mma, na eyinom ne wɔn atitiriw no; ɔne Edom. Seir Asefo (

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Na Lotan mma ne Hori ne Heman, na Lotan ne nuabea ne Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Sobal mma: Alwan, Manahat, Ebal, Sefo ne Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Sibeon mma: Aya ne Ana. Oyi ne Ana a na ɔhwɛ n'agya Sibeon mfurum no, a ohuu nsuɔhyew aniwa wɔ sare so no.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Ana mma: Dison ne Oholibama, Ana babea.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Dison mma: Hemdan Esban, Itran ne Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Eser mma: Bilhan, Saawan ne Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne Disan mma: Us ne Aran.

translation_verse: Eyinom ne Horifo atitiriw: Atitiriw Lotan, Sobal, Sibeon, Ana,

translation_verse: Dison, Eser, ne Disan. Eyinom ne Horifo atitiriw a wɔyɛɛ wɔn atitiriw wɔ Seir asase so. Edom Ahene (

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne Esau atitiriw no din, sɛnea wɔn mmusuakuw, wɔn tenabea ne wɔn din te: Atitiriw Timna, Ahoa, Yetet,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: Oholibama, Ela, Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: Kenas, Teman, Mibsar,

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: Magdiel, ne Iram. Eyinom ne Edom a ɔne Esau, Edomfo agya no atitiriw, sɛnea wɔn tenabea te wɔ asase a wonyae no so.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Na Yakob tenaa asase a n'agya yɛɛ so hɔho a ɛne Kanaan asase no so.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no se: Wɔatutu afi ha; na metee sɛ wɔkae sɛ: Momma yɛnkɔ Dotan. Na Yosef tiw ne nuanom, na okohuu wɔn wɔ Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Na esiane sɛ: Yosef yɛ ne nkwakoraa bere mu ba nti, Israel dɔ no sen ne mma nyinaa; enti ɔpam batakari fɛfɛɛfɛ bi maa no.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom hui sɛ wɔn agya dɔ no sen wɔn anuanom nyinaa no, wokyii no, na wɔamfa abodwo ne no ankasa.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Na Yosef soo dae, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom, na wokyii no sen kan no.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Muntie ɔdae a maso yi:

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, yɛrekyekyere awi afiafi wɔ afum, na hwɛ, me afi no sɔre gyinae kyerebenn, na hwɛ, mo afiafi atwa ho ahyia, na ɛkotow me afi no.

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So odi na wubedi yɛn so hene? Anaasɛ ɔhyɛ na wobɛhyɛ yɛn so? Na ne dae ne ne nsɛm no nti wɔkɔɔ so tan no pii.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsoo dae foforo bio, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Hwɛ, maso dae bio, na hwɛ, owia ne ɔsram ne nsoromma dubiako akotow me.

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n'agya ne ne nuanom no, n'agya kaa n'anim sɛ ɔdae bɛn na woaso yi? So ɔba na me ne wo na ne wo nuanom bɛba abɛkotow fam wɔ w'anim?

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom ani beree no; na n'agya de, ɔde asɛm no siei.

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Na ne nuanom kɔhwɛɛ wɔn agya nguan wɔ Sekem.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Na Israel ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Wo nuanom yɛn nguan wɔ Sekem. Bra na mensoma wo, wɔn nkyɛn. Na ose: Mini.

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ na kɔhwɛ sɛ wo nuanom ne nguan no ho ye anaa; na san bɛka kyerɛ me. Na ɔsomaa no fii Hebron bon mu, na okoduu Sekem.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi huu no, na hwɛ, ɔrewɔ wuram ntwɛtwɛdɛ. Na ɔbarima no bisaa no sɛ: Wohwehwɛ dɛn?

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me nuanom na merehwehwɛ wɔn; mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me faako a wɔyɛn wɔn mmoa no.

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Na wohuu no wɔ akyirikyiri. Na onnya nnuu wɔn nkyɛn no, wɔpam ne tiri so sɛ wobekum no.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Na wosisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔdaesofo no na ɔreba no.

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Afei mommra mma yenkum no mfa no nto mmura yi bi mu, na yɛnka sɛ: Aboa bɔne bi na awe no, na yɛahwɛ nea ne dae no bewie.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Na Ruben tee no, ogyee no fii wɔn nsam kae sɛ: Mommma yennkum no.

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Na ose: Munnhwie mogya nngu, na momfa no nto sare so ha abura yi mu; na mommfa mo nsa nnka no. Ɔyɛɛ saa na anka wayi no afi wɔn nsam de no asan akɔma n'agya.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Na Yosef duu ne nuanom nkyɛn no, wɔworɔw n'atade, ne batakari fɛfɛɛfɛ a ɔhyɛ no,

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Na wɔtenaa ase didii. Na wɔmaa wɔn ani so hwɛe, na hwɛ, Ismaelfo akwantufo kuw bi a wofi Gilead rekɔ Misraim ne wɔn yoma a wɔsoso aduhuam ne akyenkyennuru ne kurobow reba.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Sɛ yekum yɛn nua na yesiw ne mogya so a, mfaso bɛn na ɛwɔ mu?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Mommra mma yɛntɔn no mma Ismaelfo no, na mommma yɛmmfa yɛn nsa nnka no, efisɛ ɔyɛ yɛn nua ne yɛn mogya. Na ne nuanom no tiee no.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Na Midianfo aguadifo bi bɛsenee. Na wɔtwetwee Yosef yii no fii abura no mu, na wɔtɔn Yosef maa Ismaelfo no gyee nnwetɛbona aduonu. Na wɔde Yosef kɔɔ Misraim.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Na Ruben san baa abura no so, na hwɛ, Yosef nni abura no mu. Na osunsuanee ne ntade mu,

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: na ɔsan baa ne nuanom nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Abofra no nni hɔ, na afei de, dɛn na menyɛ?

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa Yosef atade no, na wokum ɔpapo bi, na wɔde atade no bɔɔ mogya no mu.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Na wɔsoma ma wɔde batakari fɛfɛ no brɛɛ wɔn agya bɛkae sɛ; Eyi na yɛahu, hwɛ sɛ wo ba no atade ni anaa?

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛe no, ɔkae sɛ ɛyɛ me ba atade a! Aboa bɔne bi na awe no, ampa ara wɔatetew Yosef mu.

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yakob sunsuanee ne ntade mu, na ɔde ayitoma bɔɔ n'asen, na osuu ne ba no kyɛe.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Na ne mmammarima nyinaa ne ne mmabea nyinaa sɔree sɛ wɔbɛkyekye ne werɛ, nanso wamma wɔankyekye ne werɛ, na ose: Mede awerɛhow yi ara mɛkɔ me ba nkyɛn wɔ asaman. Na n'agya suu no.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Na Midianfo no kɔtɔn no wɔ Misraim maa Potifar a ɔyɛ Farao piani ne n'ankɔbeafo so panyin no.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Na ɛbae sɛ, bere no ara mu, Yuda fii ne nuanom nkyɛn kɔe, na ɔkɔtenaa Adulamni bi a wɔfrɛ no Hira nkyɛn.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Na Yuda huu Kanaanni bi a wɔfrɛ no Sua, babea bi wɔ hɔ, na ɔwaree no ne no dae.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Er.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Na onyinsɛnee bio woo babarima, na ɔtoo ne din Onan.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Na onyinsɛnee bio woo babarima, na ɔtoo ne din Sela. Na ɔwoo no no, na ɔwɔ Kesib.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Na Yuda waree yere bi a wɔfrɛ no Tamar maa n'abakan Er.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na Yuda abakan Er yɛɛ bɔne AWURADE anim, na AWURADE kum no.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ Onan sɛ: Kɔ wo nua yere no ho, na fa no kunabea, na wo mma ma wo nua.

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Na Onan nim sɛ mma no renyɛ ne dea, enti sɛ ɔkɔ ne nua yere no ho a, ɔma ne ho nsu no gu fam sɛe, na wanwo mma amma ne nua no.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Na nea ɔyɛe no yɛɛ bɔne wɔ AWURADE anim, enti okum ɔno nso.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Na afei Yuda ka kyerɛɛ n'ase Tamar sɛ: Kɔtena kuna mu wɔ w'agya fi kosi sɛ me ba Sela benyin. Efisɛ ose: anyɛ saa a, ɔno nso bewu sɛ ne nuanom. Na Tamar kɔe kɔtenaa n'agya fi.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Na ɛkyɛe kyɛe no, Sua babea, Yuda yere no, wui. Na Yuda werɛ kyekyee no, ɔne n'adamfo Hira Adulamni no kɔɔ ne nguan ho twitwafo nkyɛn wɔ Timnat.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Tamar sɛ: Hwɛ, wo asew rekɔ Timnat akotwitwa ne nguan ho.

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Na oyii ne kuna atade fii ne ho, na ɔde nkataanim kataa n'anim, na ɔbobɔw ne ho, na ɔkɔtenaa Enaim kurotia wɔ Timnat kwan ho, efisɛ wahu sɛ Sela anyin, na wɔamfa no amma no aware.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Na Yuda huu no no, esiane sɛ wakata n'anim nti, obuu no sɛ oguamanfo.

english_verse: and asked her to sleep with him. She asked, “What will you give me if I do?”
translation_verse: Na ɔman kɔɔ ne nkyɛn ɔkwan no ho se: Ma me ne wo nkɔda ɛ, nso onnim sɛ n'ase a. Na ose: Dɛn na wobɛma me na wo ne me ada?

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Na ose: Mɛma wɔde aberekyi ba afi nguan mu abrɛ wo. Na ose: Ɛnne si me awowa kosi sɛ wode bɛba.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Dɛn na memfa minsi wo awowa? Na ose: Wo nsɔanokaa ne wo hama ne wo nsam poma. Na ɔde maa no, na ɔne no dae, na onyinsɛnee.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔree, na ɔkɔe, na oyii ne nkataanim fii ne ho, na ɔhyɛɛ ne kuna atade no.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Na Yuda de aberekyi ba no maa n'adamfo Adulamni no sɛ ɔmfa nkogye n'awowade no wɔ ɔbea no nsam mmrɛ no, nanso wanhu no.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Na obisaa kurom hɔfo sɛ: Oguamanfo a ɔte Enaim kwan ho no wɔ he? Na wose: Oguamanfo bi nni ha.

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsan baa Yuda nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Manhu no, nanso kurom hɔfo se: Oguamanfo bi nni hɔ.

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda se: Ma ɔmfa, na yɛn ani anwu. Hwɛ, mama wode aberekyi ba yi akɔma no, na woanhu no.

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Na ɛbɛyɛ asram abiɛsa akyi no, wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Yuda sɛ: W'ase Tamar abɔ aguaman, nanso hwɛ, wanyinsɛn aguamammɔ no mu. Na Yuda se: Monkɔfa no mmra na wɔnhyew no.

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔfaa no bae no, ɔsoma kɔka kyerɛɛ ne sew no sɛ ɔbarima a ne nneɛma ni no, ne ho na manyinsɛn. Na ose: Hwehwɛ mu ɛ, na hwɛ, hena nsɔanokaa ne hama ne poma ni?

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Na Yuda hui no, ɔkae sɛ ɔteɛ sen me, efisɛ mamfa no mamma me ba Sela. Nanso ɔne no anna bio.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Na ɔrewo no, obiako yii ne nsa, na awogyefo no soo ne nsa no mu de asaawa kɔkɔɔ kyekyeree kae sɛ: Oyi na ofii adi kan.

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwee ne nsa kɔɔ mu no, na hwɛ, ne nua no fii adi, na ɔkae sɛ ɛdɛn na wotew mu? Wo so na ntewmu no wɔ. Enti wɔtoo no din Peres.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Na akyiri no, ne nua a asaawa kɔkɔɔ bɔ ne nsa so no bae, na wɔtoo no din Sera, ase ne Kɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Na wɔde Yosef kɔɔ Misraim. Na Farao piani Potifar a ɔyɛ ankɔbeafo so panyin na ɔyɛ: Misraimni tɔɔ no Ismaelfo a wɔde no kɔɔ hɔ no nkyɛn.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Na ne wura hui sɛ: AWURADE di n'akyi na AWURADE ma nea ɔyɛ nyinaa yɛ yiye n'abasa so no,

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Yosef nyaa n'anim dom, na ɔsom no; na ɔde no sii ne fi so, na ɔde nea ɔwɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ ne nsa.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Na ɔde nea ɔwɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na ɔwɔ hɔ nti, ɔnhwɛ biribiara gye aduan a ɔno ara di. Nso Yosef ho ne n'anim yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Na ɛbae sɛ nsɛm yi akyi no, ne wura yere tuu n'ani sii Yosef so, na ɔkae sɛ: Wo ne me mmɛda.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Nanso wampene, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne wura yere no sɛ: Hwɛ, sɛ me wura anya me nti, ɔnhwɛ nea ɛwɔ ne fi, na ɔde nea ɔwɔ nyinaa ahyɛ me nsa.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Obiara nyɛ kɛse nsen me ofie ha, na ɔnkame me biribiara gye wo, sɛ ne yere ne wo ntia. Na ɛdɛn na menyɛ amumɔyɛ kɛse yi, na menyɛ bɔne mintia Onyankopɔn?

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Na ɔka saa daa daa kyerɛ Yosef, nanso Yosef ampene sɛ ɔne no bɛda, na wakɔ ne ho.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Na saa bere no mu, da bi ɔkɔɔ ɔdan no mu sɛ ɔrekɔyɛ n'adwuma, na ofie hɔfo no mu biara nni hɔ no, osoo n'atade mu kae sɛ: Wo ne me mmɛda!

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ɔfrɛfrɛɛ ne fifo ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monhwɛ, wakɔfa Hebrini yi aba rebedi yɛn ho fɛw: waba me nkyɛn sɛ ɔne me rebɛda, na mede nne kɛse meteɛɛm;

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: na ɔtee sɛ memaa me nne so meteɛɛm no, ogyaw n'atade wɔ me nsam, na oguan fii adi.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Na ɔde n'atade no guu ne nkyɛn kosii sɛ ne wura baa ofie.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: na memaa me nne so meteɛɛm no, ogyaw n'atade wɔ me nsam, na oguan fii adi.

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: na Yosef ne wura faa no de no kɔtoo afiase, nea ɔhene nneduafo gu, na ɔdaa afiase hɔ. Onyankopɔn di n'akyi

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dii Yosef akyi, na ɔdom no, na ɔmaa n'anim baa nyam wɔ afiasehwɛfo no anim.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Na afiasehwɛfo no de nneduafo a wɔwɔ afiase hɔ nyinaa hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na biribiara a wɔyɛ wɔ hɔ no, ɔno na ɔyɛ.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Afiasehwɛfo no anhaw ne ho anhwɛ biribiara a ɔde hyɛɛ Yosef nsa no, efisɛ AWURADE dii n'akyi, na nea ɔyɛe nyinaa, AWURADE ma ɛyɛɛ yiye.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔde wɔn koguu afiase wɔ ankɔbeafo so panyin no fi, faako a Yosef da hɔ.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Na ankɔbeafo so panyin no maa Yosef hwɛɛ wɔn so som wɔn; na wɔkyɛɛ afiase hɔ kakra.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Na Misraim hene nsahyɛfo ne n'abodootofo a wogu afiase hɔ no baanu nyinaa sosoo adae anadwo koro, ɛsono oyi ne ne dae asekyerɛ, na ɛsono oyi nso de.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Na Yosef kɔɔ wɔn nkyɛn anɔpa kɔhwɛɛ wɔn, na hwɛ, wɔayeyɛ bosobosoo.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛasoso adae, nso obiara nni hɔ a ɔbɛkyerɛ yɛn ase. Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: So nkyerɛase no mfi Nyankopɔn hɔ anaa? Monka nkyerɛ me ɛ!

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Ɛnna nsahyɛfo so panyin no kaa ne dae kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me dae mu no, na hwɛ, obobe bi si m'anim,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: na obobe no abɔ nkorabata abiɛsa, na ayɛ sɛ ɛrefefɛw, na anyin agu nhwiren, na abɔ akasiaw ayɛ aba a abere.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Na Farao kuruwa kura me na metetew bobe aba no mikyi miguu Farao kuruwa no mu, na mede kuruwa no mehyɛɛ Farao nsa.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ne nkyerɛase ni: Nkorabata abiɛsa no yɛ nnansa;

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: na aka nnansa na Farao ayi wo de wo asan akodi wo dibea bio, na wode Farao kuruwa ahyɛ ne nsa sɛ kan a woyɛ ne nsahyɛfo no.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ ɛyɛ a, kae me, na sɛ esi wo yiye a, yɛ me adɔe, na bɔ me din kyerɛ Farao, na beyi me ɔdan yi mu,

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: efisɛ owia na wowiaa me Hebrifo asase so, na ɛha nso menyɛɛ hwee a anka ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde me bɛto amoa yi mu.

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Na abodootofo so panyin no hui sɛ nkyerɛase no ye no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me nso, me dae mu no, na hwɛ, aboodoo nkyerɛnkyɛ abiɛsa a esisi so wɔ m'atifi.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Na kyerɛnkyɛ a edi soro no mu, na Farao anom atoduan nyinaa bi wɔ; na nnomaa redi wɔ kyerɛnkyɛ no mu wɔ m'atifi.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef buae sɛ: Ne nkyerɛase ni: Nkyerɛnkyɛ abiɛsa no yɛ nnansa;

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: na aka nnansa na Farao ayi wo afi ha, na wasɛn wo dua ho ma nnomaa adi wo nam afi wo ho.

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so abiɛsa a ɛyɛ Farao awoda no, ɔtow ne nkoa nyinaa pon, na oyii nsahyɛfo so panyin ne abodootofo so panyin no de wɔn baa ne nkoa anim;

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: na ɔsan de nsahyɛfo so panyin no sii ne nsahyɛ so bio a ɔde kuruwa hyɛ Farao nsa.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Na abodootofo so panyin no de, ɔsɛn no, sɛnea Yosef kyerɛɛ wɔn ase no.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Nanso nsahyɛfo so panyin no ankae Yosef, na ne werɛ fii no.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na mfirihyia abien akyi no, Farao soo dae, na hwɛ, ogyina asubɔnten Nil no ho.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwibere ason a wɔn ho yɛ fɛ na wɔn ho tua wɔn ho fi asubɔnten no mu bae bedidii sare no so.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Na ɔdae, na ɔsoo dae bio, na hwɛ, awi mmɛtem ason a ɛtoatoa so na eye refifi wɔ nan koro so.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mmɛtem ason nkorowankorowa a apuei mframa akisa no fifi dii akyiri bae.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Na mmɛtem nkorowankorowa no memmenee mmɛtem ason a ɛtoatoa so na awi wɔ mu no. Na Farao nyanee, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ dae.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa no ne ho hiahiaa no, na ɔsoma kɔfrɛfrɛɛ Misraim kyerɛwfo nyinaa ne ɛhɔ anyansafo nyinaa, na Farao kaa ne dae no kyerɛɛ wɔn, nanso obiara antumi ankyerɛ Farao dae no ase.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Ɛnna nsahyɛfo mu panyin no ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Mekae me mfomso nnɛ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Farao bo fuw ne nkoa, na ɔde me ne abodootofo so panyin no, kɔtoo duam ankɔbeafo so panyin fi no,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: yɛsosoo adae anadwo koro no ara, me ne no, ɛsonsono yɛn dae a yɛsosoe ne emu biara nkyerɛase.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Na Hebrini aberante bi a ɔyɛ ankɔbeafo so panyin no akoa ne yɛn na ɛwɔ hɔ, na yɛkeka kyerɛɛ no, na ɔkyerɛɛ yɛn, yɛn adae no ase, sɛnea ebiara te.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Na sɛnea ɔkyerɛɛ yɛn ase no, saa ara na ɛbae; wɔde me san kodii me dibea, na ɔno de, wɔsɛn no.

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Na Farao soma ma wɔkɔfrɛɛ Yosef na wɔyɛɛ ntɛm yii no fii afiase hɔ, na woyii ne tinwin sakraa ne ntade, na ɔbaa Farao anim.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Maso dae, nso obiara nni hɔ a otumi kyerɛ ase; na wo na mate wo nka sɛ, wote dae a, wutumi kyerɛ ase.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef buaa Farao sɛ: Enni me fam, na mmom Onyankopɔn na ɔmfa mmuae pa mma Farao.

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Me dae mu no, hwɛ, migyina asubɔnten Nil no kɔn so.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwi ason a wɔn ho tua wɔn ho na wɔn ho yɛ fɛ fi nsu no mu bae bedidii wɔ wuram hɔ.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, anantwi ason foforo nso a wɔyɛ kanyankanyan na wɔn ho yɛ tan yiye, na wɔafomfɔn a minhuu wɔn ho tan no so bi wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so da, dii wɔn akyi bae.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Na woduu wɔn yafunu mu no, obi anhu sɛ wɔadu wɔn yafunu mu, na wɔn ho da so yɛ tan sɛ kan no ara. Ɛnna minyanee.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Na mihui wɔ me dae mu sɛ awi mmɛtem ason a ɛtoatoa so na eye refifi nan koro so.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mmɛtem ason a ahow na ayɛ ntraantraa, na apuei mframa ama akisa dii akyiri fifii.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Na mmɛtem ntraantraa no memmenee mmɛtem ason a eye no. Na maka makyerɛ nkonyaayifo no, nso obiara antumi ankyerɛ me ase.

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Farao adae no yɛ biako; Onyankopɔn rekyerɛ Farao nea ɔrebɛyɛ.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Anantwi pa ason no yɛ mfe asɔn, na mmɛtem ason a eye no nso yɛ mfe asɔn; ɛyɛ dae biako.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Na anantwi ason a wɔafomfɔn a wɔn ho yɛ tan a wodii wɔn akyi bae no ne mmɛtem ason afuruntum a apuei mframa akisa no bɛyɛ mfirihyia ason kɔm.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Ɛne asɛm a maka makyerɛ Farao: Nea Onyankopɔn rebɛyɛ na ɔde akyerɛ Farao yi:

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mfirihyia ason reba a aduan bebree bɛba Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, ɔkɔm bɛba mfirihyia ason ama werɛ afi aduan bebrebe no nyinaa wɔ Misraim asase so, na ɔkɔm no bɛhyew asase no,

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: na ɔkɔm a ebedi akyiri no nti wɔrenhu asase no so aduan bebrebe no bio, efisɛ ɔkɔm no mu bɛyɛ dennennen.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Na dae no a ɛyɛɛ mmɔho abien maa Farao no ase ne sɛ: Onyankopɔn ahyɛ saa ade no ampa, na Onyankopɔn rebɛyɛ no ntɛmntɛm.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Na afei Farao nhwehwɛ onipa a ɔyɛ ɔbadwemma ne onyansafo mfa no nsi Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Na Farao nyɛ eyi, na onsisi asase no so ahwɛfo, na wonnyigye Misraim asase so aduan so ntotoso anum anum mfirihyia ason a aduan bebree wɔ mu no mu.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Na ma wɔmmoaboa mfirihyia pa a ɛrebɛba yi mu aduan nyinaa ano, na wɔmfa awi ngugu asan so sɛnea Farao bɛhyɛ, na ɛnyɛ nkurow mu aduan, na wɔmfa nsie.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Na ayɛ aduan a wɔakora ama asase no asie mfirihyia ason kɔm a ɛbɛba Misraim asase so no, na asase no ansɛe wɔ ɔkɔm no mu. Yosef anuonyamhyɛ

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Na asɛm no sɔɔ Farao ne ne nkoa nyinaa ani.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Yebetumi anya onipa bi a ɔte sɛ oyi a Onyankopɔn honhom wɔ ne mu yi anaa?

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Sɛ Onyankopɔn ayi eyi nyinaa akyerɛ wo yi, obiara nni hɔ a ɔyɛ ɔbadwemma ne onyansafo sɛ wo.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Wubedi me fi so, na w'anom asɛm so na me man nyinaa bedi, gye ahengua nko so na mɛsen wo.

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Hwɛ, mede wo masi, Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Na Farao yii nsɔanokaa fii ne nsa de hyɛɛ Yosef nsa, na ɔhyɛɛ no sedaa nnwira atade, na ɔde sika ntweaban guu ne kɔn mu,

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: na ɔma ɔtenaa ne teaseɛnam a ɛto so abien mu, na wɔteɛɛm dii n'anim sɛ: Mommɔ mo mu ase! Na ɔde no sii Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Yosef sɛ: Mene Farao, na obiara renkwati wo nyɛ bribiara wɔ Misraim asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Farao frɛɛ Yosef sɛ Safnat-panea. Na ɔde On sɔfo Potifera babea Asnat maa no aware. Na Yosef fii adi kokyinii Misraim asase so.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Na ahotɔ mfirihyia ason no mu no, aduan pii baa asase no so ma ebuu so.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Na ɔboaboaa ahotɔ mfirihyia ason a ɛbaa Misraim asase so no mu aduan nyinaa ano, na ɔde aduan no siee nkurow no mu; nkuraa a atwa ho ahyia mu aduan na ɔde siee nkurow no mu.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Na Yosef boaboaa awi ano pii pa ara sɛ mpoano anwea de kosii sɛ wogyaee kan, efisɛ wontumi nkan.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Na wɔwoo mma baanu maa Yosef ansa na ɔkɔm mfirihyia no dui; wɔn na On sɔfo Potifera ba Asnat wo maa no.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef too abakan no din Manase, efisɛ ose: Onyankopɔn ama me werɛ afi m'amane ne m'agya fi nyinaa.

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoo nea ɔto so abien no din Efraim, efisɛ ose: Onyankopɔn ama madɔ wɔ m'amanehunu asase yi so.

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Na mmoroso a ɛbaa Misraim asase so mfirihyia ason no to twae.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔm mfirihyia ason no fii ase bae, sɛnea Yosef kae no, na ɔkɔm baa nsaase nyinaa so. Na Misraim asase nyinaa so de, na aduan wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔm kaa Misraim asase nyinaa no, ɔman no kosuu kɔm kyerɛɛ Farao. Na Farao ka kyerɛɛ Misraim nyinaa sɛ: Monkɔ Yosef nkyɛn, nea ɔbɛka akyerɛ mo no, monyɛ.

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔm no baa asase no so nyinaa. Na Yosef buebuee aduankora adan no nyinaa, na ɔtɔn aburow maa Misraimfo no, na ɔkɔm no mu yɛɛ den Misraim asase so.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Na aman nyinaa baa Misraim bɛtɔɔ aduan wɔ Yosef nkyɛn, efisɛ ɔkɔm no mu yɛɛ den wɔ asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Na Yakob tee sɛ aduan wɔ Misraim no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne mmammarima no sɛ ɛdɛn na mohwehwɛ mo ho anim yi?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Monhwɛ, mate sɛ aduan wɔ Misraim. Munsian nkɔ hɔ nkɔtɔ bi wɔ hɔ mmrɛ yɛn, na yɛntena ase, na yɛanwu.

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosef nuanom mu du sian kɔɔ Misraim aduantɔ.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Na Yosef nua Benyamin de, Yakob ansoma no anka ne nuanom no ho ankɔ, na ose: Ebia abew bi bɛbew no.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Na Israel mma no de wɔn ho fraa wɔn a wɔbaa aduantɔ no mu, efisɛ ɔkɔm no aba Kanaan asase so bi.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Na Yosef ne asase no so tumfo, ɔne nea ɔtɔn aduan ma asase no sofo nyinaa. Na Yosef nuanom bae bɛkotow no de wɔn anim butubutuw fam.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef kaee adae a ɔsosoe wɔn ho no; na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moyɛ akwansrafo, asase yi ho akwan na morebɛhwehwɛ.

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dabi, me wura, na aduantɔ na wo nkoa bae.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Yɛn nyinaa yɛ ɔbarima biako mma, yɛyɛ anokwafo, wo nkoa nyɛ akwansrafo.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Dabi, na asase yi ho akwan na moreba abɛhwehwɛ.

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna wose: Wo nkoa yɛ anuanom dumien. Yɛyɛ ɔbarima biako mma wɔ Kanaan asase so, na hwɛ, ɔkaakyire no wɔ yɛn agya nkyɛn nnɛ, na obiako de, onni hɔ.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Eyi na mede mɛsɔ mo ahwɛ: Sɛ Farao te ase yi, moremfi ha nkɔ gye sɛ mo nua kumaa no ba ha ansa.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Monsoma mo mu biako, na ɔnkɔfa mo nua no mmra, na mo de, wɔmfa mungu afiase, na wɔnhwehwɛ mo nsɛm no mu, sɛ nokware wɔ mu anaa; anyɛ saa de a, sɛ Farao te ase yi, moyɛ akwansrafo.

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Na ɔde wɔn koguu afiase nnansa.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so abiɛsa no, Yosef ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monyɛ eyi, na montena ase, na me de, misuro Onyankopɔn.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Sɛ moyɛ anokwafo a, momma wɔnkyere mo nuanom yi mu biako ntena mo nnedua fi ha, na mo de, ɔkɔm a ɛwɔ mo afi mu nti, momfa aduan no nkɔ.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Na momfa mo nua kumaa no mmrɛ me, na mo nsɛm ayɛ nokware, na moanwu. Na wɔyɛɛ sa.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Na wosisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ampa ara, yedi yɛn nua no ho fɔ, sɛ yehuu ne ahohiahia, na ɔsrɛɛ yɛn mmɔborohunu, na yɛantie; enti na saa ɔhaw yi aba yɛn so.

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Na Ruben buaa wɔn sɛ: Manka mankyerɛ mo sɛ: Monnyɛ abofra no bɔne bi, na moantie? Na hwɛ, ne mogya na wɔrehwehwɛ yi.

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Na wonnim sɛ, Yosef te, efisɛ ɔkyeame na odi wɔn ntam yi wɔn ano.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Na ɔdan ne ho fii wɔn nkyɛn kosui. Na ɔsan baa wɔn nkyɛn bio ne wɔn bɛkasae, na oyii Simeon wɔ wɔn mu, na ɔkyekyeree no wɔn anim hɔ ara.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosef hyɛɛ sɛ, wɔmfa aburow nhyehyɛ wɔn nkotoku no mama, na wɔnnan wɔn mu biara dwetɛ nhyɛ mu, na wɔmma wɔn akwansoduan. Na wɔyɛɛ wɔn sa.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Na wɔde wɔn aburow no soasoaa wɔn mfurum, na wofii hɔ kɔe.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Na wɔn mu biako buee ne kotoku ano sɛ ɔrema n'afurum aduan wɔ asoɛe no, ohui, na hwɛ, ne dwetɛ hyɛ ne kotoku ano.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nuanom sɛ: Wɔadan me dwetɛ no ama me, na hwɛ, ɛhyɛ me kotoku no mu. Na wɔn koma tutui, na wɔde ahopopo sisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Dɛn na Onyankopɔn ayɛ yɛn yi?

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa wɔn agya Yakob nkyɛn Kanaan asase so, na wɔkaa nea ɛyɛɛ wɔn nyinaa kyerɛɛ no sɛ:

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: Ɔbarima a ɔyɛ asase no wura no, poopoo n'ani kasa kyerɛɛ yɛn, na obuu yɛn asase no akwansrafo.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Na yesee no sɛ: Yɛyɛ anokwafo, yɛnyɛ akwansrafo.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Yɛyɛ yɛn agya mma anuanom dumien, obiako na onni hɔ, na akumaa no wɔ yɛn agya nkyɛn wɔ Kanaan asase so mprempren.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima a ɔyɛ asase no wura no ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Eyi na mede mehu sɛ moyɛ anokwafo: Munnyaw mo nua biako wɔ me nkyɛn, na momfa aduan nkɔ nkɔhwɛ mo fifo,

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: na momfa mo nua kumaa no mmrɛ me, na mahu sɛ monyɛ akwansrafo, na moyɛ anokwafo, na mayi mo nua no mama mo, na moadi asase yi so gua.

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Na ɛbae sɛ wɔreyiyi wɔn nkotoku mu ade no, na hwɛ, wɔn mu biara dwetɛboaa hyɛ ne kotoku mu. Na wɔne wɔn agya huu wɔn dwetɛmmoaa no, wosuroe.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Na wɔn agya Yakob ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moagye me nsam mma: Yosef nni hɔ, Simeon nni hɔ, na morebɛfa Benyamin nso akɔ. Me so na eyi nyinaa ba!

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Na Ruben ka kyerɛɛ n'agya sɛ: Sɛ mamfa no mansan mammrɛ wo a, kum me mmammarima baanu. Fa no hyɛ me nsa, na mede no mɛsan mabrɛ wo.

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Me ba ne mo renkɔ, efisɛ ne nua awu, na aka ne nko, na sɛ abew bi kɔbew no wɔ ɔkwan a morekɔ no mu a, ɛnne mode me dwen bɛkɔ asaman awerɛhow mu.

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔm no mu yɛɛ den wɔ asase no so.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Na wowiee aduan a wɔde fi Misraim bae no di no, wɔn agya ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monsan nkɔtɔ aduan kakra mmrɛ yɛn.

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Na sɛ woremma ɔnkɔ a, ɛnne yɛrensian nkɔ hɔ, efisɛ ɔbarima no ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Sɛ mo nua no nka mo ho a, munnsi m'anim ha.

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Na Israel se: Ɛdɛn nti na moyɛɛ me bɔne sɛɛ, sɛ moka kyerɛɛ ɔbarima no sɛ mowɔ onua bi?

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Na wose: Obisa na ɔbarima no bisaa yɛn, yɛn ne yɛn abusua ho asɛm sɛ: Mo agya da so te ase anaa? Mowɔ onua bi anaa? Nea obisaa yɛn yi ara na yebuae. So yenim sɛ ɔbɛka akyerɛ yɛn sɛ: Momfa mo nua no mmra anaa?

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Na Yuda ka kyerɛɛ n'agya Israel sɛ: Ma abofra no ne me nkɔ, na yensim nkɔ, na yɛne wo ne yɛn mma atena ase, na yɛanwu.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Midi ne ho agyinam; me nsam na hwehwɛ no. Sɛ mamfa no mammrɛ wo, mammegyina w'anim a, ɛnne mayɛ wo bɔne daa nyinaa.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Sɛ yɛantwentwɛn yɛn nan ase a, anka sesɛɛ yɛakɔ aba mprenu.

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Na wɔn agya Israel ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ ɛte saa a, ɛnne monyɛ eyi: Momfa asase yi so nnepa ngu mo ade mu, na momfa ayɛyɛde nkɔma ɔbarima no: akyenkyennuru kakra ne ɛwo kakra, ohuam ne kurobow, nkate ne ɔsonkoran aba.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Na momfa dwetɛ foforo nkura, ne dwetɛ a wɔdan maa mo wɔ mo kotoku ano no, munkura nsan nkɔ; ebia ɛyɛ anifaso.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Na momfa mo nua no, na munsim nsan nkɔ ɔbarima no nkyɛn.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn Tweaduampɔn mma ɔbarima no nhu mo mmɔbɔ, na onnyaa mo nua no ne Benyamin mma mo. Na me de, me mma fi me nsa a, na wɔafi me nsa!

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Na mmarima no faa ayɛyɛde no, na wɔfaa dwetɛ mmɔho kurae ne Benyamin, na wɔsɔre sian kɔɔ Misraim kogyinaa Yosef anim.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef huu Benyamin sɛ ɔka wɔn ho no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne fie panyin sɛ: Fa nnipa yi kɔ fie, na kum mmoa siesie nnuan, na nnipa yi ne me rebedidi awia yi.

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no yɛe sɛnea Yosef kae no, na ɔbarima no de nnipa no kɔɔ Yosef fi.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na nnipa no suroe sɛ wɔde wɔn akɔ Yosef fi, na wose: Dwetɛ a ɛsan kekaa yɛn kotoku mu kan no nti na wɔde yɛn aba ha yi, na wabɛtoa yɛn atow ahyɛ yɛn so afa yɛn ne yɛn mfurum ayɛ nkoa.

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Na wotwiw bɛn Yosef fie panyin no ne no kasae wɔ ofi no pon ano

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: sɛ Owura, yɛpa wo kyɛw, yesian baa ha kan bɛtɔɔ aduan.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Na yekoduu asoɛe na yɛsansan yɛn nkotoku ano no, na hwɛ, yɛn nyinaa dwetɛ hyehyɛ yɛn nkotoku mu, yɛn dwetɛ sɛnea wɔkarii no pɛ, na yekurae de asan aba.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Yekura dwetɛ foforo aba de rebɛtɔ aduan. Yennim onii ko a ɔde yɛn dwetɛ no hyehyɛɛ yɛn nkotoku no mu.

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Na ose: Asomdwoe nka mo, munnsuro. Mo Nyankopɔn ne mo agya Nyankopɔn ama mo, mo nkotoku mu ademmude, mo dwetɛ no kaa me nsa. Na oyii Simeon brɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no de nnipa no hyɛn Yosef fi, na ɔmaa wɔn nsu hohoroo wɔn anan ho, na ɔmaa wɔn mfurum aduan.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Na wosiesiee ayɛyɛde no twɛn ɔba a Yosef bɛba owigyinae no, efisɛ na wɔate sɛ wɔrebedidi hɔ.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Na Yosef baa fie no, wɔde ayɛyɛde a wokurae no kɔɔ ɔdan mu kɔmaa no, na wɔkotow fam wɔ n'anim.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Na obisaa wɔn sɛ, wɔn ho ye anaa; na ose: Mo agya akwakoraa a mokaa ne ho asɛm no ho ye anaa? Ɔda so te ase anaa?

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Na wose: W'akoa, yɛn agya no ho ye, na ɔda so te ase. Na wɔbobɔɔ wɔn mu ase kotow no.
