translation_verse: Na wɔnka wo ho, na wonkura ahyiae ntamadan no ho adwuma no mu nyɛ ntamadan no ho adwuma nyinaa, na onipa foforo biara ammɛn mo.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Na monhwɛ kronkronbea no ho nnwuma ne afɔremuka no ho nnwuma no, na abufuhyew bi amma Israelfo so bio.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Na me de, hwɛ, mafa mo nuanom Lewifo afi Israelfo mu mama mo sɛ akyɛde a wɔde ama AWURADE, sɛ wɔnyɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ho som adwuma no.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na wo ne wo mma a wɔka wo ho no nhwɛ mo asɔfodi no, afɔremuka no ho nsɛm nyinaa mu, ne ntwamu mmɔhɔɔ no mu de no mu mfa nsom: mede mo asɔfodi no mama mo sɛ akyɛde som adwuma; na obi foforo biara a ɔbɛn no, wonkum no.

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nam nyɛ wo de sɛ ohim yan ne srɛ nifa no yɛ wo de no.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Akronkronne mu ade kronkron a efi ogya no mu no mu nea ɛnyɛ wo de ni: wɔn ayɛyɛde biara a wɔde ba, wɔn aduan afɔre biara, ne wɔn bɔne ho afɔre biara ne wɔn asodi ho afɔre biara a wɔde brɛ me no nyɛ akronkronne mu ade kronkron mma wo ne wo mma.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Di no faako a ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron pa ara, mmarima nyinaa nni bi, ɔnyɛ wo ade kronkron.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Na eyi nso nyɛ wo de: wɔn ayɛyɛde mu soma ade, Israelfo him afɔre nyinaa; wɔde ama wo ne wo mmammarima ne wo mmabea a wɔka wo ho sɛ daa kyɛfa; obiara a ne ho tew, wo fi mu, nni bi.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Ngo foforo mu nea eye koraa no nyinaa ne nsa foforo ne awi mu nea eye koraa no nyinaa, emu adekan a wɔde ma AWURADE no, wo na wɔde ama wo.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Wɔn asase so ade nyinaa mu adekan a wɔde brɛ AWURADE no, ɛnyɛ wo de; obiara a ne ho tew wɔ wo fi nni bi.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Ade biara a ebue yafunu ano ɔhonam nyinaa mu a wɔde brɛ AWURADE no, onipa oo, afieboa oo, ɛnyɛ wo de; nnipa mmakan, ne afieboa a wɔn ho ntew mmakan nso wonhyɛ wɔn anan mu.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Na ananmuhyɛde no de, nea wadi ɔsram no, ma wonnye no dwetɛ nnwetɛbona anum a wobɛhyɛ ama wɔn, sɛ kronkronbea dwetɛbona a ano si gera aduonu no te.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Na nantwi abakan anaa oguanten abakan anaa abirekyi abakan de, mma wonnnye: wɔyɛ kronkron; fa wɔn mogya pete afɔremuka no so na hyew wɔn srade ma ɛnyɛ ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam ma AWURADE.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Akronkronne mu soma ade a Israelfo de brɛ AWURADE nyinaa, mede mama wo ne wo mmammarima ne wo mmabea a wɔka wo ho no sɛ daa kyɛfa; ɔnyɛ AWURADE anim daa nkyene apam mma wo ne w'asefo a wɔka wo ho no.

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Aaron sɛ: Wɔn asase no bi na worenni, na worennya kyɛfa bi wɔn mu: Mene wo kyɛfa ne w'agyapade Israelfo mu.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na Lewifo no de, wɔn som a wɔsom ahyiae ntamadan no mu nti, hwɛ, mede Israel mu ntotoso du du nyinaa mama wɔn sɛ agyapade.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: na Lewifo no de, wɔn na wɔnyɛ ahyiae ntamadan no ho som adwuma, na, wɔnsoa ɛho mmusu: ɛyɛ daa ahyɛde, mo awo ntoatoaso nyinaa mu; na Israelfo mu de, wɔrennya agyapade bi.

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: Na Israelfo ntotoso du du a wɔmoma no yɛ soma ade ma AWURADE no, mede mama Lewifo no sɛ agyapade; ɛno nti na maka wɔn ho sɛ wɔrennya agyapade bi Israelfo mu no.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: Lewifo de, kasa kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ mugyigye Israelfo hɔ ntotoso du du a mede mama mo fi wɔn nkyɛn sɛ mo agyapade no a, ɛnne momma emu bi so nyɛ AWURADE soma ade, ntotoso du du no mu ntoso du.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Na wommu mo soma ade mma mo sɛ awiporowbea awi ne nsa-kyi-amoa mu adenya.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Ade a wɔbɛma mo nyinaa mu na momma AWURADE soma ade nyinaa, emu nea eye koraa no nyinaa mu akronkronne.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Morema emu nea eye koraa no so a, wommu nea aka no mma Lewifo sɛ awiporowbea nnɔbae ne nsa-kyi-amoa mu adenya.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na munni no baabiara, mo ne mo fifo, na ɛyɛ mo ahyiae ntamadan ho som adwuma so akatua.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: Eyi ne mmara mu ahyɛde a AWURADE ahyɛ sɛ: Kasa kyerɛ Israelfo sɛ wɔmfa nantwibere kɔkɔɔ a odi mu a onni dɛm a kɔndua nkɔɔ no so pɛn mmrɛ wo;

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: na momfa no mma ɔsɔfo Eleasar, na ɔmfa no mfi nkɔ nsra no akyi, na wonkum no n'anim.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Eleasar mfa ne nsatea nka ne mogya no bi, na ɔmpete ne mogya no bi ngu ahyiae ntamadan no anim fam mpɛn asɔn.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Na wɔnhyew nantwibere no wɔ n'anim, ne ne nhoma ne nam, ne mogya, ne ne n'agyanan no nyinaa no wɔnhyew.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo no mfa kyeneduru ne adwerɛ ne kuntu mfuturu kɔkɔɔ ngu nantwibere a ɔrehyew no so.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo no nhoro ne ntade na ɔmfa nsu nguare, na ɛno akyi ansa na ɔmmra nsra no mu; na ɔsɔfo no ho ntew kosi anwummere.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Na nea ɔhyewee no nhoro ne ntade nsu mu, na ɔmfa nsu nguare, na ne ho ntew kosi anwummere.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi a ne ho tew nsesaw nantwibere no nso no mfa nkogu nsra no akyi baabi a ɛhɔ tew, na ɛnyɛ Israelfo asafo no ahodwira nsu nsie; ɛyɛ bɔne ho afɔre.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na nea ɔsesaw nantwibere no nso no nhoro ne ntade, na ne ho ntew kosi anwummere. Na ɛnyɛ daa ahyɛde mma Israelfo ne ɔhɔho a ɔsoɛ wɔn mu.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Nea ɔka onipa biara funu no, ne ho ntew nnansɔn;

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: ɔno na ɔmfa eyi nnwira ne ho mfi ne bɔne mu da a ɛto so abiɛsa ne da a ɛto so ason no, na ne ho atew; na sɛ wannwira ne ho da a ɛto so abiɛsa ne da a ɛto so ason no a, ne ho rentew.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔka owufo, onipa bi a wawu funu, na wannwira ne ho no agu AWURADE tenabea ho fi, na wontwa saa ɔkra no mfi Israel mu nkyene, efisɛ wɔampete ahodwira nsu a wampete angu no so nti, ne ho ntew, ne ho fi da so wɔ ne ho.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Eyi ne mmara a ɛwɔ hɔ ma bere a obi awu wɔ ntamadan mu: Sɛ onipa wu ntamadan mu a, obiara a ɔba ntamadan no mu ne ade biara a ɛwɔ ntamadan no mu ho ntew nnansɔn;

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Na obiara a ɔka nea watɔ nkrante ano anaa funu bi anaa onipa nnompe anaa ɔda bi wuram no, ne ho ntew nnansɔn.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: na ɔbarima bi a ne ho tew mfa adwerɛ mmɔ nsu no mu, na ɔmpete ngu ntamadan no ne emu nneɛma nyinaa ne akra a wɔwɔ hɔ no ne nea waka dompe anaa ɔtɔfo anaa funu anaa ɔda bi no so.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Na nea ne ho tew no mpete ngu nea ne ho ntew no so, da a ɛto so abiɛsa ne da a ɛto so ason no, na onnwira ne ho da a ɛto so ason no, na ɔnhoro ne ntade, na ɔmfa nsu nguare, na ne ho atew anwummere.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Na onipa a ne ho ntew na wannwira ne ho no, wobetwa saa ɔkra no afi ɔman asafo no mu, efisɛ wagu AWURADE kronkronbea no ho fi; wɔampete ahodwira nsu no angu no so, enti ne ho ntew.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Na eyi nyɛ wɔn daa ahyɛde. Na nea ɔpetee ahodwira nsu no nhoro ne ntade; na nea ɔka ahodwira nsu no ho ntew kosi anwummere;

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: na ade biara a nea ne ho ntew no ka no ho ntew, na obiara a ɔka no no ho ntew kosi anwummere.

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo mu no nyinaa baa Sin sare so, ɔsram a edi kan no mu, na ɔman no tenaa Kades; na Miriam wui wɔ hɔ, na wosiee no hɔ ara.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Nso na nsu nni hɔ mma asafo no, na wohyia tiaa Mose ne Aaron.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no ne Mose hamee, na wɔkae sɛ: Ɛkaa yɛn nko a, anka yɛn nuanom wuwui AWURADE anim no, yewuwui bi.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn nti na mode AWURADE man asafo aba sare yi so sɛ yemmewuwu wɔ ha, yɛn ne yɛn mmoa yi?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn nti na muyii yɛn Misraim sɛ mode yɛn reba nea enye yi, nea wontumi nnua hwee a borɔdɔma ne bobe ne ateaa nni, na nsu po a wɔnom nni yi?

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Na Mose ne Aaron fii asafo no anim baa ahyiae ntamadan no ano, na wɔde wɔn anim butubutuw fam; na AWURADE anuonyam yii ne ho kyerɛɛ wɔn.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: Fa poma no na boa asafo no ano, wo ne wo nua Aaron, na monhyɛ ɔbotan no wɔn anim, sɛ ɔmma ne nsu, na yi ɔbotan no mu nsu ma wɔn, ne wɔn asafo ne wɔn mmoa nnom.

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na Mose faa poma no fii AWURADE anim, sɛnea ɔhyɛɛ no no;

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: na Mose ne Aaron boaboaa ɔman asafo no ano ɔbotan no anim, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ Muntie ɛ, mo atuatewfo, so yenyi nsu mfi ɔbotan yi mu mma mo?

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Na Mose maa ne nsa so de ne poma no bɔɔ ɔbotan no mpɛn abien, na nsu pii fii mu bae, na asafo no ne wɔn mmoa nomee.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron sɛ: Sɛ moannye me anni, na moanyɛ me kronkron, Israelfo anim nti, moremfa ɔman asafo yi nnu asase a mede mama wɔn no so.

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Na Mose somaa abɔfo fi Kades kɔɔ Edom hene nkyɛn sɛ: Sɛ wo nua Israel se ni: Wo ara wunim ɔhaw a ɛtoo yɛn nyinaa,

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: sɛ yɛn agyanom sian kɔɔ Misraim, na yɛtenaa Misraim nna bebree, na Misraimfo yɛɛ yɛn ne yɛn agyanom bɔne;

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: na yesu frɛɛ AWURADE, na ɔtee yɛn nne, na ɔsomaa ɔbɔfo beyii yɛn fii Misraim; na hwɛ, yɛwɔ Kades, kurow a ɛwɔ wo hye so mu.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Ma yɛmfa w'asase so; yɛremfa mfuw ne nturo mu, nanso yɛrennom mmura mu nsu bi; yɛbɛnantew ɔhene tempɔn so akɔ, yɛremman nifa anaa benkum de bɛkɔ akosi sɛ yebetwam w'asase so.

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Na Edom ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mmɛfa me ha, na mamfa nkrante mamfi adi mammehyia wo.

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: ɔtempɔn so na yɛrebɛfa, na sɛ yɛn ne yɛn mmoa nom wo nsu bi a, yebetua ka; ɛnyɛ asɛm bi, na me nan nko na ma memfa mintwam.

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Na ose: Mommetwam! Na Edom de dɔm pii ne nsa a emu yɛ den fii adi behyiaa wɔn.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Na Edom kamee Israel kwan a ɔde betwam n'asase so. Enti Israel man fii ne ho.

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo mu no nyinaa tu fii Kades, na wɔbaa Hor bepɔw ho.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: Aka kakraa bi na Aaron atiw ne mpanyimfo, na ɔrenkɔ asase a mede merema Israelfo no so, efisɛ moyɛɛ asoɔden maa m'anom asɛm, Meriba asu ho.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Fa Aaron ne ne ba Eleasar, na wo ne wɔn mforo Hor bepɔw,

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: na yi Aaron ntade no fa hyɛ ne ba Eleasar, onwu wɔ hɔ na ontiw ne mpanyimfo wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Na Mose yɛɛ sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no, na wɔforoo Hor bepɔw, asafo no nyinaa anim.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Na Mose yiyii Aaron ntade no de hyɛɛ ne ba Eleasar, na Aaron wui ɛhɔ wɔ bepɔw no atifi. Na Mose ne Eleasar fii bepɔw no so sianee.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Na asafo no nyinaa hui sɛ Aaron awu no, na Israel fi nyinaa suu no adaduasa.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Na wotu fii Hor bepɔw ho faa mmɛw po kwan so sɛ wɔretwa Edom asase ho kontonkron akɔ. Na ɔman no ahome tew wɔn pii ɔkwan no so.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no kasa tiaa Onyankopɔn ne Mose sɛ ɛdɛn nti na muyii yɛn fii Misraim sɛ yemmewuwu sare so? Aduan biara nni hɔ, nsu nso nni hɔ, na aduan hunu yi afono yɛn.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE somaa awɔ a wɔn ano wɔ bɔre baa ɔman no mu bɛkekaa ɔman no, na Israel mu nnipa pii wuwui.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no baa Mose nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Yɛayɛ bɔne sɛ yɛkasa tiaa AWURADE ne wo; pa AWURADE kyɛw na ommeyi awɔ no mfi yɛn so. Na Mose paa kyɛw maa ɔman no.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Yɛ ɔwɔ a n'ano wɔ bɔre nsɛso, na fa no sɛn frankaa dua so; na obiara a ebi aka no no, sɛ ɔhwɛ a, obenya nkwa.

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Na Mose yɛɛ kɔbere wɔ no, na ɔde no sɛn frankaa dua no so; na sɛ ɔwɔ ka obi, na ɔhwɛ kɔbere wɔ no a, na wanya nkwa. Israelfo toa wɔn akwantu no so

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tu kɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ Obot.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wofi tu kɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ Sared subon mu.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wofi tu kɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ asubɔnten Arnon a ɛsen sare so a efi Amori hye so no agya, efisɛ Arnon ne ɔhye a ɛda Moab ne Amori ntam.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Enti wɔka AWURADE akodi nhoma no mu sɛ: Wɔnam ahuntu so faa Waheb ne Arnon nsubon no,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ne nea nsubon no sensen a ɛdan kɔ Ar tenabea na etweri Moab hye ho no.

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wofi kɔɔ Beer, asubura a AWURADE kaa ho asɛm kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Boa ɔman no ano na mɛma wɔn nsu anom, no.

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ɛbere no mu na Israel too dwom yi sɛ Asubura, tue! Munnye no so!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Asubura a atitiriw tui na ɔman mu mmapɔmma fumfunui, wɔde ahempoma ne wɔn mpoma. Na wofi sare so kɔɔ Matana;

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: na wofi Matana kɔɔ Nahaliel, na wofi Nahaliel kɔɔ Bamot;

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: na wofi Bamot kɔɔ obon a ɛwɔ Moab petee mu, Pisga atifi a ɛkyerɛ sare pradada so no mu. Wodi Sihon ne Og so nkonim

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: na Hesbon ne Amorifo hene Sihon kurow, ɔno na ɔne kan Moab hene koe, na ogyee ne nsam nsaase nyinaa kosii Arnon ano.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Na Israel somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Amorifo hene Sihon nkyɛn se:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: Ma memfa w'asase so; yɛremman mfuw mu ne nturo mu, yɛrennom abura mu nsu bi; ɔhene tempɔn so na yɛbɛnantew akosi sɛ yebetwam w'asase so.

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Nanso Sihon amma Israel antwam n'asase so; na ɔboaa ne man nyinaa ano fi behyiaa Israel, sare so, na ɔbaa Yahas ne Israel bɛkoe.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Na Israel kum no nkrante ano faa n'asase fi Arnon kɔɔ Yabok so koduu Amonfo ho, efisɛ Amonfo no hye so hɔ yɛ den.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Na Israel faa nkurow yi nyinaa, na Israel tenaa Amorifo nkurow no nyinaa mu, Hesbon ne ɛho nkurow nyinaa mu;

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ɛno nti na mmebufo no ka sɛ: Mommra Hesbon! Momma wɔnkyekye na wonsiesie Sihon kurow no.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Na ogya bi fii Hesbon, ogyaframa fii Sihon kuro kɛse mu; ɛhyew Moab kurow Ar, Arnon sorɔnsorɔmmea so awuranom no.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Wo Moab, due! Kemos man, moayera! Wama ne mmammarima aguanguan, na ne mmabea adan Amorifo hene Sihon nnommum.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Na yɛabɔ wɔn agu, Hesbon ayera akodu Dibon; yɛasɛe wɔn akɔfa Memfis de akodu Medeba.

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tenaa Amorifo asase so.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Na wɔdan wɔn ho foro kɔɔ Basan kwan so. Na Basan hene Og fii adi behyiaa wɔn, ɔno ne ne man nyinaa, sɛ wɔrebɛko wɔ Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Nsuro no, na mede no ne ne man nyinaa ne n'asase mahyɛ wo nsam, na woayɛ no sɛnea woyɛɛ Amorifo hene Sihon a ɔtenaa Hesbon no.

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Na wokunkum no ne ne mma ne ne man nyinaa a obiara antumi anguan, na wɔfaa asase no dii so.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tu kɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ Moab tataw so, Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko agya.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: Na Moab suroo ɔman no pii, efisɛ wɔdɔɔso, na ehu kaa Moab, Israelfo no nti.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Na Moab ka kyerɛɛ Midian mpanyimfo sɛ: Afei dɔm yi bedi yɛn ho ade nyinaa, sɛnea nantwi di asase so wura no. Saa bere no mu na Sipor ba Balak ne Moab hene.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa abɔfo kɔɔ Beor ba Bileam nkyɛn wɔ Petor a ɛda asubɔnten no ano, ne manfo asase so sɛ, wonkohyia no sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔman bi fi Misraim aba, na hwɛ, wɔabɛkata asase ani, na wɔn ara na wogu m'anim yi.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Na afei bra bɛdome ɔman no ma me, efisɛ wɔyɛ den sen me, sɛ ebia metumi makum wɔn, na mapam wɔn afi asase yi so anaa; na minim sɛ nea wuhyira no no, wɔahyira no, na nea wodome no no, wɔadome no.

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Na Moab mpanyin ne Midian mpanyin no siim kɔe, na adebisa so akatua no wɔ wɔn nsam; na wɔkɔɔ Bileam nkyɛn de Balak asɛm no kɔtoo n'anim.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Montena ha anadwo yi, na mede mmuae bɛbrɛ mo, sɛnea AWURADE bɛkasa akyerɛ me no. Na Moab asafohene no ne Bileam tenaa hɔ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Bileam nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Mmarima bɛn na wɔne wo wɔ hɔ yi?

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn sɛ: Moab hene Sipor ba Balak na ɔsoma baa me nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɔman a wofi Misraim bae no abɛkata asase ani, afei bra bɛdome wɔn ma me, sɛ ebia metumi ne wɔn ako na mapam wɔn anaa?

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Wo ne wɔn nnkɔ, nkɔdome ɔman no, efisɛ mahyira wɔn.

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam sɔree anɔpa, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Balak asafohene no sɛ: Monkɔ mo asase so, na AWURADE ampene amma me kwan sɛ me ne mo nkɔ.

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Na Moab asafohene no sɔre baa Balak nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Bileam ampene sɛ ɔne yɛn bɛba.

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Na Balak san somaa atitiriw a wɔdɔɔso na wɔn anim yɛ nyam sen kanfo no.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔɔ Bileam nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ Sipor ba Balak se ni: Afei de, mma biribi nnsiw wo me nkyɛn ba kwan,

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: na mɛhyɛ wo anuonyam pii, na biribiara a wobɛka akyerɛ me no, mɛyɛ enti bra ara, na bɛdome ɔman yi ma me.

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Na Bileam bua see Balak nkoa no sɛ: Sɛ Balak de ne fi a dwetɛ ne sika ayɛ no ma no, ma me po a, merentumi mimmu AWURADE me Nyankopɔn asɛm so menkɔyɛ biribi ketewa anaa kɛse.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Na afei mo nso montena ha anadwo yi, na minhu nea AWURADE bɛsan aka akyerɛ me.

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn baa Bileam nkyɛn anadwo bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ nhyia na mmarima yi behyiaa wo a, sɔre na wo ne wɔn nkɔ; nanso asɛm a mɛka makyerɛ wo no nko na di so. N'afurum gye no nkwa

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Ɛnna Bileam sɔree anɔpa hyehyɛɛ n'afurum na ɔne Moab atitiriw no siim kɔe.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Na ɔrekɔ no, Onyankopɔn bo fuwii, na AWURADE bɔfo begyinaa ɔkwan no so sɛ obesiw no kwan; nso na ɔte n'afurum so na ne nkoa baanu ne no na ɛnam.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Na afurum no huu AWURADE bɔfo no sɛ ogyina ɔkwan mu kura nkrante a watwe no, ɔman fii kwan no so kɔfaa wuram; na Bileam hwee afurum no sɛ ɔredan no aba ɔkwan mu.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE bɔfo no kogyinaa bobe nturo ntam anammɔnkoro kwan bi mu a ɔfasu wɔ ha ne ha.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Na afurum no huu AWURADE bɔfo no no, ɔde ne ho miaa ɔfasu no, na ɔkaa Bileam nan miaa ɔfasu no; na ɔkɔɔ so hwee no ara.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no twiw kɔɔ anim kogyinaa nea ɛhɔ yɛ hihiaa a ɔkwan nni hɔ a wɔbɛdan akɔ nifa anaa benkum.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Na afurum no huu AWURADE bɔfo no no, obutuw fam Bileam ase; na Bileam bo fuwii, na ɔde abaa bɔɔ afurum no.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE buee afurum no ano, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Dɛn na mayɛ wo na woabɔ me mpɛn abiɛsa yi?

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ afurum no sɛ: Sɛ woagoru me ho ntia! Sɛ mikura nkrante a, anka sesɛɛ makum wo.

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Na afurum no ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: So ɛnyɛ w'afurum ne me a woatena me so ara de abesi nnɛ da yi? So mayɛ wo sɛɛ pɛn? Na ose: Dabi.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE buee Bileam ani, na ohuu AWURADE bɔfo no sɛ ogyina ɔkwan mu kura nkrante a watwe, na ɔkotow de n'anim butuw fam.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wobɔɔ w'afurum no mpɛn abiɛsa yi? Hwɛ, maba sɛ merebesiw wo kwan, efisɛ wo kwan nteɛ wɔ m'anim;

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: na afurum no huu me, na ɔman fii m'anim mpɛn abiɛsa yi; sɛ wamman amfi m'anim a, anka sesɛɛ makum wo dedaw, na ɔno de, magye no nkwa.

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE bɔfo no sɛ: Mayɛ bɔne, na minnim sɛ wo na wugyina ɔkwan mu hyia me; na afei, sɛɛ yɛ bɔne w'ani so de a, mɛsan m'akyi.

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Wo ne mmarima no nkɔ; na asɛm a mɛka makyerɛ wo no nko na ka. Na Bileam ne Balak atitiriw no siim kɔe.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Na Balak tee sɛ: Bileam reba no, ofi kohyiaa no, Moab kurow a ɛda Arnon a ɛyɛ ɔhye no so no mu, wɔ nhyenoa hɔ pɛɛ.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: So ɛnyɛ ɔsoma na mesomae sɛ, wommehyia wo mmra? Ɛdɛn nti na woamma? So wugye di sɛ merentumi menhyɛ wo anuonyam?

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Hwɛ, maba wo nkyɛn afei; so metumi maka asɛm bi anaa? Asɛm a Onyankopɔn de hyɛ m'anom no, ɛno na mɛka.

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Na Bileam ne Balak kɔe, na woduu Kiriat-husot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Na Balak de anantwi ne nguan bɔɔ afɔre ma wɔde kɔmaa Bileam ne atitiriw a wɔne no wɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, Balak faa Bileam, na ɔde no foro kɔɔ Baal sorɔnsorɔmmea so; na ofi hɔ huu ɔman no ano.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Sisi afɔremuka ason ma me wɔ ha, na pɛ anantwinini ason ne adwennini ason fa brɛ me ha.

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Na Balak yɛe sɛnea Bileam ka kyerɛɛ no no; na Balak ne Bileam de nantwinini biako ne odwennini biako bobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre, afɔremuka biara so.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Kogyina wo hyew afɔre no ho, na menkɔ: ebia AWURADE behyia me, na ade ko a ɔbɛma mahu no, mɛka makyerɛ wo. Na osiim kɔɔ koko pataa bi so.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn behyiaa Bileam, na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Masisi afɔremuka asɔn, na mede nantwinini ne odwennini mabɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ afɔremuka biara so.

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de asɛm hyɛɛ Bileam anom sɛ: San kɔ Balak nkyɛn, na sɛnea kasa ne no.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Na ɔsan kɔɔ ne nkyɛn, na hwɛ, ogyina ne hyew afɔre no ho, ɔno ne Moab atitiriw nyinaa.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Na ɔkasae sɛ: Aram na Balak kɔfaa me fii, Moab hene no faa me fii apuei mmepɔw mu sɛ Bra bɛdome Yakob ma me, na bɛbɔ Israel dua.

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mɛdome nea Onyankopɔn nnomee no no, na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na mɛbɔ nea AWURADE mmɔɔ no dua no dua?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Abotan atifi na mifi mihu no, na nkoko so na mifi migyen no: Hwɛ, ɔman a ne nko bɛtena ni, na wɔremmu wɔn mfra wiase aman.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Hena na ɔbɛkan Yakob mfutuma ne Israel abupɛn anan mu biako dodow? Ma menwu teefo wu, na m'awiei nyɛ sɛ wɔn de.

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Woyɛ me dɛn ni? M'atamfo nnome nti na mekɔfaa wo bae, na hwɛ, nhyira na wuhyira wɔn.

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Na obuae sɛ: So ɛnyɛ nea AWURADE de hyɛ m'anom no na ɛsɛ sɛ mehwɛ meka? Bileam nkɔmhyɛ a ɛto so abien

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛnne bra na yɛnkɔ baabi foforo ɛ, faako a wubehu wɔn; wɔn ano nko na wubehu, na worenhu wɔn nyinaa; na dome wɔn ma me wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Na ɔde no kɔɔ Sofim sare so, Pisga bepɔw atifi, na osii afɔremuka asɔn, na ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ afɔremuka biara so.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Gyina w'afɔremuka no ho ara, na me de, merekɔ makɔhwɛ.

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE behyiaa Bileam, na ɔde asɛm hyɛɛ n'anom sɛ: San kɔ Balak nkyɛn, na sɛɛ na kasa.

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbaa ne nkyɛn, na hwɛ, ogyina ne hyew afɔre no ho, na Moab atitiriw no ne no gyinagyina hɔ; na Balak bisaa no sɛ: Dɛn na AWURADE kae?

english_verse: Balaam answered: “Pay close attention to my words—
translation_verse: Na ɔkasaa mmebu mu sɛ: Sɔre, Balak, na tie; yɛ aso ma me, Sipor ba.

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn nyɛ onipa, na wadi atoro, anaa onipa ba, na wanu ne ho. So ɔno de, ɔbɛka asɛm bi na ɔrenyɛ, anaasɛ ɔbɛkasa na ɔremma entim?

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Wanhu amumɔyɛ Yakob mu, na wanhu ɔhaw Israel mu. AWURADE Nyankopɔn di n'akyi, na ɔhene ho ahurusi wɔ no mu.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn ayi wɔn afi Misraim, n'ahoɔden te sɛ ɛkoɔ de.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Ampa ara, adebisa nni Yakob mu, na nkɔmhyɛ nni Israel mu: Afei na wɔbɛka wɔ Yakob ne Israel ho sɛ: Dɛn na Onyankopɔn ayeyi!

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɔman yi sɔre sɛ gyatabere, na ɔma ne ho so sɛ gyata: ɔremmutuw gye sɛ wadi bɔnam, na wanom atɔfo mogya ansa.

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Nnome wɔn koraa, na nhyira nso nhyira wɔn koraa.

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Na Bileam bua ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: So manka mankyerɛ wo sɛ: Biribiara a AWURADE bɛka no, ɛno na mɛyɛ? Nkɔmhyɛ a ɛto so abiɛsa

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: Bra na memfa wo menkɔ baabi foforo, ebia ɛbɛsɔ Onyankopɔn ani sɛ wobɛdome wɔn ama me wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na Balak faa Bileam kɔɔ Peor atifi a ɛhwɛ sare pradada no so no.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Na Bileam ka kyerɛɛ Balak sɛ: Sisi afɔremuka ason ma me wɔ ha, na fa anantwinini ason ne adwennini ason brɛ me ha.

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Na Balak yɛe sɛ Bileam kae no, na ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre wɔ afɔremuka biara so.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Na Bileam hui sɛ asɔ AWURADE ani sɛ ohyira Israel no, wankɔ abisa sɛ ɔkɔe kan no, na mmom ɔde n'ani kyerɛɛ sare no so.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Na Bileam maa n'ani so, na ohuu Israel sɛ wogu hɔ mmusua mmusua; na Onyankopɔn honhom baa no so,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: na ɔkasae sɛ Beor ba Bileam asɛm a wanya sɛ ɔreka, ɔbarima a n'ani hu ade yiye no asɛm a wanya,

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: nea ɔte Nyankopɔn nsɛm no na ɔreka yi, nea ohu Tweaduampɔn anisoade, na ɔrehwe ase a, wɔtew n'ani so no:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Wo ntamadan yɛ fɛ dɛn ara, Yakob, wo tenabea no, Israel!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: Ɛyerɛw sɛ asubon, sɛ asu so nturo, te sɛ pɛprɛ nnua a AWURADE atɛw, te sɛ nsu so nkyeneduru.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Ne nsusaw ade mu nsu bubu so, na n'asefo tena nsu pii mu. Ne hene so sen Agag, na wɔbɛma n'ahenni so.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn na oyii no fii Misraim, n'ahoɔden te sɛ ɛkoɔ de. Ɔbɛmene amanaman a wɔyɛ n'atamfo, na wadwerɛw wɔn nnompe, na ɔde n'agyan awowɔ wɔn.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Ɔkotow, obutuw sɛ gyata ne gyatabere, hena na ɔbɛma wasɔre? Nhyira ne wɔn a wohyira wo, na nnome ne wɔn a wɔdome wo. Balak gya no kwan

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Balak bo fuw Bileam, na ɔbɔɔ ne nsam; na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Bileam sɛ: M'atamfo nnome nti na mihyiaa wo, na hwɛ, nhyira na woahyira wɔn mpɛn abiɛsa yi?

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Na afei guan kɔ nea wufi! Mekae sɛ anka mɛhyɛ wo anuonyam, na hwɛ, AWURADE asiw w'anuonyam ho kwan.

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: Sɛ Balak de ne fi a dwetɛ ne sika ayɛ no ma ma me mpo a, merentumi mentena AWURADE asɛm mimfi me komam menkɔyɛ papa anaa bɔne; nea AWURADE bɛka no, ɛno na mɛka?

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, merekɔ me man mu: Bra na menkasa nkyerɛ wo nea ɔman yi bɛyɛ wo man nna a edi akyiri no mu.

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Na ɔkasae sɛ: Beor ba Bileam asɛm a wanya sɛ ɔreka, ɔbarima a n'ani hu ade yiye no asɛm a wanya,

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: nea ɔte Nyankopɔn nsɛm na ohu ɔsorosoroni no ho nimdeɛ no, nea ɔhwɛ Tweaduampɔn ahwɛde, na ɔrehwe ase a, wɔtew n'ani so no:

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Mihu no, nso ɛnyɛ mprempren, mehwɛ no, nso ɔmmɛn: Nsoromma bepue Yakob mu, na ahempoma befi Israel mu asɔre, na wadwerɛw Moab afanan nyinaa na wabubu ɔko huuyɛ mma no nyinaa.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛfa Edom adi so, na wafa n'atamfo asase Seir adi so, na Israel bɛyɛ ahoɔdenne ara.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Na obi a ofi Yakob mu bedi tumi, na wasɛe wɔn a wɔaka wɔ kurow no mu no.

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Afei ɔhwɛɛ Amalek toaa ne kasa no so sɛ: Amanaman mu dikanfo ne Amalek, nanso n'awiei bewie no ɔsɛe mu.

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛɛ Kenifo toaa ne kasa no so kae sɛ: Wo tenabea si hɔ pintinn, na wode wo berebuw asie ɔbotan mu;

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: nanso wobegu Kain ase, de akosi sɛ Asur bɛfa wo nnommum.

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Na ahyɛn befi Kitim fam aba, na wɔabɛbrɛ Asur ase abrɛ Eber ase; na ɔno ara nso awie no ɔsɛe mu.

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Bileam sɔree, na osiim san kɔɔ n'atenae; na Balak nso kɔɔ ne kwan.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Na Israel tenaa Sitim. Na ɔman no fii ase ne Moab mmabaa bɔɔ aguaman;

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: na wohyiahyiaa ɔman no kɔɔ wɔn anyame afɔreduan ho; na ɔman no dii na wɔsɔree wɔn anyame no;

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: na Israel de ne ho bɔɔ Baal-peor ho. Na AWURADE bo fuw Israel;

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa ɔman no mu atitiriw no nyinaa, na sensɛn wɔn ma AWURADE, owia so, na AWURADE abufuhyew no nsan mfi Israel so.

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israel atemmufo no sɛ: Munkunkum mo mmarima a wɔde wɔn ho kɔbɔɔ Baal-peor ho no.

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, ɔbarima bi fi Israelfo no mu bae a ɔde Midianni bea bi baa ne nuanom nkyɛn, Mose aniso ne Israelfo asafo no nyinaa aniso; ɛbere a wɔn de, wɔresu ahyiae ntamadan no ano.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Aaron ba Eleasar ba Pinehas hui no, ɔsɔre fii asafo no mu kɔfaa peaw kurae,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: na odii Israelni no akyi kɔɔ pia no mu, na ɔwowɔɔ wɔn baanu no, Israelni ne ɔbea no nyinaa hwirew n'ayaase; na ɔhaw no to twae fii Israelfo no so.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: Ɔsɔfo Aaron ba Eleasar ba Pinehas asianka m'abufuw afi Israelfo so, sɛ watwe me ho ninkunu wɔ wɔn mu, a enti manhyew Israelfo wɔ me ninkuntwe mu.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: na ayɛ ɔno ne n'asefo a wɔbɛba n'akyi no daa asɔfodi apam, efisɛ watwe ninkunu ama ne Nyankopɔn, na wapata ama Israelfo.

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Na Israelni a wokum no, ne Midianni bea no din ne: Simri, Salu ba a ɔyɛ Simeonfo mpanyimfi mu bapɔmma.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Na Midianni bea a wokum no no din de Kosbi, Sur a ɔyɛ Midianfo mu mpanyimfi so man panyin no ba.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: esiane sɛ wɔn nso wɔn anifere a wɔde ahiahia mo ho, na wɔde daadaa mo de kɔsom Baal-peor, ne wɔn nuabea Kosbi, Midian safohene no ba a wokum no da a Peor ho haw no bae no nti.

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Na ɔhaw no akyi no AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne ɔsɔfo Aaron ba Eleasar sɛ:

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: Monkan Israelfo asafo no nyinaa dodow mfi nea wadi mfirihyia aduonu so mfa nkɔ, sɛ wɔn mpanyimfi te, Israel mu nnipa a wotumi kɔ ɔsa nyinaa.

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yuda mma, sɛ wɔn mmusua te ni: Sela de, Selafo abusua; Peres de, Peresfo abusua; Sera de, Serafo abusua.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Na Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar ka kyerɛɛ wɔn, Moab tataw so, Yordan fa a ɛbɛn Yeriko sɛ:

translation_verse: Na Palu mma: Eliab;

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: na Eliab mma: Nemuel ne Datan ne Abiram. Eyinom ne Datan ne Abiram, asafo no mu aguasemfo a wɔne Mose ne Aaron hamee Kora asafo no mu, wɔn ham a wɔne AWURADE hamee no mu;

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Nanso Kora mma de, wɔanwuwu.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Na Aaron nso, wɔwoo Nadab ne Abihu, Eleasar ne Itamar maa no;

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: Eyinom na wɔnkyɛ asase no mma wɔn na wonni so, sɛ wɔn din dodow te.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Ntonto so na wɔmfa nkyɛ agyapade mma wɔn a wɔdɔɔso ne wɔn a wosua. Lewifo mmusua

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Na Amram yere din ne Yokebed, Lewi ba a wɔwoo no Misraim no; na ɔwoo Aaron ne Mose ne wɔn nuabea Miriam maa Amram.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: Yɛn agya wui sare so, nso ɔno de, ɔmfra asafo a wohyia tiaa AWURADE, Kora asafo no mu, na n'ankasa ne bɔne nti na owui; nso na onni mmammarima.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛn nti na yɛn agya din mpopa mfi n'abusua mu sɛ onni babarima yi? Ma yɛn agyapade yɛn agya ne nuanom mu.

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Na Mose de wɔn asɛm no baa AWURADE anim.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ

translation_verse: Selofehad mmabea no asɛm no teɛ, na ma wɔn agyapade na wonni so wɔn agya ne nuanom mu, na ma wɔn agya agyapade no nyɛ wɔn dea.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Na sɛ onni babea nso a, ɛnne momfa n'agyapade mma ne nuammarimanom;

translation_verse: na sɛ onni nuammarima nso a, momfa n'agyapade mma n'agya nuanom.

translation_verse: Na sɛ n'agya nni nuanom nso a, momfa n'agyapade mma ne bogya a ɔbɛn no n'abusua mu na onni so. Na eyi nyɛ ahyɛde ne mmara mma Israelfo, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no. Wɔpaw Yosua sɛ Israel kannifo (Deuteronomium

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Foro Abarim bepɔw yi na kɔhwɛ asase a mede merema Israelfo no;

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: na sɛ wunya hu a, watiw wo mpanyimfo, sɛnea Aaron tiw ne mpanyimfo no,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: efisɛ moyɛɛ m'asɛm ho asoɔden, Sin sare so, asafo no ham no mu a ɛsɛ sɛ anka moyɛ me kronkron, nsu no ho wɔ wɔn ani so no. .

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: Ma AWURADE, ɔhonam nyinaa ahonhom Nyankopɔn, mpɛ ɔbarima bi nsi asafo no so

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: a obedi wɔn anim afi adi na obedi wɔn anim aba mu, nea ɔde wɔn befi adi na ɔde wɔn aba mu, na AWURADE asafo no anyɛ sɛ nguan a wonni hwɛfo.

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ: Fa Nun ba Yosua, ɔbarima a honhom wɔ ne mu no, na fa wo nsa gu no so.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Na fa no gyina ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne asafo mu no nyinaa anim, na hyɛ no mmara wɔn anim;

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: na fa w'anuonyam no bi hyɛ no, na Israelfo asafo mu no nyinaa ntie no.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Na onkogyina Ɔsɔfo Eleasar anim, na ommisa Urim atemmu mma no, AWURADE anim; ɔno na ɔka a, womfi adi, na ɔka a, wɔmmra mu, ɔno ne Israelfo a wɔka ne ho nyinaa, ne asafo mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.

translation_verse: Na AWURADE kasa kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: Hyɛ Israelfo na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: M'ayɛyɛde, m'aduan a wɔde bɔ ogya afɔre ma eyi hua huamhuam ma me no, monhwɛ na momfa mmrɛ me ne bere a ɛsɛ mu.

translation_verse: abupɛn du mu biako nka nguammaa ason no mu biara ho;

english_verse: A goat must also be sacrificed for the sins of the people. You will offer these sacrifices in addition to the sacrifice to ask forgiveness and the regular daily sacrifices. The Sacrifices during the Festival of Shelters (Leviticus
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔre papo biako, ɛsono bɔne ho mpata afɔre ne daa ɔhyew afɔre ne ɛho aduan afɔre ne ɛho ahwiesa. Asese afahyɛ afɔre

english_verse: Beginning on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and continuing for seven days, everyone must celebrate the Festival of Shelters in honor of me.
translation_verse: Na ɔsram a ɛto so ason no da a ɛto so dunum no, munhyia nhyia kronkron; monnyɛ adwumaden biara na monhyɛ fa nnansɔn mma AWURADE.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the rams,
translation_verse: ne ɛho aduan afɔre: asikresam abupɛn du mu abiɛsa a wɔde ngo afɔtɔw nka anantwinini dumiɛnsa no mu biara ho, abupɛn du mu abien nka adwennini abien no mu biara ho,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: na abupɛn du mu biako nka nguammaa dunan no mu biara ho;

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These are to be offered in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔre papo biako; ɛsono daa ɔhyew afɔre, ɛho aduan afɔre ne ɛho ahwiesa.

english_verse: On the eighth day, you must once again rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Ɛda a ɛto so awotwe no, munhyia afahyɛ nhyiam; monnyɛ adwuma den biara;

english_verse: Bring to the altar one bull, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: na momfa ɔhyew afɔre, ogya afɔre a eyi hua huamhuam mmrɛ AWURADE: nantwinini biako, odwennini biako, nguanten mma a wɔadi afe afe ason a wodi mu;

english_verse: You must also offer the proper grain sacrifices and drink offerings of wine with each animal.
translation_verse: nantwinini ne odwennini ne nguammaa no ho aduan afɔre ne ahwiesa, wɔn dodow, sɛ ɛte wɔ mmara no mu;

english_verse: And offer a goat as the sacrifice to ask forgiveness for the people. These sacrifices are made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: ne bɔne ho afɔre papo biako; ɛsono daa ɔhyew afɔre ne ɛho aduan afɔre ne ɛho ahwiesa.

english_verse: You must offer all these sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, together with any offerings that are voluntarily given or given because of a promise.
translation_verse: Eyinom na monyɛ mma AWURADE, mo fa a mohyɛ no mu, ɛsono mo bɔhyɛ ade ne mo ayamye afɔre, mo hyew afɔre ne mo aduan afɔre ne mo ahwiesa ne mo asomdwoe afɔre.

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord had told him about the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to Israel's tribal leaders:
translation_verse: Na Mose kasa kyerɛɛ Israelfo mmusuakuw no so atitiriw sɛ: Eyi ne asɛm a AWURADE ahyɛ

english_verse: When one of you men makes a promise to the Lord, you must keep your word.
translation_verse: Sɛ obi hyɛ AWURADE bɔ anaasɛ ɔka ntam tua ne kra ade bi a, ommmu n'asɛm so; nea efi n'anom nyinaa, ɔnyɛ.

english_verse: Suppose a young woman who is still living with her parents makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔbea bi hyɛ AWURADE bɔ de tua ne ho biribi n'agya fi, wɔ ne mmabaabere mu,

english_verse: But if he hears about it and objects, then she no longer has to keep her promise. The Lord will forgive her, because her father did not agree with the promise.
translation_verse: Na sɛ da a n'agya bɛte no wampene a, ɛnne ne bɔhyɛ nyinaa ne n'ahotua a ɔde tuaa ne kra biribi no rennyina hɔ; na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no, efisɛ n'agya ampene.

english_verse: Suppose a woman makes a promise to the Lord and then gets married. If her husband later hears about the promise but says nothing, she must do what she said, whether she meant it or not.
translation_verse: na ne kunu te, na da a ɔte no ɔyɛ komm a, ɛnne ne bɔhyɛ no gyina hɔ, na otua a ɔde atua ne kra biribi no gyina hɔ.

english_verse: But if her husband hears about the promise and objects, she no longer has to keep it, and the Lord will forgive her.
translation_verse: Na sɛ da a ne kunu te no, wampene a, na wasan ne bɔhyɛ a ɛda no so ne nea efii n'anom a ɔde tuaa ne kra biribi no, na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no.

english_verse: Widows and divorced women must keep every promise they make to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea kunafo anaa nea wɔako no bɔhyɛ de, ade biara a otua ne kra no da no so.

english_verse: Suppose a married woman makes a promise to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ne kunu fi na ɔhyɛ bɔ anaasɛ ɔde ntam tua ne kra biribi,

english_verse: If her husband hears about the promise and says nothing, she must do what she said.
translation_verse: na ne kunu te, na ɔyɛ komm, na wammara no a, ne bɔhyɛ no nyinaa gyina hɔ, na ade biara a watua ne kra no gyina hɔ.

english_verse: But if he hears about the promise and does object, she no longer has to keep it. The Lord will forgive her, because her husband would not allow her to keep the promise.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ ne kunu san no da a ɔtee no a, ɛnne ade biara a afi n'anom a ɔde hyɛɛ bɔ anaasɛ ɔde tuaa ne kra biribi no rennyina hɔ; ne kunu asan, na AWURADE de bɛkyɛ no.

english_verse: Her husband has the final say about any promises she makes to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɔhyɛ nyinaa ne ahotua ntam a wɔde brɛ ɔkra ase nyinaa, ne kunu na ɔmma ennyina hɔ na ne kunu na ɔnsan;

english_verse: If her husband hears about a promise and says nothing about it for a whole day, she must do what she said—since he did not object, the promise must be kept.
translation_verse: na sɛ ne kunu no nka ho hwee daa a, wahyɛ ne bɔhyɛ no nyinaa anaa n'ahotua no nyinaa mu den, efisɛ da a ɔtee no, wanka ho hwee;

english_verse: But if he waits until the next day to stop her from keeping her promise, he is the one who must be punished.
translation_verse: na sɛ ɔtee no akyi ansa na ɔresan a, ɛnne ɔnsoa ne yere amumɔyɛ.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave Moses about husbands and wives, and about young daughters who still live at home.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne ahyɛde a AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose sɛ ɛnna ɔbarima ne ne yere ntam, ɛne agya ne ne babea a ɔwɔ ne mmabaabere mu, n'agya fi ntam.

english_verse: “Before you die, make sure that the Midianites are punished for what they did to Israel.”
translation_verse: Tɔ Midianfo so were ma Israelfo, na ɛno akyi no woakɔ wo nsumankyiri.

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “The Lord wants to punish the Midianites. So tell our men to prepare for battle.
translation_verse: Na Mose kasa kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Momma mo mu mmarima mmia wɔn ho ntu Midian so sa, na wɔmfa AWURADE aweretɔ mmra Midianfo so.

english_verse: Twelve thousand men were picked from the tribes of Israel, and after they were prepared for battle,
translation_verse: Na woyiyii Israel mpem ahorow mu nnipa mpem dumien a wɔamia rekɔ ɔsa, abusuakuw biara mu apem.

english_verse: Moses sent them off to war. Phinehas the son of Eleazar went with them and took along some things from the sacred tent and the trumpets for sounding the battle signal.
translation_verse: Na Mose somaa wɔn kɔɔ ɔsa no, abusuakuw biara mu apem, wɔne ɔsɔfo Eleasar ba Pinehas, a kronkronbea hɔ nneɛma ne osebɔ ntorobɛnto no wɔ ne nsam.

english_verse: The Israelites fought against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. They killed all the men,
translation_verse: Na wɔne Midian kɔkoe, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no, na wokunkum wɔn mmarima nyinaa;

english_verse: The Israelites captured every woman and child, then led away the Midianites' cattle and sheep, and took everything else that belonged to them.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no faa Midian mmea ne mmofra nnommum, na wɔfom wɔn anantwi ne wɔn nguan ne wɔn ahode nyinaa;

english_verse: They also burned down the Midianite towns and villages.
translation_verse: na wɔtotoo wɔn nkurow nyinaa ne wɔn nsraban nyinaa, mu gya.

english_verse: Israel's soldiers gathered together everything they had taken from the Midianites, including the captives and the animals.
translation_verse: Na wɔde asade no nyinaa ne nnipa ne mmoa a wɔfae no nyinaa

english_verse: Then they returned to their own camp in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, where Moses, Eleazar, and the other Israelite leaders met the troops outside camp.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne asafo no mmapɔmma nyinaa fi nsra no mu fii adi kohyiaa wɔn.

english_verse: and said, “I can't believe you let the women live!
translation_verse: na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moagye mmea no nyinaa nkwa anaa?

english_verse: You must put to death every boy and all the women who have ever had sex.
translation_verse: Enti munkunkum mmofra no mu mmarima nyinaa, na mmea no mu biara a onim ɔbarima ne ɔbarima ada no nso, munkum no;

english_verse: But do not kill the young women who have never had sex. You may keep them for yourselves.”
translation_verse: na mmofra no mu mmea a wonhuu mmarima nna no de, munnye wɔn nkwa na momfa wɔn.

english_verse: Then Moses said to the soldiers, “If you killed anyone or touched a dead body, you are unclean and have to stay outside the camp for seven days. On the third and seventh days, you must go through a ceremony to make yourselves and your captives clean.
translation_verse: Na mo ankasa nso, mommɔ nsra ntena mu nsra no akyi nnanson; mo mu biara a wakum obi ne obiara a waka ɔtɔfo no, munnwira mo ho da a ɛto so abiɛsa ne da a ɛto so ason no, mo ne mo nnommum no.

english_verse: Then wash your clothes and anything made from animal skin, goat's hair, or wood.”
translation_verse: Na atade biara ne nhoma ade biara ne ade a wɔde abirekyi nwi ayɛ nyinaa ne dua ade nyinaa, munnwira ho.

english_verse: Eleazar then explained, “If you need to purify something that won't burn, such as gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, or lead, you must first place it in a hot fire. After you take it out, sprinkle it with the water that purifies. Everything else should only be sprinkled with the water. Do all of this, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
translation_verse: ade biara a ɛkɔ ogya mu no, momma ɛmfa ogya mu na ɛho ntew, nanso momfa ahodwira nsu nnwira ho. Na ade biara a ɛnkɔ ogya mu no, momma ɛmfa nsu mu.

english_verse: Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and after that, you will be clean and may return to the camp.” Everything Taken from the Midianites Is Divided
translation_verse: Na monhoro mo ntade da a ɛto so ason no, na mo ho ntew, na ɛno akyi ansa na mommra nsra no mu. Asade mu kyekyɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose sɛ:

english_verse: From the half that belongs to the soldiers, set aside for the Lord one out of every
translation_verse: fi wɔn fa a wonyae no mu, na fa ma ɔsɔfo Eleasar sɛ AWURADE soma afɔrebɔde.

english_verse: So we want to give the Lord all the gold jewelry we took from the Midianites. It's our gift to him for watching over us and our troops.”
translation_verse: enti na yɛde AWURADE ayɛyɛde reba yi, obiara a onyaa sika nnwinne, basa so nkapo, bakɔn so nkapo, nsɔanonkaa, asomkaa ne kɔmuade, sɛ wɔmfa mpata mma yɛn kra, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar followed the Lord's instructions
translation_verse: Na Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Mose no.

english_verse: women and gave them to Eleazar to be dedicated to the Lord. Then from the half that belonged to the people, Moses set aside one out of every
translation_verse: Nso asade a ɛyɛ asade a dɔm no fae no nkae si nguan ɔpehansia ne ɔpeduɔson anum,

english_verse: and listed everything that had been taken from the Midianites. The list included
translation_verse: ne akra, ɔpeduasa abien mmea a wonhuu mmarima nna, mu akra nyinaa si ɔpeduasa abien.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, we have counted our troops, and not one soldier is missing.
translation_verse: bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo nkoa abu akofo a wɔwɔ yɛn nsam no ano, na wɔn mu biara anyera;

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar accepted the jewelry from the commanders,
translation_verse: Na Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar gyee wɔn hɔ sika no, nnwinne no nyinaa;

english_verse: This did not include the things that the soldiers had kept for themselves.
translation_verse: Nea akofo no fom kaa ho no, wɔn ara fofae.

english_verse: So Moses and Eleazar placed the gold in the Lord's sacred tent to remind Israel of what had happened.
translation_verse: Na Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar gyee sika no, apem apem ne ɔha ɔha so asafohene no nsam, na wɔde baa ahyiae ntamadan no mu sɛ ɛnyɛ Israelfo no nkae ade, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: except Caleb and Joshua. They remained faithful to the Lord,
translation_verse: Gye Kenisini Yefune ba Kaleb ne Nun ba Yosua, efisɛ wɔn na wɔadi AWURADE akyi nokware mu.

english_verse: then after the Lord helps Israel capture the land, you can return to your own land. You will no longer have to stay with the others.
translation_verse: na wɔabrɛ asase no ase AWURADE anim ansa na moasan a, ɛnne na moayɛ mo asɛde, AWURADE ne Israel ho, na asase yi nyɛ mo agyapade, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben and Gad owned a lot of cattle and sheep, and they saw that the regions of Jazer and Gilead had good pastureland.
translation_verse: Na Ruben mma ne Gad mma wɔ mmoa pii a ɛdɔɔso pa ara, na wohuu Yaser ne Gilead asase, na hwɛ, ɛhɔ yɛ baabi a eye ma mmoa.

english_verse: So they went to Moses, Eleazar, and the other leaders of Israel and said,
translation_verse: Na Gad mma ne Ruben mma no ba bɛka kyerɛɛ Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne asafo no mu mmapɔmma no sɛ:

english_verse: “The Lord has helped us capture the land around the towns of Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon. That's good pastureland, and since we own cattle and sheep,
translation_verse: asase a AWURADE abrɛ no ase Israel asafo anim no, yɛ asase a eye ma mmoayɛn; na wo nkoa wɔ mmoa.

english_verse: would you let us stay here east of the Jordan River and have this land as our own?”
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Sɛ yɛn anim aba onyam wɔ w'anim a, ma wɔmfa asase yi mma wo nkoa na yenni so, na mfa yɛn ntwa Yordan.

english_verse: Moses answered: You mean you'd stay here while the rest of the Israelites go into battle?
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Gad mma ne Ruben mma no sɛ: So mo nuanom nkɔ, na mo de, montena ha?

english_verse: If you did that, it would discourage the others from crossing over into the land the Lord promised them.
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn na mutu Israelfo koma sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ na wɔrentwa nnkɔ asase a AWURADE de ama wɔn no so.

english_verse: This is exactly what happened when I sent your ancestors from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land.
translation_verse: Saa na mo agyanom yɛe bere a mesomaa wɔn fi Kades-barnea sɛ wɔnkɔhwɛ asase no,
