english_verse: It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no foro fii Yordan mu ɔsram a edi kan no da a ɛto so du, na wɔkɔbɔɔ nsra Gilgal, Yeriko apuei hye so.

english_verse: The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument.
translation_verse: Na abo dumien a wɔtase fii Yordan mu no, Yosua de sisii Gilgal.

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Sɛ ɔkyena bi mo mma bisa wɔn agyanom sɛ: Abo yi kyerɛ dɛn a?

english_verse: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
translation_verse: sɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn yow Yordan nsu no mo anim kosii sɛ mutwae, sɛnea AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn yɛɛ Mmɛw-Po no a ɔyow no yɛn anim kosii sɛ yetwae no,

english_verse: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_verse: na asase so aman nyinaa nhu AWURADE basa a emu yɛ den, na moasuro AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn nna nyinaa.

english_verse: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: Na Amorifo ahene a wɔwɔ Yordan agya atɔe fam no nyinaa ne Kanaan ahene a wɔwɔ po ano no nyinaa tee sɛ AWURADE ayow Yordan nsu Israelfo no anim akosi sɛ wotwae no, wɔn koma tui a ɔhome bi nni wɔn mu bio Israelfo no anim. Ɔman no twetiatwa ne Twam afahyɛ

english_verse: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
translation_verse: Ɛbere no ara mu na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Yɛ twɛrebo asekan, na san twitwa Israelfo no twetia a ɛto so abien.

english_verse: Joshua made the knives, then circumcised those men and boys at Haaraloth Hill.
translation_verse: Na Yosua yɛɛ twɛrebo asekan de twitwaa Israelfo no twetia Aralot koko so.

english_verse: This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the
translation_verse: Na wɔn mma na ɔma wɔsɔre sii wɔn ananmu; wɔn na Yosua twitwaa wɔn twetia, na wɔyɛ momonoto, efisɛ wɔantwitwa wɔn twetia ɔkwan no mu.

english_verse: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
translation_verse: Na wowiee ɔman mu no nyinaa twetiatwa no, wɔtenaa wɔn tenabea hɔ nsra no mu kosii sɛ wɔn ho tɔɔ wɔn.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Ɛnnɛ mapirew Misraim nsopa afi mo so. Ɛno nti wɔfrɛɛ hɔ sɛ: Gilgal de besi nnɛ yi ara.

english_verse: Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no bɔɔ nsra Gilgal, na wodii Twam no, ɔsram no da a ɛto so dunan no anwummere, Yeriko tataw so.

english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Na Yosua wɔ Yeriko ho no, ɔmaa n’ani so hwɛe, na hwɛ, ɔbarima bi gyina ne ntentenso kura nkrante a watwe. Na Yosua kɔɔ ne nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛn afa na wowɔ anaa yɛn atamfo afa?

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Daabi, na afei na maba sɛ AWURADE dɔm so safohene. Na Yosua de n’anim butuw fam sɔree no, na obisaa no sɛ: Ɛdɛn na me wura reka akyerɛ n’akoa?

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dɔm so safohene no ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Yi wo mpaboa fi wo nan, na nea wugyina hɔ yɛ kronkron. Na Yosua yɛɛ saa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Na Yeriko de, wɔato mu na wɔabram ano Israelfo no anim. Obi mfi adi, na obi mma mu.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Na asɔfo baasɔn nkurakura osebɔ ntorobɛnto ason mfa nni adaka no anim, na ɛda a ɛto so ason no, muntwa kurow no ho nhyia mpɛn asɔn, na asɔfo no nhyɛn ntorobɛnto no.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔhyɛn osebɔ abɛn no na mote torobɛnto no nne a, ɔman no nyinaa nhuro mmɔ ose kɛse, na kurow no ho fasu no bɛhwe fam burum, na ɔman no mforo nkokɔ wɔn anim tee.

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Na Nun ba Yosua frɛfrɛɛ asɔfo no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monsoa apam adaka no, na asɔfo baasɔn nkurakura osebɔ ntorobɛnto nni AWURADE adaka no anim.

english_verse: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE adaka no twaa kurow no ho hyiae pɛnkoro, na wɔbaa nsra mu bɛdaa hɔ.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so ason no, ade rekye pɛ, wotuaa ahema sɔree ntɛm, na wotwaa kurow no ho hyiae saa ara mpɛn asɔn; da no nko na wotwaa kurow no ho hyiae mpɛn ason.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Na nea ɛto so ason no so a asɔfo no rehyɛn ntorobɛnto no no, Yosua ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Mommɔ ose, efisɛ AWURADE de kurow no ama mo.

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: Na kurow no ne emu ade nyinaa nyɛ nea AWURADE de ne nsa ato so ama ɔsɛe; aguaman Rahab nko na onnya nkwa, ɔno ne wɔn a wɔwɔ ne nkyɛn ne ne fi nyinaa, efisɛ ɔno na ɔde abɔfo a yɛsomaa wɔn no hintawee.

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no bɔɔ ose na wɔhyɛn ntorobɛnto no. Na ɔman no tee ntorobɛnto no nne no, ɔman no huro bɔɔ ose kɛse, na ɔfasu no hwee fam burum, na ɔman no foro kɔɔ kurow no mu, wɔn nyinaa kokɔɔ wɔn anim tee, na wɔfaa kurow no.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua kaa ntam saa bere no sɛ: Nnome nka onipa a ɔbɛsɔre abɛkyekye Yeriko kurow yi, AWURADE anim: Ɔde n’abakan na ɛbɛhyɛ ase, na ɔde ne ba akumaa na ebesisi ano apon.

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dii Yosua akyi, na wɔtee ne nka asase no nyinaa so.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no too ahyirade no ho mmara, na Serah ba Sabdi Karmi ba Akan a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu no faa emu bi, AWURADE bo fuw Israelfo

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Na Yosua sunsuanee ne ntade mu, na ɔde n’anim butuw fam, AWURADE adaka no anim de kosii anwummere, ɔno ne Israel mpanyimfo, na wɔde dɔte guguu wɔn atifi.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Na Yosua bisaa sɛ: AWURADE Nyankopɔn, ɛdɛn nti na wode ɔman yi twaa Yordan sɛ wode yɛn rebɛhyɛ Amorifo nsa na wɔasɛe yɛn? Yenim a, anka yɛpene tenaa Yordan agya hɔ ara.

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Wo kyɛw ni, Awurade, sɛ Israel adan wɔn akyi akyerɛ wɔn atamfo yi, dɛn na menka?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Na Kanaanfo ne asase yi sofo nyinaa bɛte, na wɔabetwa yɛn ho ahyia, na wɔatwa yɛn din afi asase so: Na ɛdɛn na wobɛyɛ ama wo din kɛse no?

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Sɔre ɛ, ɛdɛn nti na wode w’anim abutuw fam sɛɛ yi?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Israel ayɛ bɔne, na wɔato m’apam a mehyɛɛ wɔn ho mmara no nso, na wɔafa ahyirade no bi nso, na wɔabɔ korɔn nso, na wɔasiw so nso, na wɔde asie wɔn ade mu nso.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo rentumi nnyina wɔn atamfo anim, wɔn akyi na wɔbɛdan akyerɛ wɔn atamfo, efisɛ wɔayɛ ahyirade; merenkɔ so minni mo akyi, gye sɛ muyi ahyirade no hɔ fi mo mu.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Sɔre tew ɔman no ho na ka sɛ: Monyɛ mo ho kronkron nsie ɔkyena; na sɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, se ni: Ahyirade wɔ wo mu, Israel! Worentumi nnyina w’atamfo anim kosi sɛ mubeyi ahyirade no afi mo mu.

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: Enti anɔpa, wɔmfa mo ntwiw mmɛn mmusuakuw mmusuakuw. Na abusuakuw a AWURADE bɛkyerɛ no, wontwiw mmɛn mmusua mmusua, na abusua a AWURADE bɛkyerɛ no ntwiw mmɛn afi afi, na ofi a AWURADE bɛkyerɛ no mu mmarima ntwiw mmɛn mmiako mmiako.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Na nea wɔbɛkyere no ahyirade no so no, wɔmfa ogya nhyew no ne nea ɔwɔ nyinaa, sɛ wato AWURADE ntam, na wayɛ nkwaseade Israel mu.

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua sɔree anɔpahema, na ɔde Israel twiw bɛnee abusuakuw abusuakuw; na wɔkyeree Yuda abusuakuw.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Na ɔde Yuda mmusua twiw bɛnee, na wɔkyeree Serahfo abusua. Na ɔde Serahfo abusua mu mmarima twiw bɛnee mmiako mmiako, na wɔkyeree Sabdi.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ne fi mmarima twiw bɛnee mmiako mmiako, na wɔkyeree Serah ba Sabdi ba Karmi ba Akan a ofi Yuda abusuakuw mu.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua ka kyerɛɛ Akan sɛ: Me ba, fa anuonyam ma AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, na di no ni, na ka kyerɛ me ɛ: Dɛn na woyɛe? Nsiw me so.

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Akan buaa Yosua sɛ: Nokware, me na mayɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn no, bɔne, na sɛɛ ne sɛɛ na meyɛe.

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Na woyi fii ntamadan no mu de brɛɛ Yosua ne Israelfo no nyinaa, na wɔde beguu AWURADE anim.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua faa Serah ba Akan, ne dwetɛ ne nguguso ne sika nnaame no, ne ne mmammarima ne ne mmabea, ne n’anantwi ne ne mfurum ne ne nguan, ne ne ntamadan ne nea ɔwɔ nyinaa, na Israel nyinaa ka no ho, na wɔde wɔn foro kɔɔ Akor bon mu.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Na Yosua kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn na woahaw yɛn sɛɛ yi? AWURADE nso bɛhaw wo nnɛ da yi. Na Israel nyinaa siw no abo, na wɔde ogya hyew wɔn, na wɔde abo guu wɔn so.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Na wɔhɔree no so abosiw kɛse a ɛwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ ara. Na AWURADE dan fii n’abufuhyew no ho. Ɛno nti wɔfrɛ hɔ sɛ Akor bon de besi nnɛ ara.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: na wobefi adi adi yɛn akyi akosi sɛ yɛbɛtwe wɔn afi kurow no ho; na wɔbɛka sɛ: Wɔreguan afi yɛn anim sɛ kan no; enti yebeguan afi wɔn anim.

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Na mo de, monsɔre mfi ɔtɛw no mu, na momfa kurow no, na AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn de bɛhyɛ mo nsa.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Na sɛ munya fa kurow no a, monto kurow no mu gya; monyɛ no sɛnea AWURADE ahyɛ no; monhwɛ, ɔhyɛ na mahyɛ mo no.

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Na Yosua sɔree anɔpahema siesiee ɔman no, na ɔno ne Israel mpanyimfo foro dii ɔman no anim kɔɔ Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Na akofo dɔm a wɔka ne ho nyinaa foro kɔe, na wotwiw bɛnee, na woduu kurow no ntentenso, na wɔbɔɔ nsra Ai benkum fam, na obon wɔ wɔn ne Ai ntam.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Na wɔde dɔm no sisii, ɛdɔm a wɔwɔ kurow no benkum fam ne akyiri tɛwfo no a ɛwɔ kurow no atɔe fam no nyinaa; na Yosua kɔɔ obon no mu anadwo no ara;

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Teɛ peaw a ɛwɔ wo nsam no kyerɛ Ai, na mede mɛhyɛ wo nsa. Na Yosua teɛɛ ne peaw a ɛwɔ ne nsam no kyerɛɛ kurow no.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Ɛnna atɛwfo no sɔree ntɛm fii wɔn afa hɔ, na ɔteɛɛ ne nsa no, wotutuu mmirika kɔhyɛn kurow no mu na wɔfae, na wɔyɛɛ ntɛm de ogya too kurow no mu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Na Israel wiee Aifo nyinaa kum wɔ sare so petee mu, faako a wotiw wɔn no, na wɔn nyinaa totɔe nkrante ano kosii sɛ wɔsae no, Israel nyinaa san kɔɔ Ai, de nkrante kokunkum wɔn.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na Ai hene no de, ɔsɛn no dua so kosii anwummere; na owia kɔtɔe no, Yosua hyɛe sɛ wonkoyi ne funu no mfi dua no so, na wɔde no too kurow no pon ano, na wɔhɔree no so abosiw kɛse a ɛwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ. Yosua si afɔremuka, na ɔkyerɛw mmara no gu abo so

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Na Gibeonfo tee nea Yosua yɛɛ Yeriko ne Ai no,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: wɔn de, wodii no nyansam, na wɔkɔpɛɛ akwansoduan, na wɔfaa mmɔtɔ adedaw de soasoaa wɔn mfurum, ne nsa nkotoku adedaw a asunsuane na wɔapompam.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Na wɔde mpaboa adedaw a wɔasesa kyekyeree wɔn anan, na wɔhyehyɛɛ ntade agowagow, na wɔn akwansoduan nyinaa akyenkyen na agye ntuw.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Na wosiim baa Yosua nkyɛn nsra mu wɔ Gilgal bɛka kyerɛɛ no ne Israel mma no sɛ: Akyirikyiri asase bi so na yefi bae, na afei mo ne yɛn nyɛ apam.

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Na wose: AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn no din nti na wo nkoa fi akyirikyiri asase bi so aba, efisɛ yɛate ne nka ne nea ɔyɛe Misraim nyinaa,

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: ne nea ɔyɛɛ Amorifo ahene baanu a wɔwɔ Yordan agya no, Hesbonhene Sihon ne Basan hene Og a ɔtenaa Astarot no.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Na yɛn mpanyimfo ne yɛn asase no sofo nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Momfa akwansoduan na monkɔ nkohyia wɔn, na monka nkyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo nkoa ne yɛn, na afei mo ne yɛn nyɛ apam.

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Yɛn abodoo ni, ɛda a yɛresim aba mo nkyɛn no, yɛfaa no ɔhyew de fii yɛn afi mu, sɛ yɛrebedi ɔkwan so; na afei, monhwɛ, akyenkyen na agye ntuw.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Na nsa nkotoku yi a yɛhyehyɛɛ no amaama na ɛyɛ foforo no, hwɛ, asunsuane, na ɔkwan no ware a ɛware nti yɛn ntade ne yɛn mpaboa yi asusuw.

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Na mmarima no faa wɔn akwansoduan no bi, na AWURADE anom asɛm de, wɔammisa.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ne wɔn dii no asomdwoe mu, na ɔne wɔn yɛɛ apam sɛ wɔbɛma wɔatena ase; na asafo no mu mmapɔmma kekaa wɔn ntam.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tui, na wɔkɔtoo wɔn nkurow da a ɛto so abiɛsa no; na wɔn nkurow ne Gibeon ne Kefira ne Beerot ne Kiriat-yearim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no ankum wɔn, efisɛ asafo no mu mmapɔmma akeka wɔn AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn no ntam. Na asafo no nyinaa nwiinwii hyɛɛ mmapɔmma no.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Na Yosua frɛɛ wɔn bae, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na modaadaa yɛn kae sɛ: Yɛne mo ntam ware pa ara, na mote yɛn mu yi?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Enti afei wɔadome mo, na mo mu na nkoa ne nnuatwafo ne nsusawfo a wɔbɛyɛ adwuma ama me Nyankopɔn fi no befi daa.

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Na wobuaa Yosua sɛ: Ampa ara, wɔka kyerɛɛ wo nkoa sɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ahyɛ n’akoa Mose sɛ ɔmfa asase no nyinaa mma mo na ɔnsɛe asase no sofo nyinaa mfi mo anim, na mo nti yesuroo yɛn nkwa ho papaapa, enti na yedii saa asɛm yi.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Na afei, yɛn ni, yɛwɔ wo nsam, nea eye na ɛteɛ w’ani so a wobɛyɛ yɛn no, yɛ!

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ wɔn sa, na oyii wɔn fii Israelfo no nsam, na wɔankum wɔn.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yerusalem hene Adoni-sedek tee sɛ Yosua afa Ai na wasɛe no pasaa, na sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Yeriko ne ne hene no, saa ara na wayɛ Ai ne ne hene nso,

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: ne sɛ Gibeonfo ne Israel adi asomdwoesɛm na wɔaba wɔn mu no, wosuroe papaapa, efisɛ Gibeon yɛ kurow kɛse te sɛ ahenni nkurow no bi, na ɛso sen Ai, na emu mmarima nyinaa yɛ nnɔmmarima.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Na Yerusalem hene Adoni-sedek soma kɔɔ Hebron hene Hoham ne Yarmut hene Piram ne Lakis hene Yafia ne Eglon hene Debir nkyɛn sɛ:

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: Mommra me nkyɛn mmɛboa me, na yenkunkum Gibeon, efisɛ wɔne Yosua ne Israelfo no akodi asomdwoesɛm.

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Gibeonfo no soma baa Yosua nkyɛn Gilgal nsra no mu sɛ: Nyi wo nsa mfi wo nkoa so, bra yɛn nkyɛn ntɛm begye yɛn nkwa na di boa yɛn, na Amorifo a wɔte mmepɔw so ahene nyinaa abehyia ahyɛ yɛn.

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua fii Gilgal foro kɔe, ɔno ne akofo dɔm no nyinaa ne nnɔmmarima nyinaa.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Nsuro wɔn, na wo nsam na mede wɔn mahyɛ, wɔn mu biara rennyina w’anim.

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Na Yosua baa wɔn so mpofirim, ɔde anadwo mu no nyinaa na ɛforo fii Gilgal bae.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kaa wɔn gui Israel anim, na wɔde okunkɛse kunkum wɔn wɔ Gibeon, na wotiw wɔn Bet-horon aforoee kwan no so, na wonkunkum wɔn de kosii Aseka ne Makeda.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Na wɔreguan afi Israel anim na wokoduu Bet-horon asianee mu no, AWURADE totow abo akɛse fi soro guguu wɔn so de koduu Aseka ma wowuwui; wɔn a amparuwbo no kunkum wɔn dɔɔso sen wɔn a Israelfo no kunkum wɔn nkrante ano no. Owia ne ɔsram di Yosua asɛm so

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɛda bi mmae da sɛ ɛno nea aba pɛn, anaa nea ɛbɛba a AWURADE atie onipa nne, efisɛ AWURADE ko maa Israel.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Na Yosua sanee ne Israel nyinaa baa Gilgal nsra no mu.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Yɛahu ahene baanum no sɛ wohintaw Makeda ɔbodan no mu.

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Na Yosua kae sɛ: Munkopirew abo akɛse nkata ɔbodan no ano, na momfa mmarima nnyina ho mma wɔnwɛn wɔn.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Na mo de, munnnyina hɔ, muntiw mo atamfo no, na munkum wɔn kyidɔm no; mommma wonnnu wɔn nkurow mu, efisɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn de wɔn ahyɛ mo nsa.

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Na Yosua ne Israelfo no de okum kɛse pa kunkum wɔn wiei ma wɔsae, na nnipa a wofii mu no guanguan kɔhyɛnhyɛn nkurow a wɔatoto ho afasu mu no,

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: na ɔman no nyinaa san baa nsra no mu Yosua nkyɛn wɔ Makeda dwoodwoo; obiara amma n’ano anto Israelfo no.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua kae sɛ: Mummue ɔbodan no ano, na munyi ahene baanum no mfi ɔbodan no mu mmrɛ me.

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Na wɔyɛɛ saa, na woyiyii ahene baanum no fii ɔbodan no mu brɛɛ no: Yerusalem hene, Hebron hene, Yarmut hene, Lakis hene ne Eglon hene.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Na wɔde ahene yi fi brɛɛ Yosua no, Yosua frɛɛ Israel mmarima nyinaa bae, na ɔka kyerɛɛ mmarima akofofo a wɔne no kɔe no asafohene no sɛ: Muntwiw mmra mfa mo nan mmesisi ahene yi kɔn so. Na wotwiw bae de wɔn anan besisii wɔn kɔn so.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Munnsuro, na mo bo nntu, mo ho nyɛ den na monyɛ nnam. Na saa ara na AWURADE bɛyɛ mo atamfo a mo ne wɔn ko no nyinaa.

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, Yosua bobɔɔ wɔn kunkum wɔn, na ɔde wɔn sensɛn nnua anum so, na wɔsensɛn nnua no so kosii anwummere.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Na owia rekɔtɔ no, Yosua hyɛe ma woyiyii wɔn fii nnua no so, na wɔkɔtow wɔn guu ɔbodan a wokohintaw mu no mu, na wɔde abo akɛse guu ɔbodan no ano a ɛwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ yi ara.

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Na Yosua faa Makeda da no ara, na ɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn ne emu hene nso; na ɔsɛee akra a wɔwɔ mu nyinaa pasaa, wamma obiara anka, na ɔyɛɛ Makeda hene sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Yeriko hene no.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua twaam fii Makeda kɔɔ Libna a Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, na ɔne Libna kɔkoe.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de ɛno ne emu hene nso hyɛɛ Israel nsa, na ɔde nkrante kunkum akra a wɔwɔ mu nyinaa, wamma obiara anka, na ɔyɛɛ ne hene no sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Yeriko hene no.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Na Yosua twaam fii Libna kɔɔ Lakis a Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, na ɔbɔɔ so nsra, na ɔne wɔn koe.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de Lakis hyɛɛ Israel nsa, na wɔfae da a ɛto so abien no, na ɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn ne akra a wɔwɔ mu nyinaa, sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Libna no ara.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Ɛno mu no Geser hene Horam foro bae bɛboaa Lakis. Na Yosua kum no ne ne man nyinaa a wamma obiara anka.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua twaam fii Lakis kɔɔ Eglon a Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, na wotuae, na wɔne wɔn koe.

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: Na wɔfae da no ara, na wɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn ne akra a ɛwɔ mu nyinaa; da no ara na ɔsɛee wɔn pasaa sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Lakis no ara.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Eglon and attacked Hebron.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua foro fii Eglon kɔɔ Hebron a Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, na ɔne wɔn koe.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Na wɔfae de nkrante kunkum wɔn ne emu hene ne wɔn nkurow no nyinaa ne akra a ɛwɔ mu nyinaa; wamma obiara anka, sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Eglon no ara, na ɔsɛee ɛno ne akra a ɛwɔ mu nyinaa pasaa.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua san baa Debir a Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, ne no bɛkoe.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Na ɔfae, ɛne ne hene ne ne nkurow nyinaa, na wɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn, na wɔsɛee akra a ɛwɔ mu nyinaa pasaa, wamma obiara anka; sɛnea ɔyɛɛ Hebron ne Libna ne ne hene no, saa ara na ɔyɛɛ Debir ne ne hene.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Na Yosua sɛee asase no nyinaa: Mmepɔw no ne nifa fam ne po ho tataw so ne mmepɔw ase ne wɔn ahene nyinaa, wannyaw oguanfo biara, na ade biara a ɛhome no, ɔsɛee no pasaa, sɛnea AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, hyɛe no.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Na Yosua kunkum wɔn fii Kades-barnea koduu Gasa, ne Gosen asase no nyinaa koduu Gibeon.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: ne ahene a wɔwɔ benkum fam mmepɔw so, ne Kinerot nifa fam tataw so, ne po ho tataw so, ne Dor nkoko so, Atɔe po fam;

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Kanaanfo a wɔwɔ Apuei ne atɔe ne Amorifo ne Hetifo ne Perisifo ne mmepɔw so Yebusifo ne Hewifo a wɔwɔ Hermon bepɔw ase, Mispa asase so no nkyɛn.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Nsuro wɔn anim, na ɔkyena sesɛbere, me na mɛma woakum wɔn nyinaa, Israel anim. Wɔn apɔnkɔ no, twitwa wɔn nantin, na wɔn nteaseɛnam no, fa ogya hyew.

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua ne akofo dɔm a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa baa wɔn so mpofirim, Merom asu no ano, bɛtoaa wɔn.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Na Yosua sanee bere no ara mu bɛfaa Hasor, na ɔde nkrante kum ne hene; na kan no na Hasor ne saa ahenni yi nyinaa ti.

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na Yosua faa asase yi nyinaa: Mmepɔw no ne nifa nyinaa ne Gosen asase nyinaa, ne po ho tataw no, ne Araba so ne Israel mmepɔw ne ɛho asasetaw no;

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Na Yosua bae bere no mu betwitwaa Anakfo no gui fii mmepɔw no so, fii Hebron, Debir, Anab ne Yuda mmepɔw nyinaa ne Israel mmepɔw nyinaa so, na Yosua sɛee wɔn ne wɔn nkurow nyinaa pasaa.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Wɔannyaw Anakfo Israelfo no asase so; gye Gasa ne Gad ne Asdod na ebi kae.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Na Yosua faa asase no nyinaa, sɛnea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Mose no nyinaa; na Yosua kyekyɛɛ mu maa Israel ma ɛyɛɛ wɔn agyapade, sɛnea wɔn nkyekyem te, wɔn mmusuakuw no mu. Na asase no home fii akodi mu.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne asase no so ahene a Israelfo no kunkum wɔn na wodii wɔn asase so wɔ Yordan agya owiapuei hɔ, fi Arnon subon ho de kosi Hermon bepɔw ho ne Araba a ɛwɔ apuei no nyinaa so:

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: ne Araba so de kosi Kinerot po no ano apuei fam, na ɛde kosi Araba so po no a ɛne Nkyene-Po no ano, apuei Bet-yesimot kwan so, ne nifa fam Pisga bepɔw ase no;

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: ne Basan hene Og a ofi abran akɛse a aka no mu a ɔtenaa Astarot ne Edrei no asase no.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: Na odii hene Hermon bepɔw so ne Salka ne Basan nyinaa de kosi Gesurfo ne Maakatfo hye so, ne Gilead fa, Hesbonhene Sihon hye ho.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: AWURADE akoa Mose ne Israelfo no kaa wɔn gui, na AWURADE akoa Mose de asase no maa Rubenfo ne Gadfo ne Manase abusuakuw fa no ma wodii so. Ahene a Yosua kum wɔn

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Na Yosua abɔ akora na wadi mfe pii; na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Woabɔ akora na woadi mfe pii, na asase a aka sɛ wɔbɛfa no da so dɔɔso bebree.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ne fa nso ne Rubenfo ne Gadfo anya wɔn agyapade a Mose de maa wɔn Yordan agya apuei no, sɛnea AWURADE akoa Mose de maa wɔn no,

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: efi Aroer a ɛda Arnon subon no kɔn so no ho ne kurow a ɛda subon no mu no, ne Medeba asasetaw no nyinaa kosi Dibon,

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: ne Amorifo hene Sihon a odii hene Hesbon no nkurow no de kosi Amonfo hye so,

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Nanso Israelfo antu Gesurfo ne Maakatfo, na Gesurfo ne Maakatfo no tenaa Israel mu de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Lewi abusuakuw no nko na wamma wɔn agyapade, AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn gya afɔre so ade no, ɛno ne n’agyapade, sɛnea ɔka kyerɛɛ no no. Yordan apuei fam asase yɛ mmusuakuw abien ne fa no dea

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na Mose maa Ruben mma abusuakuw no sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Na wɔn hye no fi Aroer a ɛda Arnon subon no kɔn so no ho, ne kurow a ɛda subon no mu, ne Medeba ho asasetaw no nyinaa.

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: asasetaw no so nkurow no nyinaa; ne Amorifo hene Sihon a odii hene Hesbon no ahenni nyinaa; ɔno na Mose kum no ne Midian mmapɔmma, Ewi ne Rekem ne Sur ne Hur ne Reba, Sihon asafohene a wɔtenaa asase no so no.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Na Beor ba Bileam, nkɔmhyɛfo no nso, Israelfo de nkrante kum no fraa atɔfo no mu.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Na Ruben mma no hye ne Yordan ne ɛho hye. Eyi ne Ruben mma no agyapade sɛ wɔn mmusua te, nkurow no ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Na Mose maa Gad abusuakuw Gadfo, sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: na efi Hesbon de kosi Ramat-mispe ne Betonim, na ɛde fi Mahanaim de kosi Debir hye so;

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: ne obon no mu: Bet-haram ne Bet-nimra ne Sukot ne Safon a ɛyɛ Hesbonhene Sihon ahenni no nkae, Yordan ne ɛho hye, de kosi Kineret po no awiei, Yordan agya apuei.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Eyi ne Gadfo agyapade sɛ wɔn mmusua te, nkurow no ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Na Mose maa Manase abusuakuw fa no nso bi, na ɛyɛɛ Manase abusuakuw fa no de sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: ne Gilead fa ne Astarot ne Edrei, Og ahenni nkurow a ɛwɔ Basan no. Wɔde maa Manase ba Makir mma, sɛ ɛnyɛ Makir mma fa no dea, sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Na Lewi abusuakuw no de, Mose amma wɔn agyapade bi, efisɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, ɔno ne wɔn agyapade, sɛnea ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn no.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Na Yudafo no baa Yosua nkyɛn wɔ Gilgal; na Kenisini Yefune ba Kaleb ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo ara wunim me ne wo ho asɛm a AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn nipa Mose wɔ Kades-barnea no.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Na me nuanom a wɔne me foro kɔɔ no maa ɔman no koma tui, na me de, me koma nyinaa midii AWURADE me Nyankopɔn akyi.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Na Mose kaa ntam da no ara sɛ: Asase a wo nan tiaa so no bɛyɛ wo ne wo mma agyapade daa, efisɛ wode wo koma nyinaa adi AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn akyi.

english_verse: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
translation_verse: Meda so mewɔ ahoɔden nnɛ ara, sɛnea mete da a Mose somaa me no; sɛnea m’ahoɔden te da no, saa ara na ɛte nnɛ ma ɔko ne adifi ne emuba.

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Na afei fa bepɔw yi a AWURADE kaa ho asɛm da no ma me, efisɛ da no ara, wotee sɛ Anakfo ne nkurow akɛse a wɔatoto ho afasu wɔ hɔ; ebia AWURADE bedi m’akyi na matu wɔn, sɛnea AWURADE kae no.

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Na Yosua hyiraa no, na ɔde Hebron maa Yefune ba Kaleb sɛ n’agyapade.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɛno nti na Hebron yɛɛ Kenisini Yefune ba Kaleb agyapade de besi nnɛ, efisɛ ɔde ne koma nyinaa dii AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn no akyi.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Nso kan no na Hebron din ne Kiriat-arba; Arba yi ne Anakfo mu nipa kɛse koraa. Na asase no so dwoe fii akodi no mu.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na wɔn nifa fam hye no fi Nkyene-Po no awiei no ho, dɔnnɔn a ebu fa nifa fam no ano.

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: Na ɛnam Akrabim aforoee nifa fam sen kɔ Sin, na ɛforo kɔ nifa fam wɔ Kades-barnea, na etwam kɔ Hesron, na ɛforo kɔ Adar, na ɛpono kɔ Karka.

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: Na etwam kɔ Asmon, na ekopue Misraim subon no ano, na ɛkɔpem mpoano. Eyi nyɛ mo nifa fam hye.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na apuei hye ne Nkyene-Po no de besi Yordan awiei. Na benkum fam hye no fi Nkyene-Po ho dɔnnɔn a ɛwɔ Yordan awiei no ho.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no foro kosi Bet-hogla, na ɛsen fa Bet-araba benkum fam, na ɔhye no foro kosi Ruben ba Bohan bo no ho;

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: na ɔhye no fi Akor bon no mu foro kɔ Debir, na ɛdan kɔ benkum fam kyerɛ Gilgal a ɛda Adumim aforoee a ɛwɔ subon no nifa fam ntentenso no. Na ɔhye no twam fa En-semes nsu no ano, na ɛkɔpem En-rogel.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no foro fa Hinom ba bon no mu, Yebusifo nkyɛn mu nifa fam, ɛne Yerusalem; na ɔhye no foro kɔ bepɔw a ɛwɔ Hinom bon no ntentenso wɔ atɔe wɔ Refaim bon no benkum fam awiei no atifi.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no hima fi bepɔw no atifi kɔ Neftoa asuti no ho, na efi hɔ kɔ Efron bepɔw so nkurow ho, na ɔhye no hima kɔ Baala a ɛne Kiriat-yearim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no kɔntɔn fi Baala kɔ atɔe, Seir bepɔw ho, na ɛsen kɔ Har-yearim, ɛne Kesalon, nkyɛn mu wɔ benkum fam; na esian kɔ Bet-semes, na ɛsen kɔ Timna;

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: na ɔhye no fi kɔ Ekron nkyɛn mu benkum fam, na ɛkɔntɔn kɔ Sikron, na etwam kɔ Baala bepɔw no so, na efi kɔ Yabneel, na ɔhye no kɔpem po no ano.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Na ofi hɔ foro kɔɔ Debirfo ho; nso kan no na Debir din ne Kiriat-sefer.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Na Yefune ba Kaleb de, ɔmaa no kyɛfa, Yudafo mu, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ Yosua no: Anak n’agya Arba kurow a ɛne Hebron.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Na Kaleb tuu Anak mma baasa no fii hɔ, Sesai ne Ahiman ne Talmai, Anak asefo.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Na Kaleb kae sɛ: Nea ɔbɛbɔ Kiriat-sefer na ɔbɛfa no, mede me babea Aksa mɛma no aware.

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, and Caleb let him marry Achsah.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Kaleb ne nua Kenas ba Otniel kɔfae, na ɔde ne babea Aksa maa no aware.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no kɔɔ Otniel nkyɛn no, Otniel ka kyerɛɛ Aksa sɛ ommisa n’agya [Kaleb] hɔ asase bi; na ɔbea no fi n’afurum so sii fam; na Kaleb bisaa no sɛ: Ɛdɛn na wohwehwɛ?

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma me akyɛde bi ɛ, na nifa asase na wode ama me nti, ma me mmasu nso. Na ɔmaa no atifi mmasu ne anafo mmasu. Yuda mma no kyɛfa

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Eyi ne Yuda mma abusuakuw no agyapade, sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: ne Lebaot ne Silhim ne Ain ne Rimon: Ne nyinaa si nkurow aduonu akron ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: Saaraim ne Aditaim ne Gedera ne Gederotaim: Nkurow dunan ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ne Gederot, Bet-dagon ne Naama ne Makeda: Nkurow dunsia ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Yebusifo a wɔte Yerusalem no de, Yudafo no antumi antu wɔn, na Yebusifo no ne Yudafo no tenaa Yerusalem de abesi nnɛ.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Na Efraimfo hye, sɛ wɔn mmusua te, ni: Wɔn agyapade hye ne Atarot-adar apuei de kosi atifi wɔ Bet-horon;

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: ne nkurow a woyiyi maa Efraimfo wɔ Manasefo agyapade mu no, nkurow no nyinaa ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Nanso wɔantu Kanaanfo a wɔte Geser no, na Kanaanfo no atena Efraim mu ayɛ nkoa de abesi nnɛ.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Tapua asase no yɛɛ Manase de, na Tapua kurow a ɛwɔ Manase hye so no yɛɛ Efraimfo de.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Na nkurow a Manase nyae Isakar ne Aser ntam ne Bet-sean ne ɛho nkurow, ne Yibleam ne ɛho nkurow, ne wɔn a wɔte Dor ne ɛho nkurow, ne En-dorfo ne ɛho nkurow, ne Taanakfo ne ɛho nkurow, ne Megidofo ne ɛho nkurow, nkoko abiɛsa so amantow no.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Nanso Manase mma antumi antu nkurow no mufo, na Kanaanfo no pɛɛ asase no so tena.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Na Israelfo ho yɛɛ den no, wɔhyɛɛ Kanaanfo no maa ɔsom adwuma, yii tow, na mmom, otu de wɔantu wɔn korakora. Yosef asefo nya kyɛfa foforo

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef mma no bɛka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ: Efi dɛn so na woma me agyapade ntonto biako ne susuhama biako? Na me de, meyɛ ɔman kɛse, efisɛ AWURADE ahyira me de abedu sesɛɛ.

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Na Yosua ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ woyɛ ɔman kɛse a, foro kɔ kwae no mu kobu hɔ fa, Perisifo ne abran akɛse no asase so, efisɛ wonsen Efraim mmepɔw so.

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef asefo no kae sɛ: Bepɔw no nso yɛn, nso Kanaanfo a wɔte tataw mu hɔ nyinaa wɔ dade nteaseɛnam, wɔn a wɔte Bet-sean ne ɛho nkurow mu ne wɔn a wɔte Yesreel bon no mu nyinaa.

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Na Yosua ka kyerɛɛ Yosef fi, Efraim ne Manase sɛ: Ɔman kɛse ne wo, na wowɔ ahoɔden kɛse, ɛnyɛ ntonto biako pɛ na wubenya,

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: na mmom bepɔw no nyɛ wo de; ɛwom sɛ ɛyɛ kwae de, nanso bu fa, kosi nea ano bɛka; na Kanaanfo no, sɛ wɔwɔ dade nteaseɛnam na wɔyɛ ahoɔdenfo po a, wubetu wɔn.

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo asafo no nyinaa behyiae Silo, na wosii ahyiae ntamadan no wɔ hɔ, na wɔbrɛɛ asase no ase wɔn anim.

english_verse: There were still seven tribes without any land,
translation_verse: Na aka Israelfo mu mmusuakuw ason a wɔnkyɛɛ agyapade mmaa wɔn.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna mmarima no sɔre kɔe; na Yosua hyɛɛ wɔn a wɔrekɔ akɔkyerɛw asase no ho asɛm no sɛ: Monkɔ nkokyin asase no so na monkyerɛw ho asɛm, na monsan mmra me nkyɛn, na mentwe ntonto memma mo, AWURADE anim ha wɔ Silo.

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Na mmarima no siim kɔe kɔfaa asase no so, na wɔkyerɛw no sɛnea nkurow no tetee nkyekyem ason de hyɛɛ nhoma bi so, na wɔsan baa Yosua nkyɛn Silo nsra mu.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Na Yosua twee ntonto maa wɔn, AWURADE anim wɔ Silo, na Yosua kyɛɛ asase no mu wɔ hɔ maa Israelfo sɛ wɔn nkyekyem te.

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminfo abusuakuw ntonto bae sɛ wɔn mmusua te; na wɔn ntonto no hye fi Yuda mma ne Yosef mma ntam.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔn benkum fam hye fi Yordan; na ɔhye no foro fa Yeriko nkyɛn mu benkum fam, na ɛforo kɔ bepɔw no so kɔ atɔe, na ano kodu Bet-awen sare so.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no hima na ɛkɔntɔn kɔ atɔe fam fa bepɔw a ɛda Bet-horon anim nifa fam no, na ano kodu Kiriat-baal a ɛne Kiriat-yearim, Yudafo kurow bi. Atɔe fam de ne no.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Na nifa fam de fi Kiriat-yearim kurotia, na ɔhye no fi kɔ atɔe, na efi kɔ Neftoa asuti ho.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no sian kɔ bepɔw a ɛda Hinom ba bon anim a ɛwɔ Refaim bon mu benkum fam no ano noho, na esian Hinom bon no kɔ Yebusifo nifa fam nkyɛn mu, na esian kɔ En-rogel ho.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Na ehima kɔ benkum fam, na efi kɔ En-semes, na efi kɔ Gelilot a ɛda Adumim aforoee no ntentenso, na esian kɔ Ruben ba Bohan bo no ho.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na etwam fa benkum fam nkyɛn mu Araba ntentenso, na esian kɔ Araba.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no twam kɔ Bet-hogla benkum fam nkyɛn mu, na ano kodu Nkyene-Po benkum fam dɔnnɔn no ho, Yordan nifa fam awiei. Eyi ne nifa fam hye.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Na Yordan ne n’apuei fam hye. Eyi ne Benyaminfo agyapade sɛ n’ahye te hyia sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Na ntonto a ɛto so abien no ba maa Simeon, Simeonfo abusuakuw no, sɛ wɔn mmusua te; na wɔn agyapade da Yudafo agyapade ntam.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: Bet-lebaot ne Saruhen: Nkurow dumiɛnsa ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Na efi hɔ twam kɔ apuei de kɔ Gat-hefer, Et-kasin, na efi Rimon a ehima de kɔ Nea.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Ain, Rimon ne Eter ne Asan: Nkurow anan ne ɛho nkuraa;

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: ne nkuraa a ɛdeda nkurow yi ho hyia de kosi Baalat-beer nyinaa, Ramat a ɛda nifa. Eyi ne Simeon mma abusuakuw no agyapade sɛ wɔn mmusua te.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Yudafo kyɛfa no bi na ɛyɛɛ Simeonfo agyapade, efisɛ Yudafo kyɛfa no boroo wɔn so, enti Simeonfo nyaa agyapade wɔn agyapade no mu.

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no kɔntɔn kɔ benkum fam de kɔ Hanaton, na ano kodu Yifta-el bon no mu;

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: ne Katat ne Nahalal ne Simron ne Yidala ne Betlehem: Nkurow dumien ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Eyi ne Sebulon mma agyapade, sɛ wɔn mmusua te, nkurow no ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Eyi ne Isakarfo abusuakuw no agyapade, sɛ wɔn mmusua te, nkurow no ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Na ɛsan kɔ owiapuei de kɔ Bet-dagon, na ɛkɔpem Sebulon ne Yifta-el bon mu, Bet-emek ne Neiel benkum fam, na efi kɔ Kabul benkum fam,

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: ne Ebron ne Rehob ne Hamon ne Kana de kosi Sidon Kɛse.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
translation_verse: Na ɔhye no kɔpem Tabor ne Sahasima ne Bet-Semes, na wɔn hye no ano kodu Yordan ano: Nkurow dunsia ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Eyi ne Naftalifo abusuakuw agyapade, sɛ wɔn mmusua te: Nkurow no ne ɛho nkuraa.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Eyinom ne nkurow a woyiyi totoo hɔ maa Israelfo nyinaa ne ɔhɔho a wabɛsoɛ wɔn mu, sɛ obiara a okum ɔkra bi nsapa mu no nguan nkɔ hɔ na wanwu mogya ho werefo nsam, akosi sɛ obegyina asafo no anim.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Yosua sɛ:

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Munyi guankɔbea nkurow a menam Mose so mekaa mo ho asɛm no,

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: Na nea oguan kɔ saa nkurow yi bi mu no nnyina kurow no pon ano, na ɔnka ne nsɛm no ngu kurow no mu mpanyimfo asom, na wɔmfa no nkɔ wɔn nkyɛn, kurow no mu, na wɔmma no tenabea na ɔne wɔn ntena.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Na sɛ mogya ho werefo no tiw no ba a, wɔmmfa onipakumfo no nnhyɛ ne nsa, efisɛ onnim na ɔbɔɔ ne yɔnko no, nanso bere a atwam no, na ɔntan no.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Na ɔntena nkurow no mu nkosi sɛ obegyina asafo no anim na wɔabu no atɛn, nkosi sɛ ɔsɔfopanyin a ɔwɔ so saa bere no bewu; ɛno ansa na onipakumfo no nsan nkɔ ne kurom ne ne fi, na ɔnkɔ kurow a ofi hɔ guanee no mu.

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Ɛnna woyiyii Kedes wɔ Galilea, Naftali bepɔw so, ne Sekem, Efraim bepɔw so, ne Kiriat-arba a ɛne Hebron wɔ Yuda bepɔw so.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Yordan agya, Yeriko apuei nso woyii Beser, sare so asasetaw so de fii Ruben abusuakuw mu, ne Ramot wɔ Gilead de fii Gad abusuakuw mu, ne Golan wɔ Basan de fii Manase abusuakuw mu mae.

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo de wɔn agyapade mu nkurow yi ne ɛho mfikyisaase maa Lewifo, sɛnea AWURADE hyɛe no.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Na ntonto no bae maa Kehatfo mmusua, na ɔsɔfo Aaron mma a wofi Lewifo mu no nam ntonto so nyaa Yuda abusuakuw ne Simeon abusuakuw ne Benyamin abusuakuw mu nkurow dumiɛnsa.

english_verse: towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Na kurow no ho mfuwa ne nkuraa no de, wɔde maa Yefune ba Kaleb sɛ agyapade.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Na Israelfo nam ntonto so de nkurow yi ne ɛho mfikyisase maa Lewifo, sɛnea AWURADE nam Mose so hyɛe no.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Aaron mma asɔfo no nkurow nyinaa si nkurow dumiɛnsa ne ɛho mfikyisase.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Gersonfo nkurow nyinaa, sɛ wɔn mmusua te no, esi nkurow dumiɛnsa ne ɛho mfikyisase.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de asase a ɔkaa ho ntam sɛ ɔde bɛma wɔn agyanom no nyinaa maa Israel, na wodii so tenaa so.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa wɔn asomdwoe hyiae, sɛnea ɔkaa wɔn agyanom ntam no ara, na wɔn atamfo nyinaa mu biara annyina wɔn anim; AWURADE de wɔn atamfo no nyinaa hyɛɛ wɔn nsa.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Asɛm pa a AWURADE kaa Israel fi no nyinaa mu asɛm biara antɔ fam, ne nyinaa baa mu.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yosua frɛɛ Rubenfo ne Gadfo ne Manase abusuakuw fa no,

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Moannyaw mo nuanom nna dodow yi de abedu nnɛ da yi, na moahwɛ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn mmara nsɛm no adi so.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Na afei AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn de mo nuanom atena ase dwoodwoo, sɛnea ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn no; enti monsan nkɔ mo ntamadan mu, mo agyapade asase a AWURADE akoa Mose de maa mo Yordan agya no so.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Na mo ho yiye nko na monhwɛ, na munni ahyɛde ne mmara a AWURADE akoa Mose hyɛɛ mo no so, na monnɔ AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn, na monnantew n’akwan nyinaa so, na mummu ne mmara nsɛm, na momfam ne ho na monsom no mo koma nyinaa ne mo kra nyinaa mu.

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tee sɛ wɔka sɛ: Hwɛ, Rubenfo ne Gadfo ne Manase abusuakuw fa no asi afɔremuka wɔ Kanaan asase no anim, Yordan ho asase no so, ɔfa a ɛyɛ Israelfo de no so.

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no tee no, wɔboaboaa Israelfo asafo no nyinaa ano Silo, sɛ wɔretu wɔn so sa.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no somaa ɔsɔfo Eleasar ba Pinehas kɔɔ Rubenfo ne Gadfo ne Manase abusuakuw fa no nkyɛn Gilead asase so,

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: na wɔde mmapɔmma du kaa ne ho, Israel mmusuakuw no mu biara mu bapɔmma biako; na wɔn mu biara yɛ ne mpanyimfi ti, Israel mpem no mu.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Na woduu Rubenfo ne Gadfo ne Manase abusuakuw fa no nkyɛn Gilead asase so, na wɔne wɔn kasae sɛ:

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE asafo no nyinaa se ni: Ɔfom bɛn na mode afom Israel Nyankopɔn yi sɛ nnɛ moadan mo ho afi AWURADE akyi, na moasi afɔremuka afa, na moatew AWURADE anim atua nnɛ yi!

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: So Peor mfomso a yennya nnwiraa yɛn ho mfii mu de besi nnɛ yi na ɔhaw baa AWURADE asafo so no nnɔɔ yɛn so?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Na mo de, nnɛ moresan afi AWURADE akyi? Na moretew AWURADE anim atua nnɛ yi, ɔkyena ne bo befuw Israel asafo no nyinaa.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ mo sodi asase no ho agu fi a, ɛnne muntwa mmra AWURADE sodi asase a AWURADE tenabea si hɔ no so na mommɛfa asase nni so wɔ yɛn mu; na AWURADE anim atua na monntew, na yɛn anim atua nso monntew, mo afɔremuka a musi kaa AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn afɔremuka no ho mu.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: So ɛnyɛ Serah ba Akan na ɔfomee ahyirade no mu, na abufuw baa Israel asafo no nyinaa so? Nso ɛnyɛ ɔno nko na ɔsɛee, ne mfomso no mu.

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Sɛ yesii afɔremuka sɛ yɛresan afi AWURADE akyi anaasɛ yɛrebɔ so ɔhyew afɔre anaa aduan afɔre anaasɛ yɛrebɔ so asomdwoe afɔre a, ɛnne AWURADE mmebisa yɛn.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Enti na yɛkae sɛ: Momma yensi afɔremuka mfa, ɛnyɛ ɔhyew afɔre na ɛnyɛ okum afɔre nti,
