translation_verse: Na Yotam twee ne ho guan kɔɔ Beer kɔtenaa hɔ, ne nua Abimelek ho suro nti.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Na Abimelek dii Israel so mfe abiɛsa.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Na Sekemfo no maa nnipa kɔtɛw no wɔ mmepɔw atifi, na wɔbɔɔ wɔn a wɔbɛfaa wɔn nkyɛn ɔkwan no so nyinaa apoo. Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Abimelek.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Na Ebed ba Gaal ne ne nuanom bae bɛsen kɔɔ Sekem; na Sekemfo no de wɔn ani too no so.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Na wofii adi kɔɔ mfuw mu kɔtetew wɔn bobe nturo mu aba na wokyikyii nsa, na wɔtoo anigye nnwom, na wɔkɔɔ wɔn nyame fi, na wodidi nomee, na wɔdomee Abimelek.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Na Ebed ba Gaal kae sɛ: Hena ne Abimelek, na hena ne Sekem a yɛnsom no? So ɛnyɛ Yerubaal ba ne no na Sebul yɛ ne safohene? Monsom Sekem agya Hamor mmarima no ɛ, na ɛdɛn nti na yɛn de, yɛnsom no?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Na hena na ɔde ɔman yi bɛhyɛ me nsa na anka matu Abimelek so. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Abimelek sɛ: Ma wo dɔm nnɔɔso na fi bra.

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Na kurow no so safohene Sebul tee Ebed ba Gaal nsɛm no, ne bo fuwii,

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Na afei sɔre anadwo, wo ne ɔman a wɔka wo ho no, na kɔtɛw wuram.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa a owia repue no, sɔre ntɛm bɛtow hyɛ kurow no so, na hwɛ, ɔno ne ɔman a wɔka ne ho no befi adi abehyia wo, na woayɛ no sɛnea wubetumi.

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Abimelek ne ɛdɔm a wɔka no ho no nyinaa sɔree anadwo, na wɔnam akuw anan bɛtetɛw Sekem.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Na Ebed ba Gaal fii adi kogyinaa kurow no pon ano. Na Abimelek ne nkurɔfo a wɔka no ho no sɔre fii atɛwee hɔ.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Na Gaal huu ɔman no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Sebul sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔman bi fi mmepɔw no atifi resian. Na Sebul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mmepɔw no sunsuma na wuhu sɛ nnipa no.

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Na Gaal kae bio sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔman bi fi asase funuma so resian ba, na kuw biako fi Elon-meonenim kwan so reba.

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Na Sebul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Afei, ɛhe na w’ano a ɛkae sɛ: Hena ne Abimelek a yɛnsom no no wɔ? So ɛnyɛ ɔman a wubuu wɔn abomfiaa no ni? Afei fi adi ɛ, na wo ne wɔn nkɔko.

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Na Gaal fii adi dii Sekemfo no anim, na ɔne Abimelek kɔkoe.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek pam no, na oguanee n’anim, na nnipa pii totɔe de kosii kurow no pon ano.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek tenaa Aruma; na Sebul pam Gaal ne ne nuanom no sɛ wɔnntena Sekem.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, ɔman no fii adi kokɔɔ wuram; na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Abimelek.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa ɔman no buu wɔn mu akuw abiɛsa, na ɔkɔtɛw wuram. Na ɔhwɛe, na hwɛ, ɔman no refi adi afi kurow no mu, na ɔsɔre hyɛɛ wɔn kunkum wɔn.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ne asafokuw a wɔka ne ho no bɔɔ kirididi kogyinaa kurow no pon ano, na asafokuw abien no tow hyɛɛ wɔn a wɔwɔ wuram nyinaa so kunkum wɔn.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek ne kurow no koe da mu no nyinaa, na ɔfaa kurow no, na okum nnipa a wɔwɔ mu no, na ɔbɔɔ kurow no, na ɔde nkyene petee so.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Na Sekem abankɛse mufo nyinaa tee no, wɔkɔɔ onyame Berit fi aban mu.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Abimelek sɛ Sekem aban mufo nyinaa aboaboa wɔn ho ano.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Abimelek foro kɔɔ Salmon bepɔw so, ɔne ɔman a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa, na Abimelek faa akuma kurae na okotwaa dubaa, na ɔmaa so bɔɔ ne kɔn ho, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔman a wɔka ne ho no sɛ: Nea moahu sɛ mayɛ yi, monka mo ho nyɛ sɛ meyɛe no.

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa twitwaa nnubaa de dii Abimelek akyi de beguu aban no ho, na wɔde gya too aban no mu guu wɔn so. Na Sekem abankɛse no mu nnipa nyinaa nso wuwui, mmarima ne mmea bɛyɛ apem.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Abimelek siim kɔɔ Tebes kɔbɔɔ Tebes so nsra, na ɔfae.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Na abantenten dennen bi wɔ kurow no mu, na ɛhɔ na mmarima ne mmea nyinaa ne kurow no mufo nyinaa guanguan kɔe na wɔtoo wɔn ho mu, na wɔforo kɔɔ aban no atifi.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Na Abimelek duu aban no ho bɛkoe, na otwiw bɛn aban no pon ano sɛ ɔde gya rebɛhyew.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea bi tow owiyammoba bɔɔ Abimelek ti de pɛtɛw ne tikora.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔfrɛɛ n’abofra a ɔso n’akode ntɛm ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Twe wo nkrante kum me, na wɔanka wɔ me ho sɛ ɔbea na okum no. Na n’abofra no de nkrante wɔɔ no ma ɔtɔe.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no hui sɛ Abimelek atɔ no, wɔn nyinaa kokɔɔ wɔn tenabea.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tuaa Abimelek bɔne a ɔyɛɛ n’agya, sɛ okum ne nuanom aduɔsɔn no so ka.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Na Sekem mmarima no bɔne nyinaa nso, Onyankopɔn ma ebuaa wɔn atifi, na Yerubaal ba Yotam nnome no baa wɔn so.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Na Abimelek akyi no, nea ɔsɔre begyee Israel ne Pua ba Tola a ɔyɛ Isakarni Dodo ba; na ɔtenaa Samir, Efraim bepɔw so.

english_verse: Tola was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Na odii Israel anim mfe aduonu abiɛsa. Na owui, na wosiee no Samir.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Na n’akyi no, Gileadni Yair sɔree, na obuu Israel atɛn mfe aduonu abien.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Na Yair wui, na wosiee no Kamon. Israelfo hyɛ wɔn atamfo ase bio

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo kɔɔ so yɛɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne, na wɔsom Baalim ne Astarot ne Siria anyame ne Sidon anyame ne Moab anyame ne Amonfo anyame ne Filistifo anyame, na wogyaw AWURADE hɔ na wɔansom no.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abufuw dɛw hyɛɛ Israel, na ɔtɔn wɔn hyɛɛ Filistifo ne Amonfo nsa.

english_verse: So the same year that Jair died, Israel's army was crushed by these two nations. For
translation_verse: Na wɔhom Israelfo so haw wɔn afe no ara mu. Mfe dunwɔtwe na wodii Israelfo a wɔwɔ Yordan agya, Amorifo asase so wɔ Gilead no nyinaa so.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Na Gilead man, wɔn mu atitiriw sisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Hena ne ɔbarima a ɔne Amonfo no befi ase ako? Ɔno na onkodi Gileadfo nyinaa ti.

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Na Amonfo no betwaa Yordan, ne Yuda ne Benyamin ne Efraim fi nso bɛkoe; na Israel ho hiaa wɔn sɛ.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israelfo su frɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Yɛayɛ wo bɔne, sɛ yɛagyaw yɛn Nyankopɔn na yɛakɔsom Baalim.

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Yɛayɛ bɔne! Wo de, yɛ yɛn sɛ eye w’ani so nyinaa, ogye nko na gye yɛn nnɛ da yi.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Na Amonfo no hyia bae bɛbɔɔ nsra Gilead. Na Israelfo nso boaboaa wɔn ho ano kɔbɔɔ nsra Mispa.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: na wɔka kyerɛɛ Yefta sɛ: Bra bɛyɛ yɛn safohene, na yɛne Amonfo nkɔko.

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Na Yefta ka kyerɛɛ Gilead mpanyimfo no sɛ: So ɛnyɛ mo ara na motan me na mopam me fii m’agya fi no? Na ɛdɛn nti na moba me nkyɛn afei a mowɔ ahohia mu yi?

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Na Gilead mpanyimfo no ka kyerɛɛ Yefta sɛ: Ɛno nti na afei yɛasan aba wo nkyɛn yi, na wo ne yɛn nkɔ na yɛne Amonfo nkɔko, na yɛ yɛn ti, Gileadfo nyinaa so.

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Na Yefta ka kyerɛɛ Gilead mpanyimfo no sɛ: Sɛ mode me san kɔ sɛ me ne Amonfo nkɔko na AWURADE de wɔn hyɛ me nsa a, me na minni mo ti anaa?

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Na Gilead mpanyimfo no ka kyerɛɛ Yefta sɛ: AWURADE nyɛ yɛne wo ntam dansefo. Ampa ara nea wuse yi, ɛno ara na yɛbɛyɛ.

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yefta ne Gilead mpanyimfo no siim bae, na ɔman no de no sii wɔn ti ne safohene. Na Yefta kɔkaa ne nsɛm nyinaa AWURADE anim wɔ Mispa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yefta somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Amonfo hene no nkyɛn sɛ: Asɛm bɛn na me ne wo wɔ na woreba me so ne m’asase abɛko yi?

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Na Amonfo hene no ka kyerɛɛ Yefta abɔfo no sɛ: Efisɛ Israel faa m’asase bere a wofii Misraim reba no, de fi Arnon kosi Yabok ne Yordan ano. Na afei dan ma me komm.

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Na Yefta san somaa abɔfo bio kɔɔ Amonfo hene no nkyɛn

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ Yefta se ni: Israel amfa Moab asase ne Amonfo asase bi,

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: na mmom wofi Misraim no, Israel nantew sare so kosii Mmɛw-Po ano, na wɔbaa Kades.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Na Israel somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Edom hene nkyɛn sɛ: Ma mintwam w’asase so ɛ! Na Edom hene no antie. Na ɔsoma kɔɔ Moab hene nkyɛn nso, na wampene. Na Israel tenaa Kades.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Na wɔnantew sare so kotwaa Edom asase ne Moab asase ho kɔntɔnkrɔn, na wobefii Moab asase no apuei, na wɔbɛbɔɔ nsra Arnon agya noho, na wɔamma Moab asase so, efisɛ Arnon ne Moab hye.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Amorifo hene Sihon a ɔyɛ Hesbonhene no nkyɛn, na Israel ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma yentwam w’asase so nkɔ m’afa.

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Na Sihon annye Israel anni, sɛ ɔbɛma wɔafa ne hye so, na Sihon boaa ne man nyinaa ano, na wɔbɛbɔɔ nsra Yahas, na ɔne Israel bɛkoe.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, de Sihon ne ne man nyinaa hyɛɛ Israel nsa, na wokunkum wɔn, na Israel faa Amorifo a wɔte asase no so no asase nyinaa dii so,

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: na wɔfaa Amorifo asase nyinaa fi Arnon ano kosi Yabok ano, na efi sare so kosi Yordan ano.

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: So ɛnyɛ nea wo nyame Kemos de maa wo sɛ di so na wobɛfa adi so anaa? Na ade biara a AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn agye ama yɛn sɛ yenni so no, ɛno na yɛbɛfa adi so.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Na afei, so wuye sen Moab hene Sipor ba Balak? So ɔham na ɔne Israel hamee anaasɛ ɔko na ɔne wɔn koe?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Na me de, menyɛɛ wo bɔne bi ɛ, na wo na woreyɛ me bɔne sɛ wo ne me rebɛko yi. AWURADE temmufo na ommu Israelfo ne Amonfo ntam atɛn nnɛ.

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Nanso Amonfo hene antie Yefta nsɛm a ɔsoma kɔka kyerɛɛ no no.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Na AWURADE honhom baa Yefta so, na ɔfaa Gilead ne Manase sen kɔɔ Gilead-mispe, na ofi Gilead-mispe twaam kɔɔ Amonfo no so.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Na Yefta hyɛɛ AWURADE bɔ sɛ: Sɛ wode Amonfo no hyɛ me nsa a,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: ɛnne nea ebefi me fi apon ano abehyia me da a meresan mafi Amonfo so dwoodwoo no, ɛbɛyɛ AWURADE de, na mede mɛbɔ afɔre mu.

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yefta twaam kɔɔ Amonfo no so ne wɔn kɔkoe; na AWURADE de wɔn hyɛɛ ne nsa.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yefta baa ne fi Mispa. Na hwɛ, ne babea de mpintin ne asaw fii adi behyiaa no, nso na odi no bakoro, onni ɔbabarima anaa ɔbabea ka ne ho.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Na ohuu no no, osunsuanee ne ntade mu kae sɛ: Ao! Me ba, ɔbrɛ na woabrɛ me ase, na worebɛhow me werɛ! Efisɛ mabue m’ano mama AWURADE, na mintumi mensan m’akyi.

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: M’agya, woanya abue w’ano ama AWURADE a, ɛnne yɛ me sɛnea afi w’ano no, sɛ AWURADE anya adi were ama wo, w’atamfo Amonfo no so yi.

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya bio sɛ: Wɔnyɛ eyi mma me: Gya me kwan asram abien, na minsian menkɔ mmepɔw so, na me ne me mfɛfo nkosu me mmabaabere.

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Kɔ! Na ogyaa no kwan asram abien. Na ɔne ne mfɛfo kɔe, na okosuu ne mmabaabere mmepɔw so.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Na asram abien duu no, ɔsan baa n’agya nkyɛn; na ɔyɛɛ no sɛnea ne bɔ a ɔhyɛe no te; na wanhu ɔbarima biara. Na ɛyɛɛ atɔremude Israel mu sɛ:

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: Daa afirihyia Israel mmabea de su kɔkae Gileadni Yefta babea no afe mu no nnanan.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Na Efraim mmarima hyiae, na wotwaam kɔɔ Safon, na wɔka kyerɛɛ Yefta sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wutwaam kɔe ne Amonfo kɔkoe, na yɛn de, woamfrɛ yɛn na yɛne wo ankɔ? Yɛde ogya bɛhyew wo fi agu wo so.

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Na Yefta ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Me ne me man nyinaa ne Amonfo nyaa manso kɛse; na meteɛɛm mefrɛɛ mo no, moannye me amfi wɔn nsam;

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: na mihuu sɛ momma mmegye me no, mede me nkwa metoo me nsam, na mesen mekɔɔ Amonfo no so, na AWURADE de wɔn hyɛɛ me nsa, na ɛdɛn na moforo ba me so ne me abɛko nnɛ yi?

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na Yefta boaa Gilead mmarima nyinaa ano na ɔne Efraim koe; na Gilead mmarima no kum Efraim, efisɛ wose: Mo Gileadfo aguanfo, mowɔ Efraim mu, ne Manase mu.

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Na Gilead faa Yordan atwae twaree Efraim; na sɛ Efraim aguanfo no mu bi ka sɛ: Ma mintwa, a, ɛnne Gilead mmarima no bisaa no sɛ: Woyɛ Efraimni anaa? Na ose: Dabi,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: wɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Ɛnne ka sɛ: Shibolet, na sɛ ɔka sɛ: Sibolet, efisɛ ontumi nka no yiye a, na wɔakyere no akum no Yordan atwae hɔ. Na saa bere no Efraimfo ɔpeduanan abien na ɛtotɔe.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Na Yefta dii Israel anim mfe asia. Na Gileadni Yefta wui, na wosiee no Gilead nkurow no bi mu. Ibsan, Elon ne Abdon

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na Yefta akyi no, Ibsan a ofi Betlehem dii Israel anim

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Na Ibsan wui, na wosiee no Betlehem.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Na n’akyi no, Sebulonni Elon dii Israel anim mfe du.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Na Sebulonni Elon wui, na wosiee no Ayalon, Sebulon asase so.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Na Hilel ba Abdon a ɔyɛ Piratonni no wui, na wosiee no Piraton wɔ Efraim asase a ɛwɔ Amalekfo bepɔw so no so.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Na Israelfo kɔɔ so yɛɛ nea ɛyɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne, na AWURADE de wɔn hyɛɛ Filistifo nsa mfirihyia aduanan.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi wɔ hɔ a ofi Sora a ofi Danfo abusua bi mu a ne din de Manoa; na ne yere yɛ obonin, na ɔnwo.

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea no bae bɛka kyerɛɛ ne kunu sɛ: Onyankopɔn nipa bi aba me nkyɛn, na n’anim yɛ hu pa ara sɛ Onyankopɔn bɔfo anim, na mammisa no nea ofi, na ɔno nso ankyerɛ me ne din.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ, worebenyinsɛn awo babarima; na afei nnom bobesa anaa nsa bi, na nni biribi a ɛho ntew; na abofra no bɛyɛ Onyankopɔn hotuafo afi yafunum de akosi ne wuda.

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Na Manoa yii AWURADE mpae sɛ: O, AWURADE, ma Onyankopɔn nipa a wosomaa no no mmra yɛn nkyɛn bio, na ɔmmɛkyerɛ yɛn nea yɛnyɛ abofra a wɔrebɛwo no no.

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn tiee Manoa, na Onyankopɔn bɔfo no baa ɔbea no nkyɛn bio, na ɔwɔ afum a ne kunu Manoa nka ne ho.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no yɛɛ ntɛm tutuu mmirika kɔka kyerɛɛ ne kunu sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔbarima a ɔbaa me nkyɛn nnaano no abeyi ne ho adi akyerɛ me.

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Na Manoa sɔre dii ne yere no akyi na ɔbaa ɔbarima no nkyɛn, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wone ɔbarima a wo ne ɔbea no kasae no?

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Na ose: Mene no. Na Manoa kae sɛ: Afei wo nsɛm no ba mu a, ɛdɛn ne abofra no ahyɛde, na dɛn na ɔnyɛ?

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ Manoa sɛ: Nea misee ɔbea no nyinaa ho na ɔnhwɛ ne ho yiye:

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Onnni ade biara a efi bobe mu, na ɔnnnom bobesa anaa nsa biara, na ade biara a ɛho ntew nso, onnni; nea mahyɛ no nyinaa, onni so.

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Na Manoa ka kyerɛɛ ɔbɔfo no sɛ: Ma yensianka wo na yensiesie apapowa bi mma wo ansa.

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ Manoa sɛ: Sɛ wusianka me po a, merenni w’aduan no bi; na sɛ wobɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ama AWURADE a, bɔ ɛ! Na Manoa nnim sɛ ɔyɛ AWURADE bɔfo.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Na Manoa ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE bɔfo no sɛ: Wo din de dɛn? Na sɛ wo nsɛm no nya ba mu a, yɛahyɛ wo anuonyam.

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no see no sɛ: Ɛdɛn na wubisa me din a ɛyɛ nwonwa yi?

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Na Manoa faa apapowa ne aduan, na ɔde bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ɔbotan no so maa AWURADE, nea ɔyɛ anwonwade no, na Manoa ne ne yere hwɛe.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Na ogyaframa no resɔre afi afɔremuka no so akɔ ɔsoro no, AWURADE bɔfo no foro faa afɔremuka no so gyaframa no mu kɔɔ ɔsoro. Na Manoa ne ne yere hwɛe, na wɔde wɔn anim butubutuw fam.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo no ammeyi ne ho ankyerɛ Manoa ne ne yere bio. Ɛno na Manoa huu sɛ ɛyɛ AWURADE bɔfo.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Na Manoa ka kyerɛɛ ne yere sɛ: Owu na yɛrebewuwu, sɛ yɛahu Nyankopɔn yi.

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Na ne yere no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE pɛ sɛ okum yɛn a, anka wannye yɛn nsam hyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre, na anka wanyi eyinom nyinaa ankyerɛ yɛn, na anka wamma yɛante nsɛm a ɛte sɛɛ yi saa bere yi.

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no woo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Samson. Na abofra no nyinii, na AWURADE hyiraa no.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE honhom fii ase kekaa no wɔ ne mu, Dan nsra mu, Sora ne Estaol ntam.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Na Samson sian kɔɔ Timna, na okohuu ɔbea bi wɔ hɔ a ɔyɛ Filistifo mmabea no bi.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Na ɔforo bae bɛka kyerɛɛ n’agya ne ne na sɛ: Makohu ɔbea bi wɔ Timna, Filistifo mma mu, na monkɔfa no mmrɛ me nware.

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Na n’agya ne ne na ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wo nuanom mmabea ne me man nyinaa mu nni ɔbea bi, na worekɔ akɔware ɔbea Filistifo momonotofo no mu? Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Ɔno na kɔfa no brɛ me, na ɔno na ɔsɔ m’ani.

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Na n’agya ne ne na nnim sɛ eyi fi AWURADE, na ɔrepɛ Filistifo ho kwan; efisɛ saa bere no na Filistifo di Israel so.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Na Samson ne n’agya ne ne na siim kɔɔ Timna. Na woduu Timna bobe nturo ho, na hwɛ, gyataforo bi boboom hyiaa no.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE honhom sii no so, na ɔtetew no mu, sɛnea wɔtetew abirekyi ba mu, nanso na hwee nkita ne nsam. Na wanka nea ɔyɛe no ankyerɛ n’agya ne ne na.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Na osiim kɔe ne ɔbea no kɔkasae, na ɔsɔɔ Samson ani.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa bi kurae dii no akwanakwan, na okoduu n’agya ne ne na nkyɛn, na ɔmaa wɔn bi dii; nanso wanka ankyerɛ wɔn sɛ gyata no yam na oyii ɛwo no.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Na n’agya siim kɔɔ ɔbea no nkyɛn, na Samson tow pon wɔ hɔ, efisɛ saa na mmerante taa yɛ.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Na wohuu no no, wɔde nnamfonom aduasa bɛkaa no ho.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: na sɛ moantumi ankyerɛ me a, mo nso momma me nkamisaa aduasa ne ntade nsakraho aduasa. Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: To wo aborɔme no na yentie.

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Odidifo mu na aduan fi bae, na ɔhoɔdenfo mu na adɔkɔdɔkɔde fi bae. Na wɔantumi ankyerɛ aborɔme no ase nnansa.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so ason no, wɔka kyerɛɛ Samson yere no sɛ: Daadaa wo kunu na ɔnkyerɛ yɛn aborɔme no ase, na yɛamfa ogya anhyew wo ne w’agya fi! So yɛn fow nti na mubehyiaa yɛn?

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Na Samson yere no su guu no so kae sɛ: Ɔtan nko na wotan me na wonnɔ me. Woato me nkurɔfo aborɔme, nso wonkyerɛɛ me ase. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, m’agya ne me na po menkyerɛɛ wɔn, na wo na menkyerɛ wo anaa?

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Na osu guu no so nnansɔn a apontow no gu so no nyinaa. Na da a ɛto so ason no, ɔka kyerɛɛ no, efisɛ na ɔhaw no. Na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkurɔfo no.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Na kurow no mu mmarima ka kyerɛɛ no da a ɛto so ason no ansa na owia retɔ sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ dɔkɔdɔkɔ sen ɛwo, na ɛdɛn na ne ho yɛ den sen gyata? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Moamfa me nantwi amfɛtɛw a, anka moanhu m’aborɔme no ase.

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Na wɔde Samson yere no maa ne yɔnko a odii akyi wɔ aware no mu no.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Na n’ase kae sɛ: Me de, mise, wompɛ no bio, enti mede no mama wo yɔnko bi. Ne nua kumaa no ho yɛ fɛ sen no. Fa no si n’ananmu.

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Eyi de, sɛ me ne Filistifo di no bɔne a, merenni ho so bi.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Filistifo no kae sɛ: Hena po na ɔyɛɛ eyi? Na wose: Timnani no ase Samson, sɛ ɔde ne yere ama ne yɔnko ntia. Ɛnna Filistifo no siim kɔe de ogya kɔhyew Timnani no ne n’agya fi.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ moayɛ saa a, gye sɛ matɔ mo were ansa na magyae.

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Na ɔbobɔɔ wɔn srɛ ne dwonku so kunkum wɔn okunkɛse. Na osiim kɔtenaa Etam botan tokuru mu. Samson ne afurum abogye

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Filistifo bae bɛbɔɔ Yuda so nsra, na wɔtrɛw wɔn ho mu wɔ Lehi.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda mmarima no kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na moba yɛn so yi? Na wose: Yɛreba abɛkyere Samson, na yɛayɛ no sɛnea ɔyɛɛ yɛn no.

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda mmarima mpensa siim kɔɔ Etam botan tokuru no mu, na wɔka kyerɛɛ Samson sɛ: So wunnim sɛ Filistifo na wodi yɛn so, na ɛdɛn na woayɛ yɛn yi? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ wɔyɛɛ me no, saa ara na mayɛ wɔn.

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛreba abɛkyere wo de wo akɔhyɛ Filistifo no nsa. Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monka me ntam sɛ mo ara de, morenyɛ me hwee.

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Na owiee ɔkasa no, ɔtow abogye no kyenee, na wɔfrɛɛ hɔ sɛ Ramat-lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Na osukɔm dee no sɛ, na osu frɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Wo na wode ogye kɛse yi ahyɛ w’akoa nsa, na afei osukɔm rekum me, na mahwe momonotofo nsam.

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn paee tokuru a ɛwɔ Lehi no mu, na nsu fi hɔ bae, na ɔnomee. Na ne honhom san bae na onyaa nkwa. Enti wɔfrɛ hɔ En-hakore a ɛwɔ Lehi de besi nnɛ ara.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Na odii Israel anim Filistifo bere no so mfirihyia aduonu.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Gasafo sɛ: Samson aba ha, na wotwaa ne ho hyiae, na wɔtɛw no anadwo no kurow no pon ano, na wɔtaree dinn anadwo no nyinaa kae sɛ: Ade kye anɔpa a, yebekum no.

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, ɔdɔɔ ɔbea bi Sorek subon mu a ne din de Delila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Na Filistifo asafohene baa ne nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Daadaa no na hwɛ dekode a n’ahoɔden kɛse no wɔ mu, ne dekode a yɛde betumi no na yɛakyere no abrɛ no ase, na yɛn mu biara bɛma wo nnwetɛbona apem ne ɔha.

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Na Delila ka kyerɛɛ Samson sɛ: Ka kyerɛ me ɛ, dɛn mu na w’ahoɔden kɛse no wɔ, na ɛdɛn na wɔde bɛkyere wo abrɛ wo ase?

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wɔde nhama momono ason a ɛnwoe kyere me a, ɛnne megurow, na mayɛ sɛ onipa biara.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Delila ka kyerɛɛ Samson sɛ: Hwɛ, woasisi me, na woatwa me nkontompo. Afei mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me nea wobetumi de akyere wo ɛ!

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wɔde ntampehama foforo a wɔmfa nyɛɛ adwuma da kyere me a, ɛnna megurow mayɛ sɛ onipa biara.

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Na Delila faa ntampehama foforo de kyekyeree no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Filistifo gu wo so, Samson! Nso na atɛwfo no hyɛ pia mu. Na ɔtetew fii ne basa no sɛ asaawa.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na Delila ka kyerɛɛ Samson sɛ: Woasisi me de abedu sesɛɛ yi, na woatwa me nkontompo. Kyerɛ me nea wobetumi de akyere wo. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wode me ti nwi atɔw ason no de fra ntamabamma nwene a,

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Na ɔde akoroteaa bɔɔ mu, na ɔkae sɛ: Filistifo gu wo so, Samson! Na onyan fii ne nna no mu, na otuu nea wanwene no mu akoroteaa no ne annwene no.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na wubetumi aka sɛ: Medɔ wo, na wo koma nni me ho yi? Mprɛnsa ni a woasisi me, na wonkyerɛɛ me dekode a w’ahoɔden kɛse yi wɔ mu.

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ne nsɛm guan ne ho daa nyinaa yeraw ne ho na ne kra home tew no kɔɔ owu mu no,

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: ɛnna oyii ne koma mu nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Oyiwan nkaa me ti da, efisɛ Onyankopɔn hotuafo ne me fi me na yam; sɛ woyi me ti a, na m’ahoɔden befi me ho, na magurow mayɛ sɛ onipa biara.

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Na Delila huu sɛ waka no ne komam asɛm nyinaa no, ɔsoma kɔfrɛfrɛɛ Filistifo asafohene no sɛ: Mommra pɛnkoro yi, na waka me ne komam asɛm nyinaa. Na Filistifo asafohene no baa ne nkyɛn, na wokurakura sika no wɔn nsam.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Na ɔdedaa no ne nankoroma so, na ɔfrɛɛ ɔbarima bi ma obeyii ne ti nwi mmɛsa ason no, na ofii ase brɛɛ no ase, na n’ahoɔden no fii ne ho kɔe.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no kyeree no tutuu n’aniwa, na wɔde no kɔɔ Gasa, na wɔde kɔbere nkɔnsɔnkɔnsɔn guu no, na ɔyam awi apokyerɛfo fi.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Na ne ti nwi fii ase fuwii, ne yi no akyi. Samson adeyɛ a etwa to ne ne wu

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Na Filistifo asafohene no hyiae sɛ wɔbɛbɔ afɔre kɛse ama wɔn nyame Dagon na wɔagye wɔn ani; na wose: Yɛn nyame de yɛn tamfo Samson ahyɛ yɛn nsa.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Na Samson ka kyerɛɛ abofra a okura ne nsa no sɛ: Gyaa me na minsuso adum abien a ɔdan no si so no mu, na mintweri.

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Na Samson frɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Awurade Nyankopɔn, afei kae me, na hyɛ me den prɛko pɛ yi nko ara, Onyankopɔn, na minni m’aniwa abien yi so were prɛko Filistifo so.

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Na Samson susoo mfinimfini adum abien a ɔdan no si so na ɛso no no mu, na ɔde ne nifa soo biako mu na ɔde benkum soo biako mu.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Na Samson kae sɛ: Ma me ne Filistifo no nwuwu! Na ɔde n’ahoɔden nyinaa kuntunii, na ofi no buruw guu asafohene no ne ɔman a wɔwɔ mu no nyinaa so. Na awufo a ɔma wowui ne wu mu dɔɔso sen wɔn a ɔma wowui ne nkwa bere mu.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ɛnna ne nuanom ne n’agya fi nyinaa sian kɔe kɔfaa no de no foro bae besiee no Sora ne Estaol ntam wɔ n’agya Manoa asiei. Na Samson dii Israel anim mfirihyia aduonu.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Na ɔdan dwetɛ no maa ne na bio. Na ne na faa dwetɛ ahanu de maa ogufo, na ɔde yɛɛ osenhoni ne agude, na ɛwɔ Mika fi.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Nso na ɔbarima Mika no wɔ abosomfi, na ɔyɛɛ asɔfotade ne abusua ahoni, na ɔhyɛɛ ne mma mu biako sɔfo, na odii no sɔfo.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Nna no mu no, na ɔhene bi nni Israel; obiara yɛ nea ɛteɛ n’ani so.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no fii Betlehem Yuda kurow no mu sɛ ɔkɔ baabiara a obenya; na n’akwantu no mu oduu Mika fi wɔ Efraim bepɔw so.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Na Mika ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛhe na wufi reba yi? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Meyɛ Lewini a mifi Betlehem Yuda, na menam, merekɔtena baabiara a menya.

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Na Mika ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo ne me ntena ɛ, na yɛ me agya ne ɔsɔfo, na mɛma wo dwetɛ du afirihyia ne atade biako ne w’aduan. Na Lewini no hyɛn mu.

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Na Mika hyɛɛ Lewini no sɔfo, na aberante no dii no sɔfo, na ɔtenaa Mika fi.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Na Mika kaa sɛ: Afei na mahu sɛ AWURADE rebɛyɛ me yiye sɛ manya Lewini a odi me sɔfo yi.

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Nna no mu no, na ɔhene bi nni Israel; bere koro no ara mu nso na Danfo abusuakuw no rehwehwɛ agyapade atena so, efisɛ ɛde besi saa bere no, na agyapade bi nnya mmɛtɔɔ wɔn fam Israel mmusuakuw no mu.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Na Danfo no somaa wɔn abusua mu mmarima baanum, wɔn mu mmarima a wɔyɛ nnam, fi Sora ne Estaol, sɛ wɔnkɔsra asase no na wɔnhwehwɛ mu, na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔhwɛ asase no so. Na woduu Efraim bepɔw so, Mika fi, na wɔdaa hɔ.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Wɔwɔ Mika fi no ho no, wɔtee aberante Lewini no nne, na wɔman hɔ, na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hena na ɔde wo baa ha? Na ɛdɛn na woreyɛ wɔ ha? Na ɛdɛn nso na wowɔ wɔ ha?

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Na obuaa wɔn sɛ: Sɛɛ ne sɛɛ na Mika ne me adi, na wabɔ me paa, na midi no sɔfo.

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Bisa Onyankopɔn ɛ, na yenhu sɛ yɛn kwan a yɛnam so yi bɛyɛ siade kwan anaa?

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Momfa asomdwoe nkɔ. AWURADE anim na mo kwan a monam mu no da.

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Na mmarima baanum no siim koduu Lais; na wohuu ɔman a ɛwɔ hɔ no sɛ wɔte hɔ dwoodwoo sɛ Sidonfo, wɔte hɔ komm ne dwoodwoo, na obi nni hɔ a ɔka wɔn biribiara mu na odi tumi asase no so, na wɔne Sidonfo ntam ware, na wɔne obi nni asɛm bi.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa wɔn nuanom nkyɛn wɔ Sora ne Estaol; na wɔn nuanom no bisaa wɔn sɛ: Amanneɛ?

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Danfo abusua no mu mmarima ahansia a wɔahyehyɛ akode tu fii Sora ne Estaol.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔe, kɔbɔɔ nsra Kiriat-yearim wɔ Yuda. Ɛno nti, wɔfrɛ hɔ Mahane-dan de besi nnɛ; hwɛ, ɛwɔ Kiriat-yearim akyi.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Na wotwaam hɔ kɔɔ Efraim bepɔw so, na woduu Mika fi.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna mmarima baanum a wɔkɔsraa asase no bua see wɔn nuanom no sɛ: So munim sɛ asɔfotade ne abusua ahoni a wɔasen ne agude wɔ adan yi mu? Na afei monhwɛ nea mobɛyɛ.

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛ komm, fa wo nsa mua w’ano na wo ne yɛn nkɔ, na yɛ yɛn agya ne ɔsɔfo. So eye ma wo sɛ wubedi sɔfo ama onipa biako fi anaasɛ wubedi sɔfo ama Israel mu abusuakuw ne abusua?

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsɔfo no penee, na ɔfaa asɔfotade ne abusua ahoni ne ohoni a wɔasen no, na ɔde kɔɔ ɛdɔm no mu.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔdan wɔn ho de kɔe, na wɔmaa mmofra ne afieboa ne nneɛma a ɛho hia dii wɔn anim.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Wɔne Mika fi ntam twee ara yiye no, wɔfrɛfrɛɛ nnipa a wɔwɔ afi a ɛbemmɛn Mika fi no mu no behyiae, na wotiw Danfo no.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Na wɔteɛɛm frɛɛ Danfo no, na wɔdannan wɔn ho ka kyerɛɛ Mika sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ wo na wode dɔm a ɛte sɛɛ reba yɛn so yi?

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Na ose: M’anyame a meyɛe ne ɔsɔfo no, moafa de rekɔ, na ɛdɛn na mewɔ bio? Na afei adɛn na moka kyerɛ me sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ wo, yi?

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Na Danfo no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mma wɔnnte wo nne wɔ yɛn mu, na mmarima a wɔn bo afuw ammɛtow anhyɛ mo so, na woanhwere wo nkwa ne wo fifo de.

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Na Danfo no sii wɔn kwan so kɔe. Na Mika huu sɛ wɔn ho yɛ den sen no no, ɔdan ne ho san baa ne fi.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: na wɔtoo kurow no din Dan, sɛ wɔn agya Dan a wɔwoo no maa Israel no din te; nanso anka kan no na kurow no din de Lais.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Na nna no mu a ɔhene bi nni Israel no, Lewini bi wɔ hɔ a wakɔsoɛ hɔho Efraim bepɔw asase no so akyirikyiri baabi, na ɔwaree ɔbea bi fii Betlehem Yuda.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Na ne ɔbea no fii n’akyi kɔbɔɔ aguaman, na ofii ne nkyɛn kɔɔ n’agya fi Betlehem Yuda na okodii hɔ nna bi, asram anan.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Na ne kunu no sɔre tiw no sɛ ɔkɔka no abodwoesɛm na ɔde no asan aba, na n’abofra ne mfurum abien ka ne ho. Na ɔbea no de no kɔɔ n’agya fi; na ababaa no agya huu no no, ɔde anigye hyiaa no.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Na n’ase, ababaa no agya no, siankaa no, na ɔtenaa ne nkyɛn nnansa; na wodidii, nomee na wɔtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Na ne nnaana so no, wɔsɔree anɔpatutu, na osiesiee ne ho sɛ anka ɔresim; na ababaa no agya no ka kyerɛɛ n’ase no sɛ: Fa abodoo afono ma bi dwudwo wo koma, na ɛno akyi no, moasi kwan so.

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Na wɔtenatenaa ase, na wɔn baanu no nyinaa didii na wɔnomee. Na ababaa no agya no ka kyerɛɛ ɔbarima no sɛ: Pene ɛ, na da anadwo yi, na gye w’ani.

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no sɔree sɛ ɔresim no, n’ase no siankaa no, na ɔtenaa ase daa hɔ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Na ne nnaanum so no, ɔsɔree anɔpatutu sɛ ɔrekɔ; na ababaa n'agya no kae sɛ: Dwudwo wo koma, na montwɛn nkosi sɛ owia bɛdan ne ho. Na wɔn baanu no didii.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no sɔree sɛ ɔrekɔ, ɔne ɔbea no ne n’abofra no. Na n’ase, ababaa n'agya no, ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, onwini redwo na ade reyɛ asa, monna ɛ, hwɛ, adesae abɛn, da ha na gye w’ani, na ɔkyena moatua ahema asi kwan so akɔ fie.

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no ampene sɛ ɔbɛda hɔ anadwo no; na ɔsɔre kɔe, na okoduu Yebus a ɛne Yerusalem no ntentenso; na mfurum abien a wɔahyehyɛ wɔn no ne ɔbea no ka ne ho.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Woduu Yebus no, na ade resa pa ara. Na abofra no ka kyerɛɛ ne wura no sɛ: Ma yɛmman nkɔ Yebusifo kurow yi mu nkɔda hɔ.

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Na ne wura ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mma yɛmmman nnkɔ ananafo a Israelfo mu bi nni ha kurow mu, na ma yentwam nkɔ Gibea.

english_verse: or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’abofra no sɛ: Duom na yɛmmɛn nkurow no mu biako nkɔda Gibea anaa Rama.

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Na wotwaam kɔe, na owia kɔtɔɔ wɔn wɔ Gibea a ɛyɛ Benyamin de no ho.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Na wɔman kɔɔ hɔ sɛ wɔkɔda Gibea. Na odui no, ɔtenaa kurow no abɔnten so, na obiara ammɛfa wɔn ankɔ ne fi sɛ wɔnkɔda hɔ.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, akwakoraa bi fi n’adwuma ano afum anwummere bae; na onipa no fi Efraim bepɔw so na ɔbɛsoɛɛ hɔho Gibea, na kurom hɔfo yɛ Benyaminfo.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n’ani so, na ohuu ɔbarima kwantenni no kurow no abɔnten so, na akwakoraa no bisaa no sɛ: Ɛhe na worekɔ, na ɛhe nso na wufi?

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yefi Betlehem Yuda retwam akɔ Efraim bepɔw asase no so akyirikyiri baabi; ɛhɔ na mifi na mekɔɔ Betlehem Yuda. Na AWURADE fi na merekɔ yi, nso obiara mmɛfa me nkɔsoɛ ne fi.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Nanso sare ne aduan wɔ hɔ ma yɛn mfurum no, na abodoo ne nsa wɔ hɔ ma me ne w’afenaa ne abofra a ɔka wo nkoa ho no nso, biribiara nhia yɛn.

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Na akwakoraa no kae sɛ: Asomdwoe nka wo. Mɛma wo nea ehia wo nyinaa; abɔnten so nko ara na nna!

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Na ɔde no kɔɔ ne fi, na ɔmaa mfurum no aduan, na wɔhohoroo wɔn anan ho, na wodidi nomee.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Na wɔregye wɔn ahome no, hwɛ, kurom hɔfo mmabusufo bi betwaa ofi no ho hyiae, na wɔpempem ɔpon no, na wɔka kyerɛɛ ofiwura akwakoraa no sɛ: Fa ɔbarima a ɔbɛsoɛɛ wo fi no fi adi bra na yene no nna.

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima fiwura no fii adi kɔɔ wɔn nkyɛn hɔ ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Dabi, me nuanom, monnyɛ adebɔne yi! Sɛ ɔbarima yi anya abɛsoɛ me fi yi, munnni nkwaseasɛm yi.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Na me ba ɔbaabun ne ne mpena ni, momma memfa wɔn mimfi adi na mommrɛ wɔn ase na monyɛ wɔn nea mopɛ. Na ɔbarima yi de, monnyɛ no nkwaseade a ɛte sɛɛ.

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Nanso mmarima no ampɛ sɛ wobetie no; ɛnna ɔbarima no soo ne mpena no mu de no fii adi brɛɛ wɔn abɔnten so; na wɔfaa no, yɛɛ no biribiara a wɔpɛ anadwo no ara kosii anɔpa, na ade kyee no, wogyaa no ma ɔkɔe.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Na anim reyɛ abaabae no, ɔbea no bae, na ɔbɛhwee ɔbarima no fi a ne wura wɔ mu no pon ano daa hɔ kosii sɛ anim tetewee.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Na ne wura no sɔree anɔpa hiɛɛ ofi no apon fii adi sɛ ɔrekɔ ne kwan no, na hwɛ, ne mpena no da ofi no pon no ano, na ne nsa gu apongua ase de no so.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɔre na yɛnkɔ. Nanso wammua. Ɛnna ɔbarima no faa no too afurum no so, na ɔsɔre kɔɔ ne kurom.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Na oduu ne fi no, ɔfaa ɔsekan na osoo ne mpena no mu de fofaa ne nnompe ntam kyɛɛ ne mu asinasin dumien, na ɔma wɔde kɔɔ Israel asase nyinaa so.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na obiara a ohui no, kae sɛ: Wɔnyɛe na wonhuu saa ade yi bi nso da, efi da a Israelfo fi Misraim bae de besi nnɛ da yi: Munnwen eyi ho mo tirim, muntu ho fo na monkasa.

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbarima Lewini a ɔyɛ ɔbea a wodii no awu no kunu no buae sɛ: Miduu Gibea a ɛyɛ Benyamin de no mu, me ne me mpena no, na yɛbɛdaa hɔ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Na misoo ɔbea no mu mitwitwaa no asinasin, na mema wɔde kɔɔ Israel agyapade asase nyinaa so, efisɛ wɔayɛ abusude ne nkwaseade, Israel mu.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Na afei mo Israelfo nyinaa ni, momma yɛn mo adwene ne afotu wɔ ha yi ara.

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa sɔre gyinae sɛ ɔbarima biako kae sɛ: Yɛn mu biara renkɔ ne ntamadan mu, na yɛn mu biara remman ne fi.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no nyinaa kohyia hyɛɛ kurow no; wɔapam ayɛ sɛ ɔbarima biako.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Na Israel mmusuakuw somaa nnipa kɔɔ Benyamin abusuakuw nyinaa mu kae sɛ: Dɛn adebɔne ara ne nea wɔayɛ mo mu yi?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Na afei munyi mma abusufo a wɔwɔ Gibea no mmra na yenkum wɔn, na yenyi bɔne no mfi Israel. Na Benyaminfo no ampɛ sɛ wotie wɔn nuanom Israelfo no.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminfo no fifi nkurow mu bɛboaa wɔn ho ano Gibea, sɛ wobefi ne Israelfo akɔko.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo sɔree anɔpa kɔbɔɔ Gibea so nsra.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no tu kɔɔ sɛ wɔne Benyamin rekɔko, na Israel mmarima no twitwaa wɔn so mpasua wɔ Gibea.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Na Benyaminfo no fii adi fii Gibea, na wɔbɛkaa Israel mmarima ɔpeduonu abien guu fam da no ara.

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel de atɛwfo twaa Gibea ho hyiae.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Na wɔdan wɔn akyi Israel mmarima no anim faa sare so kwan; na ɔko no tu taree wɔn, na wɔn a wofifi nkurow mu bae no dwerɛw wɔn wɔn mu.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Wɔkaa Benyamin hyɛɛ mu hyiae tiw wɔn ara koduu wɔn asoɛe pam wɔn kosii Gibea ntentenso, Apuei fam.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔdan wɔn ho guan kɔɔ sare so fam Rimon botan no ho. Na wotwitwaa wɔn sɛ wɔdɔw sare, atempɔn no so, mmarima mpemnum; na wotu taree wɔn dii wɔn akyi koduu Gidom, na wokunkum wɔn mu mmarima mpennu.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Na Benyamin atɔfo a wɔtotɔe da no nyinaa si mmarima ɔpeduonu anum a wɔtwe nkrante; eyinom nyinaa yɛ mmarima akofofo.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no san wɔn akyi baa Benyaminfo no so, na wɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn, nnipa ne mmoa, ne nea wɔn nsa kae nyinaa; nso wɔtotoo nkurow a woduu so nyinaa mu gya.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Nso na Israel mmarima no akeka ntam Mispa sɛ: Yɛn mu biara mmfa ne ba mmma Benyamin aware.

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Na ɔman no baa Betel bɛtenaa Onyankopɔn anim koduu anwummere, na wɔmomaa wɔn nne so suu osu kɛse.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: O AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, ɛdɛn nti na eyi aba Israel, sɛ nnɛ Israel mu abusuakuw biako nni hɔ yi?

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, ɔman no tuaa ahema sii afɔremuka wɔ hɔ, na wɔbobɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no kae sɛ: Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa mu hena na wamma guabɔ no mu AWURADE nkyɛn? Efisɛ wɔaka ntankɛse agu nea wamma AWURADE nkyɛn Mispa no so sɛ: Okum na wonkum no.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no yam hyehyee wɔn maa wɔn nua Benyamin, na wose: Ɛnnɛ wɔatwa abusuakuw biako afi Israel mu akyene.

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Na wohuu Yabes-gileadfo no mu mmabaa ahanan a wonnim mmarima nna, na wɔde wɔn baa nsra no mu Silo a ɛwɔ Kanaan asase so.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Ɛnna asafo no nyinaa soma ma wɔne Benyaminfo a wɔwɔ Rimon botan mu no kɔkasae, na wɔkaa wɔn asomdwoesɛm.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Na Benyamin san bae bere no mu, na wɔde mmea a wogyee wɔn nkwa wɔ Yabes-gilead mmea mu no momaa wɔn aware; nanso anso wɔn.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no yam hyehyee wɔn maa Benyamin, sɛ AWURADE ama ntewmu aba Israel mmusuakuw mu. Benyaminfo wia mmabaa

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Na asafo no mu mpanyimfo no kae sɛ: Yɛbɛyɛ dɛn anya ɔyerenom ama wɔn a wɔaka no? Efisɛ Benyamin mu mmea ase agu.

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Aguanfo a wofii mu no agyapade ntena hɔ mma Benyamin, na wɔampopa abusuakuw bi amfi Israel.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Na yɛn de, yɛrentumi mfa yɛn mma mu bi mma wɔn aware, efisɛ Israelfo akeka ntam sɛ: Nnome nka nea ɔde ɔbea bi bɛma Benyamin aware.

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Hwɛ, wɔhyɛ AWURADE fa daa afe Silo a ɛwɔ Betel benkum fam, ɔtempɔn a efi Betel kɔ Sekem no apuei fam ne Lebona nifa fam.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Na wɔhyɛɛ Benyaminfo no sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔtetɛw wɔn bobe nturo no mu,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: na monhwɛ, na sɛ Silo mmabaa no fi adi bɛsaw wɔn asaw no a, mumfi adi mfi bobe nturo no mu mmra, na obiara mmɛkyere ɔyere mfi Silo mmabaa no mu mfa nkɔ Benyamin asase so.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔn agyanom anaa wɔn nuanom ba yɛn nkyɛn ne yɛn bɛham a, yebese wɔn sɛ: Monhwɛ yɛn anim nnom wɔn, na yɛannya ɔyerenom amma wɔn mmiako mmiako, dɔm no mu; nso ɛnyɛ mo na mode wɔn maa wɔn, na anka sesɛɛ de, moadi so.
