english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminfo no yɛɛ saa, na wɔfofaa yerenom sɛ wɔn dodow te fii wɔn a wɔbɛsawee a wɔkyeree wɔn no mu. Na wosii mu san kɔɔ wɔn agyapade so, na wɔkyekyee nkurow no tenatenaa mu.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no nso fii hɔ bere no mu kokɔɔ wɔn mmusuakuw ne wɔn mmusua mu, na wofii hɔ kokɔɔ wɔn agyapade ho.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Nna no mu no, na ɔhene bi nni Israel; obiara yɛ nea ɛteɛ n’ani so.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Ɔbarima no din de Elimelek, na ne yere din de Naomi, na ne mmammarima baanu no din de Mahlon ne Kilion, wɔyɛ Efratifo a wofi Betlehem a ɛwɔ Yuda. Na woduu Moab asase so, na wɔtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Na Elimelek, Naomi ne kunu no wui, na ɛkaa ɔno ne ne mma baanu no.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Na wɔwaree yerenom Moabfo mu, obiako din de Orpa, na obiako no din de Rut. Na wɔtenaa hɔ bɛyɛ sɛ mfe du.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Na ofii nea ɔwɔ hɔ, na ne nsewnom baanu no ka ne ho. Na wosii kwan so sɛ wɔresan aba Yuda asase so.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Na Naomi ka kyerɛɛ ne nsewnom baanu no sɛ: Monsan nkɔ mo nanom fi. AWURADE ne mo nni no yiye sɛnea mo ne awufo no ne me adi no yi.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: AWURADE mma munnya atenaye mo kununom fi. Na ofifew wɔn ano; na wɔmomaa wɔn nne so susui.

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dabi, yɛne wo bɛsan akɔ wo manfo nkyɛn.

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Na Naomi kae sɛ: Me mma, monsan! Ɛdɛn na mo ne me bɛkɔ? So mmammarima da so wɔ me yam na wɔabɛyɛ mo kununom?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Me mma, monsan nkɔ! Na manyin dodo sɛ menya okunu. Sɛ mise: Mewɔ anidaso, na minya okunu anadwo yi na mewo mmammarima po a,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: so ɛno nti mobɛtwɛn wɔn akosi sɛ wobenyin anaa? So ɛno nti mobɛtena hɔ a morenware anaa? Dabi, me mma, na ɛyɛ me awerɛhow dodo mo nti, efisɛ AWURADE ne me anni no yiye.

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Na wɔmomaa wɔn nne so susui bio. Na Orpa few ne sew no ano de kraa no; na Rut de, ɔbataa ne ho.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Na Naomi kae sɛ: Hwɛ, wo kora asan kɔ ne manfo ne n’anyame nkyɛn. San di wo kora akyi!

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Na Rut kae sɛ: Nhyɛ me sɛ minnyaw wo mensan mimfi w’akyi; na nea wokɔ na mɛkɔ, na nea wosoɛ na mɛsoɛ; wo man bɛyɛ me man, na wo Nyankopɔn ayɛ me Nyankopɔn;

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: nea wubewu, na mewu, na ɛhɔ ara na wobesie me; AWURADE nyɛ me eyi ne bi nka ho, sɛ gye owu na ɛbɛtetew me ne wo ntam.

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Na Naomi hui sɛ wawe ahina so sɛ ɔne no bɛkɔ no, ɔne no gyaee kasa wɔ ho.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu no nantew beduu Betlehem. Na woduu hɔ no, wɔn nti kurow no nyinaa bɔɔ twi na wɔkae sɛ: So Naomi ni?

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mommfrɛ me Naomi, na momfrɛ me Mara, efisɛ Tweaduampɔn ne me adi no bɔnwoma so sɛ!

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Mekɔɔ no ma, na AWURADE de me hunu na aba; ɛdɛn na mofrɛ me Naomi, bere ko a AWURADE ayi me ntɛn, na Tweaduampɔn ne me adi no bɔne yi?

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Sɛ Naomi ne n’ase Moabni Rut san fii Moab asase so bae ni. Na woduu Betlehem no, na wɔafi atokotwa ase.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Boas fi Betlehem bae, na okyiaa awitwafo no sɛ: AWURADE nni mo akyi. Na wogyee no so sɛ: AWURADE nhyira wo.

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Boas bisaa n’abofra a ogyina awitwafo no akyi no sɛ: Hena ababaa ni?

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Na obuaa sɛ: Ɛyɛ Moabni ababaa a ɔne Naomi san fii Moab asase so bae no.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ɔbɛsrɛɛ sɛ: Ma minni awitwafo no akyi minni mpɛpɛw mentase afiafi no ntam. Na ɔbae, na okura mu ara de fi anɔpa de abedu sesɛɛ a bere tiaa bi pɛ na ɔde ahome.

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Ɛnna Boas ka kyerɛɛ Rut sɛ: Me ba, tie! Nkɔ afuw bi mu nkodi mpɛpɛw, nso mfi ha, na fa wo ho bɔ me mmaawa yi ho.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ afuw no fa a wotwa hɔ na di wɔn akyi. Hwɛ, mahyɛ mmerante no sɛ wɔnnhaw wo. Na sɛ osukɔm de wo a, kɔ nneɛma no ho kɔnom nea mmerante no asaw no bi.

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Rut de n’anim butuwii fam, na ɔkotow ka kyerɛɛ Boas sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na manya w’anim anuonyam, na w’ani ku me a meyɛ ɔnanani ho yi?

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Na Boas buaa no sɛ: Nea wo kunu wu akyi woyɛ maa w’ase no nyinaa, wɔaka ne nyinaa akyerɛ me: Sɛnea wugyaw w’agya ne wo na ne asase a wɔwoo wo wɔ so, na wonam baa ɔman a wunnim wɔn da yi nkyɛn no.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: AWURADE nhyɛ wo, wo nneyɛe ananmu na nya akatua mu fi AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn a woaba ne ntaban ase abɛdan no no nsam.

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Me wura, ma menkɔ so ara nya w'anim adom, efisɛ woakyekye me werɛ, na woaka w’abaawa asomdwoesɛm, nso mente sɛ wo mmaawa yi mu biara po.

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Na eduu adidibere no, Boas ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Twiw bra ha na bedi aduan no bi, na fa wo buprɛko bɔ nsa nyinyanyinya no mu. Na ɔbɛtenaa awitwafo no nkyɛn. Na ɔmaa no nkyeweɛ no bi, na ɔwe mee ma ebi kae.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔree sɛ ɔrekodi mpɛpɛwa no, Boas hyɛɛ ne mmerante no sɛ: Momma onni afiafi no nso ntam mpɛpɛw, na mummpoopoo no.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Na munyiyi afiafi no mu de no bi nnyaw ngu fam mma no, na onni no mpɛpɛw; na monnhaw no.

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ɛnna odii afuw no mu mpɛpɛw de koduu anwummere, na ɔporow mpɛpɛw a odii no; na ɛyɛɛ bɛyɛ atoko olonka biako.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Na ɔsoa baa kurow no mu; na n’ase huu nea ɔtasee no; na oyii nea odi mee na ɛkae no maa no.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ɛnna n’ase bisaa no sɛ: Ɛhe na wukodii mpɛpɛw nnɛ, na ɛhe na wokɔyɛɛ adwuma yi? Nhyira nka nea n’ani kuu wo ho no. Na ɔkyerɛɛ n’ase onii ko a ɔkɔyɛɛ ne nkyɛn adwuma no sɛ: Ɔbarima a mekɔyɛɛ ne nkyɛn adwuma nnɛ no din de Boas.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Na Naomi ka kyerɛɛ n’ase no sɛ: Nhyira nka no, AWURADE a onnyaee ateasefo ne awufo adɔeyɛ no anim. Na Naomi ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔbarima no yɛ yɛn busuani, ɔyɛ yɛn bogya.

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Na Moabni Rut kae sɛ: Nso ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Mmerante a mewɔ yi ho na bata kosi sɛ wobewie nea mewɔ nyinaa twa.

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Na Naomi ka kyerɛɛ n’ase Rut sɛ: Me ba, eye sɛ wo ne ne mmaawa no bɛkɔ, na wɔanhaw wo, wɔ afuw foforo bi mu.

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Na ɔbataa Boas mmaawa no ho dii mpɛpɛw de kosii sɛ wowiee atoko ne awi no twa. Na ɔtenaa n’ase no nkyɛn.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Na n’ase Naomi ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me ba, mennhwehwɛ ahomee memma wo na asi wo yiye anaa?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, yɛn manni, Boas a wo ne ne mmaawa nantewee no wɔ hɔ; ɔrehuw atoko so anadwo yi wɔ awiporowbea.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Na guare na sra hyɛ wo ntade na sian kɔ aporowee hɔ; na nyi wo ho adi nkyerɛ ɔbarima no kosi sɛ obewie adidi ne ɔnom ansa;

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: na sɛ ɔkɔda na wukohu ne dabere hɔ a, kɔ koyi n’anafo ntama na da hɔ; na ɔno ara bɛkyerɛ wo nea yɛ.

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Na obuaa no sɛ: Mɛyɛ nea woka nyinaa.

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Na osian kɔɔ aporowee hɔ kɔyɛe sɛnea n’ase hyɛɛ no nyinaa.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Na Boas didi nomee na ne bo tɔɔ ne yam no, ɔkɔ kɔdaa atokokuw no ano hɔ. Na ɔbae komm beyii n’anafo ntama na ɔdaa hɔ.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Na ɔdasum no, ɔbarima no bɔɔ birim, na ɔmaa ne mu so hwɛe, na hwɛ, ɔbea da n’anafo.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ɛyɛ wo hena? Na ose: Ɛyɛ me, w’abaawa Rut. Trɛw w’atade mmuano mu fa kata w’abaawa so, na abusua mu gyefo ne wo.

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE nhyira wo, me ba, woama w’akyiri adɔe ayɛ yiye sen kan de no, sɛ woanni mmerante, ahiafo oo, adefo oo, akyi.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Na afei, me ba, nsuro. Nea woka nyinaa, mɛyɛ mama wo, efisɛ me manfo a wɔfa kurow pon ano nyinaa nim sɛ woyɛ ɔbea pa.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Na afei, ɛwom sɛ abusua mu gyefo ne me, nanso abusua mu gyefo bi wɔ hɔ a ɔbɛn sen me.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Tena ha anadwo yi, na sɛ anɔpa, ɔyɛ wo ogyefo ade a, eye, ma ɔnyɛ ogyefo: Na sɛ ɔmpɛ sɛ ɔyɛ wo ogyefo ade a, ɛnne, sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, me na mɛyɛ wo ogyefo. Da ma ade nkye.

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Na ɔdaa n’anafo hɔ koduu anɔpa. Na ɔsɔree ansa na obi rehu ne yɔnko. Na ɔkae sɛ: Wɔmmma wɔnnte sɛ ɔbea no baa aporowee ha.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa mmuatama a egugu wo so no bra, na so mu. Na osoo mu, na osusuw atoko susukora asia guu mu, na ɔde soaa no, na ɔkɔɔ kurow no mu.

english_verse: Naomi asked her what had happened, and Ruth told her everything.
translation_verse: Na oduu n’ase nkyɛn no, obisaa sɛ: Ɛte dɛn, me ba? Na ɔkaa nea ɔbarima no yɛɛ no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Atoko susukora asia yi na ɔmaa me, na ose, mfa nsansa nkɔ w’ase nkyɛn.

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Na Naomi kae sɛ: Tena hɔ, me ba, kosi sɛ wubehu sɛnea asɛm yi besi, efisɛ ɔbarima no renhome gye sɛ owie asɛm yi di nnɛ ansa.

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Na Boas kɔɔ kurow pon no ano kɔtenaa hɔ; na hwɛ, abusua mu gyefo a Boas bɔɔ ne din no retwam. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Asiamasi ee, man bra bɛtena ha. Na ɔman bɛtenaa ase.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ kurow no mu mpanyin mu du bae, na ɔkae sɛ: Montena ha! Na wɔtenaa ase.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ abusua mu gyefo no sɛ: Naomi a ɔsan fii Moab asase so bae no retɔn asase a ɛyɛ yɛn nua Elimelek de no.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Na me de, mise: Meyi wo asotiw sɛ tɔ wɔ nkurɔfo yi ne me mpanyin yi anim. Sɛ wubegye a, gye, na sɛ wunnye a, ka kyerɛ me na minhu, efisɛ obi nni hɔ a obegye sɛ wo ne me a midi w’akyi. Na ɔkae sɛ: Me ara megye.

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Boas kae sɛ: Da a wobɛtɔ Naomi nsam asase no, wotɔ no Moabni bea Rut a ɔyɛ ɔsaman yere no nsam, na woama ɔsaman no din so n’awunnyade ho.

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ogyefo no kae sɛ: Merentumi minnye memfa, na mansɛe m’ankasa m’awunyade. Wo na kogye m’ade a ɛsɛ sɛ migye no fa, na merentumi minnye.

english_verse: To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other.
translation_verse: Nso ogye ne nsesa ho amanne a kan no ɛwɔ Israel ni: Obi rebɛhyɛ asɛm biara den a, oyi ne mpaboa de ma ne yɔnko; na eyi na wɔde yɛ adanse wɔ Israel.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Enti ogyefo no ka kyerɛɛ Boas sɛ: Tɔ fa! Na oyii ne mpaboa.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Na Boas ka kyerɛɛ mpanyin no ne ɔman no nyinaa sɛ: Mone adansefo nnɛ, sɛ matɔ Elimelek ho nneɛma nyinaa ne Kilion ne Mahlon ho nneɛma nyinaa afi Naomi nsam.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Na Moabni Rut, Mahlon yere no nso, matua ne ti ade aware no, na ɔsaman no din atena hɔ daa, n’agyapade mu, na wɔantwa ɔsaman no din amfi ne nuanom mu ne ne kurow pon ano; mone adansefo nnɛ!

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na ɔman a wɔwɔ kurow pon ano hɔ no nyinaa ne mpanyin no kae sɛ: Adansefo ne yɛn. AWURADE nyɛ ɔbea a waba wo fi no sɛ Rahel ne Lea a wɔn baanu akyekye Israel fi no. Na yɛ okunini wɔ Efrata, na gye din wɔ Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Na w’asefo a AWURADE de bɛma wo afi ababaa yi mu no nyɛ sɛ Peres a Tamar woo no maa Yuda fi no asefo. Dawid yɛ Rut aseni

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Na Boas faa Rut waree, na ɔkɔɔ ne ho. Na AWURADE ma onyinsɛnee na ɔwoo ɔbabarima.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Na mmea no ka kyerɛɛ Naomi sɛ: Nhyira nka AWURADE a wamma ogyefo ammɔ wo nnɛ, na nhyira nka ne din wɔ Israel.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Na ɔnyɛ wo nkwamafo ne wo mmerewabere mu hwɛfo, efisɛ wo sew a ɔdɔ wo a oye ma wo sen mmammarima baason no na awo no.

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Na Naomi gyee akokoaa no de no bɔɔ ne bo, na ɔyɛɛ no ɔba gyigyefo.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Na n’afipamfo mmea no kae sɛ: Wɔawo ɔbabarima ama Naomi. Na wotoo no din, frɛɛ no Obed, ɔno ne Dawid nana: Yese n’agya.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Na Efraimni barima bi wɔ hɔ a ofi Ramataim a ɛwɔ Efraim bepɔw no so a ne din de Elkana. Ɔyɛ Yeroham ba, na ne nana ne Elihu. Elihu nso yɛ Tohu ba na ne nana ne Suf.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ yerenom baanu, obiako din de Hana, na obiako nso de Penina. Na Penina wɔ mma, na Hana de, onni ba.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Daa afe ɔbarima yi fi ne kurom kɔ sɛ ɔkɔsom na wabɔ afɔre ama asafo AWURADE wɔ Silo. Ɛhɔ na Eli mma baanu Hofni ne Pinehas yɛ asɔfo ma AWURADE.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Da a Elkana bɔ afɔre no, ɔma ne yere Penina ne ne mmammarima ne ne mmabea nyinaa kyɛfa.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Na Hana de, ɔma no baanu kyɛfa, efisɛ ɔdɔ no nanso AWURADE ato ne yafunu mu.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Na ne kora no yi no ahii pii, de huru ne bo, efisɛ AWURADE ato ne yafunu mu.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Na saa na Penina yɛ Hana daa afe, sɛ wɔforo kɔ AWURADE fi a, ɔhyɛ no yamgya sa; na osu ara nko na Hana su na onnidi.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Na ne kunu Elkana bisaa no sɛ: Hana, ɛdɛn na wusu, na ɛdɛn na wunnidi, na ɛdɛn na wo bo nnwo? So minnye memma wo mensen mmammarima du?

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wodidii Silo na wɔnom wiei no, Hana sɔree na ɔkɔɔ AWURADE anim nanso na ɔsɔfo Eli te agua so, AWURADE asɔredan ano apongua ho.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Na Hana kra werɛ howee, na ɔbɔɔ AWURADE mpae, na ɔde yaw sui.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ bɔ sɛ: Asafo AWURADE, sɛ wohwɛ w’afenaa amanehunu na wokae me, na wo werɛ amfi w’afenaa, na woma w’afenaa ɔbabanin a, ɛnne mede no mɛma AWURADE ne nkwa nna nyinaa, na oyiwan bi renka ne ti.

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: na Hana kasae ne koma mu; na n’ano nko na ɔbesebese, na ne nne de, wɔnte. Enti Eli buu no sɛ ɔsabofo.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Eli ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Enkosi da bɛn na wobɛbow nsa? Yi nsanom fi w’ani so.

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Mfa w’abaawa nto ɔbea sansani bi ho, efisɛ m’awerɛhow ne me yaw dodow mu na makasa mabesi sesɛɛ yi.

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Eli buae sɛ: Fa asomdwoe kɔ, na Israel Nyankopɔn bɛma wo w’ade a wosrɛɛ no hɔ no.

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Na Hana buae sɛ: Ma w’afenaa nnya w’anim dom. Ɛnna ɔbea no siim kɔe kodidii, na n’anim nte sɛ kan no bio.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Na wɔsɔree anɔpatutu kɔsɔree wɔ AWURADE anim, na wɔsan baa wɔn fi wɔ Rama. Na Elkana ne ne yere Hana dae, na AWURADE kaee no;

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: na afe dui no, na Hana anyinsɛn awo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Samuel, na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE hɔ na mesrɛɛ no fii.

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima Elkana ne ne fifo nyinaa foro kɔe sɛ ɔkɔbɔ afirihyia afɔre de n’aboade akɔma AWURADE.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Na Hana de, wankɔ, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne kunu sɛ: Gye sɛ abofra no atwa nufu ansa na mede no mɛkɔ, na wakopue AWURADE anim, na watena hɔ daa.

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Na ne kunu Elkana ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛ nea eye w’ani so. Tena hɔ kosi sɛ wubetwa akokoaa no nufu ansa; AWURADE asɛm ara na ɔmma ennyina. Na ɔbea no tenaa hɔ maa ne ba no nufu de kosii sɛ otwaa no nufu.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: O me wura, sɛ wo kra te ase yi, me wura, mene ɔbea a obegyinaa wo nkyɛn ha yi bɔɔ AWURADE mpae no.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Abofra yi ho mpae na mebɔe, na AWURADE ama me nea mesrɛɛ no hɔ no.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Enti nso, mede no refɛm AWURADE; ne nna a ɔbɛtena ase nyinaa ɔyɛ AWURADE dea. Na wɔsɔree AWURADE wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Hana bɔɔ mpae sɛ: Me koma di AWURADE mu ahurusi, AWURADE mu na wɔama m’abɛn so; m’anom atrɛw m’atamfo so, efisɛ m’ani gye wo nkwagye mu.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Obiara nyɛ kronkron sɛ AWURADE, na obiara nni w’akyi, na ɔbotan bi nni hɔ sɛ yɛn Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Monnkasa ahantan kasa bebree sa, mommma ahomaso kasa mmfi mo anom, na AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn a ohu ade nyinaa, na ɔno na ɔkari nneyɛe.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Ahoɔdenfo ta bubu, na mmerɛwfo de, wɔde ahoɔden bɔ wɔn ho so;

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: AWURADE na okum, na ɔma nkwa; ɔma wosian kɔ asaman na ɔma wɔforo fi adi.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: AWURADE ma obi di hia, na ɔma obi di yiye; ɔbrɛ onipa ase, na ɔma onipa so.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Ɔma ɔbrɛfo so fi mfutuma mu, na ɔma ohiani so fi sumina so, sɛ ɔde no bɛtena mmapɔmma mu, na wama wanya anuonyam agua so atena. Na asase nnyinaso yɛ AWURADE dea, na ɔde wiase asi so.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ɔbɛhwɛ n’ahotefo anan so, na atirimmɔdenfo bɛyera esum mu; na ɛnyɛ ahoɔden so na onipa nam bedi nim.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: AWURADE atamfo bewie pasaa, na ɔbɛma n’aprannaa abom ɔsoro agu wɔn so. AWURADE bebu asase ano atɛn, ɔde ahoɔden bɛma ne hene, na wama nea wasra no ngo no abɛn so. Samuel wɔ AWURADE fi

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Na Elkana kɔɔ ne fi Rama; na abofra no som AWURADE, ɔsɔfo Eli anim.

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Na asɔfo ade a wɔyɛ ɔman no ne sɛ: Sɛ obi rebɔ afɔre a, wɔrenoa nam no, na ɔsɔfo no abofra aba, na okura adinam a ano abiɛsa,

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: na ɔde abɛbɔ dadesɛn anaa ahina anaa kyew dade anaa kutu no mu, na nea adinam no de bɛba nyinaa na ɔsɔfo no afa; saa ara na wɔyɛ Israelfo a wɔba Silo hɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Nso wonnya nhyew srade no mmaa AWURADE no, na ɔsɔfo no somfo abɛka akyerɛ nea ɔrebɔ afɔre no sɛ: Ma nam na wɔnkɔtoto mma ɔsɔfo; na onnye wo hɔ nam a wɔanoa, na mmom nammono.

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔka sɛ: Wɔrebɛhyew srade no mprempren ansa na woafa dodow biara a wopɛ a, ɔsomfo noka sɛ: Daabi, na ma me bi prɛko, anyɛ saa a, mɛfa no ɔhyɛ so.

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Enti mmerante no bɔne soe kɛse, AWURADE anim, efisɛ nnipa no buu AWURADE aduan afɔre no animtiaa.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Na Samuel de, ɔsomee AWURADE anim; ɔyɛ abofra a wɔde nwera asɔfotade abɔ ne mu.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Nso ne na pam batakari kumaa bi ma no, na ɔde brɛ no daa afe a ɔne ne kunu rebɛbɔ daa afe afɔre no.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Na Eli hyiraa Elkana ne ne yere se: AWURADE mma wo asefo mfi ɔbea yi mu nsi nea ɔde no afɛm AWURADE yi ananmu. Na wosiim kɔɔ wɔn kurom.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hyiraa Hana, na onyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo mmammarima baasa ne mmabea baanu. Na abofra Samuel no nyinii AWURADE anim. Eli ne ne mma

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nso Eli abɔ akora sɛ, na ɔtee nea ne mma de yɛ Israel nyinaa, no nyinaa ne sɛnea wɔne mmea a wɔyɛ ahyiae ntamadan ano adwuma no da.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Dabi, me mma, na ɛnyɛ atenka pa na mete sɛ AWURADE manfo no ka fa mo ho kyin yi.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Sɛ obi yɛ onipa bi bɔne a, Onyankopɔn bɛpata ama no; na sɛ obi yɛ AWURADE bɔne a, hena na ɔbɛpa kyɛw ama no? Nanso wɔantie wɔn agya asɛm, efisɛ na AWURADE repɛ akum wɔn.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Na abofra Samuel no kɔɔ so ara nyinii, na onyaa anisɔ AWURADE ne nnipa anim.

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa bi baa Eli nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Me na miyii me ho adi mekyerɛɛ w’agya fi, bere a wɔwɔ nkoasom mu Misraim, Farao fi no,

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Enti AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn asɛm a ɔka ni: Mekae ampa sɛ: Wo fi ne w’agya ofi nnantew m’anim daa; nanso afei nea AWURADE ka ni: Ɛmpare me koraa! Na wɔn a wodi me ni no, medi wɔn ni, na wɔn a wobu me animtiaa no bɛbɔ ahohora.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, nna bi reba a metwa wo basa ne w’agya fi basa, na akwakoraa bi renka wo fi.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wuhu yiye a Onyankopɔn bɛyɛ Israel no nyinaa a, ɛbɛma wo ho ahia wo wɔ me tenabea hɔ, na akwakoraa bi renka wo fi da biara da.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Nanso nea merentwa no nkyene wɔ m’afɔremuka ho, no ani bɛyɛ siamoo na wahyɛ ne kra awerɛhow; na wo fi dodow bewuwu wɔn mmerantebere mu.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Na eyi nyɛ wo nea ɛbɛba wo mma baanu, Hofni ne Pinehas, so no ho sɛnkyerɛnne: Da koro na wɔn baanu no bewuwu.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Na mɛma ɔsɔfo nokwafo so mafa: Ɔbɛyɛ nea ɛwɔ me koma ne me kra mu, na mɛkyekye ofi a etim hɔ mama no, na wanantew nea masra no no anim nna nyinaa.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Na nea ɔbɛka wo fi no bɛba abɛkotow no agye dwetɛbona ne abodoo sebɔw, na waka sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, fa me hyɛ asɔfo adwuma no biako bi mu, na manya abodoo buprɛko bi madi.

english_verse: Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room,
translation_verse: Na ɛbere no mu, ɛbae sɛ da bi a Eli da ne dabere no, nso na n’ani so afi ase ayɛ kusukusu a onhu ade yiye,

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: na Onyankopɔn kanea no nnya nnumii na Samuel da AWURADE asɔredan mu, nea Onyankopɔn adaka no si hɔ no.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: AWURADE frɛɛ Samuel se: Samuel, Samuel, na ose: Mini.

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Na otuu mmirika kɔɔ Eli nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Mini, na wofrɛɛ me. Na Eli buae sɛ: Memfrɛɛ wo ɛ, san kɔda. Na ɔkɔdae.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE frɛɛ Samuel bio sɛ Samuel; na Samuel sɔre kɔɔ Eli nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Mini, na wofrɛɛ me. Na ose: Memfrɛɛ wo ɛ, me ba, san kɔda.

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Nso na Samuel nnya nhuu AWURADE, na wonnya nyii AWURADE asɛm nkyerɛɛ no ɛ.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kɔɔ so frɛɛ Samuel nea ɛto so abiɛsa; na ɔsɔre kɔɔ Eli nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Mini na wofrɛɛ me. Ɛnna Eli hui sɛ AWURADE na ɔrefrɛ abofra no,

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: enti Eli ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Kɔda, na sɛ ɔfrɛ wo a, ka sɛ: AWURADE, kasa na w’akoa retie. Na Samuel kɔ kɔdaa ne dabere.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bae begyinaa hɔ frɛɛ sɛ kan no sɛ: Samuel, Samuel! Ɛnna Samuel se: Kasa, na w’akoa retie.

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Hwɛ, merebɛyɛ biribi Israelfo mu a obiara a ɔbɛte no aso abien mu bɛyɛ no yɔnn.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Da no na mɛma ade a maka atia Eli fi nyinaa aba mu fi mfiase de kosi awiei.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Na maka makyerɛ no sɛ merebu ne fi atɛn akosi daa, amumɔyɛ no nti, efisɛ onim sɛ ne mma reyɛ abusude, na wanka wɔn anim.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Na enti maka ntam afa Eli fi ho sɛ: Sɛ wɔde okum afɔre ne aduan afɔre pata ma Eli fi mpo a, ɛrempopa wɔn amumɔyɛ no da biara da.

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Na Samuel dae koduu anɔpa, na ohiɛhiɛɛ AWURADE fi apon no. Na Samuel suroe sɛ ɔbɛka ade a ohui no akyerɛ Eli.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Eli frɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Me ba Samuel! Na ose: Mini!

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Asɛm bɛn na ɔka kyerɛɛ wo no? Nsiw me so. Sɛ wusiw me asɛm a ɔka kyerɛɛ wo no nyinaa bi so a, Onyankopɔn ntua wo ka, na ɔmfa bi nka ho.

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel kaa nsɛm no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no, na wansiw no bi so. Na Eli se: Ɛyɛ AWURADE, nea eye n’ani so no, ɔnyɛ.

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Na Samuel renyin no, na AWURADE di n’akyi, na asɛm biara a ɔkae no baa mu.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Na Israel nyinaa, efi Dan kosi Beer-seba, hui sɛ wɔde Samuel asi hɔ, sɛ ɔnyɛ AWURADE diyifo.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE kɔɔ so yii ne ho adi wɔ Silo; na AWURADE de n’asɛm yii ne ho kyerɛɛ Samuel wɔ Silo.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Na Samuel asɛm duu Israel nyinaa. Na Israel tu kɔe sɛ wokohyia Filistifo ne wɔn ako; na wɔkɔbɔɔ nsra wɔ Ebeneser, na Filistifo nso bɛbɔɔ nsra wɔ Afek.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no twaa mpasua hyiaa Israel, na ɔko no mu trɛwee, na Israelfo dii nkogu Filistifo no anim, na wokum wɔn mu nnipa bɛyɛ mpemnan.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no soma kɔɔ Silo kɔsoaa asafo AWURADE a ɔte Kerubim ntam no apam adaka no bae, na Eli mma baanu no, Hofni ne Pinehas, na wɔwɔ Onyankopɔn apam adaka no ho.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no baa nsra no mu no, Israel mpanyin kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na AWURADE ama yɛadi nkogu nnɛ Filistifo anim yi? Momma yɛnkɔfa AWURADE apam adaka no mfi Silo mmra yɛn nkyɛn, na ɛmmra yɛn mu mmegye yɛn mfi yɛn atamfo nsam.

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE apam adaka no duu nsram hɔ no, Israel nyinaa bɔɔ ose kɛse maa asase wosowee.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Na Filistifo tee osebɔ no, wɔkae sɛ: Hebrifo nsram osebɔ kɛse yi ase ne dɛn? Na wɔtee sɛ AWURADE adaka no aba nsra no mu.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Filistifo no suroe, na wose: Onyankopɔn aba nsra no mu. Na wɔkae sɛ: Buei, yennue! Na ɛmmae sɛɛ pɛn.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Buei, yennue! Hena na obeyi yɛn afi anyame atumfo yi nsam? Eyinom ne anyame a wɔde ɔhaw ahorow haw Misraimfo wɔ sare so no.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Mo Filistifo, monhyɛ mo ho den, na monyɛ mmarima, na moansom Hebrifo sɛnea wɔsom mo no; enti monyɛ mmarima na monko.

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn adaka no, Filistifo no fae, na Eli mma baanu no, Hofni ne Pinehas nso totɔe.

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminni bi fi mpasua no so tutuu mmirika baa Silo da no ara, na n’atade asunsuane, na dɔte gu n’atifi.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Na odui no, na hwɛ, Eli te agua so kwankyɛn rehwɛ kwan; na Onyankopɔn adaka no nti na ne bo ntɔ ne yam. Na ɔbarima no ba bɛkae, na kurow mu no nyinaa sui.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima no ka kyerɛɛ Eli sɛ: Mene nea ofi mpasua so mebae no. Ɛnnɛ na mifi mpasua no so miguanee. Na ose: Asɛm no te dɛn, me ba?

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo no buae sɛ: Israelfo adi nkogu Filistifo anim, na wɔakunkum Israelman no mu nnipa pii nso, na wo mma baanu no, Hofni ne Pinehas nso atotɔ, na atamfo no afa Onyankopɔn adaka no.

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔɔ Onyankopɔn adaka no din no, Eli fi n’agua so tew faa n’akyi hwee ase ɔpon kɛse no ho, na ne kɔn mu bui, na owui, efisɛ ɔyɛ akwakoraa na ɔyɛ duru. Na wahwɛ Israel so mfe aduanan.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Na ne sew, Pinehas yere, anyinsɛn na n’awo bere reyɛ adu. Na ɔtee asɛm no sɛ wɔafa Onyankopɔn adaka no, na n’ase ne ne kunu awuwu no, awoko yaw patu kaa no, na ɔkotow woe amonom hɔ ara, na yaw dodow no nti, owui.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Na ɔregyaa mu no, mmea a wogyinagyina ne nkyɛn no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro, na ɔbarima na woawo yi. Nanso wammua, na wammu.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no faa Onyankopɔn adaka no, na wɔde fi Ebeneser kɔɔ Asdod.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no de Onyankopɔn adaka no kɔɔ Dagon fi, na wɔde kosii Dagon nkyɛn.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee a Asdodfo sɔree anɔpatutu no, hwɛ na, Dagon ahwe ase a n’anim butuw fam, wɔ AWURADE adaka no anim. Na wɔmaa Dagon so de no sii ne sibea.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee a wɔsɔree anɔpatutu no, hwɛ, Dagon ahwe ase a n’anim butuw fam, AWURADE adaka no anim, na Dagon ti ne ne nsa abien abubu gugu apongua no so, na Dagon kuntunsin nko na aka.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Enti Dagon asɔfo ne wɔn a wɔba Dagon fi nyinaa ntia apongua no so wɔ Asdod de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE twee Asdodfo aso, na oyii wɔn hu, na ɔde mpɔmpɔ bobɔɔ wɔn, Asdod ne ɛho nkurow nketewa nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Na nnipa a wɔte Asdod hui saa no, wɔkae sɛ: Mommma Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no nntena yɛn nkyɛn, efisɛ ɛde ɔhaw pii abrɛ yɛn ne yɛn nyame Dagon.

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Na wɔsoma kohyiahyiaa Filistifo asafohene nyinaa baa wɔn nkyɛn kae sɛ: Dɛn na yɛnyɛ Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no? Na wose: Wɔnsoa Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no nkɔ Gat. Na wɔsoaa Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no kɔɔ hɔ.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Na wɔsoa kɔe no, AWURADE asotwe baa kurow no so, wibɔ kɛse pa ara, na ɔbobɔɔ kurow no mufo nketewa ne akɛse nyinaa, na mpobia sisii wɔn.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Na wɔma wɔde Onyankopɔn adaka no kɔɔ Ekron. Na wɔde Onyankopɔn adaka no duu Ekron no, Ekronfo no teɛɛm sɛ: Wɔde Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no aba yɛn nkyɛn de rebekunkum yɛn ne yɛn man!

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Na wɔsoma kohyiahyiaa Filistifo asafohene nyinaa boaa ano, na wɔkae sɛ: Momma wɔmfa Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no nsan nkɔ ne sibea, na ankunkum yɛn ne yɛn man. Na owu anikrakra baa kurow no mu nyinaa, na Onyankopɔn nsa yɛɛ duru wɔ wɔn so wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Na nnipa a wɔanwuwu no, mpobia sisii wɔn, na kurow no mufo su foro kɔɔ soro.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE adaka no dii Filistifo asase so asram asɔn.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Filistifo frɛfrɛɛ asɔfo ne akɔmfo sɛ: Yɛnyɛ AWURADE adaka yi dɛn? Monkyerɛ yɛn dekode a yɛmfa nka ho nkɔ ne sibea.

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Sɛ morema wɔde Israel Nyankopɔn adaka no akɔ a, mommma wɔmmfa no hunu nnkɔ, na mmom momfa asodi afɔre nka ho nkɔ. Ɛno ansa na wɔbɛsa mo yare, na mubehu nea enti a ne nsa mfi mo so yi.

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Na wɔkae sɛ: Asodi afɔre bɛn na yɛmfa mma? Na wose: Momfa sika na wɔnyɛ no sɛ mpobia anum ne sika nkura anum, sɛnea Filistifo asafohene ano si, efisɛ ɔhaw koro no ara na ɛwɔ mo nyinaa ne mo asafohene so.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Enti monyɛ mo mpobia no sɛso ne mo nkura a wɔsɛe mo asase no sɛso, na momfa anuonyam mma Israel Nyankopɔn: Ebia ne nsa bɛyɛ hare afi mo ne mo anyame ne mo asase so.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn nti na moyɛ mo koma dennen sɛ Misraimfo ne Farao yɛɛ wɔn koma dennen no? So ɛnyɛ sɛ ɔyɛɛ wɔn ade wiei no ansa na wɔtoo wɔn kwan ma wɔkɔe?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Na afei monyɛ teaseɛnam foforo, na momfa anantwibere abien a wɔma nufu a kondua nkɔɔ wɔn so da, na momfa anantwi no nsesa teaseɛnam no, na montetew wɔn mma mfi wɔn ho nkɔ ofie;

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: na momfa AWURADE adaka no nsi teaseɛnam no so, na momfa sika nnwinne a mode rekɔyɛ asodi afɔre ama no no ngu adakawa mu mfa nsi nkyɛn, na munnya no kwan na ɛnkɔ.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Na monhwɛ: Sɛ ɛfa n’ankasa ne hye so kwan foro kɔ Bet-semes a, ɛnne na ɔno na ɔyɛ yɛn bɔne kɛse yi; na sɛ anyɛ saa a, na yɛahu sɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno na ne nsa haw yɛn, na asiane bi na asiane yɛn.

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Na nnipa no yɛɛ sa, na wɔfaa anantwi abien a wɔma nufu de wɔn sesaa teaseɛnam no, na wɔtoo wɔn mma mu ofie;

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: na wɔde AWURADE adaka no sii teaseɛnam no so, na wɔde adakawa a sika nkura ne wɔn mpobia sɛso no wɔ mu no kaa ho.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Na anantwi no faa ɔkwan tee kɔɔ Bet-semes kwan so; wɔnam ɔtempɔn koro so, na wɔrekɔ no na wɔde su, na wɔamman ankɔ nifa anaa benkum; na Filistifo asafohene no dii wɔn akyi koduu Bet-semes hye so.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Nso na Bet-semesfo retwa wɔn awi obon bi mu; na wɔmomaa wɔn ani so huu adaka no, na ne hu no yɛɛ wɔn anigye.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo asafohene baanum no hui no, wɔsan kɔɔ Ekron da no ara.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Na eyinom ne sika mpobia a Filistifo de yɛɛ asodi afɔre de brɛɛ AWURADE no: Asdod de biako, Gasa de biako, Askelon de biako, Gat de biako, Ekron de biako;

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: ne sika nkura no, sɛnea Filistifo nkurow a ɛyɛ asafohene baanum no de ano si no, efi nkurow a wɔatoto ho afasu so de kosi petee mu nkuraa so. Na adanse ne ɔbo kɛse a wɔde AWURADE adaka no sii so no, na ɛwɔ Bet-semesni Yosua afuw mu besi nnɛ da yi.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Na Bet-semesfo no kae sɛ: Hena na obetumi agyina AWURADE, Onyankopɔn kronkronni yi anim, na hena nkyɛn na omfi yɛn nkyɛn nkɔ?

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Na wɔsomaa abɔfo kɔɔ Kiriat-yearimfo nkyɛn sɛ: Filistifo de AWURADE adaka no aba na mommɛfa nkɔ mo nkyɛn.

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Na Kiriat-yearimfo bae bɛfaa AWURADE adaka no de foro kɔɔ Abinadab fi, koko no so, na wodwiraa ne ba Eleasar sɛ ɔnhwɛ AWURADE adaka no so. Samuel di Israelfo so

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Israel fi nyinaa sɛ: Sɛ mode mo koma nyinaa resan aba AWURADE nkyɛn a, munyi ananafo anyame ne Astarot no mfi mo mu, na munsiesie mo koma mma AWURADE, na monsom no nko, na obeyi mo Filistifo nsam.

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israelfo no yii Baal nyinaa ne Astarot, na wɔsom AWURADE nko.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel kae sɛ: Munhyia Israel nyinaa mmra Mispa, na memmɔ AWURADE mpae memma mo.

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Na wobehyiae wɔ Mispa, na wɔsaw nsu hwie guu AWURADE anim, na wobua dae da no, na wɔkae hɔ sɛ: Yɛayɛ AWURADE bɔne. Na Samuel dii Israelfo hene wɔ Mispa.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo tee sɛ Israelfo akohyia Mispa no, Filistifo asafohene foro baa Israel so. Na Israelfo tee no, wosuroo Filistifo no.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Nnyae osu a woresu afrɛ AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn ama yɛn no, na onnye yɛn mfi Filistifo nsam.

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Na Samuel rebɔ ɔhyew afɔre no, Filistifo no twiw bɛnee sɛ wɔne Israelfo rebɛko, na AWURADE paepaee aprannaa akɛse guu Filistifo no so da no, na ɔkaa wɔn gui ma wɔtotɔe Israelfo anim.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima fii adi fii Mispa kɔtaa Filistifo no, na wokunkum wɔn ara kosii Betkar ase.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Na wɔdan nkurow a Filistifo agye Israel nsam no maa Israel, efi Ekron kosi Gat, ne ɛho nsaase nso, Israel gyee Filistifo nsam. Na asomdwoe baa Israelfo ne Amorifo ntam. Samuel yɛ ɔkannifo nso

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Na Samuel yɛɛ ɔkannifo wɔ Israel ne nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Na afe biara afe okyin kɔ Betel ne Gilgal ne Mispa, na ɔyɛ ɔkannifo wɔ nkurow yi nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Na ɔsan ba Rama, na ɛhɔ na ne fi wɔ; na odi Israel so wɔ hɔ, na osii afɔremuka wɔ hɔ maa AWURADE.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: N’abakan din de Yoel, na nea ɔka ho no de Abiya; wɔyɛɛ akannifo wɔ Beer-seba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Na ne mma no de, wɔansɛ wɔn agya ɔkwan biara so, na wɔman kodii mfaso akyi, wogyigyee adammude, na wobubuu ntɛnkyew. Israelfo hwehwɛ ɔhene

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel mpanyin nyinaa hyia baa Samuel nkyɛn wɔ Rama

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, woabɔ akora, na wo mma mfa w’akwan so. Afei si ɔhene ma yɛn na onni yɛn kan sɛ amanaman nyinaa te.

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Na asɛm no ansɔ Samuel ani sɛ wɔkae sɛ: Ma yɛn ɔhene na onni yɛn kan no. Na Samuel bɔɔ AWURADE mpae.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Tie nea ɔman no se ne nea wɔka kyerɛ wo no nyinaa, efisɛ ɛnyɛ wo na wɔapa wo, na me na wɔapa me, sɛ minnni wɔn so hene.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Wɔn nneyɛe nyinaa fi da a miyii wɔn fii Misraim mebae de abedu nnɛ yi, sɛnea wɔagyaw me akɔsom anyame foforo no, saa ara na wɔreyɛ wo nso yi.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Enti tie wɔn; na kasa kyerɛ wɔn, kyerɛ wɔn ɔhene a obedi wɔn so no apɛde.

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Na Samuel kaa AWURADE nsɛm no nyinaa kyerɛɛ ɔmanfo a wobisaa no hɔ ɔhene no.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Eyi ne ɔhene a obedi mo so no apɛde: Ɔbɛpaw mo mmammarima de wɔn akɔ ne nteaseɛnam ne n’apɔnkɔsotefo mu, na wama wɔatu mmirika adi ne nteaseɛnam anim sɛ n’awɛnfo

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛfa mo mmabea ayɛ adufrafo, soodofo ne abodootofo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛfa mo mfuw ne mo bobe nturo mu nea eye de ama n’asomfo.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Na obegye mo awifuw ne bobe nturo aba mu ntotoso du du de ama ne gyaasefo ne n’asomfo.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛfa mo nkoa ne mo mfenaa ne mo mmerante mu ahoɔdenfo, ne mo mfurum de ayɛ n’adwuma.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Obegye mo nguan mu ntotoso du du. Na mobɛyɛ no nkoa.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Na bere bi bɛba a, mo hene a moayi no adi mo so no nti, mubesu afrɛ AWURADE, nanso ɔremmua mo.

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: na yɛn nso nyɛ sɛ amanaman nyinaa, na yɛn hene no nni yɛn anim nni ako mma yɛn.

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Na Samuel tee ɔman no nsɛm nyinaa no, ɔka guu AWURADE asom.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Tie wɔn, na si ɔhene ma wɔn. Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Israelfo nyinaa sɛ: Obiara nkɔ ne kurom.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Nso ɔdefo bi wɔ hɔ a ne din de Kis. Ofi Benyamin abusua mu. N’agya din de Abiel, na nena ne Sero, wofi Bekorat fi wɔ Afia abusua mu.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ ɔbabarima bi a ne din de Saul; aberante no ho yɛ fɛ, Israelfo mu de obiara nsen no ahoɔfɛ. Efi ne mmati rekɔ no, ɔware sen obiara, ɔman no mu.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na Saul n’agya Kis mfurum yerae. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne ba Saul sɛ: Fa mmerante no mu biako ka wo ho, na sɔre kɔhwehwɛ mfurum no.

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔfaa Efraim bepɔw so, na wɔfaa Salisa asase so, nanso wɔanhu wɔn; na wɔfaa Saalim asase so, nanso na wonni hɔ; na wɔfaa Benyamin asase so, nanso wɔanhu wɔn.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Na woduu Suf asase so no, Saul ka kyerɛɛ n’abofra sɛ: Bra ma yɛnsan nkɔ, na m’agya annyae mfurum no ho dwen ammedi yɛn ho nkɔmmɔ.

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, Onyankopɔn nipa bi wɔ kurow yi mu, ɔyɛ onipa a n’anim yɛ nyam, nea ɔka nyinaa ba mu; ma yɛnkɔ hɔ, ebia ɔbɛka yɛn ɔkwan a yɛrekɔ yi ho asɛm bi akyerɛ yɛn.

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ n’abofra no sɛ: Hwɛ, yɛkɔ a, dɛn na yɛde bɛkɔ akɔma ɔbarima no? Abodoo asa wɔ yɛn kotoku mu, na ayɛyɛde bi nni hɔ a yɛde rekɔma Onyankopɔn nipa no; dɛn na yɛwɔ?

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na n’abofra no buaa bio sɛ: Hwɛ, mikura dwetɛ dwetɛbona abupɛn anan mu biako, ɛno na mede bɛma Onyankopɔn nipa no, na wama yɛn akwankyerɛ.

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ n’abofra no sɛ: Ɔsɛmpa, bra ma yɛnkɔ. Na wɔkɔɔ kurow a Onyankopɔn nipa no wɔ mu no mu.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Na wɔreforo koko no akɔ kurow no mu no, wohuu mmabaa a wɔrefi akɔsaw nsu. Na wobisaa wɔn sɛ: Ɔdehufo no wɔ hɔ anaa?

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Na wobuaa wɔn sɛ: Ɔwɔ hɔ, hwɛ, ɔwɔ mo anim ha yi ara; monyɛ ntɛm, na ɛnnɛ waba kurow no mu, na ɔman no bɔ afɔre nnɛ sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Mudu kurow no mu ara pɛ a, mubehu no ansa na wakɔ sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ akodidi; efisɛ ɔman no nnidi kosi sɛ ɔbɛba: Na ɔno na ohyira afɔre no so ansa na wɔn a wɔahyia wɔn no adidi. Enti momforo nkɔ, na ɛnnɛ ara na mubehu no.

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Na wɔforo kɔɔ kurow no mu. Woduu hɔ no na hwɛ Samuel refi adi abehyia wɔn aforo akɔ afɔrebɔbea hɔ.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Nso na AWURADE ayi Samuel asitiw dedaw ansa na Saul reba sɛ:

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: Ɔkyena sesɛbere mɛsoma ɔbarima bi afi Benyamin asase so aba wo nkyɛn, na sra no ngo si no me man Israel so panyin, na onnye me man mfi Filistifo nsam; na mahu me man no yaw, efisɛ wɔn su adu m’anim.

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel huu Saul no, AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, onipa a misee wo sɛ obedi me man so no ni.

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Na Saul twiw bɛn Samuel kurow pon no ano kae sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, kyerɛ me nea ɔdehufo no fi wɔ.

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Na Samuel buaa Saul sɛ: Mene ɔdehufo no. Foro di m’anim kɔ afɔrebɔbea hɔ, na mo ne me bedidi nnɛ, na ade kye a, magya mo kwan; na mɛka wo nea ɛwɔ wo komam nyinaa.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Na wo mfurum a wɔyerae nnɛ nnansa no de, mfa w’adwene nto so, na wɔahu wɔn. Na hena na Israel nyinaa ani wɔ no so? So ɛnyɛ wo ne w’agya fi?

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Na Saul buae sɛ: Me de, meyɛ Benyaminni, na Israel mmusuakuw mu ketewa no mu na mifi, na m’abusua ne Benyamin abusuakuw mu mmusua nyinaa mu ketewa. Na ɛdɛn nti na woka saa asɛm yi kyerɛ me?

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Na Samuel faa Saul ne n’abofra no, na ɔde wɔn kɔɔ adidii, na ɔmaa wɔn atenae wɔn a wɔahyia wɔn no ti. Wɔbɛyɛ sɛ nnipa aduasa.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Na osoodoni no kɔfaa ɔsrɛ ne nea ɛwɔ ho no de besii Saul anim; na Samuel kae sɛ: Hwɛ, nea wɔagyaw ni; fa si w’anim na di, efisɛ wɔde asie ama wo, bere a mise mahyia ɔman no. Na Saul ne Samuel didii da no.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Na wofii afɔrebɔbea hɔ sian baa kurow no mu, na ɔne Saul kasae ɔdan atifi.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Na wɔsɔree nhema; a ade rekye no, Samuel frɛɛ Saul fii ɔdan atifi sɛ: Sɔre na minnya wo kwan. Na Saul sɔree, na wɔn baanu no, ɔno ne Samuel, fii adi.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Wosian koduu kurotia no, Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Ka kyerɛ w’abofra no na ɔmmɛsen nni yɛn anim nkɔ, na aberante no bɛsen kɔ a, wo de, gyina hɔ, afei ma menka nhyehyɛe a Onyankopɔn wɔ ma wo no, nkyerɛ wo, na tie.

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel faa ngo toa hwie guu Saul atifi, na ofew n’ano kae sɛ: AWURADE asra wo asi ne man Israel so panyin. Na wobedi AWURADE nkurɔfo anim, agye wɔn afi wɔn atamfo a atwa wɔn ho nyinaa nsam. Na eyi ne wo nsɛkyerɛnne sɛ AWURADE asra wo ngo adi ne nkurɔfo ne n’agyapade so.

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Wufi me nkyɛn nnɛ rekɔ yi, wobɛto mmarima baanu wɔ Selsa, Rahel da so, Benyamin hye so, na wɔbɛka akyerɛ wo sɛ: Mfurum a wokɔhwehwɛɛ wɔn no, wɔahu wɔn, na hwɛ, w’agya agyae mfurum no ho dwen, na mo so na ne dadwen abesi sɛ: Menyɛ me ba yi ho dɛn?

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Na wufi hɔ kɔ w’anim, na wudu Tabor dupɔn no ho a, mmarima baasa a wɔrekɔ Onyankopɔn nkyɛn Betel behyia wo hɔ, obiako so mmirekyi abiɛsa, na obiako so brodo sebɔw abiɛsa, na obiako so bobesa ahina ma.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
