translation_verse: Na wobekyia wo, na wɔama wo brodo abiɛsa na woagye wɔn nsam.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Ɛno akyi no, wubedu Gibeat-elohim, wɔ nea Filistifo bansifo wɔ no; na sɛ wudu kurow no mu hɔ a, wubehyia adiyifo asafo a wɔresian afi sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ, na bɛnta sanku ne mpintin ne mmɛn ne asanku di wɔn anim, na wɔrehyɛ nkɔm.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE honhom besi wo so, na wo ne wɔn ahyɛ nkɔm, na woadan ayɛ onipa foforo.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Na sɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne yi ba mu ma wo a, yɛ nea wo nsa bɛso so fa, na Onyankopɔn di w’akyi.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Na di m’anim sian kɔ Gilgal, na hwɛ, me nso meresian maba wo nkyɛn mabɛbɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre. Tena hɔ twɛn nnansɔn kosi sɛ mɛba wo nkyɛn mabɛkyerɛ wo nea yɛ.

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Na ɔdan ne ho sɛ ɔrefi Samuel nkyɛn akɔ no, Onyankopɔn maa no koma foforo; na nsɛnkyerɛnne yi nyinaa baa mu da no ara.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Na woduu Gibea kurow no mu no, hwɛ, adiyifo asafo behyiaa no, na Onyankopɔn honhom besii Saul so, na ɔhyɛɛ nkɔm wɔ wɔn mu.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Na wɔn a wonim no kan no nyinaa huu no sɛ ɔrehyɛ nkɔm adiyifo mu no, nkurɔfo no sisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Dɛn ne nea ayɛ Kis ba no yi? So Saul nso fra adiyifo no mu anaa?

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Na obi a ofi hɔnom buae sɛ: Na eyinom nso kannifo ne hena? Enti ɛdan abebusɛm sɛ: So Saul nso fra adiyifo no mu anaa?

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Na ne nkɔmhyɛ honhom no twae no, ɔbaa sorɔnsorɔmmea hɔ.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Na Saul n’agya ne nua ka kyerɛɛ no ne abofra no sɛ: Ɛhe na mokɔe? Na ose: Yɛkɔhwehwɛɛ mfurum no, na yehui sɛ wonni hɔ no, yɛkɔɔ Samuel nkyɛn.

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Na Saul n’agya ne nua no kae sɛ: Ka me nea Samuel ka kyerɛɛ mo no ɛ!

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ n’agya ne nua no sɛ: Ɔkaa no pefee kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ wɔahu mfurum no. Na ahenni no ho asɛm a Samuel kae no de, wanka ankyerɛ no.

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Samuel hyiaa ɔman no baa AWURADE nkyɛn Mispa.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Israelfo no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn se ni: Me na miyii Israel Misraim mebae, na migyee mo Misraim nsam ne ahenni a ɛhyɛɛ mo so nyinaa nsam;

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: nanso ɛnnɛ moapa mo Nyankopɔn a ɔno na ogye mo mo amane ne mo ahohia nyinaa mu no, na muse no sɛ: Dabi, na si yɛn so hene. Na afei mummegyina AWURADE anim sɛ mo mmusuakuw ne mo mpem dodow te.

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Na Samuel maa Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa twiw bɛnee, na wɔtwee ntonto ma ɛbɔɔ Benyamin abusuakuw.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa Benyamin abusuakuw no twiw bɛnee, sɛ ne mmusua no te: Na wɔtwee ntonto ma ɛbɔɔ Matri abusua, na wɔtwee mmarima no so ntonto ma ɛbɔɔ Kis ba Saul. Nanso wɔhwehwɛɛ no no, wɔanhu no.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Na wokobisaa AWURADE bio sɛ: So onipa no baa ha anaa? Na AWURADE se: Hwɛ, wakohintaw nneɛma no mu.

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Na wotutuu mmirika kɔfaa no fii hɔ. Na obegyinaa ɔman no mu no, na ɔware sen ɔman no mufo nyinaa fi ne mmati so kɔ soro.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no nyinaa sɛ: Monhwɛ nea AWURADE apaw no, na obiara nte sɛ ɔno, ɔman yi nyinaa mu. Na ɔman no nyinaa bɔɔ ose sɛ: Ɔhene tiri nkwa!

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel kaa ahenni no ho nhyehyɛe kyerɛɛ ɔman no, na ɔkyerɛw hyɛɛ nhoma mu de too AWURADE anim. Na Samuel gyaa ɔman no nyinaa kwan ma wɔkokɔɔ wɔn afi mu.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Na Saul nso kɔɔ ne fi Gibea, na dɔm no mu akokodurufo binom a Onyankopɔn aka wɔn koma no ne no kɔe.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Na nnipahunu bi kae sɛ: Oyi bɛyɛ dɛn na wagye yɛn? Na wobuu no animtiaa, na wɔamfa ayɛyɛde ammrɛ no. Nanso ɔyɛɛ sɛ nea ɔnte.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Na Amonni Nahas foro ba bɛbɔɔ Yabes-gilead so nsra. Na Yabes mmarima nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ Nahas sɛ: Wo ne yɛn mpam na yɛnsom wo.

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Na Amonni Nahas no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ansa na me ne mo bɛpam no, gye sɛ mitutu mo aniwa nifa nyinaa na mede mayɛ ahohora mato Israel nyinaa so.

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Na Yabes mpanyin no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma yɛn nnanson, na yɛnsomasoma abɔfo nkɔ Israel ahye nyinaa so, na sɛ obi nni hɔ a obegye yɛn a, yɛafi adi aba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Ɛnna abɔfo no baa Gibea faako a Saul fi bɛkaa asɛm no ɔman no asom; na ɔman no nyinaa momaa wɔn nne so susui.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Saul di anantwi akyi fi afuw mu reba; na Saul kae sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ ɔman yi na wɔresu yi? Na wɔkaa Yabesfo nsɛm no kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Na Saul tee nsɛm yi no, AWURADE honhom sii no so, na ne bo fuwii kɛse.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa anantwi mpamho twitwaa no asinasin de hyehyɛɛ abɔfo no nsam soma ma wɔkɔɔ Israel asase nyinaa so kɔkae sɛ: Obiara a wamfi adi ammedi Saul ne Samuel akyi no, sɛ wɔbɛyɛ n’anantwi ni. Ɛnna AWURADE ho hu tɔɔ ɔman no so, na wofi bae sɛ onipa biako.

english_verse: at Bezek. Saul had them organized and counted. There were
translation_verse: Na ɔkan wɔn Besek, na Israelfo no ano si ɔpehasa, na Yuda mmarima si ɔpeduasa.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ abɔfo a wɔbae no sɛ: Sɛ monkɔka nkyerɛ Yabes-gileadfo no ni: Ɔkyena a owia mu reyɛ den no, mubenya ogye. Na abɔfo no ba bɛka kyerɛɛ Yabesfo no, wɔn ani gyei.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Na Yabesfo no kae sɛ: Ɔkyena yebefi adi aba mo nkyɛn, na moayɛ yɛn sɛ eye mo ani so nyinaa.

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, Saul buu ɔman no mu asafokuw abiɛsa na wɔkɔɔ nsra no mu anɔpa dasu mu, na wokunkum Amonfo koduu awia ketee; na wɔn a ɛkae no bɔ petee a anka wɔn mu baanu po wɔ faako.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔman no ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Hena na ɔkae sɛ: Saul na ɔrebedi yɛn so hene yi, no? Fa nnipa no bra ma yenkum wɔn.

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Wonnkum obiara nnɛ da yi, efisɛ ɛnnɛ AWURADE ayɛ nkwagyede Israel mu.

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Mommra mma yɛnkɔ Gilgal, na yɛnkɔyɛ ahenni no foforo wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa kɔɔ Gilgal, na wokosii Saul hene AWURADE anim wɔ Gilgal; na wɔbobɔɔ asomdwoe afɔre AWURADE anim wɔ hɔ. Na Saul ne Israel mmarima nyinaa ani gyee.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Israel nyinaa sɛ: Hwɛ, matie mo, sɛnea moka kyerɛɛ me no nyinaa, na masi mo so hene.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, ɔhene no na odi mo anim yi. Na me de, mabɔ akora na mafuw dwen, na me mma nso, hwɛ, wɔne mo na ɛwɔ hɔ; na me de, mifi me mmofraase na manantew mo anim mabedu nnɛ da yi.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mini, munni me adanse, AWURADE ne nea wasra no yi anim: Hena nantwi na mafa? Na hena afurum na mafa? Na hena na mahyɛ no so? Na hena na madi no amim? Anaa hena hɔ na magye ademmude na mede mamua m’ani mama no? Na mennan memma mo. Momfa nto gua na metua onipa ko ka

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Na wose: Dabi wunnii yɛn amim na wonhyɛɛ yɛn so na wunnyee obiara hɔ biribi ɛ.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE ne mo dansefo, na nea wasra no yi ne ɔdansefo nnɛ, sɛ moanhu biribiara me nsam. Na wɔkae sɛ: Ɔne dansefo.

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: AWURADE a oyii Mose ne Aaron na ɔde mo agyanom fii Misraim asase so bae no!

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Na afei mummegyina ha, na minyi mo ntɛn AWURADE anim, AWURADE trenee a wayɛ ama mo ne mo agyanom no nyinaa ho:

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Sɛnea Yakob kɔɔ Misraim na mo agyanom su frɛɛ AWURADE, na AWURADE somaa Mose ne Aaron na woyii mo agyanom fii Misraim ma wɔbɛtenaa ha yi.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Na wɔn werɛ fii AWURADE wɔn Nyankopɔn, na ɔtɔn wɔn hyɛɛ Hasor sahene Sisera nsa, ne Filistifo nsa, ne Moab hene nsa, na wɔne wɔn bɛkoe.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Na wosu frɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Yɛayɛ bɔne sɛ yɛagyaw AWURADE akɔsom Baalim ne Astarot, na afei yi yɛn yɛn atamfo nsam, na yɛbɛsom wo.

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE somaa Yerubaal ne Bedan ne Yefta ne Samuel, na oyii mo mo atamfo nsam hyiae ma motenaa ase dwoodwoo.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Na muhui sɛ Amonfo hene Nahas reba mo so no, moka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Dabi, na ɔhene mmedi yɛn so, bere a AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn ne mo hene.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, ɔhene a moapaw no a mosrɛɛ no no ni; na hwɛ, AWURADE asi mo so hene.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Sɛ musuro AWURADE na mosom no na mutie no, na moantew AWURADE anom asɛm atua a, ɛnne mo ne ɔhene a odi mo so no nyinaa bedi AWURADE mo Nyankopɔn akyi. Na ebesi mo yiye.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Na sɛ moantie AWURADE na motew AWURADE anom asɛm atua a, ɛnne AWURADE nsa bɛda mo so sɛnea ɛdaa mo agyanom so no.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Afei nso mummegyina ha nhwɛ ade kɛse a AWURADE rebɛyɛ mo anim yi:

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: So ɛnyɛ awitwa bere ne nnɛ? Mɛfrɛ AWURADE na wama ɔprannaa ne osu aba, na moahwɛ ahu sɛ mo bɔne a moayɛ AWURADE anim sɛ moabisa ɔhene afa no so.

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel frɛɛ AWURADE, na AWURADE maa ɔprannaa ne osu bae da no. Na ɔman no nyinaa suroo AWURADE ne Samuel sɛ.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Bɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn mpae ma wo nkoa, na yɛanwu, efisɛ yɛde bɔne yi aka yɛn bɔne nyinaa ho, sɛ yɛabisa ɔhene afa.

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ ɔman no sɛ: Munnsuro; moayɛ bɔne yi nyinaa de, nanso AWURADE akyi na monnsan mmfi, na momfa mo koma nyinaa nsom AWURADE.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Na mommman nnkodi ade hunu a mfaso ne ogye nni ho no akyi, na ɛyɛ ade hunu.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE din kɛse no nti ɔrempa ne man; na ɛsɔ AWURADE ani sɛ ɔde mo bɛyɛ ne man.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Me nso, ɛmpare me sɛ megyae mo ho mpaebɔ de ayɛ AWURADE bɔne; na mɛkyerɛ mo ɔkwan pa a ɛteɛ no.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Osuro nko na munsuro AWURADE, na momfa mo koma nyinaa nsom no nokware mu. Na monhwɛ ade kɛse a wayɛ ama mo no.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Na sɛ bɔne ara na mobɛyɛ a, ɛnne wɔbɛsesaw mo ne mo hene nyinaa akɔ.

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Na Israel nyinaa tee sɛ Saul aka Filistifo bansifo no agu, ne sɛ Israel ama wɔn ho ayɛ Filistifo ahi. Na wohyiahyiaa ɔman no boaa ano, Saul nkyɛn wɔ Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no hui sɛ ɛreden wɔn, efisɛ wɔhyɛɛ ɔman no ahometew: Na ɔman no hintahintaw abodan ne mmena ne abotan ne aboda ne mmura mu.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Na Hebrifo no bi twaa Yordan kɔɔ Gad ne Gilead asase so. Na Saul da so wɔ Gilgal, na ɔman no nyinaa de ahopopo dii n’akyi. Saul afɔrebɔ a ɛmfata

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Na ɔtwɛnee nnansɔn a ɛne bere a Samuel hyɛe no; nanso Samuel amma Gilgal, na ɔman no fii ne ho petee.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul kae sɛ: Momfa ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre no mmrɛ me. Na ɔbɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre no.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, owiee ɔhyew afɔre no bɔ ara pɛ, na Samuel bae; na Saul fii adi sɛ ɔrekohyia no akyia no.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn na woayɛ yi? Na Saul se: Mihui sɛ ɔman no refi me ho apete, na wo nso woamma bere a wohyɛe no, na Filistifo aboa wɔn ho ano Mikmas,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: ɛnna mise: Afei Filistifo rebesian aba me so wɔ Gilgal, nso minnya minyii AWURADE mpae ɛ, enti na mehyɛɛ me ho mebɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre no.

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Woadi nkwaseasɛm, woanni AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn mmara asɛm a ɔhyɛɛ wo no so. Na anka afei na AWURADE rebɛma w’ahenni atim Israel so daa:

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Na afei w’ahenni rennyina. AWURADE bɛhwehwɛ ne koma so barima afa, na AWURADE asi no ne man so hene, efisɛ woanni nea AWURADE hyɛɛ wo no so.

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Na Samuel sɔre fii Gilgal kɔɔ Gibea-benyamin. Na Saul kan dɔm a wɔne no wɔ hɔ no, mmarima bɛyɛ ahansia.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Na Saul ne ne ba Yonatan ne dɔm a wɔne wɔn wɔ hɔ no tenaa Gibea-benyamin, nso na Filistifo abɔ nsra wɔ Mikmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Na afowfo akuw abiɛsa fi Filistifo nsram bae: Asafokuw biako tew faa Ofra kwan so kɔɔ Saul asase so;

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: na asafokuw biako tew faa Bet-horon kwan so, na asafokuw biako nso tew faa ɔhye a ɛkyerɛ Seboim bon no kwan so kɔɔ sare so fam.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Nanso na ɔtomfo biara nni Israel asase no so baabiara, efisɛ Filistifo kae sɛ: Anyɛ saa a, Hebrifo bɛbɔ nkrante ne mpeaw.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: na wogye fɛtɛw nnade ne nsosɔw no biara ho dwetɛbona nkyemu abiɛsa mu biako, na wɔsew nkuma anaa wosiesie nnade a wɔde ka, mmoa nso a, wogye dwetɛbona nkyemu abiɛsa mu biako no mmɔho.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na koda no, wɔanhu nkrante anaa peaw dɔm a wɔne Saul ne Yonatan wɔ hɔ no mu biara nsam gye Saul ne ne ba Yonatan nsam na wohuu bi.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Na Filistifo bansifo no fii adi kɔɔ baabi a Mikmas fa.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ aberante a okura n’akode no sɛ: Bra ma yentwam nkɔ momonotofo bansifo yi ho, ebia AWURADE bedi ama yɛn, na biribiara nsiw AWURADE kwan sɛ ɔde ade bebree anaa ketewa begye nkwa.

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Na n’akodekurafo no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Yɛ nea ɛwɔ wo komam nyinaa; dan wo ho, hwɛ, meka wo ho sɛ wo koma pɛ.

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yonatan kae sɛ: Hwɛ, yɛrebetwam akɔ nnipa no ho akoyi yɛn ho akyerɛ wɔn,

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: na sɛ wɔka kyerɛ yɛn sɛ: Munnyina hɔ na yɛmmra mo nkyɛn a, ɛnne yebegyina yɛn gyinabea na yɛremforo nkɔ wɔn nkyɛn.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔka sɛ: Momforo mmra yɛn so a, ɛnne yɛbɛforo akɔ, efisɛ AWURADE de wɔn ahyɛ yɛn nsa, na eyi bɛyɛ yɛn sɛnkyerɛnne.

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan de ne nsa ne ne nan foroe, na n’akodekurafo no dii n’akyi, na wɔtotɔe Yonatan anim, na n’akodekurafo no kunkum dii n’akyi.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: na menne sɛ anka dɔm yi dii wɔn atamfo asade a wonyae no bi; enti nso na Filistifo kum no anyɛ kɛse no. Saul ne amanaman no di ako

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Na Saul ne dɔm a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa hyia boaa wɔn ho ano kɔɔ nsra no mu, na hwɛ, obiara nkrante kyerɛ ne yɔnko so, na ɛyɛɛ kitikiti kɛse pa ara.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Na ehu baa nsra no mu, petee mu ne dɔm no nyinaa mu; bansifo no ne afowfo no nso, ehu kaa wɔn, na asase no wosowee; na ɛyɛɛ ehu kɛse pa ara.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Na Saul awɛmfo a wɔwɔ Gibea-benyamin no hwɛe, na hwɛ, nnipakuw no rehwete, fa ha sen ha.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ dɔm a wɔne no wɔ hɔ no sɛ: Monkan na munhu nea wafi yɛn mu kɔ. Na wɔkanee, na hwɛ, Yonatan ne n’akodekurafo nni hɔ.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Ahiya sɛ: Kɔfa Onyankopɔn adaka no bra. Nso da no, na Onyankopɔn adaka no wɔ Israelfo no nkyɛn.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Na Saul ne ɔsɔfo no rekasa no, Filistifo nsram kitikitiyɛ no kɔɔ so dɔɔso ara. Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo no sɛ: Twe wo nsa!

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Nso Hebrifo a wɔka Filistifo no ho kan a wɔne wɔn foro baa nsra no mu fi asase a atwa ho ahyia no so no, wɔn nso bɛkaa Israelfo a wɔka Saul ne Yonatan ho no ho.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo a wokohintahintaw Efraim bepɔw so no nyinaa tee sɛ Filistifo aguan no, wɔn nso tu bɛtaree wɔn ne wɔn koe.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Na ɛden Israel mmarima da no; na Saul kaa ɔman no ntam sɛ: Nnome nka obiara a obedidi ansa na onwini adwo, na minni m’atamfo so were. Enti ɔman no mu biara amfa aduan anka n’ano.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no duu kwae no mu no, na hwɛ, ɛwo resosɔ; nanso obiara amfa ne nsa ankɔ n’ano, efisɛ ɔman no suro ntam no.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Nso Yonatan de, n’agya reka ɔman no ntam no, wante; na ɔde poma a okurae no ano kaa ɛwo no bi, na ɔde ne nsa kɔɔ n’ano, na n’ani so tetew no.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Na nkurɔfo no mu biako buae sɛ: W’agya aka dɔm no ntam sɛ: Nnome nka obiara a obedidi nnɛ; na nkurɔfo no retɔ piti.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan kae sɛ: M’agya ahaw asase yi. Monhwɛ sɛ mekaa ɛwo yi kakra mehwɛe yi, m’ani so atetew me;

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Na wokum Filistifo no da no fi Mikmas koduu Ayalon; na ɛdɔm no tɔɔ piti sɛ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Na dɔm no tow kɔhyɛɛ asade no so, na wɔfaa nguan ne anantwi ne anantwi mma kunkum wɔn ɛfam, na dɔm no dii no mogya mu.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Hwɛ, dɔm no reyɛ AWURADE bɔne sɛ wodi no mogya mu. Na ɔkae sɛ: Moafom, mumpirew ɔbo kɛse mmrɛ me nnɛ.

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Monhwete nkɔ dɔm no mu nkɔka nkyerɛ wɔn sɛ: Momfa mo anantwi ne mo nguan mmra me nkyɛn mmekum wɔn ha nni, na monnyɛ AWURADE bɔne sɛ mubedi no mogya mu. Na dɔm no nyinaa kurakura wɔn anantwi bae anadwo no bekunkum wɔn hɔ.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Na Saul sii afɔremuka maa AWURADE. Ɛno ne afɔremuka a edi kan a osi maa AWURADE.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Momma yensian nkotiw Filistifo no anadwo yi, na yɛmfom wɔn nkodu adekyee, na yɛannyaw wɔn mu nipa biako. Na wɔkae sɛ: Nea eye w’ani so nyinaa, yɛ! Na ɔsɔfo no kae sɛ: Momma yentwiw mmɛn Onyankopɔn wɔ ha.

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Na Saul bisaa Onyankopɔn sɛ: So minsian mintiw Filistifo no anaa? So wode wɔn bɛhyɛ Israel nsa anaa? Na wammua no da no.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul kae sɛ: Mo dɔm mu atitiriw nyinaa, muntwiw mmɛn ha, na monhwɛ nhu dekode a enti bɔne yi aba nnɛ.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE a ogye Israel te ase yi, sɛ ɛwɔ me ba Yonatan po so a, owu na obewu. Na dɔm no mu biara ammua no.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔka kyerɛɛ Israel nyinaa sɛ: Mo de, monkɔ afa, na me ne me ba Yonatan nso nkɔ afa. Na dɔm no ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Nea eye w’ani so no, yɛ!

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul kae sɛ: Mommɔ me ne me ba Yonatan ntam ntonto. Na ɛbɔɔ Yonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Yonatan sɛ: Kyerɛ me nea woyɛe. Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔka na mede me nsam poma ti mekaa ɛwo kakra mehwɛe. Hwɛ, owu na mewu!

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Yonatan, Onyankopɔn nyɛ saa na ɔnkɔ so nyɛ saa, sɛ owu na wubewu.

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na ɛdɔm no ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: So Yonatan a wayɛ Israel mu ogye adwuma kɛse yi nwu anaa? Ɛmpare no! Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, ne ti nwi biako po rentɔ fam, efisɛ ɔne Nyankopɔn na ayɛ ade nnɛ da yi. Na ɔman no gyee Yonatan na wanwu.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul fii Filistifo no akyidi san bae; na Filistifo no kɔɔ wɔn nkurow mu.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Na ɔko dennen daa Filistifo so Saul nna nyinaa. Na sɛ Saul hu ɔbarima hoɔdenfo biara anaa obiara a ɔyɛ nnam a, ɔkɔfa no ba ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Me na AWURADE somaa me sɛ memmɛsra wo ngo minsi wo ne man so hene; na afei tie AWURADE nsɛm:

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Sɛɛ na asafo AWURADE se: Mahu nea Amalek yɛɛ Israel, sɛnea wofi Misraim reba no wobetwaree wɔn ɔkwan mu.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na afei kɔ na kokum Amalek, na monsɛe nea wɔwɔ nyinaa pasaa, na nkyɛe wɔn so, na kum mmarima ne mmea, mmofra ne nkokoaa, anantwi ne nguan, yoma ne mfurum.

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul maa ɔman no tee, na ɔkan wɔn wɔ Telaim, mmarima a wɔnam anammɔn mu ɔpehanu ne Yuda mmarima ɔpedu.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE asɛm baa Samuel nkyɛn sɛ:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Na Saul duu Amalek kurokɛse no so, na ɔde atɛwfo sisii obon no mu.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Kenifo no sɛ: Monkɔ, mumfi Amalek mu nsian nkɔ, na mampra wo mamfra wɔn; na wo de, woyɛɛ Israelfo nyinaa adɔe bere a wofi Misraim reba no. Ɛnna Kenifo fii Amalek mu kɔe.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Saul kunkum Amalek fii Hawila de kosii baabi a w’ani kyerɛ Sur a ɛda Misraim apuei fam no.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Na Saul ne dɔm no kyɛe Agag ne nguan ne anantwi a woye ne wɔn a wɔadodɔ srade ne nguammuruwa ne nea eye no nyinaa so, na wɔampɛ sɛ wɔsɛe wɔn; na ade biara a wommu na enye mma hwee no de, wɔsɛee no pasaa.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: Manu me ho sɛ misii Saul hene, efisɛ wasan afi m’akyi, na wamma me nsɛm annyina. Na ɛyɛɛ Samuel awerɛhow, na osu frɛɛ AWURADE anadwo no nyinaa.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel tuaa ahema sɛ okohyia Saul anɔpa; na wɔka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Saul aba Karmel, na hwɛ, wasi ne nkaedum, na wadan ne ho atwam asian rekɔ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel duu Saul nkyɛn no, Saul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: AWURADE nhyira nka wo. Mama AWURADE asɛm no atim.

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Na Samuel kae sɛ: Na ɛdɛn ne nguan su a egu m’asom yi ne anantwi su a mete yi?

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Na Saul se: Amalekfo mu na wɔde fi bae, efisɛ ɔman no kyɛe nguan ne anantwi a eye no so, sɛ wɔde rebɛbɔ afɔre ama AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn, na nkae no de, yɛasɛe wɔn pasaa.

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Gyae, ma menka nea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ me anadwo yi menkyerɛ wo. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kasa ɛ!

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel kae sɛ: Ɛwom sɛ woyɛ wo ara w’ani so ketewa de, nanso wone Israel mmusuakuw ti, AWURADE sraa wo sɛ di Israel so hene;

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: na AWURADE somaa wo akwankɔ bi sɛ: Kɔ na kɔsɛe Amalekfo nnebɔneyɛfo no pasaa, na wo ne wɔn nko nkosi sɛ wobɛhyew wɔn.

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛn nti na woantie AWURADE, na woatow ahyɛ asade so, na woayɛ nea ɛyɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne yi?

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Sɛ matie AWURADE, na makɔ ɔkwan a AWURADE somaa me no, na mede Amalek hene Agag maba, na masɛe Amalek pasaa!

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Na ɔman no faa asade no mu nguan ne anantwi, ahyirade no mu adikanne, sɛ wɔde rebɛbɔ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn afɔre Gilgal.

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Na Samuel kae sɛ: So AWURADE pɛ ɔhyew afɔre ne okum afɔre sɛ otie a wotie AWURADE anaa? Hwɛ, osetie ye sen afɔre, na asoyɛ kyɛn adwennini srade.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Na atuatew te sɛ woakɔ abisa, na asoɔden te sɛ amumɔyɛ ne ahonisom! Esiane sɛ woapo AWURADE asɛm nti, ɔno nso apa wo afi ahenni no so.

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Mayɛ bɔne sɛ mafom AWURADE anom asɛm ne wo nsɛm so, sɛ misuroo ɔman no na mitiee wɔn.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na afei fa me bɔne firi me, na wo ne me nsan na menkɔsɔre AWURADE.

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Me ne wo rensan nkɔ, efisɛ woapa AWURADE asɛm, na AWURADE nso apa wo sɛ nni Israel so hene.

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Na Samuel dan ne ho rekɔ no, Saul soo ne batakari ano, na esuanee.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Osuan na AWURADE asuan Israel ahenni afi wo nsam nnɛ, na ɔde ama wo yɔnko a oye sen wo.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Nso Israel Tumfo no renni atoro na ɔrennu ne ho, efisɛ ɔnyɛ onipa na wanu ne ho.

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ose: Mayɛ bɔne de, nanso afei di me ni me man mpanyin ne Israel anim: Wo ne me nsan nkɔ, na menkɔsɔre AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel san kodii Saul akyi; na Saul kɔsɔree AWURADE.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel se: Momfa Amalek hene Agag mmrɛ me ha. Na Agag baa ne nkyɛn anigye so. Na Agag se: Ampa, owuyaw atwam kɔ.

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Na Samuel se: Sɛ wo nkrante maa mmea dii mmasigyaw no, saa ara nso na wo na bedi basigyaw mmea mu. Na Samuel twitwaa Agag AWURADE anim wɔ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel siim kɔɔ Rama. Na Saul nso foro kɔɔ ne fi Gibea-saul.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel ammɛhwɛ Saul bio kosii ne wuda, na Samuel gyam Saul; na AWURADE nuu ne ho sɛ ɔde Saul dii Israel so hene.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Wubegyam Saul akosi da bɛn? Na me de, mapa no sɛ onnni Israel so hene. Fa ngo hyɛ w’abɛn ma, na bra ma mensoma wo Betlehemni Yese nkyɛn, efisɛ ne mma mu na mayi ɔhene mafa.

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Na Samuel se: Mɛyɛ dɛn makɔ? Na Saul te a, obekum me. Na AWURADE se: Fa nantwi ba kura na kɔka sɛ: AWURADE afɔrebɔ na mebae.

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Na frɛ Yese bra afɔre no ho, na me ara mɛkyerɛ wo nea yɛ, na sra nea mɛka makyerɛ wo no ma me.

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Na Samuel yɛe sɛnea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no no, na ɔkɔɔ Betlehem. Na kurow no mu mpanyin de ahopopo behyiaa no kae sɛ: Woba no asomdwoe mu anaa?

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Na ose: Asomdwoe mu: AWURADE afɔrebɔ na mebae yi; munnwira mo ho na mo ne me nkɔ afɔre no ho. Na odwiraa Yese ne ne mma no, na ɔfrɛɛ wɔn baa afɔre no ho.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Na wɔbaa mu no, ohuu Eliab, na ose: Ampa, nea AWURADE asra no no na ɔwɔ n’anim yi.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Samuel sɛ: Nhwɛ ne ho tebea ne ne nipadua tentenyɛ, na mempɛ no; na menhwɛ nea onipa hwɛ, na onipa hwɛ nea etua aniwa, na AWURADE de, ɔhwɛ komam.

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yese frɛɛ Abinadab ma otwaa mu Samuel anim. Na ose: Oyi nso, AWURADE mfaa no ɛ.

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Na Yese maa Sama twaa mu. Na ose: Oyi nso, AWURADE mfaa no ɛ.

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Na Yese maa ne mma baasɔn betwaa mu Samuel anim. Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Yese sɛ: AWURADE mpaw eyinom ɛ.

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Yese sɛ: So mmerante no nyinaa ni? Na ose: Aka akumaa no, na hwɛ, ɔrehwɛ nguan. Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Yese sɛ: Soma ma wɔnkɔfa no mmra, na yɛrentena ase gye sɛ waba ansa.

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsoma ma wɔkɔfaa no bae. Nso ɔbere, na n’aniwa yɛ fɛ, na ne ho nso yɛ fɛ. Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Sɔre sra no, na ɔno ara ni.

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Ɛnna Samuel faa ngo abɛn no, na ɔsraa no ne nuanom mu. Na AWURADE honhom sii Dawid so fi da no ara de rekɔ no. Ɛnna Samuel sɔre baa Rama. Dawid ba Saul ahemfi

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE honhom fii Saul so, na honhommɔne fi AWURADE nkyɛn bɛhaw no.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Na Saul nkoa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ ɛ, honhommɔne bi efi Nyankopɔn na ɛrehaw wo yi.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Ma yɛn wura nka nkyerɛ wo nkoa a wɔwɔ w’anim yi, na wɔnkɔhwehwɛ obi a onim sankubɔ, na sɛ Onyankopɔn honhommɔne no ba wo so a, ɔde ne nsa abɔ ama wo ho atɔ wo.

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Monhwehwɛ obi a onim bɔ yiye mma me ɛ, na momfa no mmrɛ me.

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Na mmerante no mu biako buae sɛ: Hwɛ, mahu Betlehemni Yese ba bi a onim bɔ, ɔyɛ ɔbarima a otumi, na ɔyɛ ɔkofoni, na onim kasa nso, ne ho nso yɛ fɛ, na AWURADE di n’akyi.

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Na Saul somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Yese nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Ma wo ba Dawid a ɔhwɛ nguan no mmra me nkyɛn.

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Na Yese faa afurum de abodoo ne nsa tumpan kɛse biako, ne ɔpapo soaa no, na ɔde somaa ne ba Dawid kɔmaa Saul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Na Dawid baa Saul nkyɛn, na ɔbɛyɛɛ ne somfo. Na Saul dɔɔ no sɛ, na ɔde no yɛɛ n’akodekurafo.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Na Saul soma kɔɔ Yese nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Ma Dawid nsom me, na wanya m’anim anuonyam.

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Na ɛbae, sɛ honhom no fi Onyankopɔn nkyɛn ba Saul so a, na Dawid afa sanku na ɔde ne nsa abɔ, na Saul ho adwo no, na ne ho atɔ no, na honhommɔne no afi no so kɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo boaboaa wɔn dɔm ano sɛ wɔrebedi ako, na wɔbɛboaa wɔn ho ano Soko a ɛyɛ Yuda dea no, na wɔbɛbɔɔ nsra Soko ne Aseka ntam wɔ Efes-damim.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo gyina bepɔw so ɔfa ha, na Israel nso gyina bepɔw so ɔfa ha, na obon da wɔn ntam.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima katakyi bi fi Filistifo nsram fii adi, ne din de Goliat, ofi Gat, ne tenten si basafa abiɛsa ne nsama,

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: na kɔbere nkataho kata ne nan ho, na kɔbere pɛmɛ wɔ ne mmati so.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Na Dawid fi Filistini no kum resan aba no, Abner faa no de no baa Saul anim, na Filistini no ti no kura no.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Na ne peaw dua te sɛ ɔtamanwemfo nsadua, na ne peaw ti kari dade nnwetɛbona ahansia; na ɔkyɛmkurafo di n’anim.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Na obegyinaa hɔ teɛɛm frɛɛ Israel mpasua ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdɛn na moafi aba mpasua so rebɛko yi? So menyɛ Filistini na mo nso moyɛ Saul nkoa? Munyi mo barima bi na onsian mmra me nkyɛn.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Sɛ otumi ne me ko na okum me a, ɛnne yɛbɛyɛ mo nkoa; na sɛ me nso mitumi no, na mikum no a, ɛnne monyɛ yɛn nkoa na monsom yɛn.

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Na Filistini no kae sɛ: Me de, mabɔ Israel mpasua ahohora nnɛ da yi, momma me ɔbarima bi na yɛnko.

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Na Saul ne Israel nyinaa tee Filistini no nsɛm yi no, wɔn bo tui, na wosuroe pa ara.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Nso Efratini bi a wɔfrɛ no Dawid, a ofi Betlehem Yuda, wɔfrɛ n’agya se Yese, na ɔwɔ mmammarima baawɔtwe. Saul bere so no, na ɔbarima no abɔ akora adi mfe ara sann.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: na Dawid de, ɛyɛ a, ofi Saul nkyɛn san kɔhwɛ n’agya nguan Betlehem.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Na adaduanan, na Filistini no fi begyina hɔ anɔpatutu ne anwummere biara de ne ho kyerɛ.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa ne poma kurae, na ɔpaw mmosea a akokwaw anum fii subon no mu de guu ne nguanhwɛfo kotoku, ne bɔtɔ mu, na okuraa n’ataabo ne nsam, na otwiw bɛn Filistini no.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Na Yese ka kyerɛɛ ne ba Dawid sɛ: Fa wo nuanom nneɛma yi, nkyeweɛ olonka yi ne abodoo du yi, tu mmirika kɔ nsram kɔma wo nuanom;

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: na fa nufusu a akyenkyen sebɔw du yi kɔma apem so safohene no, na hwɛ sɛnea wo nuanom ho te, na fa wɔn ho biribi bra.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Nso Saul ne wɔn ne Israel mmarima nyinaa wɔ Ela bon no mu ne Filistifo reko.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Na Dawid sɔree anɔpahema gyaw nguan no hyɛɛ ɔhwɛfo foforo nsa na ɔsoaa nneɛma no kɔe, sɛnea Yese hyɛɛ no no; na okoduu nteaseɛnam aboae; na ɛdɔm no refi adi akɔ mpasua so na wɔrebɔ ɔko se,

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: na Israel ne Filistifo a twitwa mpasua a dɔm kyerɛ dɔm anim.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid gyaw ne nneɛma a okurae no hyɛɛ nneɛma sohwɛfo nsa, no otutuu mmirika kɔɔ mpasua no so kobisaa ne nuanom sɛnea wɔte.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Na ɔne wɔn rekasa no, hwɛ, Filistini katakyi a wɔfrɛ no Goliat a ofi Gat no fi Filistifo mpasua no so bae, na ɔbɛkekaa nsɛm no ara, na Dawid tee.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no nyinaa, wohu ɔbarima no a, woguanguan fi n’anim, na wosuro sɛ.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no kekae sɛ: Sɛ moahu ɔbarima a ɔreforo aba yi? Israel ahohorabɔ na ɔreba yi; na onii ko a obekum no no, ɔhene bɛma wanya ne ho sɛ, na ɔde ne babea bɛma no aware, na wama n’agya fi ade wɔn ho wɔ Israel.

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ mmarima a wɔne no gyina hɔ no sɛ: Dɛn na wɔbɛyɛ onipa a obekum Filistini yi na wayi ahohora afi Israel so no? Na hena po ne Filistini momonoto yi a ɔbɔ Onyankopɔn teasefo mpasua ahohora yi?

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Na nkurɔfo no kaa saa asɛm no ara kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛɛ na wɔbɛyɛ onipa a obekum no no.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Na ne nua panyin Eliab tee sɛ ɔne mmarima no rekasa; na Eliab bo fuw Dawid kae sɛ: Dɛn nti na wusian baa ha? Na hena na wugyaw nguan kakra a wɔwɔ wuram no hyɛɛ ne nsa? Me de, minim w’anuɔden ne wo koma mu bɔne dedaw sɛ ɔko no hwɛ nti na wusian bae.

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid se: Dɛn na mayɛ? So ɛnyɛ asɛm bi nti?

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Na ɔdan ne ho fii ne nkyɛn kyerɛɛ obi, na ɔkaa saa asɛm no ara. Na nkurɔfo no de kan asɛm no ara buaa no.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Na wɔtee Dawid nsɛm a ɔkae no, wɔde kɔtoo Saul anim, na ɔma wɔkɔfaa no bae.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Mma ne ho nnyɛ obiara abotu; w’akoa bɛkɔ ne Filistini yi akɔko.

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Wuntumi nkɔ ne Filistini no nkɔko, efisɛ wo de, woyɛ abofra, na ɔno de, ɔyɛ ɔbarima kofoni fi ne mmofraase.

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: W’akoa rehwɛ n’agya nguan na sisi ba bɛkyere oguammaa fi kuw no mu a,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mifi adi mitiw no mekɔbɔ no, na miyi no mifi n’anom; na sɛ ɔsɔre hyɛ me a, miso ne bogyesɛ mu mebɔ no mikum no.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: W’akoa akum gyata ne sisi nyinaa, na Filistini momonoto yi nyɛ sɛ wɔn mu biako, sɛ wabɔ Onyankopɔn teasefo mpasua ahohora yi.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: AWURADE a oyii me gyata ne sisi nsam no, ɔno ara beyi me Filistini yi nsam. Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Kɔ, na AWURADE bedi w’akyi.

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Na Saul de ne ntade hyɛɛ Dawid na ɔde kɔbere kyɛw soaa no, na ɔde nkatabo hyɛɛ no.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Na Dawid de ne nkrante bɔɔ n’atade no so, na ɔde nantew hwɛe; efisɛ na onnya nsɔ nhwɛe ɛ. Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Merentumi mfa eyinom nkɔ, efisɛ mensɔ menhwɛe da. Na Dawid yi fii ne ho.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Na Filistini no nso nam reba, na otwiw bɛn Dawid; na ɔbarima a ɔso kyɛm no di n’anim.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Na Filistini no totoo n’ani na ohuu Dawid no, obuu no animtiaa; efisɛ ɔyɛ abofra, na ɔbere, nso ne ho yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Na Filistini no ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Ɔkraman ne me na wode mpoma reba me nkyɛn? Na Filistini no frɛɛ ne nyame domee Dawid.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Na Filistini no ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Bra me nkyɛn na memfa wo nam memma wim nnomaa ne wuram mmoa.

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Filistini no sɛ: Wo de, wode nkrante ne peaw ne pɛmɛ na ɛreba me nkyɛn, na me de, mede asafo AWURADE, Israel mpasua a woabɔ wɔn ahohora no Nyankopɔn din na mereba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Ɛnnɛ da yi AWURADE de wo bɛhyɛ me nsa, na makum wo, na matwa wo ti afi so, na mede Filistifo dɔm afunu mama wim nnomaa ne asase so mmoadoma nnɛ ara, na asase nyinaa ahu sɛ Onyankopɔn bi wɔ Israel,

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: na bagua yi nyinaa nso ahu sɛ ɛnyɛ nkrante ne peaw na AWURADE de gye nkwa, efisɛ ɔko no yɛ AWURADE dea, na ɔde mo bɛhyɛ yɛn nsa.

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: na Dawid teɛɛ ne nsa hyɛɛ kotoku no mu yii ɔbo wɔ mu, na ɔtow ataabo no bɔɔ Filistini no moma so, na ɔbo no hyɛn ne tirim, na ɔhwee ase maa n’anim butuw fam.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Saa na Dawid de ataabo ne ɔbo faa Filistini no so, na ɔbɔɔ Filistini no kum no; nanso na nkrante bi nkura Dawid nsam.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Enti Dawid tutuu mmirika kogyinaa Filistini no so, na osoo ne nkrante mu twe fii boha mu, na okum no, na ɔde twaa ne ti. Na Filistifo no hui sɛ wɔn bran no awu no, woguanee.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel ne Yuda mmarima sɔre bɔɔ ose na wotiw Filistifo no koduu Gat ne Ekron apon akyi. Na Filistifo apirafo no totɔe Saaraim kwan so de koduu Gat ne Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no san fii Filistifo no akyidi ne ɔtaa dennen no mu, na wɔbɛfow wɔn nsra no.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Na Dawid faa Filistini no ti, na ɔde baa Yerusalem; na n’akode de, ɔde guu ne ntamadan mu.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Na Saul huu Dawid sɛ ɔrefi adi akohyia Filistini no no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne sahene Abner sɛ: Abner, hena ba ne aberante yi? Na Abner se: Ɔhene, sɛ wo kra te ase yi, minnim.

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Aberante, hena ba ne wo? Na Dawid buae sɛ: W’akoa Yese, Betlehemni no, ba ne me.

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Na Saul faa no da no ara, na wamma wansan ankɔ n’agya fi.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ne Dawid pam apam bi, efisɛ ɔdɔ no sɛ n’ankasa ne kra.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan yii ne batakari a ɔhyɛ no maa Dawid, ne ne ntade koduu ne nkrante ne ne ta ne n’abɔso so.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Na Dawid fi adi kɔ baabiara a Saul soma no, na ne biribiara kɔ so; na Saul de no sii akofofo so, na ɔsɔɔ ɔman no nyinaa ne Saul nkoa nso ani. Saul twe Dawid ho ninkunu

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Na wɔreba a Dawid resan afi Filistini no kum aba no, mmea fii Israel nkurow nyinaa mu de nnwom ne asaw ba behyiaa ɔhene Saul; wɔde mpintin ne anigye ne ahinasa sanku ade.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Na mmea a wɔregoru no gyigyee wɔn ho so sɛ: Saul akum apem mu, na Dawid akum wɔ ɔpedu mu

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Na Saul bo fuwii kɛse, na asɛm no anyɛ no dɛ. Na ɔkae sɛ: Wɔde ɔpedu, ɔpedu ama Dawid, na me de, wɔde apem, apem ama me, na dɛn na aka no bio sɛ ahenni no?

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Na n’adekyee no, Onyankopɔn honhommɔne no sii Saul so, na ɔrekɔm ofie, na Dawid de ne nsa rebɔ sanku, sɛnea ɔyɛ daa no; Saul kura peaw.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Na Saul tow peaw no, na ose: Mɛbɔ Dawid mafam ɔfasu ho; na Dawid dan ne ho fii n’anim mprenu.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Na Saul suroo Dawid, efisɛ AWURADE di n’akyi, na Saul de, wafi ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔɔ so n’akwan nyinaa mu, na AWURADE dii n’akyi.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Na Saul hui sɛ ne biribiara kɔ so no, osuroo no kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Na Israel ne Yuda nyinaa dɔɔ Dawid, efisɛ ɔno na odi wɔn anim ahyɛmfiri.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Hwɛ, me ba panyin Merab ni, ɔno na mede no mɛma wo aware. Nnam ara na yɛ ma me, na ko ma AWURADE! Efisɛ Saul se: Wɔmmma me nsa nnka no, na Filistifo na wɔn nsa nka no.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Hena ne me, na m’abusuafo ne hefo, m’agya abusua ne dɛn wɔ Israel, na memmɛyɛ ɔhene sew?

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Na bere dui a anka wɔde Saul babea Merab rebɛma Dawid no, wɔde no maa Meholani Adriel aware.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Na Saul ba Mikal dɔ Dawid; na wɔka kyerɛɛ Saul no, asɛm no yɛɛ no anigye.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Na Saul se: Mede no mɛma no, na ayɛ no afiri, na Filistifo nsa aka no. Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Dawid ne mprenu so sɛ: Wobɛyɛ me sew nnɛ.

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Na Saul nkoa no kaa nsɛm yi guu Dawid asom. Na Dawid kae sɛ: So ɛyɛ mo ani so adewa sɛ obi bɛyɛ ɔhene sew? Na me de, meyɛ onipa hiani a m’akyi nyɛ duru.

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Na Saul nkoa kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛnea Dawid kae ni.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Sɛ monkɔka nkyerɛ Dawid ni: Ɔhene mpɛ tiade bi, sɛ Filistifo mmarima ano were ɔha, na wontɔ ɔhene atamfo so were. Na Saul susuwii sɛ ɔnam Filistifo nsa so bɛma Dawid atɔ.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa kɔkaa nsɛm yi kyerɛɛ Dawid no, ɛyɛɛ Dawid fɛ sɛ ɔbɛyɛ ɔhene sew. Na nna no nnya nnui no,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Na Saul hwɛ hui sɛ AWURADE di Dawid akyi; na Saul babea Mikal dɔ no.

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Na Saul kɔɔ so suroo Dawid ara, na ɛmaa Saul tan Dawid daa.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo mmapɔmma no fii adi bɛkoe. Na da biara a wofi adi ba no, Dawid di nkonim pii sen Saul nkoa nyinaa; ɛno nti, na wɔbɔ ne din nidi mu sɛ.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ ne ba Yonatan ne ne nkoa nyinaa sɛ wonkum Dawid. Nanso Saul ba Yonatan pɛ Dawid asɛm sɛ.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: na me de, mefi adi makogyina m’agya nkyɛn wuram baabi a wowɔ no, na me ne m’agya aka wo ho asɛm, na mete biribi a, maka makyerɛ wo.

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Na ɔde ne kra too ne nsam kokum Filistini no, na AWURADE dii nkonim kɛse maa Israel nyinaa. Wuhui na w’ani gyei; na ɛdɛn nti na worebɛyɛ mogya a edi bem ho bɔne na woakum Dawid kwa?

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Na Saul tiee Yonatan, na Saul kaa ntam sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, wɔrenkum no da!

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan frɛɛ Dawid; na Yonatan kaa nsɛm no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no. Ɛnna Yonatan de Dawid baa Saul nkyɛn, na ɔbɛtenaa n’anim sɛ kan no.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Na ɔko baa bio, na Dawid fii adi ne Filistifo kɔkoe, na okum wɔn kunkɛse, na woguan fii n’anim.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Na Saul hwehwɛɛ sɛ ɔde peaw no bɔ Dawid fam ɔfasu no ho, nanso ɔtwee ne ho fii Saul anim, na ɔtow peaw no wɔɔ ɔfasu no mu; na Dawid guanee, na ofii mu anadwo no.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Dawid fi sɛ wɔnkɔwɛn no na wonkum no anɔpa. Na Dawid yere Mikal ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ woannye wo kra anadwo yi a, ɔkyena wobekum wo.

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Na Mikal de Dawid faa mfɛnsere mu sii fam, na ɔkɔe, na oguan fii mu.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Na Mikal faa ohoni de too mpa no so, na ɔde abirekyi nwi sumii too atifi, na ɔde ntama kataa so.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Na Saul somaa abɔfo sɛ wɔnkɔfa Dawid no, ɔkae sɛ: Ɔyare.
