english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul somaa abɔfo no sɛ wɔnkɔhwɛ Dawid, na ose: Momfa no mfi mpa no so mmrɛ me, na minkum no.

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Na abɔfo no duu hɔ no, na hwɛ, ohoni na ɛda mpa no so, na abirekyi nwi sumii da atifi.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Mikal sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woadaadaa me sɛɛ, na woagya me tamfo kwan na wafi mu afi yi? Na Mikal ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Ɔno na ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Ma menkɔ! Ɛdɛn nti na minkum wo!

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Na Dawid guan fii mu, na ɔkɔɔ Samuel nkyɛn Rama kɔkaa nea Saul ayɛ no nyinaa kyerɛɛ no. Na ɔne Samuel kɔe kɔtenaa Naiot.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Hwɛ, Dawid wɔ Naiot wɔ Rama.

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Na Saul somaa abɔfo sɛ wɔnkɔfa Dawid; na wohuu adiyifo no sɛ wɔrehyɛ nkɔm na Samuel gyina hɔ rehwɛ wɔn so no, Onyankopɔn honhom baa Saul abɔfo no so, na wɔn nso hyehyɛɛ nkɔm.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Saul no, ɔsomaa abɔfo foforo; na wɔn nso hyehyɛɛ nkɔm saa ara. Na Saul somaa abɔfo bio, ne mprɛnsa so, na wɔn nso hyehyɛɛ nkɔm.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔno ara kɔɔ Rama, na oduu abura kɛse a ɛwɔ Seku no ho no, obisae sɛ: Ɛhe na Samuel ne Dawid wɔ? Na wose: Hwɛ, wɔwɔ Naiot wɔ Rama.

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔɔ Naiot wɔ Rama hɔ; na Onyankopɔn honhom baa ɔno nso so, na ɔrekɔ no, ɔhyɛɛ nkɔm ara kɔ kosii sɛ oduu Naiot wɔ Rama.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Na ɔno nso worɔw ne ntade, na ɔno nso hyɛɛ nkɔm Samuel anim, na ɔde adagyaw daa hɔ da mu no nyinaa ne anadwo mu no nyinaa. Enti na wɔka sɛ: So Saul nso fra adiyifo no mu anaa?

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid guan fii Naiot wɔ Rama, na ɔbae bɛka kyerɛɛ Yonatan sɛ: Dɛn na mayɛ? M’amumɔyɛ ne dɛn, na me bɔne ne dɛn wɔ w’agya anim a enti ɔrehwehwɛ me akum me yi?

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛmpare wo, worenwu, hwɛ, m’agya renyɛ ade kɛse anaa ade ketewa bi gye sɛ oyi me asotiw ansa; na ɛdɛn nti na m’agya de asɛm yi behintaw me? Ɛnte sa.

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kaa ntam nso sɛ: W’agya nim sɛ manya w’anim anuonyam, enti na ose: Wɔmmma Yonatan nnhu eyi, na ɛmmmɛyɛ no yaw; na ampa ara, AWURADE te ase na wo kra nso te ase yi, ɔnammɔn pɛ na ɛda me ne owu ntam.

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Biribiara a wo kra se no, mɛyɛ mama wo.

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Yonatan sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔkyena na ɔsram fi, a ɛsɛ sɛ anka me ne ɔhene kɔtena adidii; na ma menkɔ minkohintaw wuram nkosi da a ɛto so abiɛsa no anadwofa.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Sɛ w’agya bisa m’akyi kwan a, ɛnne ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Dawid asrɛ me kwan sɛ ɔretu mmirika akɔ ne kurom Betlehem, na abusua no nyinaa wɔ afirihyia afɔrebɔ wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔka sɛ: Eye a, na asomdwoe wɔ hɔ ma w’akoa, na sɛ ne bo fuw a, ɛnne hu sɛ wakyere ne mu sa bɔne.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Na yɛ w’akoa adɔe, efisɛ AWURADE apam mu na woama wo ne w’akoa ahyɛn; na sɛ amumɔyɛ bi wɔ me mu a, wo ara kum me, na ɛdɛn nti na wode me rekɔma w’agya?

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan se: Ɛmpare wo sɛ, sɛ minim sɛ m’agya asusuw bɔne de reba wo so na merenka menkyerɛ wo.

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Bra ma yemfi nkɔ wuram. Na wɔn baanu fii adi kɔɔ wuram.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn nyɛ ɔdansefo sɛ, sɛ ɔkyena anaa ɔkyena akyi sesɛbere, mehwɛ m’agya adwene, na eye wɔ Dawid ho, na mansoma amma wo nkyɛn ammeyi wo asotiw a!

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛsɔ m’agya ani sɛ bɔne mmra wo so na mamma mammeyi wo asotiw, na mannya wo kwan amma woankɔ asomdwoe mu a, AWURADE nyɛ Yonatan sa na ɔnka ho sa! Na AWURADE nni w’akyi sɛnea odi m’agya akyi no.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: na ntwa w’adɔe no to mfi me fi ho da. Na sɛ AWURADE twitwa Dawid atamfo fi asase so a, mma Yonatan din mfi Dawid da.

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan maa Dawid kaa ne dɔ a ɔde dɔ no no ho ntam bio, efisɛ ɔdɔ no sɛ n’ankasa ne kra.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ no se: Ɔkyena na ɔsram fi, na wobehu sɛ wunni hɔ, efisɛ wo tenabea bɛda mpan.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wudi nnansa a, sian ntɛm bra nea asɛm no bae no, wuhintawee hɔ, na tena Esel bo no ho.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Na mɛtotow agyan abiɛsa mafa ho, sɛnea merebɔ botae mu.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mɛsoma abofra sɛ: Kɔhwehwɛ agyan no. Sɛ mise abofra no sɛ: Hwɛ, agyan no wɔ wo nkyɛn mu ha, tase bra a, ɛnne bra, na, sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, asomdwoe na ɛwɔ hɔ ma wo, asɛm bi nni hɔ.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Na sɛ mise akwankwaa no sɛ: Hwɛ, m’agyan no wɔ w’anim fam noho a, ɛnne kɔ, na AWURADE agya wo kwan.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Na asɛm a me ne wo kae no ho de, hwɛ, AWURADE wɔ me ne wo ntam daa.

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid kohintaw wuram. Na ɔsram fii no, ɔhene kɔtenaa adidii.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene tenaa n’atenae sɛnea ɔyɛ daa no wɔ ɔfasu ho agua no so; na Yonatan sɔree, na Abner tenaa ɔhene nkyɛn, na Dawid atenae no da mpan.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Na Saul anka hwee da no; efisɛ ose: Biribi ayɛ no; ne ho ntew, ampa ara ne ho ntew.

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Na n’adekyee a ɛyɛ ɔsram no da a ɛto so abien a Dawid atenae da mpan no, Saul ka kyerɛɛ ne ba Yonatan sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na Yese ba no mmaa adidi ase nnɛra ne nnɛ yi?

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: na ose: Gya me kwan ɛ, na yɛwɔ abusua afɔrebɔ bi wɔ kurow no mu, na me nua ahyɛ me sɛ memmra. Enti afei, sɛ manya w’anim anuonyam a, ma menkɔ menkɔhwɛ me nuanom. Enti na wamma ɔhene pon ho yi.

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul bo fuw Yonatan, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo, ɔbea brakyewni tuatewfo ba, so minhui sɛ woafa Yese ba no adamfo de rehyɛ wo ho ne wo na adagyaw mu aniwu?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Na mmere dodow a Yese ba no te ase asase so yi, wo ne w’ahenni rennyina. Enti soma ma wɔnkɔfa no mmrɛ me, na owu ara na obewu.

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan buaa n’agya Saul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wonkum no? Dɛn na wayɛ?

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul tow peaw sɛ ɔde rebɔ no. Na Yonatan huu sɛ n’agya awe ahinam sɛ obekum Dawid.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan de abufuhyew sɔre fii ɔpon no ho, na wannidi ɔsram no da a ɛto so abien no. Na odii Dawid ho yaw sɛ n’agya asopa no.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Na anɔpa no Yonatan fii adi kɔɔ wuram nea ɔhyɛɛ Dawid no, na abofra kumaa bi ka ne ho.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’abofra no sɛ: Tutu mmirika kɔhwehwɛ agyan a merebɛtotow no. Abofra no retu mmirika no, ɔtow agyan no traa no.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Na abofra no duu nea agyan a Yonatan towee no wɔ no, Yonatan bɔn abofra no sɛ: So agyan no ngu w’anim noho anaa?

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Na Yonatan bɔn abofra no sɛ: Yɛ ntɛm, ka wo ho, nnyina. Na Yonatan abofra no tasee agyan no de brɛɛ ne wura.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Nso na abofra no nnim ho hwee; Yonatan ne Dawid nko na wonim asɛm no.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yonatan de ne nneɛma no maa abofra no na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa kɔ kurow no mu.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Abofra no kɔe; na Dawid sɔre fii abokuw no ho, na ɔde n’anim bebutuw fam na ɔkotowee mprɛnsa, na wofefew wɔn ho ano, na wɔn baanu sui ara maa Dawid de boroo so.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Kɔ asomdwoe mu. Sɛ yɛn baanu akeka AWURADE ntam no, AWURADE ntena me ne wo ntam ne m’asefo ne w’asefo ntam nkosi daa. Na osii mu kɔe; na Yonatan baa kurow no mu.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid baa Nob sɔfo Ahimelek nkyɛn. Na Ahimelek de ahopopo behyiaa no, ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo nko nam na onipa bi nka wo ho yi?

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Ahimelek sɛ: Ɔhene ahyɛ me asɛm bi di, na waka akyerɛ me sɛ: Mma obiara nnhu dekode a meresoma wo ho, ne nea mahyɛ wo no ho biribi; na mmerante no nso, mahyɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnkɔ baabi.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Na afei, dɛn na ɛwɔ wo nsam? Ma me abodoo anum anaa biribiara a wubenya.

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo no buaa Dawid sɛ: Abodoo hunu bi nni me nsam, sɛ abodoo kronkron na ɛwɔ hɔ; sɛ mmerante no akora wɔn ho afi mmea ho nko a!

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bua see ɔsɔfo no sɛ: Ampa, nnansa ni a misiim yi, yennyaa ɔbea ho kwan da; ɔkwan hunu a yɛretu no mu mpo, na mmerante no ade ho tew, na menne nnɛ a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔn ade ho tew yi.

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsɔfo no de akronkronne no maa no, efisɛ na abodoo bi nni hɔ sɛ kyerɛ abodoo a woyi fi AWURADE anim de abodoohyew begu hɔ da a woyii no.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Nso Saul nkoa mu nipa bi wɔ hɔ da no a wɔato no mu, AWURADE anim, ne din de Doeg, Edomni a ɔyɛ Saul mmoahwɛfo mu panyin no.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Ahimelek sɛ: So peaw anaa nkrante bi nni wo nsam ha? Na me nkrante ne me nneɛma po mamfa mankura, efisɛ ɔhene asɛm no, wɔpɛ no ntɛm.

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo no kae sɛ: Filistini Goliat a wukum no Ela bon mu no nkrante, hwɛ, ɛno na wɔabobɔw no ntama mu da asɔfotade no akyi no, ɛno na wobɛfa a, fa, na foforo bi nni ha sɛ ɛno. Na Dawid kae sɛ: Ebi nte sɛ ɛno, fa ma me!

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Na Dawid sɔre guanee da no fii Saul anim, na ɔkɔɔ Gat hene Akis nkyɛn.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Na Akis nkoa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So ɛnyɛ Dawid, asase no so hene no ni? Ɛnyɛ oyi na wɔtoo ne ho dwom asaw mu kae sɛ: Saul akum n’apem, apem na Dawid akum ne ɔpedu, ɔpedu, no?

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Na Dawid de nsɛm yi siee ne koma mu, na osuroo Gat hene Akis anim sɛ.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Na ɔsakraa ne suban wɔn anim, na ɔboapa yɛɛ ne ho bɔdamfo wɔn nsam, na ɔnworannworan kurow no apon ho, na ɔmaa ne ntasu sensann ne bogyesɛ mu.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Ɛnna Akis ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Hwɛ, muhu sɛ onipa yi abɔ dam, na ɛdɛn nti na mode no abrɛ me?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: So abɔdamfo abɔ me na mode oyi aba sɛ ommedi me so abɔdamsɛm yi? So oyi mmra me fi anaa?

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Na Dawid fii hɔ kɔe, na oguan kɔɔ Adulam bodan mu. Na ne nuanom ne n’agya fi nyinaa tee no, wosian kɔɔ ne nkyɛn hɔ.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Na wɔn a wɔn ho akyere wɔn ne wɔn a ɛdede aka ne wɔn a wɔn werɛ ahow boaboaa wɔn ho ano baa ne nkyɛn, na odii wɔn so safohene. Mmarima bɛyɛ ahanan na wɔbɛkaa ne ho.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid fii hɔ kɔɔ Mispe wɔ Moab, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Moab hene sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, ma m’agya ne me na mmɛtena mo nkyɛn nkosi sɛ mehu nea Onyankopɔn bɛyɛ me ansa.

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Na ogyaw wɔn Moab hene no nkyɛn, na wɔtenaa ne nkyɛn nna a Dawid wɔ bepɔw so atenae hɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Na odiyifo Gad ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Ntena bepɔw so atenae hɔ, na sim kɔ Yuda asase so. Na Dawid siim baa Heret kwae mu.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Na Saul tee sɛ wɔahu nea Dawid ne nnipa a wɔka ne ho no wɔ. Na Saul te Gibea, ɔsantɛw bi ase wɔ koko bi so, na ne okura peaw, na ne nkoa nyinaa gyinagyina ne ho.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa a wogyinagyina ne ho no sɛ: Mo Benyaminfo, muntie! So Yese ba no nso bɛmoma mo nyinaa mfuw ne bobe nturo na ɔde mo nyinaa asisi mpem so asafohene ne ɔha ha so asafohene?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Sɛ mo nyinaa moapam me tiri so, na obiara nni hɔ a oyi me asotiw sɛ me ba ne Yese ba no apam, na mo mu biara nni hɔ a odi me ho yaw na oyi me asotiw sɛ me ba de m’akoa agyina hɔ ne me redi asi, sɛ ɔntɛw me sɛnea ɛte nnɛ yi?

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Edomni Doeg a ɔno nso gyina Saul nkoa no nkyɛn no buae sɛ: Mihuu Yese ba no sɛ ɔbaa Nob, Ahitub ba Ahimelek nkyɛn,

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: na obisaa AWURADE maa no, na ɔmaa no akwansoduan, na ɔde Filistini Goliat nkrante no maa no.

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene soma kohyiaa Ahitub ba ɔsɔfo Ahimelek ne n’agya fi asɔfo a wɔwɔ Nob no nyinaa, na wɔn nyinaa baa ɔhene nkyɛn.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Na Saul kae sɛ: Ahitub ba, tie ɛ! Na obuae sɛ: Mini, me wura.

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo ne Yese ba no apam me tiri so, na womaa no aduan ne nkrante, na wubisaa Onyankopɔn maa no, sɛ ɔnsɔre ntɛw me sɛnea ɛte nnɛ yi?

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Na Ahimelek buaa ɔhene sɛ: Na wo nkoa nyinaa mu hena na ɔyɛ ɔnokwafo sɛ Dawid a ɔyɛ ɔhene sew, na otie w’asɛm, na wodi no ni wɔ wo fi?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: So nnɛ na merefi ase mabisa Onyankopɔn mama no anaa? Eyi mpare me! Mma ɔhene mmfa asɛm bi nnto n’akoa anaa m’agya fi nyinaa so, na w’akoa nnim eyinom nyinaa ho hwee, ketewa oo, kɛse oo!

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Ahimelek, owu ara na wubewu, wo ne w’agya fi nyinaa.

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ mmirikatufo a wogyinagyina ne ho no sɛ: Monnannan mo ho nkum AWURADE asɔfo no, na wɔn nsa nso wɔ Dawid de mu, na wonim sɛ ɔreguan, na wɔanyi me asotiw. Na ɔhene nkoa no ampɛ sɛ wɔteɛ wɔn nsa ka AWURADE asɔfo no.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Doeg sɛ: Wo de, dan wo ho ka asɔfo no. Na Edomni Doeg dan ne ho na ɔkaa asɔfo no kum mmarima aduɔwɔtwe anum a wɔhyɛ nwera asɔfotade no da no ara.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Na asɔfo kurow Nob no nso, ɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn; mmarima ne mmea, mmofra ne nkokoaa, anantwi ne mfurum ne nguan nyinaa na ɔde nkrante kunkum wɔn.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Na Ahitub ba Ahimelek babarima biako a wɔfrɛ no Abiatar fii mu guan tiw Dawid.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Na Abiatar ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ Saul akum AWURADE asɔfo no.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abiatar sɛ: Da no a Edomni Doeg wɔ hɔ no na mihui sɛ ɛyɛ dɛn ara a, ɔbɛkɔ akɔka akyerɛ Saul; me na midi w’agya fi akra nyinaa ho so.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Tena me nkyɛn, nsuro, na nea ɔhwehwɛ me akum me no ara na ɔhwehwɛ wo nso. Na me nkyɛn de, wɔbɛhwɛ wo so.

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Hwɛ, Filistifo ne Keila reko na wɔrefow awiporowbea.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa AWURADE sɛ: So menkɔ minkokum Filistifo yi? Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Kɔ na kokum Filistifo no, na gye Keila.

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Na Dawid mmarima no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, Yuda ha mpo, yesuro, na nkantom sɛ yɛbɛkɔ Keila ne Filistifo dɔm akɔko.

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔɔ so bisaa AWURADE bio. Na AWURADE buaa no sɛ: Sɔre sian kɔ Keila, na me na mede Filistifo no merehyɛ wo nsa.

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ne ne nnipa no siim kɔɔ Keila, na ɔne Filistifo no kɔkoe, na ɔkaa wɔn mmoa fae, na okum wɔn okunkɛse, na Dawid gyee Keilafo.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid huu sɛ Saul rebɔ ne ho pɔw bɔne no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Abiatar sɛ: Fa asɔfotade no bra.

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, w’akoa ate ampa ara sɛ Saul repɛ aba Keila, na me nti wabɛsɛe kurow no.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: So Keilafo de me bɛhyɛ ne nsa? So Saul besian aba sɛnea w’akoa tee no? AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, ka kyerɛ w’akoa ɛ! Na AWURADE kae sɛ: Obesian aba.

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: So Keilafo beyi me ne me nnipa ahyɛ Saul nsa? Na AWURADE se: Wobeyi wo ama.

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔtenaa sare so bepɔw so atenae horow no mu; na ɔtenaa bepɔw bi so Sif sare so. Na Saul hwehwɛɛ no da biara; nanso Onyankopɔn amfa no anhyɛ ne nsa.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Na Dawid hui sɛ Saul afi adi rebɛhwehwɛ no akum no. Nso Dawid wɔ Sif sare so wɔ Hores.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ba Yonatan sɔre kɔɔ Dawid nkyɛn wɔ Hores, na ɔhyɛɛ ne nsa den Onyankopɔn mu.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro, na m’agya Saul nsa renka wo, na wo na wubedi Israel so hene, na mayɛ w’abediakyiri; na m’agya Saul nso nim sa.

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Na wɔn baanu pamee AWURADE anim. Na Dawid tenaa Hores, na Yonatan kɔɔ fie.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sififo foro kɔɔ Saul nkyɛn Gibea kɔkae sɛ: So ɛnyɛ Dawid na ohintaw yɛn nkyɛn wɔ atenae a ɛwɔ Hores, Hakila koko a ɛwɔ sare pataa no nifa fam no so no?

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul kae sɛ: AWURADE nhyira nka mo sɛ moahu me mmɔbɔ.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Monkɔ nkɔhwehwɛ mu yiye, na monhwɛ nhu faako a ɔhyɛ ne onii ko a ohuu no hɔ. Na mate sɛ ɔyɛ oniferefo sɛ.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Na monhwɛ nhu faako a ohintahintaw no nyinaa, na sɛ ɛyɛ ampa a, monsan mmra me nkyɛn, na me ne mo nkɔ. Na sɛ ɔwɔ asase no so a, mɛtwee mapɛ no Yuda mpem nyinaa mu.

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Na wɔsɔre dii Saul anim kɔɔ Sif. Na Dawid ne ne nnipa no wɔ Maon sare so, tataw a ɛwɔ sare pataa no nifa fam no so.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Na Saul ne ne nnipa kɔe sɛ wɔkɔhwehwɛ no. Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid; na osian ɔbotan no kɔtenaa Maon sare so. Na Saul tee no, otiw Dawid baa Maon sare so.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Na Saul nam bepɔw no fa ha, na Dawid ne ne nnipa nso nam bepɔw no fa ha; na Dawid repɛ ntɛm afi Saul anim akɔ no, Saul ne ne nnipa no twaa Dawid ne ne nnipa no ho hyiae sɛ wɔrekyere wɔn.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo bi baa Saul nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Ka wo ho bra, na Filistifo abegu asase no so.

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Enti Saul san fii Dawid akyi kɔe kohyiaa Filistifo no. Enti wɔfrɛ hɔ sɛ: Sela-hamahlekot

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Na Dawid fii hɔ foro kɔtenaa En-gedi bepɔw so atenae mu.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Na Saul san fii Filistifo akyi bae no, wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, Dawid wɔ En-gedi sare so.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Na oduu nguannan a ɛwɔ ɔkwan no so no ho; na ɔbodan bi wɔ hɔ, na Saul hyɛn mu sɛ okogyaa n’anan; na Dawid ne ne nnipa nso tete ɔbodan no mu nohoa

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Na Dawid nnipa no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, da a AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ wo sɛ: Hwɛ, mede wo tamfo mɛhyɛ wo nsa, na woayɛ no sɛnea eye w’ani so no ni. Ɛnna Dawid sɔre wiawiaa ne ho kotwaa Saul batakari ano.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, Dawid koma bɔɔ no paa sɛ watwa Saul atade ano.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Na Dawid de nsɛm yi bɔɔ ne nnipa no pem, na wampene amma wɔansɔre anhyɛ Saul. Na Saul sɔre fii ɔbodan no mu sii ne kwan so.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, Dawid nso sɔre fii ɔbodan no mu fii adi, na ɔbɔn Saul sɛ: Me wura ɔhene! Na Saul hwɛɛ n’akyi no, Dawid bɔɔ ne ti ase na ɔkotowee.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wutie nnipa nsɛm a wɔkeka sɛ: Hwɛ, Dawid pɛ wo bɔne, no?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ɛnnɛ da yi w’aniwa ahu sɛnea AWURADE de wo hyɛɛ me nsa nnɛ ɔbodan no mu; na wɔkae sɛ minkum wo, nanso mekyɛee wo so, na mise: Merenteɛ me nsa menka me wura, efisɛ nea AWURADE asra no ne no.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Nso, m’agya, ampa ara, hwɛ sɛ mikura wo batakari ano. Na sɛ matwa wo batakari ano na mankum wo yi, hu na hwɛ sɛ bɔne anaa mmarato bi nni me nsam; na menyɛɛ wo bɔne bi ɛ, nso wo de, worepɛ me akum me.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: AWURADE mmu me ne wo ntam atɛn, na AWURADE nnye m’aweretɔde wo nsam. Na me nsa de, ɛrenka wo.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Sɛnea tete bɛ no ka no: Abɔnefo so na bɔne fi; na me nsa de, ɛrenka wo.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Ɛhena akyi na Israel hene atu di yi? Hena na woretiw no yi? Ɔkraman funu akyi, ɔkraman dwiw biako akyi.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nyɛ ɔtemmufo, na ommu me ne wo ntam atɛn, na onhu na onni m’asɛm mma me, na ommu me atɛn nyi me wo nsam.

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Woteɛ kyɛn me, efisɛ wode papa atua me ka, na me de, mede bɔne matua wo ka.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Na woakyerɛ me nnɛ sɛ wo ne me adi no yiye, sɛ AWURADE de me hyɛɛ wo nsa na woankum me.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Na sɛ obi to ne tamfo a, ɔbɛma ɔde ne ho sɔnn akɔ anaa? Enti AWURADE ntua wo ka pa nhyɛ nea woayɛ me nnɛ yi ananmu.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, minim sɛ wubedi hene, na Israel ahenni betim, wo nsam;

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: na afei ka me AWURADE ntam sɛ worentwa m’asefo a wobedi m’akyi ngu, na worempopa me din mfi m’agya fi.

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kaa Saul ntam no. Na Saul siim kɔɔ fie; na Dawid ne ne nnipa no foro kɔɔ bepɔw so a.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Na munse no sɛ: Asomdwoe nka wo, asomdwoe nka wo fi, na asomdwoe nka nea wowɔ nyinaa.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Na afei, mate sɛ wowɔ nguan ho twitwafo; afei wo nguanhwɛfo a wowɔ wɔn no ne yɛn tenae no, yɛanhunahuna wɔn, na wɔn biribiara nso anyera bere a wɔtenaa Karmel no nyinaa;

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: bisabisa wo mmerante no na wɔbɛka akyerɛ wo; enti ma mmerante no nnya w’anim anuonyam, na afahyɛ da na yɛaba yi, fa nea ɛtɔ wo nsam ma wo nkoa ne wo ba Dawid ɛ!

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Na Dawid mmerante no dui no, wɔde Dawid din kaa nsɛm yi nyinaa kyerɛɛ Nabal, na wɔtwɛnee.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Na Nabal buaa Dawid nkoa no sɛ: Hena ne Dawid na hena ne Yese ba? Ɛnnɛ nkoa a wɔtetew wɔn ho fi wɔn wuranom ho dɔɔso.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Na memfa m’aduan ne me nsu ne me nam a makum de rema me nguan ho twitwafo no memma nnipa a minnim nea wofi anaa?

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid mmerante no dan wɔn ho sii kwan so, na wɔsan bɛkaa nsɛm yi nyinaa kyerɛɛ no. Dawid ne Abigail

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ne nnipa no sɛ: Mo nyinaa mmobɔ mo nkrante. Na wɔn nyinaa bobɔɔ wɔn nkrante, na Dawid nso bɔɔ ne nkrante, na ɛbɛyɛ mmarima ahanan foro dii Dawid akyi, na ahanu tenaa nneɛma no ho.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Na afei hwɛ, na dwen nea wobɛyɛ, na wɔakyere yɛn wura ne ne fi nyinaa so sa bɔne, nso ɔyɛ ɔbahuhuni a obi ntumi nkasa nkyerɛ no.

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne mmerante no sɛ: Monsen nni me kan, hwɛ, meredi mo akyi maba. Na ne kunu Nabal de, wanka ankyerɛ no.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Na ɔte afurum so resian aba bepɔw no ase no, na hwɛ, Dawid ne ne nnipa no nso resian ahyia no, na ohyiaa wɔn.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Nso Dawid aka sɛ: Ɔkwa ara kwa na mahwɛ oyi ade a ɔwɔ sare so nyinaa so, na nea ɛyɛ ne de nyinaa mu biribiara anyera, nso bɔne na ɔde ahyɛ me papa ananmu.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Sɛ ekosi ɔkyena anɔpa, migyaw n’ade a ɔwɔ nyinaa mu onini biako pɛ po a, Onyankopɔn nyɛ Dawid atamfo sa na ɔnka ho sa!

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Na Abigail huu Dawid no, ɔyɛɛ ntɛm fii n’afurum so sii fam, na ɔde n’anim butuw Dawid anim, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase kɔɔ fam,

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wo, mma me wura mmfa ne koma nnto onipa huhuni Nabal yi so, na sɛ ne din te no, sɛ ɔte ara ne no, Nabal ne ne din, agyennyentwisɛm wɔ ne mu; na me, w’afenaa de, manhu me wura mmerante a wosomaa wɔn no.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Fa ɔso yi firi w’afenaa ɛ! Na ampa ara, AWURADE bɛkyekye ofi a atim ama me wura, efisɛ me wura reko ama AWURADE, na wɔrenhu wo mu bɔne bi wo nna nyinaa mu.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Na sɛ onipa asɔre retiw wo abɛhwehwɛ wo akum wo a, ɛnne wɔnkyekyere me wura ɔkra, nkwa boaa mu, AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nkyɛn, na w’atamfo kra de, wɔntow no sɛ ade a efi ataabo mu.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE nya yɛ me wura papa a waka wɔ wo ho no nyinaa na ɔde wo si Israel so hene a,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: me wura werɛ renhow na ne koma remmɔ no paa, sɛ waka mogya agu kwa anaasɛ me wura ankasa atɔ were. Na AWURADE bɛyɛ me wura yiye, na woakae w’afenaa.

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abigail sɛ: Nhyira nka AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn a ɔsomaa wo behyiaa me nnɛ yi.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Na nhyira nka w’adwempa, na nhyira nka wo sɛ woasianka me nnɛ da yi na mankodi mogya ho so, na mamfa m’ankasa nsa mantɔ were.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Na ampa ara, sɛ AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn a wasianka me na manyɛ wo bɔne no te ase yi, sɛ woanyɛ ntɛm ammehyia me a, anka ebedu ɔkyena anɔpa, obiara a ɔyɛ onini renka mma Nabal.

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid gyee nea ɔde brɛɛ no no ne nsam, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Foro kɔ wo fi asomdwoe mu, hwɛ, matie wo, na mahwɛ w’anim.

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Na Abigail kɔɔ Nabal nkyɛn, na hwɛ, watow ne ho pon ne fi hɔ sɛ ɔhene pon; na Nabal ani agye ne ho, na wabow tintaan. Na wanka no hwee kosii n’adekyee.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa a nsa tetew Nabal ani so no, ne yere kaa nsɛm yi nyinaa kyerɛɛ no, na ne koma gyenee ne yam, na ɔdan sɛ ɔbo.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na ɛbɛyɛ dadu no, AWURADE bɔɔ Nabal, na owui.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔre bɔɔ ne ti ase kotowee, kae sɛ: Hwɛ, w’afenaa yɛ abaawa a ɔbɛhohoro me wura nkoa nan ho.

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Na Abigail yɛɛ ntɛm sɔre tenaa afurum so, ne mmaawa baanum a wɔnenam ne nan ase, na odii Dawid abɔfo no akyi kɔyɛɛ ne yere.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Na Dawid waree Ahinoam a ofi Yesreel nso, na wɔn baanu no yɛɛ ne yerenom.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Na Saul de ne ba Mikal, Dawid yere no, ama Lais ba Palti a ofi Galim.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Na Sififo baa Saul nkyɛn Gibea bɛkae sɛ: So ɛnyɛ Dawid na ohintaw Hakila koko a ɛkyerɛ benkum sare pataa no anim no so no?

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Na Saul bɔɔ nsra Hakila koko a ɛkyerɛ sare pataa no anim no so, ɔkwan ho, na Dawid de, ɔtenaa sare no so, na ohui sɛ Saul retiw no aba sare no so.

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: Na Dawid somaa akwansrafo, na ohui sɛ Saul aba ampa.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid sɔre kɔɔ nea Saul abɔ nsra hɔ. Na Dawid huu faako a Saul ne ne sahene Ner ba Abner dedae; nso Saul da nteaseɛnam aboae hɔ, na dɔm no abɔ nsra atwa ne ho ahyia.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Hetini Ahimelek ne Suruia ba Abisai, Yoab ne nua sɛ: Hena na ɔne me besian akɔ Saul nkyɛn wɔ nsram hɔ? Na Abisai se: Me ne wo besian akɔ.

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne Abisai kɔɔ dɔm no nkyɛn anadwo, na hwɛ Saul da hɔ ada, nteaseɛnam aboae hɔ, na ne peaw si fam wɔ n’atifi. Na Abner ne dɔm no deda ne ho hyia.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Na Abisai ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Onyankopɔn de wo tamfo ahyɛ wo nsa nnɛ, na afei ma memfa peaw no menwɔ no minkita fam prɛko, na meremfea no so.

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abisai sɛ: Nkum no, na hena na ɔteɛ ne nsa ka nea AWURADE asra no na odi bem?

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, gye AWURADE na ɔbɛka no: Sɛ ne da bedu na wawu, anaasɛ ɔbɛkɔ ɔsa na apra no akɔ.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: AWURADE mma ɛmpare me sɛ mɛteɛ me nsa maka nea AWURADE asra no no. Na afei fa peaw a ɛwɔ n’atifi no ne nsu kuruwa no na yɛnkɔ.

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid faa peaw ne nsu kuruwa no fii Saul atifi, na wɔkɔe: Na obiara anhu, obiara ante, na obiara annyan, na wɔn nyinaa adeda, efisɛ AWURADE nnahɔɔ atotɔ wɔn so.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Na Dawid sen kɔɔ ɔfa noho, na okogyinaa bepɔw no atifi wɔ akyirikyiri a ɔkwan pa ara da wɔn ntam.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bɔn dɔm no ne Ner ba Abner sɛ: Abner ee! Worennye so? Ɛnna Abner gyee so sɛ: Ɛyɛ wo hena na wobɔn ɔhene no?

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abner sɛ: So wonyɛ ɔbarima? Na hena na ɔte sɛ wo Israel mu? Na ɛdɛn nti na woanwɛn wo wura ɔhene? Na dɔm no mu bi bae sɛ anka ɔrebekum wo wura ɔhene.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Asɛm a woadi yi nye. Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, mosɛ owu, sɛ moanwɛn mo wura a AWURADE asra no no. Na afei, hwɛ nea ɔhene peaw ne nsu kuruwa a esisi n’atifi no wɔ.

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul huu sɛ ɛyɛ Dawid nne, na ɔkae sɛ: Wo nne ni, me ba Dawid? Na Dawid se: Ɛyɛ me nne, me wura ɔhene.

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na me wura di n’akoa akyi sɛɛ? Mayɛ dɛn? Anaasɛ bɔne bɛn na ɛwɔ me nsam?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Enti afei ma me wura ɔhene ntie n’akoa asɛm. Sɛ AWURADE na wahwanyan wo ahyɛ me a, ɛnne ma onnye aduan afɔre. Na sɛ ɛyɛ nnipa nso a, wɔadome wɔn, AWURADE anim, sɛ wɔapam me nnɛ sɛ minnnya AWURADE agyapade no bi, na wose: Kɔ na kɔsom anyame foforo.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Enti afei wɔmmma me mogya nngu fam wɔ faako a ɛnyɛ AWURADE anim, efisɛ Israel hene afi adi rehwehwɛ ɔkraman dwiw, sɛnea wotiw akokɔhwerew wɔ mmepɔw so.

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul kae sɛ: Mayɛ bɔne, san bra, me ba Dawid, na merenyɛ wo bɔne bio, efisɛ me kra bo ayɛ den w’ani so nnɛ da yi. Hwɛ, madi nkwaseasɛm na mafom so bebree pa ara.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Na Dawid buae sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔhene peaw ni, na ma mmerante no mu biako mmra mmɛfa.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɛdan onipa biara trenee ne ne nokwaredi ama no, sɛ nnɛ AWURADE de wo hyɛɛ me nsa, na mampɛ sɛ meteɛ me nsa meka nea AWURADE asra no no.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, sɛnea wo kra asom bo nnɛ m’ani so yi, saa ara na me kra nso nsom bo AWURADE ani so, na onyi me mfi ahohia nyinaa mu.

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Nhyira nka wo, me ba Dawid. Ampa ara, wobɛyɛ ahoɔdenne, na otumi nso, wubetumi. Ɛnna Dawid sii ne kwan so. Na Saul san kɔɔ ne tenabea.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae ne koma mu sɛ: Anhwɛ a, da bi Saul nsa na ebekum me; biribiara nye mma me sɛ meguan makɔ Filistifo asase so, na Saul agyaa me na wanhwehwɛ me bio Israel asase nyinaa so, na mafi ne nsa.

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Dawid aguan kɔ Gat; na wankɔ so anhwehwɛ no bio.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Akis sɛ: Sɛ manya w’anim anuonyam a, ma wɔmma me tenabea bi wuram nkurow no bi mu, na menkɔtena hɔ: Na ɛdɛn nti na w’akoa ne wo ntena ahenkurow mu?

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Akis de Siklag maa no da no ara; enti Siklag dan Yuda ahene de de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Na nna a Dawid de tenaa Filistifo asase so no yɛ afirihyia ne asram anan.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne ne mmarima no kɔe kotuaa Gesurfo ne Gersifo ne Amalekfo; na wɔn na wɔtete asase no so fi teteete, de kodu Sur a ɛde kɔ Misraim asase so.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Na Dawid bɔɔ asase no, na wannyaw ɔbarima anaa ɔbea anikan, na ɔfaa nguan ne anantwi ne mfurum ne yoma ne ntade, na ɔsan baa Akis nkyɛn.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Na Dawid annyaw ɔbarima anaa ɔbea bi anikan sɛ ɔde wɔn bɛba Gat, efisɛ ose: Anyɛ a, wɔbɛka yɛn ho asɛm sɛ: Sɛɛ na Dawid ayɛ. Na nna a ɔde tenaa Filistifo asase so no nyinaa, sɛ ɔyɛe ara nen.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Na Akis gyee Dawid dii, kae sɛ: Wama ne ho abɔn ne man Israel pa ara, enti ɔbɛyɛ m’akoa daa.

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no boaboaa wɔn ho ano bae bɛbɔɔ nsra Sunem. Na Saul boaboaa Israelfo nyinaa ano, na wɔbɔɔ nsra Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Na Saul huu Filistifo nsra no no, osuroe, na ne koma tui papaapa.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: Na Saul kobisaa AWURADE, nanso ɔdae mu oo, Urim ntonto so oo, adiyifo anom oo, AWURADE ammua no.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Saul ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Monkɔhwehwɛ ɔbea samanfrɛfo bi mma me, na menkɔ ne hɔ abisa. Na ne nkoa no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔbea samanfrɛfo bi wɔ Endor.

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Na Saul sakraa ne ho hyɛɛ atade foforo, na osiim kɔe, ɔno ne nnipa baanu a wɔka ne ho, na woduu ɔbea no nkyɛn anadwo; na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa ɔsamanfrɛ so hyɛ me nkɔm, na ma nea mɛbɔ ne din makyerɛ wo no mforo mmra mma me.

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, wo ara wunim nea Saul ayɛ, sɛnea watwitwa asamanfrɛfo ne asumanfo afi asase yi so, na ɛdɛn nti na woresum me kra afiri ama wɔakum me yi?

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Na Saul kaa no AWURADE ntam sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, worenni asɛm yi mu so bi.

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea no kae sɛ: Hena na memma ɔmforo mmra mma wo? Na ose: Ma Samuel mforo mmra mma me.

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no huu Samuel no, ɔde nne kɛse teɛɛm, na ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woadaadaa me yi? Na wone Saul.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro! Na ɛdɛn na wuhu? Na ɔbea no se: Onyame bi na mihu sɛ ofi asase mu reforo aba.

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ne su te dɛn? Na ose: Akwakoraa bi a ɔhyɛ atade yuu na ɔreforo ba. Na Saul hui sɛ ɛyɛ Samuel, na ɔbɔɔ ne mu ase kotow sɔree no.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Na Samuel ka kyerɛɛ Saul sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wohaw me ma meforo mebae yi? Na Saul buae sɛ: Me ho hia me papaapa, na Filistifo ne me reko, na Onyankopɔn apa m’akyi, na ommua me bio, ɔmfa adiyifo so, na ɔmfa adae mu nso, enti na mafrɛ wo yi, sɛ kyerɛ me nea menyɛ.

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Na Samuel kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wunim sɛ AWURADE apa w’akyi na wadan wo tamfo na wubisa me ade yi?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ayɛ sɛnea ɔnam me so kae no, na AWURADE ahuam wo nsam ahenni no de akɔma wo yɔnko Dawid.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Esiane sɛ woantie AWURADE nne na woanyɛ n’abufuhyew so ade Amalekfo so nti, na AWURADE ayɛ wo ɛso ade nnɛ yi.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE de Israel nso ne wo bɛhyɛ Filistifo nsa: Na ɔkyena wo ne wo mma bɛba abɛka me ho, na AWURADE de Israel dɔm nso bɛhyɛ Filistifo nsa.

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ntɛm ara Saul hwee ase tɔtɔtee birim, na Samuel nsɛm no nti osuroe papaapa, nso ahoɔden biara nni ne mu, efisɛ na onnidii da mu no nyinaa ne anadwo mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no baa Saul nkyɛn, na ohuu sɛ wayɛ yoo, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, w’afenaa atie wo, na mede me kra mato me nsam, na matie wo nsɛm a woka kyerɛɛ me no,

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: na wo nso tie w’afenaa, na ma memfa abodoo buprɛko mimmesi w’anim, na di, na woanya ahoɔden de asi wo kwan so akɔ.

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Na wampene, kae sɛ: Merenni. Na ne nkoa ne ɔbea no nso hyɛɛ no, na otiee wɔn, na ɔsɔre fii fam tenaa mpa so.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Nso ɔbea no wɔ nantwi ba a wadɔ ofie hɔ, na ɔyɛɛ ntɛm kum no, na ɔfaa asikresam fɔtɔwee, na ɔde too apiti;

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: na ɔde besii Saul ne ne nkoa no anim na wodii; na wɔsɔre siim kɔe anadwo no.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo asafohene no bo fuw no, na Filistifo asafohene no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma ɔbarima yi nsan, na ɔnsan nkɔ ne tenabea a wode no tenae hɔ, na mma ɔne yɛn nnkɔ ɔsa no, na wannan n’ani ankyerɛ yɛn ɔko no mu; na ɛdɛn na oyi de bɛpata ne wura? So ɛnyɛ nnipa yi ti?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: So ɛnyɛ Dawid a wogyee ne ho dwom so asaw mu sɛ: “Saul akum n’apem, apem na Dawid akum ne ɔpedu ɔpedu, no ni anaa?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Akis frɛɛ Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, woteɛ, na me de, anka eye ma me sɛ wo ne me bedi akɔneaba ɔsa yi mu; efisɛ efi da a wobaa me nkyɛn de besi nnɛ, minhuu wo ho bɔne bi ɛ; na asafohene no na ɛmpɛ wo.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Enti san, na kɔ asomdwoe mu, na wo ho anyɛ Filistifo asafohene no ahi.

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Akis sɛ: Na dɛn na mayɛ, na dɛn na woahu w’akoa ho fi da a mebaa w’anim de abesi nnɛ yi a enti mennkɔ na me ne me wura ɔhene atamfo nnkɔko yi?

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Na Akis bua see Dawid sɛ: Minim sɛ wuye m’ani so sɛ Onyankopɔn bɔfo; nso Filistifo asafohene no se: Ɔne yɛn renkɔ ɔsa no.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Enti monsɔre anɔpahema, wo ne wo wura nkoa a wɔne wo bae no; na mosɔre ahema no na anim tetew ara pɛ a, moasim akɔ.

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ne ne mmarima no tuaa ahema siim sɛ wɔresan akɔ Filistifo asase so. Na Filistifo no baa Yesreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne ne mmarima no duu Siklag da a ɛto so abiɛsa no, na Amalekfo abetua atifi fam ne Siklag, na wɔabɔ Siklag, na wɔde gya ahyew.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne ne mmarima no duu kurow no mu no, na hwɛ, wɔde gya ahyew, na wɔn yerenom ne wɔn mmammarima ne wɔn mmabea no, wɔafa wɔn nnommum kɔ.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ne dɔm a wɔka ne ho no momaa wɔn nne so sui ara kosii sɛ wonnya ahoɔden nsu bio.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Na Dawid yerenom baanu no, Yesreelni Ahinoam ne Karmelni Abigail, Nabal yere no, nso, wɔafa wɔn nnommum bi.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Na Dawid ho kyeree no papaapa, efisɛ ɛdɔm no kae sɛ wobesiw no abo, na dɔm no nyinaa kra botowee, wɔn mmammarima ne wɔn mmabea nti; nanso Dawid hyɛɛ ne ho den AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn mu.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Ahimelek ba Abiatar sɛ: Fa asɔfotade no brɛ me. Na Abiatar de asɔfotade no brɛɛ Dawid.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa AWURADE sɛ: Mintiw dɔm yi anaa? So mɛto wɔn? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Tiw wɔn, na wobɛto wɔn, na ogye nso wubegye.

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Na wohuu Misraimni bi wuram hɔ, na wɔde no brɛɛ Dawid; na wɔmaa no abodoo dii, na wɔmaa no nsu nomee,

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: na wɔmaa no borɔdɔma tɔw sin ne bobe aba atɔw abien; na odii no, n’ani so baee no, efisɛ nnansa, awia ne anadwo, na onnidii na ɔnnomee.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hena ba ne wo, na ɛhe na wufi? Na ose: Meyɛ Misraimni ba, Amalekni bi akoa, na me wura gyaw me, efisɛ ɔyare bɔɔ me nnɛ nnansa.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Yekotuaa Keretifo nifa ne nea ɛyɛ Yuda dea no ne Kaleb nifa, na yɛde gya hyew Siklag.

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wode me besian akɔ dɔm no nkyɛn? Na ose: Ka me Onyankopɔn sɛ worenkum me, nso woremfa me nhyɛ me wura nsa, na mede wo mesian makɔ dɔm no nkyɛn.

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Na ɔde no sian kɔe; na hwɛ, asade bebree a wɔakɔfa Filistifo asase so ne Yuda asase so no nti, wɔboaboa fam hɔ nyinaa redidi na wɔrenom na wɔresaw.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kunkum wɔn fi ahemadakye kosii da a edi so no anwummere; na wɔn mu biara amfi mu gye mmerante ahanan a wɔtenatenaa yoma so guanee.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Na Dawid gyee nea Amalekfo fae no nyinaa; ne yerenom baanu no nso, Dawid gyee wɔn;

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: na anka wɔn biribiara, ketewa oo, kɛse oo, mmammarima oo, mmabea oo, asade a wɔbɛfae no mu biara oo, Dawid de ne nyinaa san bae.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Na Dawid faa nguan ne anantwi no nyinaa, na wɔde mmoa no dii n’anim bae, na wɔkae sɛ: Eyi de, Dawid asade ni.

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna mmarima a wɔne Dawid kɔe no mu nnipa bɔne ne ahuhufo bi buae sɛ: Sɛ wɔne yɛn ankɔ nti, wɔremma wɔn asade a yɛakogye no bi, gye wɔn yerenom ne wɔn mma na wɔmfa wɔn nkɔ.

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: Anuanom, monnyɛ sa, nea AWURADE de ama yɛn, na wahwɛ yɛn so, na ɔde dɔm a wɔbaa yɛn so no ahyɛ yɛn nsa.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Na hena na obetie mo, asɛm yi mu? Na sɛnea ɔkɔ akono kyɛfa te no, saa ara na nea ɔtena nneɛma ho no nso kyɛfa te: Wɔnkyɛ mu pɛ.

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Na efi da no ara de rekɔ no, ɔde too hɔ yɛɛ ahyɛde ne atemmude maa Israel de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid duu Siklag no, ɔsomae ma wɔde asade no bi kɔmaa Yuda mpanyin a wɔyɛ ne nnamfo kae sɛ: Hwɛ, AWURADE atamfo asade mu akyɛde a wɔde rebrɛ mo ni.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo ne Israel koe; na Israel mmarima guanee Filistifo anim, na wɔtotɔe Gilboa bepɔw so.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo tu taree Saul ne ne mma, na Filistifo no kum Saul mma Yonatan ne Abinadab ne Malkisua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Na ɔko no den Saul, na bɛmmatofo, mmarima a wokura ta huu no, na wɔtow no, piraa no.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Na Saul ka kyerɛɛ n’akodekurafo sɛ: Twe wo nkrante fa wɔ me, na momonotofo yi amma ammɛwɔ me ammɛyɛ me ade angoru me atɔprɛ. Na n’akodekurafo no ampene, efisɛ osuro pii. Ɛnna Saul faa nkrante na ɔhwee so.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Na n’akodekurafo no hui sɛ Saul awu no, ɔno nso hwee ne nkrante so saa ara, na ɔne no wui.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Saa na Saul ne ne mma baasa ne n’akodekurafo ne ne mmarima nyinaa nso wuwui prɛko da no ara.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima a wɔwɔ obon no agya ne wɔn a wɔwɔ Yordan agya hui sɛ Israel mmarima aguan na Saul ne ne mma atotɔ no, wogyigyaw nkurow no guanguanee, na Filistifo na bae bɛtenaa mu.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee a Filistifo bae beyiyii atɔfo ho ade no, wohuu Saul ne ne mma baasa no sɛ wɔatotɔ Gilboa bepɔw so.

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: akofo nyinaa sɔree, nam anadwo mu no nyinaa kɔfaa Saul funu ne ne mma afunu no fii Bet-san fasu no ho de baa Yabes, na wɔhyewee wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa wɔn nnompe kɔkorae ɔsantɛw dua no ase wɔ Yabes, na wodii mmuada nnanson.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Na Saul wu akyi a Dawid asan afi Amalek kum aba no, Dawid dii Siklag nnanu.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so abiɛsa no, hwɛ, ɔbarima bi fi Saul nsra no mu bae, na n’atade asunsuan, na dɔte gu n’atifi; na oduu Dawid nkyɛn no, ɔhwee fam kotow no.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa no sɛ: Ɛhe na wufi reba yi? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Israel nsram na mifi miguanee yi.

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa no sɛ: Asɛm no kɔɔ dɛn? Ka kyerɛ me ɛ! Na ose: Ɔman no aguan afi ɔko no ano, na ɔman no mufo pii atotɔ na wɔawuwu, na Saul ne ne ba Yonatan nso awuwu.

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa aberante a ɔka kyerɛɛ no no sɛ: Woyɛɛ dɛn hui sɛ Saul ne ne ba Yonatan awuwu?

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Na aberante a ɔka kyerɛɛ no no kae sɛ: Mikofii Gilboa Bepɔw so, na hwɛ, Saul tweri ne peaw ho, na hwɛ, nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔsotefo retaa no.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Na ɔhwɛɛ n’akyi no, ohuu me, na ɔfrɛɛ me. Na migyee no so sɛ: Mini.
