english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Na obisaa me sɛ: Woyɛ hena? Na mibuaa no sɛ: Meyɛ Amalekni.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Begyina me so kum me, na nketenkete akita me, nanso me kra nyinaa da so wɔ me mu.

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Ɛnna migyinaa no so mikum no, na minim sɛ n’asehwe akyi no, ɔrennya nkwa. Na mefaa abotiri a ɛbɔ ne ti ne kapo a ɛhyɛ ne nsa no, na mede mabrɛ me wura ha.

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid soo n’atade mu suan mu, na mmarima a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa nso yeyɛɛ saa.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Na wotwaa adwo na wosui, na wɔkyen kɔm ara koduu anadwofa maa Saul ne ne ba Yonatan ne AWURADE man ne Israel fi, sɛ wɔatotɔ nkrante ano.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa aberante a ɔka kyerɛɛ no no sɛ: Wufi he? Na ose: Ɔhɔho Amalekni bi ba ne me.

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wo mogya ngu w’atifi na w’ano na adi wo adanse sɛ: Me na makum nea AWURADE asra no no. Dawid twa kwadwom ma Saul ne Yonatan

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Na Dawid twaa Saul ne ne ba Yonatan ho kwadwom yi;

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: Israel, w’anuonyam no wo sorɔnsorɔmmea so na wɔahwirow wɔn mu. Ahoɔdenfo atotɔ dɛn ara!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Monnka wɔ Gat, mommmɔ no kaseɛ wɔ Askelon mmɔnten so, na Filistifo mmabea ani annye, na momonotofo mmabea anni ahurusi.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Mo Gilboa mmepɔw, wɔmmma obosu ne osu nngu mo so, na nnɔbae mfuw mmma mo so, na ɛhɔ na wɔtow ɔhoɔdenfo kyɛm kyenee, nsaase a wɔbɔ so afɔre, Saul kyɛm, sɛ nea wɔnsraa no ngo de.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Atɔfo mogya, ahoɔdenfo srade, Yonatan bɛmma ansan amfi ho da, na Saul nkrante nso ansan amfi ho kwa.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Saul ne Yonatan te ase, na wɔyɛ ahoɔfɛfo a wɔn ho yɛ anika, na wɔn wu mu nso wɔanni mpaepaemu. Wɔn ho yɛ hare sen akɔre, wɔn ho yɛ den sen agyata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Israel mmabea, Saul na munsu no, ɔno na ofuraa mo atankɔkɔɔ ma ɛyɛɛ fɛ, na ɔde sika ahyehyɛde guguu mo ntade so.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Ahoɔdenfo atotɔ ɔko mu dɛn ara! Wɔahwirow Yonatan mu wo sorɔnsorɔmmea so.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: Wo nti me ho hia me, me nua Yonatan, w’asɛm yɛɛ me dɛ sɛ, wo dɔ yɛɛ me nwonwa sen mmea dɔ.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Ahoɔdenfo atotɔ dɛn ara, na akode asɛe yi.

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Na eyi akyi no Dawid bisaa AWURADE sɛ: So memforo menkɔ Yuda nkurow bi mu anaa? Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Foro kɔ! Na Dawid kae sɛ: Ɛhe na memforo menkɔ? Na ose: Hebron.

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid kɔɔ hɔ, ɔne ne yerenom baanu no nso, Yesreelni Ahinoam ne Abigail, Karmelni Nabal yere no.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Na Dawid de mmarima a wɔne no nam no nso ne wɔn fifo bae, na wɔbɛtenatenaa Hebron nkurow mu.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yuda mmarima bae bɛsraa Dawid sii Yuda fi so hene wɔ hɔ. Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Yabes-gileadfo na wosiee Saul.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Na Dawid somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Yabes-gileadfo no nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: AWURADE nhyira nka mo sɛ moayɛ mo wura Saul adɔe sɛɛ, na moasie no.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Na afei AWURADE ne mo nni no adɔe ne nokware so, na sɛ moayɛ saa ade yi nti, me nso mɛyɛ mo saa yiye yi bi.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Na afei monhyɛ mo abasam den, na monyɛ mo ho mmarima na mo wura Saul awu, nanso Yuda fi asra me asi wɔn so hene. Is-boset di Israel so hene

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Na Saul safohene Ner ba Abner faa Saul ba Is-boset de no kɔɔ Mahanaim,

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: na ɔde no yɛɛ Gilead ne Asurifo ne Yesreel ne Efraim ne Benyamin ne Israel nyinaa so hene.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Na nna a Dawid dii Yuda fi so hene Hebron no ano si mfirihyia ason ne asram asia. Israel ne Yuda ntam ɔko

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Na Ner ba Abner ne Saul ba Is-boset nkoa tu fii Mahanaim baa Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Na Seruia ba Yoab ne Dawid nkoa tu kɔe na wohyiae boaboaa wɔn ho ano Gibeon tare ho, eyinom boa ɔtare no fa ha, na eyinom boa ɔtare no fa ha.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Na Abner ka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Ma mmerante no nsɔre ngoru yɛn anim ɛ! Na Yoab kae sɛ: Wɔnsɔre ɛ!

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wobubuu wɔn ho ano sɔre kɔe. Benyamin ne Saul ba Is-boset de dumien, ne Dawid nkoa mu dumien.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Na wɔn nyinaa susoo wɔn mfɛfo ti de wɔn nkrante wowɔɔ wɔn mfɛfo mfem na wɔtotɔe prɛko. Enti wɔfrɛɛ hɔ sɛ Helkat-hasurim a ase ne: Ano nnamnam afuw a ɛwɔ Gibeon.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔko no mu yɛɛ den sɛ biribi da no, na Abner ne Israel mmarima no dii nkogu Dawid nkoa no anim. Abner kum Asahel

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Na Seruia mma baasa no wɔ hɔ. Yoab ne Abisai ne Asahel. Na Asahel nan ase yɛ hare sɛ wuram atwe no bi.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Abner hwɛɛ n’akyi, na ɔkae sɛ: So wo Asahel ni? Na ose: Mene no.

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Na Abner ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Man wo nifa anaa wo benkum kɔkyere mmerante no mu bi na gye n’asade fa! Na Asahel ampɛ sɛ ɔsan fi n’akyi.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Na Abner kɔɔ so ka kyerɛɛ Asahel bio sɛ: San fi m’akyi kɔ! Ɛdɛn nti na memmɔ wo menhwe fam? Na metumi mama m’ani so makyerɛ wo nua Yoab dɛn?

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Nanso wampɛ sɛ ɔsan. Ɛnna Abner de ne peaw to wɔɔ ne yafunum, na peaw no hwirew n’akyi, na ɔhwee hɔ wui hɔ ara. Na ɛbae sɛ obiara du nea Asahel hwe wui hɔ a, ogyina komm.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne Abisai tiw Abner. Na owia kɔtɔe no na, wɔadu Amma koko a ɛda Gia anim Gibeon sare so kwan ho no so.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Na Benyaminfo boaboaa wɔn ho ano gyinaa Abner akyi yɛɛ kuw biako, na wokogyinaa koko bi atifi.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Na Abner frɛɛ Yoab sɛ: So nkrante nsɛe ade nkosi daa? So wunnim sɛ akyiri bɛyɛ awerɛhow? Na enkodu da bɛn ansa na woaka akyerɛ ɔman no sɛ wɔnsan mfi wɔn nuanom akyi?

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Na Yoab se: Sɛ Onyankopɔn te ase yi, sɛ woankasa a, anka efi anɔpa no, mmarima agyae wɔn nuanom akyidi kɔ dedaw.

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab hyɛn torobɛnto, na ɔman no nyinaa gyinae, na wɔantaa Israel bio, nanso wɔankɔ so anko bio.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Abner ne ne nnipa no faa Araba; tataw so nam anadwo no nyinaa twaa Yordan, nam awia mu no nyinaa koduu Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Na Yoab san fii Abner akyi na ɔboaboaa ɔman no nyinaa ano, na aka Dawid nkoa no mu dunkron ne Asahel.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Na wɔsoaa Asahel kosiee no n’agya da a ɛwɔ Betlehem no mu. Na Yoab ne ne mmarima no nam anadwo no nyinaa, na ade kyee wɔn Hebron.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Na bere a akodi da Saul fi ne Dawid fi ntam no, Abner kɔɔ so yɛɛ den Saul fi mu ara.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Nso Saul wɔ ɔyefam bi a ne din de Rispa a ɔyɛ Aya babea. Na Is-boset ka kyerɛɛ Abner sɛ. Ɛdɛn nti na wokɔ m’agya yefam ho?

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Na Is-boset asɛm no yɛɛ Abner abufuw sɛ, na ɔkae sɛ: So ɔkraman ne me a, me ne Yuda asidi mu meyɛ w’agya Saul fi, ne nuanom ne ne nnamfonom adɔe nnɛ, na minyii wo menhyɛɛ Dawid nsa na worehwehwɛ me ho amumɔyɛ ɔbea yi ho?

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Saa na Onyankopɔn nyɛ Abner na saa na ɔnkɔ so nyɛ no, sɛnea AWURADE kaa Dawid ntam no, saa na mɛyɛ mama no,

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Na sɛ osuro no nti, wantumi ammua Abner asɛm bi bio.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Na Abner somaa abɔfo sii n’ananmu kɔɔ Dawid nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ. Hena na asase yi wɔ no? Ɔkae nso sɛ. Wo ne me mpam; na hwɛ, me nsa bɛka wo ho de adan Israel nyinaa aba wo nkyɛn.

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ. Wiɛ, me ne wo bɛpam. Na ade biako pɛ na merebisa wo hɔ sɛ: Nhu m’anim gye sɛ wode Saul babea Mikal ba ansa na woaba abɛhwɛ m’anim.

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Na Dawid somaa abɔfo kɔɔ Saul ba Is-boset nkyɛn kɔkae sɛ: Fa me yere Mikal a mede Filistifo mmarima ano ɔha migyee no aware no brɛ me.

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Na Is-boset soma ma wɔkɔfaa no fi ne kunu Lais ba Paltiel nkyɛn.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Na ne kunu no ne no kɔe, na ɔde osu dii n’akyi ara koduu Bahurim. Ɛnna Abner ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: San kɔ! Na ɔsanee.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Na Abner ne Israel mpanyin kasae sɛ: Mmere a atwam no, na mohwehwɛ Dawid sɛ ommedi mo so hene.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Na afei monyɛ ɛ! Efisɛ AWURADE aka akyerɛ Dawid sɛ: M’akoa Dawid nsa na mede megye me man Israel, Filistifo ne wɔn atamfo nyinaa nsam.

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Na Abner kasa guu Benyamin asom nso, na Abner kɔe nso kɔkaa nea eye, Israel ne Benyamin fi nyinaa ani so, guu Dawid asom Hebron.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Na Abner baa Dawid nkyɛn Hebron a nnipa aduonu ka ne ho. Na Dawid tow Abner ne mmarima a wɔka ne ho no pon.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Na Abner ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Mɛsɔre makɔ makɔboaboa Israel nyinaa ano mabrɛ me wura, na wɔne wo apam na woadi wɔn a wɔpɛ nyinaa so hene. Na Dawid gyaa Abner kwan na ɔkɔe asomdwoe mu. Wokum Abner

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Dawid nkoa ne Yoab fii akofo asafo mu bae, na wɔde asade pii nso bae. Na Abner nni Dawid nkyɛn Hebron, efisɛ wagya no kwan ma ɔkɔ dwoodwoo.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne dɔm a wɔka ne ho nyinaa bae no, wɔka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Ner ba Abner aba ɔhene nkyɛn na wagya no kwan na ɔkɔ asomdwoe mu.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Na Yoab baa ɔhene nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Dɛn na woayɛ yi? Hwɛ, Abner aba wo nkyɛn, ɛdɛn nti na woagya no kwan na ɔkɔ yi?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Wunim Ner ba Abner sɛ ɔbae sɛ ɔbɛdaadaa wo na wahu wo kɔree ne bae na wahu nea woreyɛ nyinaa.

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Na Yoab fii adi fii Dawid nkyɛn na ɔsomaa abɔfo kotiw Abner na wɔde no fii Sira abura ho san bae. Na Dawid de na onnim.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Na Abner san baa Hebron no, Yoab de no man kɔɔ kurow pon no mu, sɛ ɔne no kɔkasa brɛoo, ɛhɔ na ne nua Asahel mogya nti ɔkɔwɔɔ ne yafunum ma owui.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi Dawid tee na ɔkae sɛ: Me ne m’ahenni di Ner ba Abner mogya ho bem AWURADE anim daa.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Wɔmma emmua Yoab atifi ne n’agya fi nyinaa so nanso wɔmmma nea ne ho sen nsu bi, ne ɔkwatani ne nea otweri poma so, ne nea ɔtɔ nkrante ano ne nea aduan bɔ no, mmpa Yoab fi da.

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne ne nua Abisai dii Abner awu, efisɛ okum wɔn nua Asahel Gibeon ko no mu. Wosie Abner

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Yoab ne ɔman a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa sɛ: Munsunsuane mo ntade mu na mumfurafura atweatam na muntwa adwo mma Abner. Na ɔhene Dawid dii funnaka no akyi.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Na wɔkoraa Abner wɔ Hebron. Na ɔhene maa ne nne so sui Abner da so na ɔman no nyinaa sui.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Na ɔhene twaa Abner ho kwadwom yi sɛ: So ɛsɛ sɛ Abner wu ogyennyentwi wu?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Wɔankyere wo nsa da, na wɔanto wo nan mpokyerɛ da. Sɛ wɔtɔ amumɔyɛ mma anim na woatɔ yi. Na ɔman no nyinaa kɔɔ so suu no bio.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Na ade nsae no, ɔman no nyinaa bae sɛ wɔbɛma Dawid adidi nanso Dawid kaa ntam sɛ: Saa na Onyankopɔn nyɛ me na ɔnkɔ so nyɛ, sɛ mede aduan anaa biribiara meka m’ano ansa na owia kɔtɔ a!

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa hui, na ɛsɔɔ wɔn ani, sɛ ade a ɔhene yɛ nyinaa sɔ ɔman no nyinaa ani no.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa ne Israel nyinaa hui da no, sɛ ɛnyɛ ɔhene na ɔma wokum Ner ba Abner.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: So munnim sɛ ɔsafohene ne onipa kɛse atɔ nnɛ da yi Israel?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Na me de, ɛnnɛ meyɛ mmerɛw na wɔasra me asi me hene; na mmarima yi, Seruia mma yi, yɛ den ma me. AWURADE ntua nea ɔyɛ bɔne no ka sɛnea ne bɔne te.

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Na Saul ba Is-boset tee sɛ Abner awu Hebron no, ne nsam gowee na Israel nyinaa yɛɛ yoo.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na Saul ba no wɔ mmarima baanu a wodi no asafohene, obiako din de Baana na nea ɔka ho no din de Rekab; wɔyɛ Beerotni Rimon mma a wofi Benyamin mma mu. Na wobu Beerot nso fra Benyamin.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Na Beerotfo no guan kɔɔ Gitaim kɔyɛɛ hɔ ahɔho, na wɔwɔ hɔ de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Na Saul ba Yonatan wɔ ɔbabarima bi a ne nan abien asinsen. Saul ne Yonatan ho asɛm no fi Yesreel bae no na wadi mfe anum na ne gyigyefo maa no so guanee. Na ɔreyɛ ntɛm aguan no, ɔhwee ase na ɔtɔɔ apakye. Na ne din de Mefiboset.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Na Beerotni Rimon mma Rekab ne Baana siim baa Is-boset fi awia ketee, nso na wada awianna.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Na woduu ɔdan no mu na ɔno nso da mpa so ne dabekyiri no wɔwɔɔ no kum no na wotwaa ne ti na wɔde ne ti no nam tataw so kwan anadwo no nyinaa kɔe.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Na wɔde Is-boset ti no brɛɛ Dawid wɔ Hebron na wɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Hwɛ wo tamfo Saul ba Is-boset a anka ɔhwehwɛ wo akum wo no ti ni, na ɛnnɛ da yi AWURADE atɔ Saul ne n’asefo so were ama me wura ɔhene.

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Na Dawid buaa Beerotni Rimon mma Rekab ne ne nua Baana ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE a ogyee me kra ahohia nyinaa mu te ase yi,

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: nea ɔbɛka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Hwɛ, Saul awu na ɛyɛɛ n’ani so sɛ asɛmpa na ɔde brɛɛ me no, mekyeree no mikum no Siklag, mede mituaa no n’asɛm no so ka,

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: na menne sɛ nnipa bɔne adi onipa trenee awu ne fi, ne nnae so. Na afei, so meremmisa ne mogya mo nsam na merenyi mo mimfi asase so anaa?

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Na Dawid hyɛɛ ne mmerante no ma wokum wɔn na wotwitwaa wɔn nsa ne wɔn anan de sensɛn ɔtare a ɛwɔ Hebron no ho. Na Is-boset ti no de wɔfae na wosiee no Abner da mu Hebron.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Na Tiro hene Hiram somaa abɔfo ma wɔde nkyeneduru nnua ne nnuasenfo ne abantofo baa Dawid nkyɛn na wɔkyekyeree ofi maa Dawid.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Odii Yuda so hene Hebron mfe ason ne asram asia, na odii Israel ne Yuda nyinaa so hene mfe aduasa abiɛsa Yerusalem. Dawid ko fa Yerusalem

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ne ne mmarima kɔɔ Yerusalem kotuaa Yebusifo a wɔte asase no so no. Na Yebusifo no ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Woremma ha na anifuraefo ne mpakye mpo besiw wo kwan. Na wodwen sɛ Dawid renkɔ mu hɔ.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔɔ so yɛɛ kɛse ara na AWURADE, asafo Nyankopɔn, dii n’akyi. Dawid fifo ne ne nkonimdi horow no

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Na Dawid hui sɛ AWURADE de no asi Israel so hene pintinn ne sɛ ne man Israel nti wama n’ahenni so.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Na Dawid fi Hebron bae akyi no, ɔkɔɔ so warewaree yefam ne yerenom fii Yerusalem, na wɔwowoo mmammarima ne mmabea maa Dawid bio.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: ne Yibhar ne Elisua ne Nefet ne Yafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: ne Elisama ne Eliada ne Elifelet. Filistifo so nkonimdi (

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo tee sɛ wɔasra Dawid de no asi Israel so hene no, Filistifo nyinaa foro bae sɛ wɔbɛhwehwɛ Dawid. Na Dawid tee no, osian kɔɔ aban no mu.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no bae bɛtrɛw wɔn ho mu Refaim bon mu.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa AWURADE sɛ. Menkɔ Filistifo no so anaa? So wode wɔn bɛhyɛ me nsa anaa? Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Kɔ na mede Filistifo no mɛhyɛ wo nsa ampa.

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔɔ Baal-perasim na Dawid kunkum wɔn hɔ, na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE apae m’atamfo mu m’anim sɛ wɔpae nsu mu no. Enti ɔfrɛɛ hɔ din sɛ Baal-perasim ase ne: Ntewmubea.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Na wogyigyaw wɔn ahoni hɔ; na Dawid ne ne nnipa no tasee.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Na Filistifo no san foro bae bio bɛtrɛtrɛw wɔn ho mu Refaim bon mu.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Na Dawid bisaa AWURADE no, ɔkae sɛ: Nkɔ! Dan wo ho kosi wɔn akyi na fa baka nnua no ntentenso bra wɔn so.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wote nantew nka balsam nnua no atifi a, ɛno de ka wo ho, efisɛ ɛno de na AWURADE afi redi w’anim akokum Filistifo nsra no.

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Na Dawid yɛe sɛnea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no na okunkum Filistifo no fi Geba de koduu Geser.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wɔn a wɔso AWURADE adaka no tutu anammɔn asia a, ɔde nantwi ne aboa a wadɔ bɔ afɔre.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Na Dawid de n’ahoɔden nyinaa sawee AWURADE anim; nso Dawid hyɛ nwera asɔfotade.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne Israel fi nyinaa de osebɔ ne torobɛntohyɛn de AWURADE adaka no foro bae.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE adaka no duu Dawid kurow mu no, Saul babea Mikal hwɛɛ mfɛnsere mu, na ohuu ɔhene Dawid sɛ ɔrehuruhuruw na ɔresaw AWURADE anim, na obuu no animtiaa ne koma mu.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Na wɔde Onyankopɔn adaka no sii teaseɛnam foforo so, na wɔmaa so fii Abinadab fi a ɛwɔ koko no so na Abinadab mma Usa ne Ahio na ɛkaa teaseɛnam foforo no.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Na Dawid sɔree, na ɔne ɔman a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa kɔe kofii Baaleyuda, sɛ wɔrekɔfa Onyankopɔn adaka a wɔbɔ din sɛ asafo AWURADE a ɔte Kerubim so no afi hɔ aba.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne Israel fi nyinaa de wɔn ahoɔden nyinaa, ne nnwom ne asanku ne bɛnta asanku a wɔde ɔpopaw nnua ayɛ ne mpintin ne nnɔnnɔmma ne nsammɔ nnawuru gorui, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Na woduu Nakon awiporowbea no, Usa teɛɛ ne nsa kɔkaa Onyankopɔn adaka no soo mu, efisɛ anantwi no hintiwii.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bo fuw Usa na mfomso no nti Onyankopɔn bɔɔ no wɔ hɔ na owui Onyankopɔn adaka no nkyɛn hɔ.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Na ɛyɛɛ Dawid awerɛhow sɛ AWURADE abufuw aba Usa so. Na ɔfrɛɛ hɔ din sɛ Peres-usa, ase ne: Usa so abufuw, de besi nnɛ yi.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Na Dawid suroo AWURADE da no na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE adaka no bɛba me nkyɛn dɛn?

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Enti Dawid ampɛ sɛ ɔde AWURADE adaka no ba ne nkyɛn, Dawid kurow no mu, na Dawid de man kɔɔ Gitni Obed-edom fi.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ. AWURADE ahyira Obed-edom fi ne nea ɔwɔ nyinaa, Onyankopɔn adaka no nti. Na Dawid kɔe kɔfaa Onyankopɔn adaka no fii Obed-edom fi de baa Dawid kurow mu anigye mu.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Na wɔde AWURADE adaka no bae de besii ne sibere, ntamadan a Dawid asi ama no no mu. Na Dawid bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre, AWURADE anim.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Na Dawid wiee ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre no bɔ no, ɔde asafo AWURADE din hyiraa ɔman no.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Na ɔkyɛɛ ade maa ɔman no nyinaa, Israel man mu no nyinaa, mmarima ne mmea; ɔmaa wɔn mu biara abodoo sebɔw biako ne nankum ne bobe aba tetare. Ɛnna ɔman no nyinaa siim kokɔɔ wɔn afi.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid san behyiraa ne fi. Na Saul ba Mikal fii adi behyiaa Dawid na ɔkae sɛ: Anuonyam bɛn na Israel hene anya nnɛ, sɛ wapa ne ho nnɛ ne nkoa mfenaa anim, sɛ ahuhufo no bi pa ne ho animguase so a n’ani mmu no dwɛ yi!

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Mikal sɛ: AWURADE a ɔpaw me fii w’agya ne ne fi nyinaa akyi, yii me na ɔhyɛɛ me sɛ minni ne man Israel so panyin no anim na migorui.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Na mɛyɛ ayemfo masen eyi bio na mayɛ m’ani so famni. Nanso mfenaa a woka no, wɔn ara na ɛbɛhyɛ me anuonyam.

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Na Saul babea Mikal annya ɔba de kosii ne wuda.

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Na m’adɔe remfi ne ho sɛnea efii Saul a mituu no w’anim no ho no.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Odiyifo Natan sɛ: Hwɛ, me de, mete kyeneduru dan mu, na Onyankopɔn adaka no si ntamadan mu.

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Na Natan ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Nea ɛwɔ wo koma mu nyinaa kɔyɛ, na AWURADE di w’akyi.

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Na anadwo no ara AWURADE asɛm baa Natan nkyɛn sɛ:

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: Kɔ na kɔka kyerɛ m’akoa Dawid sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni. So wo na wubesi dan ama matena mu?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Na efi da a miyii Israelfo fii Misraim bae de bedu nnɛ yi, mentenaa ofi mu da na mmom menam ntamadan tenabea mu.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Bere a me ne Israelfo nyinaa nantewee no nyinaa mu no, so maka asɛm bi makyerɛ Israel abusuakuw biara a mahyɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnyɛn me man Israel sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na munsi kyeneduru dan mma me?

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Na afei kɔka kyerɛ m’akoa Dawid sɛ: Sɛ asafo AWURADE se ni. Me na mefaa wo mifii nguan hwɛbea, fii nguan akyi, sɛ bɛyɛ me man Israel so panyin.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Na midii w’akyi baabiara a wokɔe na matwitwa w’atamfo nyinaa afi w’anim, na mɛma woanya din kɛse sɛ asase so nnipa akɛse din.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Na mesiesie tenabea mama me man Israel, na medua wɔn na wɔatena wɔn tenabea, na wɔanhwanyan wɔn bio, na amumɔyɛ mma anhaw wɔn bio sɛ kan no,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: ne bere a mehyɛɛ akannifo sɛ wonni me man Israel so no; na mɛma woahome afi w’atamfo nyinaa ho. Na AWURADE aka akyerɛ wo sɛ AWURADE na ɔbɛkyekye ofi ama wo.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Sɛ wo nna wie du, na wo ne w’agyanom kɔda wɔ asaman a, mɛma w’aseni a ofi wo yam so, w’akyi na mɛma n’ahenni atim.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Ɔno na obesi dan ama me din na mɛma n’ahenni agua atim akosi daa.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Me na mɛyɛ no agya na ɔno nso ayɛ me ɔba, na sɛ ɔfom a, mede nnipa poma ne nnipa mma mmaa mɛteɛ no so.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Na wo, O Asafo AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, woayi w’akoa asotiw sɛ: Mɛkyekye ofi mama wo, enti na w’akoa asi ne bo rebɔ wo sɛɛ mpae yi.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene Dawid bae bɛtenaa AWURADE anim na ɔkae sɛ: Hena ne me, AWURADE Nyankopɔn, na me fi ne dɛn sɛ wode me abedu sesɛɛ yi?

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Nanso eyi da so yɛ w’ani so ketewa, O AWURADE Nyankopɔn, na woaka daakye a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri ho asɛm nso akyerɛ w’akoa fi, na woakyerɛ me awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba, O Awurade Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Na ɛdɛn na Dawid nkɔ so nka nkyerɛ wo bio? Na wo na wunim w’akoa, O Awurade Nyankopɔn.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: W’asɛm nti ne sɛ wo koma te no na woayɛ ade akɛse yi, sɛ wobɛma w’akoa ahu.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Enti woso kokuroo, O AWURADE Nyankopɔn na obiara nni hɔ a ɔte sɛ wo, onyame biara nso nni w’akyi, sɛ nsɛm a yɛde yɛn aso ate no nyinaa te no.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Na ɔman biako bɛn na ɛwɔ asase so a ɛte sɛ wo man, sɛ Israel a Onyankopɔn akogye wɔn afa ayɛ ɔman de agye din na wayɛ ade akɛse ne ade a ɛyɛ hu ama mo, ama w’asase, wo man a wugyee wɔn fae fii Misraim, amanaman ne wɔn anyame nsam no anim?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Na woasiesie wo man Israel afa de wɔn ayɛ wo man akosi daa, na wo AWURADE, woayɛ wɔn Onyankopɔn.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Na afei, O AWURADE Nyankopɔn, asɛm a woaka w’akoa ne ne fi ho no, ma ennyina nkosi daa na yɛ sɛnea woaka no.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Na ma wo din nso nkosi daa sɛ: Asafo AWURADE ne Israel so Nyankopɔn. Na ma w’akoa Dawid fi nnyina w’anim pintinn.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Na afei, O AWURADE Nyankopɔn, wo ara ne Onyankopɔn, na wo nsɛm yɛ nokware, na wode adepa yi ahyɛ w’akoa bɔ,

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: na afei ma ɛnyɛ wo fɛ sɛ wubehyira w’akoa fi na agyina w’anim. Na wo, AWURADE Nyankopɔn na woaka na wo nhyira mu na wobehyira w’akoa fi daa.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: na Yoiada ba Benaia na odi Keretifo ne Peletifo no so, na Dawid mma ne asɔfo.

english_verse: David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Na Dawid san fii Siriafo kum no, ogyee din Nkyene-bon mu sɛ okum Edomfo mpem dunwɔtwe.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Na ɔkaa Moab nso gui na ɔma wɔdedaa fam, de susuhama susuw wɔn; na osusuw ahama abien sɛ wonkum wɔn, ne hama biako a edu pɛpɛɛpɛ sɛ wɔntena ase. Na Moab yɛɛ Dawid nkoa a wɔsoa ayɛyɛde ba.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kaa Soba hene Rehob ba Hadadeser gui, bere a ɔkɔe sɛ okogye ne nsaase a ɛwɔ asubɔnten Eufrate ho no mu.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Na Damasko Siriafo bae sɛ wɔbɛboa Soba hene Hadadeser; na Dawid kum Siriafo no mu nnipa ɔpeduonu abien.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid de bansifo kɔtenaa Damasko a ɛwɔ Aram, na Siriafo yɛɛ Dawid nkoa a wɔsoa ayɛyɛde ba. Na AWURADE boaa Dawid ma odii nim nea ɔkɔe nyinaa.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Dawid gyigyee sika akyɛm a Hadadeser nkoa kurae no de baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Dawid faa kɔbere pii pa fii Hadadeser nkurow Beta ne Berotai mu.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: Toi somaa ne ba Yoram baa ɔhene Dawid nkyɛn bekyiaa no hyiraa no, sɛ ɔne Hadadeser ako na waka no agu, efisɛ Hadadeser ne Toi taa di dɔm; na Yoram de dwetɛ nnwinne ne sika nnwinne ne kɔbere nnwinne bae.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Ɛno nso na ɔhene Dawid de yɛɛ akronkronne maa AWURADE, ɛne dwetɛ ne sika a efi amanaman a ɔbrɛɛ wɔn ase no nyinaa mu a ɔde yɛɛ akronkronne no:

english_verse: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Efi Edom ne Moab ne Amonfo ne Filistifo ne Amalekfo ne Soba hene Rehob ba Hadadeser asade mu.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: na Ahitub ba Sadok ne Abiatar ba Ahimelek ne asɔfo, na Seraia ne ɔkyerɛwfo,

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Na Seruia ba Yoab na odi dɔm so na Ahilud ba Yehosafat ne ɔsɛnkaefo;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kae sɛ: So obi da so wɔ hɔ a waka Saul fi, na Yonatan nti menyɛ no adɔe?

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Na Saul fi akoa bi wɔ hɔ a ne din de Siba. Na wokohyiaa no baa Dawid nkyɛn no, ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wone Siba? Na ose: W’akoa ne no.

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So obi nni hɔ bio Saul fi a mede Onyankopɔn adɔe mɛyɛ no? Na Siba se: Yonatan babarima bi da so wɔ hɔ a ne nan asinsen.

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔwɔ he? Na Siba ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔwɔ Amiel ba Makir fi wɔ Lo-debar.

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Na Saul ba Yonatan ba Mefiboset duu Dawid nkyɛn no, ɔde n’anim hwee fam kotow no. Na Dawid kae sɛ: Mefiboset! Na ose: W’akoa ni.

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nsuro, na w’agya Yonatan nti mɛyɛ wo adɔe na madan w’agya Saul asase nyinaa mama wo na woadidi me pon so daa yi.

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkotow kae sɛ: W’akoa ne hena a worehwɛ no teta sɛ, ɔkraman funu yi?

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene frɛɛ Saul abofra Siba na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ade nyinaa a ɛyɛ Saul ne ne fi nyinaa de no, mede mama wo wura ba.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Na ahemfo a wɔyɛ Hadadeser nkoa no nyinaa hui sɛ wɔagu Israel anim no wɔne Israel yɛɛ asomdwoe apam na wɔsom wɔn. Na Siriafo suroe sɛ wɔbɛboa Amonfo no bio.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid kae sɛ: Mɛyɛ Nahas ba Hanun adɔe, sɛnea n’agya yɛɛ me adɔe no. Na Dawid somaa ne nkoa sɛ wɔnkɔma no hyɛden n’agya wu no nti. Na Dawid nkoa no duu Amonfo asase so.

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Amonfo asafohene ka kyerɛɛ wɔn wura Hanun sɛ: So wususuw sɛ w’agya ni na Dawid di nti na ɔsomaa wo nkyɛn hyɛdenmafo yi? So ɛnyɛ kurow yi mu pɛepɛe ne ne nsra ne ne butuw nti na Dawid somaa ne nkoa baa wo nkyɛn yi?

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Na Hanun faa Dawid nkoa no yiyii wɔn bogyesɛ fa fa, na otwitwaa wɔn ntade mu fa fa beduu wɔn to ase na ogyaa wɔn kwan.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Dawid no, ɔsoma kohyiaa wɔn, efisɛ wɔasopa mmarima no pa ara. Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Montena Yeriko nkosi sɛ mo bogyesɛ befuw ansa na moasan aba.

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Na Amonfo no hui sɛ wɔn ho abɔn Dawid no, Amonfo no soma kɔbobɔɔ Bet-rehob Siriafo ne Soba Siriafo paa, anammɔnmufo ɔpeduonu ne Maaka hene nnipa apem ne Tob mmarima ɔpedumien.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Hyɛ wo ho den na ma yɛnhyɛ yɛn ho den mma yɛn man ne yɛn Nyankopɔn nkurow. Na AWURADE nyɛ nea eye n’ani so.

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Na Dawid tee no, ɔsomaa Yoab ne akofofo dɔm no nyinaa kɔe.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Na Amonfo fii adi betwitwaa mpasua kurow no pon ano; na Soba ne Rehob Siriafo ne Tob ne Maaka mmarima no nko gyina wuram.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Na Yoab hui sɛ dɔm no ani kyerɛ no anim ne akyiri no, ɔpaw Israel mu dɔmmarima nyinaa mu bi ma wotwitwa kohyiaa Siriafo.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Na dɔm no nkae no, ɔde wɔn hyɛɛ ne nua Abisai nsa ma otwa kohyiaa Amonfo.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ Siriafo yɛ den sen me a, bɛboa me, na sɛ Amonfo na wɔyɛ den sen wo a, mɛba mabɛboa wo.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne dɔm a wɔka ne ho no ne Siriafo de bɔɔ ani, na woguanee n’anim.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Amonfo no hui sɛ Siriafo aguan no, wɔn nso woguanee Abisai anim kɔhyɛn kurow no mu. Ɛnna Yoab san fii Amonfo no ho baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Na Siriafo hui sɛ wɔagu Israel anim no, wɔboaboaa wɔn ho ano faako.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Na Hadadeser soma kɔfaa Siriafo a wɔwɔ asuogya no bae na wɔbaa Helam. Na Hadadeser sahene Sobak dii wɔn anim.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Dawid no, ɔboaboaa Israel nyinaa ano na okotwaa Yordan kɔɔ Helam. Na Siriafo twitwaa mpasua hyiaa Dawid na wɔne no koe.

english_verse: The Arameans attacked, but then they ran from Israel. David killed
translation_verse: Na Siriafo guanee Israel anim na Dawid kunkum Siriafo mu nteaseɛnamfo ahansɔn ne apɔnkɔsotefo ɔpeduanan, na opiraa ɔsahene Sobak ma owui hɔ.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Afe bi mu ɔpɛ bere mfiase, a ahemfo taa tu sa no, Dawid somaa Yoab ne ne nkoa kaa ne ho ne Israel nyinaa sɛ wɔnkɔsɛe Amonfo; na wokotuaa Raba nso. Na Dawid de, ɔtenaa Yerusalem.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: na ɔhene bo huru na ɔka kyerɛ wo sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na mobɛn kurow no kɔkoe sɛɛ? So munnim sɛ wobefi ɔfasu no so abɛtotow?

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Na Dawid soma kɔɔ Yoab nkyɛn sɛ: Ma Hetini Uria mmra me nkyɛn. Na Yoab somaa Uria baa Dawid nkyɛn.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Na Uria duu ne nkyɛn no, Dawid bisaa no sɛnea Yoab ne dɔm no te ne sɛ ɔsa no te.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Uria sɛ: Sian kɔ wo fi kɔhohoro wo nan ase. Na Uria fii ɔhene fi kɔe no, wɔde ɔhene ayɛyɛde fi dii n’akyi.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Na Uria kɔdaa ɔhene fi pon ano, ɔne ne wura nkoa nyinaa, na wansian ankɔ ne fi.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Uria ansian ankɔ ne fi. Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Uria sɛ: So ɛnyɛ ɔkwan na wufi bae? Ɛdɛn nti na woansian ankɔ wo fi?

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Na Uria ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Onyankopɔn Adaka no, ne Israel ne Yuda tete asese mu na me wura Yoab ne me wura nkoa abobɔ wuram nsra na me de, menkɔ me fi minkodidi na mennom na me ne me yere nna anaa? Sɛ wote ase na wo kra te ase yi, merenni saa asɛm yi.

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Uria sɛ: Tena ha nnɛ nso na ɔkyena mɛma woakɔ. Ɛnna Uria tenaa Yerusalem da no ne n’adekyee.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Na Dawid frɛɛ no ne no didi nomee na ɔma ɔbowee; na anadwofa no, ofii adi kɔdaa ne nnae so, ɔne ne wura nkoa, na wansian ankɔ ne fi.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Na ade kyee anɔpa no, Dawid kyerɛw nhoma maa Uria de kɔmaa Yoab,

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: na ɔkyerɛw nhoma no mu sɛ: Momma Uria nkodi dɔm a ɛyɛ den no ano na montwe mo ho mfi n’akyi na wɔmmɔ no na ɔntɔ.

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Na Yoab retua kurow no no, ɔde Uria kodii nea onim sɛ dɔmmarima wɔ no.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Na kurow no mu mmarima fii adi ne Yoab bɛkoe, na dɔm a wɔyɛ Dawid nkoa no mu bi totɔe, na Hetini Uria nso tɔe.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab soma kɔkaa ɔsa no mu nsɛm nyinaa kyerɛɛ Dawid.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ ɔbɔfo no sɛ: Sɛ woka ɔsa no mu nsɛm nyinaa kyerɛ ɔhene wie,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Hena na ɔbɔɔ Yerubeset ba Abimelek? Ɛnyɛ ɔbea bi na ɔtow owiyammo ba fi ɔfasu so bɔɔ no ma ɔtɔe, Tebes no? Ɛnne ka sɛ: W’akoa Uria, Hetini no nso atɔ.

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo no siim, na ɔbɛkaa asɛm a Yoab de somaa no no nyinaa kyerɛɛ Dawid.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Mmarima no yɛɛ yɛn so den na wofi baa yɛn so petee mu no, yɛsaa wɔn ara koduu kurow no pon ano;

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: na atowfo no fi ɔfasu so totow guu wo nkoa so na ɔhene nkoa no bi totɔe na w’akoa Uria, Hetini no nso atɔ.

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ɔbɔfo no sɛ: Sɛɛ na kɔka kyerɛ Yoab: Mma asɛm yi nnhaw wo, na nkrante twa ha na etwa ha. Ma wo ko no mu nyɛ den nhyɛ kurow no, na dwiriw gu. Na fa hyɛ no nkuran.

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Na Uria yere no tee sɛ ne kunu Uria awu no, ogyam ne wura no.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Na kunayɛ bere twaa mu no, Dawid soma kɔfaa no baa ne fi, na ɔbɛyɛɛ ne yere no ɔwoo babarima maa no. Na asɛm a Dawid dii no ansɔ AWURADE ani.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Ɔdefo no wɔ nguan ne anantwi bebree pa,

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Na da koro bi a ɔhɔho bi baa ɔdefo no nkyɛn no, wampɛ sɛ ɔde ne nguan ne n’anantwi no bi yɛ ɔkwantenni a wabɛsoɛ no no hɔho, na ɔkɔfaa ohiani no guan no siesie maa ɔbarima a ɔbaa ne nkyɛn no.

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid bo hurui pii hyɛɛ ɔbarima no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Natan sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, ɔbarima a ɔyɛɛ eyi no sɛ owu.

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Na oguan no, ɔnhyɛ ananmu mpɛn anan, sɛ wadi saa asɛm yi na wanhu mmɔbɔ.

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Ɛnna Natan ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ. Wone ɔbarima no! Sɛ AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn se ni. Me na mesraa wo ngo na mede wo misii Israel so hene, na miyii wo Saul nsam;

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: na mede wo wura fi memaa wo, na mede wo wura yerenom nso miguu wo kokom, na mede Israel ne Yuda fi memaa wo; na sɛ esua a, anka mede sɛɛ ne sɛɛ mɛka wo ho.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛn nti na woabu AWURADE asɛm animtiaa ayɛ n’anim bɔne yi? Wode nkrante akum Hetini Uria, na woafa ne yere ayɛ wo yere, na ɔno de, wode Amonfo nkrante adi no awu.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Na afei nkrante remfi wo fi kosi daa, esiane sɛ woabu me animtiaa na woafa Hetini Uria yere aware no.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Hwɛ, mɛma bɔne aba wo so ne wo fi so, na magye wo yerenom w’anim mede mama wo yɔnko, na ɔne wo yerenom adeda petee mu awia ketee.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Na wo de woyɛɛ no ahintawee mu, na me de, medi asɛm yi Israel nyinaa anim awia ketee.

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ wode asɛm a woadi yi ama AWURADE atamfo anya kwan aka abususɛm atia no nti, ɛyɛ dɛn ara ɔba a wɔwoo no maa wo bewu.

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Na Natan kɔɔ ne fi. Dawid ba no wu Na AWURADE de owuyare bɔɔ ɔba a Uria yere no wo maa Dawid no.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Na Dawid paa Onyankopɔn kyɛw maa abofra no; na Dawid bua dae na ɔkɔɔ mu kɔdaa fam anadwo no.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Na ne fi mpanyimfo kogyinaa no so sɛ wɔbɛma no so afi fam; nanso wampene na ɔne wɔn nso annidi.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Na da a ɛto so ason no, akokoaa no wui. Na Dawid nkoa suroe sɛ wɔbɛka akyerɛ no sɛ akokoaa no awu na wɔkae sɛ: Hwɛ, akokoaa no da so te ase no po, yɛne no kasae, na wantie yɛn. Na yɛbɛyɛ dɛn aka akyerɛ no sɛ akokoaa no awu na ɔrenyɛ bɔne bi?

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Na Dawid hui sɛ ne nkoa reyɛ huhuhuhu no, Dawid hui sɛ akokoaa no awu; na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa no sɛ: So akokoaa no awu anaa? Na wose: Wawu.

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Asɛm bɛn na woadi yi? Akokoaa no da so te ase no, wubua dae na wusui; na akokoaa no wui mmom no woasɔre adidi.

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Na ose. Akokoaa no da so te ase no, mibua medae, na misui na mise: Hena na onim sɛ ebia AWURADE bɛdom me na akokoaa no anya nkwa;

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: na afei wanya awu; ɛdɛn nti na minni abuada? So metumi masan no aba bio? Me na mɛkɔ ne nkyɛn, na ɔno de, ɔrensan mma me nkyɛn. Solomon awo

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Na Dawid kyekyee ne yere Batseba werɛ; na ɔkɔɔ ne nkyɛn ne no kɔdae; na ɔwoo babarima, na ɔtoo no din Solomon, na AWURADE dɔ no.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa odiyifo Natan ma ɔkɔtoo no din Yedidia ase ne: AWURADE dɔfo, AWURADE nti. Dawid ko fa Raba Nnommum (

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne Amonfo a wɔwɔ Raba koe na ogyee ahenkurow no.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Na Yoab somaa abɔfo baa Dawid nkyɛn sɛ: Me ne Raba ako, nso magye nsu ano kurow no.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Na afei boaboa ɔman a aka no ano bɛbɔ kurow no ho nsra na gye, na me, mannye kurow no, na wɔamfa me din anto.

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Na Dawid boaboaa ɔman no nyinaa ano kɔɔ Raba ne no kɔkoe na ogyei.

english_verse: and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about
translation_verse: Na oyii wɔn hene abotiri fii ne ti; ne duru si sika dwetikɛse, na aboɔden abo wɔ mu, na wɔde bɔɔ Dawid ti, na ɔde kurow no mu asade bebree pa fi bae.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ɔman a wɔwɔ mu no fi bae, na ɔma wɔde sradaa ne fatudade ne dade mmonnua yɛɛ adwuma na wɔyɛɛ ntayaa fononoo ho adwuma dennen. Na sɛɛ na ɔde yɛɛ Amonfo nkurow nyinaa. Ɛnna Dawid ne ne man nyinaa san baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Na eyi akyi no na Dawid ba Absalom wɔ nuabea fɛfɛ bi a ne din de Tamar, na Dawid ba Amnon pɛ no.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Na Amnon ne nuabea Tamar nti ne ho hiaa no ma ɔyaree, na ɔyɛ ɔbaabun na ɛyɛɛ Amnon den sɛ ɔbɛyɛ no biribi.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Na Amnon wɔ adamfo bi a wɔfrɛ no Yonadab, Dawid ne nua Simea ba. Na Yonadab yɛ onitefo sɛ.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo ɔhene ba mu wofɔn sɛɛ daa anɔpa yi? So worenka nkyerɛ me? Na Amnon ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mepɛ me nua Absalom nuabea Tamar.

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Na Yonadab ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔda wo nnae so na twa mpayare; na sɛ w’agya bɛhwɛ wo a, ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Ma me nua Tamar mmra mmɛma me aduan, nanso ɔnyɛ aduan no m’anim, na minhu, na minni ne nsam.

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Amnon kɔdae na ɔboapa yaree. Na ɔhene bae bɛhwɛɛ no no, Amnon ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Mesrɛ ma me nua Tamar mmra mmɛyɛ tetare abien m’anim na minni ne nsam.

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid soma kɔɔ Tamar nkyɛn ofie sɛ: Kɔ wo nua Amnon fi ɛ na kɔyɛ aduan ma no.

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Na Tamar kɔɔ ne nua Amnon fi; faako a ɔda hɔ. Na ɔfaa mmɔre fɔtɔwee na ɔyɛɛ tetare n’anim na ɔkyew tetare no.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Na ɔtoɛɛ kyew dade no na ohwiei n’anim; nso wampɛ sɛ odi. Na Amnon kae sɛ: Ma nnipa nyinaa mfi me ho mfi adi. Na nnipa no nyinaa fii ne ho fii adi.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Na Amnon ka kyerɛɛ Tamar sɛ: Fa aduan no bra piam, na minni wo nsam. Na Tamar faa tetare a ɔyɛe no de kɔmaa ne nua Amnon pia no mu.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Na ɔde rema no sɛ onni no, osoo no mu na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Bra, bɛda me nkyɛn, me nua!

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Daabi, me nua nhyɛ me, na wɔnyɛ saa ade yi Israel mu; nni nkwaseasɛm yi!

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Na me de, ɛhe po na mede m’ahohora mɛkɔ? Na wo nso, wobɛyɛ sɛ Israel mu nkwaseafo no bi. Enti mesrɛ, wo ne ɔhene nkɔkasa na ɔremfa me nkame wo.

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Nanso wampɛ sɛ otie no na sɛ ne ho yɛ den sen no nti, ɔhyɛɛ no ne no dae.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Amnon de ɔtan kɛse tan no pii, ma ɔtan a ɔde tan no no sen ɔdɔ a ɔdɔɔ no no. Na Amnon ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɔre kɔ!

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dabi, me nuabarima, ɔpam a worepam me yi sen bɔne a woyɛɛ me no. Na Amnon ampɛ sɛ otie no.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ n’abofra a ɔsom no no sɛ: Pam ɔbea yi fi me so fi adi na to ɔpon no akyi korɔkorɔ mu wɔ n’akyi.

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Nso atade nworannworan yuu bi hyɛ no na saa mmatakari no na ɔhene mmabea a wɔyɛ mmabun no hyɛ. Na ne somfo no de no fii adi na ɔtoo ɔpon akyi korɔkorɔ mu guu n’akyi.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ɛnna Tamar sesaw nso guu n’atifi na osunsuanee n’atade nworannworan a ɛhyɛ no no mu na ɔde ne nsa soaa ne ti de benabɔ ara kɔe.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Na ne nua Absalom ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wo nua Amnon akɔ wo ho anaa? Na afei, me nua, mua w’ano, ɔyɛ wo nua. Mfa wo koma nto asɛm yi so. Na Tamar tenaa ne nua Absalom fi komm. Absalom tɔ Amnon so were

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Na Absalom ne Amnon ankasa bɔne anaa papa so. Na Absalom tan Amnon, sɛ wahyɛ ne nua Tamar ne no ada nti. Absalom aweretɔ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Na mfe abien akyi no, Absalom ma wokotwitwaa ne nguan ho wɔ Baal-hasor a ɛda Efraim ho na Absalom hyiaa ɔhene mma nyinaa kɔɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Na Absalom baa ɔhene nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Hwɛ w’akoa rema wɔakotwitwa ne nguan ho; enti ma ɔhene ne ne nkoa ne w’akoa nkɔ.

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Absalom sɛ: Dabi, me ba, mma yɛn nyinaa nnkɔ na yɛankɔyɛ wo so duru. Na ɔhyɛɛ no nanso wampɛ sɛ ɔkɔ, na ohyiraa no.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Absalom kae sɛ: Sɛ ɛnte saa a, ma me nua Amnon ne yɛn nkɔ. Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na ɔne wo nkɔ?

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Na Absalom hyɛɛ no ara na ɔmaa Amnon ne ɔhene mma no nyinaa ne no kɔe.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Nso Absalom ahyɛ ne mmerante sɛ: Monhwɛ na sɛ Amnon nom nsa na n’ani gye na mise mo sɛ: Mommɔ Amnon a, munkum no. Munnsuro, so ɛnyɛ me na mahyɛ mo? Monyɛ den na monyɛ mo ho mmarima.

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
