translation_verse: Na Absalom mmerante no yɛɛ Amnon sɛnea Absalom hyɛɛ wɔn no. Ɛnna ɔhene mma no nyinaa sɔresɔre tenatenaa wɔn mfurum so guanguanee.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Na wɔwɔ ɔkwan mu no, asɛm no duu Dawid nkyɛn sɛ: Absalom akum ɔhene mma no nyinaa na wɔn mu biako pɛ anka.

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene sɔre sunsuan ne ntade mu na ɔdaa fam na ne nkoa nyinaa gyinagyina hɔ asunsuan wɔn ntade mu.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne nua Simea ba Yonadab buae sɛ. Mma me wura nnnwen sɛ wɔakum ɔhene mma mmerante no nyinaa na Amnon nko na wawu, na ɛwɔ Absalom anom ara fi da no a ɔhyɛɛ ne nua Tamar ne no dae no.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Na afei mma me wura ɔhene mmfa asɛm no nnhyɛ ne koma mu, sɛ ɔhene mma nyinaa awuwu na Amnon nko na wawu. Absalom aguan

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Na Absalom guanee. Na aberante a ɔwɛn no maa n’ani so hwɛe na hwɛ, nnipa bebree nam Horonaim kwan a ɛwɔ n’akyi no so, bepɔw nkyɛn mu, reba.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Na Yonadab ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔhene mma no reba; sɛ w’akoa kae no, sɛ ɛte neno.

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Na owiee ɔkasa no pɛ na hwɛ, ɔhene mma no bae na wɔmomaa wɔn nne so sui, na ɔhene nso ne ne nkoa nyinaa nso suu osu kɛse pa ara.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Dawid ani gyinaa Absalom, efisɛ na ne werɛ akyekye Amnon wu no ho.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Na Seruia ba Yoab hui sɛ ɔhene koma wɔ Absalom ho.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Na Tekoani bea no rekɔka akyerɛ ɔhene no, ɔde n’anim hwee fam kotow no kae sɛ: Ɔhene, boa!

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ wo? Na ose: Ampa, meyɛ okunafo, me kunu awu.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Na w’afenaa wɔ mmammarima baanu na wɔn baanu no kɔkoe wuram na ɔpatafo bi nni hɔ na obiako bɔɔ obiako ma owui.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, abusua no nyinaa asɔre ahyɛ w’afenaa na wose: Yi nea ɔbɔɔ ne nua no ma, na ne nua a wadi no awu no kra nti yenkum no na yɛnsɛe ɔdedifo no nso. Na wɔde rebɛhyew m’ase nyinaa, na wɔannyaw din anaa okyikafo bi amma me kunu, asase ani.

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no sɛ: Kɔ wo fi na mɛhyɛ wo ho ahyɛde.

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Na Tekoani bea no ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Me wura ɔhene, me ne m’agya fi so na ɛso yi nna na ɔhene ne n’agua nni bem.

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Obi ka wo asɛm bi a, fa no brɛ me na ɔrensan nka wo bio.

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no kae sɛ: Ma ɔhene nkae AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn na mogya ho weretɔfo no ansɛe ade bio na wankum me ba. Na ose: Sɛ AWURADE te ase yi wo ba no nwi biako po rentɔ fam!

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea no kae sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, ma w’afenaa nka me wura ɔhene asɛm bi. Na ose: Ka ɛ!

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no se: Ɛnne ɛdɛn nti na woasusuw saa ade yi Onyankopɔn man ho na sɛ ɔhene reka asɛm yi a, ɔte sɛ nea odi so, sɛ ɔhene nkɔfa ne nipa a wɔapam no no nsan mma.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Na owu de, yebewu ara na yɛte sɛ nsu a wɔahwie agu fam a wontumi nsesaw bio; nso Onyankopɔn de, onkum na mmom odwen nea ɛbɛyɛ na nea wɔapam no no wɔrempam no mfi ne ho.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Na afei nea enti a mebae na me ne me wura ɔhene abɛka asɛm yi ne sɛ, ɔman no ma misuroe na w’afenaa kae sɛ: Me ne ɔhene bɛkɔ akɔkasa; ebia ɔhene bɛyɛ nea n’abaawa se no;

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: sɛ ɔhene betie na wayi n’abaawa afi onipa a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔsɛe me ne me ba fi Onyankopɔn agyapade mu no nsam.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Na w’afenaa se: Wɔmma me wura ɔhene asɛm nyɛ me awerɛkyekye; efisɛ me wura ɔhene te sɛ Onyankopɔn bɔfo a ohu papa ne bɔne, enti AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn nni w’akyi.

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene bua ka kyerɛɛ ɔbea no se: Nsiw me asɛm a merebisa wo yi so. Na ɔbea no se. Me wura ɔhene nkasa ɛ!

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: So Yoab nsa wɔ nsɛm yi nyinaa mu anaa? Na ɔbea no buae sɛ. Sɛ wo kra te ase yi, me wura ɔhene, ɛnyɛ sɛ obi bɛman nifa anaa benkum afi nea me wura ɔhene aka no nyinaa ho. Na w’akoa Yoab na ɔhyɛɛ me na ɔno ara na ɔde nsɛm yi nyinaa hyɛɛ w’afenaa anom.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔbɛdan asɛm no ani aka nti na w’akoa Yoab yɛɛ saa ade yi nanso me wura yɛ onyansafo sɛ Onyankopɔn bɔfo na ohu nea ɛwɔ asase so nyinaa.

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Hwɛ, mema wo kwan, na kɔ na kɔfa aberante Absalom san bra.

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Na Yoab de n’anim butuw fam, kotowee na ohyiraa ɔhene. Na Yoab kae sɛ: Ɛnnɛ na w’akoa ahu sɛ manya me wura ɔhene anim anuonyam, sɛ ɔhene ayɛ nea n’akoa aka akyerɛ no.

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Na Yoab siim kɔɔ Gesur kɔfaa Absalom baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Ma ɔmman nkɔ ne fi na m’anim na ɔrenhu. Ɛnna Absalom man kɔɔ ne fi na wanhu ɔhene anim. Absalom ne Dawid nkabom

english_verse: No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom.
translation_verse: Nso Israel nyinaa mu obiara nni hɔ a wɔkamfo n’ahoɔfɛ sɛ Absalom. Efi ne nan ase kosi ne mpampam dɛm biara nni ne ho.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Na sɛ oyi ne ti, nso daa afe du a, oyi, efisɛ ɛyɛ no duru a, oyi na wɔkari ne ti nwi no a, esi nnwetɛbona ahanu, ɔhene abrammo so.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Na wɔwoo mmammarima baasa maa Absalom ne ɔbea biako a wɔfrɛ no Tamar; ɔyɛ ɔbea a n’anim yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Na Absalom dii Yerusalem mfe abien nanso wanhu ɔhene anim.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Na Absalom soma kɔfrɛɛ Yoab sɛ ɔrebɛsoma no ɔhene nkyɛn nso wampɛ sɛ ɔba ne nkyɛn; na ɔsomae ne mprenu so bio nso wampɛ sɛ ɔba.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Monhwɛ, Yoab afuw wɔ me de ho na ɔwɔ atoko wɔ hɔ, monkɔ nkɔto mu gya.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab sɔre baa Absalom nkyɛn ofie bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo nkoa de ogya akɔto m’afuw a mewɔ no mu?

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Na Absalom ka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Hwɛ, masoma maba wo nkyɛn sɛ: Bra na mensoma wo ɔhene nkyɛn nkose no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na mifi Gesur mebae? Eye ma me sɛ anka meda so mewɔ hɔ. Enti afei mehu ɔhene anim; na sɛ ɛso bi da me so a, onkum me.

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab baa ɔhene nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no na ɔfrɛɛ Absalom na ɔbaa ɔhene nkyɛn na ɔkotow no de n’anim butuw fam ɔhene anim na ɔhene few Absalom ano.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Na eyi akyi no, Absalom siesiee nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔ, ne mmarima aduonum a wɔbɛwɛn no, dii n’anim.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Na Absalom tuaa ahema kogyina kurow no pon ano kwan ho. Na obiara a ɔwɔ asɛm bi na ɔreba ɔhene nkyɛn abedi no, Absalom frɛ no sɛ: Kurow bɛn so na wufi? Na ose: Israel mmusuakuw bi mu na w’akoa fi a,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ wo nsɛm ye na ɛteɛ, nanso obi nni hɔ a ofi ɔhene fam a obetie ama wo.

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Absalom ka nso sɛ: Hena na ɔde me besi asase yi so temmufo na me nkyɛn na anka obiara a okura asɛm bi anaa atemmude bi bɛba na mabu no atɛntrenee.

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ obi twiw bɛn no bɛkotow no a, ɔteɛ ne nsa so no mu na ofew n’ano.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Na sɛɛ na Absalom yɛ Israelfo a wɔba ɔhene nkyɛn asenni nyinaa; na Absalom de nyaa Israel mmarima baa n’afa.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Na mfirihyia anan twaa mu no, Absalom ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, ma menkɔ menkɔma m’aboade a mede mehyɛɛ AWURADE bɔ wɔ Hebron.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Efisɛ metenaa Gesur wɔ Aram no w’akoa hyɛɛ bɔ sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE de me san ba Yerusalem a, ɛnne mɛsom AWURADE.

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa asomdwoe kɔ. Na osiim kɔɔ Hebron.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo bi baa Dawid nkyɛn bɛkae sɛ: Israel mmarima koma di Absalom akyi.

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa a wɔne no wɔ Yerusalem nyinaa sɛ: Monsɔre mma yenguan na yɛrennya mu afiye Absalom anim. Monyɛ ntɛm mma yɛnkɔ na wanyɛ ntɛm ammɛto yɛn anyɛ yɛn bɔne bi na wamfa nkrante ammɛbɔ kurow yi.

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene nkoa ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Sɛnea me wura ɔhene pɛ nyinaa no, hwɛ wo nkoa bɛyɛ.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa nyinaa sen faa ne nkyɛn; na Keretifo nyinaa ne Peletifo nyinaa ne Gatfo nyinaa, mmarima ahansia a wodii n’akyi fi Gat bae no, betwaam ɔhene anim.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Gatni Itai sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wo nso ne yɛn rekɔ? San kɔ na kɔtena ɔhene nkyɛn na woyɛ ɔnanani ne nea wɔatu no afi ne kurow mu nso.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Nnɛra nko na wobae na ɛnnɛ memma wo ne yɛn nkokyin? Na me de, merekɔ baabiara a metumi makɔ; san na fa wo nuanom nso ka wo ho san kɔ adɔe ne nokware so.

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Na Itai buaa ɔhene sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase na me wura ɔhene nso te ase yi, faako a me wura ɔhene bɛtena no, owu mu oo, nkwa mu oo, ɛhɔ ara na w’akoa bɛtena!

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Itai sɛ: Bra bɛsen! Na Gatni Itai ne ne mmarima nyinaa ne mmofra a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa betwaam.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Na asase no sofo nyinaa de nne kɛse sui na ɔman no nyinaa twaam kɔe na ɔhene twaa asu Kidron na ɔman no nyinaa twae kɔfaa sare so kwan fam.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Na Abiatar bae na hwɛ, Sadok nso ni, a Lewifo nyinaa ka ne ho. Wɔso Onyankopɔn apam adaka no na wɔsoɛɛ Onyankopɔn adaka no sii hɔ, kosii sɛ ɔman no nyinaa fii kurow no mu twaam wiei ansa.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Sadok sɛ: Fa Onyankopɔn adaka no san kɔ kurow no mu. Sɛ menya AWURADE anim anuonyam a, ɔde me bɛsan aba na wama mabehu no ne ne tenabea bio.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔka sɛ: Mempɛ wo a, hwɛ, mini, ma ɔnyɛ me sɛnea eye n’ani so.

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene nso ka kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Sadok sɛ: Hwɛ woyɛ ɔdehufo? So wohu w’ani so anaa? San kɔ kurow no mu dwoodwoo, na wo ba Ahimaas ne Abiatar ba Yonatan, mo mma baanu no ne mo ntena.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, mɛtwentwɛn me nan ase sare so tataw mu akosi sɛ asɛm a mobɛka akyerɛ me befi mo nkyɛn aba.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sadok ne Abiatar de Onyankopɔn adaka no san baa Yerusalem na wɔbɛtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Na Dawid foroo Ngo-bepɔw, na ɔreforo no na ɔde su, na wakata ne ti na ɔnam anammɔn hunu mu; na nnipa a wɔne no nam no nyinaa akatakata wɔn ti na wɔreforo no na wɔresu.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Na obi ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Ahitofel fra wɔn a wɔne Absalom apam no mu. Na Dawid kae sɛ: AWURADE, mesrɛ wo, ma Ahitofel agyinatu nnan nkwaseasɛm.

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Na Dawid duu atifi nea wɔsɔre Onyankopɔn no, hwɛ, Arkini Husai behyiaa no, wasunsuane n’atade mu na ɔde dɔte agu n’atifi.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ wo ne me sen kɔ a, wobɛyɛ adesoa ama me.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wosan kɔ kurow no mu kɔka kyerɛ Absalom sɛ: Ɔhene, mɛyɛ w’akoa sɛnea kan no meyɛɛ w’agya akoa no, na afei de, mɛyɛ w’akoa a wobɛma Ahitofel agyinatu no ayɛ ɔkwa ama me.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Na asɔfo Sadok ne Abiatar nni wo nkyɛn hɔ anaa? Enti asɛm biara a wobɛte ahemfi no, ka kyerɛ ɔsɔfo Sadok ne Abiatar.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Hwɛ wɔn mma baanu no, Sadok ba Ahimaas ne Abiatar ba Yonatan wɔ wo nkyɛn hɔ na wɔn so na momma asɛm biara a mobɛte mfa nnu me nkyɛn.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Na Dawid adamfo Husai baa kurow no mu, mmere a na Absalom rehyɛn Yerusalem no.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Na Dawid twaam fii atifi hɔ kakra no, hwɛ, Mefiboset abofra Siba behyiaa no; ɔde mfurum abien a wɔahyehyɛ wɔn a wɔsoso abodoo sebɔw ahanu ne bobe aba a wɔabɔ no atɔwatɔw ɔha ne awia bere mu borɔdɔma ɔha ne nsa aboa nhoma kotoku ma.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene bisaa Siba sɛ: Wode eyinom rebɛyɛ dɛn? Na Siba se: Mfurum yi wɔmfa mma ɔhene fifo na wɔntenatena so, na abodoo ne awia bere mu nnuaba yi, mmerante no nni, na nsa yi nso, wɔmfa mma wɔn a wɔabrɛ sare so na wɔnnom.

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Na ɛhe na wo wura ba no wɔ? Na Siba ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Ɔte Yerusalem, na ose: Ɛnnɛ na Israel fi bɛdan m’agya ahenni ama me.

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Siba sɛ: Hwɛ, nea ɛyɛ Mefiboset de nyinaa yɛ wo dea. Na Siba kae sɛ: Mekotow wo, ma minnya me wura ɔhene anim anuonyam.

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Dawid duu Bahurim no, hwɛ, ɔbarima bi a ofi Saul abusua mu a wɔfrɛ no Simei a ɔyɛ Gera ba fii adi fii hɔ bae; na ɔreba no, na ɔredome.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Na ɔpaa Dawid ne ɔhene Dawid nkoa nyinaa abo; nso ɔman no nyinaa ne mmarima akofofo no nyinaa wowɔ ne nifa ne ne benkum.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Na Simei redome no, sɛ ɔkae ni: Fi adi kɔ, fi adi kɔ, mogyapɛfo, onipa huhuni!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: AWURADE adan Saul a wubesii n’ananmu dii hene no fi mogya nyinaa aba wo so, na AWURADE de ahenni no ahyɛ wo ba Absalom nsa, na hwɛ, w’amane mu na woda yi, efisɛ onipa a wahwie mogya agu ne wo.

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Seruia ba Abisai ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na ɔkraman funu yi dome me wura ɔhene yi? Ma menkɔ menkotwa ne ti ɛ!

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene se: Dɛn na me ne mo Seruia mma wɔ yɛ? Ma ɔnnome ara, na AWURADE ase no sɛ: Dome Dawid! Na ɛhena na ɔbɛka akyerɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woyɛ sɛɛ?

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abisai ne ne nkoa sɛ: Hwɛ, me ba a ofi me yam na ɔrehwehwɛ me akum me yi, na afei menne Benyaminni yi. Munnyaa no mma ɔnnome, efisɛ AWURADE na wahyɛ no.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Ebia AWURADE bɛhwɛ m’amanehunu, na AWURADE de papa ahyɛ me nnome a ɔredome me nnɛ yi ananmu.

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Na Dawid ne ne nnipa nam ɔkwan no so rekɔ no na Simei nam bepɔw no ho ne ntentenso rekɔ; na ɔrekɔ no, na ɔdome ara, na osianee no paa no abo, na ɔtow mfutuma petee.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ne nnipa a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa duu Yordan no; na wɔabrɛ, na wɔhomee wɔ hɔ. Absalom wɔ Yerusalem

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Absalom ne Israel mmarima nyinaa baa Yerusalem na Ahitofel ka ne ho.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Na Husai, Arkini no, a ɔyɛ Dawid adamfo no baa Absalom nkyɛn no, Husai ka kyerɛɛ Absalom sɛ: Ɔhene tiri nkwa, ɔhene tiri nkwa!

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Na Absalom ka kyerɛɛ Husai sɛ: W’adɔe a wode yɛ w’adamfo ni? Ɛdɛn nti na wo ne w’adamfo no ankɔ?

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Na Husai buaa no sɛ: Daabi, na nea AWURADE ne ɔman yi ne Israel mmarima nyinaa afa no no, ɔno na mɛyɛ ne de na me ne no atena.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Bio nso, hena na mɛsom no? So ɛnyɛ ne ba? Sɛnea mesom w’agya no, saa ara na mɛyɛ wo.

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Absalom ka kyerɛɛ Ahitofel sɛ: Muntu nea yɛnyɛ ho agyina.

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Na Ahitofel ka kyerɛɛ Absalom sɛ: Kɔ w’agya yefamnom a ogyaw wɔn sɛ wɔnhwɛ ofie no ne wɔn nna, na Israel nyinaa nte sɛ woama wo ho abɔn w’agya, na wɔn a wɔwɔ wo nkyɛn nyinaa nsa bɛyɛ den.

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wosii Absalom ntamadan, aban no atifi, na Absalom kɔɔ n’agya yefamnom no ho, Israel nyinaa anim.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Na Ahitofel ɛfo a otui nna no mu te sɛnea obi kobisa Onyankopɔn hɔ ade, saa na Ahitofel afotu nyinaa te ma Dawid ne Absalom.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Na yɛkɔto no baabiara a wobehu no a, yɛatow ahyɛ no so sɛnea obosu gu fam, na ɔno ne mmarima a wɔka ne ho no mu biako po anka.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: na mɛkɔ makɔto no a wabrɛ na ne nsam agow na mayi no hu, na nnipa a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa aguan na makum ɔhene no nko;

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: na mede ɔman no nyinaa bɛsan abrɛ wo, sɛnea ayeforo san ba ne kunu nkyɛn. Onipa biako pɛ na worehwehwɛ no akum no te sɛ ɔman no nyinaa sanba; na ɔman no nyinaa bɛyɛ komm.

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Na asɛm no tɔɔ Absalom ne Israel mpanyimfo nyinaa asom.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Na Absalom kae sɛ: Kɔfrɛ Arkini Husai nso bra, na yentie nea ɔno nso wɔ ka.

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Na Husai baa Absalom nkyɛn no, Absalom ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ Ahitofel aka ni. So yenni n’asɛm no so anaa? Sɛ ɛnte saa a, wo nso ka bi.

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Na Husai buaa Absalom sɛ: Ɛfo a Ahitofel tui seisei yi de, enye.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Na Husai se: Wo ara wunim w’agya ne ne mmarima sɛ wɔyɛ ahoɔdenfo, na wɔn ani abere sɛ osisi a wɔafa ne mma wuram, na w’agya nso yɛ dɔmmarima, na ɔrenna nkurɔfo no nkyɛn.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, sesɛɛ wakohintaw amoa bi mu anaa baabi. Na sɛ mfiase no wɔn mu bi totɔ a, obiara a ɔbɛte no bɛka sɛ: Ɔman a wodi Absalom akyi no adi nkogu.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Na nea ɔyɛ ɔbarima na ne koma te sɛ gyata koma no mpo, ɛno nti obegurow. Na Israel nyinaa nim sɛ w’agya yɛ dɔmmarima na wɔn a wɔka ne ho nso yɛ akokodurufo.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Enti meretu wo fo sɛ: Boaboa Israel nyinaa ano wɔ wo nkyɛn fi Dan kosi Beer-seba, sɛ mpoano awea dodow, na w’ankasa kɔ ɔsa no.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ ɔtwe ne ho kɔ kurow bi mu a, Israel nyinaa de ntampehama bɛto kurow no ho, na yɛatwe akɔ asu mu akosi sɛ wɔrenhu ɔbo ketewa biako po wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Ɛnna Absalom ne Israel mmarima nyinaa kae sɛ: Arkini Husai afotu no ye sen Ahitofel de no. Na AWURADE na ahyɛ sɛ wɔmma Ahitofel afotu pa no nyɛ ɔkwa, na AWURADE de bɔne aba Absalom so. Wɔbɔ Dawid kɔkɔ ma oguan

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Husai ka kyerɛɛ asɔfo Sadok ne Abiatar sɛ: Ɛfo a Ahitofel atu Absalom ne Israel mpanyimfo ni, na ɛfo a me nso matu ni.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Na afei monsoma ntɛm na wɔnkɔka nkyerɛ Dawid sɛ: Ntena sare so tataw mu anadwo yi, na otwa mmom na twa kɔ, na wɔammemmene ɔhene ne nkurɔfo a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa.

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Nso Yonatan ne Ahimaas tete En-rogel; na abaawa bi kɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ wɔnkɔka nkyerɛ ɔhene Dawid, efisɛ wontumi nkɔ kurow no mu mma wonhu wɔn.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nso aberante bi kohuu wɔn, na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Absalom. Na wɔn baanu no kɔɔ ntɛm koduu Bahurim barima bi fi, na ɔwɔ abura wɔ n’adiwo hɔ, na wosian kɔɔ mu.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no faa nkataso bi de kataa abura no ano, na ɔde atoko a wɔasiw trɛtrɛw so na obi anhu biribi.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Absalom nkoa no duu ɔbea no nkyɛn ofie hɔ no, wɔkae sɛ: Ɛhe na Ahimaas ne Yonatan wɔ? Na ɔbea no se: Wɔatwa asuwa no kɔ. Na wɔhwehwɛɛ wɔn; na wɔanhu wɔn no wɔsan baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Na wɔn kɔ akyi no wofii abura no mu fii adi na wɔkɔe kɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene Dawid, na wɔka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Monsɔre nkotwa asu no ntɛm, na ɛfo a Ahitofel atu mo ho ni.

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ne nkurɔfo a wɔka ne ho no nyinaa sɔre kotwaa Yordan; ade kyee anɔpa no, na wɔn mu biako po nkae a onnya ntwaa Yordan.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Dawid duu Mahanaim; na Absalom kotwaa Yordan, ɔno ne Israel mmarima nyinaa.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Na Absalom de Amasa sii Yoab ananmu sii dɔm no so. Nso Amasa yɛ ɔbarima bi a wɔfrɛ no Yitra, Israelni a ɔkɔɔ Nahas babea Abigail, Yoab ne na Seruia ne nua ho no ba.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Na Israel ne Absalom kɔbɔɔ nsra Gilead asase so.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Na Dawid duu Mahanaim no, Nahas ba Sobi a ofi Amonfo Raba ne Amiel ba Makir a ofi Lo-debar ne Gileadni Barsilai a ofi Rogelim no

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: ne ɛwo, ne nufusu ani srade ne anantwi nufusu a akyenkyen sebɔw brɛɛ Dawid ne nkurɔfo a wɔka ne ho no sɛ wonni na wose: Ɔkɔm de nkurɔfo no, wɔabrɛ, na osukɔm de wɔn sare so.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid gyaa dɔm no kwan de abupɛn abiɛsa mu biako hyɛɛ Yoab nsa, na ɔde abupɛn abiɛsa mu biako hyɛɛ Seruia ba Abisai, Yoab ne nua nsa, na ɔde abupɛn biako hyɛɛ Gatni Itai nsa. Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ dɔm no sɛ: Ofi na me nso me ne mo refi akɔ.

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Na dɔm no kae sɛ: Mfi nkɔ, na sɛ yeguan a, ɛrenyɛ wɔn asɛm; na yɛn mu fa nso wu a, ɛrenyɛ wɔn asɛm, nso wote sɛ yɛn mu ɔpedu; enti eye mmom sɛ wufi kurow no mu di boa yɛn.

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi kohui na ɔkɔka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Hwɛ makohu Absalom sɛ ɔsɛn odupɔn bi so.

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Na ɛhɔ ko no trɛw asase no nyinaa ani na dɔm no mu wɔn a wowui kwae no mu dɔɔso sen wɔn a wowui nkrante ano da no.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Na Absalom hyiaa Dawid nkoa no; nso Absalom te afurumpɔnkɔ so, na afurumpɔnkɔ no de no faa odupɔn kɛse bi baa kusuu ase, na ne ti kɔsoaa odupɔn no ma ɔsensɛn ɔsoro ne fam ntam, na afurumpɔnkɔ a ɔwɔ n’ase no sen kɔe.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Na Yoab ka kyerɛɛ ɔbarima a ɔka kyerɛɛ no no sɛ: Hwɛ, wuhui no, ɛdɛn nti na woammɔ no anhwe fam hɔ? Na anka mɛma wo dwetɛ du ne abɔso.

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Anka me ara na mayɛ me ho bɔne, efisɛ asɛm biara nhintaw ɔhene na anka wo nso wobɛpa m’akyi.

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Na Yoab kae sɛ: Merentwentwɛn me nan ase w’anim sa. Na ɔfaa mpɛmɛ abiɛsa kurae na ɔde kɔwowɔɔ Absalom komam bere a ɔda so yɛ anikan odupɔn no mu.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Na mmerante du a wokura Yoab akode twaa Absalom ho hyiae na wɔbobɔɔ no kum no.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab hyɛn torobɛnto na dɔm no nyinaa san fii Israel akyi; na Yoab siankaa dɔm no.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Na woyii Absalom de no too kwae mu hɔ amoa kɛse bi mu, na wɔboaboaa abokuw kɛse pa ano guu no so. Na Israel nyinaa guanguan kokɔɔ wɔn ntamadan mu.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Nso Absalom te ase no, osii nkae dum bi a ɛwɔ ɔhene bon mu fae, na ose: Minni ɔbabarima a wɔde no bɛkae me din. Na ɔde ne din too odum no, na wɔfrɛ no Absalom sɛnkyerɛnne besi nnɛ. Wɔka Absalom wu kyerɛ Dawid

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sadok ba Ahimaas kae sɛ: Ma mintu mmirika menkɔbɔ ɔhene kaseɛ pa yi, sɛ AWURADE abu atɛn ama no n’atamfo so.

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Na Yoab ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛnyɛ wo na wobɛyɛ kaseɛbɔfo nnɛ. Da bi na yɛ kaseɛbɔfo, na ɛnnɛ de, nkɔbɔ kaseɛ, na ɔhene ba atɔ.

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ka kyerɛɛ Kusni no sɛ: Kɔ na kɔka nea woahu kyerɛ ɔhene. Na Kusni no kotow Yoab, na otuu mmirika.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Sadok ba Ahimaas ka kyerɛɛ Yoab bio sɛ: Nea ɛbɛba mmra! Ma me nso mintu mmirika minni Kusni no akyi. Na Yoab se: Me ba, ɛdɛn nti na worebetu mmirika yi? Worennya kaseɛ a wobɛbɔ no mu hwee!

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Na ose: Nea ɛbɛba mmra! Metu mmirika makɔ! Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Tu mmirika kɔ ɛ! Ɛnna Ahimaas tuu mmirika faa nsunoa kwan so kotwaa Kusni no ho.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Na Dawid te kurow no apon abien no ntam. Na ɔwɛmfo no kɔɔ kurow pon no atifi, ɔfasu no so, na ɔmaa n’ani so hwɛe, na hwɛ, ɔbarima bi a ne nko de mmirika reba.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Na ɔwɛmfo no teɛɛm ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene. Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Sɛ ɛyɛ ɔno nko a, na kaseɛ bi wɔ n’anom. Na ɔde ba ara, na ɔbɛnee.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɛmfo no huu ɔbarima foforo sɛ ɔde mmirika reba; na ɔwɛmfo no teɛɛ mu kyerɛɛ ɔpon ano hwɛfo no sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔbarima bi nko de mmirika reba. Na ɔhene se: Ɔno nso yɛ kaseɛbɔfo.

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɛmfo no kae sɛ: Me de, mihu odikanfo no mmirikatu sɛ ɛte sɛ Sadok ba Ahimaas mmirikatu. Na ɔhene se: Onipa pa ni, na ɔde kaseɛ pa reba.

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Na Ahimaas teɛɛm ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Asomdwoe! Na ɔkotow ɔhene de n’anim butuw fam, na ɔkae sɛ: Nhyira nka AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn a wayi nnipa a wɔmaa wɔn nsa so hyɛɛ me wura ɔhene no ahyɛ wo nsa.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Aberante Absalom ho ye anaa? Na Ahimaas se: Yoab resoma ɔhene akoa bi ne w’akoa no, mihuu kitikiti kɛse bi na minnim dekode.

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene se: Sen gyina ha! Na ɔsen kogyinaa hɔ.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Kusni no bae; na Kusni no kae sɛ: Me wura ɔhene ntie kaseɛ, sɛ AWURADE abu atɛn ama wo nnɛ afi wɔn a wɔsɔre hyɛɛ wo no nyinaa so.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Kusni no sɛ: Aberante Absalom ho ye anaa? Na Kusni no buae sɛ: Ma me wura ɔhene atamfo ne wɔn a wɔsɔre hyɛ wo, pɛ wo bɔne no nyinaa nyɛ sɛ aberante no!

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ho popoe na ɔforo kɔɔ kurow pon no so pia mu, na osui. Na ɔrekɔ no, ɔkae sɛ: O Me ba Absalom, me ba, me ba Absalom! Ɛkaa me nko a, anka misii w’ananmu wui! Absalom, meba, me ba!

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔhene resu, na ɔretwa Absalom ho adwo.

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Na nkonimdi no dan ɔman no nyinaa nkɔmmɔdi da no, na ɔman no tee da no sɛ ɔhene yam rehyehye no ama ne ba.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no wiawiaa wɔn ho baa kurow no mu da no, sɛnea dɔm a woguan akono na wɔabɔ wɔn ho ahohora wiawia wɔn ho no.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kataa n’anim na ɔhene de nne kɛse teɛɛm sɛ: O me ba Absalom, O Absalom, me ba, me ba!

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Na Yoab baa ɔhene nkyɛn ofie, na ɔkae sɛ: Woahyɛ wo nkoa nyinaa a ɛnnɛ wɔagye wo kra ne wo mmammarima ne wo mmabea kra ne wo yerenom kra ne wo yefamnom kra no aniwu nnɛ,

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: efisɛ wodɔ w’atamfo na wotan w’adɔfo. Na woakyerɛ nnɛ sɛ asafohene ne nkoa nyɛ hwee mma wo; na nnɛ mahu sɛ, sɛ Absalom nyaa nkwa na yɛn nyinaa wuwui nnɛ a, anka wopɛ.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Na afei sɔre fi adi na kɔka abotɔyam asɛm kyerɛ wo nkoa. Na meka AWURADE sɛ, sɛ woamfi adi a, obiara rentena wo nkyɛn anadwo yi, na ɛno mmom bɛyɛ bɔne ama wo asen bɔne a aba wo so fi wo mmerantebere de abedu sesɛɛ no.

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene sɔre bɛtenaa kurow pon no mu. Na wɔka kyerɛɛ ɔman no nyinaa sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔhene te kurow pon no mu. Ɛnna ɔman no nyinaa baa ɔhene anim. Afei na Israelfo no nyinaa aguanguan, obiara kɔ n’ankasa fi. Dawid san kɔ Yerusalem

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Dawid tee nea Israel nyinaa aka no, ɔsoma kɔɔ asɔfo Sadok ne Abiatar nkyɛn sɛ: Monkɔka nkyerɛ Yuda mpanyimfo sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na motwentwɛn sɛ mobɛba abɛfa ɔhene asan akɔ ne fi mmere a ɔman no nsɛm nyinaa adu m’asom yi?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Me nuanom ne mo, me nnompe ne me honam ne mo, na ɛdɛn nti na motwentwɛn sɛ mobɛba abɛfa ɔhene asan akɔ?

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Na Amasa nso, monka nkyerɛ no sɛ: So ɛnyɛ me nnompe ne me honam ne wo? Sɛ woanyɛ dɔm so safohene m’anim nna nyinaa ansi Yoab ananmu a, Onyankopɔn nyɛ me sɛɛ na ɔnkɔ so nyɛ me sɛɛ!

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Na ɔkom Yuda mmarima nyinaa koma sɛ onipa biako de, na wɔsoma baa ɔhene nkyɛn sɛ: Wo ne wo nkoa nyinaa, monsan mmra.

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Na Benyaminni Gera ba Simei a ofi Bahurim no yɛɛ ntɛm ne Yuda mmarima no sian bae behyiaa ɔhene Dawid,

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Na w’akoa nim sɛ mayɛ bɔne, na hwɛ, me na madi Yosef fi nyinaa kan maba nnɛ sɛ meresian mabehyia me wura ɔhene.

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Na ɔkorow no twa kɔe sɛ wɔde rekɔfa ɔhene fifo, na wɔayɛ nea eye n’ani so. Na ɔhene twaa Yordan bae no, Gera ba Simei hwee fam n’anim. Dawid yi ne dɔ adi kyerɛ Simei

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Mma me wura mmmu amumɔyɛ nnto me so, na nkae nea w’akoa fom so yɛɛ no da a me wura ɔhene fii Yerusalem no, na ɔhene mmfa nnhyɛ ne komam.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Na Seruia ba Abisai buae sɛ: So eyi nti wɔrenkum Simei, sɛ wadome nea AWURADE asra no no?

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Na Dawid se: Dɛn na me ne mo Seruia mma wɔ yɛ, sɛ moyɛ me nnipa a wɔne me di asi nnɛ yi? So nnɛ wonkum obi Israel anaa? So minnim sɛ ɛnnɛ mene Israel so hene anaa?

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Simei sɛ: Wɔrenkum wo. Na ɔhene kaa no ntam.

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Na ose: Me wura ɔhene, m’akoa na ɔdaadaa me; na w’akoa kae sɛ: Mɛhyehyɛ afurum matena no so makɔ ɔhene nkyɛn, efisɛ w’akoa yɛ apakye.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Na obetwirii w’akoa maa me wura ɔhene. Na me wura ɔhene te sɛ Onyankopɔn bɔfo, enti yɛ nea eye w’ani so.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Na m’agya fi nyinaa nyɛ hwee sɛ owu mma ma me wura ɔhene, nanso wode w’akoa sii wɔn a wodidi wo pon so mu. Na asɛntrenee bɛn na mewɔ bio, nso dɛn na mede mɛteɛm mafrɛ ɔhene bio.

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woda so ka w’asɛm yi bio? Mise wo ne Siba nkɔkyɛ asase no mu.

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Na Mefiboset ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Sɛ me wura ɔhene de asomdwoe anya aba ne fi yi, ma ɔmfa ne nyinaa po. Dawid de Barsilai mfomso kyɛ no

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Na Gileadni Barsilai sian fii Rogelim bae na ɔne ɔhene twaa Yordan, sɛ ɔrekogya no Yordan agya.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Barsilai sɛ: Wo de, wo ne me ntwa nkɔ, na menhwɛ wo, me nkyɛn wɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Na Barsilai ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Me nkwa nna si ahe na me ne ɔhene mforo nkɔ Yerusalem yi?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Ma w’akoa nkogya ɔhene kwan Yordan agya nko ara. Na ɛdɛn nti na ɔhene de akatua yi betua me?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Ma w’akoa nsan nkowu ne kurom, m’agya ne me na damoa ho. Na hwɛ, ma w’akoa Kimham ne me wura ɔhene ntwa nkɔ, na yɛ no nea eye w’ani so.

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Kimham ne me ntwa nkɔ, na mɛyɛ no nea eye w’ani so; na biribiara a wobɛhwehwɛ me hɔ no, mɛyɛ mama wo.

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa twaa Yordan na ɔhene nso twae; na ɔhene few Barsilai ano na ɔsan kɔɔ fie. Yuda ne Israel nya akasakasa wɔ ɔhene ho

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene sen kɔɔ Gilgal, na Kimham ne no kɔe. Na Yuda man nyinaa de ɔhene sen kɔe, ne Israel man fa nso ka ne ho.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Israel mmarima nyinaa baa ɔhene nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na yɛn nuanom Yuda mmarima awia wo kɔ, na wɔde ɔhene ne ne fifo ne Dawid mmarima nyinaa a wɔka ne ho akotwa Yordan aba?

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yuda mmarima nyinaa buaa Israel mmarima sɛ: Efisɛ ɔhene yɛ yɛn busuani. Na ɛdɛn nti na asɛm yi nti mo bo huru yi? So yɛadi ɔhene ho biribi anaasɛ wakyɛ yɛn biribi?

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Israel mmarima no buaa Yuda mmarima no sɛ: Yɛwɔ kyɛfa du ɔhene mu, na Dawid mu nso yɛwɔ sen mo. Na adɛn nti na moammu yɛn? So ɛnyɛ yɛn na yedii kan kae sɛ wɔnkɔfa yɛn hene mmra? Na Yuda mmarima no ano yɛɛ den sen Israel mmarima no.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima huhuni bi wɔ hɔ a ne din de Seba a ɔyɛ Benyaminni Bikri ba. Na ɔhyɛn torobɛnto sɛ: Yenni kyɛfa bi Dawid mu, na yenni agyapade Yese ba no nkyɛn, O! Israel, obiara nkɔ ne fi.

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel mmarima nyinaa fii Dawid akyi kɔe kodii Bikri ba Seba akyi. Na Yuda mmarima de wɔbataa wɔn hene ho fi Yordan ho ara de baa Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Na Dawid baa ne fi Yerusalem. Na Dawid faa mmea du, mpenafo a ogyaw wɔn sɛ wɔnhwɛ ofie no, de wɔn koguu ɔhwɛ fi, na ɔbɔɔ wɔn akɔnhama, na wɔn ho de wankɔ. Na wɔtoo wɔn mu kosii wɔn wuda ma wodii wɔn nkwa bere te sɛ akunafo.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Amasa sɛ: Kohyiahyia Yuda mmarima brɛ me ha nnansa yi mu ara na wo nso bra bi.

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Na Amasa kɔe sɛ okohyiahyia Yuda; na ɔkyɛe sen bere a wɔhyɛɛ no no.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Abisai sɛ: Afei de, Bikri ba Seba bɛyɛ yɛn bɔne asen Absalom de no. Wo de, fa wo wura nkoa na tiw no, na wannya banbɔ mu nkurow bi amfa, na wanhaw yɛn anyi ne ho amfi yɛn anim.

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoab mmarima ne Keretifo ne Peletifo ne nnɔmmarima no nyinaa tu dii n’akyi; na wofii Yerusalem sɛ wɔretiw Bikri ba Seba.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Na woduu Gibeon bo kɛse no ho no, Amasa befii wɔn anim. Na Yoab de wabɔ n’akotade a ɔhyɛ no so, ɛso na ne nkrante abɔso wɔ, ɛsɛn n’asen so, boha mu; na ɔrefi adi no, ɛworɔw tɔɔ fam.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Na Yoab ka kyerɛɛ Amasa sɛ: Me nua wo ho ye? Na Yoab nsa nifa kosoo Amasa bogyesɛ mu sɛ ɔrefew n’ano.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Na Amasa anhwɛ nkrante a ekura Yoab nsam no, na ɔde wɔɔ ne yafunu mu tuee ne nsono guu fam, na wamfea no so, na owui. Na Yoab ne ne nua Abisai tiw Bikri ba Seba.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Na Yoab mmerante no mu bi gyinaa ne nkyɛn na ɔkae sɛ: Nea ɔpɛ Yoab asɛm ne nea ɔyɛ Dawid de no, ma onni Yoab akyi!

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Na Amasa yantayantam mogya mu ɔtempɔn no so. Na ɔbarima no hui sɛ dɔm no nyinaa gyinagyina hɔ no, ɔtwee Amasa fii ɔtempɔn no so kɔtoo wuram. Na sɛ ohui sɛ obiara a obedu no so no gyina nti, ɔde ntama kataa no so.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Na woyii no fii ɔtempɔn no so no wɔn nyinaa sen kodii Yoab akyi tiw Bikri ba Seba.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Na otwaa Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa mu koduu Abel ne Bet-maaka ne Bikrifo nyinaa so, na wohyia boaa ano ba bedii n’akyi nso.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔe kɔkaa no hyɛɛ Abel a ɛwɔ Bet-maaka, na wɔtotoo kurow no ho mpempe wɔ afasu no akyi. Na dɔm na wɔka Yoab ho nyinaa pempemee sɛ wɔredwiriw afasu no agu.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea nyansafo bi fi kurow no mu teɛɛm sɛ: Muntie! Muntie! Monka nkyerɛ Yoab sɛ ontwiw mmɛn ha na me ne no nkasa.

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Na otwiw bɛn no no, ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wone Yoab anaa? Na ose: Mene no. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Tie w’afenaa nsɛm. Na ose: Meretie.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Meyɛ wɔn a wɔpɛ asomdwoe ne nokware no mu biako. Wo de, worehwehwɛ asɛe Israel mu kurow ne ɔman no; na ɛdɛn nti na worebɛmene AWURADE agyapade?

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Na Yoab buae sɛ: Ɛmpare me, ɛmpare me sɛ mɛmene anaasɛ mɛsɛe.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Asɛm no nte sa, na ɔbarima bi a ofi Efraim bepɔw so a ne din de Bikri ba Seba na wama ne nsa so ahyɛ ɔhene Dawid. Munyi no nko mma, na mefi kurow no ho makɔ. Na ɔbea no ka kyerɛɛ Yoab sɛ: Hwɛ wɔbɛtow ne ti akyene afasu akyi ama wo.

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea no faa nyansa kwan so kɔɔ ɔman no nyinaa nkyɛn. Na wotwaa Bikri ba Seba ti tow kyenee Yoab. Na ɔhyɛn torobɛnto, na wofii kurow no ho bɔ petee kokɔɔ wɔn afi mu. Na Yoab san baa Yerusalem ɔhene nkyɛn. Dawid asomfo

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Nso Yoab na odi Israel dɔm nyinaa so, na Yoiada ba Benaia di Keretifo ne Peletifo so.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Na Adoram na ɔhwɛ ɔhyɛ adwuma tow so, na Ahilud ba Yosafat ne ɔsenkaefo.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Na Seia ne ɔkyerɛwfo, na Sadok ne Abiatar ne asɔfo.

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: Na Yairini Ira nso yɛ Dawid sɔfo.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene frɛɛ Gibeonfo no ka kyerɛɛ wɔn, nso Gibeonfo no mfi Israelfo mu na wɔyɛ Amorifo nkae no bi, nso Israelfo aka wɔn ntam, nanso Saul hwehwɛe sɛ okum wɔn, ne mmɔden a ɔbɔ maa Israel ne Yudafo no mu,

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Gibeonfo no sɛ: Dɛn na menyɛ memma mo? Na ɛdɛn na memfa mempata na moahyira AWURADE agyapade?

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Ɔbarima a ɔdwerɛw yɛn a otuu yɛn tiri so agyina sɛ wɔnsɛe yɛn na yɛannya Israel asase biara so antena no,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: ma wɔmfa ne mma mu mmarima baasɔn mma yɛn na yɛnsensɛn wɔn mma AWURADE wɔ Saul a AWURADE faa no no kurow Gibea mu. Na ɔhene se: Mɛma.

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ntam a ɛda wɔn ntam, na ɛda Dawid ne Saul ba Yonatan ntam no nti, ɔhene kyɛe Saul ba Yonatan ba Mefiboset so.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: na ɔde wɔn hyɛɛ Gibeonfo no nsa, na wɔsensɛn wɔn bepɔw no so AWURADE anim, na wɔn baasɔn no totɔe prɛko. Na wokunkum wɔn twabere nna a edi kan mu, atokotwa mfiase mu.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Na Aia babea Rispa faa atweaatam de trɛw ɔbotan no so fae fii twabere mfiase no kosii sɛ osu fi soro guguu wɔn so, na wamma wim nnomaa ammesisi wɔn so awia, na wuram mmoadoma nso amma wɔn so anadwo.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na Dawid kɔe kogyee Saul nnompe ne ne ba Yonatan nnompe Yabes-gileadfo nsam, na wɔn na wokowiae Bet-san abɔnten so, nea Filistifo de sensɛnee da a Filistifo kum Saul wɔ Gilboa no.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Na wosiee Saul ne ne ba Yonatan nnompe Benyamin asase so wɔ Sela, n’agya Kis da mu; na wɔyɛɛ nea ɔhene hyɛɛ wɔn nyinaa. Na ɛno akyi no, Onyankopɔn dom asase no. Filistifo akofo so nkonimdi

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Na ɔko bae bio wɔ Gat. Na ɔbarima tenten bi wɔ hɔ a ɔwɔ nsatea ne nansoa asia asia ma ano si aduonu anan, na ɔno nso yɛ abran no bi ba.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Nso Filistifo ne Israel dii ako bio. Na Dawid ne ne nkoa sian kɔe ne Filistifo no kɔkoe; na Dawid brɛe.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Na Yisbi-benob a ɔyɛ abran mma no mu bi a ne peaw duru kari kɔbere nnwetɛbona ahasa na ɔde nkrante foforo abɔ no kae sɛ ɔrebekum Dawid.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Na Seruia ba Abisai boaa no, na ɔbɔɔ Filistini no kum no. Ɛno na Dawid mmarima no kaa ntam sɛ: Wo ne yɛn mmfi nnkɔ ɔsa bio na wɔannum Israel kanea.

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Eyi akyi no wɔne Filistifo nyaa ɔko bio wɔ Gob. Ɛno mu na Husani Sibekai kum Saf a ɔyɛ abran mma no mu bi no.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na wɔne Filistifo nyaa ɔko bio wɔ Gob. Na Betlehemni Yaare-oregim ba Elhanan kum Gatni Goliat a ne peaw dua te sɛ ɔtamanwemfo nsadua.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Na ɔretwitwa Israel mpoa no, Dawid ne nua Simea ba Yonatan kum no.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Baanan yi yɛ Gat abran no bi mma, na wɔtotɔe Dawid ne ne nkoa nsam.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Ogyee me fii me tamfo nuɔdenfo ne wɔn a wokyi me nsam, efisɛ wɔsen me ahoɔden.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Na da a AWURADE yii Dawid n’atamfo nyinaa nsam ne Saul nsam no, ɔkaa dwom yi mu nsɛm kyerɛɛ AWURADE,

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Enti AWURADE, mɛkamfo wo amanaman mu, na mabɔ wo din mato ayeyi nnwom,

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: na ose: AWURADE, me botan ne m’abankɛse ne me gyefo,

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: me botantim Nyankopɔn a miguan metoa no; me kyɛm ne me nkwagye abɛn, m’abantenten ne me guankɔbea, m’agyenkwa a wugyee me fii akakabensɛm mu.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: AWURADE a woyi no ayɛ no na misu mefrɛ no, na wogye me m’atamfo nsam.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Na owu asorɔkye twaa me ho hyiae, na ɔsɛe asuasu woro yii me hu.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Asaman nhama twaa me ho kɔntɔnkrɔn, owu afiri behyiaa me.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: M’ahohia mu misu mefrɛɛ AWURADE, me Nyankopɔn na meteɛɛm mefrɛɛ no. Na ɔtee me nne n’asɔrefi, na me nteɛm duu n’asom.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Ɛnna asase hinhimii, na ɛwosowee, ɔsoro nnyinaso nso popoe, na ehinhimii, efisɛ ne bo ahuru.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Owusiw tu fii ne hwenem, na ogya fii n’anom hyew ade, na nnyansramma sɔe wɔ no mu.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Okuntun ɔsoro na odurui, na esum kabii wɔ ne nan ase.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Na ɔtenaa Kerub so tui, na wohuu no mframa ntaban so.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Na ɔde esum yɛɛ ne ho asese, nsu mmoaano, amununkum kusuu.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Ne ho haran mu na nnyansramma dɛwee.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: AWURADE boom fii soro, na ɔsorosoroni no ma wɔtee ne nne.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: Na ɔtotow agyan de bɔɔ wɔn petee, asraman na ɔde tan wɔn ani.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Na ɛpo mu aka yiyii adi, wiase nnyinaso ho daa hɔ. Ɛnam AWURADE ateɛteɛ so, efi ne hwene mu home hahyeehayee hahyeehayee mu.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Ɔteɛɛ ne nsa fii soro bɛfaa me, ɔtwee me fii nsu pii mu.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Wɔbɛtoaa me m’amanehunu da mu, na AWURADE bɛyɛɛ me akyigyina,

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: na oyii me kogyinaa nea ɛhɔ trɛw, ogyee me, efisɛ ɔpɛ m’asɛm.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: AWURADE tuaa me ka sɛ me trenee te, sɛ me nsa ho a afi te no na ɔdan maa me.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Na mehwɛɛ AWURADE akwan, na menyɛɛ bɔne mimfii me Nyankopɔn ho ɛ.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Na n’atemmude nyinaa wɔ m’ani so, na n’ahyɛde nso, mimfii ho ɛ.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Na mayɛ me ho pɛ mama no, na mahwɛ me ho so mafi m’amumɔyɛ ho.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dan maa me sɛ me trenee, sɛ m’ahotew a ɛda n’anim no te.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Adɔeyɛfo na wo ne no bedi no adɔe so, ɔbarima a odi mu na wo ne no bedi no mudi so.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Nea ɔtew ne ho na wobɛtew wo ho akyerɛ no, na ɔkɔntɔnkyefo de wubekyinkyim wo ho akyerɛ no.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Na ɔman a wohu amane no wugye wɔn, na w’ani sa ahantanfo na woabrɛ wɔn ase.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Na wo, AWURADE, wone me kanea, na AWURADE haran me sum mu.

english_verse: You help me defeat armies and capture cities.
translation_verse: Na wo na mede wo metow mehyɛ asafo so, mede me Nyankopɔn mihuruw metra ɔfasu.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn de, ne kwan yɛ pɛ, AWURADE asɛm mu tew, ɔyɛ ɔkyɛm ma wɔn a wɔde wɔn ho to no so nyinaa.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Na hena ne Nyame sɛ AWURADE nko? Na hena na ɔyɛ ɔbotan sɛ yɛn Nyankopɔn?

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn ne m’aban a ɛyɛ den, na ɔma me kwan yɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛɛ m’anan sɛ aforotebere de, na ɔma migyina me sorɔnsorɔmmea so.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Ɔkyerɛ me nsa akodi, na m’abasa akuntun kɔbere ta.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Na wode wo nkwagye kyɛm maa me, na w’asɛm tie ma meyɛɛ kɛse.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Wotrɛw m’anammɔn tutu mu wɔ m’ase na m’anan anwatiri.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Mitiw m’atamfo na mesɛee wɔn, na mansan de kosii sɛ mehyew wɔn,

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: na memenee wɔn na mebobɔɔ wɔn na wɔansɔre, na wɔtotɔe me nan ase.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Na wode ahoɔden bɔɔ me ho so maa akodi; wobrɛɛ wɔn a wɔsɔre hyɛɛ me no ase hyɛɛ m’ase.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Na womaa m’atamfo dan wɔn akyi kyerɛɛ me, wɔn a wokyi me no, na mesɛee wɔn.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Wɔhwɛe, na ogyefo bi nni hɔ, wɔhwɛɛ AWURADE, na wammua wɔn.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Na mepɛtɛw wɔn pasaa sɛ fam mfutuma, mitiatiaa wɔn so mewɔw wɔn sɛ mmorɔn so dɔte.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Wuyii me fii m’amanko mu, woahwɛ me sɛ meyɛ amanaman ti. Ɔman a minnim wɔn na ɛsom me.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Ananafo gurowee, na wɔde ahopopo fi wɔn aban mu bae.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: AWURADE te ase, na nhyira ne me botantim no. Na me nkwagye botan Nyankopɔn no, wɔmma no so.
