english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn na odii were maa me na ɔbrɛɛ aman ase hyɛɛ m’ase,

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: na oyii me fii m’atamfo nsam, na womaa me so fii wɔn a wɔsɔre hyɛɛ me no mu; wugyee me fii onuɔdenfo nsam.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: sɛ wone nea ɔma ne hene nkwagye so, na ɔyɛ nea wasra no no adɔe, Dawid ne n’asefo daa.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: AWURADE honhom nam me so kasa, na n’asɛm wɔ me tɛkrɛma so.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel Nyankopɔn akasa, me na Israel botan no kasa kyerɛɛ me. Nea odi nnipa so a ɔteɛ, nea odi so Onyankopɔn suro mu.

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbɛyɛ sɛ anɔpa hann, bere a owia repue, sɛ anɔpa a amununkum nni hɔ, sɛ owia gyigye ne osutɔ nti wura fifi fam.

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: So ɛnyɛ sɛ me fi te ne no Onyankopɔn anim? Na ɔne me ayɛ daa apam a wɔasiesie no ade nyinaa mu na etim hɔ. Na nea mepɛ ne nea mehwehwɛ nyinaa, so ɔremma ɛmfefɛw?

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Na ahuhufo de, wɔn nyinaa te sɛ nsɔe a wɔatow agu, na wɔmfa nsa nso mu.

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Na onipa a ɔka wɔn no de dade ne peaw dua mia, na wɔde gya bɛhyew wɔn dwerɛbee. Dawid nnɔmmarima ne wɔn nneyɛe (

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Ɔno na ɔsɔre kunkum Filistifo no kosii sɛ ne nsam gowee na ne nsa fam ne nkrante ho. Na AWURADE yɛɛ nkonim ade kɛse da no, na dɔm no dan kodii n’akyi sɛ wɔbɛfow ade nko.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Na onyaa anuonyam kɛse wɔ nnipa aduasa no mu, na odii wɔn so safohene, nanso wanto baasa a edi kan no.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Eyinom ne nnɔmmarima a Dawid wɔ no din. Tahkemonni Yoseb-basebet a odi akunini no mu titiriw. Ɔno na ɔmaa ne peaw so kunkum nnipa ahanwɔtwe prɛko.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Na nea odi n’akyi ne Ahohi ba Dodo ba Eleasar a ɔfra nnɔmmarima baasa a wɔka Dawid ho bere a wɔresopa Filistifo a wɔaboaboa wɔn ho ano rebɛko na Israel mmarima foro kɔe no mu.

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: Na ɔno de, ogyinaa asase no mfinimfini na ɔperee, na okum Filistifo no, na AWURADE yɛɛ nkonim ade kɛse.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Na atitiriw aduasa no mu baasa sian baa Dawid nkyɛn twabere wɔ Adulam bodan mu. Na Filistifo asafo bi abɔ nsra Refaim bon mu.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Nso ɛbere no mu na Dawid wɔ bepɔw so atenae no mu, na Filistifo bansifo wɔ Betlehem bere no mu.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Na ɛdɔɔ Dawid kɔn na ɔkaa sɛ: Hena na ɔbɛma me Betlehem asubura a ɛwɔ kurow pon ho no mu nsu manom?

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Na nnɔmmarima baasa no tew faa Filistifo nsra no mu kɔsaw Betlehem asubura a ɛwɔ kurow pon ho no mu nsu de brɛɛ Dawid. Nanso wampɛ sɛ ɔnom, na ohwie gu maa AWURADE,

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: na ose: Ɛmpare me, AWURADE, sɛ mɛyɛ eyi. So mennom mmarima a wɔde wɔn kra too wɔn nsam kɔe no mogya? Na wampɛ sɛ ɔnom. Eyi na nnɔmmarima baasa no yɛe.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Na Yehoiada ba Benaia yɛ ɔkofoni barima a ofi Kabseel, a ɔyɛɛ mmaninne. Okum Ariel mma baanu wɔ Moab; na ɔno nso sian kokum gyata, abura mu, sukyerɛma da bi;

english_verse: Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed
translation_verse: Na Yoab ne nua Seruia ba Abisai nso di baasa no mu titiriw. Ɔno na ohwinhwim ne peaw nnipa ahasa so kunkum wɔn, na ogyee din baasa no mu.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: na okum Misraimni barima hoɔfɛfo bi, na Misraimni no kura peaw ne nsam, na Benaia de poma sian kɔɔ ne nkyɛn, na ohuam Misraimni ankasa peaw fii ne nsam de kum no.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Arauna kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na me wura ɔhene ba n’akoa nkyɛn yi? Na Dawid se: Merebɛtɔ wo hɔ awiporowbea no, na masi afɔremuka mama AWURADE, na wɔasiw ɔhaw no kwan afi ɔman no so.

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: na wɔkɔɔ Gilead ne Kades a ɛwɔ Hitifo asase so ne Tatim-hodsi asase so, na wɔkɔɔ Dan fi hɔ kɔɔ Dan-yaan ne Sidon.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ ɔsahene Yoab a ɔka ne ho no sɛ: Kokyin Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa mu fi Dan kosi Beer-seba, na monkan ɔman no, na minhu ɔman no dodow.

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Nanso ɔhene asɛm no yɛɛ Yoab ne dɔm no mu asafohene no so den. Na Yoab ne dɔm no mu asafohene no fii ɔhene anim fii adi, sɛ wɔrekɔkan Israel man no.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Na wokotwaa Yordan, na wɔkɔsoɛɛ Aroer, kurow bi a ɛda Gad subon no mu a ɛkyerɛ Gad na ɛkɔ Yaser no,

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Na wokyin asase no nyinaa so, na asram akron ne adaduonu akyi no, wɔbaa Yerusalem,

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Na Arauna hwɛe no, ohuu ɔhene ne ne nkoa sɛ wɔreba ne nkyɛn. Na Arauna fii adi kɔkotow ɔhene de n’anim butuw fam.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Na Dawid huu ɔbɔfo a ɔresɛe ɔman no no, ɔka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Hwɛ, me na mayɛ bɔne, na me na mafom, na nguan yi de, dɛn na wɔayɛ? Ma wo nsa mmra me ne m’agya fi so.

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Na Dawid kan ɔman no saa no, ne koma bɔɔ no pan, na Dawid ka kyerɛɛ AWURADE sɛ: Nea mayɛ yi, mayɛ bɔne pa ara, na afei AWURADE, mesrɛ wo, ma w’akoa amumɔyɛ nsen nkɔ, na madi nkwaseasɛm sɛ!

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Na Dawid sɔree anɔpa no, AWURADE asɛm baa odiyifo Gad, Dawid dehufo no nkyɛn sɛ:

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Na Gad baa Dawid nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So ɔkɔm mmra w’asase so mfe asɔn, anaasɛ wubeguan w’atamfo a wɔtaa wo anim asram abiɛsa, anaasɛ ɔyaredɔm mmra w’asase so nnansa? Afei hwɛ, na hu asɛm ko a memfa mensan menkɔma nea ɔsomaa me no.

english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Dawid ka kyerɛɛ Gad sɛ: Me ho hia me sɛ! Ma yɛnhwe AWURADE nsam ɛ, na ne mmɔborohunu dɔɔso; na nnipa nsam na wɔmmma mennhwe.

english_verse: So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over,
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔfo no teɛɛ ne nsa Yerusalem so sɛ ɔresɛe no no, AWURADE nuu ne ho bɔne no ho, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔbɔfo a ɔresɛe ɔman no sɛ: Adɔɔso afei, pono wo nsa. Na AWURADE bɔfo no adu Yebusini Arauna awiporowbea ho.

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Na Arauna ka kyerɛɛ Dawid sɛ: Ma me wura ɔhene mfa na ɔmmɔ afɔre sɛnea eye n’ani so. Hwɛ, ɔhyew afɔrebɔ nantwi ne porow nteaseɛnam ne anantwi no adwumayɛ nnua a wɔde bɛyɛ nnyina ni.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Ɔhene, Arauna de ne nyinaa ma ɔhene. Na Arauna ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ani nsɔ wo.

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Arauna sɛ: Daabi, na ɔtɔ na mɛtɔ no wo hɔ, sɛ ne bo te, na meremfa ade biara a ɛnsom me bo memmɔ AWURADE me Nyankopɔn ɔhyew afɔre. Na Dawid tɔɔ awiporowbea no ne anantwi no maa dwetɛ nnwetɛbona aduonum.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_verse: Na Dawid sii afɔremuka maa AWURADE wɔ hɔ na ɔbɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre. Na AWURADE gyee mpata no maa asase no, na wosiw ɔhaw no kwan fii Israel so.

english_verse: King David was now an old man, and he always felt cold, even under a lot of blankets.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Dawid abɔ akora na wadi nna pii. Na sɛ wɔde ntama kata no ho mpo a, ne ho nyɛ no hyew.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.”
translation_verse: Enti ne nkoa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ma wɔnhwehwɛ ababaa a ɔyɛ ɔbaabun bi mmrɛ me wura ɔhene, na ommegyina ɔhene anim nyɛ wo hwɛfo, na ɔnna wo kokom na me wura ɔhene nnya ahoɔhyew.

english_verse: They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her. Adonijah Tries To Become King
translation_verse: Na ababaa no ho yɛ fɛ pa ara, na ɔyɛɛ ɔhene hwɛfo na ɔsom no. Nanso ɔhene ne no anna. Adonigya pere ahengua no

english_verse: Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired
translation_verse: Nanso n’agya anka asɛm a ɛyɛ yaw bi ankyerɛ no da sɛ: Adɛn na woyɛ sɛɛ yi? Na ɔno nso yɛ ɔhoɔfɛfo, na ɔno na wɔwoo no dii Absalom akyi.

english_verse: Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help.
translation_verse: Na ɔne Seruia ba Yoab ne Ɔsɔfo Abiatar na edi atirimsɛm, na wodii Adonigya akyi boaa no.

english_verse: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
translation_verse: Na Ɔsɔfo Sadok ne Yoiada ba Benaia ne odiyifo Natan ne Simei ne Rei ne Dawid nnɔmmarima no de, wonni Adonigya fam.

english_verse: Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves.
translation_verse: Na Adonigya kunkum nguan ne anantwi ne anantwi a wɔadɔ srade, Sohelet bo a ɛwɔ En-rogel ho no so, na ohyiahyiaa ne nuanom ahenemma no nyinaa ne Yuda mmarima a wɔyɛ ɔhene nkoa no nyinaa.

english_verse: But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
translation_verse: Na odiyifo Natan ne Benaia ne nnɔmmarima no ne ne nua Solomon de, wanhyia wɔn.

english_verse: When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother: Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Natan ka kyerɛɛ Solomon ne na Batseba sɛ: So wontee sɛ Hagit ba Adonigya di hene, na yɛn wura Dawid nnim?

english_verse: You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you.
translation_verse: Afei bra ma yentu agyina, na gye wo kra ne wo ba Solomon kra nkwa.

english_verse: Go say to David, “You promised me that Solomon would be the next king. So why is Adonijah now king?”
translation_verse: Kɔ ɔhene Dawid nkyɛn, na ka kyerɛ no sɛ: So ɛnyɛ wo, me wura ɔhene, na wokaa w’afenaa ntam sɛ: Wo ba Solomon na obedi m’ade, na ɔno na ɔbɛtena m’agua so? Na adɛn nti na Adonigya di hene yi?

english_verse: While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
translation_verse: Hwɛ, wo ne ɔhene da so rekasa wɔ hɔ no, me nso medi w’akyi maba, na mabɛfoa wo nsɛmmoa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in
translation_verse: Na Batseba kɔɔ ɔhene nkyɛn pia mu; na ɔhene abɔ akora pa ara, na Sunamni Abisag som ɔhene.

english_verse: and bowed down. “What can I do for you?” David asked.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Batseba bɔɔ ne mu ase kotow ɔhene. Na ɔhene bisaa no sɛ: Dɛn na ɛyɛ wo?

english_verse: Bathsheba answered: Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king.
translation_verse: Na obuaa no sɛ: Me wura, wo na wokaa AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ntam kyerɛɛ w’abaawa sɛ: Wo ba Solomon na obedi m’ade, na ɔno na ɔbɛtena m’agua so.

english_verse: But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, Adonigya na odi hene yi; nanso me wura ɔhene, wunnim.

english_verse: He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
translation_verse: Na wakunkum anantwi ne nyɛmmoa ne nguan bebree, na wahyiahyia ahenemma nyinaa ne ɔsɔfo Abiatar ne ɔsahene Yoab, na w’akoa Solomon de, wanhyia no.

english_verse: Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king.
translation_verse: Na wo, me wura ɔhene, Israel nyinaa ani da wo so sɛ, kyerɛ wɔn nea ɔbɛtena me wura ɔhene agua no so ne wu akyi.

english_verse: If you don't, they will say that Solomon and I have rebelled. They will treat us like criminals and kill us as soon as you die.
translation_verse: Anyɛ saa a, me wura ɔhene bɛkɔ n’agyanom nkyɛn asaman no, wobebu me ne me ba Solomon nnebɔneyɛfo.

english_verse: Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Hwɛ, odiyifo Natan ni. Na oduu ɔhene anim no, ɔkotow ɔhene de n’anim butuw fam.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king?
translation_verse: Na Natan kae sɛ: Me wura ɔhene, wo na wuse: Adonigya nni w’ade na ɔno na ɔntena w’agua so, anaa?

english_verse: Earlier today, he sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. He invited the army commanders, Abiathar, and all your sons to be there. They are already eating and drinking and shouting, “Long live King Adonijah!”
translation_verse: Na ɛnnɛ wasian kɔ, na wakokum anantwinini, ne anantwi a wɔadɔ srade, ne nguan bebree, na wahyia ahenemma nyinaa ne asafohene ne ɔsɔfo Abiatar, na hwɛ, wɔredidi na wɔrenom n’anim, na wɔka sɛ: Ɔhene Adonigya tiri nkwa!

english_verse: But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon.
translation_verse: Na me, w’akoa ne ɔsɔfo Sadok ne Yoiada ba Benaia ne w’akoa Solomon de, wanhyia yɛn.

english_verse: Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king? Solomon Becomes King
translation_verse: So me wura ɔhene nkyɛn na asɛm yi fi, na woamma w’akoa anhu nea ɔbɛtena me wura ɔhene wu akyi agua no so?

english_verse: David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene Dawid buae sɛ: Momfrɛ Batseba mma me. Na ɔbaa ɔhene anim begyinaa hɔ.

english_verse: Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
translation_verse: sɛnea mekaa AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn ntam mekyerɛɛ wo sɛ: Wo ba Solomon na obedi m’ade, na ɔno na ɔbɛtena m’agua so asi m’ananmu no, saa ara na mɛyɛ nnɛ da yi.

english_verse: Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Batseba bɔɔ ne mu ase de n’anim butuw fam kotow ɔhene kae sɛ: Me wura ɔhene nnya nkwa daa! Wɔsra Solomon si no hene

english_verse: Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.” When they arrived,
translation_verse: Na Ɔhene Dawid kae sɛ: Momfrɛ ɔsɔfo Sadok ne odiyifo Natan ne Yoiada ba Benaia mma me. Na wɔbaa ɔhene anim.

english_verse: he told them: Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Momfa mo wura nkoa nka mo ho, na momfa me ba Solomon ntena m’afurumpɔnkɔ so, na momfa no nsian nkɔ Gihon.

english_verse: When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Sadok ne odiyifo Natan nsra no mfa no nsi Israel so hene wɔ hɔ, na monhyɛn torobɛnto sɛ: Ɔhene Solomon tiri nkwa!

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Na momforo nni n’akyi, na ɔmmra mmɛtena m’agua so, na ɔno na onni m’ade, na ɔno na mahyɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ Israel ne Yuda so panyin.

english_verse: Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoiada ba Benaia buaa ɔhene sɛ: Amen! Saa ara nso na AWURADE, me wura ɔhene Nyankopɔn, nka.

english_verse: The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
translation_verse: Sɛnea AWURADE ne me wura ɔhene tenae no, saa ara nso na ɔne Solomon ntena, na ɔmma n’agua nso nsen me wura ɔhene Dawid agua no.

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Sadok ne odiyifo Natan ne Yoiada ba Benaia ne Keretifo ne Peletifo sian kɔe, na wɔde Solomon tenaa ɔhene afurumpɔnkɔ so, na wɔde no kɔɔ Gihon.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Sadok faa ngo abɛn fii ntamadan no mu de bɛsraa Solomon. Na wɔhyɛn torobɛnto, na ɔman no nyinaa kae sɛ: Ɔhene Solomon tiri nkwa!

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Na ɔman no nyinaa foro dii n’akyi bae, na ɔman no hyenhyɛn mmɔtɔwa, na wɔn ani gyee kɛse, na wɔn gyegyeegye no reyɛ ama asase mu apae.

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Na Adonigya ne wɔn a wahyia wɔn a wɔne no wɔ hɔ no nyinaa tee; na wɔawie adidi; na Yoab tee torobɛnto no nka no, ɔkae sɛ: Kurow no mu hooyɛ a yɛte yi ase ne dɛn?

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Na ɔda so rekasa no, hwɛ, ɔsɔfo Abiatar ba Yonatan bae; na Adonigya kae sɛ: Bra, na woyɛ ɔbarima a wutumi, na wukura kaseɛ pa.

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan bua ka kyerɛɛ Adonigya sɛ: Ampa, yɛn wura ɔhene Dawid de Solomon asi hene.

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: na ɔsɔfo Sadok ne odiyifo Natan asra no de no asi hene Gihon, na wɔde anigye de no aforo afi hɔ aba, na kurow no mu ayɛ hoo: Ɛno ne gyegyeegye a motee no.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Nso Solomon te ahenni agua no so.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Nanso ɔhene nkoa aba abehyira yɛn wura ɔhene Dawid sɛ: Onyankopɔn mma Solomon din nyɛ kɛse nsen wo din, na ɔmma n’agua nso nsen w’agua. Na ɔhene abɔ ne mu ase ne nnae so;

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: nanso sɛ ɔhene kae ni: Nhyira ne AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn a wama obi atena m’agua so nnɛ yi, na m’aniwa ahu.

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Ɛnna nnipa a Adonigya ahyia wɔn no nyinaa bobɔɔ piriw, na wɔsɔresɔree, na obiara sii ne kwan so kɔe.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ Solomon sɛ: Hwɛ, Adonigya suro ɔhene Solomon, na hwɛ, wakosuso afɔremuka abɛn mu sɛ: Ɔhene Solomon nka me ntam nnɛ, sɛ ɔremfa nkrante nkum n’akoa.

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Na Solomon kae sɛ: Sɛ ɔdan onipa a ɔsɛ a, ne nwi biako rentɔ fam; na sɛ wohu bɔne wɔ no mu a, obewu.

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon soma ma wɔkɔfaa no fii afɔremuka no ho sian bae. Na ɔbae bɛkotow ɔhene Solomon, na Solomon ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ wo fi.

english_verse: Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
translation_verse: Afei Dawid nna bɛnee sɛ obewu, na ɔhyɛɛ ne ba Solomon sɛ:

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: Me de, merekɔ asase sofo nyinaa kwan: Enti yɛ den na yɛ ɔbarima.

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ AWURADE wo Nyankopɔn ahyɛde, sɛ wobɛnantew n’akwan so, sɛ wubedi n’ahyɛde, ne mmara nsɛm ne n’atemmude ne n’adansesɛm so, sɛnea wɔakyerɛw Mose mmara mu, na woadi yiye nea woyɛ nyinaa mu, baabiara a wobɛkɔ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ama n’asɛm a ɔkae me ho no atim sɛ: Wo mma hwɛ wɔn kwan sɛ wɔbɛnantew m’anim nokware mu, wɔn koma nyinaa ne wɔn kra nyinaa mu a, ɛnne ose Israel agua so barima remmɔ wo.

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: Nanso wo ara wunim nea Senuia ba Yoab yɛɛ me, nea ɔyɛɛ Israel asahene baanu, Ner ba Abner ne Yeter ba Amasa, a odii wɔn awu na ɔkaa ɔsa mu mogya gui asomdwoe bere mu, na ɔde ɔsa mu mogya kekaa n’abɔso a ɛbɔ n’asen ne ne mpaboa a ɛhyɛ ne nan ho no.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Enti di no nyansa so, na mma ne dwen mmfa asomdwoe mu nnsian nnkɔ asaman.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, Benyaminni Gera ba Simei a ofi Bahurim na ɔwɔ wo nkyɛn yi, ɔno na ɔdomee me nnome dennen da a mekɔɔ Mahanaim no. Nanso osian behyiaa me Yordan ho, na mekaa no AWURADE sɛ meremfa nkrante minkum no.

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Na afei de, mma ne ho nnyɛ tɔtorɔtɔɔ, na woyɛ ɔba nyansafo, na wubehu ade a wobɛyɛ no, na woama ne dwen nam mogya mu asian akɔ asaman.

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Simei sɔre hyehyɛɛ n’afurumpɔnkɔ, na osiim kɔɔ Gat, Akis nkyɛn sɛ ɔrekɔhwehwɛ ne nkoa no; na Simei kɔe kɔfaa ne nkoa no fii Gat bae.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: na wɔn mogya nsan mmebua Yoab atifi ne n’asefo atifi nkosi daa, na Dawid ne n’asefo ne ne fi ne n’agua nnya AWURADE nkyɛn asomdwoe daa.

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Na Solomon tenaa n’agya Dawid agua so, na n’ahenni timii pintinn pa. Solomon nneyɛe bi

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Na Hagit ba Adonigya baa Solomon ne na Batseba nkyɛn. Na obisaa no sɛ: So asomdwoe so na woba yi? Na ose: Asomdwoe so.

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Mewɔ asɛm bi meka kyerɛ wo. Na ose: Ka ɛ!

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Wo ara wunim sɛ anka ahenni no yɛ me dea, na me so na Israel nyinaa de wɔn ani toe sɛ medi hene, nanso ahenni no danee, na akɔyɛ me nua de; na efi AWURADE na ɛkɔyɛɛ ne de.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Na afei ade biako pɛ na merebisa wɔ wo hɔ, na nkame me. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kasa ɛ!

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Mesrɛ wo, ka kyerɛ ɔhene Solomon, na ɔrenkame wo, na ɔmfa Sunamni Abisag mma me aware.

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Na Batseba kae sɛ: Yoo, mɛka makyerɛ ɔhene mama wo.

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Batseba baa ɔhene Solomon nkyɛn sɛ ɔne no rebɛkasa ama Adonigya. Na ɔhene sɔre kohyiaa no na ɔkotow no, na ɔtenaa n’agua so; na wɔde agua sii hɔ maa ɔhene ne na, na ɔtenaa ne nifa so.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ade ketewa bi na merebebisa wo hɔ, na nkame me. Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Awo, bisa, na merenkame wo.

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Na ose: Ma wɔmfa Sunamni Abisag mma wo nua Adonigya aware.

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon bua ka kyerɛɛ ne na sɛ: Na adɛn nti na wubisa Sunamni Abisag ama Adonigya? Bisa ahenni no nso ma no, na ɔno ne me nua a ɔsen me panyin, bisa ma no ne ɔsɔfo Abiatar ne Seruia ba Yoab.

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene Solomon kaa AWURADE ntam sɛ: Onyankopɔn nyɛ me sɛɛ na ɔnkɔ so sa, sɛ Adonigya aka asɛm yi ahyɛ n’ankasa ne kra.

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Na afei, sɛ AWURADE a wama matim na ɔde me atena m’agya Dawid agua so na wakyekye ofi ama me sɛnea ɔkae no te ase yi, ɛnnɛ ara wobekum Adonigya.

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon somaa Yoiada ba Benaia ma ɔkɔbɔɔ no ma owui.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Abiatar nso, ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ Anatot, w’ankasa asase so, na wosɛ owu; nanso ɛnnɛ yi de, merenkum wo, efisɛ woasoa AWURADE Nyankopɔn adaka m’agya Dawid anim, na wuhuu amane a m’agya hui no nyinaa nso bi.

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Saa na Solomon tuu Abiatar sɛ onnni AWURADE sɔfo, sɛ ɔbɛma AWURADE asɛm a ɔkae Eli fi ho wɔ Silo no aba mu.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Na asɛm no duu Yoab nkyɛn; nso na Yoab adan akodi Adonigya akyi, na Absalom akyi de, wannan ankodi; na Yoab guan kɔɔ AWURADE ntamadan ho kosusoo afɔremuka abɛn mu.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ ɔhene Solomon sɛ: Yoab aguan akɔ AWURADE ntamadan ho, na hwɛ, ɔwɔ afɔremuka no ho. Na Solomon somaa Yoiada ba Benaia sɛ: Kɔ kɔbɔ no ade.

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Na Benaia kɔɔ AWURADE ntamadan no ho kɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔhene se: Fi adi! Na ose: Dabi, na ɛha na mewu. Na Benaia san bɛka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Sɛnea Yoab aka ni, sɛnea wabua me ni.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE mma ne mogya mmua n’atifi, sɛ okunkum mmarima baanu a wɔteɛ na woye sen no, na ɔde nkrante dii wɔn awu: Ner ba Abner, Israel sahene, ne Yeter ba Amasa, Yuda sahene no, a m’agya Dawid nnim ho bi;

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Na Yoiada ba Benaia foro kɔe kɔbɔɔ no kum no; na wosiee no ne fi wɔ sare so.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Na ɔhene de Yoiada ba Benaia sii n’ananmu dii dɔm no so, na ɔsɔfo Sadok nso, ɔhene de no sii Abiatar ananmu.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Na ɔhene soma kohyiaa Simei bae na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Si dan wɔ Yerusalem, na tena hɔ, na mfi hɔ nkɔ baabiara.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Na da a wubefi adi akotwa Kidron subon no, hu sɛ owu na wubewu, na wo mogya bebua w’atifi.

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Na Simei ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene sɛ: Eye, sɛnea me wura ɔhene aka no, saa ara na w’akoa bɛyɛ. Na Simei tenaa Yerusalem nna pii.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Na mfe abiɛsa akyi no, Simei nkoa baanu guan kɔɔ Gat hene Maaka ba Akis nkyɛn, na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Simei sɛ: Hwɛ, wo nkoa no wɔ Gat.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Solomon sɛ: Simei afi Yerusalem akɔ Gat, na wasan aba.

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Na ɔhene soma kɔfrɛɛ Simei sɛ: So manka wo AWURADE ntam manni wo adanse sɛ da a wubefi adi akɔ baabiara no, hu sɛ owu na wubewu? Na woka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Nea woka no ye, mate.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na woanni AWURADE ntam ne mmara a mehyɛɛ wo no so?

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ Simei sɛ: Wo ara wunim, wo koma mu, bɔne a wode yɛɛ m’agya Dawid no nyinaa, na AWURADE adan wo bɔne no agu w’atifi.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Na nhyira bɛka ɔhene Solomon, na Dawid agua betim AWURADE anim akosi daa.

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene hyɛɛ Yoiada ba Benaia, na ofii adi kɔbɔɔ no ma owui. Na ahenni no timii Solomon nsam.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Nanso ɔman no bɔɔ afɔre sorɔnsorɔmmea ara, efisɛ ɛde besi saa bere no na wonsii ɔdan bi mmaa AWURADE din ɛ.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Nanso nea wummisae no mama wo, ahonya ne anuonyam a ahene mu biara rento wo wo nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Na Solomon nam n’agya Dawid ahyɛde no mu dɔ AWURADE, nanso ɔbɔ afɔre na ɔhyew aduhuam sorɔnsorɔmmea no so.

english_verse: The most important shrine was in Gibeon, and Solomon had offered more than
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kɔɔ Gibeon sɛ ɔkɔbɔ afɔre, efisɛ ɛhɔ ne afɔrebɔbea kɛse a agye din. Solomon bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre apem wɔ afɔremuka no so. Solomon mpaebɔ

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yii ne ho adi kyerɛɛ Solomon anadwo dae mu wɔ Gibeon, na Onyankopɔn kae sɛ: Srɛ nea memma wo.

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Na Solomon se: Wo na woyɛɛ w’akoa, m’agya Dawid, adɔe kɛse, sɛnea ɔnantew w’anim nokware ne trenee mu ne wo ho komam teeyɛ mu, na wode adɔe kɛse yi asie ama no, na woama no ɔba a ɔte n’agua so sɛ ɛte nnɛ yi.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Na afei, AWURADE me Nyankopɔn, wo na woasi w’akoa ɔhene asi m’agya Dawid ananmu, na me de, meyɛ abofra ketewa, minnim adifi ne emuba.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Na w’akoa wɔ wo man a woapaw wɔn no mu, ɔman kɛse a wɔn dodow nti wontumi nkan wɔn mmu wɔn ano.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Enti ma w’akoa koma a etie, na memfa mimmu wo man atɛn, na minhu papa ne bɔne mu, na hena na obetumi abu ɔman duruduru yi atɛn?

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Esiane sɛ wubisaa asɛm yi, na woammisa nna dodo amfa, na woammisa ahonyade amfa, nanso woammisa w’atamfo kra, na wubisa nhumu, sɛ wode betie atemmu yi,

english_verse: So I'll make you wiser than anyone who has ever lived or ever will live.
translation_verse: hwɛ, mayɛ sɛ w’asɛm no se. Hwɛ, mama wo nyansa ne nhumu koma a obiara a odii w’anim nte sɛ wo, na w’akyi nso obi rensɔre a ɔsɛ wo.

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wonantew m’akwan mu na wudi m’ahyɛde ne me mmara nsɛm so sɛnea w’agya Dawid nantewee no a, mɛma wo nna aware.

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Na Solomon nyanee, na hwɛ, ɛyɛ ɔdae. Na ɔbaa Yerusalem, na obegyinaa AWURADE apam adaka no anim, na ɔbɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre, na ɔtow ne nkoa nyinaa pon. Solomon atemmu bi

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Ɛbere no mu no, mmea nguaman baanu bi baa ɔhene nkyɛn begyinaa n’anim.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Na ɔbea biako kae sɛ: Me wura, mepa wo kyɛw, me ne ɔbea yi te fi koro mu, na mewoo ɔba wɔ ne nkyɛn ofie hɔ.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea yi ba no wui anadwo, efisɛ ɔdaa no so.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔree ɔdasu mu bɛfaa me ba no wɔ me nkyɛn, nso na w’afenaa ada, na ɔde no too ne kokom, na ɔde ne ba a wawu no bɛtoo me kokom.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Na mesɔree anɔpa sɛ merema me ba nufu no, na hwɛ, wawu. Na mifeefee no anɔpa no, na hwɛ, ɛnyɛ me ba a mewoo no nen.

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Na ɔbea biako no se: Dabi, na me ba ne onikanfo no, na wo ba ne owufo no. Na oyi se: Dabi, na wo ba ne owufo no, na me ba ne ɔteasefo no. Na wɔkasakasae ɔhene anim hɔ.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Mommrɛ me nkrante. Na wɔde nkrante baa ɔhene anim.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene kae sɛ: Monkyɛ ɔba onikanfo no mu abien, na momfa ɔfa mma obiako, na momfa ɔfa mma obiako.

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbea a ne ba ne onikanfo no ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene, efisɛ ne yam hyehye no ne ba no ho sɛ: Me wura, mepa wo kyɛw, momfa ɔba onikanfo no mma no, na okum de, munnkum no! Na oyi se: Mma ɔnnyɛ me de, nso ɔnnyɛ wo de, monkyɛ mu!

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene buae sɛ: Momfa ɔba onikanfo no mma ɔno, na okum de wonnkum no, ɔne ne na.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Na Israel nyinaa tee atɛn a ɔhene bui no, wosuroo ɔhene anim, efisɛ wohui sɛ Onyankopɔn nyansa wɔ no mu a ɔde bu atɛn.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Na Solomon wɔ tow sohwɛfo dumien Israel nyinaa so a wɔhwɛ ɔhene ne ne fi aduan so; afirihyia mu ɛtɔ obiako so ɔsram biako sɛ ɔma aduan.

english_verse: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Wɔn din ni: Hur ba wɔ Efraim bepɔw so;

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: Deker ba wɔ Makas ne Saalbim ne Bet-semes ne Elon-bet-hanan;

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: Abinadab ba wɔ Nafat-dor nyinaa ɔwaree Solomon babea Tafat.

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Geber ba wɔ Ramot-gilead, ne de ne Manase ba Yair atenae a ɛwɔ Gilead no, ne de nso ne Argob asase a ɛwɔ Basan, nkurow akɛse aduosia a ɛho wɔ afasu ne kɔbere adaban;

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: Ahimaas wɔ Naftali ɔno nso faa Solomon ba Basmat waree;

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Uri ba Geber wɔ Gilead asase so, Amorifo hene Sihon ne Basan hene Og asase so, na tow sohwɛfo biako na ɔwɔ asase no so. Solomon ahenni nkɔso

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Na Solomon dii ahenni nyinaa so fi asubɔnten Eufrate ano kosi Filistifo asase so ne Misraim hye so. Wɔde ayɛyɛde ba na wɔsom Solomon ne nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him.
translation_verse: Na odi asubɔnten no agya ha ahene a wɔwɔ asubɔnten no fa ha nyinaa so tumi fi Tifsa bedu Gasa, na onyaa ɔmannwoe n’afa nyinaa hyiae.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Na Yuda ne Israel tenaa ase dwoodwoo wɔn bobe ne wɔn borɔdɔma ase mmiako mmiako, efi Dan kosi Beer-seba, Solomon nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,
translation_verse: Na tow sohwɛfo no hwɛɛ aduan so maa ɔhene Solomon ne wɔn a wɔbaa ɔhene Solomon pon ho nyinaa, wɔn sram so mmiako mmiako; wɔmma hwee nka.

english_verse: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn maa Solomon nyansa ne nhumu bebree pa, ne adwene a emu trɛw sɛ mpoano nwea.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Na onim nyansa sen nnipa nyinaa, ɔsen Esrani Etan ne Heman ne Kalkol ne Darda a wɔyɛ Mahol mma no, na ne din hyetaa amanaman nyinaa mu hyiae.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
translation_verse: Na ɔkasae nnua ho fi kyeneduru a ɛwɔ Lebanon so kosii adwerɛ a efifi ɔfasu mu so, na ɔkaa mmoa ne nnomaa ne wɔn a wɔwea ne mpataa ho nsɛm.

english_verse: Kings all over the world heard about Solomon's wisdom and sent people to listen to him teach.
translation_verse: Na amanaman nyinaa mu bi bae sɛ wobetie Solomon nyansa, wofi asase so ahene a wɔtee ne nyansa no nyinaa nkyɛn bae.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre had always been friends with Solomon's father David. When Hiram learned that Solomon was king, he sent some of his officials to meet with Solomon.
translation_verse: Na Tiro hene Hiram somaa ne nkoa baa Solomon nkyɛn; efisɛ wate sɛ ɔno na wɔasra no asi no hene n’agya ananmu; efisɛ Hiram dɔɔ Dawid daa.

english_verse: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
translation_verse: Na hwɛ, mise merebesi ɔdan mama AWURADE me Nyankopɔn din, sɛnea AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ m’agya Dawid no sɛ: Wo ba a mede no mesi w’ananmu matena w’agua so no, ɔno na obesi ɔdan ama me din.

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: Na afei hyɛ na wɔntow nkyeneduru mfi Lebanon mma me, na me nkoa bɛba abɛka wo nkoa ho, na mede wo nkoa apaade mɛma wo, sɛnea wobɛka nyinaa; na wo ara wunim sɛ obi nni yɛn mu a onim nnuatow sɛ Sidonfo.

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Na Hiram tee Solomon nsɛm no, n’ani gyei sɛ, na ɔkae sɛ: Nhyira nka AWURADE nnɛ, sɛ wama Dawid ɔba nyansafo de no asi ɔman kɛse yi so.

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Na Hiram soma baa Solomon nkyɛn sɛ: Mate nea enti a wosoma baa me nkyɛn no; me de, mɛyɛ nea wopɛ nyinaa nkyeneduru nnua ne ɔpopaw nnua fam.

english_verse: My workers will carry them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea. They will tie the logs together and float them along the coast to wherever you want them. Then they will untie the logs, and your workers can take them from there. To pay for the logs, you can provide the grain I need for my household.
translation_verse: Me nkoa de befi Lebanon asian aba mpoano, na makyekye no ntɛnani ɛpo so mabedu nea wobɛma wɔaka akyerɛ me no, na masansan hɔ, na wo nso woama wɔabɛfa akɔ. Na wo nso yɛ nea mepɛ ma me, sɛ wobɛma me fi aduan.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa Solomon nyansa sɛnea ɔhyɛɛ no ase no; na ɔmannwoe daa Hiram ne Solomon ntam, na wɔn baanu pamee.

english_verse: and he put Adoniram in charge of these workers. Solomon divided them into three groups of
translation_verse: Na ɔsomaa wɔn Lebanon so, nnipa ɔpedu daa ɔsram ma wodii no nnyigye, wodi ɔsram Lebanon, na wodi asram abien ofie, na Adoniram na odi tow adwuma no so.

english_verse: He ordered the workers to cut and shape large blocks of good stone for the foundation of the temple.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene hyɛe ma wɔpaee abo akɛse, abo a ne bo yɛ den, sɛ wɔde bɛhyɛ ɔdan no ase, abo a wɔasinsen.

english_verse: Solomon's and Hiram's men worked with men from the city of Gebal, and together they got the stones and logs ready for the temple.
translation_verse: Na Solomon abantofo ne Hiram abantofo ne Gebalfo no sinsenee, na wosiesiee nnua ne abo sɛ wɔde besi ɔdan no.

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ ɔdan no ho mfɛnsere a emu ahunaniankansa tintim mu.

english_verse: Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room.
translation_verse: Na ɔde kerubim no sisii akyiri dan no mu, na kerubim no trɛtrɛw wɔn ntaban mu, na obiako ntaban ka ɔfasu, na obiako ntaban ka ɔfasu biako no nso, na wɔn ntaban no hyia ɔdan no mfinimfini, ntaban pem ntaban anim.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Na osii dan no wiei no, ɔde kyeneduru mpuran ne ntaaboo kataa ɔdan no so.

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: Ase mpia no, basafa abien ne fa ne ne trɛw, na mfinimfini de no, basafa abiɛsa ne ne trɛw, na nea ɛto so abiɛsa no, basafa abiɛsa ne fa ne ne trɛw, na ɔyɛɛ ɔdan no akyi mmamma hyiae, na mpuran no anhyɛn ɔdan no afasu mu.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Na wɔresi ɔdan no, wɔde abo amuamu a wɔasiesie fi abotubea saa na esii: Na wɔresi no, wɔante asae anaa pɛe anaa adwinnade biara nka ɔdan no ho.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: Na osisii nsɛmso no twaa ɔdan no ho nyinaa hyiae, basafa abien ne fa ne ebiara korɔn, na wɔde kyeneduru mpuran na esusoo ɔdan no mu.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE asɛm baa Solomon nkyɛn sɛ:

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: Na ɔde kyeneduru ntaaboo pam ɔdan no afasu no wɔ mu, ɔde nnua kataa mu fi ɔdan no fam kosi nsɛmso ani, na ɔde ɔpopaw ntaaboo sɛm ɔdan no fam.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: Na ɔde kyeneduru ntaaboo sii ɔdan no akyiri fam basafa du, fi fam kɔpem nsɛmso mpuran, na osii de emu yɛɛ mpiakyiri, ɛne kronkronbea no.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Na ɔdan no mu kyeneduru ntaaboo no anim no, wodii so kukuduuduu ne nhwiren a ahanhan adwinni; ne nyinaa yɛ kyeneduru, wɔanhu ɔbo biara.

english_verse: The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place.
translation_verse: Na osiesiee mpiakyiri no ɔdan no mu, sɛ wɔmfa AWURADE apam adaka no nsi hɔ.

translation_verse: wo ara tie ɔsoro, wo tenabea hɔ, na yɛ sɛ ɔhɔho no su frɛ wo no nyinaa, nea ɛbɛyɛ na asase so aman nyinaa ahu wo din na wɔasuro wo, sɛ wo man Israel, na wɔahu sɛ wo din na wɔde frɛ ɔdan a masi yi.

english_verse: Our Lord, sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.
translation_verse: Sɛ wo man fi adi ne wɔn atamfo kodi ako, ɔkwan a wobɛsoma wɔn so, na wɔbɔ AWURADE mpae kyerɛ kurow a woayi ne ɔdan a masi mama wo din yi a,

english_verse: Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
translation_verse: ɛnne tie wɔn mpaebɔ ne wɔn nkotɔsrɛ ɔsoro, na di wɔn asɛm ma wɔn.

english_verse: Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries.
translation_verse: Sɛ wɔyɛ wo bɔne, efisɛ onipa bi nni hɔ a ɔnyɛ bɔne, na wofa wɔn abufuw, na wuyi wɔn ma wɔn atamfo, na dɔm soa wɔn nnommum kɔ atamfo asase so akyirikyiri oo, mmɛnkyɛnee oo,

english_verse: Forgive your people no matter how much they have sinned against you. Make the enemies who defeated them be kind to them.
translation_verse: na fa wo man bɔne a wɔayɛ wo ne wɔn mmarato a wɔato afom wo no nyinaa kyɛ wɔn, na ma wonnya wɔn nnommumfafo no anim mmɔborohunu, na wonhu wɔn mmɔbɔ.

english_verse: Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
translation_verse: Efisɛ wɔyɛ wo man ne w’agyapade a wuyii wɔn Misraim fii dade fononoo mu de wɔn bae no,

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help.
translation_verse: na bue w’aniwa ma w’akoa nkotɔsrɛ ne wo man Israel nkotɔsrɛ, na tie wɔn nea wosu frɛ wo no nyinaa mu.

english_verse: When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.” Solomon Blesses the People
translation_verse: Na wo AWURADE Nyankopɔn, wo ara na wuyii wɔn yɛɛ agyapade fii asase so aman nyinaa mu, sɛnea wonam w’akoa Mose so kae ɛbere a wuyii yɛn agyanom fii Misraim bae no.

english_verse: When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up,
translation_verse: Na Solomon wiee mpae a ɔbɔɔ AWURADE ne nkotɔsrɛ yi nyinaa no, ɔsɔre fii afɔremuka no anim, na ogyaee ne nankoroma anim kotow ne ne nsam trɛw a ɔtrɛw kyerɛɛ ɔsoro no.

english_verse: turned toward the people, blessed them, and said loudly:
translation_verse: Na ogyinaa hɔ de nne kɛse hyiraa Israel asafo no nyinaa sɛ:

english_verse: Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
translation_verse: Nhyira ne AWURADE a wama ne man Israel ɔmannwoe sɛnea ɔkae no nyinaa. N’asɛmpa a ɔnam n’akoa Mose so kae no nyinaa mu asɛm biako po antɔ fam.

english_verse: The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us.
translation_verse: AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn nni yɛn akyi, sɛnea odii yɛn agyanom akyi no, onnnyaw yɛn, nanso ɔmmpa yɛn.

english_verse: May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
translation_verse: Na ɔnkom yɛn koma mmra ne ho, na yɛanantew n’akwan nyinaa mu, na yɛadi ne mmara nsɛm ne n’ahyɛde ne n’atemmude a ɔhyɛɛ yɛn agyanom no so.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it.
translation_verse: Na ma me nsɛm a mede mekotɔ mesrɛ AWURADE anim yi mmɛn AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn awia ne anadwo, na onni n’akoa asɛm ne ne man Israel asɛm mma wɔn, sɛnea ehia da biara,

english_verse: Then every nation will know that the Lord is the only true God.
translation_verse: na asase so aman nyinaa nhu sɛ: AWURADE ne Onyankopɔn, na obi nni hɔ bio.

english_verse: Obey the Lord our God and follow his commands with all your heart, just as you are doing today. Solomon Dedicates the Temple (
translation_verse: Na momma mo koma mmɔ AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn ho pɛ, sɛ mobɛnantew n’ahyɛde so na moadi ne mmara nsɛm so sɛ ɛte nnɛ yi.

english_verse: On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
translation_verse: Da no ara ɔhene yɛɛ AWURADE dan no anim abangua no kronkron, na ɛhɔ na ɔhyew ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre ho srade no, efisɛ kɔbere afɔremuka a esi AWURADE anim no sua dodo sɛ ɛbɛhyew ɔhyew afɔre ne aduan afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre ho srade no.

english_verse: Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Na Solomon dii nnapɔnna no ɛbere no mu, na Israel nyinaa ka ne ho, asafo kɛse, wofi nea wɔrekɔ Hamat de besi Misraim subon ano, wodii AWURADE yɛn Nyankopɔn anim nnapa nnawɔtwe abien.

english_verse: Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_verse: Da a ɛto so awotwe no, ogyaa ɔman no kwan ma wɔkɔe; na wohyirahyiraa ɔhene, na wɔde papa a AWURADE ayɛ ama n’akoa Dawid ne ne man Israel no nyinaa ho anigye ne koma pa sii mu kokɔɔ wɔn afi mu.

english_verse: I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: ɛnne metwa Israel afi asase a mede mama wɔn no ani, na ofi a mayɛ no kronkron mama me din no, mɛtow afi m’anim akyene, na Israel bɛdan bɛ ne nkasaguaa aman nyinaa mu.

english_verse: Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. They were his soldiers, officials, leaders, commanders, chariot captains, and chariot drivers. But he did make slaves of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites could not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
translation_verse: Na Israelfo no mu de, Solomon amfa obi anyɛ akoa, efisɛ wɔn na wɔyɛ akofofo ne ne gyaasefo ne ne mmapɔmma ne ne mmarima akunini ne ne nteaseɛnam so ahwɛfo ne n’apɔnkɔsotefo.

english_verse: The Lord said: I heard your prayer and what you asked me to do. This temple you have built is where I will be worshiped forever. It belongs to me, and I will never stop watching over it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Mate wo mpaebɔ ne wo nkotɔsrɛ a wobɛsrɛɛ m’anim no, na mayɛ ofi a woasi yi kronkron, sɛ mede me din mɛto hɔ akosi daa, na m’aniwa ne me koma atena hɔ nna nyinaa.

english_verse: You must obey me, as your father David did, and be honest and fair. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Na wo de, sɛ wonantew m’anim sɛnea w’agya Dawid nantewee no, koma mu pɛyɛ ne tee mu, sɛ wobɛyɛ sɛnea mahyɛ wo nyinaa, na woadi m’ahyɛde ne m’atemmude so a,

english_verse: and I will keep my promise to David that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: ɛnne mɛma wo hene a wudi Israel so no agua atim akosi daa, sɛnea mekae w’agya Dawid ho sɛ: Onipa remmɔ wo, Israel ahengua so, no.

english_verse: Then they will answer, “We know why the Lord did this. The people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.” Other Things Solomon Did (
translation_verse: Na wobebua sɛ: Efisɛ wɔagyaw AWURADE wɔn Nyankopɔn a oyii wɔn agyanom fii Misraim asase so bae no, na wɔakosuso anyame foforo mu asɔre wɔn asom wɔn, enti na AWURADE de bɔne yi nyinaa aba wɔn so yi. Solomon ne Hiram yɛ apam (

english_verse: Baalath, and Tamar in the desert of Judah.
translation_verse: ne Baalat ne Tadmor a ɛwɔ sare so asase no so,

english_verse: When Hiram went to see the towns, he did not like them.
translation_verse: Na Hiram fii adi fii Tiro sɛ ɔbɛhwɛ nkurow a Solomon ama no no, nanso ansɔ n’ani.

english_verse: He said, “Solomon, my friend, are these the kind of towns you want to give me?” So Hiram called the region Cabul because he thought it was worthless.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Nkurow bɛn na wode ama me yi, me nua? Na ɔfrɛɛ no sɛ: Kabul asase, de besi nnɛ.

english_verse: After Solomon's workers had finished the temple and the palace, he ordered them to fill in the land on the east side of Jerusalem, to build a wall around the city, and to rebuild the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
translation_verse: Na adwuma tow a ɔhene Solomon gyei sɛ ɔde besi AWURADE fi ne n’ankasa ne fi ne Milo ne Yerusalem fasu ne Hasor ne Megido ne Geser no ho asɛm ni:

english_verse: Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon.
translation_verse: Misraim hene Farao aforo abɛfa Geser de ogya ahyew, na wakunkum Kanaanfo a wɔte kurow no mu no, na ɔde ama ne babea, Solomon yere no, sɛ awarede.

english_verse: So Solomon had the town rebuilt. Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon,
translation_verse: Na Solomon kyekyee Geser ne anafo Bet-horon,

english_verse: They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
translation_verse: ne aduankora nkurow a Solomon wɔ nyinaa ne nteaseɛnam nkurow ne apɔnkɔsotefo nkurow ne Solomon ade a ɔpɛ sɛ osi Yerusalem ne Lebanon ne asase a odi so nyinaa no so.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
translation_verse: Nso Farao babea no fii Dawid kurow no mu baa ne dan a osi maa no no mu. Ɛno na ɔkyekyee Milo.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Na Solomon bobɔɔ afɔre, afe mu mprɛnsa, ɔhyew afɔre ne asomdwoe afɔre, afɔremuka a osi maa AWURADE no so, na ɔhyew aduhuam nea esi AWURADE anim no so. Na owiee ofi no koraa.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon yɛɛ ahyɛn wɔ Esion-geber a ɛwɔ Elot ho, Mmɛw Po ano, Edom asase so.

english_verse: King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔɔ Ofir kogyee sika hɔ, dwetikɛse ahanan aduonu, na wɔde brɛɛ ɔhene Solomon.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Na Solomon buaa no ne nsɛm nyinaa; asɛm biara anhintaw ɔhene a wanka ankyerɛ no.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: ne ne pon so nnuan ne ne nkoa atenae ne n’asomfo gyinabea ne wɔn ntade ne ne nsahyɛfo ne n’aforoe a ɔnam so kɔ AWURADE fi no, ne home tew no, na ɛyɛɛ no nwonwa.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ɔhene no sɛ: Wo nsɛnnii ne wo nyansa ho asɛm a metee m’asase so no yɛ nokware;

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: na mannye nsɛm no manni de besii sɛ mebae, na mede m’aniwa mabehu yi; na hwɛ, wɔanka me emu fa po: Wo nyansa ne wo yiye sen nka a metee no.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Nhyira ne wo nnipa, nhyira ne wo nkoa yi a wogyinagyina w’anim daa yi te wo nyansa no.

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, many jewels, and more spices than anyone had ever brought into Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa ɔhene sika dwetikɛse ɔha aduonu, ne nnuhuam bebree pa ara, ne aboɔden abo; nnuhuam bebree saa bi amma bio, sɛnea Seba hemmaa de maa ɔhene Solomon no.

english_verse: He was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon soe sen asase so ahene nyinaa, ade dodow ne nyansa fam.

english_verse: The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
translation_verse: ɛsono nea efi aguadifo hɔ ne akwantemfo batadi mu ne nea efi Arabia ahemfo nyinaa ne asase no so amradofo no nsam.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene yɛɛ asonse ahengua kokuroo, na ɔde sika amapa duraa ho.

english_verse: Since silver was almost worthless in those days, everything was made of gold, even the cups and dishes used in Forest Hall.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Solomon nkuruwa a ɔnom mu nyinaa yɛ sika, na Lebanon kwae dan mu nneɛma nyinaa yɛ sika kronkron; dwetɛ nni mu: Wommu no hwee Solomon bere so.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene wɔ Tarsis ahyɛn ɛpo no so a ɛka Hiram ahyɛn ho; mfe abiɛsa biara mu, Tarsis ahyɛn no ba pɛnkoro de sika ne dwetɛ, asonse ne nkyeneboa ne koohaa ba.

english_verse: People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him.
translation_verse: Na asase nyinaa hwehwɛɛ Solomon anim ahu, sɛ wobetie ne nyansa a Onyankopɔn de ahyɛ ne koma mu no.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Na wɔde wɔn ayɛyɛde ba mmiako mmiako, dwetɛ nneɛma ne sika nneɛma ne ntade ne akode ne nnuhuam, apɔnkɔ ne mfurumpɔnkɔ, afe biara ne ne de.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene maa dwetɛ yɛe sɛ abo wɔ Yerusalem, ne nkyeneduru nso sɛ ankye nnua a ɛwɔ asasetaw so.

english_verse: Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid
translation_verse: Na wɔde teaseɛnam fi Misraim ba a ne bo yɛ dwetɛ nnwetɛbona ahansia, ne ɔpɔnkɔ nso, ɔha aduonum; na saa ara na aguadifo de bi brɛ Hetifo ahemfo nyinaa ne Siria ahemfo.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Na Solomon kodii Sidonfo nyamewa Astoret ne Amonfo Milkom a ɛyɛ akyide no akyi.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Na Solomon yɛɛ nea ɛyɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne, na wanwie AWURADE akyidi sɛ n’agya Dawid.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ɛno mu na Solomon sii sorɔnsorɔmmea maa Moabfo Kemos a ɛyɛ akyide bepɔw a ɛwɔ Yerusalem apuei no so, ne Amonfo Molek a ɛyɛ akyide;

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: na saa na ɔyɛ maa ne yerenom ananafo a wɔhyew aduhuam na wɔbɔ afɔre ma wɔn anyame no nyinaa.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry,
translation_verse: na wahyɛ no asɛm yi ho mmara sɛ onnkodi anyame foforo akyi, nanso wanni nea AWURADE hyɛɛ no no so no ho.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ Solomon sɛ: Esiane sɛ eyi wɔ wo ho na woanni m’apam ne m’ahyɛde a mehyɛɛ wo no so nti, ɔtew na mɛtew ahenni no afi wo nsam, na mede mama w’akoa.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Nanso wo bere so de, merenyɛ, w’agya Dawid nti, na wo ba nsam na mɛtew afi;

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: nanso m’akoa Dawid ne Yerusalem a mafa no nti merentew ahenni no nyinaa, na mede abusuakuw biako mɛma wo ba. Solomon atamfo ne ne wu

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE maa ɔperedifo bi, Edomni Hadad, sɔre hyɛɛ Solomon; ofi ɔhene asefo mu wɔ Edom.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: na Tahpenes ne nua no woo ɔbabarima Genubat maa no, na Tahpenes twaa no nufu Farao fi, na Genubat wɔ Farao fi, Farao mma mu.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Na Hadad tee Misraim sɛ Dawid ne n’agyanom akɔda na ɔsahene Yoab awu no, Hadad ka kyerɛɛ Farao sɛ: Gya me kwan ma menkɔ m’asase so.

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Ɛnna Farao ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Na ɛdɛn na ehia wo me nkyɛn ha na worehwehwɛ w’asase so akɔ yi? Na obuae sɛ: Ɛnyɛ biribiara, nanso gya me kwan ma menkɔ.

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn maa ɔperedifo bi, Eliada ba Reson a oguan fii ne wura Hadad-eser, Soba hene, nkyɛn no sɔre hyɛɛ no.

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Na Nebat ba Yeroboam, Efraimni a ofi Sereda, a ɔyɛ Solomon akoa, na ne na din de Serua, ɔbea kunafo bi, nso tew ɔhene so atua.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Na asɛm a ɛma ɔtew ɔhene so atua ne sɛ: Solomon kyekyee Milo na otuatuaa n’agya Dawid kurow ho fasu mu.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima Yeroboam no yɛ ɔbarima a otumi, na Solomon huu aberante no sɛ ɔyɛ ɔdeyɛfo no, ɔma ɔyɛɛ Yosef fi adwuma nyinaa so hwɛfo.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: na m’akoa Dawid ne kurow Yerusalem a mafa afi Israel mmusuakuw nyinaa mu no nti abusuakuw biako na ɛnyɛ ne de;

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: esiane sɛ wagyaw me na wakɔsɔre Sidonfo nyamewa Astoret ne Moabfo nyame Kemos ne Amonfo nyame Milkom, na wannantew m’akwan mu sɛ ɔbɛyɛ nea ɛteɛ m’ani so ne m’ahyɛde ne m’atemmude sɛ n’agya Dawid.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Nanso merennye ne nsam ahenni no nyinaa, na m’akoa Dawid a mafa no a odii me mmara nsɛm ne m’ahyɛde so no nti, mesi no ɔman so panyin ne nkwa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Na megye ahenni no ne ba nsam, na mede mmusuakuw du mama wo.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Na ne ba no, mede abusuakuw biako mɛma no nea ɛbɛyɛ na ɔkanea atena hɔ ama m’akoa Dawid nna nyinaa wɔ m’anim Yerusalem kurow a mayi mafa sɛ mede me din mɛto hɔ no mu.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Na wo na mɛfa wo mama woadi hene sɛnea wo kra pɛ nyinaa, na woayɛ Israel so hene.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Na sɛ wutie nea mɛhyɛ wo nyinaa na wonantew m’akwan so na woyɛ nea ɛteɛ m’ani so, sɛ wubedi m’ahyɛde ne me mmara nsɛm so sɛnea m’akoa Dawid yɛe no a, ɛnne medi w’akyi na masi ofi a etim hɔ mama wo; sɛnea misi memaa Dawid no, na mede Israel mama wo;

english_verse: “I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
translation_verse: na eyi nti mɛbrɛ Dawid asefo ase, nanso ɛnyɛ nna nyinaa.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Na Solomon ho nsɛm nkae ne nea ɔyɛe nyinaa ne ne nyansa no, wɔakyerɛw no Solomon ho nsɛm nhoma no mu?

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Na Solomon tiw n’agyanom wɔ asaman, na wosiee no n’agya Dawid kurow mu; na ne ba Rehoboam bedii n’ade.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: na wɔsoma kohyiaa no bae, na Yeroboam ne Israel asafo nyinaa bae, na wɔbɛka kyerɛɛ Rehoboam sɛ:

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monkɔ na nnansa akyi monsan mmra me nkyɛn. Na ɔman no kɔe.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Na ɔhene Rehoboam ne mpanyimfo a n’agya Solomon da so te ase no, wɔyɛ n’afotufo no tuu agyina sɛ: Ɛfo bɛn na moretu me na mede mabua ɔman yi?

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ nnɛ woyɛ akoa ma ɔman yi na wosom wɔn na wubua wɔn na woka wɔn asɛmpa a, ɛnne wɔbɛyɛ wo nkoa nna nyinaa.

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Na ogyaw mpanyimfo fo a wotuu no no, na ɔne mmerante a wɔne no nyinii a wɔyɛ n’afotufo no kotuu agyina,
