english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Na ose: Mahu Israel nyinaa sɛ wɔapete mmepɔw so sɛ nguan a wonni hwɛfo, na AWURADE se: Eyinom nni wura, ma wɔnsan nkokɔ wɔn afi asomdwoe mu.

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔkae sɛ: Enti tie AWURADE asɛm: Mahu AWURADE sɛ ɔte n’agua so, na ɔsoro asafo nyinaa gyinagyina ne ho, ne nifa ne ne benkum.

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Wode dɛn? Na ose: Mefi makɔyɛ atoro honhom n’adiyifo nyinaa anom. Na ɔkae sɛ: Wobɛdaadaa no na wubetumi nso; fi kɔ na kɔyɛ saa.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Na afei, hwɛ, AWURADE de atoro honhom ahyɛ w’adiyifo yi nyinaa anom, na AWURADE akasa wo ho bɔne.

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Kenaana ba Sedekia twiw bɛnee bɛbɔɔ Mikaia sotɔre kae sɛ: Ɛhe na AWURADE honhom nam fii me nkyɛn kɔka kyerɛɛ wo yi?

english_verse: years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
translation_verse: Na Mikaia se: Hwɛ, da a wubefi pia mu akɔ pia mu akohintaw no na wubehu.

translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel hene kae sɛ: Kyere Mikaia fa no kɔ kurow no so hwɛfo Amon ne ɔhene ba Yoas nkyɛn,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi twee ne ta mu anibiannaso so, na ɔde saa Israel hene no mmɔtoam ne nkatabo no ntam. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne teaseɛnamkafo no sɛ: Dan wo nsa fa me fi dɔm yi mu, na mapira.

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Na Israel hene ne Yuda hene Yehosafat foro kɔɔ Ramot-gilead.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Na Israel hene ka kyerɛɛ Yehosafat sɛ: Mɛsakra me ho na makɔ dɔm no mu, na wo de, hyɛ wo ntade. Na Israel hene no sakraa ne ho, na ɔkɔɔ dɔm no mu.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Na nteaseɛnam so asafohene no huu Yehosafat no, wɔkae sɛ: Ampa, Israel hene no ni! Na wɔmanee ne no kɔkoe; na Yehosafat teɛɛm.

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: Na nteaseɛnam so asafohene no hui sɛ ɛnyɛ Israel hene ne no no, wɔsan fii n’akyi.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Na wɔpae faa nsra no mu owiatɔ bere sɛ: Nnipa nyinaa nkokɔ wɔn kurom ne wɔn asase so.

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene no wui, na wɔde no baa Samaria; na wosiee ɔhene no Samaria.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔhohoroo teaseɛnam no mu Samaria ɔtare mu, na akraman bɛtaforoo ne mogya, na mmea nguaman nso guaree hɔ, sɛnea AWURADE aka no.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Ahab ho nsɛm nkae ne nea ɔyɛe nyinaa ne asonse dan a osii, ne nkurow a ɔkyekyee nyinaa, so wɔankyerɛw Israel ahene beresosɛm nhoma no mu?

translation_verse: Na Ahab wui, na ne ba Ahasia bedii n’ade. Yehosafat di Yuda so hene (

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in Ahab's fourth year as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Israel hene Ahab afe a ɛto so anan so na Asa ba Yehosafat bedii Yuda so hene.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene bi nni Edom; na n’abediakyiri na ɔhwɛ akyi sɛ hene.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat had seagoing ships built to sail to Ophir for gold. But they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber and never sailed.
translation_verse: Yehosafat yɛɛ Tarsis ahyɛn sɛ ɛnkɔ Ofir nkɔpɛ sika kɔkɔɔ; nanso ankɔ, efisɛ ahyɛn no bobɔe Esion-geber.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Ɛno mu na Ahab ba Ahasia ka kyerɛɛ Yehosafat sɛ: Ma me nkoa ne wo nkoa nkɔ ahyɛn no mu. Na Yehosafat ampene.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Na Yehosafat wui, na wosiee no kaa n’agyanom ho, n’agya Dawid kurow mu; na ne ba Yehoram bedii n’ade. Ahasia di Israel so hene

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Ahab ba Ahasia bedii Israel so hene Samaria, Yuda hene Yehosafat afe a ɛto so dunsɔn so, na odii Israel so mfe abien.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ nea ɛyɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne, na ɔfaa n’agya kwan so ne ne na kwan so ne Nebat ba Yeroboam a ɔmaa Israel yɛɛ bɔne no kwan so;

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: na ɔsom Baal na ɔsɔree no, na ohuruu AWURADE, Israel Nyankopɔn, bo sɛnea n’agya yɛe no ara.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Na Ahasia fii n’abansorodan a ɛwɔ Samaria no mfɛnsere mu hwee ase, na ɔyaree; na ɔsomaa abɔfo, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Monkɔ nkobisa Ekron nyame Baalsebub sɛ menya yare yi mu nkwa anaa?

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔfo ka kyerɛɛ Tisbini Elia sɛ: Sɔre foro kohyia Samaria hene abɔfo no, na ka kyerɛ wɔn sɛ: So Onyankopɔn bi nni Israel nti na morekɔ akobisa Ekron nyame Baalsebub hɔ ade yi?

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Enti AWURADE se: Mpa a woaforo no, woremfi so nsian, na owu na wubewu! Na Elia kɔe.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna abɔfo no san baa ɔhene nkyɛn, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛdɛn na moasan aba yi?

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɔbarima bi foro behyiaa yɛn, na ɔka kyerɛɛ yɛn sɛ: Monsan nkɔ ɔhene a ɔsomaa mo no nkyɛn nkɔka nkyerɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: So onyame bi nni Israel nti na woasoma rekɔ Ekron nyame Baalsebub hɔ adebisa yi? Enti mpa a woaforo no, woremfi so nsian, na owu na wubewu.

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Atade a ɔhyɛ no yɛ aboa nwin, na nhoma abɔso bɔ n’asen. Na ose: Ɛyɛ Tisbini Elia. Elia ne asafohene baasa no

english_verse: “If I am a man of God,” Elijah answered, “God will send down fire on you and your
translation_verse: Na Elia bua ka kyerɛɛ aduonum so safohene no sɛ: Sɛ Onyankopɔn nipa ne me a, ogya mfi soro nsian mmɛhyew wo ne w’aduonum! Na ogya fi soro duru bɛhyew ɔno ne n’aduonum no.

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Hwɛ, ogya afi soro aduru abɛhyew kan aduonum so asafohene baanu no ne wɔn aduonum aduonum no, na afei ma me kra bo nyɛ den w’ani so.

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Ɛnna AWURADE bɔfo ka kyerɛɛ Elia sɛ: Wo ne no nsian nkɔ, nsuro n’anim. Na ɔsɔree ne no sian kɔɔ ɔhene no nkyɛn. Ahasia wu

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Esiane sɛ woasoma abɔfo sɛ wonkobisa Ekron nyame Baalsebub hɔ ade, te sɛnea Onyame bi nni Israel a wokobisa no asɛm nti, mpa a woaforo no, woremfi so nsian, na owu na wubewu.

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Na owui, sɛnea AWURADE maa Elia kae no. Na Yehoram sii n’ananmu dii hene, Yuda hene Yehosafat ba Yehoram afe a ɛto so abien so, efisɛ onni ba.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Ahasia ho nsɛm nkae, nea ɔyɛe no, so wɔankyerɛw Israel ahene beresosɛm nhoma no mu?

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE rebɛfa Elia ahum mu akɔ ɔsoro no, Elia ne Elisa fi Gilgal kɔe.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Na Elia ka kyerɛɛ Elisa sɛ: Tena ha ɛ, na AWURADE asoma me Betel. Na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase na wo kra te ase yi, merennyaw wo. Na wosian kɔɔ Betel.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma a wɔwɔ Betel no fii adi baa Elisa nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wunim sɛ ɛnnɛ AWURADE rebɛfa wo wura afi wo nkyɛn akɔ? Na ose: Yiw minim; monyɛ komm!

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Na Elia ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Elisa, tena ha ɛ, na AWURADE asoma me Yeriko. Na ose: Sɛ AWURADE te ase na wo kra te ase yi, merennyaw wo. Na woduu Yeriko.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma a wɔwɔ Yeriko no twiw baa Elisa nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: So wunim sɛ ɛnnɛ AWURADE bɛfa wo wura afi wo nkyɛn akɔ? Na ose: Yiw minim; monyɛ komm!

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Na Elia ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Tena ha ɛ, na AWURADE asoma me Yordan ano. Na ose: Sɛ AWURADE te ase na wo kra te ase yi, merennyaw wo. Na wɔn baanu no kɔe.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma no mu aduonum kɔe kogyinagyinaa wɔn ntentenso akyirikyiri, na wɔn baanu no gyinaa Yordan ano.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Na Elia faa ne nguguso bobɔw de bɔɔ nsu no mu, na ɛpae kɔɔ ha ne ha, na wɔn baanu no nam asase kesee so twae.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Na wotwae no, Elia ka kyerɛɛ Elisa se: Bisa nea menyɛ mma wo ansa na wɔafa me afi wo nkyɛn akɔ. Na Elisa sɛ: Ma wo honhom abupɛn abien mmra me so.

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Woabisa ade a ɛyɛ den; nanso sɛ wuhu me sɛ wɔrefa me afi wo nkyɛn a, ɛbɛyɛ saa ama wo; na sɛ woanhu me de a, ɛrenyɛ.

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Na wɔnam rekɔ na wɔrekasa no, hwɛ, ogya teaseɛnam ne ogya apɔnkɔ a ɛbɛpaee wɔn baanu no ntam bae, na Elia faa ahum mu foro kɔɔ ɔsoro.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Na Elisa hwɛe na ɔteɛɛm sɛ: M’agya, m’agya! Israel nteaseɛnam ne wɔn apɔnkɔsotefo na ɔrekɔ no! Na wanhu no bio. Na osoo n’atade mu suanee mu abien,

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: na ɔmaa Elia nguguso a efii ne ho gui no so, na ɔsan begyinaa Yordan ano.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: Na ɔde Elia nguguso a efii ne ho gui no bɔɔ nsu no mu kae sɛ: Ɛhe na AWURADE, Elia Nyankopɔn no, wɔ? Na ɔbɔɔ nsu no mu no, ɛpae kɔɔ ha ne ha, na Elisa twae.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma a wɔwɔ Yeriko wɔ ne ntentenso no huu no no, wɔkae sɛ: Elia honhom abesi Elisa so. Na wɔbae behyiaa no, na wɔkotow no butuw fam.

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Na wɔhyɛɛ no ara ma ɛyɛɛ no ahometew no, ɔkae sɛ: Monsoma! Na wɔsomaa mmarima aduonum, na wɔkɔhwehwɛe nnansa, nanso wɔanhu no.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Na wɔsan baa ne nkyɛn, na ɔno de, ɔte Yeriko, na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: So manka mankyerɛ mo sɛ monnkɔ oo? Elisa sa yare na ɔdome

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Na kurow no mufo no ka kyerɛɛ Elisa sɛ: Hwɛ, kurow yi dabea yɛ fɛ, sɛnea me wura hu yi; nanso nsu no nye, na asase no ma ɔpɔn.

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Na ose: Mommrɛ me asanka foforo, na momfa nkyene ngu mu. Na wɔde brɛɛ no.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Na ofii adi kɔɔ nsuaniwa no ho, na okohwiee nkyene no guu mu hɔ, na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Masa nsu yi yare, owu anaa ɔpɔn bi remfi mu hɔ bio.

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Na nsu no yɛɛ yiye de besi nnɛ da yi, sɛ Elisa kae no.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Na ofii hɔ foro kɔɔ Betel; na ɔreforo akɔ ɔkwan no so no, mmofra nketewa fii kurow no mu bae begoruu ne ho ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Tipae, foro ɛ, tipae, foro ɛ!

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔdan ne ho, ohuu wɔn no, ɔde AWURADE din domee wɔn. Na asisibere abien fi kwae no mu bae, bɛkyeree mmofra no mu aduanan abien, tetew wɔn mu.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Na ofii hɔ kɔɔ Karmel bepɔw ho, na ofii hɔ nso san baa Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Na Ahab ba Yehoram bedii Israel so hene Samaria, Yuda hene Yehosafat afe a ɛto so dunwɔtwe so; na odii hene mfe dumien.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne, nanso ɛnte sɛ n’agya ne ne na; efisɛ oyii Baal honi a n’agya yɛe no hɔ.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Nanso ɔbataa Nebat ba Yeroboam a ɔmaa Israel yɛɛ bɔne no bɔne ho, na wansan amfi ho.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Na Moab hene Mesa yɛ nguanhwɛfo, na ɔmaa Israel hene nguanten mma ɔpeha ne adwennini ɔpeha ho nwi.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Na Ahab wui no, Moab hene tew Israel hene anim atua.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Na Yehoram fii Samaria da no ara, boaboaa Israel nyinaa ano.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔe, na ɔsoma kɔɔ Yuda hene Yehosafat nkyɛn sɛ: Moab hene atew m’anim atua, na wo ne me bɛkɔ ne Moab akɔko anaa? Na ose: Mɛkɔ, mete sɛ wo, me man te sɛ wo man, m’apɔnkɔ te sɛ w’apɔnkɔ.

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ɔkwan bɛn so na yɛbɛfa akɔ? Na ose: Edom sare so kwan no.

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Israel hene ne Yuda hene ne Edom hene siim kɔe; na wokyinii nnansɔn kwan, na nsu nni hɔ mma dɔm no ne mmoa a wodi wɔn akyi.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Na Israel hene kae sɛ: Ao, sɛ AWURADE afrɛ ahene baasa yi ahyia sɛ ɔde wɔn rekɔhyɛ Moab nsa!

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Na Yehosafat se: So AWURADE diyifo bi nni ha a yɛbɛkɔ ne nkyɛn akobisa AWURADE? Na Israel hene nkoa mu biako buae sɛ: Ɛha na Safat ba Elisa a ohwiee nsu guu Elia nsa so no wɔ.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Na Yehosafat kae sɛ: AWURADE asɛm wɔ ne nkyɛn. Ɛnna Israel hene ne Yehosafat ne Edom hene sian kɔɔ ne nkyɛn.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa ka kyerɛɛ Israel hene no sɛ: Dɛn na me ne wo wɔ yɛ? Kɔ w’agya adiyifo ne wo na adiyifo no nkyɛn! Na Israel hene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dabi, na AWURADE afrɛ ahene baasa yi ahyia sɛ ɔde wɔn rekɔhyɛ Moab nsa.

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa se: Sɛ asafo AWURADE a migyina n’anim te ase yi, sɛ ɛnyɛ Yuda hene Yehosafat anim na mehwɛ a, anka merenhwɛ wo na merenhu wo.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Na afei momfa ɔsankubɔfo mmrɛ me. Na ɔsankubɔfo no rebɔ no, AWURADE nsa baa no so,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Mɛma nsu abɛhyɛ abon a emu awo yi mu ma.

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE se ni: Morenhu mframa na morenhu osu, nanso nsu bɛyɛ obon yi ma; na moanom, mo ne mo anantwikuw ne mo mmoa.

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Na eyi nso yɛ mmerɛw AWURADE ani so, na obeyi Moab nso ahyɛ mo nsa.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Na mobɛbobɔ afasu mu nkurow nyinaa ne nkurow a ɛyɛ fɛ nyinaa, na moatotow nnua pa nyinaa, na moasisiw nsuaniwa nyinaa, na mode abo asɛe mfuw pa nyinaa.

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Na anɔpa a wɔrebɔ aduan afɔre no, hwɛ, nsu fii Edom kwan so bae, na nsu no yɛɛ asase no ma.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Na Moabfo nyinaa tee sɛ ahene no reforo aba ne wɔn abɛko no, wɔfrɛfrɛɛ wɔn a wobetumi amia amiade nyinaa efi mmofra so kosii mpanyimfo so ne wɔn hyiae, na wobegyinaa ɔhye so.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Na wɔsɔree anɔpatutu na owia repue nsu no so no, Moabfo huu nsu no agya noho sɛ ɛbere sɛ mogya;

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: na wɔkae sɛ: Mogya ni! Ahene no ne wɔn ho adi nnɔmmata akunkum wɔn ho, na afei, Moabfo, monkɔ asade ho.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Na nkurow no, woburuwii, na mfuw pa nyinaa, wɔtotow abo mmiako mmiako guguu so kosii sɛ ɛso katae, na wosisiw nsuaniwa nyinaa, na wɔtotow nnua pa nyinaa; gye Kir-hareset na wogyaw n’abo, na ataabotowfo kotwaa ho hyiae bɔɔ no.

english_verse: King Mesha of Moab saw that he was about to be defeated. So he took along
translation_verse: Na Moab hene hui sɛ dɔm no ano ayɛ den papa ama no no, ɔfaa mmarima ahansɔn a wɔtwe nkrante kaa ne ho sɛ ɔretew mu akɔ Edom hene ho, nanso wɔantumi.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔfaa n’abakan a anka obesi n’ananmu adi hene no, na ɔde no bɔɔ ɔhyew afɔre ɔfasu no so. Na abufuw kɛse baa Israel mu, na wofii ne ho san baa wɔn asase so.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma no mu biako yere teɛɛm frɛɛ Elisa sɛ: W’akoa, me kunu, awu, no wo ara wunim sɛ w’akoa suro AWURADE; na ɔkafo aba rebɛfa me mma baanu akɔyɛ ne nkoa.

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Dɛn na menyɛ memma wo? Kyerɛ me ɛ, dɛn na wowɔ ofie? Na ose: W’afenaa nni hwee ofie gyee ngohina biako pɛ.

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Fi adi kɔfemfɛm nhina wɔn a wɔtete bɛn wo nyinaa nkyɛn, nhina hunu, ma ɛnnɔɔso.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ woba mu a, to wo ne wo mma no pon mu, na hwiehwie gu nhina no nyinaa mu, na fa nea ayɛ ma no sisi nkyɛn.

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Na ofii ne nkyɛn kɔe, na ɔkɔtoo ne ho ne ne mma pon mu; wɔn de, wɔde nhina no brɛɛ no, na ɔno nso hwiehwie guguu mu.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Na nhina no yeyɛɛ amaama no, ɔka kyerɛɛ ne ba sɛ: Fa nhina bi brɛ me bio! Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Nhina bi nni hɔ bio; na ngo no twae.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔba bɛka kyerɛɛ Onyankopɔn nipa no. Na Onyankopɔn nipa kae sɛ: Kɔ na kɔtɔn ngo no, na fa tua wo ka, na wo ne wo mma nni nea aka no ntena ase. Elisa ne Sunemni bea

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Na da bi Elisa sen kɔɔ Sunem. Na ɔbea ɔdefo bi wɔ hɔ a ɔhyɛɛ no sɛ ommedidi. Enti daa ɔretwam a, ɔman hɔ kodidi.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne kunu sɛ: Hwɛ, mahu sɛ Onyankopɔn nipa kronkron ne oyi a ɔbɛsen yɛn nkyɛn daa yi;

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: ma yɛnyɛ abansoro fasu mu pia ketewa bi, na yɛmfa mpadua ne ɔpon ne agua ne kaneadua nsisi hɔ mma no, na sɛ ɔba yɛn nkyɛn a, waman akɔ hɔ.

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Na da bi ɔbaa hɔ, na ɔman kɔɔ abansoro pia no mu kɔdaa hɔ.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ka kyerɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, wode ɔhaw yi nyinaa ahaw wo ho ama yɛn. Dɛn na yɛnyɛ mma wo? Wowɔ asɛm bi a wɔnkɔka nkyerɛ ɔhene anaa ɔsafohene? Na ose: Me de, mete me nkurɔfo mu.

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Na dɛn na wɔnyɛ mma no? Na Gehasi se: Ampa, onni ba, na ne kunu nso anyin.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Afedan sesɛɛ bere yi mu no, wobɛwo ɔba. Na ose: Nyɛ sa, me wura, Onyankopɔn nipa, nni atoro nkyerɛ w’afenaa.

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no nyinsɛnee, na ɔwoo ɔbabarima afedan no mu, bere a Elisa ka kyerɛɛ no no mu.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Na abofra no nyinii. Na da bi ofii adi kɔɔ n’agya nkyɛn awitwafo nkyɛn.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’agya sɛ: Me ti, me ti! Na ɔka kyerɛɛ aberante bi sɛ: Ma no so kɔma ne na.

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa no so de no brɛɛ ne na; na ɔde no tenaa ne nankoroma so kosii owigyinae, na owui.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Na ɔforo de no kɔtoo Onyankopɔn nipa no mpa no so, na ɔtoo ɔpon no mu na ofii adi.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔfrɛɛ ne kunu sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, soma mmerante no mu biako ne mfurum abere no mu biako brɛ me, na mintutu mmirika menkɔ Onyankopɔn nipa no nkyɛn na memmra.

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na wopɛ sɛ wokɔ ne nkyɛn nnɛ yi? Ɛnyɛ ɔsram foforo, na ɛnyɛ homeda. Na ose: Ɛwom.

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhyehyɛɛ afurummere no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’abofra no sɛ: Ka no kɔ ntɛm ara, ngow ammirikatu mu mma me, gye sɛ meka mekyerɛ wo.

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Na osiim, na obeduu Onyankopɔn nipa no nkyɛn Karmel bepɔw so. Na Onyankopɔn nipa no huu no akyirikyiri no, ɔka kyerɛɛ n’abofra Gehasi sɛ: Hwɛ, Sunemni no ni.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Afei tu mmirika kohyia no, na bisa no se: Wo ho ye anaa? Wo kunu ho ye anaa? Abofra no ho ye anaa? Na ose: Wɔn ho ye.

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Na oduu Onyankopɔn nipa no nkyɛn bepɔw no so no, obesusoo ne nan; na Gehasi twiw bɛnee sɛ obesum no. Na Onyankopɔn nipa no kae sɛ: Gyaa no, na ne kra werɛ ahow wɔ no mu, na AWURADE de ahintaw me, na wanka ankyerɛ me.

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbea no kae sɛ: So mebɛsrɛɛ me wura hɔ ɔba? So manka sɛ: Nnaadaa me!

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔka kyerɛɛ Gehasi sɛ: Bɔ wo ho so, na fa me poma kura na kɔ; woto obi a, nkyia no, nso obi kyia wo a, nnye no so: Na fa me poma no kɔto abofra no anim.

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Na abofra no na kae sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE te ase na wo kra te ase yi, merennyaw wo! Ɛnna ɔsɔre dii n’akyi.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Na Gehasi dii wɔn anim kɔe, na ɔde poma no kɔtoo abofra no anim; nanso wante ɛnne bi, na wanhu nkwa ho sɛnkyerɛnne bi. Na ɔsan kohyiaa no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Abofra no nnyanee ɛ.

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Na Elisa duu ofie hɔ no, na hwɛ, abofra no awu da ne mpa so.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔkɔɔ mu, na ɔtoo wɔn baanu pon mu, na ɔbɔɔ AWURADE mpae.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Na ɔforo kobutuw abofra no so, na ɔde n’ano butuw n’ano, na ɔde n’aniwa butuw n’aniwa so, na ɔde ne nsam totoo ne nsam, na ɔponoo ne mu, abofra no so, na abofra no honam yɛɛ hyew.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsan bae bɛnantew ɔdan no mu dii hɔ akɔneaba, na ɔforo kɔɔ bio kɔponoo ne mu wɔ no so. Ɛnna abofra no nwansii mpɛn asɔn, na abofra no buee n’aniwa.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛɛ Gehasi sɛ: Frɛ Sunemni no! Na ɔfrɛɛ no, na ɔbaa ne nkyɛn. Na ɔkae sɛ: Fa wo ba no!

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔbae bɛhwee ne nan ase kotow no butuw fam, na ɔfaa ne ba no fii adi. Ɔsɛn mu awuduru. Nnipa ɔha aduanma

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa san baa Gilgal. Na ɔkɔm aba asase no so, na adiyifo mma no tete n’anim. Na ɔka kyerɛɛ n’abofra sɛ: Fa ɔsɛnkɛse si so noa aduan ma adiyifo mma no.

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Na obiako fi kɔɔ wuram sɛ ɔkɔtetew fan, na okohuu wuram hama bi, na ɔtetew so wuram ɛfere ne ntama ma, na ɔba betwitwaa mu guu ɔsɛn a aduan wɔ mu no mu; nso na wonnim.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna wohwie maa nnipa no sɛ wonni. Na wɔredi aduan no bi no, wɔteɛɛm sɛ: Awuduru wɔ ɔsɛn no mu, Onyankopɔn nipa! Na wontumi nni.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ɛnne momfa osiam mmra. Na ɔde guu ɔsɛn no mu, na ɔkae sɛ: Hwie ma nkurɔfo no na wonni. Na biribi bɔne bi nni ɔsɛn no mu bio.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔde sii wɔn anim; na wodii, na wogyaw bi, sɛnea Awurade kae no.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Na Siria hene sahene Naaman yɛ onipa kɛse ne wura anim, na ɔwɔ anuonyam, efisɛ ɔno so na AWURADE nam gyee Siria; na onipa no yɛ dɔmmarima a otumi, nso ɔyare kwata.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Nso na da bi Siria asafo bi, afi adi kɔ, nam ɔhyɛ so akɔfa Israel asase so abaawa kumaa bi dommum aba; na ɔsom Naaman yere.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔkɔ kɔka kyerɛɛ ne wura sɛ: Sɛɛ ne sɛɛ na abaawa a ofi Israel asase so no ka.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Na Siria hene no kae sɛ: Kɔ na bra, na mɛkyerɛw Israel hene no nhoma. Na osiim kɔe, na ɔfaa dwetɛ dwetikɛse du ne sika nnwetɛbona mpemnsia ne ntade nsakraho du kurae.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Na ɔde nhoma no brɛɛ Israel hene sɛ: Sɛ nhoma yi ka wo nsa a, hwɛ, masoma m’akoa Naaman aba wo nkyɛn sɛ sa ne kwata no ma no.

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa somaa ɔbɔfo kɔɔ ne nkyɛn sɛ: Kɔ na koguare mpɛn ason Yordan mu, na wo ho bɛsan aba wo ho, na wo ho afi.

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Na Israel hene kan nhoma no, osunsuanee ne ntade mu kae sɛ: So Onyankopɔn ne me na mekum na mama nkwa, sɛ oyi resoma aba me nkyɛn sɛ mensa obi kwata yi? Ampa, monhwɛ nhu sɛ asɛm na ɔrepɛ me.

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa Elisa tee sɛ Israel hene asunsuane ne ntade mu no, ɔsoma kɔɔ ɔhene no nkyɛn sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na woasunsuane wo ntade mu? Ma ɔmmra me nkyɛn ɛ, na onhu sɛ odiyifo wɔ Israel.

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Naaman ne n’apɔnkɔ ne ne nteaseɛnam ba begyinaa Elisa fi pon ano.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Naaman bo fuwii, osiim kɔe kae sɛ: Hwɛ, misusuwii sɛ: Ofi na obefi aba abegyina hɔ abɔ AWURADE ne Nyankopɔn din, na ɔde ne nsa asra hɔ, na wasa kwata no.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: So Damasko nsubɔnten Abana ne Farpar nye nsen Israel nsu nyinaa? So anka merenguare mu na me ho mfi anaa? Na ɔdan ne ho de abufuw sii mu.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa twiw bɛnee bɛka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Agya, sɛ ade kɛse bi na odiyifo no ka kyerɛɛ wo a, anka worenyɛ anaa? Na menne sɛ waka akyerɛ wo sɛ: Koguare na wo ho mfi!

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Ɛnna osianee de ne ho kɔbɔɔ Yordan mu mpɛn asɔn, sɛnea Onyankopɔn nipa no asɛm no te; na ne honam san baa mu sɛ abofra ketewa honam, na ne ho fii.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Na ɔsan baa Onyankopɔn nipa no nkyɛn, ɔno ne n’asafo nyinaa, na wɔba begyinaa n’anim kae sɛ: Hwɛ, mahu sɛ Onyankopɔn bi nni asase nyinaa so sɛ Israel nko, na afei gye akyɛde yi w’akoa nsam.

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nnipa no se: Sɛ AWURADE a migyina n’anim te ase yi, merennye hwee. Na Naaman hyɛɛ no sɛ onnye, nso wampene.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Naaman kae sɛ: Sɛ ɛnte saa a, ma wɔmfa dɔte a mfurumpɔnkɔ abien betumi asoa mma w’akoa, na w’akoa remmɔ ɔhyew afɔre anaa afɔre biara mma onyame biara bio sɛ AWURADE nko.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Asɛm yi mu nko na AWURADE mfa nkyɛ w’akoa: Sɛ me wura rekɔ Rimon fi akɔsɔre hɔ, na otweri me nsa so, na mekotow Rimon fi. Sɛ mekotow Rimon fi a, AWURADE mfa nkyɛ w’akoa, asɛm yi mu.

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ asomdwoe mu. Gehasi sikapɛ ne ɛho asotwe Na osiim fii ne nkyɛn kɔɔ ɔkwantiaa bi.

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa Elisa abofra Gehasi kae sɛ: Hwɛ, me wura agyaa Siriani Naaman yi, sɛ wannye nea ɔde bae no ne nsam; sɛ AWURADE te ase yi, metu mmirika matiw no makogye no hɔ biribi.

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Na Gehasi tiw Naaman. Na Naaman hui sɛ obi de mmirika di n’akyi no, ofii teaseɛnam no mu sii fam behyiaa no kae sɛ: Asomdwoe mu anaa?

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Na Gehasi se: Asomdwoe mu. Me wura asoma me sɛ: Hwɛ, mprempren yi mmerante baanu a wofi adiyifo mma no mu fi Efraim bepɔw so aba me nkyɛn, mesrɛ wo, ma wɔn dwetɛ talente biako ne ntade nsakraho abien.

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Na Naaman kae sɛ: Pene so na gye talente abien. Na ɔhyɛɛ no, na ɔkyekyeree talente abien no mmoaa abien ne ntade nsakraho abien no, na ɔde soaa ne mmerante no mu baanu, na wɔsoa dii n’anim.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Na oduu koko no ho no, Gehasi gye fii wɔn nsam, na ɔde maa asie ofie, na ogyaa mmarima no kwan ma wɔkɔe.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Na ɔno de, ɔbae begyinaa ne wura ho. Na Elisa kae sɛ: Gehasi, ɛhe na wufi? Na ose: W’akoa nkɔɔ baabi ɛ!

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Me koma ne wo ankɔ bere a ɔbarima no dan ne ho fii ne teaseɛnam mu behyiaa wo no? So bere a wogye dwetɛ na wogye ntade ne ngo nnua ne bobe nturo ne nguan ne anantwi ne nkoa ne mfanaa ni?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Na Naaman kwata no bɛfam wo ne w’asefo ho daa. Na ofii n’anim fii adi, na kwata ayɛ no fitaa sɛ sukyerɛma.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Na adiyifo mma no ka kyerɛɛ Elisa sɛ: Hwɛ, w’anim ha a yɛte yi yɛ hihiaa papa ma yɛn.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Ma yɛnkɔ Yordan ano na yɛnkɔfofa mpuran mmiako mmiako mfi hɔ, na yensiesie baabi wɔ hɔ ntena hɔ. Na ose: Monkɔ ɛ!

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Na obiako kae sɛ: Pene so na wo ne wo nkoa nkɔ. Na ose: Me nso mɛkɔ.

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Na ɔne wɔn siim kɔe. Na woduu Yordan ano no, wɔtotow nnua no.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa no kae sɛ: Ɛhe na ɛtɔe? Na ɔkyerɛɛ no hɔ. Na otwaa dua bi too hɔ, na dade no bɛtɛn ani.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Ma so fa! Na ɔteɛɛ ne nsa fae. Wɔde anifurae bɔ Siriafo

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Na Siria hene ne Israel bedii dɔm; na ɔne ne nkoa tuu agyina sɛ: Ɛha ne ha na mɛbɔ me nsra.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa no soma kɔɔ Israel hene nkyɛn sɛ: Hwɛ yiye, na woamfa ha, efisɛ ɛhɔ na Siriafo nam reba.

english_verse: So the king would warn the Israelite troops in that place to be on guard.
translation_verse: Na Israel hene soma kɔɔ faako a Onyankopɔn nipa no ka kyerɛɛ no na otuu no ho fo no, na ɔsraa hɔ, ɛnyɛ pɛnkoro na ɛnyɛ mprenu nko.

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Siria hene koma peree no asɛm yi ho; na ɔfrɛɛ ne nkoa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: So morenkyerɛ me yɛn mu nea ɔwɔ Israel hene afa?

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa no mu biako kae sɛ: Me wura ɔhene, ɛnte sa, na mmom odiyifo Elisa a ɔwɔ Israel no na ɔka nsɛm a woka wo dabekyiri no kyerɛ Israel hene.

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Na ose: Monkɔ nkɔsra nea ɔwɔ, na mensoma mma wɔnkɔfa no mmra. Na wɔkyerɛɛ no sɛ: Hwɛ, ɔwɔ Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsomaa apɔnkɔ ne nteaseɛnam ne dɔm kɛse kɔɔ hɔ, na wodui anadwo, na wobetwaa kurow no ho hyiae.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Na Onyankopɔn nipa no somfo tuaa ahema sɛ ɔresɔre afi adi no, na hwɛ, dɔm ne apɔnkɔ ne nteaseɛnam atwa kurow no ho ahyia. Na n’abofra no ka kyerɛɛ, no sɛ: Ao, me wura, yɛbɛyɛ dɛn?

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Nsuro, na wɔn a wɔka yɛn ho dɔɔso sen wɔn a wɔka wɔn ho no.

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Na Elisa bɔɔ mpae sɛ: AWURADE, bue n’ani na onhu. Na AWURADE buee aberante no aniwa, na ohui, na hwɛ, ogya apɔnkɔ ne nteaseɛnam ayɛ bepɔw no so ma atwa Elisa ho ahyia.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Ɛnna wosian baa ne nkyɛn; na Elisa bɔɔ AWURADE mpae sɛ: Mesrɛ wo, fa anifurae bɔ dɔm yi! Na ɔde anifurae bɔɔ wɔn, sɛ Elisa kae no.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Na Elisa ka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Ɛnyɛ ɔkwan ni, na ɛnyɛ kurow no ni, munni m’akyi, na memfa mo menkɔ ɔbarima a morehwehwɛ no no nkyɛn. Na ɔde wɔn kɔɔ Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Na woduu Samaria no, Elisa kae sɛ: AWURADE, bue eyinom aniwa, na wohui, na hwɛ, wɔwɔ Samaria mfinimfini.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Na Israel hene huu wɔn no, ɔka kyerɛɛ Elisa sɛ: Agya, so memmobɔ wɔn anaa?

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Na ose: Mmobɔ wɔn. Nea wode wo nkrante ne wo ta afa no dommum no na wobɔ no. Fa aduan ne nsu sisi wɔn anim na wonni na wɔnnom, na wɔnkɔ wɔn wura nkyɛn.

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Na ɔtow pon kɛse maa wɔn; na wodidii na wɔnomee no, ogyaa wɔn kwan, na wosiim kɔɔ wɔn wura nkyɛn. Na Siria afowfo asafo no antoa so amma Israel asase so bio. Ɔkɔm ba Samaria

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Na ɛno akyi no, Siria hene Ben-hadad boaa ne dɔm nyinaa ano hyiae, na ɔforo ba betuaa Samaria.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔm kɛse baa Samaria, na hwɛ, wɔkaa wɔn hyɛɛ mu ara de kosii sɛ wɔtɔn afurum ti gyee nnwetɛbona aduɔwɔtwe, na mmorɔnoma bin abupɛn anan mu biako gyee nnwetɛbona anum.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Na Israel hene retwam ɔfasu so no, ɔbea bi bɔn no sɛ: Owura ɔhene, boa me!

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Na ose: Sɛ AWURADE ammoa wo a, mefi he na maboa wo? Emfi awiporowbea anaa nsa-kyi-amoa mu?

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Ɛdɛn na ɛyɛ wo? Na ose: Ɔbea yi ka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Fa wo ba ma yenni no nnɛ, na yɛadi me ba ɔkyena.

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Na yɛnoaa me ba no dii; na ade kyee no, meka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Fa wo ba no bra ma yenni ɛ! Nanso ɔde ne ba no asie.

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene tee ɔbea no nsɛm no, osunsuanee ne ntade mu; na ɔretwam ɔfasu no so no, nkurɔfo no hwɛe, na hwɛ, ofura atweatam wɔ ase de akata ne honam ani.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ Safat ba Elisa ti toa no so nnɛ adesae a, Onyankopɔn nyɛ me sɛɛ na ɔnto so sɛɛ!

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Nso na Elisa te ne fi, na mpanyimfo no tete ne nkyɛn. Na ɔhene somaa onipa dii n’anim. Na ɔbɔfo no nnya nnuu ne nkyɛn no, ɔno ara ka kyerɛɛ mpanyimfo no sɛ: Sɛ muhu sɛ owudifo ba yi asoma sɛ wɔmmɛfa me ti? Monhwɛ, sɛ ɔbɔfo no ba a, monto pon mu, na mumpia no nkɔ ɔpon ano; so ɛnyɛ ne wura nan ase pim pim na edi n’akyi yi?

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Na ɔda so ne wɔn rekasa no, hwɛ, na ɔbɔfo no resian aba ne nkyɛn. Na ɔkae sɛ: Hwɛ, bɔne yi fi AWURADE nkyɛn, dɛn na mentwɛn AWURADE minnye bio?

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna Elisa kae sɛ: Muntie AWURADE asɛm: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Ɔkyena sesɛɛ awisam susuw ade biako bedi dwetɛbona, na atoko susuw ade abien bedi dwetɛbona, Samaria kurow pon ano.

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Ɛnna okunini a ɔhene tweri ne nsa so no buaa Onyankopɔn nipa no sɛ: Hwɛ, sɛ AWURADE reyɛ mfɛnsere ɔsoro po a, so saa asɛm yi bɛbam anaa? Na ose: Wo ara wode w’aniwa behu, nanso worenni bi.

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Na mmarima akwatafo baanan wɔ kurow no pon ano, na wosisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Ɛdɛn na yɛtete ha kosi sɛ yebewuwu?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Sɛ yese: Yɛbɛhyɛn kurow no mu a, ɛnne ɔkɔm wɔ kurow no mu na yebewuwu hɔ; na sɛ yɛtete ha yi nso a, yebewuwu; na afei mommra mma yɛnkɔhwe Siriafo nsra no mu: Sɛ wogye yɛn nkwa a, yɛbɛtena ase, sɛ wokum yɛn nso a, yɛawu!

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna wosisee wɔn ho wɔn ho sɛ: Nea yɛreyɛ yi nye, ɛnnɛ da yi yɛ asɛmpa da, na yɛn de, yɛayɛ komm; na sɛ yɛtwɛn kosi adekyee a, asotwe bi bɛto yɛn; enti momma yɛnkɔ ahemfi nkɔka!

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Na wɔba bɛfrɛɛ kurow no apon ano hwɛfo, na wɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Yɛkɔɔ Siriafo nsram, na hwɛ, onipa biara ne onipa nne biara nni hɔ, gye apɔnkɔ a wɔasesa wɔn ne mfurum a wɔasesa wɔn ne ntamadan no.

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔpon ano hwɛfo no frɛ ma wɔkɔkae ahemfi.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔhene sɔree anadwo no, na ɔka kyerɛɛ ne nkoa sɛ: Mɛkyerɛ mo nea Siriafo ayɛ yɛn yi: Wonim sɛ ɔkɔm de yɛn, enti na wɔafi nsram hɔ kɔ sɛ wokohintaw wuram se: Sɛ wofi kurow no mu ba a, yɛakyekyere wɔn animono, na yɛakɔhyɛn kurow no mu.

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa no mu biako buae sɛ: Ɛnne ma wɔmfa apɔnkɔ nkae a wɔaka kurom ha no mu anum, hwɛ, wɔte sɛ Israel dodow a wɔaka mu no, hwɛ, wɔte sɛ Israel dodow a wɔahyew no: Na ma yɛnsoma wɔn na yɛnhwɛ.

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Na wɔfaa apɔnkɔ nteaseɛnam abien na ɔhene somaa wɔn dii Siriafo dɔm no akyi sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔhwɛ!

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Na wodii wɔn akyi koduu Yordan ano, na hwɛ, ntade ne nneɛmanneɛma a Siriafo atotow agu wɔn ntɛmpɛ no mu ayɛ ɔkwan no nyinaa so ma. Na abɔfo no san ba bɛka kyerɛɛ ɔhene.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ɛnna nkurɔfo no fii adi kɔfow Siriafo nsra no. Na ɛmo susuw ade biako dii dwetɛbona, na atoko susuw ade abien nso dii dwetɛbona, sɛnea AWURADE kae no.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Na ɔhene yii okunini a otweri ne nsa so no sɛ ɔnhwɛ ɔpon ano; na nkurɔfo no tiatiaa no so ɔpon no mu, na owui, sɛnea Onyankopɔn nipa no kae, bere a ɔhene sian baa ne nkyɛn no.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Na ɛbaa mu sɛnea Onyankopɔn nipa no ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene no sɛ: Atoko susuw ade bedi dwetɛbona, na awisam susuw ade biako nso bedi dwetɛbona ɔkyena sesɛɛ, Samaria kurow pon ano.

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: Na ɔsafohene no buaa Onyankopɔn nipa no sɛ: Na hwɛ, sɛ AWURADE reyɛ mfɛnsere ɔsoro po a, so ɛbɛba saa anaa? Na ose: Hwɛ, wo de, wode w’aniwa behu, nanso worenni bi.

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Na ɛyɛɛ no saa ara, na nkurɔfo no tiatiaa no kurow pon no mu, na owui.

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
translation_verse: Na mfe ason no awiei no, ɔbea no san fii Filistifo asase so bae, na ofii adi kosu hyɛɛ ɔhene sɛ ɔregye ne fi ne n’asase.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Nso na ɔhene ne Onyankopɔn nipa no abofra Gehasi rekasa sɛ: Ka me nneɛma akɛse a Elisa ayɛ no ɛ!

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: Na ɔreka ɔhene sɛnea onyan awufo no, hwɛ, ɔbea a onyan ne ba ma onyaa nkwa no besu hyɛɛ ɔhene sɛ ɔregye ne fi ne n’asase. Na Gehasi kae sɛ: Me wura ɔhene, ɔbea no ni, nea ne ba a Elisa ma onyaa nkwa no ni.

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Na Elisa kɔɔ Damasko; nso na Siria hene Ben-hadad yare; na wɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Onyankopɔn nipa no aba ha.

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Na Hasael ba behyiaa no, na ɔfaa ayɛyɛde kurae, ɛyɛ Damasko nneɛma pa nyinaa bi, yoma aduanan na ɛsosoe. Na ɔba begyinaa n’anim sɛ: Wo ba Ben-hadad, Siria hene, na ɔsomaa me wo nkyɛn sɛ: So menya ɔyare yi mu nkwa anaa?

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Kɔ kɔka kyerɛ no sɛ: Nkwa de, wubenya, nanso AWURADE akyerɛ me sɛ obewu ara.

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Na ogyen n’ani hwɛɛ no dinn kosii sɛ n’ani bui, na Onyankopɔn nipa no sui.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Na Hasael kae sɛ: Ɛdɛn nti na me wura resu? Na ose: Efisɛ minim bɔne a wobɛyɛ Israelfo. Wɔn nkurow a ɛyɛ den no wobɛtoto mu gya, na wode nkrante bekunkum wɔn mmerante, na woatetew wɔn nkokoaa ahwehwe fam, na woapaapae wɔn apemfo mu.

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Na Hasael kae sɛ: Hena ne w’akoa ɔkraman yi a ɔbɛyɛ ade kɛse yi? Na Elisa se: AWURADE ama mahu sɛ wo na wubedi Siria so hene.

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Na ade kyee no, ɔfaa mmuatama no bɔɔ nsu mu de kataa n’anim, na owui. Na Hasael bedii n’ade. Yoram di Yuda so hene (

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Na Yoram twaam kɔɔ Sair a ne nteaseɛnam nyinaa ka ne ho; na ɔsɔree anadwo kokunkum Edomfo a wɔatwa ne ho ahyia ne nteaseɛnam so asafohene no; na nkurɔfo no guan kokɔɔ wɔn ntamadan mu.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Ne bere so na Edom tew atua fii Yuda nsa ase, na wokosii wɔn so hene.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Israel hene Ahab ba Yoram afe a ɛto so anum so, bere a Yehosafat dii Yuda hene no, na Yuda hene Yehosafat ba Yehoram bedii hene.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa Israel ahene kwan so sɛnea Ahab fi yɛe; efisɛ ne yere yɛ Ahab ba. Na ɔyɛɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Nanso n’akoa Dawid nti AWURADE ampɛ sɛ ɔsɛe Yuda, sɛnea ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ ɔbɛma ɔno ne ne mma kanea nna nyinaa no.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Yoram ho nsɛm nkae ne nea ɔyɛe nyinaa, so wɔankyerɛw Yuda ahene beresosɛm nhoma no mu?

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Na Yoram wui, na wosiee no kaa n’agyanom ho Dawid kurow mu; na ne ba Ahasia bedii n’ade. Ahasia di Yuda so hene (

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Israel hene Ahab ba Yoram afe a ɛto so dumien so na Yuda hene Yehoram ba Ahasia bedii hene.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: Na ɔfaa Ahab fi kwan so, na ɔyɛɛ AWURADE ani so bɔne sɛ Ahab fi, efisɛ Ahab sew ne no.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Na ɔne Ahab ba Yoram kɔe ne Siria hene Hasael kɔkoe Ramot-gilead. Na Siriafo piraa Yoram.

english_verse: One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said: Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Na odiyifo Elisa frɛɛ adiyifo mma no mu biako ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Bɔ wo ho so, na fa ngo toa yi kura, na kɔ Ramot-gilead.

english_verse: When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone,
translation_verse: Na sɛ wudu hɔ a, hwehwɛ Nimsi ba Yehosafat ba Yehu fi, na kɔ mu, na ma ɔnsɔre mfi ne nuanom mu, na fa no kɔ mpiakyiri pia mu,

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: na fa ngo toa no hwie gu n’atifi, na ka sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Masra wo masi Israel so hene. Na hiɛ ɔpon no na guan, na nnyina.

english_verse: The young prophet left for Ramoth.
translation_verse: Ɛnna aberante a ɔyɛ odiyifo aberante no siim kɔɔ Ramot-gilead.

english_verse: When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said. “For which one of us?” Jehu asked. “You, sir,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Na odui no, na hwɛ, dɔm so asafohene tete hɔ; na ɔkae sɛ: Mewɔ asɛm bi ka kyerɛ wo, ɔsafohene. Na Yehu se: Wode yɛn nyinaa mu hena? Na ose: Mede wo, ɔsafohene.

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsɔre kɔɔ ɔdan no mu, na ohwiee ngo no guu n’atifi, na ɔka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE Israel Nyankopɔn se ni: Masra wo masi wo AWURADE man Israel so hene;

english_verse: I want you to wipe out the family of Ahab, so Jezebel will be punished for killing the prophets and my other servants.
translation_verse: na wobɛbɔ wo wura Ahab fi, na matɔ me nkoa adiyifo no mogya ne AWURADE nkoa nyinaa mogya so were Yesebel nsam;

english_verse: Every man and boy in Ahab's family must die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: na Ahab fi nyinaa asɛe, na matwa Ahabni barima biara afi Israel mu akyene, sɛ ɔyɛ akoa, anaa ɔdehye.

english_verse: His whole family must be destroyed, just like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.
translation_verse: Na mɛyɛ Ahab fi sɛ Nebat ba Yeroboam fi ne Ahia ba Basa fi.

english_verse: As for Jezebel, her body will be eaten by dogs in the town of Jezreel. There won't be enough left of her to bury.” Then the young prophet opened the door and ran out.
translation_verse: Na akraman bedi Yesebel nam, Yesreel asase so, na obi nni hɔ a obesie no. Na ohiɛɛ ɔpon no guanee.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Na Yehu fii adi baa ne wura nkoa nkyɛn. Na obi ka kyerɛɛ no sɛ: Eye anaa? Ɛdɛn nti na ɔbɔdamfo yi baa wo nkyɛn yi? Na ɔka kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ: Mo ara munim ɔbarima no ne ne nsɛnkekae.

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Na wose: Atoro! Ka kyerɛ yɛn ɛ! Na ose: Sɛɛ ne sɛɛ na ɔka kyerɛɛ me sɛ: Sɛ AWURADE se ni: Masra wo masi wo Israel so hene.

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Ɛnna wɔyɛɛ ntɛm yiyii wɔn ntama de hyehyɛɛ n’ase atrapoe no ara so, na wɔhyɛn torobɛnto sɛ: Yehu adi hene! Yehu kunkum Yoram ne Ahasia

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɛmfo gyina Yesreel abantenten so; na ohuu Yehu asafokuw no sɛ wɔreba, na ɔkae sɛ: Mihu asafokuw bi. Na Yoram se: Frɛ ɔpɔnkɔsotefo soma no ma onkohyia wɔn, na ɔnka sɛ: Asomdwoe so anaa?

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Na ɔpɔnkɔsotefo bi ka kohyiaa no, na ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ ɔhene se ni: Asomdwoe so anaa? Na Yehu se: Asomdwoe fa wo ho dɛn? Bɛsen kɔ m’akyi! Na ɔwɛmfo no kaa sɛ: Ɔbɔfo no adu wɔn nkyɛn, nso ɔnsan mma.

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
translation_verse: Ɛnna ɔsomaa ɔpɔnkɔsotefo a oto so abien, na okoduu wɔn nkyɛn no, ɔkae sɛ: Sɛ ɔhene se ni: Asomdwoe so anaa? Na Yehu se: Asomdwoe fa wo ho dɛn? Bɛsɛn kɔ m’akyi!

english_verse: The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
translation_verse: Na ɔwɛmfo no kae sɛ: Wadu wɔn nkyɛn, nso ɔnsan mma. Na [teaseɛnam no] ka no te sɛ Nimsi ba Yehu de, na ɔka no dennen pa ara.

english_verse: Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoram kae sɛ: Munsiesie teaseɛnam no! Na wosiesiei. Na Israel hene Yoram ne Yuda hene Ahasia fii adi, wɔn nteaseɛnam mu, na wofi kohyiaa Yehu, na wɔkɔtoo no Yesreelni Nabot asase no so.

english_verse: Joram asked, “Jehu, is this a peaceful visit?” “How can there be peace?” Jehu asked. “Your mother Jezebel has caused everyone to worship idols and practice witchcraft.”
translation_verse: Na Yoram huu Yehu no, ɔkae sɛ: Yehu, asomdwoe so anaa? Na ose: Asomdwoe bɛyɛ dɛn aba, bere a wo na Yesebel aguamammɔ ne n’abayigoru bebree no rekɔ so yi?

english_verse: “Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape,
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yoram dan ne ho guanee, na ɔka kyerɛɛ Ahasia sɛ: Atirisopamsɛm ni, Ahasia!

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
translation_verse: Na Yehu de ne nsa soo bɛmma mu tow bɔɔ Yoram abasa ntam, na agyan no hwirew ne koma mu, na ɔhwee ne teaseɛnam mu.

english_verse: Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
translation_verse: Ampa ara, mihuu Nabot mogya ne ne mma mogya nnɛra! AWURADE na ose: Na metua wo ɛso ka, asase yi so, AWURADE na ose. Na afei ma no so tow no kyene asase yi so, sɛ AWURADE asɛm no te no.

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.
translation_verse: Na Yuda hene Ahasia hui no, ɔfaa turom dan kwan so guanee. Na Yehu tiw no, na ɔkaa sɛ: Mommɔ ɔno nso teaseɛnam no mu. Wɔyɛɛ saa Gur aforoe a ɛwɔ Yibleam ho no; na oguan kɔɔ Megido, na okowuu wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Na ne nkoa de no nam teaseɛnam mu kɔɔ Yerusalem; na wosiee no n’asiei kaa n’agyanom ho, Dawid kurow mu.

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Na Ahab ba Yoram afe a ɛto so dubiako so na Ahasia bedii Yuda so hene. Yesebel awiei a ɛyɛ hu

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Ɛnna Yehu baa Yesreel. Na Yesebel tee no, ɔkekaa n’aniwa ho adubiri na ɔhyehyɛɛ ne ti, na ɔhwɛɛ mfɛnsere mu.

english_verse: As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
translation_verse: Na Yehu duu ɔpon no ano no, ɔkae sɛ: So ɛyɛ asomdwoe, Simri a okum ne wura?

english_verse: He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window,
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa n’ani so hwɛɛ mfɛnsere no, na ɔkae sɛ: Hena na ɔwɔ m’afa, hena? Ɛnna pia mufo baanu anaa baasa buu wɔn ani kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
translation_verse: Na ɔkae sɛ: Montow no nhwe fam! Ɛnna wɔtow no hwee fam, na ne mogya bi petee ɔfasu ho ne apɔnkɔ no ho, na ɔde ne teaseɛnam faa no so.

english_verse: Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛn mu; na odidii na ɔnomee no, ɔkae sɛ: Monkɔ nkɔhwɛ ɔbea a wɔadome no no, na munsie no, efisɛ ɔyɛ ɔhene babea.

english_verse: But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet.
translation_verse: Na wɔkɔe sɛ wokosie no, nanso wɔanhu ne ho biribi gye ne tikora ne ne nan ne ne nsayam.

english_verse: They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Na wɔsan bɛka kyerɛɛ no; na ɔkae sɛ: AWURADE asɛm a ɔnam n’akoa Elia Tisbini no so kae no ni sɛ: Yesreel asase so na akraman bedi Yesebel nam,

english_verse: And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_verse: na Yesebel funu bɛpete ayɛ sɛ agyanan wɔ, Yesreel asase so, na obiara renhu mpo nka sɛ: Yesebel ni!

english_verse: Your town is strong, and you're protected by chariots and an armed cavalry. And I know that King Ahab's descendants live there with you. So as soon as you read this letter,
translation_verse: Sɛ nhoma yi ka mo nsa a, sɛ mo wura mma wɔ mo nkyɛn na nteaseɛnam ne apɔnkɔ ne ɔfasu mu kurow ne akode nso wɔ mo nkyɛn yi:

english_verse: choose the best person for the job and make him the next king. Then be prepared to defend Ahab's family.
