translation_verse: Ɔka kyerɛɛ nnipa no se, “Monsan mfi saa nnipabɔnefo yi ntamadan no mu! Mommfa mo nsa nka wɔn biribiara, anyɛ saa a wɔbɛsɛe mo ne wɔn nyinaa, esiane wɔn bɔne nti.”

english_verse: So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
translation_verse: Enti nnipa no fii Kora, Datan ne Abiram ntamadan no mu. Na Datan ne Abiram nso ne wɔn yerenom ne wɔn mma begyinagyinaa wɔn ntamadan no akwan ano.

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Mose kae se, “Ɛnam eyi so bɛma moahu sɛ, Awurade na ɔsomaa me sɛ menyɛ nea mayɛ yi nyinaa. Ɛnyɛ me ara mʼadwene mu na mifi yɛɛ saa.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Sɛ owu nko ara na ɛbɛto saa nnipa yi, anaa sɛ wohu nea ɛtaa ba nnipa so nko ara a, na ɛnyɛ Awurade na wasoma me.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na sɛ Awurade ma ade a ɛyɛ foforo koraa ba, na asase bue nʼanom mene wɔn ne wɔn ahode na sɛ wɔkɔ asaman anikann a, ɛbɛma moahu sɛ, saa nnipa yi abu Awurade animtiaa.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Ka a ɔkaa eyinom wiei ara pɛ, na asase a ɛwɔ wɔn ase no mu paee,

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Wowuraa asase mu anikann kɔɔ asaman na asase no san ka too mu ma wɔyera fii ɔman no mu.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Israelfo nyinaa guanee a na wɔreteɛteɛ mu se, “Asase rebɛmene yɛn nso!”

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent a fire that burned up the
translation_verse: Na ogya fi Awurade nkyɛn bɛhyew nnipa ahannu aduonum a na wɔrehyew aduhuam no nyinaa.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Ka kyerɛ ɔsɔfo Aaron babarima Eleasar sɛ onyi aduhuamyɛfo nkuku no mfi nso no mu, efisɛ ɛyɛ kronkron, na ɔntrɛtrɛw nnyansramma no mu nkɔ akyiri

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: mfi saa nnipa a wɔayɛ bɔne awu no aduhuamyɛfo nkuku no ase. Boro aduhuamhyew nkuku no mma ɛnyɛ ntrantraa na momfa nkata afɔremuka no so. Saa aduhuamyɛfo nkuku yi yɛ kronkron, efisɛ wɔde baa Awurade anim. Ma ɛnyɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne mma Israelfo no.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Enti ɔsɔfo Eleasar faa wɔn a wɔahyew no aduhuamyɛfo nkuku no na ɔboro maa ɛyɛɛ ntrantraa na ɔde kataa afɔremuka no so,

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: sɛnea Awurade nam Mose so kyerɛɛ no no. Na Israelfo no nam so akae se obiara a omfi Aaron ase no nni ho kwan sɛ ɔba Awurade anim bɛhyew aduhuam. Sɛ ɔyɛ saa a, asɛm a ɛtoo Kora ne ne ne dɔm no bi bɛto no.

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Ade kyee anɔpa no, Israelfo no nyinaa nwiinwii tiaa Mose ne Aaron se, “Moakum Awurade nkurɔfo.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Nanso bere a nnipa no nyinaa boaa wɔn ho ano sɛ wɔretia Mose ne Aaron na wotwaa wɔn ani hwɛɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan no, prɛko pɛ, omununkum no kataa so ma wohuu Awurade anuonyam.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Mose ne Aaron begyinaa Ahyiae Ntamadan no kwan ano,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Twe wo ho fi saa nnipa yi mu na matumi asɛe wɔn prɛko pɛ.” Na Mose ne Aaron de wɔn anim butubutuu fam.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: Na Mose ka kyerɛɛ Aaron se, “Fa aduhuamyɛfo kuku no na yi ogya fi afɔremuka no so gu mu. Fa aduhuam gu so na fa nnipa no mu ntɛm so fa kɔyɛ mpata ma wɔn, efisɛ Awurade abufuw adu wɔn so. Ɔyaredɔm no afi ase.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ɔyaredɔm no gyaee no, Aaron san kɔɔ Mose nkyɛn wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Momfa pema yi ngu Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu ahyiae mu wɔ baabi a mihyia mo wɔ adaka no anim hɔ no.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Menam pema yi so bɛkyerɛ onipa a meyi no no na ne pema no ho bɛfefɛw, na meyi Israelfo anwiinwii a wɔtaa nwiinwii tia wo no nyinaa afi hɔ.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Enti Mose maa Israelfo no maa no pema dumien a wɔn abusua no biara panyin de wɔ mu a na Aaron ka de ka ho bi.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose de guu Awurade anim wɔ Adanse Ntamadan no mu hɔ.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Ade kyee a ɔkɔɔ mu no, ohuu sɛ Aaron pema a ɛwɔ hɔ ma Lewi abusuakuw no afefɛw ayɛ frɔmm, asow aba a ɛsensɛn so.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Na Mose de pema no fii Awurade anim ba bɛkyerɛɛ Israelfo no. Wɔhwɛe, na ɔpanyin biara faa ne pema.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Fa Aaron pema no san kɔto adaka no anim na fa yɛ nsɛnkyerɛnne ma atuatewfo no. Eyi de anwiinwii a wonwiinwii tia me no bɛba awiei na wɔanwuwu.” Na ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde ba bɛkyerɛ nnipa no bio na sɛ anwiinwii bi wɔ hɔ a etia Aaron tumi a, ebesiw amanehunu foforo a anka ɛbɛba nnipa no so no ano.

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Mose yɛɛ nea Awurade hyɛɛ no sɛ ɔnyɛ no pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Israelfo no ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Yebewuwu! Yɛayera, yɛayera!

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Mpo, obiara a ɔbɛbɛn Awurade Ahyiae Ntamadan no bewu. Yɛn nyinaa rebewuwu ana?”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Fa wo nkurɔfo a wɔwɔ Lewi abusuakuw no mu na wɔmmoa wo mmabarima no wɔ dwuma kronkron a wodi no Ahyiae Ntamadan no anim no ho.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Ɛsɛ sɛ Lewifo no hwɛ yiye na wɔammɛn biribiara a ɛyɛ kronkron wɔ afɔremuka no so. Sɛ wɔyɛ saa a, wo ne wɔn bewuwu.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔka mo ho na mohwɛ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu hɔ; ɛhɔ nnwuma nyinaa. Ɛnsɛ sɛ onipa foforo biara bɛn beae a wowɔ no.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: “Wo na ɛsɛ sɛ wohwɛ kronkronbea hɔ ne afɔremuka no so, na mʼabufuwhyew amma Israelfo no so bio.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Mʼankasa na mapaw wo nkurɔfo Lewifo afi Israelfo mu sɛ akyɛde ama wo, atew wɔ ho ama Awurade sɛ wɔnyɛ adwuma wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Nanso wo ne wo mmabarima nkutoo na na mubedi dwuma sɛ asɔfo wɔ nea ɛfa afɔremuka ne nea ɛwɔ ntwamtam no mu no ho. Mede asɔfodwuma ɔsom rema mo sɛ akyɛde. Ɛsɛ sɛ wokum onipa foforo biara a ɔbɛbɛn kronkronbea hɔ no.”

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Saa mmoa yi nyinaa nam bɛyɛ mo de te sɛnea ohim afɔrebɔde koko ne ne srɛ nifa yɛ mo de no.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Munni no sɛ ade a ɛyɛ kronkron pa ara; ɔbarima biara nni bi. Mummu no sɛ ade kronkron.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: “Eyi nso yɛ mo de: nea wobeyi agu nkyɛn afi Israelfo ohim afɔrebɔde mu no. Mede ma wo ne wo mmabarima ne wo mmabea nyinaa sɛ mo kyɛfa afebɔɔ. Obiara a ɔwɔ wo fi na ne ho tew no tumi di bi.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Aba a edi kan mu akyɛde a nnipa no de bɛba sɛ afɔrebɔde a wɔde rebrɛ Awurade no a ɛyɛ ngo pa, bobesa pa, aburow ne nnɔbae biara no, mede ma mo.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Asase no so aba a edi kan a wɔde bɛbrɛ Awurade no bɛyɛ mo de. Obiara a ɔwɔ wo fi na ne ho tew no tumi di bi.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: “Biribiara a ɛwɔ Israel a wɔde bɛma Awurade no yɛ mo de.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Israelfo abakan ne wɔn mmoa nyinaa abakan a wɔde bɛma Awurade no yɛ mo dea. Nanso mmoa a memmaa mo kwan sɛ wɔnwe wɔn nam no de, munnnye wɔn abakan. Na mmom, ɛsɛ sɛ wotua sika kakra de si abakan biara anan.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Sɛ abakan no di ɔsram a, na ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ogye bo a ɛyɛ dwetɛ nkaribo gram aduonum asia sɛnea kronkronbea hɔ nkaribo a ɛyɛ gram dubaako ne nkyemu anum mu baako no te no ba.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Nanso anantwi, nguan ne mmirekyi mmakan de, ɛnsɛ sɛ wogye wɔn; wɔyɛ kronkron. Fa wɔn mogya pete afɔremuka no so na hyew wɔn srade no sɛ aduan afɔre, ehua a ɛsɔ Awurade ani.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Biribiara a Israelfo de bɛbrɛ Awurade a wobefi afɔrebɔ kronkron mu ayi ato hɔ no, mede ma wo ne wo mmabarima ne wo mmabea sɛ mo kyɛfa afebɔɔ. Ɛyɛ ahyɛde a ɛda mo ne Awurade ne mo asefo ntam daa nyinaa.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Aaron se, “Morennya agyapade biara mfi wɔn asase mu, na morennya kyɛfa biara mfi wɔn mu; mene mo kyɛfa ne mo agyapade wɔ Israelfo no mu.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “Mede Israel ntotoso du du no nyinaa ma Lewifo no sɛ wɔn agyapade de retua wɔ som a wɔsom wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no mu no so ka.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Lewifo no nko ara na wɔbɛyɛ adwuma wɔ hɔ, na wɔasoa mfomso biara a wɔbɛyɛ no ho asodi. Ɛyɛ mmara a ɛda hɔ afebɔɔ ma awo ntoatoaso a ɛbɛba no. Wɔrennya agyapade biara wɔ Israelfo no mu.

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: Mmom, ntotoso du du a Israelfo no de ba sɛ Awurade afɔrebɔde no na mede rema Lewifo no. Ɛno nti na meka faa wɔn ho se: ‘Wɔrennya agyapade wɔ Israelfo no mu no.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Ka kyerɛ Lewifo no se, ‘Sɛ munya ntotoso du du a mede rema mo sɛ mo agyapade no fi Israelfo no nkyɛn a, momfa nkyɛmu du mu baako mmrɛ Awurade sɛ nʼafɔrebɔde.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Na Awurade begye no sɛ mo afɔrebɔde a efi mo awiporowbea anaa nsa a efi mo nsakyi amoa mu.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Biribiara a wɔde bɛma mo no, momfa emu nea eye pa ara na ɛyɛ kronkron no mma Awurade.’

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: “Ka kyerɛ Lewifo no se: ‘Sɛ mode emu nea eye pa ara no ba a, wɔbɛfa no sɛ nea efi mo ankasa mo awiporowbea anaa mo nsakyibea hɔ.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mo ne mo fifo betumi adi nkae no wɔ baabiara a mopɛ, efisɛ ɛyɛ mo adwuma a moyɛ no wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan mu no so akatua.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Sɛ mode emu nea ɛsɔ ani no ba a, munni eyi ho afɔbu; saayɛ remma mungu Israelfo no afɔrebɔ kronkron no ho fi, na morenwuwu.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Eyi yɛ mmara a ɛsɛ sɛ wodi so a Awurade ahyɛ: Ka kyerɛ Israelfo se wɔmfa nantwi ba bere kɔkɔɔ a onnii dɛm na ɔntwee nneɛma da mmrɛ me.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Momfa no mma ɔsɔfo Eleasar na ɔde no bɛkɔ atenae no akyi baabi na wɔakum no wɔ nʼanim.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo Eleasar de ne nsateaa bɛbɔ mogya no mu na ɔde apete Ahyiae Ntamadan no anim mpɛn ason.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Afei, ɔbɛhwɛ ama obi ahyew nantwi ba no. Wɔbɛhyew ne ho nhoma, ne nam, ne mogya ne ne nsono.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Na egu so rehyew no, Eleasar bɛfa sida dua, adwerɛ ne asaawa kɔkɔɔ na watow agu nantwi ba bere a wɔrehyew no so.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Eyi akyi no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔsɔfo no horo ne ntade na oguare. Afei obetumi aba atenae hɔ, nanso ne ho rentew kosi anwummere.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Onipa a ɔhyew aboa no nso, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntade na oguare, na ɔno nso ho rentew kosi anwummere.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: “Ɔbarima a ne ho nguu fi no bɛsesaw aboa a wɔhyew no no nsõ de akogu atenae no akyi baabi a ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron. Ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo no de sie na wɔde agu wɔn ahodwira nsu mu; ɛyɛ nea wɔde dwira wɔn ho fi bɔne ho.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Onipa a ɔbɛboaboa nantwi ba no nsõ no ano no nso, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntade, na ɔno nso ho rentew kosi anwummere. Eyi bɛyɛ mmara a ɛbɛtena hɔ afebɔɔ ama Israelfo no ne ahɔho a wɔte wɔn mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Obiara a obeso onipa funu mu no ho begu fi nnanson.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Na ne nnansa ne ne nnanson so no, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔde nsu dwira ne ho ma ne ho tew. Sɛ wannwira ne ho nnansa ne nnanson so a ne ho rentew.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɔn a woso nnipa funu mu na wonnwira wɔn ho no, wogu Awurade Ntamadan no ho fi. Ɛsɛ sɛ woyi saa nnipa no fi Israelfo mu. Esiane sɛ wɔamfa ahodwira nsu no bi ampete wɔn ho no nti, wɔn ho ntew; wɔn ho a agu fi no da so wɔ wɔn so.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Sɛ obi wu wɔ ntamadan mu a, ɛho mmara ni: Obiara a obewura saa ntamadan no mu ne wɔn a wɔwɔ mu dedaw ansa na onipa no rewu no nyinaa ho begu fi nnanson,

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: na ade biara a enni mmuaso na wɔde asa no nso ho begu fi.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Sɛ obi a ɔwɔ abɔnten de ne nsa ka obi a ɔtɔɔ wɔ afoa ano funu anaasɛ obi a ɔnyɛ ɔtɔfo funu, anaasɛ obi de ne nsa ka onipa dompe anaa ɔda a, ne ho begu fi nnanson.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Na obi a ne ho tew no mfa adwerɛ mmɔ nsu no mu mpete ntamadan no so ne nkuku ne nkaka a ɛwɔ ntamadan no mu no nso so ne obiara a na ɔwɔ ntamadan no mu a ne ho agu fi no so. Saa ara nso na obi a osoo dompe mu anaa obi a wokum no anaa nea ɔde ne ho aka ɔda no nso, wodwira ne ho.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Wɔyɛ eyi ne nnansa ne ne nnanson so. Na nea ne ho agu fi no nso, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntade na oguare, na saa anwummere no ne ho bɛtew.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ wɔn a wɔn ho agu fi na annwira wɔn ho a, ɛsɛ sɛ wotwa wɔn asu, efisɛ wɔagu Awurade kronkronbea hɔ ho fi. Wɔmfaa ahodwira nsu mpetee wɔn so ɛ, na wɔn ho ntew.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Eyi yɛ mmara a ɛbɛtena hɔ afebɔɔ ama wɔn. “Onipa a obetu ahodwira nsu no apete no nso, ɛsɛ sɛ ɔhoro ne ntade, na obiara a ɔde ne nsa bɛka ahodwira nsu no nso ho begu fi akosi anwummere.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Na biribiara a obi a ne ho agu fi no beso mu no nso ho begu fi akosi anwummere.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Israelfo no nyinaa duu Sin sare so ɔsram a edi kan no mu, na wɔtenaa Kades. Ɛhɔ na Miriam wu maa wosiee no.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Na nsu a wɔbɛnom nni hɔ nti, nnipa no sɔre tiaa Mose ne Aaron.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nnipa no ne Mose hamee se, “Sɛ yɛne yɛn nuanom wuwuu wɔ Awurade anim a anka yɛpɛ.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na mode Awurade man ne yɛn nguan ne yɛn anantwi aba sare yi so sɛ yemmewuwu?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na muyii yɛn fii Misraim de yɛn baa asase bɔne yi so? Borɔdɔma, atoko ne bobe nni asase yi so. Nsu a yɛbɛnom nso nni ha.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Mose ne Aaron fii dɔm no hɔ kɔɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano de wɔn anim butubutuw fam wɔ Awurade anim; na wohuu Awurade anuonyam.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Fa abaa no na wo ne wo nua Aaron mfrɛ nnipa no nyinaa. Wɔrehwɛ mo no, kasa kyerɛ ɔbotan no na nsu befi mu aba. Mubenya wɔn nsu a ɛbɛso wɔn ne wɔn anantwi afi ɔbotan no mu!”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mose yɛɛ nea Awurade hyɛe no. Ɔfaa abaa no fii baabi a wɔde asie wɔ Awurade anim.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Mose ne Aaron frɛɛ nnipa no nyinaa ma wobehyiaa wɔ ɔbotan no anim na Mose ka kyerɛɛ wɔn se, “Atuatewfo, muntie! Yɛmma nsu mfi saa ɔbotan yi mu mmra ana?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Afei Mose maa ne nsa so de abaa no bɔɔ ɔbotan no mprenu maa nsu bebree fii mu ba maa nnipa no ne wɔn anantwi nomee.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Nanso Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne Aaron se, “Esiane sɛ moannya me mu ahotoso anhyɛ me anuonyam sɛ ɔkronkronni wɔ Israelfo no ani so nti, moremfa wɔn nkɔ asase a mede rema wɔn no so.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Wɔfrɛɛ beae hɔ Meriba a ase ne: Atuatew Nsu, efisɛ ɛhɔ ne baabi a Israelfo tew Awurade atua, na ɛhɔ ara nso na Awurade daa ne ho adi kyerɛɛ wɔn sɛ ɔyɛ ɔkronkron. Edom Siw Israel Kwan

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Mose somaa abɔfo fii Kades kɔɔ Edomhene nkyɛn sɛ wɔnkɔka nkyerɛ no se: “Sɛɛ na wo nua Israelfo reka: Wunim abɛbrɛsɛ a yɛafa mu no nyinaa.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Yɛn agyanom kɔtenaa Misraim, yɛtenaa hɔ mfe bebree. Misraimfo no yɛɛ yɛne yɛn agyanom ayayade,

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: nanso yesu frɛɛ Awurade no, otiee yɛn na ɔsomaa ɔbɔfo ma obeyii yɛn fii Misraim. “Mprempren yɛwɔ Kades wɔ mo asase hye so.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Yɛsrɛ mo sɛ, ma yentwa mu mfa wo man yi mu. Yɛbɛhwɛ yiye sɛ yɛremfa mo mfuw ne mo bobe nturo mu. Na mpo, yɛrennom mo abura mu nsu. Yɛbɛfa Ɔhene Tempɔn so na yɛremfi so kosi sɛ yɛbɛtra wo hye no.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Nanso Edomhene buae se, “Mommfa mʼasase so, anyɛ saa a mede asraafo ne afoa betua mo ano!”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Israelfo no buae se, “Owura, yɛbɛfa ɔtempɔn no so. Sɛ yɛn nyɛmmoa nom mo nsu a, yebetua ka. Yɛpɛ sɛ yetwa mu wɔ mo asase so na yenni adwemmɔne bi.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Nanso Edomhene buae se, “Mommfa yɛn asase so!” Ɔboaboaa nʼakofo ano de wɔn kɔɔ ɔhye no so.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Esiane sɛ Edom amma wɔn kwan amma Israelfo no amfa wɔn man mu no nti, wɔman faa nkyɛn. Aaron Wu

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israelfo no nyinaa fii Kades kɔɔ Bepɔw Hor so.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Bere adu sɛ Aaron wu, na ɔrenkɔ asase a mede ama Israelfo no so bi, efisɛ mo baanu no tew mʼahyɛde ho atua wɔ Meriba nsu no ho.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Fa Aaron ne ne babarima Eleasar kɔ Bepɔw Hor so.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na wubeyi Aaron asɔfotade no de ahyɛ ne babarima Eleasar. Ɛhɔ na Aaron bewu na watoa nʼagyanom.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mose yɛɛ nea Awurade hyɛɛ no no. Wɔn baasa nyinaa kɔɔ bepɔw Hor so a nnipa no nyinaa hwɛ wɔn.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Mose yii Aaron asɔfotade no de hyɛɛ ne babarima Eleasar, na Aaron wuu wɔ bepɔw no apampam. Na Mose ne Eleasar san fii bepɔw no so bae,

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: na nnipa no tee Aaron wu no, Israelfo no suu no adaduasa.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Afei, Israelfo no fii Bepɔw Hor so de wɔn ani kyerɛɛ Po Kɔkɔɔ sɛ wobetwa dantaban afa Edom ho. Nanso wɔrekɔ no nipa no aba mu bui;

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: wonwiinwii tiaa Onyankopɔn ne Mose se, “Adɛn nti na moayi yɛn afi Misraim de yɛn aba sɛ yemmewuwu wɔ sare yi so? Aduan nni ha! Nsu nni ha! Yɛmpɛ saa awerɛhow aduan yi!”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Enti, Awurade maa awɔ a wɔn ano wɔ bɔre yiye kɔkekaa wɔn mu bebree ma wowuwui.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Na nnipa no baa Mose nkyɛn bɛsrɛɛ se, “Yɛayɛ bɔne, efisɛ yɛakasa atia Awurade ne wo. Bɔ mpae kyerɛ Awurade na awɔ no nkɔ.” Enti Mose bɔɔ mpae maa nnipa no.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Fa kɔbere yɛ saa awɔ yi mu baako sɛso na fa no sɛn abaa tenten bi so, na sɛ awɔ no bi ka obi na ɔhwɛ no a, ɔrenwu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Enti Mose yɛɛ ɔwɔ sɛso no, de sɛn dua tenten so. Na obiara a ɔwɔ no bi bɛka no no, sɛ ɔma nʼani so hwɛ no a, onwu. Israelfo Kɔ Moab

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israelfo no fi hɔ no, wɔtoaa wɔn akwantu no so kɔɔ Obot kɔtenaa hɔ.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Afei, wotu fii hɔ kɔɔ Asubɔnten Arnon nkyɛn hɔ baabi a wɔne Amorifo bɔ hye. Asubɔnten Arnon na ɛyɛ ɔhye a ɛda Moabfo ne Amorifo ntam.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Ɛno nti na, wɔka wɔ Awurade akodi nhoma no mu se, asubɔnten Arnon subon ne kurow Waheb

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Israelfo no fi hɔ toaa wɔn akwantu no so kɔɔ Beer a ase ne “Abura.” Ɛha na Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Frɛfrɛ nnipa no nyinaa bra na mɛma wɔn nsu.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na Israelfo too dwom yi, “Tue Ao, Abura! To ho dwom!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: To dwom fa abura a mmapɔmma tutu no ho, sɛ nnipa mu akunini na wotitii mu; akunini a wokura ahempeaw ne pema.” Afei, Israelfo no fii sare no so kɔfaa Matana,

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: na wɔkɔɔ Pisga atifi a ɛwɔ Moab bon no mu, baabi a wugyina a wuhu asase tamaa no. Sihon Ne Og So Nkonimdi

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Na Hesbon yɛ Amorihene Sihon kuropɔn. Sihon na da bi ɔko tiaa Moabhene faa ne nsase nyinaa besii Asubɔnten Arnon no.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Israelfo no tuu abɔfo ma wɔde nkra kɔmaa Amorihene Sihon se:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Momma yentwa mu mfa mo man yi mu. Yɛbɛfa ɔtempɔn no so tee, na yɛremfi so kosi sɛ yɛbɛtra mo hye. Yɛrentiatia mo nnɔbae so, yɛremfa yɛn nsa nka mo bobe nturo, na yɛrennom mo abura mu nsu kosi sɛ yebefi mo man no mu.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Nanso ɔhene Sihon ampene so. Na mmom, ɔboaboaa nʼakofo ano kɔtow hyɛɛ Israelfo no so wɔ sare so hɔ ne wɔn koo wɔ Yahas.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Nanso Israelfo no kunkum wɔn faa wɔn asase a efi Asubɔnten Arnon kosi asu Yabok ho toaa so kosii Amorifo ahye so a na bammɔ wɔ hɔ no.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Israelfo no faa Amorifo no nkurow akɛse nyinaa a Hesbon kuropɔn ne ne nkuraase nyinaa ka ho tenaa mu.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ne saa nti, tete anwensɛm kyerɛwfo kyerɛw eyi faa ne ho se, “Bra Hesbon, Sihon kuropɔn, yɛnkyekye na ensi ne dedaw mu.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: “Ogya turuw fii Hesbon Ogyaframa fii Sihon ahenkurow mu, Ɛhyew Ar kuropɔn a ɛwɔ Moab; ɛsɛee kurowmma a wɔwɔ Arnon mmepɔw so.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Ao Moabfo, mo sɛe bɛba mu! Wɔawie mo, mo a mosom Kemos! Wagyaw ne mmabarima sɛ atutenafo, Ne ne mmabea sɛ Amorihene Sihon nnommum.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: “Yɛatu wɔn agu, efi Hesbon tɔnn kosi Dibon. Yɛasɛe wɔn ara akosi Nofa De kɔ ara kosi Medeba.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Enti Israelfo no tenaa Amorifo asase no so.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Mose somaa akwansrafo sɛ wɔnkɔsrasra Yaser fa mu hɔ. Ɔde asraafo toaa wɔn, faa wɔn nkurow nyinaa, pam Amorifo no.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Afei, wɔde wɔn ani kyerɛɛ kurow kɛse Basan, nanso Basanhene Og de nʼasraafo hyiaa wɔn wɔ Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Nsuro no, efisɛ mede nʼasraafo ne nʼasase nyinaa ahyɛ wo nsa. Yɛ no sɛnea woyɛɛ Amorihene Sihon a odii Hesbon so no.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Israelfo dii nkonim na wokum ɔhene Og ne ne mmabarima ne ne nkurɔfo nyinaa a anka wɔn mu baako mpo. Na Israelfo no faa nʼasase no.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Afei, Israelfo no kɔɔ Moab tataw so kɔtenaa Asubɔnten Yordan apuei fam a ɛhɔ ne Yeriko di nhwɛanim no.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Moabfo no ka kyerɛɛ Midian mpanyimfo no se, “Saa dɔm yi bɛwe biribiara a ɛwɔ ha no, sɛnea nantwi we sare.” Enti Sipor ba Balak a na ɔyɛ Moabhene saa bere no

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: somaa nnipa ma wɔkɔɔ Beor babarima Balaam nkyɛn wɔ Petor a ɛbɛn Asubɔnten Eufrate ho. Balak kae se, “Nnipadɔm bi fi Misraim aba. Wɔkata asase ani nyinaa na wɔabɛtena abɛn me.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Mɛsrɛ wo, bra na bɛdome wɔn ma me, efisɛ wɔyɛ den sen me. Ebia ɛbɛma matumi adi wɔn so nkonim na mapam wɔn afi asase no so. Efisɛ minim nhyira a ɛba wɔn a wuhyira wɔn no so, na minim mmusu a ɛba wɔn a wodome wɔn no so nso.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Moab ne Midian mpanyimfo no fii hɔ a na wokita sika a wɔde rekotua Balaam ka ama wadome Israelfo no. Enti wɔkɔɔ Balaam nkyɛn kɔkaa nea ehia Balak no kyerɛɛ no.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Balaam kae se, “Monna mma ade nkye mo. Ade kye a, nea Awurade bɛkyerɛ me sɛ menyɛ no, mɛka akyerɛ mo.” Enti Moab mpanyimfo no dae.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Anadwo no, Onyankopɔn baa Balaam nkyɛn bebisaa no se, “Saa nnipa yi yɛ hefo?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Obuae se, “Wɔde nkra afi Moabhene Balak nkyɛn abrɛ me se:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: Nnipadɔm bi fi Misraim aba ne hye so. Enti bra na bɛdome wɔn sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a metumi ne wɔn ako apam wɔn.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Balaam se, “Nkɔ. Ɛnsɛ sɛ wodome wɔn, efisɛ mahyira wɔn!”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Ade kyee anɔpa no, Balaam ka kyerɛɛ Balak nkurɔfo no se, “Monsan nkɔ fie! Awurade ampene sɛ me ne mo nkɔ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Enti Balak mpanyimfo no san bɛbɔɔ amanneɛ se, “Balaam ne yɛn amma.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Balak somaa nnipa dodow pa ara a anuonyamfo a wɔkyɛn kan dɔm no fra wɔn mu.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Wɔbaa Balaam nkyɛn bɛka kyerɛɛ no se, “Sɛnea Sipor ba Balak se ni, ‘Mma biribiara nsiw wo kwan sɛ wobɛba me nkyɛn,

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: efisɛ metua wo ka yiye. Bra na bɛdome saa nnipa no ma me.’ ”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Nanso, Balaam buae se, “Sɛ Balak ma me dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ a ɛwɔ nʼahemfi hɔ nyinaa mpo a, merentumi nyɛ biribiara mmu saa ahyɛde a Awurade a ɔyɛ me Nyankopɔn no ahyɛ no so.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Nanso, monna ha mma ade nkye na yɛnhwɛ sɛ Awurade bɛka asɛm foforo bi aka nea waka dedaw no ho anaa.”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Anadwo no, Onyankopɔn ka kyerɛɛ Balaam se, “Esiane sɛ nnipa no abɛfrɛ wo no nti, Sɔre na wo ne saa nnipa no nkɔ na mmom, hwɛ yiye na yɛ nea mɛkyerɛ wo sɛ yɛ no nko ara.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Ade kyee anɔpa no, ɔhyehyɛɛ nʼafurum, tenaa ne so ne Moab mpanyimfo no sii mu.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Nanso, Onyankopɔn bo fuw Balaam ahopere a ɔde kɔe no; enti ɔsomaa Awurade bɔfo ma ogyinaa akwantemfi sɛ onsiw no kwan. Na Balaam te nʼafurum so a nʼasomfo baanu ka ne ho.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Afurum no huu Awurade bɔfo no sɛ okura afoa gyina kwan no mfimfini no, ɔman faa wuram. Balaam hwee no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɔbɛfa ɔkwan no so.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Na Awurade ɔbɔfo no gyina ɔkwan hiahiaa bi a ɛwɔ bobeturo afasu abien ntam.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Bere a afurum no huu Awurade bɔfo no, otwerii ɔfasu no ho maa Balaam nan pemee. Enti Balaam san hwee aboa no.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Afei, Awurade bɔfo no kɔɔ nʼanim kogyinaa baabi a ɛhɔ kyere pa ara a na afurum no nnya baabi nnan ne ho mfa nifa anaa benkum.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Enti obutuw ɔkwan no mu. Balaam bo fuw yiye ma ɔde abaa no hwee no.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Afei, Awurade buee afurum no ano, na obisaa Balaam se, “Mayɛ wo dɛn na nti a wohwe me mprɛnsa saa?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Balaam nso buaa no se, “Woama mayɛ ɔkwasea! Na sɛ mikura afoa a, anka mekum wo mprempren.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Afurum no nso bisaa no se, “Menyɛ wʼafurum a woatena me so daa de abesi nnɛ? So mayɛ sɛɛ pɛn?” Obuae se, “Dabi.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Afei, Awurade buee Balaam ani ma ohuu ɔsoro bɔfo no sɛ watwe afoa gyina ɔkwan no mfimfini. Enti ɔde nʼanim butuw fam.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Awurade bɔfo no bisaa no se, “Adɛn nti na woahwe wʼafurum no mprɛnsa saa? Maba sɛ merebesiw wo kwan, efisɛ wʼakwan mu no wunni ahwɛyie wɔ mʼanim.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Afurum no huu me a ɔman faa nkyɛn mprɛnsa. Sɛ wamman a, anka mekum wo na magyaa no.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balaam ka kyerɛɛ Awurade bɔfo no se, “Mafom. Na minnim sɛ wugyina ɔkwan no mu a worebesiw me kwan. Sɛ wʼani nnye ho a mɛsan akɔ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Awurade bɔfo no ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Wo ne nnipa no nkɔ, nanso asɛm a mɛka akyerɛ wo no nko ara na ka.” Enti Balaam ne Balak mpanyimfo no kɔe.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Bere a Balak tee sɛ Balaam reba no, ofii kurow no mu kohyiaa no wɔ Moabfo kurow mu wɔ Arnon hye so, wɔ nʼasase ano.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Balak bisaa Balaam se, “Mamfrɛ wo ɔhare so ana? Adɛn nti na woamma me nkyɛn? So merentumi ntua wo ka ana?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Balaam buae se, “Ɛwɔ mu sɛ maba de, nanso merentumi nka nea mepɛ biara. Asɛm a Onyankopɔn de bɛhyɛ mʼano no nko ara na ɛsɛ sɛ meka.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Balaam kaa Balak ho ne no kɔɔ Kiria-Husot.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Balak kum anantwi ne nguan bɔɔ afɔre na ɔde mmoa no bi maa Balaam ne ne mpanyimfo a wɔka ne ho.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ade kyee anɔpa no, Balak faa Balaam de no kɔɔ Bamot-Baal atifi. Ofi hɔ too nʼani huu sɛ Israelfo no sam wɔn atenae hɔ.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam ka kyerɛɛ ɔhene no se, “Si afɔremuka ason wɔ ha, na siesie anantwinini ason ne adwennini ason ma me.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak yɛɛ sɛnea Balaam kae no, na wɔn baanu no de nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ afɔremuka no biara so afɔre.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Afei Balaam ka kyerɛɛ Balak se, “Tena wʼafɔre no ho na merekɔ nkyɛn. Ebia na Awurade bɛba abehyia me, na nea ɔbɛda no adi akyerɛ me biara no mɛka akyerɛ wo.” Enti, ɔforo kɔɔ sorosoro baabi a ɛhɔ yɛ petee.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔ na Onyankopɔn hyiaa no ma ɔkae se, “Masiesie afɔremuka ason, na mede nantwinini ne odwennini abɔ afɔre wɔ biara so.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Awurade de asɛm hyɛɛ Balaam anom se, “San kɔ Balak nkyɛn na kɔka asɛm yi kyerɛ no.”

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Ɔsan bae no ɔbɛtoo no sɛ ɔne Moab mpanyimfo no nyinaa gyinagyina afɔre no ho.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Na Balaam hyɛɛ ne nkɔm: “Balak soma bɛfrɛɛ me fii Aram, Moabhene frɛɛ me fii apuei fam nkoko so. Ɔkae se, ‘Bra bɛdome Yakob ma me; bra bɛka mmususɛm gu Israel so.’

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na matumi adome wɔn a Onyankopɔn nnome ɛ? Ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na matumi aka mmususɛm agu wɔn a Awurade mmuu wɔn fɔ so?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Mihu wɔn fi ɔbotan atifi; mehwɛ wɔn fi nkoko so. Mihu nnipa a wɔatew wɔn ho a wommu wɔn ho sɛ wɔyɛ aman no bi mu nnipa.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Hena na obetumi akan Yakob mfutuma, anaa ɔbɛkan Israelfo nkyemu anan mu baako? Ma minwu atreneefo wu, na mʼawiei nyɛ sɛ wɔn de.”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Balak bisaa Balaam se, “Dɛn na woayɛ me yi? Mede wo baa sɛ bɛdome mʼatamfo, nanso woahyira wɔn mmom!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Obuae se, “So ɛnsɛ sɛ meka nea Awurade de ahyɛ mʼano no ana?” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Abien

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Afei, Balak ka kyerɛɛ no se, “Bra na yɛnkɔ baabi foforo a yebehu wɔn; worenhu wɔn nyinaa, gye wɔn atenae no nkyɛn nkyɛn. Gyina hɔ na dome wɔn ma me.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Enti ɔde no kɔɔ Sofim bepɔw Pisga atifi. Osii afɔremuka ason wɔ hɔ na ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ afɔre afɔre wɔ afɔremuka biara so.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Balaam ka kyerɛɛ Balak se, “Tena wʼafɔre no ho wɔ ha na me nso merekohyia Awuradewɔ hɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Awurade hyiaa Balaam na ɔde asɛm hyɛɛ nʼanom se, “San kɔ Balak hɔ na kɔka asɛm yi kyerɛ no.”

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Enti ɔsan ba bɛtoo no no sɛ ogyina nʼafɔre no ho a Moab mpanyimfo no ka ne ho. Balak bisae se, “Awurade aka dɛn?”

english_verse: Balaam answered: “Pay close attention to my words—
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛɛ ne nkɔm: “Balak, sɔre na tie; Sipor babarima tie me.

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn nyɛ onipa na wadi atoro; Ɔnyɛ onipa na wasesa nʼadwene. Ɔka asɛm a ɔnyɛ ana? Wahyɛ bɔ bi pɛn a wanni so ana?

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: “Wonhu ɔyawdi bi wɔ Yakob mu, wonhuu awerɛhowdi biara wɔ Israel mu. Awurade, wɔn Nyankopɔn ka wɔn ho; Ɔhene ka wɔn ho!

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn yii wɔn fii Misraim; ɔte sɛ nantwi hoɔdenfo ma wɔn.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Nnome biara mmaa Yakob so ɛ, mmusu biara nni Israel so. Afei, wɔbɛka afa Yakob ne Israel ho se, ‘Hwɛ nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ!’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Nnipa no sɔre sɛ gyatabere. Wɔwosow wɔn ho sɛ gyata a onnye nʼahome de kosi sɛ ɔbɛtetew nea wakyere no no nam pasaa na ɔnom nea wakyere no no mogya.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Na Balak ka kyerɛɛ Balaam se, “Sɛ worennome wɔn a, ɛno de nhyira wɔn koraa.”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Balaam buaa no se, “Manka ankyerɛ wo se nea Awurade bɛka biara na mɛyɛ ana?” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Abiɛsa

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Afei, Balak ka kyerɛɛ Balaam se, “Bra mma memfa wo nkɔ baabi foforo. Ebia, ɛhɔ bɛyɛ anisɔ ama Onyankopɔn sɛ wubegyina hɔ adome wɔn.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Na Balak faa Balaam de no kɔɔ bepɔw Peor a ani kyerɛ nweatam no atifi pɛɛ no so.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Bio, Balaam kae se, “Si afɔremuka ason na siesie anantwinini ason ne adwennini ason ma me.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak yɛɛ nea Balaam kae no, enti ɔde nantwinini ne odwennini bɔɔ afɔre wɔ afɔremuka no biara so.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Afei, Balaam huu sɛ ɛsɔ Awurade ani sɛ ohyira Israel no, wankɔ abisa sɛnea ɔtaa yɛ no; mmom, ɔtoo nʼani hwɛɛ sare no so.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Bere a Balaam huu sɛ Israelfo no abobɔ wɔn atenae sɛnea wɔn mmusuakuw te no, Onyankopɔn honhom baa ne so,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: na eyi ne nkɔmhyɛ a ɔmae: “Beor ba Balaam nkɔmhyɛ, nkɔmhyɛ a efi obi a nʼani hu ade yiye,

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: nea ɔte Onyankopɔn nsɛm nkɔmhyɛ; nea onya anisoadehu a efi Otumfo no hɔ; na ɔda fam, a nʼani hu ade:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: “Yakob, mo ntamadan yɛ fɛ, Israel, mo atenae yɛ ahomeka!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: “Ɛtrɛtrɛw sɛ abon, sɛ nturo a ɛwɔ asubɔnten ho. Wɔte sɛ pɛprɛ a Awurade adua, te sɛ sida a esisi nsu ho.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Nsu bɛsen afi wɔn ahina mu. Wɔn aba benya nsu ama aboro so. “Wɔn hene bɛyɛ kɛse asen Agag; wɔn ahenni bɛkorɔn.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: “Onyankopɔn de wɔn fii Misraim na ɛbae; wɔwɔ ahoɔden sɛ wuram nantwi. Wɔsɛe atirimɔdenfo aman na wobubu wɔn nnompe mu asinasin, wɔde wɔn bɛmma wowɔ wɔn.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Wobutuw da sɛ gyata; te sɛ gyatabere, hena na obetumi agyigye wɔn? “Wobehyira wɔn a wohyira wo, na wɔbɛdome wɔn a wɔdome wo.”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Balak bo fuw Balaam. Ɔbɔɔ ne nsam guu ne so kae se, “Mefrɛɛ wo se bɛdome mʼatamfo, nanso woahyira wɔn mprɛnsa yi nyinaa.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Fi ha kɔ wo nkyi ntɛm! Mekae se mɛkyɛ wo ade a ɛsom bo nanso, Awurade amma woannya akyɛde no.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Sɛ Balak ma me dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ a ɛwɔ nʼahemfi hɔ nyinaa koraa a, minni tumi sɛ mɛyɛ biribi atia Awurade ahyɛde, sɛ ɛyɛ papa anaa bɔne.’ Mmom nea Awurade aka no nko ara na ɛsɛ sɛ meka.

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Afei, meresan akɔ me nkurɔfo nkyɛn. Nanso ma menka nea Israelfo no bɛyɛ wo nkurɔfo no daakye no nkyerɛ wo.” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Anan

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Eyi ne nkɔmhyɛ a Balaam de mae: “Beor ba Balaam nkɔmhyɛ, nkɔmhyɛ a efi ɔbarima a nʼani hu ade yiye,

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: nea ɔte Onyankopɔn nsɛm no nkɔmhyɛ, nea ɔwɔ nimdeɛ a efi Ɔsorosoroni no hɔ, nea onya anisoadehu a efi Otumfo no hɔ, na ɔda fam, a nʼani hu ade no:

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: “Mihu no, nanso ɛnyɛ mprempren; mehwɛ no, nanso ɔmmɛn. Nsoromma bepue afi Yakob mu; ahempema bepue afi Israel mu. Ɔbɛdwerɛw Moabfo ti, Moabfo nyinaa tikora.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Wɔbɛfa Edom, na Seir a ɔyɛ ne tamfo no, wobedi ne so nkonim, na Israel bɛkɔ so ayɛ den.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Ɔhene bi bɛsɔre wɔ Yakob mu ɔno na ɔbɛsɛe kurow no mu nkaefo.” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Anum

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Afei, Balaam hwɛɛ Amalekfo na ɔhyɛɛ nkɔm: “Amalek na na ɔyɛ aman nyinaa abakan, nanso nʼawiei bɛyɛ ɔsɛe pasaa.” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Asia

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Afei, ohuu Kenifo, na ɔhyɛɛ ne nkɔm: “Mo atenae wɔ bammɔ, wɔanwen mo berebuw wɔ abotan mu;

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Nanso wɔbɛsɛe mo Kenifo bere a Asur fa mo nnommum no.” Balaam Nkɔmhyɛ A Ɛto So Ason

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Afei ɔhyɛɛ ne nkɔm: “Aa! Sɛ Onyankopɔn yɛ sɛɛ a, hena na ɔbɛtena nkwa mu?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Ahyɛn befi Kipro mpoano aba; wobedi Eber ne Asur so. Nanso wɔn nso, wɔbɛsɛe wɔn pasaa.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Afei, Balaam sɔree na ɔsan kɔɔ ne kurom, na Balak nso kɔɔ ne kwan.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Bere a Israelfo no tenaa Sitim no, wɔn mu mmarima no bi fii ase ne Moab mmea no bɔɔ aguaman de guu wɔn ho fi.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Saa mmea yi too nsa frɛɛ wɔn ma wɔkɔbɔɔ afɔre maa wɔn anyame. Wodii Moabfo anyame so afɔrebɔ nnuan na wɔkotow wɔn nso.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Enti Baal a ɛwɔ Peor no som bɛyɛɛ ɔhyɛ maa Israelfo. Eyi maa Awurade bo fuw ne nkurɔfo no yiye.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Fa saa nnipa yi ntuanofo no nyinaa, kunkum wɔn na fa wɔn gu owia so wɔ Awurade anim sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a, nʼabufuwhyew no befi Israel so.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Enti Mose ka kyerɛɛ Israel atemmufo no no se, “Ɛsɛ sɛ mo mu biara kunkum mo nkurɔfo a wɔde wɔn ho akɔhyɛ Baal a ɛwɔ Peor no ase no nyinaa.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Na Israelni bi de Midiani bea bi baa wɔn atenae hɔ maa Mose ne nnipa no nyinaa huu wɔn bere a na wogyinagyina Ahyiae Ntamadan pon no ano retwa adwo no.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Bere a Pinehas a ɔyɛ Eleasar babarima a na ɔyɛ ɔsɔfo Aaron nena huu eyi no, ofii wɔn mu, kɔfaa peaw kitae;

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: na odii Israelni no akyi kɔɔ ntamadan no mu. Ɔde peaw no wɔɔ ɔbarima no san de wɔɔ ɔbea no yafunu mu. Enti ɔyaredɔm a na aba Israelfo no so no to twae;

english_verse: Israelites had already died.
translation_verse: ) awuwu dedaw.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: “Eleasar babarima Pinehas a ɔyɛ ɔsɔfo Aaron nena ayi mʼabufuw afi Israelfo no so. Esiane sɛ wako apere mʼanuonyam wɔ wɔn mu sɛnea mepɛ ayɛ no nti, sɛnea meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mɛsɛe Israelfo no, magyae.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Saa apam yi mu, ɔno ne nʼasefo bɛyɛ asɔfo afebɔɔ, efisɛ watwe me ho ninkunu wɔ Israelfo mu de ayɛ mpata ama wɔn.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Ɔbarima a wokum no ne Midiani bea no, na ne din de Simri a na ɔyɛ Salu a otua Simeon abusuakuw ano no babarima.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Ɔbea no nso, na ne din de Kosbi a na ɔyɛ Midianhene babarima Sur babea.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: Efisɛ wɔfaa mo sɛ atamfo, na wɔdaadaa mo ma mo som Baal a ɛwɔ Peor, ne Kosbi a ɔyɛ Midian ntuanoni babea, a wokum no wɔ Peor ɔyaredɔm da no.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Ɔyaredɔm no akyi no, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose ne ɔsɔfo Aaron babarima Eleasar se,

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: “Monkan Israelfo mmarima a wɔadi mfe aduonu ne nea ɛboro saa nyinaa na monhwɛ dodow a wobetumi akɔ ɔsa ama Israel wɔ abusua biara mu.”

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Enti Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar kasa kyerɛɛ wɔn wɔ Moab tataw so, wɔ Asubɔnten Yordan ho a na wɔatra Yeriko no se,

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Na Palu yɛ Eliab babarima,

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: na Eliab mmabarima ne Nemuel, Datan ne Abiram. Saa Datan ne Abiram yi ara na wɔyɛ nnipa no ntuanofo a wɔka Kora akyidifo a wɔyɛɛ adwene tiaa Mose ne Aaron, de buu Awurade animtiaa no ho.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Na asase mu bue menee wɔne Kora. Ogya fi Awurade nkyɛn bɛsɛee wɔn akyidifo ahannu aduonum. Na wɔyɛɛ kɔkɔbɔ nsɛnkyerɛnne.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Nanso Kora ase antɔre. Simeon Abusuakuw

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Na saa nnipa yi mu biara nni hɔ a ɔfra wɔn a Mose ne Aaron kan wɔn wɔ Sinai sare so no mu.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aaron woo Nadab, Abihu, Eleasar ne Itamar.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Afei, Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Kyekyɛ asase no ma mmusua no sɛ wɔn agyapade, sɛnea wɔn dodow te.

english_verse: The total number of Israelite men listed was
translation_verse: Nnipa dodow a wɔkan wɔn no ano si mpem ahansia ne baako ahanson aduasa (

english_verse: so the larger tribes have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Ma abusua a ɛso no agyapade kɛse na abusua a esua no agyapade ketewa.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ ntonto wɔ agyapade no kyekyɛ so wɔ akuw akɛse ne nketewa no mu.”

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Eyinom nso yɛ Lewifo mmusua: Libnifo, Hebronfo, Mahlifo, Musifo ne Korafo. Kohat yɛ Amram tete agya.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Bere a Lewi wɔ Misraim no, wɔwoo ɔbabea a ne din de Yokebed. Kehat babarima Amram waree no. Wɔn na wɔwoo Aaron, Mose ne Miriam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nanso, bere a Nadab ne Abihu de ogya a ɛnyɛ kronkron brɛɛ Awurade no, wowuwui.

english_verse: In the tribe of Levi there were
translation_verse: Nnipakan no mu no, na Lewifo nyinaa dodow yɛ mpem aduonu abiɛsa (

english_verse: men and boys at least a month old. They were not listed with the other tribes, because they would not receive any land in Canaan.
translation_verse: ). Wɔkan mmarima a wɔadi fi ɔsram kosi mpanyimfo so. Nanso, wɔammu Lewifo no ano anka Israel nnipakan no ho, efisɛ wɔrekyɛ nsase no ama mmusuakuw no, wɔamma Lewifo no bi.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Enti sɛnea Mose ne ɔsɔfo Eleasar fa kyerɛɛ nnipa no ano wɔ Moab bepɔw a ɛbɛn Asubɔnten Yordan a na wɔatwa Yeriko ne no.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Efisɛ Awurade ka kyerɛɛ saa Israelfo no se wobewuwu wɔ sare no so. Anka wɔn mu biara, gye Yefune ba Kaleb ne Nun babarima Yosua.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Wɔbaa Mose, ɔsɔfo Eleasar, mpanyimfo ne wɔn a wɔahyia wɔ Ahyiae Ntamadan no ano no nyinaa anim bɛkaa se,

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Yɛn agya wuu wɔ sare so nanso na ɔnka wɔn a wɔne Kora yɛɛ dɔm tiaa Awurade a enti ɛma wowuwuu no ho. Ɔno ankasa bɔne nti na owui a wannyaw mmabarima.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Adɛn nti na esiane sɛ yɛn agya anwo ɔbabarima nti ne din ayera fi nʼabusua mu? Momma yɛn yɛn agya abusua mu agyapade no bi.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Enti Mose de wɔn asɛm too Awurade anim.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Awurade buaa no se,

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Asɛm a Selofehad mmabea no ka no yɛ nokware. Ma wɔn ne wɔn agya nuanom no asase. Fa agyapade a sɛ wɔn agya no te ase a anka obenya no ma wɔn.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Na sɛ onni ɔbabea nso a, ɛsɛ sɛ agyapade no kɔ ne nuabarimanom nkyɛn.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Na sɛ onni nuabarimanom a, ɛkɔ ne wɔfanom nkyɛn.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na sɛ onni wɔn mu biara bi a, ɛkɔ ne busuani bi a ɔbɛn no nkyɛn. Ɛsɛ sɛ Israelfo di saa mmara a Awurade hyɛɛ Mose no so.” Woyi Yosua Sɛ Mose Abediakyiri

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se, “Kɔ bepɔw a ɛwɔ Abarim mmepɔw no so na hwɛ asase a mede maa Israelfo no.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Sɛ wohwɛ wie a, wubewu sɛnea wo nua Aaron wui no,

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: efisɛ wɔsɔre tiaa me mmara wɔ Sin sare so hɔ, mo baanu no buu mʼahyɛde so na moanhyɛ me anuonyam sɛ ɔkronkronni wɔ wɔn ani so.” Na ɔretwe nʼadwene aba Meriba nsu “Akoe” a ɛwɔ Kades a ɛwɔ Sin sare so no so.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: “Awurade, Onyankopɔn a woyɛ nnipa nyinaa honhom ti, yi obi ma onni dɔm yi anim

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: a ɔde wɔn befi adi na ɔde wɔn aba mu sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a Awurade nnipa renyɛ sɛ nguan a wonni ɔhwɛfo.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Enti Awurade buaa Mose se, “Kɔ na kɔfrɛ Nun babarima Yosua a ɔwɔ akanni honhom wɔ ne mu no, na fa wo nsa to no so.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Fa no kɔ ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne nnipa no nyinaa anim na fa ne dwumadi hyɛ ne nsa.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Fa wo tumi no bi ma no sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a Israelfo nyinaa betie no.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Sɛ wohia akwankyerɛ a efi Awurade hɔ a, Yosua begyina ɔsɔfo Eleasar anim, na ɔsɔfo Eleasar abɔ ntonto kronkron de abisa Awurade apɛde. Ɔno na ɔbɛhyɛ ama Israelfo no nyinaa afi adi na wahyɛ ama wɔaba mu.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Mose yɛɛ sɛnea Awurade hyɛɛ no no. Ɔde Yosua kyerɛɛ ɔsɔfo Eleasar ne nnipa no nyinaa.

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: Na ɔde ne nsa guu no so, de nʼadwuma hyɛɛ ne nsa sɛnea Awurade nam ne so hyɛe no.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: na oguamma biara nso, mode asikresiam lita abiɛsa. Eyi bɛyɛ ɔhyew afɔre a ɛsɔ ani, aduan afɔre a wɔbɔ ma Awurade.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Awurade ka kyerɛɛ Mose se,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Ka kyerɛ Israelfo se, ‘Monhwɛ na momfa mʼaduan afɔre mmrɛ me wɔ ne bere ano sɛ ehua a ɛsɔ mʼani.’

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Ka kyerɛ wɔn se, ‘Eyi ne aduan afɔre a ɛsɛ sɛ mode brɛ Awurade: nguamma abien a wɔadi afe a dɛm nni wɔn ho; momfa mmra sɛ daa ɔhyew afɔre.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde ɔnom afɔrebɔde a ɛyɛ nsa a apae lita baako a oguamma ka ho ka afɔrebɔde no ho a wobehwie agu beae bi a ɛhɔ yɛ kronkron wɔ Awurade anim.

translation_verse: “ ‘Saa ara nso na da a edi kan wɔ ɔsram biara mu no, ɛsɛ sɛ mobɔ ɔhyew afɔre foforo bi ka ho de ma Awurade. Afɔrebɔde no bɛyɛ nantwinini abien, Odwennini baako ne nguantenmma ason a wɔadi afe a wonnii dɛm biara.
