translation_verse: Ɔda, obonin awotwaa, asase a ɛyɛ wosee daa, ne ogya a ɛnka da se, ‘Eye!’

english_verse: Don't make fun of your father or disobey your mother— crows will peck out your eyes, and buzzards will eat the rest of you.
translation_verse: “Ani a eyi agya ahi, na ebu ɛna animtiaa no, obon mu kwaakwaadabi betutu, na apete abedi.

english_verse: There are three or four things I cannot understand:
translation_verse: “Nneɛma abiɛsa na ɛyɛ me nwonwa, anan na mente ase:

english_verse: How eagles fly so high or snakes crawl on rocks, how ships sail the ocean or people fall in love.
translation_verse: Ɔkwan a ɔkɔre nam so wɔ wim, sɛnea ɔwɔ nantew ɔbotan so, ɔkwan a hyɛn nam so wɔ po tamaa so, ne sɛnea ɔbarima dɔ ababaa.

english_verse: An unfaithful wife says, “Sleeping with another man is as natural as eating.”
translation_verse: “Ɔbea ɔwaresɛefo kwan ni: Odidi, ɔpepa nʼano na ɔka se, ‘Menyɛɛ mfomso biara.’

english_verse: There are three or four things that make the earth tremble and are unbearable:
translation_verse: “Nneɛma abiɛsa na ɛma asase wosow, anan na asase ntumi nnyina ano:

english_verse: A slave who becomes king, a fool who eats too much,
translation_verse: akoa a wabɛyɛ ɔhene, ɔkwasea a wadidi amee,

english_verse: a hateful woman who finds a husband, and a slave who takes the place of the woman who owns her.
translation_verse: ɔbea a wɔmpɛ no na waware, afenaa a otu nʼawuraa tena nʼanan mu.

english_verse: On this earth four things are small but very wise:
translation_verse: “Nneɛma nketenkete anan na ɛwɔ asase so, nanso wɔyɛ anyansafo ankasa:

english_verse: Ants, who seem to be feeble, but store up food all summer long;
translation_verse: Ntɛtea yɛ abɔde nketewa a wonni ahoɔden, nanso wɔboaboa wɔn aduan ano ahuhuru bere mu;

english_verse: badgers, who seem to be weak, but live among the rocks;
translation_verse: Nkukuban yɛ abɔde a wonni ahoɔden, nanso wɔyɛ wɔn afi wɔ abotan mu,

english_verse: locusts, who have no king, but march like an army;
translation_verse: mmoadabi nni ɔhene, nanso wɔsa so akuwakuw, kɔ wɔn anim;

english_verse: lizards, which can be caught in your hand, but sneak into palaces.
translation_verse: wotumi de nsa kyere ɔketew, nanso wohu no abirɛmpɔn ahemfi.

english_verse: Three or four creatures really strut around:
translation_verse: “Nneɛma abiɛsa na wɔwɔ abirɛmpɔnnantew, anan na wɔkeka wɔn ho te sɛ abirɛmpɔn:

english_verse: Those fearless lions who rule the jungle,
translation_verse: gyata, mmoadoma hene a, biribiara mmɔ no hu;

english_verse: those proud roosters, those mountain goats, and those rulers who have no enemies.
translation_verse: akokɔnini a ɔretutu taataa, ɔpapo, ne ɔhene a nʼasraafo atwa no ho ahyia.

english_verse: If you are foolishly bragging or planning something evil, then stop it now!
translation_verse: “Sɛ woayɛ ɔkwasea ama wo ho so, anaa woadwene bɔne a, ma wʼani nwu na mua wʼano!

english_verse: If you churn milk you get butter; if you pound on your nose, you get blood— and if you stay angry, you get in trouble.
translation_verse: Sɛnea wɔka nufusu nu mu a srade fi mu ba, na wokyinkyim hwene a etu mogya no, saa ara na abufuw de akasakasa ba.”

english_verse: These are the sayings that King Lemuel of Massa was taught by his mother.
translation_verse: Ɔhene Lemuel nsɛm a ɛyɛ nkuranhyɛ a ne na kyerɛɛ no:

english_verse: My son Lemuel, you were born in answer to my prayers, so listen carefully.
translation_verse: Tie, me babarima! Tie, me yafunu ba, Tie, me bɔhyɛ ba, me mpaebɔ ho mmuae!

english_verse: Don't waste your life chasing after women! This has ruined many kings.
translation_verse: Nsɛe wʼahoɔden wɔ mmea ho, wɔn a wogu ahemfo asu no.

english_verse: Kings and leaders should not get drunk or even want to drink.
translation_verse: Enye mma ahemfo, Lemuel, asanom nye mma ahemfo, ɛnsɛ sɛ sodifo pere bobesa ho;

english_verse: Beer and wine are only for the dying or for those who have lost all hope.
translation_verse: Fa bobesa ma wɔn a wɔresɛe, na fa nsa ma wɔn a wɔwɔ amanehunu mu;

english_verse: Let them drink and forget how poor and miserable they feel.
translation_verse: Momma wɔnnom, na wɔn werɛ mfi wɔn hia, na wɔnnkae wɔn awerɛhow bio.

english_verse: But you must defend those who are helpless and have no hope.
translation_verse: Kasa ma wɔn a wontumi nkasa mma wɔn ho, kasa ma mmɔborɔfo yiyedi.

english_verse: Be fair and give justice to the poor and homeless. In Praise of a Good Wife
translation_verse: Kasa na bu atɛntrenee; kasa ma ahiafo ne onnibi yiyedi. Awiei: Ɔyere A Ɔsom Bo

english_verse: A truly good wife is the most precious treasure a man can find!
translation_verse: Ɔyere pa, hena na obenya? Ɔsom bo pa ara sen nhene pa.

english_verse: Her husband depends on her, and she never lets him down.
translation_verse: Ne kunu wɔ ne mu ahotoso pa ara, na biribiara a ɛwɔ bo nhia no.

english_verse: She is good to him every day of her life,
translation_verse: Ɔde nea eye brɛ no, na ɛnyɛ ɔhaw, ne nkwanna nyinaa mu.

english_verse: and with her own hands she gladly makes clothes.
translation_verse: Ɔhwehwɛ oguannwi ne asaawa na ɔde ne nsa nwen wɔ fɛw so.

english_verse: She is like a sailing ship that brings food from across the sea.
translation_verse: Ɔte sɛ aguadifo ahyɛn, ɔde ne nnuan fi akyirikyiri ba.

english_verse: She gets up before daylight to prepare food for her family and for her servants.
translation_verse: Ade nnya nkyee no na wasɔre; osiesie aduan ma nʼabusuafo na ɔkyekyɛ nnwuma ma ne mmaawa.

english_verse: She knows how to buy land and how to plant a vineyard,
translation_verse: Osusuw afuw ho na ɔtɔ; ofi nea onya mu yɛ bobeturo.

english_verse: and she always works hard.
translation_verse: Ɔde nsi yɛ nʼadwuma; nʼabasa mu wɔ ahoɔden ma nʼadwuma.

english_verse: She knows when to buy or sell, and she stays busy until late at night.
translation_verse: Ɔhwɛ sɛ nʼaguadi so wɔ mfaso, na ne kanea anum anadwo.

english_verse: and she helps the poor and the needy.
translation_verse: Ogow ne nsam ma ahiafo na ne nsa so ohiani so.

english_verse: Her family has warm clothing, and so she doesn't worry when it snows.
translation_verse: Sɛ sukyerɛmma tɔ a ne yam nhyehye no wɔ ne fifo ho; efisɛ wɔn nyinaa wɔ adurade a wɔde ko awɔw.

english_verse: She does her own sewing, and everything she wears is beautiful.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛ ne mpasotam; na ofura nwera ne sirikyi ntama.

english_verse: Her husband is a well-known and respected leader in the city.
translation_verse: Ne kunu wɔ anuonyam wɔ kuropɔn pon ano, faako a ɔne asase no so mpanyimfo tena.

english_verse: She makes clothes to sell to the shop owners.
translation_verse: Ɔpempam nwera ntade tontɔn, na otu nkyekyeremu ma aguadifo.

english_verse: She is strong and graceful, as well as cheerful about the future.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ ahoɔden ne anuonyam; na onsuro nna a ɛwɔ nʼanim.

english_verse: Her words are sensible, and her advice is thoughtful.
translation_verse: Ɔkasa nyansa mu, na nokware nkyerɛkyerɛ wɔ ne tɛkrɛma so.

english_verse: She takes good care of her family and is never lazy.
translation_verse: Ɔhwɛ ne fi mu nnwuma so na onnyigye anihaw so.

english_verse: Her children praise her, and with great pride her husband says,
translation_verse: Ne mma sɔre a wɔfrɛ no nhyira; ne kunu nso saa ara, na ɔkamfo no se,

english_verse: “There are many good women, but you are the best!”
translation_verse: “Mmea pii yɛ nneɛma a ɛwɔ din na wo de, wosen wɔn nyinaa.”

english_verse: Charm can be deceiving, and beauty fades away, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves to be praised.
translation_verse: Ɔbea kɔnnɔfo yɛ nnaadaa, na ahoɔfɛ twa mu ntɛm so; nanso ɔbea a osuro Awurade no fata nkamfo.

english_verse: Show her respect— praise her in public for what she has done.
translation_verse: Fa abasobɔde a wanya no ma no, na wɔnkamfo ne nnwuma wɔ kuropɔn pon ano.

english_verse: When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
translation_verse: Eyinom ne nsɛm a Ɔsɛnkafo, ɔhene Dawid babarima a ɔyɛ ɔhene wɔ Yerusalem se:

english_verse: Nothing makes sense! Everything is nonsense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense!
translation_verse: “Ahuhude! Ahuhude!” Ɔsɛnkafo no na ose. “Ahuhude mu ahuhude Biribiara yɛ ahuhude.”

english_verse: What is there to show for all of our hard work here on this earth?
translation_verse: Dɛn na onipa nya fi nʼadwumayɛ nyinaa mu, nea okum ne ho yɛ no owia so no?

english_verse: People come, and people go, but still the world never changes.
translation_verse: Awo ntoatoaso ba na ɛkɔ, nanso asase tim hɔ daa.

english_verse: The sun comes up, the sun goes down; it hurries right back to where it started from.
translation_verse: Owia pue na owia kɔtɔ, na ɛyɛ ntɛm kɔ nea epue fii hɔ no.

english_verse: The wind blows south, the wind blows north; round and round it blows over and over again.
translation_verse: Mframa bɔ kɔ anafo fam na ɛdan hwɛ atifi fam; ekyinkyin kɔ baabiara, na ɛsan bɔ fa ne kwan so.

english_verse: All rivers empty into the sea, but it never spills over; one by one the rivers return to their source.
translation_verse: Nsubɔnten nyinaa sen kogu po mu, nanso po nyɛ ma da. Faako a nsubɔnten no fi no hɔ na wɔsan kɔ bio.

english_verse: All of life is far more boring than words could ever say. Our eyes and our ears are never satisfied with what we see and hear.
translation_verse: Biribiara yɛ ɔbrɛ a ɛboro nea obi bɛka so. Ani nhwɛ ade nwie da na aso nso ntie nsɛm mma ɛnyɛ mma da.

english_verse: Everything that happens has happened before; nothing is new, nothing under the sun.
translation_verse: Nea aba no bɛba bio, nea wɔayɛ no, wɔbɛyɛ bio; ade foforo biara nni owia yi ase.

english_verse: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
translation_verse: Biribi wɔ hɔ a wobetumi aka wɔ ho se: “Hwɛ! eyi yɛ ade foforo” ana? Ɛwɔ hɔ dedaw fi tete nteredee; ɛwɔ hɔ ansa na wɔwoo yɛn.

english_verse: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
translation_verse: Wɔnkae tetefo no, na wɔn a wonnya nnwoo wɔn no nso, wɔn a wobedi wɔn akyi no renkae wɔn. Nimdeɛ Yɛ Ahuhude

english_verse: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
translation_verse: Me, Ɔsɛnkafo, na meyɛ Israelhene wɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do.
translation_verse: Mituu me ho sii hɔ sɛ mede nimdeɛ besua ayɛ nhwehwɛmu wɔ biribiara a wɔyɛ no owia yi ase ho. Adesoa duruduru a Onyankopɔn de ato adesamma so!

english_verse: I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Mahu biribiara a wɔyɛ no owia yi ase; ne nyinaa nka hwee, ɛte sɛnea obi tu mmirika taa mframa.

english_verse: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
translation_verse: Nea akyea no wontumi nteɛ; na nea enni hɔ no wontumi nkan.

english_verse: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
translation_verse: Mekaa wɔ me tirim se, “Hwɛ, manyin na manya nimdeɛ bebree asen obiara a watena Yerusalem ahengua so ansa na merebedi ade. Manya nhumu ne nimdeɛ mu osuahu.”

english_verse: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Afei meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mɛhwehwɛ na mate nimdeɛ, ne adammɔsɛm ne nkwaseasɛm ase. Nanso mihuu sɛ eyi nso te sɛnea obi tu mmirika taa mframa.

english_verse: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
translation_verse: Nimdeɛ bebree de awerɛhow na ɛba; nyansa dɔɔso a, awerɛhowdi dɔɔso.

english_verse: I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense.
translation_verse: Mekaa wɔ me koma mu se, “Afei bra, mede anigye bɛsɔ wo ahwɛ na yɛahu nea eye.” Nanso ankosi hwee.

english_verse: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
translation_verse: Mekae se, “Ɔserew yɛ nkwaseade. Na dɛn na anigye tumi yɛ?”

english_verse: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
translation_verse: Mepɛɛ sɛ mihu nea eye pa ara ma yɛn wɔ bere tiaa a yɛwɔ wɔ asase yi so no. Enti meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mede nsa bɛsɛpɛw me ho na mahwehwɛ, ahu nkwaseasɛm nkyerɛase, a na nyansa da so bɔ mʼankasa mʼadwene ho ban.

english_verse: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
translation_verse: Mede me nsa hyɛɛ nnwuma akɛse ase; misisii adan yɛɛ bobe nturo.

english_verse: I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees.
translation_verse: Meyɛɛ nturo ne ahomegyebea na miduaduaa nnuaba ahorow bebree wɔ mu.

english_verse: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
translation_verse: Misisii nsukorae a mɛtwe nsu afi mu, de agugu nnua a ɛrenyin no so.

english_verse: I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Metɔɔ nkoa ne mfenaa, na minyaa ebinom nso a wɔwoo wɔn wɔ me fi. Afei nso, minyaa anantwi ne nguan bebree sen obiara a wadi mʼanim wɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
translation_verse: Mepɛɛ dwetɛ ne sikakɔkɔɔ, gyigyee ahemfo ne amantam no ademude kaa ho. Mefaa mmarima ne mmea nnwontofo, pɛɛ mmea atenae nso; nea ɛyɛ ɔbarima koma anigyede biara.

english_verse: I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise.
translation_verse: Migyee din sen obiara a wadi mʼanim wɔ Yerusalem. Eyinom nyinaa mu no me nimdeɛ kɔɔ so yɛɛ adwuma.

english_verse: I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work.
translation_verse: Nea mʼani hwehwɛe biara mamfa ankame no; mansiw me koma anigye ho kwan. Me koma ani gyee me nnwuma nyinaa ho, na eyi yɛ mʼadwumayɛ so akatua.

english_verse: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
translation_verse: Nanso sɛ mehwɛ nea me nsa ayɛ nyinaa ne nea mabrɛ anya a, ne nyinaa nka hwee, ɛte sɛnea wotu mmirika taa mframa mannya mfaso biara wɔ owia yi ase. Nimdeɛ Ne Nkwaseade Yɛ Ade Huhuw

english_verse: I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity.
translation_verse: Mede mʼadwene kɔɔ nimdeɛ, adammɔsɛm ne nkwaseasɛm so. Dɛn bio na nea wadi ɔhene ade betumi ayɛ asen nea wɔayɛ dedaw no?

english_verse: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
translation_verse: Mihuu sɛ nimdeɛ ye sen nkwaseasɛm, sɛnea hann yɛ sen sum no.

english_verse: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
translation_verse: Onyansafo ani wɔ ne tirim, na ɔkwasea de, ɔnantew sum mu; nanso mihuu sɛ wɔn nyinaa nkrabea yɛ pɛ.

english_verse: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Afei misusuw wɔ me koma mu se, “Ɔkwasea nkrabea bɛto me nso. Enti sɛ mihu nyansa a mfaso bɛn na minya?” Mekaa wɔ me koma mu se, “Eyi nso nka hwee.”

english_verse: This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Ɛno nti asetena fonoo me, na adwuma a yɛyɛ wɔ owia yi ase no haw me. Ne nyinaa yɛ ahuhude, te sɛnea wotu mmirika taa mframa.

english_verse: Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all.
translation_verse: Mikyii nea mayɛ adwuma apɛ nyinaa wɔ owia yi ase, efisɛ ɛsɛ sɛ migyaw hɔ ma nea obedi mʼade.

english_verse: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Na hena na onim sɛ onipa ko no bɛyɛ onyansafo anaa ɔkwasea? Nanso nea mabiri me mogya ani apɛ wɔ owia yi ase nyinaa bɛkɔ ne nsam. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
translation_verse: Enti mepaa abaw wɔ owia yi ase adwumaden ho.

english_verse: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
translation_verse: Na onipa befi ne nimdeɛ, nyansa ne adwumayɛ ho nimdeɛ mu ayɛ nʼasɛde, na afei ɛsɛ sɛ ogyaw nʼadwumayɛ so aba ma obi a ɔnyɛɛ adwuma biara. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, na ɛhaw adwene.

english_verse: What do we really gain from all of our hard work?
translation_verse: Dɛn na onipa nya fi ne brɛ ne dadwen a ɔde yɛ adwuma wɔ owia yi ase mu?

english_verse: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Ne nkwanna nyinaa, nʼadwumayɛ yɛ ɔyaw ne ɔhaw; anadwo mpo nʼadwene yɛ adwuma. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
translation_verse: Biribiara nsen sɛ onipa bedidi na wanom na wanya ahotɔ wɔ adwumayɛ mu. Eyi nso mihuu sɛ efi Onyankopɔn,

english_verse: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
translation_verse: efisɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno a anka hena na obetumi adidi anaasɛ obenya ahotɔ?

english_verse: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Onipa a ɔsɔ Onyankopɔn ani no, ɔma no nimdeɛ, nyansa ne anigye, nanso omumɔyɛfo de, ɔma ɔboaboa ahonyade ano ma nea ɔsɔ Onyankopɔn ani. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, sɛnea wɔde mmirikatu taa mframa no.

english_verse: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
translation_verse: Biribiara wɔ ne bere, na dwumadi biara a ɛwɔ ɔsoro ase wɔ ne bere.

english_verse: There is a time for birth and death, planting and reaping,
translation_verse: Awo wɔ ne bere, na owu wɔ ne bere, ogu wɔ ne bere na otwa nso wɔ ne bere,

english_verse: There is a time for finding and losing, keeping and giving,
translation_verse: adehwehwɛ wɔ ne bere na adehwere wɔ ne bere, adekora wɔ ne bere na adetowgu wɔ ne bere,

english_verse: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
translation_verse: ɔdɔ wɔ ne bere na ɔtan wɔ ne bere, ɔko wɔ ne bere na asomdwoe wɔ ne bere.

english_verse: What do we gain by all our hard work?
translation_verse: Mfaso bɛn na odwumayɛni nya fi nʼadwumaden mu?

english_verse: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
translation_verse: Mahu adesoa a Onyankopɔn de ato nnipa so.

english_verse: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
translation_verse: Wayɛ biribiara fɛfɛ wɔ ne bere mu. Ɔde nkwa a ɛnsa da ahyɛ nnipa koma mu, nanso wontumi nte nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ fi mfiase kosi awiei no ase.

english_verse: I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life,
translation_verse: Minim sɛ biribiara nni hɔ a eye ma nnipa kyɛn sɛ wobegye wɔn ani na wɔayɛ nea eye bere a wɔte ase.

english_verse: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
translation_verse: Sɛ obiara bedidi na wanom na wanya anigye wɔ ne dwumadi nyinaa mu, eyi ne Onyankopɔn akyɛde.

english_verse: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
translation_verse: Minim sɛ biribiara a Onyankopɔn yɛ no bɛtena hɔ daa, wɔrentumi mfa biribi nka ho na wɔrentumi nyi biribi mfi mu. Onyankopɔn yɛ eyi sɛnea nnipa de nidi bɛma no.

english_verse: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
translation_verse: Biribiara a ɛwɔ hɔ nnɛ no, aba pɛn, na nea ɛbɛba no nso aba dedaw; na Onyankopɔn bɛfrɛ nea asi dedaw no ama akontaabu.

english_verse: Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice.
translation_verse: Na mihuu biribi foforo wɔ owia yi ase sɛ: Amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ nea atemmu wɔ, atɛntreneebea no, amumɔyɛsɛm wɔ hɔ.

english_verse: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
translation_verse: Medwenee wɔ me koma mu se, “Onyankopɔn bebu atreneefo ne amumɔyɛfo nyinaa atɛn, efisɛ adwuma biara benya ne bere, nneyɛe biara ne ne bere.”

english_verse: I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals.
translation_verse: Afei medwenee se, “Nnipa de, Onyankopɔn sɔ wɔn hwɛ ma wohu sɛ wɔte sɛ mmoa.

english_verse: Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense.
translation_verse: Onipa nkrabea te sɛ mmoa de na ɛda hɔ ma wɔn nyinaa. Sɛnea ɔbaako wu no, saa ara na ɔfoforo nso wu. Wɔn nyinaa wɔ ɔhome baako; onipa nni biribi a ɔde kyɛn aboa. Biribiara yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
translation_verse: Wɔn nyinaa kɔ faako; wɔn nyinaa fi dɔte mu na wɔsan kɔ dɔte mu.

english_verse: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
translation_verse: Hena na onim sɛ onipa honhom foro soro na aboa de sian kɔ asase mu ana?”

english_verse: We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_verse: Enti mihuu sɛ biribiara nni hɔ a eye ma onipa kyɛn sɛ nʼani bɛka nʼadwuma ho, efisɛ ɛno ne ne kyɛfa. Na hena na obetumi de no asan aba sɛ ɔmmɛhwɛ nea ebesi ne wu nʼakyi?

english_verse: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
translation_verse: Bio, mehwɛ mihuu nhyɛso a ɛrekɔ so wɔ owia yi ase: Mihuu wɔn a wɔredi wɔn nya no nusu na wonni ɔwerɛkyekyefo biara; tumi no wɔ wɔn nhyɛsofo no nsam na wonni ɔwerɛkyekyefo biara.

english_verse: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
translation_verse: Na mekae se: Awufo a wɔawuwu dedaw no, ani gye sen ateasefo; wɔn a wɔda so wɔ nkwa mu no.

english_verse: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
translation_verse: Na nea oye sen baanu yi ne nea onnya mmae, nea onnya nhuu bɔne a wɔyɛ wɔ owia yi ase.

english_verse: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Na mihuu sɛ adwumayɛ mu ɔbrɛ ne nea onipa tumi yɛ nyinaa nnyinaso ne sɛ nʼani bere ne yɔnko. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, mmirika a wotu taa mframa.

english_verse: Fools will fold their hands and starve to death.
translation_verse: Ɔkwasea bobɔw ne nsa gu ne ho na ɔsɛe ne ho.

english_verse: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nsammua baako a asomdwoe wɔ mu ye sen nsammua abien a ɔbrɛ bata ho; ɛte sɛ nea wotaa mframa.

english_verse: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
translation_verse: Afei nso mihuu biribi a ɛnka hwee wɔ owia yi ase:

english_verse: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
translation_verse: Na ɔbarima bi wɔ hɔ a ɔyɛ ankonam; onni ɔbabarima anaa onuabarima. Nʼadwumaden amma nʼawie da, nanso nʼani ansɔ nʼahonya. Obisaa ne ho se, “Na hena na merebrɛ ama no, na adɛn nti na mede anigye kame me kra?” Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, ɛyɛ ɔhaw kwa.

english_verse: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
translation_verse: Baanu ye sen ɔbaakofo, efisɛ wonya wɔn brɛ so mfaso a ɛsɔ ani:

english_verse: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔbaako hwe ase a ne yɔnko betumi aboa no. Nanso onipa a ɔhwe ase a onni ɔboafo no, yɛ mmɔbɔ.

english_verse: If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night.
translation_verse: Bio, sɛ baanu da bɔ mu a wɔka wɔn ho hyew. Na ɛbɛyɛ dɛn na ankonam bɛka ne ho hyew?

english_verse: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
translation_verse: Ɔbaakofo de, wobetumi aka no ahyɛ nanso baanu tumi pere wɔn ti. Hama a wɔawɔ no mmɛsa no, wontumi ntetew mu ntɛm. Nkɔso Yɛ Adehunu

english_verse: You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice.
translation_verse: Ɔbabun nyansafo a odi hia ye sen ɔhene akwakoraa a ɔyɛ ɔkwasea na ontie kɔkɔbɔ bio.

english_verse: Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king.
translation_verse: Ebia na ɔbabun no fi afiase na obedii ade anaasɛ wɔwoo no too ohia mu wɔ adehye abusua mu.

english_verse: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
translation_verse: Mihuu sɛ wɔn a wɔtenaa ase na wɔnantew owia yi ase nyinaa dii ɔbabun no akyi, nea odii ɔhene no ade no.

english_verse: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nnipadɔm a wontumi nkan wɔn dii nʼakyi. Nanso nkyirimma no ani annye ne ho. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, ɛte sɛ wotaa mframa.

english_verse: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
translation_verse: Sɛ wokɔ Onyankopɔn fi a, hwɛ wʼanammɔntu yiye. Bɛn no na tie no sen sɛ wobɛbɔ nkwaseafo afɔre, wɔn a wonnim mfomso a wɔyɛ no.

english_verse: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
translation_verse: Mpɛ ntɛm nkasa. Mpere wo ho wɔ wo koma mu sɛ wobɛka asɛm bi wɔ Onyankopɔn anim. Onyankopɔn te ɔsoro na wo de, wowɔ asase so, enti ma wo nsɛm nyɛ kakraa bi.

english_verse: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
translation_verse: Adaeso fi adwennwen bebree mu ba, na nsɛm dodow da adi wɔ ɔkwasea kasa mu.

english_verse: God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God.
translation_verse: Sɛ wohyɛ Onyankopɔn bɔ a, ntwentwɛn wo nan ase wɔ ho. Onni anigye wɔ nkwaseafo mu; enti di wo bɔhyɛ so.

english_verse: It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it.
translation_verse: Sɛ woanhyɛ bɔ koraa a eye sen sɛ wobɛhyɛ bɔ na wunni so.

english_verse: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
translation_verse: Mma wʼano mfa wo nkɔ bɔne mu. Nyi wʼano nkyerɛ asɔredan mu somfo se, “Me bɔhyɛ no yɛ mfomso.” Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ Onyankopɔn bo fuw nea woka na ɔsɛe wo nsa ano adwuma?

english_verse: Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
translation_verse: Adaeso ne nsɛnkeka bebree nka hwee. Enti suro Onyankopɔn. Ahonya Yɛ Ahuhude

english_verse: Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do.
translation_verse: Sɛ wuhu ohiani a wɔhyɛ ne so wɔ ɔmansin bi mu, na atɛntrenee ne ahofadi abɔ no a, mma eyinom nyɛ wo nwonwa, efisɛ nea ɔso sen no hwɛ no so, na nea ɔso sen wɔn baanu no nso hwɛ wɔn so.

english_verse: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
translation_verse: Wɔn nyinaa fa asase no so siade; na ɔhene no ankasa nya mfuw no so mfaso.

english_verse: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
translation_verse: Nea nʼani bere sika no nnya nea ɛdɔɔso da; na nea ɔpɛ ahonyade dodow no ani nsɔ nea onya. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
translation_verse: Adetɔnnne bu so a, saa ara na atɔfo no nso dɔɔso. Na mfaso bɛn na nea ɛwɔ no no nya sen sɛ ɔde nʼani bɛhwɛ?

english_verse: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
translation_verse: Ɔpaani da ma nʼani kum, sɛ wadidi amee, anaasɛ wammee, nanso ɔdefo ahonya dodow nti ontumi nna.

english_verse: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
translation_verse: Mahu bɔne kɛse wɔ owia yi ase: wɔde ahode sie de haw ne wuranom,

english_verse: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
translation_verse: anaasɛ ahode fa atoyerɛnkyɛm bi so hwere sɛ ɛbɛyɛ na wonya mma a wɔremmɛto hwee mfa.

english_verse: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
translation_verse: Adagyaw na onipa de fi ne na yafunu mu bae, na sɛnea ɔbae no, saa ara na ɔbɛkɔ. Ɔremfa nʼadwumayɛ so mfaso biara a obetumi akita wɔ ne nsa mu no nkɔ.

english_verse: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
translation_verse: Eyi nso yɛ ɔhaw kɛse: Sɛnea onipa ba no, saa ara na ɔkɔ, na mfaso bɛn na onya wɔ bere a ɔyɛ adwuma ma mframa?

english_verse: Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
translation_verse: Ne nna nyinaa mu no, odidi a nʼanom nyɛ no dɛ, efisɛ abawpa, ateetee ne abufuw wɔ no so.

english_verse: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
translation_verse: Afei mihuu sɛ eye ma onipa sɛ obedidi na wanom na wama nʼani agye nʼadwumaden ho wɔ owia yi ase, wɔ mmere kakra a Onyankopɔn de ama no yi mu, efisɛ eyi ne ne kyɛfa.

english_verse: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
translation_verse: Nea ɛka ho ne sɛ, sɛ Onyankopɔn ma onipa bi ahonyade ne adenya, na onya ahotɔ, de anigye yɛ nʼadwuma, na ohu sɛ ne kyɛfa ne no a, ɔnkae sɛ ɛyɛ Onyankopɔn akyɛde.

english_verse: God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_verse: Ɔntaa ntena ase nnwen ne nkwanna ho, efisɛ Onyankopɔn de koma mu anigye ama no.

english_verse: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
translation_verse: Mahu bɔne foforo bi wɔ owia yi ase a ɛhyɛ nnipa so yiye:

english_verse: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn ma onipa ahonyade, adenya ne anuonyam sɛnea biribiara a ne koma pɛ no ɛremmɔ no, nanso Onyankopɔn amma no kwan sɛ ɔmfa nnye nʼani, na ɔhɔho mmom na ɔde gye nʼani. Eyi yɛ ahuhude, ɔhaw a ɛyɛ yaw.

english_verse: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
translation_verse: Onipa betumi anya mma ɔha na wanyin akyɛ; nanso ne mfe dodow yi akyi no, nʼahonya no amma nʼani annye na ne sie nso anyɛ fɛ a, ɔpɔn ba so wɔ mfaso sen no.

english_verse: That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you,
translation_verse: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ wanhu owia na onnim hwee de, nanso obenya ahomegye bebree sen nea saa ɔbarima no benya,

english_verse: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
translation_verse: mpo sɛ ɔtena ase mfe apem mmɔho na wamfa nʼahonyade annye nʼani a, wɔn nyinaa nkɔ faako ana?

english_verse: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
translation_verse: Onipa brɛ nyinaa yɛ nʼano ntia, nanso nʼakɔnnɔde mmee no da.

english_verse: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
translation_verse: Na dɛn na onyansafo wɔ de sen ɔkwasea? Sɛ ohiani yɛ nʼakwan yiye wɔ afoforo anim a mfaso bɛn na obenya?

english_verse: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Nea aniwa hu no ye sen nea akɔnnɔ kyin hwehwɛ. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude, ɛte sɛ wotaa mframa.

english_verse: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
translation_verse: Nea ɛwɔ hɔ biara, wɔato din dedaw, na sɛnea onipa te nso, wonim dedaw; onipa biara rentumi ne nea ɔwɔ ahoɔden sen no nnye eyi ho akyinnye.

english_verse: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
translation_verse: Nsɛm dɔɔso a, mu ntease sua, na so wɔ mfaso ma onipa ana?

english_verse: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_verse: Na hena na onim nea eye ma onipa wɔ ne nkwanna kakraa bi a ɛyɛ ahuhude na ɔfa mu kɔ sɛ sunsuma no mu? Hena na obetumi aka nea ebesi wɔ owia yi ase akyerɛ no bere a ɔkɔ no?

english_verse: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
translation_verse: Din pa yɛ sen aduhuam papa, na owuda yɛ sen awoda.

english_verse: It's better to go to a funeral than to attend a feast; funerals remind us that we all must die.
translation_verse: Eye sɛ obi bɛkɔ ayi ase sen sɛ ɔbɛkɔ aponto ase, efisɛ owu yɛ onipa biara nkrabea na ɛsɛ sɛ ateasefo hyɛ eyi nsow.

english_verse: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
translation_verse: Awerɛhow ye sen ɔserew, efisɛ anim a ayɛ mmɔbɔmmɔbɔ de koma mu nsiesie pa ba.

english_verse: A sensible person mourns, but fools always laugh.
translation_verse: Onyansafo koma wɔ ayi ase, nanso nkwaseafo koma wɔ ahosɛpɛwfo fi.

english_verse: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
translation_verse: Eye sɛ wobetie onyansafo animka sen sɛ wobetie nkwaseafo dwom.

english_verse: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
translation_verse: Sɛnea nsɔe turuturuw wɔ ɔsɛn ase no saa ara na nkwaseafo serew te. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: Corruption makes fools of sensible people, and bribes can ruin you.
translation_verse: Asisi ma onyansafo dan ɔkwasea, na kɛtɛasehyɛ sɛe koma.

english_verse: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
translation_verse: Asɛm awiei ye sen ne mfiase, na ntoboase ye sen ahantan.

english_verse: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
translation_verse: Mma wo koma nsɔre ntɛmntɛm, na abufuw da nkwaseafo srɛ so.

english_verse: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
translation_verse: Nka se, “Adɛn nti na tete nna no ye sen nnɛ mmere yi?” Onyansafo mmisa nsɛm sɛɛ.

english_verse: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
translation_verse: Sɛnea nimdeɛ yɛ bammɔ no, saa ara na sika nso te; nanso nhumu ho ade a eye ne sɛ: nea ɔwɔ nimdeɛ no bɔ ne nkwa ho ban.

english_verse: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
translation_verse: Dwene nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ ho: Hena na obetumi ateɛ nea wɔama akyea?

english_verse: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
translation_verse: Mmere pa mu, ma wʼani nnye; nanso mmere bɔne mu, hu sɛ Onyankopɔn na wayɛ ne nyinaa. Ɛno nti onipa rentumi nhu nea ɛbɛto no daakye.

english_verse: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
translation_verse: Me nkwanna a ɛyɛ ahuhude yi mu, mahu nneɛma abien: Ɔtreneeni a owu wɔ ne trenee mu, ne omumɔyɛfo a ɔtena ase kyɛ wɔ nʼamumɔyɛ mu.

english_verse: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
translation_verse: Nyɛ wo ho ɔtreneeni ntra so, na nyɛ wo ho onyansafo mmoro so; adɛn nti na wosɛe wo ho?

english_verse: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
translation_verse: Nyɛ omumɔyɛfo ntra so, na nyɛ ɔkwasea nso, adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ wuwu ansa na wo bere aso.

english_verse: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
translation_verse: Eye sɛ wubeso baako no mu den nanso nnyaa nea aka no mu. Onipa a osuro Onyankopɔn no besiw nneyɛe mmoroso nyinaa ano.

english_verse: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
translation_verse: Nimdeɛ ma onyansafo baako tumi bebree sen kuropɔn mu asodifo du.

english_verse: No one in this world always does right.
translation_verse: Onipa treneeni biara nni asase so a ɔyɛ papa na ɔnyɛ bɔne da.

english_verse: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
translation_verse: Mfa nea nnipa ka nyinaa nyɛ asɛm, anyɛ saa a wobɛte sɛ wo somfo redome wo,

english_verse: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
translation_verse: Mede nimdeɛ asɔ eyinom nyinaa ahwɛ, na mekae se, “Masi mʼadwene pi sɛ mɛyɛ onyansafo” nanso na eyi boro me so.

english_verse: The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep.
translation_verse: Sɛnea nimdeɛ te biara, ɛwɔ akyiri na emu dɔ, hena na obetumi ahwehwɛ ahu?

english_verse: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
translation_verse: Afei meyɛɛ mʼadwene sɛ mɛte ase, ayɛ nhwehwɛmu na mapɛɛpɛɛ nimdeɛ ne sɛnea nneɛma nhyehyɛe te na mate amumɔyɛ mu agyimisɛm ase, ne nkwaseasɛm mu adammɔsɛm nso.

english_verse: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
translation_verse: Mahu nea ɛyɛ nwene sen owu; ɔbea a ɔyɛ afiri; ne koma yɛ nnaadaa na ne nsa yɛ mpokyerɛ. Onipa a ɔsɔ Onyankopɔn ani no renkɔ ne ho nanso ɔbɔnefo de ɔbɛtɔ nʼafiri mu.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
translation_verse: Ɔsɛnkafo no se, “Hwɛ eyi ne nea mahwehwɛ ahu: “Mekekaa nneɛma bobɔɔ so pɛɛ sɛ mihu sɛnea nneɛma nhyehyɛe te,

english_verse: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
translation_verse: mereyɛ nhwehwɛmu, na minhu hwee no, mihuu ɔbarima treneeni baako wɔ mmarima apem mu, nanso manhu ɔbea treneeni biara wɔ wɔn mu.

english_verse: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_verse: Eyi nko ara na mahu: Onyankopɔn yɛɛ adesamma atreneefo, nanso nnipa adan wɔn ho hwehwɛ nhyehyɛe foforo.”

english_verse: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
translation_verse: Hena na ɔte sɛ onyansafo? Hena na onim sɛnea nneɛma te? Nimdeɛ te nnipa anim, na ɛbrɛ ne denyɛ ase. Yɛ Osetie Ma Ɔhene

english_verse: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
translation_verse: Mise: Di ɔhene mmaransɛm so, efisɛ wokaa ntam wɔ Onyankopɔn anim.

english_verse: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
translation_verse: Mpɛ ntɛm mfi ɔhene anim. Nnyina mu mma obi asɛm a ɛnyɛ dɛ na onii no anyɛ nea ɔpɛ biara.

english_verse: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
translation_verse: Esiane sɛ ɔhene asɛm boro obiara de so nti, hena na obetumi aka akyerɛ no se: “Dɛn na woreyɛ yi?”

english_verse: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
translation_verse: Nea odi ne mmaransɛm so no renkɔ ɔhaw biara mu, na nyansa koma behu bere a ɛsɛ, ne ne kwan.

english_verse: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
translation_verse: Nneyɛe biara wɔ ne bere a ɛfata ne kwan a wɔfa so yɛ, nanso onipa haw hyɛ no so bebree.

english_verse: though no one can tell the future.
translation_verse: Esiane sɛ obiara nnim daakye asɛm nti, hena na obetumi akyerɛ ɔfoforo nea ɛreba?

english_verse: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
translation_verse: Obiara nni mframa so tumi na waboa ano; saa ara na obiara nni ne wuda so tumi. Sɛ wonnyaa obiara wɔ ɔko bere mu no, saa ara na amumɔyɛ rennyaa wɔn a wodi amumɔyɛsɛm no.

english_verse: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
translation_verse: Mihuu eyinom nyinaa bere a medwenee nneɛma a wɔyɛ wɔ owia yi ase no ho. Bere bi wɔ hɔ a onipa hyɛ afoforo so ma ɛdan ɔhaw ma no.

english_verse: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
translation_verse: Bio, mihuu sɛ wɔasie amumɔyɛfo, wɔn a anka wodi akɔneaba wɔ kronkronbea hɔ de gye nkamfo wɔ kuropɔn a wɔyɛɛ saa no mu. Eyi nso yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
translation_verse: Sɛ bɔne bi ho asotwe amma ntɛm a, nnipa dwene nhyehyɛe a wɔde yɛ bɔne ho.

english_verse: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
translation_verse: Ɛwɔ mu sɛ omumɔyɛfo bi yɛ bɔne mpɛn ɔha nanso ɔtena ase kyɛ, nanso minim sɛ ebesi wɔn a wosuro Onyankopɔn no yiye, wɔn a wodi Onyankopɔn ni no.

english_verse: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
translation_verse: Nanso esiane sɛ amumɔyɛfo nsuro Onyankopɔn nti, ɛrensi wɔn yiye na wɔn nna renware sɛ sunsuma.

english_verse: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
translation_verse: Ade bi nso a ɛyɛ ahuhude a esi wɔ asase so, ɛne sɛ, atreneefo bi nya akatua a ɛfata amumɔyɛfo, na amumɔyɛfo bi nya akatua a ɛfata atreneefo. Eyi nso, mise ɛyɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: Enti mekamfo wiase mu anigye, efisɛ biribiara nni owia yi ase a eye ma onipa sen sɛ obedidi, anom ama nʼani agye. Na afei obenya anigye wɔ nʼadwumayɛ mu wɔ nna a Onyankopɔn ama no wɔ owia yi ase nyinaa.

english_verse: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
translation_verse: Bere a mepɛ sɛ mɛte nimdeɛ ase ne ɔbrɛ adwuma a onipa yɛ wɔ asase so a ɔnna awia anaa anadwo no,

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: mihuu nea Onyankopɔn ayɛ nyinaa. Obiara rentumi nte nea ɛkɔ so wɔ owia yi ase no ase. Ne mmɔdemmɔ nyinaa akyi, onipa rentumi nhu nkyerɛase da. Sɛ mpo onyansafo bi ka se onim a, ɔrentumi nte ase yiye da.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: Enti medwenee eyinom nyinaa ho na mihuu sɛ atreneefo, anyansafo ne nea wɔyɛ wɔ Onyankopɔn nsam; nanso obiara nnim sɛ ɔdɔ anaasɛ ɔtan retwɛn no.

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: Wɔn nyinaa nkrabea yɛ baako; atreneefo ne amumɔyɛfo, nnipa pa ne nnipa bɔne, wɔn a wɔn ho tew ne wɔn a wɔn ho ntew, wɔn a wɔbɔ afɔre ne wɔn a wɔmmɔ. Sɛnea ɛte ma onipa pa no, saa ara na ɛte ma ɔbɔnefo; sɛnea ɛte ma wɔn a wɔka ntam no, saa ara na ɛte ma wɔn a wosuro sɛ wɔbɛka ntam.

english_verse: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
translation_verse: Eyi ne bɔne a ɛwɔ biribiara a esi wɔ owia yi ase mu. Nkrabeakoro ba yɛn nyinaa so. Nea ɛka ho ne sɛ, bɔne ahyɛ nnipa koma mu ma na adammɔ nsɛm wɔ wɔn koma mu, bere a wɔwɔ nkwa mu, na akyiri no wɔkɔka awufo ho.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔka ateasefo ho no wɔ anidaso, mpo ɔkraman a ɔte ase ye sen gyata a wawu.

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Na ateasefo nim sɛ wobewu, nanso awufo nnim hwee; wonni akatua biara bio, na wɔn ho nkae mpo ayera.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Wɔn dɔ, ɔtan ne ninkunu atu ayera dedaw; wonni hwee yɛ wɔ biribiara a esi wɔ owia yi ase mu.

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: Enti kɔ, fa anigye di wʼaduan, na fa ahosɛpɛw koma nom wo nsa, efisɛ saa bere yi na Onyankopɔn pene nea woyɛ so.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Bere biara ma wʼadurade nyɛ fitaa na fa ngohuam sra wo tirim.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Wo ne wo yere, munnye mo ani, ɔbea a wodɔ no no, wɔ nna a ɛnka hwee a Onyankopɔn de ama mo wɔ owia yi ase, mo ahuhude nna no. Efisɛ ɛyɛ mo kyɛfa wɔ mo nkwanna mu, ne mo adwumaden wɔ owia yi ase.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Nea wo nsa bɛso so biara, fa wʼahoɔden nyinaa yɛ, efisɛ ɔda a wɔrekɔ mu no, adwumayɛ, adwennwene, nhumu ne nimdeɛ nni hɔ.

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: Mihuu biribi foforo wɔ owia yi ase: Mmirikakansi nni hɔ mma nea ne ho yɛ hare anaasɛ ɔko nni hɔ mma ɔhoɔdenfo, aduan mma onyansafo nkyɛn anaasɛ ahonya nnkɔ nhumufo hɔ, na adom nnkɔ nimdefo nkyɛn; nanso bere ne akwannya wɔ hɔ ma wɔn nyinaa.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Bio, onipa biara nnim dɔn ko a ne bere bɛso: Sɛnea asau buma mpataa, ne sɛnea afiri yi nnomaa no saa ara na mmere bɔne to nnipa wɔ bere a wɔn ani nni wɔn ho so. Nimdeɛ Ye Sen Nkwaseasɛm

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: Bio, mihuu saa nimdeɛ ho nhwɛso yi wɔ owia yi ase ma mʼani gyee ho yiye:

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Bere bi na kuropɔn ketewa bi wɔ hɔ a mu nnipa yɛ kakraa bi. Ɔhene bi a ɔwɔ tumi tow hyɛɛ kuropɔn yi so, otwaa ho hyiae na osisii mpie akɛse tiaa no.

english_verse: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
translation_verse: Na ohiani bi a onim nyansa wɔ kuropɔn no mu, na ɔnam ne nimdeɛ so gyee kuropɔn no sii hɔ. Nanso obiara ankae saa ohiani no.

english_verse: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
translation_verse: Enti mekae se, “Nimdeɛ ye sen ahoɔden.” Nanso wobuu ohiani no nimdeɛ no animtiaa, na obiara ntie nʼasɛm bio.

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
translation_verse: Ɛsɛ sɛ wotie onyansafo nsɛm a ɔka no brɛoo no na ɛnyɛ nkwaseafo sodifo nteɛteɛmu.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Nimdeɛ ye sen akode, nanso ɔdebɔneyɛni baako sɛe nnepa bebree.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Sɛnea nwansena funu ma aduhuam yi nka bɔne no, saa ara na nkwaseasɛm kakraa bi boro nimdeɛ ne anuonyam so no.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Onyansafo koma sian kɔ nifa, nanso ɔkwasea koma kɔ benkum.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: Mpo sɛ ɔkwasea nam ɔkwan so a, wohu sɛ onnim nyansa na ɔma obiara hu sɛ wagyimi.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: Sɛ sodifo bo fuw wo a, nnyaw wʼadwuma nto hɔ; na ntoboase dwudwo mfomso kɛse ano.

english_verse: Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair:
translation_verse: Bɔne bi wɔ hɔ a mahu wɔ owia yi ase ɛyɛ mfomso bi a efi sodifo:

english_verse: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
translation_verse: Wɔma nkwaseafo dibea a ɛkorɔn, na asikafo nya nea ɛwɔ fam.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: Mahu nkoa sɛ wɔtete apɔnkɔ so, na mmapɔmma nam fam sɛ nkoa.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Obiara a otu amoa no betumi atɔ mu; na nea obubu ɔfasu no, ɔwɔ betumi aka no.

english_verse: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔpae abo no, abo no betumi apira no; na nea ɔpae nnua no betumi anya mu akwanhyia.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Sɛ abonnua ano kum na wɔansew ano a ebehia ahoɔden bebree, nanso adwumayɛ ho nimdeɛ de nkonimdi bɛba.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔwɔ ka obi ansa na wɔadwudwo no a nea odwudwo ɔwɔ no rennya so mfaso biara.

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Onyansafo anom nsɛm yɛ nyam, nanso ɔkwasea ano fafa de no kɔ ɔsɛe mu.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: Mfiase no, wɔn nsɛm yɛ nkwaseasɛm; awiei no, ɛyɛ adammɔ atirimɔdensɛm,

english_verse: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
translation_verse: na ɔkwasea woro nsɛm. Obiara nnim nea ɛreba, hena na obetumi aka nea ebesi wɔ obi akyi akyerɛ no?

english_verse: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
translation_verse: Ɔkwasea adwumayɛ ma ɔbrɛ; na ɛmma onhu ɔkwan a ɛkɔ kurom.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Nnome nka wo, asase a na wo hene yɛ ɔsomfo na wo mmapɔmma to pon anɔpa.

english_verse: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
translation_verse: Nhyira nka wo, asase a wo hene yɛ ɔdehye na wo mmapɔmma didi bere a ɛfata de pɛ ahoɔden na ɛnyɛ nsabow.

english_verse: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
translation_verse: Sɛ obi yɛ akwadworɔ a ne mpuran yɛ mmerɛw; sɛ ne nsa nka hwee a ne fi nwini.

english_verse: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
translation_verse: Wɔto pon ma serew, na nsa ma onipa ahosɛpɛw, nanso sika na ɛyɛ biribiara safe.

english_verse: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
translation_verse: Wʼadwene mu mpo nkasa ntia ɔhene, na wo pia mu nso nnome ɔdefo, efisɛ anomaa a ɔnam wim de wʼasɛm bɛkɔ, na anomaa a otu bɛkɔ akɔka.

english_verse: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
translation_verse: Fa wʼawi twa po; na daakye bi wubenya so mfaso.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: Fa hyɛ aguadi ason mu, yiw, nea ɛto so awotwe mu, wunnim atoyerɛnkyɛm a ɛbɛba asase no so.

english_verse: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
translation_verse: Obiara a ɔtwɛn wim nsakrae no rennua, na nea ɔhwɛ omununkum no nso rentwa.

english_verse: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
translation_verse: Sɛnea wunnim ɔkwan a mframa nam so, anaa sɛnea wɔnwen nipadua wɔ ɔyafunu mu no, saa ara na worentumi nte Onyankopɔn nnwuma ase, ade nyinaa Yɛfo no.

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: Dua wʼaba anɔpa, na anwummere nso ma wo nsa nna ho, na wunnim nea ɛbɛyɛ yiye, sɛ eyi anaa eyi, anaasɛ ebia abien no nyinaa bɛyɛ yie. Kae Wo Bɔfo Wɔ Wo Mmerante Bere Mu

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Hann yɛ fɛ; na ɛyɛ aniwa dɛ sɛ ohu owia.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Mfe dodow a onipa bɛtena nkwa yi mu nyinaa ɛsɛ sɛ onya ahotɔ. Nanso ɛsɛ sɛ ɔkae nnabɔne na ɛbɛdɔɔso. Biribiara a ɛbɛba no yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Ma wʼani nnye, aberante, bere a woyɛ ɔbabun, ma wo koma mma wo anigye wɔ wo mmerantebere mu. Di nea wo koma pɛ ne nea wʼaniwa hu akyi, nanso hu sɛ eyinom nyinaa ho Onyankopɔn de wo bɛba atemmu mu.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Enti yi adwennwen biara fi wo koma mu na tow ɔhaw biara a ɛwɔ wo mu no gu, efisɛ mmeranteyɛ ne ahoɔden yɛ ahuhude.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Kae wo Bɔfo wɔ wo mmerantebere mu, ansa na nnabɔne no aba na mfe a wobɛka se, “Minni mu anigye biara” no reba,

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: ansa na owia ne hann, ɔsram ne nsoromma aduru sum, na omununkum asan aba osutɔ akyi.

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: bere a wɔatoto abɔnten no apon mu na awiyambea nnyigyei ano abrɛ ase; bere a nnipa te nnomaa su na wɔanyan, nanso wɔn nnwonto ano abrɛ ase;

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: bere a nnipa suro sorokɔ ne mmɔnten so amanenyasɛm; bere a “ɔsonkoran” dua begu nhwiren na tɛwtɛw twe ne ho kɔ no na nkatede ho adwudwo. Afei onipa kɔ ne daa home mu na agyaadwotwafo tu gu mmɔnten so.

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: Kae no, ansa na dwetɛ hama no atew, anaasɛ sikakɔkɔɔ asanka no abɔ; ansa na sukuruwa no abobɔ wɔ asuten ho, anaasɛ asubura so nkyimii abubu,

english_verse: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
translation_verse: na dɔte san kɔ asase a efi mu bae, na honhom no tu kɔ Onyankopɔn a ɔde mae no nkyɛn.

english_verse: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
translation_verse: “Ahuhude mu ahuhude” ɔsɛnkafo no na ose. “Biribiara yɛ ahuhude!” Asɛm No Awiei

english_verse: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛnkafo no yɛ onyansafo na ɔde nimdeɛ maa nnipa nso. Ɔdwenee na ɔyɛɛ nhwehwɛmu na obubuu mmɛ bebree.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛnkafo no hwehwɛɛ sɛ obenya nsɛm a ɛfata, na nea ɔkyerɛw no yɛ pɛ na ɛyɛ nokware nso.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Anyansafo nsɛm te sɛ nantwikafo mpeaw. Wɔn nsɛm a wɔaboa ano te sɛ nnadewa a wɔde abobɔ dua mu ma akɔ mu yiye. Saa nsɛm yi nyinaa fi Oguanhwɛfo baako nkyɛn.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: Mebɔ wo kɔkɔ sɛ twe wo ho fi biribiara a ɛka eyinom ho, me babarima. Nhoma bebrebe nkyerɛw nni awiei, na ne sua pii no ma honam yɛ mmerɛw.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Afei ne nyinaa atɔ asom; nsɛm no awiei ni: Suro Onyankopɔn na di nʼahyɛde so, na onipa asɛde nyinaa ni.

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Onyankopɔn bebu nneyɛe biara atɛn, nea wɔayɛ asie nso ka ho, sɛ ɛyɛ papa anaa bɔne.

english_verse: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Salomo nnwom mu dwom. Ababaa:

english_verse: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
translation_verse: Ma ɔmfa nʼano mfewano no mfew mʼano, efisɛ wo dɔ no yɛ anigye sen bobesa.

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: Wʼaduhuam yi hua a ɛyɛ anigye; wo din te sɛ aduhuam a wɔahwie. Na ɛnyɛ nwonwa sɛ mmabaa no dɔ wo!

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Fa me kɔ, ma yɛnyɛ ntɛm! Ma ɔhene mfa me nkɔ ne pia mu. Nnamfonom: Yebedi ahurusi na yɛn ani agye wo ho. Yɛbɛkamfo wo dɔ asen bobesa. Ababaa: Sɛ wɔkamfo wo a, na ne kwan so ara ne no!

english_verse: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
translation_verse: Mibiri de, nanso me ho yɛ fɛ, Yerusalem mmabea, mobiri te sɛ Kedar ntamadan, te sɛ, Salomo ntamadan mu ntwamtam!

english_verse: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
translation_verse: Nhwɛ me haw sɛ mibiri nti, efisɛ owia na ayɛ me saa. Me na mmabarima bu fuw me, enti wɔma me kɔhwɛɛ bobe nturo so; na amma manhwɛ mʼankasa me bobeturo.

english_verse: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Kyerɛ me, me dɔfo, faako a wode wo nguankuw kɔ adidi na owigyinae nso, faako a woma wo nguan home. Adɛn nti na ɛsɛ sɛ meyɛ sɛ ɔbea a wakata nʼanim wɔ wo nnamfonom nguankuw ho? Nnamfonom:

english_verse: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
translation_verse: Sɛ wunnim a, mmea mu ɔhoɔfɛfo koraa, fa ɔkwan a nguan fa so so na fa wo mpapomma kɔ adidi wɔ nguanhwɛfo no ntamadan ho. Aberante:

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo, mede wo toto ɔpɔnkɔbere a wɔde hama asa no wɔ Farao nteaseɛnam baako ho no ho.

english_verse: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
translation_verse: Asokaa ama wʼafono ho ayɛ fɛ, na abohemaa a woasina agu wo kɔn mu no fata wo.

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Yɛbɛyɛ sikakɔkɔɔ asokaa a wɔde dwetɛ asisi mu ama wo. Ababaa:

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Bere a ɔhene te ne didipon ho no, nʼaduhuam hua no gyee hɔ.

english_verse: My darling, you are perfume between my breasts;
translation_verse: Me dɔfo ayɛ me sɛ kurobow toa a ɛda me nufu ntam.

english_verse: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Me dɔfo ayɛ me sɛ nhwiren boa a ayɛ frɔmfrɔm wɔ En-Gedi bobeturo mu. Aberante:

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Me dɔfo, wo ho yɛ fɛ! Ao, ahoɔfɛ ni! Wʼaniwa aba te sɛ mmorɔnoma. Ababaa:

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: Me dɔfo, wo ho yɛ fɛ! Ao, ahoɔfɛ ni! Yɛn mpa so yɛ akɔnnɔakɔnnɔ. Aberante:

english_verse: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Yɛn fi mpuran yɛ sida; yɛn nsɛmso yɛ ɔpepaw.

english_verse: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Sɛnea sukooko a ɛwɔ nsɔe mu te no, saa ara na me dɔfo te wɔ mmabaa mu. Ababaa:

english_verse: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
translation_verse: Sɛnea aprɛ te wɔ kwae mu nnua mu no, saa ara na me dɔfo te wɔ mmerante mu. Sɛ metena ne nwini mu a minya ahomeka na nʼaba nso yɛ mʼanom dɛ.

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: Ɔde me akɔ aponto ase, na mʼagyiraehyɛde yɛ ɔdɔ.

english_verse: Refresh and strengthen me with raisins and apples. I am hungry for love!
translation_verse: Momma me bobe aba na minya ahoɔden, momma me aprɛ na ennwudwo me, efisɛ ɔdɔ ama matɔ beraw.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Ne nsa benkum da mʼatiko, na ne nsa nifa aka me afam ne bo.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: Yerusalem mmabea, mede atwewa ne wuram ɔforote hyɛ mo sɛ: Monnkanyan na munnyan ɔdɔ kosi bere a ɛsɛ mu.

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: Tie! me dɔfo! Hwɛ! ɔno na ɔreba no, ɔrehuruhuruw wɔ mmepɔw no so na ɔbɔ pentenkwa wɔ nkoko no so.

english_verse: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
translation_verse: Me dɔfo te sɛ ɔtwe anaa ɔforote. Hwɛ! ogyina yɛn fasu akyi, ɔhwɛ mfɛnsere no mu, wagyen nʼani rehwɛ mfɛnsere no mu.

english_verse: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo kasa kyerɛɛ me se, “Sɔre, me dɔfo ne mʼahoɔfɛ na bra me nkyɛn.

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Hwɛ! awɔwbere atwa mu; na asusow atwa mu kɔ.

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: Nhwiren afifi asase ani: nnwonto bere aso. Wɔte mmorɔnoma su wɔ yɛn asase so.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Borɔdɔma agu nhwiren; na bobe hua agye baabiara. Sɔre bra, me dɔfo; mʼahoɔfɛ, bra me nkyɛn.” Aberante:

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: Mʼaborɔnoma a wohyɛ abotan ntokuru mu, ahintaw wɔ mmepɔw so, ma minhu wʼanim; ma mente wo nne; wo nne yɛ dɛ, na wʼanim yɛ fɛ.

english_verse: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Monkyekyere sakraman no mma yɛn, sakraman nketewa no a wɔsɛe bobe nturo, yɛn bobe nturo a ayɛ frɔmfrɔm no. Ababaa:

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo yɛ me dea, na mewɔ no; ɔhwehwɛ sukooko no mu.

english_verse: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
translation_verse: Enkosi sɛ ade bɛkyɛ na sunsuma bɛsen akɔ no, dan wo ho, me dɔfo, na yɛ sɛ ɔtwewa anaa ɔforote a ɔwɔ nkoko mmonkyi mmonka no so.

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Anadwo mu nyinaa, wɔ me mpa so mehwehwɛɛ nea me koma da no so; mehwehwɛɛ no, nanso manhu no.

english_verse: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Mɛsɔre afei na makokyinkyin kuropɔn no mu, ne mmɔnten so ne gua so; na mahwehwɛ nea me koma da no so. Enti mehwehwɛɛ no nanso manhu no.

english_verse: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
translation_verse: Awɛmfo no huu me bere a wɔrebɔ aprɔw wɔ kuropɔn no mu. “Moahu nea me koma da no so no ana?”

english_verse: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
translation_verse: Mereyɛ atwa wɔn ho pɛ na mihuu nea me koma da no so no. Misoo ne nsa sɛ meremma no nkɔ kosii sɛ mede no baa me na fi, de no kɔɔ nea onyinsɛnee me no dan mu.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem mmabea, mede atwewa ne wuram ɔforote hyɛ mo sɛ Monnkanyan na munnyan ɔdɔ kosi bere a ɛsɛ mu.

english_verse: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
translation_verse: Hena na ofi sare so reba te sɛ wusiw kumɔnn a efi kurobow, aduhuam ne aguadifo pɛprɛ ahorow mu, atutu ne ho yi?

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Monhwɛ, ɛyɛ Salomo teaseɛnam a akofo aduosia bɔ no kyidɔm; ade a ɛwɔ anuonyam pa ara wɔ Israel,

english_verse: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
translation_verse: Wɔn nyinaa bobɔ afoa, wɔn nyinaa wɔ akodi ho nyansa. Wɔn afoa bobɔ wɔn nkyɛn mu, na obiara asiesie ne ho ama nea ebesi anadwo a ɛyɛ hu biara.

english_verse: The throne is made of trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Ɔhene Salomo yɛɛ teaseɛnam no maa ne ho; ɔde Lebanon nnua na ɛyɛe.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Ɔde dwetɛ na ɛyɛɛ nʼadum, ɔde sikakɔkɔɔ na ɛyɛɛ ne nnyinaso. Wɔde biridum ntama na eduraa mu nkongua ho; mu asiesie yɛ ahomeka na Yerusalem mmabea na wɔyɛe.

english_verse: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
translation_verse: Mumfi adi, mo Sion mmabea, mommɛhwɛ ɔhene Salomo sɛ ɔhyɛ ahenkyɛw nea ne na de hyɛɛ no nʼayeforohyia da no, da a odii ahurusi wɔ ne koma mu no.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Wo ho yɛ fɛ, me dɔfo! Ao, wo ho yɛ fɛ! Wʼaniwa a ɛhyehyɛ wo nkataanim mu no te sɛ aborɔnoma. Wo nwi te sɛ mpapokuw a wɔresian Gilead Bepɔw.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Wo se te sɛ nguankuw a wɔatwitwa wɔn ho nwi foforo, a wofi aguaree. Baako mpo nyeraa ɛ.

english_verse: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
translation_verse: Wʼanofafa te sɛ koogyan hama; wʼano yɛ fɛ. Wʼasontɔre a ɛhyɛ wo nkataanim mu te sɛ ntunkum aduaba fa.

english_verse: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
translation_verse: Wo kɔn te sɛ Dawid abantenten, a wɔasi no fɛɛfɛ; na akokyɛm apem sensɛn ho, a ne nyinaa yɛ akofo kyɛm.

english_verse: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
translation_verse: Wo nufu te sɛ atwemma abien, atwemma nta a wodidi wɔ sukooko mu.

english_verse: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
translation_verse: Enkosi sɛ ade bɛkye, ama honhom aguan no, mɛkɔ kurobow bepɔw ne aduhuam nkoko no so.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo, wo ho yɛ fɛ papa; wo ho nni dɛm biara.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: Ma yemfi Lebanon, mʼayeforo, wo ne me mfi Lebanon nkɔ. Sian fi Amana atifi bra, fi Senir atifi, Hermon apampam hɔ, fi gyata buw mu ne mmepɔw a asebɔ dɛɛdɛɛ hɔ.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: Woagye me koma abɔ so, me nuabea, mʼayeforo; woagye me koma abɔ so; wode wʼani a ɛbɔɔ me so, ne wo kɔnmuade mu ɔbohemaa baako.

english_verse: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
translation_verse: Wo dɔ yɛ anigye, me nuabea, mʼayeforo! Hwɛ, wo dɔ sɔ ani sen bobesa, na wʼaduhuam yɛ huam sen pɛprɛ biara.

english_verse: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Asɛm dɛdɛ fi wʼano sɛ ɛwokyɛm, mʼayeforo; nufusu ne ɛwo wɔ wo tɛkrɛma ase. Wo ntade mu hua te sɛ Lebanon de.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
translation_verse: Wote sɛ turo a wɔato ano pon mu, me nuabea, mʼayeforo; woyɛ asuti a wɔagye ho ban, asubura a wɔasɔw ano.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: Wo nnua yɛ nnuabafuw so ntunkum a ɛsow aba pa, ahuahaa ne nnuannua,

english_verse: saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes —all the finest spices.
translation_verse: nnuannua ne mmetire, osiko ne sinamon, a ohuamfufu nnua ahorow, kurobow ne dupapo ne pɛprɛ papa ahorow nyinaa ka ho.

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Woyɛ asubura turo, abura a nsu sen fi mu a ɛsen fi Lebanon. Ababaa:

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: Sɔre, atifi fam mframa! Bra, anafo fam mframa! Bɔ fa me turo mu, sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ne hua no begyigye afa baabiara. Ma me dɔfo mmra ne turo mu na ɔmmɛka ne nnuaba papa no nhwɛ.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Maba me turo mu, me nuabea, mʼayeforo; maboaboa me kurobow ne me nnuhuam ano. Madi me wokyɛm ne ɛwo; manom me bobesa ne me nufusu. Nnamfonom: Nnamfonom, munnidi na monnom; Adɔfonom, monnom nea ɛbɛmee mo dɔ. Ababaa:

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Medae, nanso me koma anna. Tie! me dɔfo rebɔ pon no mu; “Bue me, me nuabea, me dɔ, mʼaborɔnoma, a ne ho nni dɛm. Obosu afɔw me tirim, anadwo mu bosu afɔw me nwi.”

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Maworɔw mʼatade, mensan mfa nhyɛ ana? Mahohoro mʼanan ase, memma ho nyɛ fi bio ana?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo yɛɛ sɛ ɔrebue pon no me koma fii ase bɔɔ kim kim wɔ me mu.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Mesɔree sɛ merekobue me dɔfo, na me nsa ho kurobow ne me nsateaa ho aduhuam, yɛɛ korɔkorɔ no nsa ho.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: Mibue maa me dɔfo no, nanso na ɔkɔ. Ne kɔ no maa me ho dwiriw me. Mehwehwɛɛ no nanso manhu no baabiara. Mefrɛɛ no nanso wannye me so.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Awɛmfo no huu me bere a wɔrebɔ aporɔw wɔ kuropɔn no mu. Wɔbobɔɔ me pirapiraa me; woyii mʼatade kɔe; saa awɛmfo a wɔwɛn afasu no!

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Yerusalem mmabea, mehyɛ mo, sɛ muhu me dɔfo no a, asɛm bɛn na mobɛka akyerɛ no? Monka nkyerɛ no se ɔdɔ ama matɔ beraw. Nnamfonom:

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: Dɛn na wo dɔfo de sen afoforo, mmea ahoɔfɛfo mu ahoɔfɛ? Dɛn na wo dɔfo de sen afoforo a enti wohyɛ yɛn sɛɛ? Ababaa:

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Me dɔfo ho twa na ogyigye, wɔfa mpem du a, ɔyɛ sononko.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: Ne ti yɛ sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa; ne ti so nwi yɛ kuhaa, na ɛyɛ tuntum sɛ kwaakwaadabi.

english_verse: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
translation_verse: Nʼaniwa aba te sɛ aborɔnoma a ogyina asuwa bi ho; ɛte sɛ nea wɔde nufusu aguare no, na etuatua hɔ sɛ abohemaa.

english_verse: His face is a garden of sweet-smelling spices; his lips are lilies dripping with perfume.
translation_verse: Nʼafono te sɛ pɛprɛ a wɔasɛw no kɛtɛ. Ɛho hua te sɛ aduhuam. Nʼanofafa te sɛ sukooko a ɛsosɔ kurobow.

english_verse: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.
translation_verse: Nʼabasa te sɛ sikakɔkɔɔ abaa a wɔde sikabereɛbo asisi mu. Ne nipadua te sɛ asonse a wɔatwiw ho na wɔde hoabo adura ho.

english_verse: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
translation_verse: Nʼanan te sɛ abohemaa afadum a esisi sikakɔkɔɔ ankasa nnyinaso so. Ne bɔbea te sɛ Lebanon a ɔyɛ sononko sɛ ne sida.

english_verse: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
translation_verse: Nʼano te sɛ ɔdɛ ankasa; ɔkwan biara so, ne ho yɛ fɛ. Me dɔfo ni, mʼadamfo ni, Yerusalem mmabea.
